children.text:
Avadānaśatakam* |
|| namaḥ śrīsarvajñāya ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Avadānaśatakam</s> (The Hundred Avadānas) |
|| Homage to the glorious Omniscient One ||
[editorial page reference] The first <s>varga</s> (section) |

children.text: tasyoddānam* |
children.translated_text: Its <s>uddāna</s> (summary verse) |

children.text: pūrṇabhadro yaśomatī kusīdo vaṇijas tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, <s>Yaśomatī</s>, <s>Kusīda</s>, the merchant likewise |

children.text: somo vaḍikaḥ padmāṅkaḥ pañcālo dhūpa eva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s>, <s>Vaḍika</s>, <s>Padmāṅka</s>, <s>Pañcāla</s>, and <s>Dhūpa</s> as well |

children.text: rājānaṃ paścimaṃ kṛtvā vargo hy eṣa samudditaḥ || AVŚ_1 ||
children.translated_text: With the king as the last, this <s>varga</s> (section) is thus proclaimed || AVŚ_1 ||

children.text: AVŚ_1 pūrṇabhadraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_1 <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | tatra bhagavato 'cirābhisaṃbuddhabodher yaśasā ca sarvaloka āpūrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents) — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known as one of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicines for the sick, together with the <s>saṃgha</s> (community) of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s> in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove) at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground). There, since the <s>Bhagavān</s> had recently attained <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), the entire world was filled with his fame ||

children.text: atha dakṣiṇāgiriṣu janapade saṃpūrṇo nāma brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalas tyāgaruciḥ pradānaruciḥ pradānābhirato mahati tyāgo vartate ||
children.translated_text: Now in the southern mountain region there dwelt a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder named <s>Saṃpūrṇa</s>, wealthy, possessing great riches, great fortune, with vast and extensive possessions, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) in wealth, competing with the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. He was faithful, virtuous, of noble disposition, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>dharma</s> (the teaching), tender toward his people, delighting in generosity, delighting in giving, devoted to giving — he practiced great liberality ||

children.text: yāvad asau sarvapāṣaṇḍikaṃ yajñam ārabdho yaṣṭum*, yatrānekāni tīrthikaśatasahasrāṇi bhuñjate sma | yadā bhagavatā rājā bimbisāraḥ saparivāro vinītaḥ, tasya ca vinayād bahūni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi vinayam upagatāni, tadā rājagṛhāt pūrṇasya jñātayo 'bhyāgatya pūrṇasya purastād buddhasya varṇaṃ bhāṣayituṃ pravṛttā dharmasya saṃghasya ca | atha pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālo bhagavato guṇasaṃkīrtanaṃ pratiśrutya mahāntaṃ prasādaṃ pratilabdhavān* | tataḥ śaraṇam abhiruhya rājagṛhābhimukhaḥ sthitvā ubhau jānumaṇḍale pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya puṣpāṇi kṣipan*, dhūpam udakaṃ ca bhagavantam āyācituṃ pravṛttaḥ: āgacchatu bhagavān yajñaṃ me anubhavituṃ yajñavāṭam iti | atha tāni puṣpāṇi buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvenopari bhagavataḥ puṣpamaṇḍapaṃ kṣiptvā tasthuḥ dhūpo 'bhrakūṭavad udakaṃ vaiḍūryaśalākavat ||
children.translated_text: In time, he undertook a great sacrifice open to all sects, at which many hundreds of thousands of <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics) ate. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had converted King <s>Bimbisāra</s> together with his retinue, and through his conversion many hundreds of thousands of beings had come to the teaching, then relatives of <s>Pūrṇa</s> came from <s>Rājagṛha</s> and began to proclaim before <s>Pūrṇa</s> the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Then <s>Pūrṇa</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder, having heard the recitation of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> qualities, obtained great faith. Thereupon, ascending to a high place and standing facing toward <s>Rājagṛha</s>, placing both his knees on the ground, casting flowers, and offering incense and water, he began to invite the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> come to partake of my sacrifice, to the sacrificial ground!" Then those flowers, through the supernatural power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and the supernatural power of the <s>devatās</s> (deities), rose up and formed a canopy of flowers above the <s>Bhagavān</s> and remained suspended; the incense stood like a mass of clouds, and the water like a crystal wand of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) ||

children.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha: kuta idaṃ bhadanta nimantraṇam āyātam iti | bhagavān āha: dakṣiṇāgiriṣv ānanda janapade saṃpūrṇo nāma brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ prativasati,
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "From where, <s>Bhadanta</s> (Reverend), has this invitation come?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "In the southern mountain region, <s>Ānanda</s>, there dwells a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder named <s>Saṃpūrṇa</s>,
[editorial page reference]

children.text:
tatrāsmābhir gantavyam, sajjībhavantu bhikṣava iti | bhagavān bhikṣusahasraparivṛtto dakṣiṇāgiriṣu janapade cārikāṃ caritvā pūrṇasya brāhmaṇamahāśālasya yajñavāṭasamīpe sthitvā cintām āpede: yanv ahaṃ pūrṇabrāhmaṇam ṛddhiprātihāryeṇāvarjayeyam iti | atha bhagavāṃs taṃ bhikṣusahasram antardhāpya ekaḥ pātracarakavyagrahastaḥ pūrṇasmīpe sthitaḥ | atha pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālo bhagavantaṃ dadarśa dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyaṃjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punas tvaritatvaritaṃ bhagavataḥ samīpam upasaṃkramya bhagavantam uvāca: svāgataṃ bhagavan, niṣīdatu bhagavān, kriyatāṃ āsanaparigraho mamānugrahārtham iti | bhagavān āha: yadi te parityaktaṃ dīyatām asmin pātra iti | atha pūrṇo brāhmamahāśālaḥ pañcamāṇavakaśataparivṛto bhagavato vividhabhakṣyabhojyakhādyalehyapeyacoṣyādibhir āhārair ārabdhaḥ pātraṃ paripūrayitum* | bhagavān api svakāt pātrād bhikṣupātreṣv āhāraṃ saṃkramayati | yadā bhagavato viditaṃ pūrṇāni bhikṣusahasrasya pātrāṇīti, tadā svapātraṃ pūrṇam ādarśitum* | tato bhikṣusahasraṃ pūrṇapātram ardhacandrākāreṇa darśitavān | devatābhir apy ākāśasthābhiḥ śabdam udīritam: pūrṇāni bhagavato bhikṣusahasrasya ca pātrāṇīti |
  tataḥ prātihāryadarśanāt pūrṇaḥ prasādajāto mūlanikṛtta iva drumo hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditaḥ udagraprītisaumanasyajāto bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhiṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayitā, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text:
we must go there; let the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) prepare themselves." The <s>Bhagavān</s>, attended by a thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>, wandered through the southern mountain region and, standing near the sacrificial ground of <s>Pūrṇa</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder, reflected: "Let me win over the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s> through a display of supernatural power." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having made those thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> invisible, stood alone near <s>Pūrṇa</s> with his bowl and wandering-monk's staff in hand. Then <s>Pūrṇa</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder beheld the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being) and resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with an aura extending a <s>vyāma</s> (fathom), surpassing the radiance of a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on every side. Having seen him, he swiftly approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said: "Welcome, <s>Bhagavān</s>! Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> be seated; please accept a seat for my benefit." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "If you are willing to give, then give into this bowl." Then <s>Pūrṇa</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder, attended by five hundred young <s>brāhmaṇa</s> students, began to fill the bowl with various foods — solid foods, cooked foods, hard foods, lickable foods, drinkable foods, suckable foods, and other provisions. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> transferred the food from his own bowl into the bowls of the <s>bhikṣus</s>. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> knew that the bowls of the thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> were full, he then revealed his own bowl as full. Thereupon he displayed the thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> with their full bowls in a half-moon formation. And the <s>devatās</s> (deities) standing in the sky proclaimed: "The bowls of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and of the thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> are full!"
Then, from witnessing this miracle, <s>Pūrṇa</s>, filled with faith, like a tree cut at the root, joyful, delighted, elated, with exultant gladness and happiness arisen, fell at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and began to make a vow: "By this root of merit, by this arising of the thought of awakening, and by this relinquishing of gifts, may I become a <s>Buddha</s> in this blind world without a guide, without a leader — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed over, who liberates those not yet freed, who comforts those without comfort, and who leads to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) those who have not yet attained it" ||

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrṇasya brāhmaṇamahāśālasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ, api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the chain of causes and the chain of <s>karma</s> (actions) of <s>Pūrṇa</s> the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householder, produced a smile. For it is the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, produce a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays of light issue from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having reached the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down as something cool, and in the cold hells they fall down as something warm. Thereby the exceptional sufferings of those beings are allayed. They think: "Have we, friends, departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?" To generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth a magical emanation. Seeing the emanation, they think: "Indeed we have not, friends, departed from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere; rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and through his power our exceptional sufferings have been allayed." Having placed their minds in faith toward the emanation, they exhaust their <s>karma</s> that was to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among <s>devas</s> (gods) and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those rays that go upward reach the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> (Four Great Kings), <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three),  <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>,
[editorial page reference]

children.text: nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> (Delighting in Creation), <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> (Controlling Others' Creations), <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s> (Limited Radiance), <s>Apramāṇābha</s> (Immeasurable Radiance), <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Streaming Radiance), <s>Parīttaśubha</s> (Limited Virtue), <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> (Immeasurable Virtue), <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (Total Virtue), <s>Anabhraka</s> (Cloudless), <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> (Merit-Born), <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (Great Fruit), <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s> (Fair-Seeing), <s>Sudarśana</s> (Beautiful to Behold), and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (Highest) heavens, and proclaim among those <s>devas</s>: "All is impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self," and they recite a pair of verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of death, as an elephant crushes a hut of reeds! || AVŚ_1.1 ||

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_1.2 || iti
children.translated_text:
Whoever shall dwell heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline),
having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering" || AVŚ_1.2 ||

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm, follow behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>, ever behind him. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to prophesy about past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If he wishes to prophesy the future, they vanish in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (lesser universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth among <s>devas</s>, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (awakening as a disciple), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they vanish at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), they vanish at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) ||

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and vanished at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance). Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "Of myriad kinds, adorned with a thousand hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: this sheaf of rays issued from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_1.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun" || AVŚ_1.3 ||

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recites verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "Free from worldly existence, having abandoned wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s>, supreme causes of good in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile, white as a conch-shell or lotus-fiber" || AVŚ_1.4 ||

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself realized this at the proper time through your wisdom, O hero,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are longing to know, O <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast and supreme words, O bull among sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_1.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen, with your auspicious speech" || AVŚ_1.5 ||

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
children.translated_text:
"Not without cause do the perfectly awakened ones, the protectors,
steadfast as the ocean, mountains, and kings, display a smile;
[editorial page reference]

children.text:
yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_1.6 || iti
  <Speyer 7> bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | eṣa ānanda pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ | anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya pūrṇabhadro nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti || yadā bhagavatā pūrṇo brāhmaṇamahāśālo 'nuttarāyāṃ smyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtaḥ, tadā pūrṇena bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghas traimāsyaṃ yajñavāṭe bhojitaḥ | bhūyaś cānena citrāṇi kuśalamūlāni samavaropitāni ||
children.translated_text: The wise ones display a <s>smita</s> (smile) for a purpose— the masses of people long to hear that purpose. || AVŚ_1.6 || Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke: So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-Gone Ones), <s>Arhats</s> (Worthy Ones), <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> (Perfectly Awakened Ones) display a <s>smita</s> (smile). This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the brahmin householder. Through this <s>kuśalamūla</s> (root of merit), this arising of the mind, and this relinquishing of gifts, having accumulated the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) that is brought to completion over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), and having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) suffused with <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion), he shall become a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, endowed with the ten <s>balas</s> (powers), the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the three <s>āveṇika smṛtyupasthānas</s> (special mindfulnesses), and <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion). This is the gift-merit of his serene faith in my presence. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had thus given <s>Pūrṇa</s> the brahmin householder a <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prophecy) of supreme perfect awakening, <s>Pūrṇa</s> fed the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>śrāvaka-saṃgha</s> (community of disciples) for three months in the sacrificial enclosure. And further, he planted manifold <s>kuśalamūlas</s> (roots of merit).

children.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ, śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), you should train thus: 'We shall honor the Teacher, revere the Teacher, respect and worship the Teacher; having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell in dependence upon him.' Thus, <s>bhikṣus</s>, should you train.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_2 yaśomatī | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_2 <s>Yaśomatī</s> | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: <Speyer 8> buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho vaiśālīm upaniśritya viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām* | atha pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghpuraskṛto vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat | sāvadānīṃ vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā yena siṃhasya senāpater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, respected, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (eagle-beings), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents)—thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>—the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, renowned and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the <s>śrāvaka-saṃgha</s> (community of disciples), was dwelling near <s>Vaiśālī</s> at the Monkey Pond, in the Gabled Hall. Then in the forenoon, having dressed and taken up his bowl and robe, surrounded by the company of <s>bhikṣus</s> and preceded by the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>, he entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms. Having walked through <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms, he approached the dwelling of General <s>Siṃha</s>. Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: atha siṃhasya senāpateḥ snuṣā yasomatī nama abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā | sā bhagavato vicitralakṣaṇojjvalakāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā atyarthaṃ prasādaṃ labdhavatī | sā śvaśuraṃ papraccha: asti kaścid upāyo yenāham apy evaṃguṇayuktā syām iti | atha siṃhasya senāpater etad abhavat: udārādhimuktā bateyaṃ dārikā | yadi punar iyaṃ pratyayam āsādayet, kuryād anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānam iti viditvoktavān*: dārike yadi hetuṃ samādāya vartiṣyasi, tvam apy evaṃvidhā bhaviṣyasi yādṛśo bhagavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Now General <s>Siṃha</s>'s daughter-in-law, named <s>Yaśomatī</s>, was beautiful, lovely, and charming. Seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s body blazing with wondrous marks, she was filled with the utmost faith. She asked her father-in-law: 'Is there some means by which I too could become endowed with such qualities?' Then General <s>Siṃha</s> thought: 'This girl has lofty aspirations indeed! If she were to find the right conditions, she would make a <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vow) for supreme perfect awakening.' Having understood this, he said: 'Girl, if you undertake the cause and persist in it, you too shall become like the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

children.text: <Speyer 9> tataḥ siṃhena senāpatinā yaśomatyāḥ prasādābhivṛddhyarthaṃ prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ ratnāni ca dattāni | tato yaśomatyā dārikayā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then General <s>Siṃha</s>, in order to increase <s>Yaśomatī</s>'s faith, gave her abundant gold, silver, and jewels. Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s> invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>śrāvaka-saṃgha</s> for a meal in the inner quarters the next day.

children.text: adhivāsitaṃ ca bhagavatā tasyā anugrahārtham* || atha yaśomatī dārikā suvarṇamayāni puṣpāṇi kārayitvā rūpyamayāṇi ratnamayāni prabhūtagandhamālyavilepanasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā śatarasam āhāraṃ sajjīkṛtya bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati: samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti | atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena siṃhasya senāpater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | atha yaśomatī dārikā sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śatarasenāhāreṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpya puṣpāṇi bhagavati kṣeptum ārabdhā | atha tāni puṣpāṇi upari bhagavato ratnakūṭāgāro ratnacchatraṃ ratnamaṇḍapa ivāvasthitam*, yan na na śakyaṃ suśikṣitena karmakāreṇa karmāntevāsinā vā kartum*, yathāpi tad buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devānubhāvena || atha yaśomatī dārikā tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ sarvaśarīreṇa bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhā: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayitā, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: And the <s>Bhagavān</s> consented, for the sake of her benefit. Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>, having had flowers made of gold, of silver, and of jewels, having gathered abundant incense, garlands, and ointments, and having prepared a meal of a hundred flavors, announced the time to the <s>Bhagavān</s> through a messenger: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready; may the <s>Bhagavān</s> come at his convenience.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the company of <s>bhikṣus</s> and preceded by the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>, approached the dwelling of General <s>Siṃha</s>. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared at the head of the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>. Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>, knowing the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, satisfied them with her own hands with the meal of a hundred flavors, and began to cast flowers upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then those flowers remained suspended above the <s>Bhagavān</s> like a jeweled pavilion, a jeweled parasol, a jeweled canopy—such as could not be fashioned even by a well-trained craftsman or his apprentice; for such is the <s>buddhānubhāva</s> (power of the Buddhas) and the <s>devānubhāva</s> (power of the gods). Then the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>, seeing that utterly wondrous miracle that captivated gods and humans, fell with her whole body at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet like a tree cut at the root, and began to make a <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vow): 'By this <s>kuśalamūla</s> (root of merit), this arising of the mind, and this relinquishing of gifts, may I become a <s>Buddha</s> in this blind world without a leader, without a guide—one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates the unliberated, who gives comfort to the uncomforted, who leads to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) those who have not attained it.'

children.text: atha bhagavān yaśomatyā dārikāyā hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ, api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>'s chain of causes and chain of <s>karmas</s> (actions), displayed a <s>smita</s> (smile). For it is the <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law) that whenever the <s>Buddha Bhagavāns</s> display a <s>smita</s>, at that time rays of blue, yellow, red, and white issue forth from their mouths—some descend downward, some ascend upward. Those that descend downward go to the hells—<s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s>—and in the hot hells they fall down as something cool, and in the cold hells they fall down as something warm. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are allayed. They think: 'Have we, friends, departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' To generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth an emanation (<s>nirmita</s>). Seeing the emanation, they think: 'We have indeed not departed from here, friends, nor have we been reborn elsewhere; rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our distinctive sufferings have been allayed.' Having placed their faith in the emanation and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those rays that ascend upward go to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens, and proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!'—and they recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: Strive forth! Renounce! Apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_2.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant crushes a reed hut. || AVŚ_2.1 ||

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_2.2 || iti
children.translated_text: For whoever shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma-Vinaya</s> (Doctrine and Discipline), having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering. || AVŚ_2.2 ||

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world system), follow behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>, close behind him. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> is about to prophesy past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind him. If he is about to prophesy the future, they disappear in front of him. If he is about to prophesy rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet. If he is about to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels. If he is about to prophesy rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they disappear at his big toe. If he is about to prophesy rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees. If he is about to prophesy the sovereignty of a lesser <s>Cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), they disappear in his left palm. If he is about to prophesy the sovereignty of a <s>Cakravartin</s>, they disappear in his right palm. If he is about to prophesy rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel. If he is about to prophesy <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (the awakening of a disciple), they disappear at his mouth. If he is about to prophesy <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (the awakening of a solitary realizer), they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he is about to prophesy supreme perfect awakening, they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha: <Speyer 12>
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and disappeared at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance). Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: A cluster of rays, variegated with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: issued forth from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_2.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the sun when it rises. || AVŚ_2.3 ||

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recites verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, rid of misery and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: are the supreme source of benefit in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_2.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a <s>smita</s> (smile) as white as a conch shell or a lotus stalk. || AVŚ_2.4 ||

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: Having yourself understood with your <s>buddhi</s> (wisdom) at this very moment, O Hero,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are filled with longing, O <s>Śramaṇa</s> (Ascetic), O Lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steady, supreme words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_2.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen, with your auspicious words. || AVŚ_2.5 ||

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_2.6 || iti
children.translated_text: Not without cause do the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> (Fully Awakened Ones), the Protectors, steadfast as the ocean and the king of mountains, display a <s>smita</s> (smile). The wise ones display a <s>smita</s> for a purpose— the masses of people long to hear that purpose. || AVŚ_2.6 ||

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anayā yaśomatyā dārikayā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣā ānanda yaśomatī dārikā anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke: So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> display a <s>smita</s> (smile). Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s> has rendered such worship to me? 'Indeed, Venerable Sir.' This, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the girl <s>Yaśomatī</s>: through this <s>kuśalamūla</s> (root of merit), this arising of the mind, and this relinquishing of gifts, having accumulated the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) that is brought to completion over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), suffused with <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion),

children.text: ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya ratnamatir nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittasyābhiprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), she shall become a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Ratnamati</s>, endowed with the ten <s>balas</s> (powers), the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the three <s>āveṇika smṛtyupasthānas</s> (special mindfulnesses), and <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion). This is her gift-merit: the serene faith of mind in my presence.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_3 kusīdaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_3 <s>Kusīda</s> | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī prativasati, āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena saḍṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato na putro na duhitā | sa kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham* | na me putro na duhitā | mamātyayāt sarvasvāpateyam aputrakam iti kṛtvā rājavidheyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇanaimittikasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavair ucyate: devatāyācanaṃ kuruṣveti || asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti | tac ca naivam* | yady evam abhaviṣyat, ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ | api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | katameṣāṃ trayāṇām* | mātāpitarāu raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau | mātā kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī | gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati | eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | tathā hy asau śramaṇabrāhmaṇanaimittikasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavavipralabdho 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate sma | tadyathā ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ | sahajāḥ sahadharmikā nityānubandhā api devatā āyācate sma | sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati | anyatamaś ca satvo 'nyatamasmāt satvanikāyāc cyutvā tasyāḥ prajāpatyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntaḥ | pañcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme | katame pañca | raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti, viraktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti | kālaṃ jānāti ṛtuṃ jānāti | garbham avakrāntaṃ jānāti | yasya sakāśād garbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti | dārakaṃ jānāti | dārikāṃ jānāti | saced dārako bhavati dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | saced dārikā bhavati vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | sā āttamanāttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati: diṣṭyā āryaputra vardhase | āpannasatvāsmi saṃvṛttā | yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti | so 'py āttamanāttamanāḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there lived a certain guild-master — rich, of great wealth, of great possessions, with extensive and vast property, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. With her he enjoyed himself, took his pleasure, and dallied. But as he enjoyed, took pleasure, and dallied, no son or daughter [was born]. Placing his chin upon his hand, he remained absorbed in thought: 'My household is endowed with manifold wealth; I have neither son nor daughter. After my death, all my property, being without an heir, will become subject to the king.' He was told by ascetics, Brahmins, soothsayers, friends, relatives, and kinsmen: 'Make prayers to a deity!' And indeed there is this popular saying: 'Through prayers, sons and daughters are born.' But that is not so. If it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just like a wheel-turning king (<s>Cakravartin</s>). Rather, it is from the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. What three? The parents must be passionate and united; the mother must be healthy and in her fertile period; and a <s>Gandharva</s> (spirit seeking rebirth) must be present. From the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born. And so this man, deceived by ascetics, Brahmins, soothsayers, friends, relatives, and kinsmen, being childless yet longing for a son, made prayers to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), <s>Brahmā</s>, and other particular deities — such as garden deities, forest deities, crossroad deities, intersection deities, and deities who accept offerings. He also prayed to deities who are innate, who share the same <s>dharma</s>, and who are constant attendants. While he remained thus devoted to prayers, a certain being, having passed away from a certain class of beings, descended into the womb of his wife. There are five special faculties in certain women of the wise kind: she knows when a man is passionate; she knows when a man is dispassionate; she knows the time; she knows the fertile period; she knows when conception has taken place; she knows from whom the embryo was conceived; she knows if it is a boy; she knows if it is a girl. If it is a boy, it rests on the right side of the womb; if it is a girl, it rests on the left side. She, overjoyed, informed her husband: 'Rejoice, noble son! I have become pregnant. And since it rests on my right side, it will certainly be a boy.' He too was overjoyed,

children.text:
pūrvakāyam atyunnamayya *{abhyunnamayya}* dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya udānam udānayati: apy evāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam* | jāto me syān nāvajātaḥ | kṛtyāni me kurvīta | bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyāt | dāyād yaṃ pratipadyeta | kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt* | asmākaṃ cāpy atītakālagatānām alpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni datvā kṛtyāni kṛtvā asmākaṃ nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādekṣyati: idaṃ tayor yatratatropapannayor gacchator anugacchatv iti | āpannasatvāṃ caināṃ viditvopariprāsādatalagatām ayantritāṃ dhārayati | śīte śītopakaraṇair uṣṇe uṣṇopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptair āhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhārair hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīm apsarasam iva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcān mañcaṃ pīṭhāt pīṭham anavatarantīm adharimāṃ bhūmim* | na cāsyāḥ kiṃcid amanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ yāvad eva garbhasya paripākāya | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jātaḥ | abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ | janmani cāsya tat kulaṃ nanditam* | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātayaḥ ūcuḥ: yasmād asya janmani sarvakulaṃ nanditam, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya nanda iti nāmeti | tasya nanda iti nāma vyavasthāpitam* || nando dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* |
  yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ paṃcavarṣaḥ ṣaḍvarṣo vā, tadā kusīdaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ paramakusīdaḥ | necchati śayanāsanād apy utthātum* | tena tīkṣṇaniśitabuddhitayā antargṛhasthenaiva śāstrāṇy adhītāni || atha śreṣṭhina etad abhavat: so 'pi me kadācit karhicid devatārādhanayā putro jātaḥ, so 'pi kusīdaḥ paramakusīdaḥ | śayanāsanād api nottiṣṭhate | tat kiṃ mamānenedṛgjātīyena putreṇa, yo nāma svasthaśarīro bhūtvā paśur iva saṃtiṣṭhatīti || sa ca śreṣṭhī pūraṇābhiprasannaḥ | tena ṣaṭ tīrthikāḥ śāstāraḥ svagṛham āhūtāḥ: api nāma ayaṃ dārakas teṣāṃ darśanād gauravajātaḥ śayanāsanād api tāvad uttiṣṭhet* | atha kusīdo dārakas tāṃś chāstṝn dṛṣṭvā cakṣuḥsaṃprekṣaṇām api na kṛtavān*, kaḥ punar vāda utthāsyati vā abhivādayiṣyati vā, āsanena vā upanimantrayiṣyati | atha sa gṛhapatis tām evāvasthāṃ dṛṣṭvā suṣṭhutaram utkaṇṭhitaḥ kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ |
  atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ
children.translated_text: raising his upper body high and extending his right arm, he uttered an exclamation of joy: 'May I indeed see the long-desired face of a son! May he be born to me, not stillborn! May he perform my duties! May he repay what has been nurtured! May he receive his inheritance! May my family lineage endure for a long time! And when we have passed away, having given little or much in charity and performed the rites, he shall dedicate the merit in our name: "May this reach those two, wherever they may be reborn."' Knowing her to be pregnant, he kept her on the upper floor of the palace, unrestricted, and cared for her — in cold weather with articles for cold, in hot weather with articles for heat — with foods prescribed by physicians, not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent, avoiding bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent [extremes] — her limbs adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>Apsaras</s> wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, not descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the ground below — and no unpleasant sound reached her ears until the ripening of the pregnancy. She, at the end of eight or nine months, gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing. At his birth, that family rejoiced. At his birth, having performed the birth-celebration, a name was assigned: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since at his birth the entire family rejoiced (<s>nandita</s>), therefore let the boy's name be <s>Nanda</s>.' Thus the name <s>Nanda</s> was assigned. The boy <s>Nanda</s> was given to eight nurses: two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, skimmed ghee, and other choice provisions, and grew rapidly — like a lotus in a lake. When he had grown up, five or six years old, he became lazy — extremely lazy. He did not wish to rise even from his bed. But with his sharp and keen intelligence, while remaining inside the house, he mastered the scriptures. Then the guild-master had this thought: 'That son who was born to me through prayers to a deity — he too is lazy, extremely lazy; he does not even rise from his bed. What use is such a son to me, who, though healthy in body, sits like an animal?' Now that guild-master was devoted to <s>Pūraṇa</s> (Pūraṇa Kāśyapa, a non-Buddhist teacher). He invited the six heretical teachers to his house [thinking]: 'Perhaps this boy, out of respect upon seeing them, might at least rise from his bed.' But the lazy boy, seeing those teachers, did not even give them a glance — let alone rising or greeting them or offering them a seat. Then the householder, seeing this state of affairs, became even more distressed, placed his chin upon his hand, and remained absorbed in thought. Meanwhile — there is nothing unknown, unseen, unlearned, or unrealized by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. For it is the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones — who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, possessed of singular protection, abiding in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three matters of taming, who have crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, who have long practiced the four means of winning over [beings], who have abandoned the five limbs [of desire], who have transcended the five destinies, who are endowed with the six limbs [of enlightenment], who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), who are adorned with the blossoms of the seven factors of awakening, who are guides on the eightfold path,

children.text: navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya ca buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam* | kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām* | kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam* | kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi | kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam* | kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam* | kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: who are skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, who are strong with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who are distinguished beyond a thousand rulers of the ten [directions] — three times at night and three times during the day to survey the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, and knowledge-and-vision arises: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has come to difficulty? Who has come to a strait? Who has come to distress? Who has come to difficulty, strait, and distress? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who gravitates toward the lower realms? Whom shall I, having lifted from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, shall I extend a hand to pull them out? Whom, deprived of the noble wealth, shall I establish in the sovereignty of the noble riches? Whose eyes, covered by the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? For whom shall I plant unplanted roots of merit? For whom shall I ripen those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already ripened?' And [the scripture] says:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the [appropriate] time for those who are to be trained, like [a cow never abandons] her calves.' // AVŚ_3.1 //

children.text: paśyati bhagavān: ayaṃ dārakaḥ kusīdo maddarśanād vīryam ārapsyate yāvad anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ pariṇāmayiṣyatīti | tato bhagavatā tīrthyānāṃ madadarpacchittyarthaṃ dārakasya ca kuśalamūlasaṃjananārthaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāḥ kanakavarṇamarīcaya utsṛṣṭāḥ, yais tad gṛhaṃ samantād avabhāsitam* | kalpasahasraparibhāvitāś ca maitryaṃśava utsṛṣṭāḥ, yair asya spṛṣṭamātraṃ śarīraṃ prahlāditam* | sa itaś cāmutaś ca prekṣitum ārabdhaḥ: kasya prabhāvān mama śarīraṃ prahlāditam iti | tato bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛtas tad gṛhaṃ praviveśa | dadarśa kusīdo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣulakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛta aśītyā cānuvyaṃjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ paraṃ prasādam āpannaḥ | sahasā svayam evotthāya bhagavato 'rthe āsanaṃ prajñapayati | evaṃ cāha: etu bhagavān, svāgataṃ bhagavataḥ, niṣīdatu bhagavān prajñapta evāsana iti | athāsya mātāpitarāv antarjanaś cādṛṣṭapūrvaprabhāvaṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ vismayam āpannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One perceived: 'This lazy boy, upon seeing me, will rouse his energy and will even turn his mind toward supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' Then the Blessed One, for the purpose of cutting the pride and arrogance of the heretics and for the purpose of generating roots of merit in the boy, emitted rays of golden color surpassing the radiance of a thousand suns, by which that entire house was illuminated. And he emitted rays of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) that had been cultivated for a thousand <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages), by which the boy's body was instantly refreshed and gladdened. He began to look this way and that: 'By whose power has my body been refreshed?' Then the Blessed One, surrounded by the assembly of monks, entered that house. The lazy one beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a <s>vyāma</s> (fathom's span), of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him, he was filled with supreme faith. Of his own accord, he suddenly rose and prepared a seat for the Blessed One, and spoke thus: 'Let the Blessed One come! Welcome to the Blessed One! Let the Blessed One sit on this prepared seat.' Then his parents and the household, seeing this unprecedented display of power, were filled with the utmost wonder.

children.text: tataḥ kusīdo dārako harṣavikasitābhyāṃ nayanābhyāṃ bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā anekaprakāraṃ kausīdyasyāvarṇo bhāṣitaḥ, vīryārambhasya cānuśaṃsaḥ | candanamayīṃ cāsya yaṣṭim anuprayacchati: imāṃ dāraka yaṣṭim ākoṭayeti | sa tām ākoṭayitum ārabdhaḥ | athāsau yaṣṭir ākoṭyamānā manojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ karoti, vividhāni ca ratnanidhānāni paśyati | tasyaitad abhavat: mahān batāyaṃ vīryārambhe viśeṣo yanv ahaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā vīryam ārabheyeti | sa śrāvastyāṃ ghaṇṭāv avaghoṣaṇaṃ sārthavāham ātmānam udghoṣya ṣaḍvārān mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | tataḥ siddhayānapātreṇa mahāratnasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā bhagavān antarniveśane saśrāvakasaṃgho bhojitaḥ | anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: Then the boy <s>Kusīda</s> (Lazy), his eyes blooming with joy, having paid homage at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, sat down before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke to him at length about the faults of laziness and the benefits of exertion of effort. He then handed him a sandalwood staff, saying: 'Strike this staff, boy.' He began to strike it. And that staff, when struck, produced a delightful sound, and he saw various treasure-stores of gems. This thought arose in him: 'Great indeed is the reward of exertion of effort! I should exert myself with even greater intensity.' In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, having announced himself as a caravan-leader by the ringing of a bell, he descended into the great ocean six times. Then, having gathered a great collection of jewels in a successful voyage, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was fed in his inner mansion along with the community of disciples. And he made an aspiration for the supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: atha bhagavān kusīdasya dārakasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā
children.translated_text: Now the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the chain of causes and the chain of deeds of the boy <s>Kusīda</s>, displayed a smile. It is a natural law that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, display a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue forth from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that

children.text: adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti, tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: go downward proceed to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — and in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed, and thereby the specific torments of those beings are alleviated. This thought arises in them: 'Have we departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' For the purpose of generating faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth a magical creation. Having seen the magical creation, they think thus: 'We have indeed not departed from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is an unprecedented being, by whose power our specific torments have been alleviated.' Having set their minds with faith upon the magical creation, and having exhausted the karma that was to be experienced in hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those [rays] that go upward proceed to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' — and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: 'Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant [shakes off] a reed hut.' // AVŚ_3.1 //

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_3.2 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live heedfully, having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering.' // AVŚ_3.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra (billion-world) universe, follow the <s>Bhagavān</s> from behind. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to prophesy about past deeds, they vanish behind him. If he wishes to prophesy about the future, they vanish in front of him. If he wishes to prophesy a birth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy an animal birth, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy a birth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy a human birth, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (lesser universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy a divine birth, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of supreme, perfect awakening, they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha ca tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha: <Speyer 21>
children.translated_text: And those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: 'A sheaf [of rays], variegated, adorned with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: has issued forth from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: as if by the sun at its rising.' // AVŚ_3.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he speaks [these] verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: 'Free from [the cycle of] arising, rid of wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme causes [of good] in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile as white as a conch, a lotus-stalk.' // AVŚ_3.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: 'Having yourself understood [this matter] at this very time by your heroic wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, <s>Jinendra</s> (Lord of Victors), for the listeners who are longing [to know] —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_3.5 ||
children.translated_text: O Bull among Sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen.' // AVŚ_3.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_3.6 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Not without reason do the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> (Fully Awakened), the Lords, steady as the ocean and the king of mountains, display a smile; those masses of people desire to hear about that for whose sake the Steadfast Ones display their smile.' // AVŚ_3.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena kusīdena dārakeṇa mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda kuśido dārako 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrya atibalavīryaparākramo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how this boy <s>Kusīda</s> has made such an offering to me?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, this boy <s>Kusīda</s>, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, having accumulated the awakening that is accomplished over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), and having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) imbued with great compassion, shall become a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Atibalavīryaparākrama</s> (Of Exceedingly Powerful Heroic Effort), endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special mindful establishments, and great compassion. This is [the fruit of] his <s>Dharma</s>-offering — namely, his act of faith in my presence.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

children.text: AVŚ_4 sārthavāhaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_4: The Caravan Leader (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta's</s> Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: śrāvastyām anyatamo mahāsārthavāho mahāsamudrād bhagnayānapātra āgataḥ | sa dvir api trir api svadevatāyācanaṃ kṛtvā mahāsamudram avatīrṇo bhagnayānapātra evāgataḥ | tato 'sya mahān kheda utpannaḥ | sa imāṃ cintām āpede: ko me upāyaḥ svādyena dhanārjanaṃ kuryām iti | tasyaitad abhavat: ayaṃ buddho bhagavān sarvadevaprativiśiṣṭataraḥ ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahādharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ, yanv aham idānīm asya nāmnā punar api mahāsamudram avatareyam* | siddhayānapātras tv āgaccheyaṃ ced upārdhena dhanenāsya pūjāṃ kuryām iti ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a certain great caravan-leader had returned from the great ocean with his ship wrecked. Having twice and thrice prayed to his own deity, he descended into the great ocean [again] but returned with his ship wrecked each time. Then great dejection arose in him. He pondered: 'What means do I have to earn wealth properly?' This thought came to him: 'This <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, is superior to all gods, devoted to the welfare of himself and others, compassionate, a great lover of <s>Dharma</s>, fond of his creatures. Let me now descend into the great ocean once more in his name. If I return with a successful voyage, I shall worship him with half my wealth.'

children.text: sa evaṃ kṛtavyavasāyaḥ punar api mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | buddhānubhāvena ca ratnadvīpaṃ saṃprāpya mahāratnasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā kuśalasvastinā svagṛham anuprāptaḥ | sa mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya bhāṇḍaṃ pratyavekṣitum ārabdhaḥ | tasya nānāvicitrāṇi ratnāni dṛṣṭvā mahāṃllābha utpannaḥ | cintayati ca: mayā īdṛśānāṃ ratnānāṃ śramaṇasya gautamasya upārdhaṃ dātavyaṃ bhaviṣyati | yanv aham etāni svasyāḥ patnyā āyaḥ | tena kārṣāpaṇadvayena vikrīya bhagavato gandhaṃ dadyām iti | sa kārṣāpaṇadvayenāgaruṃ krītvā jetavanaṃ gataḥ | tato 'patrapamāṇarūpo dvārakoṣṭhake sthitvāgaruṃ dhūpitavān* ||
children.translated_text: Having thus made his resolution, he descended once more into the great ocean. By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, he reached the Jewel Island and, having gathered a great collection of gems, returned safely to his own home. Having rested from the fatigue of the journey, he began to inspect his merchandise. Seeing the various and splendid jewels, great profit arose. He thought: 'I will have to give half of such jewels to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. Let me [instead] give these to my own wife as her income. With two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> I shall buy [incense] and give the <s>Bhagavān</s> perfume.' Having bought <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) incense for two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>, he went to <s>Jetavana</s>. Then, feeling ashamed, he stood in the gate-chamber and burned the <s>aguru</s> incense.

children.text: atha bahagavāṃs tad rūpam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskṛtavān yena sa dhūpa upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya sarvāṃ ca śrāvastīṃ sphuritvā mahadabhrakūṭavad avasthitaḥ | tasya tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahān prasāda utpannaḥ | sa svacittaṃ paribhāṣitavān: naitan mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ ratnair nābhyarcayeyam iti || atha tena sārthavāhena bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho 'ntarniveśane bhaktenopanimantritaḥ | tataḥ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya mahāratnair avakīrṇaḥ | tatas tāni ratnāni upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya mūrdhni bhagavato ratnakūṭāgāro ratnacchatraṃ ratnamaṇḍapaś cāvasthitaḥ, yan na śakyaṃ suśikṣitena karmakāreṇa karmāntevāsinā vā kartum*, yathāpi tad buddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> performed a feat of supernatural power such that the incense-smoke rose upward into the sky, pervaded all of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and remained like a great mass of clouds. Having seen that utterly wondrous miracle, which captivated gods and humans, great faith arose in him. He reproached himself: 'It would not be fitting for me if I did not worship the <s>Bhagavān</s> with jewels.' Then that caravan-leader invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of disciples for a meal in his inner mansion. After satisfying them with choice food, he showered them with great jewels. Then those jewels rose up into the sky, and above the <s>Bhagavān's</s> head stood a jewel pavilion, a jewel parasol, and a jewel pavilion-hall — such as could not be fashioned by even the most skilled artisan or craftsman's apprentice — for such is the power of the <s>Buddha</s> by the <s>Buddha's</s> influence and of the deities by the deities' influence.

children.text: atha sārthavāho dviguṇajātaprasādas tatpratihāryadarśanān mūlanikṛtta iva drumo bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then the caravan-leader, his faith doubled by the sight of that miracle, falling at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> like a tree cut at the root, began to make his aspiration: 'By this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, may I, in a blind world, without a guide, without a leader, become a <s>Buddha</s> — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates those who are not liberated, who gives comfort to those who are not comforted, who brings to complete <s>nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained complete <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya sārthavāhasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāviṣkārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>), knowing the chain of causes and the chain of actions of that caravan-leader, manifested a smile. It is indeed the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, manifest a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward and some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed.
