Thereby the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. It occurs to them: 'Have we perhaps departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation. Seeing the emanation, they think: 'Indeed, we have neither departed from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having gained faith in the emanation and having exhausted the karma to be experienced in that hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels of the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 13]

children.text: parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Non-self!' and recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_4.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!" // <s>AVŚ</s> 4.1 //

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_4.2 || iti
children.translated_text:
"He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,
having abandoned the cycle of births, shall make an end of suffering." // <s>AVŚ</s> 4.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire three-thousand-fold great-thousand world-system, follow behind the Blessed One. If the Blessed One wishes to prophesy past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind the Blessed One. If he wishes to prophesy future events, they disappear in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in a hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they disappear at the heel. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a hungry ghost (<s>preta</s>), they disappear at the big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they disappear at the knees. If he wishes to prophesy the sovereignty of a powerful universal monarch, they disappear in the left palm. If he wishes to prophesy universal monarchy (<s>cakravartin</s>), they disappear in the right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a god, they disappear at the navel. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappear at the mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared at the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A sheaf of a thousand various, multicolored hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: emitted from within your mouth —

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the quarters in all directions were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_4.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the sun at its rising — // <s>AVŚ</s> 4.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recited verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, who are beyond birth, free from despondency and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme causes in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: they do not without reason display

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: a smile white as a conch-shell or lotus-stalk, those Victors who have conquered their foes." // <s>AVŚ</s> 4.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself comprehended this moment with the understanding of a hero, O <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager, O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, Lord of Victors —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with firm, supreme, auspicious words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_4.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen." // <s>AVŚ</s> 4.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
children.translated_text:
"The Fully Awakened Ones, the Lords, possessing the steadfastness of the mountain-king of the salt sea,
do not display a smile without cause.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 14]

children.text:
yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_4.6 || iti
children.translated_text:
For whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile —
those multitudes of people desire to hear that." // <s>AVŚ</s> 4.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena sārthavāhena mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda sārthavāho 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya ratnottamo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittasyābhiprasādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this caravan-leader has performed such worship toward me?" "Indeed, Venerable Sir." "This caravan-leader, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, having accumulated the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) accumulated over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) pervaded by great compassion, shall become a Fully Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Ratnottama</s> (Supreme Jewel), endowed with the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the three unique bases of mindfulness, and great compassion. This is his gift of <s>dharma</s>: the serene faith of his mind directed toward me."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The monks, delighted in spirit, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_5 somaḥ | [L o s t] (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 5 — <s>Soma</s>. [Lost] (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: AVŚ_6 vaḍikaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 6 — <s>Vaḍika</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, merchants, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: śrāvastyām anyatamo gṛhapatiḥ śreṣṭhī prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ gṛhapateḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā navānāṃ māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ || tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā vaḍika iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtavān pitā | vaḍiko dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattaḥ aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍena anyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ pañcavarṣo ṣaḍvarṣo vā, tadā gurau bhaktiṃ kṛtvā sarvaśāstrāṇi adhītāni | tīkṣṇabuddhitayā śīghraṃ sarvaśāstrasya pāraṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there dwelt a certain householder, a guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He had taken a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As the householder was sporting, delighting, and enjoying himself, his wife became pregnant. At the end of nine months she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing. At his birth, the father held a birth-festival and gave him the name <s>Vaḍika</s>. The boy <s>Vaḍika</s> was entrusted to eight nurses: two carrying-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, ghee-cream, and other choice, well-prepared provisions. He grew up quickly, like a lotus in a lake. When he had grown up, being five or six years old, having shown devotion to his teacher, he studied all the sciences. By the sharpness of his intellect, he quickly reached the far shore of all knowledge.

children.text: tad anantaraṃ tasya vaḍikasya kiṃcit pūrvajanmakṛtakarmavipākena śarīre kāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ patitam iti duḥkhī bhūtaś cintāparaḥ sthitaḥ: kiṃ pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā, yad idaṃ kāyikaṃ duḥkhaṃ mama śarīre jātam* | tasya pitāpi putrasyedaṃ kāyikaṃ duḥkhabhāvaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahadudvignaḥ putrātyayaśaṅkhayā dīnamānasaḥ śokāśruvyāptavadanas tvaritaṃ vaidyam āhūya tasya putrasya rogaṃ darśayati: ko rogaḥ,
children.translated_text: After that, through the ripening of karma performed in a previous life, bodily suffering fell upon the body of <s>Vaḍika</s>, and he stood afflicted, absorbed in anxiety: 'What sin did I commit, that this bodily suffering has arisen in my body?' His father too, seeing this condition of bodily suffering in his son, became greatly distressed, his mind despondent with the fear of losing his son, his face covered with tears of grief; he quickly summoned a physician and showed him his son's disease: 'What is this illness,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 15]

children.text:
kena hetunā mama putrasya dehe jāta iti | tataḥ sa vaidyas tasya rogacihnaṃ dṛṣṭvā cikitsāṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ | tathāpi tasya rogaśāntir na bhavati, punar vṛddhir bhavati | pitā putrasya rogaṃ vṛddhaṃ jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā avaśyaṃ putro mariṣyati, yad vaidyenāpi cāsya rogasya cikitsituṃ na śakyate, iti mūrcchayā bhūmau patitaḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyo 'pi putrasya cintā jātā | bhūyo 'pi cintayā mānasī vyathā jātā | sa dārako rogī bhūto 'śakyo 'pi vadituṃ kathaṃcit pitaraṃ babhāṣe: mā tāta sāhasam* | dhairyam avalambyottiṣṭha | mamātyayāśaṅkayā mā bhūs tvam api mādṛśaḥ | mama nāmnā devānāṃ pūjāṃ kuru, dānaṃ dehi | tato mama svasthā *{svāsthaṃ}* bhaviṣyati | sa gṛhapatir iti putrasya vaca ākarṇya sarvadevebhyaḥ pūjāṃ kṛtavān* | sarvabrāhmaṇatīrthikaparivrājakebhyo dānaṃ dattavān* | tathāpi tasya rogaśāntir na bhavati | tadā tasya mahān mānaso duḥkho 'bhūt* | sarvadeveṣu pūjā kṛtā, dāno 'pi dattaḥ pitrā mama, tathāpi svasthā na bhavati | tatas tathāgataguṇān anusmṛtya buddhaṃ namaskāraṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ |
  atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam* | kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām* | kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam* <| kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam* | kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam* | kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: 'What is the cause that [this disease] has arisen on my son's body?' Then that physician, having observed the symptoms of his disease, began treatment. Even so, his disease found no abatement, but rather increased. The father, seeing his son's disease had grown worse, [thought]: 'My son will surely die, since even the physician is unable to treat his disease' — and fell to the ground in a faint. Seeing that, the son's worry grew further. From that worry, a mental anguish arose. That sick boy, though barely able to speak, somehow addressed his father: 'Do not be rash, father! Take hold of your courage and rise! Out of fear for my death, do not become like me! Perform worship of the gods in my name; give charity. Then I shall recover.' That householder, hearing his son's words, performed worship to all the gods and gave charity to all Brahmins, heretical teachers, and wandering ascetics. Even so, his disease found no abatement. Then great mental suffering arose in him: 'Worship has been performed to all the gods, and charity has been given by my father, yet I do not recover.' Then, recalling the virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he began to pay homage to the <s>Buddha</s>. Meanwhile — there is nothing unknown, unseen, unlearned, or unrealized by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. For it is the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones — who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, possessed of singular protection, abiding in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three matters of taming, who have crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, who have long practiced the four means of winning over [beings], who have abandoned the five limbs [of desire], who have transcended the five destinies, who are endowed with the six limbs [of enlightenment], who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), who are adorned with the blossoms of the seven factors of awakening, who are guides on the eightfold path, who are skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, who are strong with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who are distinguished beyond a thousand rulers of the ten [directions] — three times at night and three times during the day to survey the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, and knowledge-and-vision arises: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has come to difficulty? Who has come to a strait? Who has come to distress? Who has come to difficulty, strait, and distress? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who gravitates toward the lower realms? Whom shall I, having lifted from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, shall I extend a hand to pull them out? Whom, deprived of the noble wealth, shall I establish in the sovereignty of the noble riches? Whose eyes, covered by the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? For whom shall I plant unplanted roots of merit? For whom shall I ripen those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already ripened?' And [the scripture] says:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_6.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the [appropriate] time for those who are to be trained, like [a cow never abandons] her calves.' // AVŚ_6.1 //

children.text: tato bhagavatā vaḍikasya gṛhapateḥ putrasya tām avasthāṃ dṛṣṭvā sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāḥ kanakavarṇā marīcayaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ, yais tad gṛhaṃ samantād avabhāsitam* | kalpasahasraparibhāvitāś ca maitryaṃśava utsṛṣṭāḥ, yair asya spṛṣṭamātraṃ śarīraṃ prahlāditam* | tato bhagavāṃs tasya dvārakoṣṭhakam anuprāptaḥ | dauvārikapuruṣeṇāsya niveditaṃ bhagavān dvāre tiṣṭhatīti | atha vaḍikaḥ śreṣṭhiputro labdhaprasādo 'dhigatasamāśvāsa āha: praviśatu bhagavān, svāgataṃ bhagavate, ākāṅkṣāmi bhagavato darśanam iti | atha bhagavān praviśya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | niṣadya bhagavān vaḍikam uvāca: kiṃ te vaḍika bādhata iti | vaḍika uvāca: kāyikaṃ ca me duḥkhaṃ cetasikaṃ
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having seen the condition of <s>Vaḍika</s>, the householder's son, emitted rays of golden color surpassing the radiance of a thousand suns, by which that entire house was illuminated. And he emitted rays of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) cultivated for a thousand <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages), by which the boy's body was instantly refreshed and gladdened. Then the Blessed One reached the entrance of his house. The doorkeeper informed him: 'The Blessed One stands at the door.' Then <s>Vaḍika</s>, the guild-master's son, having gained faith and obtained comfort, said: 'Let the Blessed One enter! Welcome to the Blessed One! I long for the sight of the Blessed One.' Then the Blessed One entered and sat upon the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said to <s>Vaḍika</s>: 'What ails you, <s>Vaḍika</s>?' <s>Vaḍika</s> said: 'Both physical suffering and mental

children.text: ceti | tato 'sya bhagavatā sarvasatveṣu maitryupadiṣṭā: ayaṃ te cetasikasya pratipakṣa iti | laukikaṃ ca cittam utpādayāmāsa: aho bata śakro devendro gandhamādanāt parvatāt kṣīrikām oṣadhīm ānayed iti | sahacittotpādād bhagavataḥ śakro devendro gandhamādanāt parvatāt kṣīrikām oṣadhīm ānīya bhagavate dattavān* | bhagavatā ca svapāṇinā gṛhītvā vaḍikāya dattā: iyaṃ te kāyikasya duḥkhasya paridāhaśamanīti ||
children.translated_text: [suffering].' Then the Blessed One taught him loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward all beings: 'This is the antidote for your mental [suffering].' And he generated a worldly thought: 'If only <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, would bring a milk-producing medicinal herb from <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain!' The moment the Blessed One generated that thought, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, brought the milk-producing medicinal herb from <s>Gandhamādana</s> mountain and gave it to the Blessed One. The Blessed One, taking it with his own hand, gave it to <s>Vaḍika</s>: 'This is the remedy for the burning of your physical suffering.'

children.text: sa kāyikaṃ prasrabdhisukhaṃ labdhvā bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādayāmāsa | prasannacittaś ca rājñaḥ prasenajito nivedya bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojayitvā śatasahasreṇa vastreṇācchadya sarvapuṣpamālyair abhyarcitavān* | tataś cetanāṃ puṣṇāti sma, praṇidhiṃ ca cakāra: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena yathaivāhaṃ bhagavatā anuttareṇa vaidyarājena cikitsitaḥ, evam aham apy anāgate 'dhvani andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained the bliss of physical tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>), he generated faith in the Blessed One. With a mind full of faith, he informed King <s>Prasenajit</s>, fed the Blessed One together with the community of disciples, covered [them] with a hundred thousand garments, and worshipped [them] with all kinds of flowers and garlands. Then he cultivated an intention and made a resolve: 'By this root of merit, by this generation of the thought [of awakening], and by this gift of <s>dharma</s> — just as I have been healed by the Blessed One, the supreme king of physicians, so may I too, in a future time, in a blind world without a guide or leader, become a <s>Buddha</s> — a deliverer of beings who have not crossed over, a liberator of those who are not liberated, a comforter of those who are not comforted, a bringer to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> of those who have not attained <s>Nirvāṇa</s>!'

children.text: atha bhagavān vaḍikasya dhātuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣu uṣṇībhūtā nipatanti, tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavantaḥ itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having known the successive dispositions (<s>dhātuparaṃparā</s>) and the successive <s>karmas</s> of <s>Vaḍika</s>, displayed a smile. For it is the nature that whenever the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some going downward, some going upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down having become cool, and in the cold hells they fall down having become warm, so that the various torments of those beings are alleviated. They think: 'Have we, friends, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' To generate faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a magical creation. Seeing the creation, they think: 'We have neither passed away from here nor been reborn elsewhere; rather, this is a being of unprecedented appearance, by whose power our torments have been alleviated.' Having generated faith in the creation, having exhausted their hell-bound <s>karma</s>, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those [rays] that go upward, having gone to the gods — of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — they proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' And they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: 'Strive! Go forth! Yoke yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_6.2 ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of Death, as an elephant [shakes off] a reed-hut!' // AVŚ_6.2 //

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_6.3 || iti
children.translated_text: 'He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering.' // AVŚ_6.3 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante |
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm (the billion-fold world-system), follow behind the Blessed One. If the Blessed One wishes to declare past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the Blessed One;

children.text: anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: if he wishes to declare the future, they vanish in front of him. If he wishes to declare rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to declare rebirth among animals, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to declare rebirth among hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to declare rebirth among humans, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to declare the sovereignty of a subordinate wheel-turning king, they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to declare the sovereignty of a wheel-turning king, they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to declare rebirth among gods, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to declare the awakening of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to declare the awakening of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair between the eyebrows). If he wishes to declare supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha ca tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, vanished at the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: 'A cluster of variegated [rays], painted with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: has issued from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions on all sides have been illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_6.4 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun.' // AVŚ_6.4 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he spoke [these] verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: 'Free from [worldly] existence, having abandoned wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme causes in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the victorious <s>Jinas</s>, who have conquered their enemies,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_6.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile white as a conch-shell or lotus-fiber.' // AVŚ_6.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya dhīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: 'Having yourself understood the [appropriate] time, O resolute one, with your wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are filled with curiosity, O lord of the victorious ones —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with resolute and supreme words, O bull among sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_6.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen, with your auspicious [speech]!' // AVŚ_6.5 //

children.text: NOTE on 6.5a: S usually vīrya, but here dhīra.
children.translated_text: NOTE on 6.5a: S usually vīrya, but here dhīra.

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_6.6 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Not without cause do the fully awakened ones, the protectors, steadfast as the lord of salty-watered mountains (the ocean), display a smile; for what purpose the resolute ones display a smile — that the crowds of people long to hear.' // AVŚ_6.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy anena vaḍikena gṛhapatiputreṇa mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda vaḍiko gṛhapatiputro 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya śākyamunir nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how this boy <s>Vaḍika</s>, the householder's son, has made such an offering to me?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, this boy <s>Vaḍika</s>, the householder's son, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, having accumulated the awakening that is accomplished over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), and having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) imbued with great compassion, shall become a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special mindful establishments, and great compassion. This is [the fruit of] his <s>Dharma</s>-offering — namely, his act of faith in my presence.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

children.text: AVŚ_7 padmaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_7: <s>Padma</s> (The Lotus). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme || yadā bhagavāṃl loke notpanna āsīt, tadā rājā prasenajit tīrthikadevatārcanaṃ kṛtavān puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanaiḥ | yadā tu bhagavāṃl loke utpannaḥ, rājā ca prasenajid daharasūtrodāharaṇena vinīto bhagavacchāsane śraddhāṃ pratilabdhavān, tadā prītisaumanasyajātas trir bhagavantam upasaṃkramya dīpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanair abhyarcayati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta's</s> Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had not yet arisen in the world, King <s>Prasenajit</s> used to worship the deities of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretical teachers) with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, and unguents. But when the <s>Bhagavān</s> had arisen in the world and King <s>Prasenajit</s>, guided by a young boy's exposition, had gained faith in the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching, then, filled with joy and gladness, he would approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and worship him with lamps, incense, fragrances, garlands, and unguents.

children.text: athānyatama ārāmiko navaṃ padmam ādāya rājñaḥ prasenajito 'rthaṃ śrāvastīṃ praviśati | tīrthikopāsakena ca dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭhaś ca: kim idaṃ padmaṃ vikrīṇiṣye? sa kathayati: āmeti | sa kretukāmo yāvad anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatis taṃ pradeśam anuprataḥ || tena tasmād dviguṇena mūlyena vardhitam* | tataḥ parasparaṃ vardhamānau yāvac chatasahasraṃ vardhitavantau | athārāmikasyaitad abhavat*: ayam anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir acañcalaḥ sthirasatvaḥ | nūnam atra kāraṇena bhavitavyam iti | tena saṃśayajātena sa tīrthikābhiprasannaḥ puruṣaḥ pṛsṭaḥ: kasyārthe bhavān evaṃ vardhata iti | sa āha: ahaṃ bhagavato nārāyaṇasyārthe iti || anāthapiṇḍada āha: ahaṃ bhagavato buddhasyārthe iti | ārāmika āha: ka eṣa buddho nāmeti? tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena vistareṇāsya buddhaguṇā ākhyātāḥ | tata ārāmiko 'nāthapiṇḍadam āha: gṛhapate ahaṃ svayam eva taṃ bhagavantam abhyarcayiṣya iti ||
children.translated_text: Now a certain gardener, carrying a fresh lotus, was entering <s>Śrāvastī</s> for the sake of King <s>Prasenajit</s>. He was seen by a lay-follower of the <s>tīrthikas</s>, who asked: 'Will you sell this lotus?' He replied: 'Yes.' That man wished to buy it, when <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, the householder, happened to arrive at that spot. He raised the price to double. Then, competing with each other, they raised [the price] until it reached a hundred thousand. Then this thought occurred to the gardener: 'This householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> is unwavering, of firm resolve. There must be a reason for this.' Filled with doubt, he asked the man devoted to the <s>tīrthikas</s>: 'For whose sake do you bid so high?' He replied: 'I [bid] for the sake of the <s>Bhagavān Nārāyaṇa</s>.' <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said: 'I [bid] for the sake of the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.' The gardener asked: 'Who is this one called <s>Buddha</s>?' Then <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> described to him at length the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. The gardener then said to <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'Householder, I myself shall worship that <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

children.text: tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir ārāmikam ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | dadarśārāmiko buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyaṃjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc ca ārāmikeṇa tat padmaṃ bhagavati kṣiptam* | tataḥ kṣiptamātraṃ śakaṭacakramāṇaṃ bhūtvā upari bhagavataḥ sthitam* ||
children.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, taking the gardener, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The gardener beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with the eighty minor characteristics, embellished with a fathom-wide halo, of surpassing brilliance exceeding a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides. At the very moment of seeing him, the gardener cast that lotus toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And the moment it was cast, it became the size of a cart-wheel and remained suspended above the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: atha sa ārāmikas tat pratihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūlanikṛtta iva drumo bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya kṛtakarapuṭaś cetanāṃ puṣṇāti, praṇidhiṃ ca kartum ārabdhaḥ: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: Then that gardener, seeing that miracle, falling at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> like a tree cut at the root, with palms joined, nourished his aspiration and began to make his vow: 'By this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, may I, in a blind world, without a guide, without a leader, become a <s>Buddha</s> — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates those who are not liberated, who gives comfort to those who are not comforted, who brings to complete <s>nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained complete <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyārāmikasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the chain of causes and the chain of deeds of that gardener, displayed a smile. It is a natural law that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, display a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue forth from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward

children.text: gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: proceed to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — and in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the specific torments of those beings are alleviated. This thought arises in them: 'Have we departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' For the purpose of generating faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth a magical creation. Having seen the magical creation, they think thus: 'We have indeed not departed from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is an unprecedented being, by whose power our specific torments have been alleviated.' Having set their minds with faith upon the magical creation, and having exhausted the karma that was to be experienced in hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those [rays] that go upward proceed to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' — and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: 'Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_7.1 ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant [shakes off] a reed hut.' // AVŚ_7.1 //

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_7.2 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live heedfully, having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering.' // AVŚ_7.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra (billion-world) universe, follow the <s>Bhagavān</s> from behind. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to prophesy about past deeds, they vanish behind him. If he wishes to prophesy about the future, they vanish in front of him. If he wishes to prophesy a birth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy an animal birth, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy a birth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy a human birth, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (lesser universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy a divine birth, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of supreme, perfect awakening, they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: And those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: 'A sheaf [of rays], variegated, adorned with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: has issued forth from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_7.3 ||
children.translated_text: as if by the sun at its rising.' // AVŚ_7.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he speaks [these] verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: 'Free from [the cycle of] arising, rid of wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme causes [of good] in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_7.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile as white as a conch, a lotus-stalk.' // AVŚ_7.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: 'Having yourself understood [this matter] at this very time by your heroic wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, <s>Jinendra</s> (Lord of Victors), for the listeners who are longing [to know] —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_7.5 ||
children.translated_text: O Bull among Sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen.' // AVŚ_7.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_7.6 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Not without reason do the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> (Fully Awakened), the Lords, steady as the ocean and the king of mountains, display a smile; those masses of people desire to hear about that for whose sake the Steadfast Ones display their smile.' // AVŚ_7.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anenārāmikeṇa prasādajātena mamaivaṃvidhāṃ pūjām kṛtām* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ārāmiko 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya padmottamo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how this gardener, filled with faith, has made such an offering to me?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'This gardener, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, having accumulated the awakening that is accomplished over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), and having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) imbued with great compassion, shall become a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Padmottama</s> (Supreme Lotus), endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special mindful establishments, and great compassion. This is [the fruit of] his <s>Dharma</s>-offering — namely, his act of faith in my presence.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

children.text: AVŚ_8 pañcālaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_8: <s>Pañcāla</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text:
buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme || tena khalu samayenottarapañcālarājo dakṣiṇapañcālarājena saha prativiruddho babhuva | # # # [gap in all MSS]
  atha rājā prasenajit kauśalyo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekānte niṣaṇṇo rājā prasenajit kauśalyo bhagavantam idam avocat* : bhagavān nāma bhadanta anuttaro dharmarājo vyasanagatānāṃ satvānāṃ paritrātā, anyonyavairiṇāṃ vairapraśamayitā | ayaṃ cottarapañcālo rājā dakṣiṇapañcālarājena saha prativiruddhaḥ | tau parasparam eva mahājanavipraghātaṃ kurutaḥ | tayor bhagavān dīrgharātrānugatasya vairasyopaśamaṃ
children.translated_text:
The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, the king of Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> had come into conflict with the king of Southern <s>Pañcāla</s>. [gap in all MSS]
Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> approached the Blessed One. Having approached and worshiped the Blessed One's feet with his head, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'The Blessed One, Venerable Sir, is indeed the supreme King of <s>Dharma</s>, the protector of beings who have fallen into misfortune, the pacifier of enmity between those who bear mutual hostility. Now, this king of Northern <s>Pañcāla</s> is in conflict with the king of Southern <s>Pañcāla</s>. The two are causing great slaughter of people against each other. May the Blessed One, out of compassion, bring about the pacification of their long-standing enmity
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 21]

children.text: kuryād anukampām upādāyeti | adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalyasya tūṣṇībhāvena | atha rājā prasenajit kauśalyo bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: .' The Blessed One consented to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>'s request by his silence. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, knowing the Blessed One's consent by his silence, rose from his seat, worshiped the Blessed One's feet with his head, and departed.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyā eva rātrer atyayāt pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya yena vārāṇasī kāśīnāṃ nagaraṃ tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ | anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīm anuprāpto vārāṇasyāṃ viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvat tayor viditaṃ bhagavān asmadvijitam anuprāpta iti | yāvad bhagavatā ṛddhibalena caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ nirmāyottarapañcālarājas trāsitaḥ | sa bhīta ekaratham abhiruhya bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | tasya bhagavatā vairapraśamāya dharmo deśitaḥ | sa taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā bhagavatsakāśe pravrajite | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, when that night had passed, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken up his robe and bowl, set out on a journey toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the city of the <s>Kāśis</s>. Journeying by stages, he arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and dwelt at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in the Deer Park at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (<s>Sārnāth</s>). When the two kings learned that the Blessed One had arrived in their territory — then the Blessed One, through his supernatural power, created a four-division army and terrified the king of Northern <s>Pañcāla</s>. Frightened, he mounted a single chariot and approached the Blessed One's presence. The Blessed One taught him the <s>Dharma</s> for the pacification of his enmity. Having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, he went forth into the homeless life in the Blessed One's presence. Striving, exerting himself, and applying himself diligently, through the abandonment of all defilements (<s>kleśas</s>), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇapañcālarājenāpi bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghas traimāsyaṃ śatarasenāhāreṇopanimantritaḥ, śatasahasreṇa ca vastreṇācchāditaḥ | praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: The king of Southern <s>Pañcāla</s> also invited the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples for a three-month meal at a cost of a hundred <s>rasas</s> (lavish food), and covered them with a hundred thousand garments. He made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, may I, in a blind world without a guide, without a leader, become a <s>Buddha</s> — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates those who are not liberated, who gives comfort to those who are not comforted, who brings to complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs dakṣiṇapañcālarājasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca evaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the chain of causes and the chain of actions of the king of Southern <s>Pañcāla</s>, manifested a smile. It is indeed the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, manifest a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward and some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. It occurs to them: 'Have we perhaps departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation. Seeing the emanation, they think: 'Indeed, we have neither departed from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having gained faith in the emanation and having exhausted the karma to be experienced in that hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels of the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Non-self!' and recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_8.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!" // <s>AVŚ</s> 8.1 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 22]

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_8.2 || iti
children.translated_text:
"He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,
having abandoned the cycle of births, shall make an end of suffering." // <s>AVŚ</s> 8.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe kara{tale} 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire three-thousand-fold great-thousand world-system, follow behind the Blessed One. If the Blessed One wishes to prophesy past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind the Blessed One. If he wishes to prophesy future events, they disappear in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in a hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they disappear at the heel. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a hungry ghost (<s>preta</s>), they disappear at the big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they disappear at the knees. If he wishes to prophesy the sovereignty of a powerful universal monarch, they disappear in the left palm. If he wishes to prophesy universal monarchy (<s>cakravartin</s>), they disappear in the right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a god, they disappear at the navel. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappear at the mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared at the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A sheaf of a thousand various, multicolored hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: emitted from within your mouth —

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the quarters in all directions were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_8.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the sun at its rising — // <s>AVŚ</s> 8.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recited verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, who are beyond birth, free from despondency and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme causes in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: they do not without reason display

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_8.4 ||
children.translated_text: a smile white as a conch-shell or lotus-stalk, those Victors who have conquered their foes." // <s>AVŚ</s> 8.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself comprehended this moment with the understanding of a hero, O <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager, O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, Lord of Victors —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with firm, supreme, auspicious words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_8.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen." // <s>AVŚ</s> 8.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_8.6 || iti
children.translated_text:
"The Fully Awakened Ones, the Lords, possessing the steadfastness of the mountain-king of the salt sea,
do not display a smile without cause.
For whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile —
those multitudes of people desire to hear that." // <s>AVŚ</s> 8.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda dakṣiṇapañcālarājena mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda pañcālarājo 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this king of Southern <s>Pañcāla</s> has performed such worship toward me?' 'Indeed, Venerable Sir.' 'This king of <s>Pañcāla</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, having accumulated the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) accumulated over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) pervaded by great compassion,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 23]

children.text: ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya vijayo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: shall become a Fully Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vijaya</s> (Victorious), endowed with the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the three unique bases of mindfulness, and great compassion. This is his gift of <s>Dharma</s>: the serene faith of his mind directed toward me.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The monks, delighted in spirit, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_9 dhūpaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 9 — <s>Dhūpa</s> (Incense). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme || tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ dvau śreṣṭhinau | tāv anyonyaṃ prativiruddhau babhūvatuḥ | tābhyām ekaḥ pūraṇo 'bhiprasannaḥ, dvitīyo buddhe bhagavati | tatas tayoḥ parasparaṃ kathāsāṃkathyaviniścaye vartamāne pūraṇopāsaka āha: buddhāt pūraṇo viśiṣṭatara iti | buddhopāsaka āha: bhagavān samyaksaṃbuddho viśiṣṭatara iti | tatas tābhyāṃ sarvasvāpaharaṇe bandhanikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, in <s>Śrāvastī</s> there were two guild-masters. The two had come into conflict with each other. One of them was devoted to <s>Pūraṇa</s> (Kāśyapa), the other to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. Then, as the two were engaged in disputation and counter-disputation, the devotee of <s>Pūraṇa</s> said: '<s>Pūraṇa</s> is more eminent than the <s>Buddha</s>.' The devotee of the <s>Buddha</s> said: 'The Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened One, is more eminent.' Then the two made a wager, staking their entire property.

children.text: yāvad rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ śrutam* | tenāmātyānām ājñā dattā: tayor mīmāṃsā kartavyeti | tatas tair amātyaiḥ sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam*: saptame divase buddhatīrthikopāsakayor mīmāṃsā bhaviṣyati, ye cādbhutāni draṣṭukāmās te āgacchantv iti | tataḥ saptame divase vistīrṇāvakāśe pṛthivīpradeśe 'nekeṣu prāṇiśatasahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu gaganatale cānekeṣu devatāsahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu gomayamaṇḍalake kḷpte sarvagandhamālyeṣūpahṛteṣu pūrvataraṃ tīrthikopāsakena satyopayācanaṃ kṛtam*: yena satyena pūraṇaprabhṛtayaḥ ṣaṭ śāstāro loke śreṣṭhāḥ, anena satyenemāni puṣpāṇi ayaṃ ca dhūpaḥ idaṃ ca pānīyaṃ tān upagacchantv iti || evaṃ pravyāhatamātre (Speyer: pravyāhṛtamātre) tāni puṣpāṇi bhūmau patitāni, agnir nirvṛtaḥ, pānīyaṃ pṛthivyām astaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gatam* | tato mahājanakāyena kilakilāprakṣveḍoccair nādo muktaḥ, yam abhivīkṣya tīrthyopāsakas tūṣṇībhūto maṅkubhūtaḥ (Speyer: madgubhūtaḥ), srastaskandho 'dhomukho niṣpratibhānaḥ, pradhyānaparamaḥ kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> heard of this. He gave an order to his ministers: "A trial between those two must be conducted." Then those ministers had a bell proclamation made throughout the entire realm: "On the seventh day there will be a trial between the Buddhist and the heretic lay followers; let those who wish to see marvels come!" Then on the seventh day, in a broad open area of ground, when many hundreds of thousands of living beings had assembled, and in the sky many thousands of <s>devatās</s> (deities) had assembled, when a circle of cow-dung had been prepared and all manner of garlands and incense had been brought, the heretic's lay follower first made a truth-invocation: "By the truth that <s>Pūraṇa</s> and the other six teachers are the most excellent in the world, by this truth may these flowers, this incense, and this water go to them!" As soon as he had thus spoken, the flowers fell to the ground, the fire went out, and the water sank into the earth, was exhausted, and disappeared. Then the great crowd let out a loud cry of jeering, and seeing this the heretic's lay follower became silent and dejected, his shoulders drooping, his face downcast, without any reply, absorbed in brooding, resting his cheek on his hand, overcome with anxiety.

children.text: tato bhagavacchrāvakeṇa harṣotkaṇṭhajātena prasādavikasitābhyāṃ nayanābhyām ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya satyopayācanaṃ kṛtam*: yena satyena bhagavān sarvasatvānām agryaḥ, anena satyenemāni puṣpāṇi dhūpa udakaṃ bhagavantam upagacchantv iti | evaṃ pravyāhṛtamātro tāni puṣpāṇi haṃsapaṃktir ivākāśe jetavanābhimukhaṃ saṃprasthitāni, dhupo 'bhrakūṭavat*, udakaṃ vaiḍūryaśalākavat* | atha sa mahājanakāyas tat prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā kilakilāpravekṣveḍoccaiḥśabdhaṃ kurvaṃs teṣāṃ saṃprasthitānāṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s (Blessed One's) disciple, filled with joy and eagerness, with eyes wide open with faith, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and made a truth-invocation: "By the truth that the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) is the foremost of all beings, by this truth may these flowers, the incense, and the water go to the <s>Bhagavat</s>!" As soon as he had thus spoken, the flowers set forth through the sky like a row of geese toward <s>Jetavana</s>, the incense like a mass of clouds, and the water like a shaft of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli). Then that great crowd, having seen this marvel, following behind those things as they traveled forth, making loud cries of joy, accompanied them.
[editorial page reference]

children.text:
tatas tāni puṣpāṇi bhagavata upari sthitāni, dhūpa udakaṃ cāgrataḥ | tataḥ sa mahājanakāyo labdhaprasādo bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśrāvaṇāya | teṣāṃ bhagavān idaṃ sūtraṃ bhāṣate sma:
  tisra imā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo 'graprajñaptayaḥ | katamās tisraḥ? buddhe agraprajñaptiḥ, dharme, saṃghe agraprajñaptiḥ | buddhe agraprajñaptiḥ katamā? ye kecid brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ satvā apadā vā dvipadā vā bahupadā vā, rūpiṇo vā arūpiṇo vā, saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā, naivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñinaḥ, tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ | ye kecid buddhe 'bhiprasannāḥ, agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ | teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām* | iyam ucyate brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo buddhe agraprajñaptiḥ | dharme agraprajñaptiḥ katamā? ye kecid dharmāḥ saṃskṛtā vā asaṃskṛtā vā, virāgo dharmas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ | ye kecid dharme 'bhiprasannā, agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ | teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām* | iyam ucyate brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo dharme agraprajñaptiḥ | saṃgheṣu agraprajñaptiḥ katamā? ye kecit saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā pariṣado vā, tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ | ye kecit saṃghe 'bhiprasannāḥ, agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ | teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām* | iyam ucyate brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo saṃghe agraprajñaptiḥ |
  asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe teṣāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ kaiścid buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu prasādaḥ pratilabdhaḥ, kaiścic charaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni, kaiścit pravrajya idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā, sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikaraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya, sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | tena ca tīrthyopāsakena tathāgatāntike prasādaḥ pratilabdhaḥ | tato mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ {bhagavataḥ} pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text:
Then those flowers stood above the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), and the incense and water before him. Then that great crowd, having gained faith, paid homage at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> and sat down before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching). The <s>Bhagavat</s> spoke to them this <s>sūtra</s> (discourse):
"There are, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, these three supreme designations. Which three? The supreme designation of the <s>Buddha</s>, of the <s>Dharma</s>, and of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. What is the supreme designation of the <s>Buddha</s>? Whatever beings there are, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders — footless, two-footed, or many-footed, with form or formless, with perception or without perception, neither with perception nor without perception — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), the Perfectly Enlightened One is declared the foremost among them. Whoever have faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, they have faith in the foremost. For those who have faith in the foremost, the foremost result is to be expected: among the <s>devas</s> (gods) for those reborn as <s>devas</s>, or among humans for those reborn as humans. This, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, is called the supreme designation of the <s>Buddha</s>. What is the supreme designation of the <s>Dharma</s>? Whatever <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) there are, conditioned or unconditioned, dispassion is declared the foremost among them. Whoever have faith in the <s>Dharma</s>, they have faith in the foremost. For those who have faith in the foremost, the foremost result is to be expected: among the <s>devas</s> for those reborn as <s>devas</s>, or among humans for those reborn as humans. This, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, is called the supreme designation of the <s>Dharma</s>. What is the supreme designation of the <s>Saṃgha</s>? Whatever <s>saṃghas</s> (communities), groups, guilds, or assemblies there are, the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples is declared the foremost among them. Whoever have faith in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, they have faith in the foremost. For those who have faith in the foremost, the foremost result is to be expected: among the <s>devas</s> for those reborn as <s>devas</s>, or among humans for those reborn as humans. This, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, is called the supreme designation of the <s>Saṃgha</s>."
While this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) was being spoken, some of those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders gained faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>; some took the refuges and the training rules; and some, having gone forth and understood this fivefold cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (rebirth) to be unstable, having overcome all conditioned states of existence through their nature of crumbling, falling, disintegrating, and being destroyed, realized <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an Arhat) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). And that heretic's lay follower gained faith in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.
