Then, falling at the feet of the <s>Bhagavat</s> like a tree cut at the root, he began to make a vow: "By this root of merit, this arising of the aspiration for awakening, and this relinquishing of gifts, may I become a <s>Buddha</s> in this blind world without a leader or guide — a deliverer of beings who have not crossed over, a liberator of those not yet freed, a comforter of those not yet comforted, one who brings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) those who have not yet attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>."

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya tīrthikopāsakasya hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati:
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), knowing the succession of causes and the succession of <s>karmas</s> (deeds) of that heretic's lay follower, displayed a smile. For it is the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> hells — in the hot hells they fall down having become cool, and in the cold hells they fall down having become warm. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think: "Have we, sirs, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?" To generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavat</s> sends forth an emanation. Having seen the emanation, they think:
[editorial page reference]

children.text: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: "We have indeed, sirs, neither passed away from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our distinctive sufferings have been alleviated." Having gained faith through the emanation, they exhaust their <s>karma</s> (deeds) that is to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among <s>devas</s> (gods) and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens, proclaim: "All is impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self," and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive! Renounce! Apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_9.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) as an elephant crushes a hut of reeds!

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_9.2 || iti
children.translated_text:
For whoever shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (Discipline),
having abandoned the cycle of birth and <s>saṃsāra</s> (rebirth), shall make an end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm, followed behind the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One). Now, if the <s>Bhagavat</s> wishes to prophesy past <s>karma</s> (deeds), they disappear behind the <s>Bhagavat</s>. If he wishes to prophesy the future, they disappear in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they disappear at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they disappear at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they disappear at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy the sovereignty of a powerful <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch), they disappear in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s>, they disappear in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a <s>deva</s> (god), they disappear at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (the awakening of a disciple), they disappear at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they disappear at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (the tuft of hair between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy supreme perfect awakening, they disappear at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (the crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) three times and disappeared at the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance). Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavat</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A multiform cluster, adorned with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: issued from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_9.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun.

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he spoke these verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, with wretchedness and pride abandoned,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: are the supreme cause of benefit in the world.

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: Not without reason do the victorious <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), who have vanquished their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_9.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile white as a conch shell or lotus fiber.
[editorial page reference]

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: Having yourself realized the truth at that very moment, O Hero, through your <s>buddhi</s> (wisdom),

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are filled with longing, O <s>Śramaṇa</s> (Ascetic), O Lord of <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors),

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with steadfast and supreme words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_9.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen, with auspicious speech!"

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_9.6 || iti
children.translated_text:
"Not without cause do the Fully Awakened Ones, the Protectors, firm as the ocean, salt-water, and king of mountains,
display a smile.
The throngs of people long to hear
about the one for whose sake the Steadfast Ones display a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena tīrthikopāsakena mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda tīrthopāsako 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena {deyadharmaparityāgena} ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya acalo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) said: "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s> (Worthy Ones), Perfectly Enlightened Ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this heretic's lay follower has performed such worship of me?" "Yes, <s>Bhadanta</s> (Venerable Sir)." "This heretic's lay follower, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this arising of the aspiration for awakening, and by this relinquishing of gifts, having accumulated the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) that is gathered over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) suffused with great compassion, shall become a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Acala</s> (Immovable), endowed with the ten powers, the four kinds of <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness), the three special <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), and great compassion. This is his meritorious offering, namely, the arising of faith in my presence."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One). Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavat</s>.

children.text: AVŚ_10 rājā | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>Avadānaśataka</s> 10: The King. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena rājā prasenajit kauśalo rājā ca ajātaśatruḥ ubhāv apy etau parasparaṃ viruddhau babhūvatauḥ | athā rājā ajātaśatruś caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnahya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalam abhiniryāto yuddhāya ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta's</s> Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> and King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> had both become hostile to each other. Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, marshaling his fourfold army — the elephant corps, the cavalry, the chariot corps, and the infantry — marched out against King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> for battle.

children.text: aśrauṣīd rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ: rājā ajātaśatruś caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnahya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ ca abhiniryāto yuddhāyeti | śrutvā ca caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnahya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ rājānam ajātaśatruṃ pratyabhiniryāto yuddhāya | atha rājñā ajātaśatruṇā rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya sarvo hastikāyaḥ paryastaḥ, aśvakāyo rathakāyaḥ pattikāyaḥ paryastaḥ | rājā prasenajit kauśalo jito bhīto bhagnaḥ parājitaḥ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛta ekarathena śrāvastīṃ praviṣṭaḥ | evaṃ yāvat trir api ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> heard: 'King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having marshaled his fourfold army — the elephant corps, the cavalry, the chariot corps, and the infantry — has marched out for battle.' Having heard this, he too marshaled his fourfold army — the elephant corps, the cavalry, the chariot corps, and the infantry — and marched out against King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> for battle. Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> overthrew the entire elephant corps, the cavalry, the chariot corps, and the infantry of King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, defeated, frightened, broken, vanquished, put to flight, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> with a single chariot. This happened as many as three times.

children.text: atha rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ śokāgaraṃ praviśya kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ | tatra ca śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena śrutaṃ yathā rājā prasenajit kauśalo jito bhagnaḥ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛtaḥ, ekaratheneha praviṣṭa iti | śrutvā ca punar yena rājā prasenajit kauśalas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ jayenāyuṣā ca vardhayitvā ca (Speyer: uvāca): kimarthaṃ deva śokaḥ kriyate? ahaṃ devasya tāvat suvarṇam anuprayacchāmi, yena devaḥ punar api yatheṣṭapracāraṇaṃ kariṣyatīti | tena tasya mahān suvarṇarāśiḥ kṛtaḥ, yatropaviṣṭaḥ puruṣa utthitaṃ puruṣaṃ na paśyati, utthito vā upaviṣṭam* ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, entering the chamber of grief, placing his cheek upon his hand, remained absorbed in thought. Now in <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He heard that King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> had been defeated, broken, put to flight, and had entered [the city] with a single chariot. Having heard this, he approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>. Having approached, he congratulated King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> with wishes of victory and long life, and said: 'Why does Your Majesty grieve? I shall provide Your Majesty with enough gold so that Your Majesty may again campaign as he pleases.' He made for him a great heap of gold, so large that a man sitting down could not see a man standing up, nor a standing man one sitting.

children.text: atha rājñā prasenajitkauśalyena svaviṣaye carapuruṣāḥ samantata utsṛṣṭāḥ: śṛṇuta janapravādān iti | yāvaj jetavane dvau mallāv anyonyaṃ saṃjalpaṃ kurutaḥ: asti kesarī nāma saṃgrāmaḥ | tatra ye kātarāḥ puruṣās te saṃgrāmaśirasi sthāpyante, ye madhyās te madhye, ye utkṛṣṭāḥ śūrapuruṣās te pṛṣṭhata iti | tatas te rājñe iti veditavantaḥ | śrutvā ca rājā prasenajit kauśalas tathā caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ ca rājānam ajātaśatrum abhiniryāto yuddhāya | tato rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena rājño 'jātaśatror vaidehīputrasya sarvo hastikāyaḥ paryastaḥ, aśvakāyo rathakāyaḥ pattikāyaḥ paryastaḥ | rājānam apy ajātaśatruṃ vaidehīputraṃ jitaṃ bhītabhagnaparājitaṃ parāpṛṣṭhīkṛtaṃ jīvagrāhaṃ gṛhītvā ekarathe 'bhiropya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣīdati | ekāntaniṣaṇṇo rājā prasenajitkauśalo bhagavantam ity avocat: ayaṃ hi bhadanta rājā ajātaśatrur dīrgharātram avairasya me vairī, asapatnasya sapatnaḥ | na cecchāmy enaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayitum*, yasmād vayasyaputro 'yaṃ bhavati | muñcāmy enam iti | muñca mahārājety uktvā bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> sent out spies throughout his realm in all directions: 'Listen to what the people are saying.' In <s>Jetavana</s>, two wrestlers were conversing with each other: 'There is a battle-formation called <s>Kesarī</s> (Lion). In it, the timid men are placed at the front of the battle, the middling ones in the center, and the superior, heroic men at the rear.' They reported this to the king. Having heard it, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> accordingly marshaled his fourfold army — the elephant corps, the cavalry, the chariot corps, and the infantry — and marched out against King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> for battle. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> overthrew the entire elephant corps, the cavalry, the chariot corps, and the infantry of King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s>. Having captured King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, the son of <s>Vaidehī</s> — defeated, frightened, broken, vanquished, put to flight — as a living prisoner, and having mounted him on a single chariot, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, having bowed with his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, this King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> has long been an enemy to me who had no enemies, a rival to me who had no rivals. But I do not wish to deprive him of his life, since he is the son of my friend. I release him.' Having said 'Release him, great king,' the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that moment spoke this verse:

children.text: jayo vairaṃ prasavati duḥkhaṃ śete parājitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Victory begets enmity; the defeated sleeps in suffering.

children.text: upaśāntaḥ sukhaṃ śete hitvā jayaparājayam* || AVŚ_10.1 ||
children.translated_text: The tranquil one sleeps in happiness, having abandoned both victory and defeat.' // AVŚ_10.1 //

children.text: atha rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasyaitad abhavat: yan mayā rājyaṃ pratilabdham*, tad asya śreṣṭhinaḥ prasādāt* | yanv aham enaṃ vareṇa pravārayeyam iti | atha rājā prasenajit kauśalas taṃ śreṣṭhinaṃ vareṇa prāvarayati | sa kathayati: ākāṃkṣāmi varam*, saptāhaṃ me yathābhirucitaṃ rājyam anuprayacchateti | tato rājñā sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam*: dattaṃ me śreṣṭhine saptāham ekaṃ rājyam iti | yāvat tena śreṣṭhinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ saptāhaṃ bkahtenopanimantritaḥ, rājā ca prasenajit saparivāraḥ | yāvantaś ca kāśikośaleṣu janakāyāḥ prativasanti, teṣāṃ dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam*: saptāhaṃ yūyaṃ sakalā yatheṣṭacāriṇaḥ sukhasparśaṃ viharata | kiṃcid āgatya buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchata, dharmaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then this thought arose in King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: 'I have regained my kingdom through the favor of this guild-master. Let me honor him with a boon.' Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> offered the guild-master a boon. He said: 'I desire a boon — grant me the kingdom for seven days as I wish.' Then the king had a bell-proclamation made throughout his entire realm: 'I have given the guild-master my kingdom for seven days.' And that guild-master invited the <s>Buddha</s> at the head of the community of monks for a meal for seven days, along with King <s>Prasenajit</s> and his retinue. To all the people dwelling in <s>Kāśī</s> and <s>Kośala</s>, he sent messengers: 'For seven days, all of you, free to go as you please, dwell in the ease of comfort. Come and take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and

children.text: bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca | māmakaṃ ca bhojanaṃ muñjānās tathāgataṃ paryupāsadhvam iti | tena saptāhaṃ bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho mahatā satkāreṇa satkṛtaḥ, bahūni ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kuśale niyojitāni | saptāhasyātyayena bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya cetanāṃ puṣṇāti, praṇidhiṃ ca cakāra: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: the community of monks. Partaking of my food, attend upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' For seven days he honored the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of disciples with great reverence, and established many hundreds of thousands of living beings in what is wholesome. At the end of the seven days, he fell at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, nourished his aspiration, and made his vow: 'By this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, may I, in a blind world, without a guide, without a leader, become a <s>Buddha</s> — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates those who are not liberated, who gives comfort to those who are not comforted, who brings to complete <s>nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained complete <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya śreṣṭhino hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the chain of causes and the chain of deeds of that guild-master, displayed a smile. It is a natural law that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, display a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue forth from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward proceed to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — and in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the specific torments of those beings are alleviated. This thought arises in them: 'Have we departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' For the purpose of generating faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth a magical creation. Having seen the magical creation, they think thus: 'We have indeed not departed from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is an unprecedented being, by whose power our specific torments have been alleviated.' Having set their minds with faith upon the magical creation, and having exhausted the karma that was to be experienced in hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those [rays] that go upward proceed to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' — and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: 'Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_10.1 ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant [shakes off] a reed hut.' // AVŚ_10.1 //

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_10.2 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live heedfully, having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering.' // AVŚ_10.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ {karma} vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati,
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra (billion-world) universe, follow the <s>Bhagavān</s> from behind. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to prophesy about past deeds, they vanish behind him. If he wishes to prophesy about the future, they vanish in front of him. If he wishes to prophesy a birth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy an animal birth, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy a birth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy a human birth, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (lesser universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy a divine birth, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of supreme, perfect awakening,

children.text: nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: And those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: 'A sheaf [of rays], variegated, adorned with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: has issued forth from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_10.3 ||
children.translated_text: as if by the sun at its rising.' // AVŚ_10.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he speaks [these] verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: 'Free from [the cycle of] arising, rid of wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme causes [of good] in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_10.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile as white as a conch, a lotus-stalk.' // AVŚ_10.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: 'Having yourself understood [this matter] at this very time by your heroic wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, <s>Jinendra</s> (Lord of Victors), for the listeners who are longing [to know] —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_10.5 ||
children.translated_text: O Bull among Sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen.' // AVŚ_10.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_10.6 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Not without reason do the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> (Fully Awakened), the Lords, steady as the ocean and the king of mountains, display a smile; those masses of people desire to hear about that for whose sake the Steadfast Ones display their smile.' // AVŚ_10.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasi tvam ānanda anena śreṣṭhinā tathāgatasya saśrāvakasaṃghasyaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam*, mahājanakāyaṃ ca kuśale niyuktam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda śreṣṭhī 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya abhayaprado nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati, daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how this guild-master has performed such an offering to the <s>Tathāgata</s> together with the community of disciples, and has engaged a great multitude of people in wholesome deeds?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, this guild-master, by this root of merit, by this generation of the thought [of awakening], and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, having accumulated the awakening that is accomplished over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), and having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) imbued with great compassion, shall become a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Abhayaprada</s> (Giver of Fearlessness), endowed with the ten powers, the four confidences, the three special mindful establishments, and great compassion. This is [the fruit of] his <s>Dharma</s>-offering — namely, his act of faith in my presence.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text:
dvitīyo vargaḥ |
tasyoddānam*:
children.translated_text:
The Second Section.
Its summary:

children.text: nāvā stambhaṃ ca snātraṃ ca tathetiḥ pratisārakam* (pratihāryakam*) |
children.translated_text: 'The boat, the pillar, the bathing, and thus the [saying] "iti," the protective charm (or miracle),

children.text: pāñcavārṣikaṃ stutir varadaḥ kāśikaṃ divyabhojanam* ||
children.translated_text: the quinquennial festival, the hymn of praise, the boon-giver, the cloth of Kāśī, and the divine feast.'

children.text: AVŚ_11 nāvikāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_11: The Boatmen. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati nadyā ajiravatyā adhastān nāvikagrāme | atha te nāvikā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdan* | ekāntaniṣaṇṇāṃs tān nāvikān bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati | anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm* | atha te nāvikā utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam ūcuḥ: adhivāsayatu bhagavān asmākaṃ nadyā ajiravatyās tīre śvo bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena | nausaṃkrameṇottārayiṣyāma iti | adhivāsayati bhagavān nāvikānāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Ajiravati</s>, in a village of boatmen. Then those boatmen approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the boatmen seated to one side, the Blessed One instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened them with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened them with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then the boatmen, rising from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, and with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said: 'May the Blessed One consent to [a meal] on the morrow with food, together with the community of monks, on the bank of the river <s>Ajiravati</s>; we shall ferry [you] across by boat-crossing.' The Blessed One consented to the boatmen by his silence.

children.text: atha nāvikā nadyā ajiravatyās tīram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpayāmāsur ucchritacchatradhvajapatākaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ gandhaghaṭikāvadhūpitam* | praṇītam āhāraṃ kṛtavantaḥ | prabhūtaṃ ca puṣpasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā nausaṃkramaṃ puṣpamaṇḍapair alaṃkārayāmāsuḥ | bhagavataś ca dūtena kālam ārocayāmāsuḥ: samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktam*, yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti | atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena nāvikagrāmakas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat* | atha te nāvikāḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati | anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcatarāṇy āsanāni gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavāṃs teṣāṃ nāvikānām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā anekair nāvikaiḥ srotaāpattiphalāni prāptāni, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalāni kaiścid anāgāmiphalāni, kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, kaiścic chrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekabodhau, kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | sarvā ca sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā | tatas tair nāvikair bhagavān mahatā satkāreṇa nausaṃkrameṇottāritaḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena ||
children.translated_text: Then the boatmen prepared the bank of the river <s>Ajiravati</s>, clearing it of stones, gravel, and rubble, with raised parasols, banners, and flags, strewn with various flowers, and perfumed with incense-balls. They prepared fine food. And having gathered an abundance of flowers, they decorated the boat-crossing with flower-pavilions. By a messenger they informed the Blessed One of the time: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the food is ready. May the Blessed One come at whatever time he sees fit.' Then the Blessed One, surrounded by the assembly of monks, with the community of monks before him, approached the boatmen's village. Having approached, he sat on the seat prepared in front of the community of monks. Then the boatmen, having ascertained that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with their own hands served and satisfied them with pure and fine hard and soft foods. Having in many ways served and satisfied them with pure and fine hard and soft foods with their own hands, and knowing that the Blessed One had finished eating, with washed hands and the bowl removed, they took lower seats and sat in front of the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, having known the dispositions, latent tendencies, nature, and character of those boatmen, gave such a discourse on <s>Dharma</s> penetrating the four noble truths, that upon hearing it many boatmen attained the fruit of stream-entry, some attained the fruit of once-returning, some the fruit of non-returning, some — having gone forth — through the abandonment of all defilements directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>, some generated the thought toward <s>Śrāvaka</s>-awakening, some toward <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-awakening, and some toward supreme perfect awakening. And that entire assembly was established inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, tending toward the <s>Dharma</s>, gravitating toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Then by those boatmen, the Blessed One, together with the community of monks, was ferried across with great honor on the boat-crossing.

children.text: bhikṣavo buddhapūjādarśanād āvarjitamanaso buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kutremāni bhagavataḥ kuśalamūlāni kṛtānīti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni, yena tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā | icchatha bhikṣavaḥ śrotum? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The monks, their minds attracted by having witnessed the worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One: 'Where were these roots of merit of the Blessed One planted?' The Blessed One said: 'It was by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in former lives, that deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur — by which such worship [now] accrues to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Do you wish to hear, monks?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then listen, monks, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani bhāgīratho nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto janapadacārikāṃ caran gaṅgātīram anuprāptaḥ | tasmin samaye 'nyataraḥ sārthavāho 'nekaśataparivāro nadyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ sārtham uttārayati | tasmiṃś ca pradeśe mahattaskarabhayam* | atha dadarśa sārthavāho bhāgīrathaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛtam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ cittaṃ prasādayāmāsa | prasannacittaś ca bhagavantam āmantritavān: tatprathamataram eva bhagavantaṃ tārayiṣyāmīti | adhivāsayati bhāgīrathaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sārthavāhasya tūṣṇībhāvena | tatas tena sārthavāhena bhāgīrathaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto mahatyā vibhūtyā nausaṃkrameṇottāritaḥ | praṇītena cāhāreṇa saṃtarpyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: 'In the distant past, monks, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Bhāgīratha</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He, surrounded by sixty-two thousand <s>Arhats</s>, was wandering through the countryside on a teaching tour and arrived at the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. At that time, a certain caravan-leader with a retinue of many hundreds was ferrying his caravan across the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. And in that region there was great danger from robbers. Then the caravan-leader saw the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhāgīratha</s>, surrounded by sixty-two thousand <s>Arhats</s>. Having seen him, he generated faith. With a mind full of faith, he addressed the Blessed One: "I shall ferry the Blessed One across first of all." The Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhāgīratha</s> consented to the caravan-leader by his silence. Then by that caravan-leader, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhāgīratha</s>, surrounded by sixty-two thousand <s>Arhats</s>, was ferried across with great splendor on a boat-crossing. And having satisfied him with fine food, a resolve toward supreme perfect awakening was made.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena sārthavāho babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | mayā sa bhāgīrathaḥ, samyaksaṃbuddho dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto nausaṃkrameṇottāritaḥ, praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ, praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam* | tasya me karmaṇo vipākenānantasaṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam* | idānīm apy anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasyaivavidhā pūjā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the caravan-leader — that was I. I ferried the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhāgīratha</s>, surrounded by sixty-two thousand <s>Arhats</s>, across by boat-crossing, satisfied him with fine food, and made the resolve. By the ripening of that deed of mine, I have experienced great happiness throughout endless cycles of rebirth. And now, having attained supreme perfect awakening, such worship [still accrues to me]. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_12 stambhaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_12: The Pillar. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kauravyeṣu janapadacārikāṃ caran kauravyaṃ nagaram anuprāptaḥ | sa ca kauravyo janakāyo buddhavaineya udāracitaḥ pradānaruciś ca | tato bhagavata etad abhavat*: yanv ahaṃ śakraṃ devendraṃ marudgaṇaparivṛtam āhveyeyam, yaddarśanād eṣāṃ kuśalamūlavivṛddhiḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was wandering through the countryside of the <s>Kauravyas</s> and arrived at the city of <s>Kauravya</s>. That populace of <s>Kauravya</s> was amenable to being trained by the <s>Buddha</s>, noble-minded, and fond of giving. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: 'Suppose I were to summon <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, surrounded by the host of <s>Maruts</s>, so that by seeing [them], the growth of these people's roots of merit

children.text: syād iti | tato bhagavāṃl laukikaṃ cittam utpādayati: aho bata śakro devendro marudgaṇasahāyo gośīrṣacandanamayaṃ stambham ādāya gacched iti || sahacittotpādāc chakro devendro marudgaṇaparivṛto āgato yatra viśvakarmā catvāraś ca mahārājā anekadevanāgayakṣakumbhāṇḍaparivṛto gośīrṣacandanastambham ādāya | hāhākārakilakilāprakṣveḍoccair nādaṃ kurvāṇā bhagavato 'rthe gośīrṣacandanamayaṃ prāsādam abhisaṃskṛtavantaḥ | tatas tasmin prāsāde śakreṇa devendreṇa bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho divyenāhāreṇa divyena śayanāsanena divyair gandhamālyapuṣpaiḥ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may occur.' Then the Blessed One generated a worldly thought: 'If only <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, together with the host of <s>Maruts</s> as companions, would come bringing a pillar made of <s>gośīrṣa</s> (bull's-head) sandalwood!' The moment the thought was generated, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, surrounded by the host of <s>Maruts</s>, arrived — along with <s>Viśvakarman</s> and the four great kings, attended by many gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s> — bringing the <s>gośīrṣa</s>-sandalwood pillar. With cries of 'Hāhā!' and shouts and cheers and loud exclamations, they constructed a palace of <s>gośīrṣa</s> sandalwood for the Blessed One. Then in that palace, by <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, the Blessed One together with the community of disciples was honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with divine food, divine bedding-and-seats, and divine fragrances, garlands, and flowers.

children.text: atha kauravyo janakāyas tāṃ divyāṃ vibhūṣikāṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpanna imāṃ cintām āpede: nūnaṃ buddho bhagavāṃl loke 'gryaḥ | yat tu nāma sendrair devaiḥ pūjyata iti āvarjitamanā bhagavantam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvaikānte nyaṣīdat* | ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ kauravyo janakāyas tasmin prāsāde 'tyarthaṃ prasādam utpādayati ||
children.translated_text: Then the populace of <s>Kauravya</s>, seeing that divine splendor, was filled with the utmost wonder and fell to thinking: 'Surely the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, is the foremost in the world, since he is worshipped even by gods headed by <s>Indra</s>!' With their minds thus won over, they approached the Blessed One. Having bowed at the Blessed One's feet, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the <s>Kauravya</s> populace, in that palace, generated the highest faith.

children.text:
tena bhagavāṃs tat prāsādam antardhāpya anityatāpratisaṃyuktāṃ tādṛśīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān*, yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ kauravyanivāsibhir manuṣyaiḥ srotaāpattiphalāny anuprāptāni, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalāni kaiścid anāgāmiphalāni, kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, kaiścic chrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau, kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | sarvā ca sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā |
  tatas te bhikṣavo bhagavato divyapūjādarśanād āvarjitamanaso buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kutremāni bhagavatā kuśalamūlāni kṛtānīti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni, yena tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā | icchatha bhikṣavaḥ śrotum? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text:
Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having caused that palace to disappear, delivered such a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> connected with impermanence that, upon hearing it, many people dwelling in <s>Kauravya</s> attained the <s>srotaāpattiphala</s> (fruit of stream-entry), some the <s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s> (fruit of once-returning), some the <s>anāgāmiphala</s> (fruit of non-returning), some, having gone forth, directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), some generated the aspiration toward <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), some toward <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), and some toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). And that entire assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.
Then those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), their minds captivated by the sight of the divine worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Where did the <s>Bhagavān</s> plant these <s>kuśalamūlāni</s> (roots of merit)?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It was the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, who in former times, in other births, performed and accumulated these deeds, whose provisions were gathered, whose conditions had ripened, which stood present like a flood, inevitable in their fruition — whereby the <s>Tathāgata</s> receives such worship. Do you wish to hear, O <s>bhikṣus</s>?" "Yes, <s>Bhadanta</s> (Venerable One)." "Then listen, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, and pay attention well and carefully; I shall speak."

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani brahmā nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | atha brahmā samyaksaṃbuddho dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ: brahmā samyaksaṃbuddho dvāṣaṣṭyarhatsahasraparivṛto janapadacārikāṃ carann asmākaṃ vijitam anuprāpta iti | śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena yena bhagavān brahmā samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya brahmaṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdat* | ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ bhagavān bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati | atha sa labdhaprasāda utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat*: adhivāsayatu
children.translated_text: "In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in a former age, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Brahmā</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, surrounded by sixty-two thousand <s>Arhats</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital. A king, a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior-noble) anointed on the head, heard: '<s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, surrounded by sixty-two thousand <s>Arhats</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, has arrived in our domain.' Having heard this, with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. Having approached and having bowed his head at the feet of <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, he sat down to one side. To the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, who was seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave instruction in the <s>dharmas</s> that lead to awakening. Then he, having gained faith, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May it please

children.text:
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 33 --------------------
me bhagavān asyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ traimāsyavāsāya | ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti | adhivāsayati brahmā samyaksaṃbuddho rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena | atha sa rājā mūrdhābhiṣikto bhagavato 'rthe gośīrṣacandanamayaṃ prāsādaṃ kārayāmāsa | sa taṃ vicitrair vastrālaṃkārair alaṃkṛtaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ gandhaghaṭikādhūpitaṃ bhagavataḥ saśrāvakasaṃghasya niryātya traimāsyaṃ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya vividhair vastraviśeṣair ācchādyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhiṃ cakāra ||
children.translated_text:
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 33 --------------------
the <s>Bhagavān</s> to stay in this royal capital for the three-month rainy season retreat. I shall attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples with robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick.' <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, consented to the king by silence. Then that king, anointed on the head, had a palace made of <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> (goat-head sandalwood) constructed for the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having adorned it with various cloths and ornaments, strewn it with manifold flowers, perfumed it with incense-balls, and having offered it to the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, and having satisfied them for the three months with excellent food and clothed them with various fine garments, he made a vow toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening)."

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | yan mayā brahmaṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā kṛtā, tasya me karmaṇo vipākenānantasaṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam* | idānīm apy anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhasyaivavidhā pūjā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who at that time, at that occasion, was the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head — that was I. Because I performed such worship of <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, by the ripening of that deed I experienced great happiness throughout endless <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). And now too, having fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening), I receive such worship. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, you should train thus: 'We shall honor the Teacher, we shall revere the Teacher, we shall respect the Teacher, we shall worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell in dependence upon him.' Thus should you train, O <s>bhikṣus</s>."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_13 snātram* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_13 <s>Snātram</s> (The Bath). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ pañcamātrāṇi vaṇikśatāni kāntāramārgapratipannāni | te mārgāt paribhraṣṭā vālukāsthalam anuprāptāḥ | te dharmaśramaparipīḍitāḥ kṣīṇapathyādanāś ca madhyāhnasamaye tīkṣṇakararaśmisaṃtāpitā jaloddhṛtā iva matsyāḥ pṛthivyām āvartante duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānāḥ | tāni devatāsahasrāṇy āyācante: tadyathā śivavaruṇakuberavāsavādīni | na cainān kaścit paritrātuṃ samarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, respected, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (eagle-beings), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents) — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, five hundred merchants in <s>Śrāvastī</s> had set out on a desert road. They strayed from the path and arrived at a sandy wasteland. Afflicted by heat and exhaustion, their provisions for the journey exhausted, at midday, scorched by the fierce rays of the sun, they writhed upon the ground like fish pulled from water, experiencing painful, intense, sharp, bitter, unpleasant sensations. They called upon thousands of deities — such as <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), and others — but none was able to rescue them.

children.text: tatra cānyatara upāsako buddhaśāsanābhijñaḥ | sa tān vaṇija āha: bhavanto buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchantv iti | tata ekaraveṇa sarva eva buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among them there was a certain <s>upāsaka</s> (lay devotee) who was devoted to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>. He said to those merchants: "Sirs, take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>!" Thereupon, with a single cry, all of them took refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ
children.translated_text: At that moment — there is nothing whatsoever that is unknown, unseen, unperceived, or unrecognized by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. For it is the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who are greatly compassionate, who act for the benefit of the world, who are single-minded in protection, who abide in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), who are skilled in the three bases of taming, who have crossed beyond the four floods, who are firmly established on the soles of the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), who have long practiced the four <s>saṃgrahavastus</s> (means of gathering disciples), who have abandoned the five limbs [of evil], who have transcended the five <s>gatis</s> (destinies of rebirth), who are endowed with the six limbs [of virtue], who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), who are adorned with the flowers of the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), who are guides of the eightfold path,

children.text: navānupūrva{vihāra}samāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: who are skilled in the nine successive <s>samāpattis</s> (meditative attainments), who are mighty with the ten <s>balas</s> (powers), whose fame fills the ten directions, who are distinguished above rulers of a thousand in the ten [ways] — three times during the night and three times during the day, surveying the world with the <s>buddhacakṣus</s> (Buddha-eye), knowledge and vision arises: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into difficulty, distress, and hardship? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is headed toward the lower realms? Who is tending toward the lower realms? Whom shall I, having lifted from the lower realms, establish in heaven and in liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, shall I extend the hand of rescue? Whom, bereft of the noble treasures, shall I establish in the sovereignty of the <s>āryadhana</s> (noble wealth)? For whom, whose eyes are covered by the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I purify vision with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? For whom shall I plant the unplanted <s>kuśalamūlāni</s> (roots of merit)? For whom shall I ripen those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already ripened?' And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: "The ocean, abode of <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters), might transgress its boundary,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_13.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the time for those who are to be guided, who are like his calves." (AVŚ 13.1)

children.text: yāvat paśyati bhagavān saṃbahulān vaṇijo vyasanasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptān* | tataś cakṣuḥsaṃpreṣaṇamātreṇa jetavane 'ntarhito bhikṣugaṇaparivṛtas taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ | dadṛśus te vaṇijo bhagavataṃ sabhikṣusaṃgham* | dṛṣṭvā ca uccair nādaṃ muktavantaḥ | tato bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittam utpāditam*: aho bata śakro devendro māhendraṃ varṣam utsṛjatu, śītalāś ca vāyavo vāntv iti | sahacittotpādād bhagavataḥ śakreṇa māhendraṃ varṣam utsṛṣṭam*, śītalāś ca vāyavaḥ preṣitāḥ, yatas teṣāṃ vaṇijāṃ tṛṣā vigatā, dāhaś ca praśāntaḥ | tatas tair vaṇigbhiḥ saṃjñā pratilabdhā | bhagavatā caiṣāṃ mārga ākhyāto yena śrāvastīm anuprāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> saw those many merchants who had fallen into misfortune, distress, and hardship. Thereupon, merely by sending forth his gaze, he disappeared from <s>Jetavana</s> and, surrounded by the company of <s>bhikṣus</s>, arrived at that place. Those merchants saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of <s>bhikṣus</s>. Having seen him, they uttered a loud cry. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> generated a worldly thought: 'May <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the <s>devas</s>, release an <s>Māhendra</s> (great Indra) rain, and may cool winds blow!' At the very instant of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mental intention, <s>Śakra</s> released a <s>Māhendra</s> rain, and cool winds were sent forth, whereby the thirst of those merchants was removed and their burning was quelled. Then those merchants regained consciousness. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> showed them the road by which they reached <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

children.text: te mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya tato bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntāḥ | teṣāṃ bhagavatā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā kaiścit srotaāpattiphalam adhigatam*, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam*, kaiścid anāgāmiphalam*, kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, kaiścic chrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni, kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau, kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | yadbhūyasā ca sā parṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṃghaprāgbhārā vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: Having relieved their fatigue from the journey, they then approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> delivered to them such a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> leading to penetration of the <s>caturāryasatya</s> (four noble truths) that, upon hearing it, some attained the <s>srotaāpattiphala</s> (fruit of stream-entry), some the <s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s> (fruit of once-returning), some the <s>anāgāmiphala</s> (fruit of non-returning), some, having gone forth, directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship) through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), some generated the aspiration toward <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), some toward <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), and some toward <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). And for the most part, that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and tending toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhagavān*, yāvad ime vaṇijo bhagavatā kāntāramārgāt paritrātāḥ | sahacittotpādāc ca māhendravarṣaṃ vṛṣṭam* | śītalāś ca vāyavaḥ pravātā iti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s>, having doubts arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: "It is wonderful, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that these merchants were rescued by the <s>Bhagavān</s> from the desert road, and that at the very instant of his mental intention, a <s>Māhendra</s> rain fell, and cool winds blew!" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It was the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, who in former times, in other births, performed and accumulated these deeds, whose provisions were gathered, whose conditions had ripened, which stood present like a flood, inevitable in their fruition. These deeds were performed and accumulated by me. Who else would experience their results? O <s>bhikṣus</s>, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, deeds performed ripen only in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), whether wholesome or unwholesome;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_13.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and the right time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. (AVŚ 13.1)

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani candano nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā
children.translated_text: "In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in a former age, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Candana</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher

children.text:
devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | atha candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto yena candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya candanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdat* | ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ candanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddo bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati | atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya candanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat*: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān asyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ traimāsyavāsāya sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃgheneti | adhivāsayati candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena | tatra ca samayena mahatī anāvṛṣṭiḥ prādurbhūtā, yayā nadyudapānāny alpasalilāni saṃvṛttāni, puṣpaphalaviyuktāś ca pādapāḥ || tato rājā candanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham adhyeṣituṃ pravṛttaḥ | bhagavann asmin nagaramadhye puṣkariṇīṃ gandhodakaparipūrṇāṃ karayiṣyāmi, yatra bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ snāsyati | apy eva nāma bhagavataḥ snānād asmin me vijite devo varṣed iti | adhivāsayati bhagavāṃś candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rajñas tuṣṇībhāvena |
  tato rajñā kṣatriyeṇa mūrdhābhiṣiktenāmātyebhya ājñā dattā: gandhodakaṃ sajjīkurvantu bhavantaḥ, ratnamayāṃś ca kumbhān*, yena vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ snāpayiṣyāma iti | tato rājñā āmātyagaṇaparivṛtena tan nagaram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitum ucchritadhvajapatākaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ gandhodakapariṣiktaṃ vicitradhūpadhūpitam* | puṣkariṇī cāsya kāritā | tato bhagavāṃś candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddaḥ sarvānugrahārtham ekacīvarakaḥ puṣkariṇyāṃ sthitaḥ | tato rājñāmātyagaṇaparivṛtena candanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saśrāvakasaṃgho nānāgandhaparibhāvitenodakena snāpitaḥ | sahasnānād eva candanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya śakreṇa devendreṇa tathāvidhaṃ māhendraṃ varṣam utsṛṣṭaṃ yena sarvasasyāni niṣpannāni | taddhaitukaṃ ca mahājanakāyena buddhe bhagavati śraddhā pratilabdhā | aneke ca gandhastūpāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ | ye ca tatra candanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ, sarve te parinirvṛtāḥ | aham ekas teṣām avaśiṣṭaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text:
of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. Then <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One), while wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital. Then the king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> who had received the consecration upon his head, approached <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. Having approached and worshiped the feet of <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> with his head, he sat down to one side. To the king, the consecrated <s>Kṣatriya</s>, seated to one side, <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> gave instruction in the teachings that lead to awakening. Then the king, the consecrated <s>Kṣatriya</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms in salutation toward <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, said this to <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>: 'May the Blessed One consent to dwell in this royal capital for the three-month rains retreat together with the <s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (community of monks).' <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> consented to the king by his silence. Now at that time a great drought had arisen, by which the rivers and wells had become depleted of water, and the trees were bereft of flowers and fruit. Then the king set about making a request to <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>: 'Venerable Sir, I shall have a pool filled with perfumed water constructed in the midst of this city, where the Blessed One together with the <s>Śrāvakasaṃgha</s> (community of disciples) may bathe. Perhaps by the Blessed One's bathing, rain may fall in my kingdom.' The Blessed One <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> consented to the king by his silence.
Then the king, the consecrated <s>Kṣatriya</s>, gave orders to his ministers: 'Prepare perfumed water, sirs, and jeweled pitchers, so that we may bathe the Blessed One together with the <s>Śrāvakasaṃgha</s>.' Then the king, surrounded by his retinue of ministers, had that city made free of stones, gravel, and rubble, with banners and flags raised aloft, strewn with various flowers, sprinkled with perfumed water, and fumigated with various kinds of incense. And a pool was constructed for him. Then the Blessed One <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, for the benefit of all, stood in the pool wearing a single robe. Then the king, surrounded by his retinue of ministers, bathed <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> together with the <s>Śrāvakasaṃgha</s> with water infused with various fragrances. Immediately upon the bathing of <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, released such a great <s>Māhendra</s> rain that all the crops were brought to fruition. And on account of that, a great multitude of people gained faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. And many <s>gandhastūpas</s> (fragrance-stūpas) were erected. And all those who had taken refuge in <s>Candana</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> have all attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>. I alone remain among them. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall revere, honor, respect, and worship the Teacher. Having revered, honored, respected, and worshiped the Teacher, we shall dwell in dependence upon him." Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_14 ītiḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 14 — <s>Īti</s> (Pestilence). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe |
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrels' Feeding Ground).
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 36]

children.text: tasmiṃś ca nāḍakanthāyāṃ mahājanamarako babhūva | tato janakāyo rogaiḥ pīḍitaḥ tāni tāni devatāsahasrāṇy āyācate śivavaruṇakuberavāsavādīni | na cāsya sā ītir upaśamaṃ gacchati | athānyatama upāsako nāḍakanthāyāṃ prativasati | sa nāḍakantheyān brāhmaṇagṛhapatīn idam avocat: eta yūyaṃ buddhaṃ śarāṇaṃ gacchata, taṃ ca bhagavantam āyācadhvam ihāgamanāya | apy eva bhagavatā svalpakṛcchreṇāsyā īter vyupaśamaḥ syād iti | atha nāḍakantheyā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavantam āyācituṃ pravṛttāḥ: āgacchatu bhagavān asmād vyasanasaṃkaṭān mocanāyeti ||
children.translated_text: And in <s>Nāḍakanthā</s> there arose a great plague among the people. Then the populace, afflicted by diseases, prayed to those thousands upon thousands of deities — <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), and others — but that pestilence did not subside. Now a certain <s>upāsaka</s> (lay follower) was dwelling in <s>Nāḍakanthā</s>. He said this to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Nāḍakanthā</s>: 'Come, all of you, take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, and entreat the Blessed One to come here. Perhaps the Blessed One may with little difficulty bring about the subsiding of this pestilence.' Then the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Nāḍakanthā</s> began to entreat the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One come, for our deliverance from this calamitous affliction!'
