children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrva{vihāra}samāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, there is nothing whatsoever that is unknown, unseen, unperceived, or uncomprehended by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. It is indeed the nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones — who are great in compassion, devoted to the benefit of the world, sole protectors, abiding in <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three means of taming, who have crossed beyond the four floods, firmly established on the ground of the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipādas</s>), who have long practiced the four means of attracting beings (<s>saṃgrahavastus</s>), who have abandoned the five limbs [of wrong conduct], who have transcended the five destinies, who are endowed with the six limbs [of right conduct], who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), who are adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>), who are guides on the eightfold path, skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments (<s>anupūrvasamāpattis</s>), empowered with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who surpass even a ruler of ten hundred [worlds] — three times by night and three times by day to survey the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, and their knowledge-and-vision proceeds: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into straits? Who has fallen into difficulty, distress, and straits? Who is headed for a bad destiny? Who is inclined toward a bad destiny? Who is rushing headlong toward a bad destiny? Whom shall I, having lifted out of a bad destiny, establish in heaven and in liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of sensual desires, shall I extend the hand of rescue? Whom, deprived of the noble treasures, shall I establish in the sovereignty and dominion of the noble treasures? Whose eyes, covered with the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? Whose wholesome roots that have not been planted shall I plant? Whose planted ones shall I bring to maturity? Whose matured ones shall I liberate?' And he speaks:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: "The ocean, abode of <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters), may transgress its bounds,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_14.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the time for those to be trained." // <s>AVŚ</s> 14.1 //

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto nāḍakanthām anuprāptaḥ | tato bhagavatā tan nagaraṃ sarvaṃ hṛdimaitryā sphuṭam*, yato marakāḥ prakrāntāḥ, ītiś ca vyupaśāntā | tatas teṣāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ buddhadarśanān mahāprasāda utpannaḥ, prasādajātaiś ca bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ saṃpravāritaḥ | tatas tebhyo bhagavatā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā anekair brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ srotaāpattiphalam anuprāptam*, aparaiḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalam, aparaiḥ anāgāmiphalam*, aparaiḥ pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sarvaṃ ca tan nagaraṃ buddhanimnaṃ dharmapravaṇaṃ saṃghaprāgbhāraṃ saṃvṛttam* ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken up his bowl and robe, surrounded and attended by the community of monks, arrived at <s>Nāḍakanthā</s>. Then the Blessed One suffused that entire city with the loving-kindness of his heart, whereupon the plagues departed and the pestilence subsided. Then, at the sight of the <s>Buddha</s>, a great faith arose in those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, and filled with faith, they presented the Blessed One together with the <s>Śrāvakasaṃgha</s> with robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites. Then the Blessed One gave them such a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> for the penetration of the Four Noble Truths (<s>Caturāryasatya</s>) that, upon hearing it, many <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>Srotaāpattiphala</s>), others attained the fruit of once-returning (<s>Sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), others attained the fruit of non-returning (<s>Anāgāmiphala</s>), and others, having gone forth into homelessness, through the abandonment of all defilements (<s>kleśas</s>), directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. And that entire city became inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text:
bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yāvad ime satvā bhagavataḥ prasādād vyasanagatāḥ santo vyasanāt parimuktā iti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni |
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 37 --------------------
children.translated_text:
The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, questioned the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that these beings, by the grace of the Blessed One, while caught in calamity, have been delivered from calamity!' The Blessed One said: 'It was indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, who in previous births performed and accumulated these <s>karmas</s> (actions), which, having gathered their requisite conditions and ripened in their causes, stand present like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. It was I who performed and accumulated these <s>karmas</s>.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 37]

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: Who else would experience their results? Monks, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth-element, nor in the water-element, nor in the fire-element, nor in the wind-element; rather, <s>karmas</s> performed ripen only in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), whether wholesome or unwholesome;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{sonst: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_14.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and the right time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings." // <s>AVŚ</s> 14.1 //
"<s>Karmas</s> do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani candro nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | atha candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ: candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho 'smākaṃ vijitam anuprāpta iti | śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgato yena candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya candrasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte nyaṣīdat* | ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati | atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto labdhaprasāda utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya candraṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat*: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān iha vāsaṃ traimāsyaṃ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena | ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti | adhivāsayati candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena | tasya ca rājño nagare tena samayena mahājanamarako babhūva, ītiś ca, yena sa mahājanakāyo 'tīva saṃtarpyate | tato rājñā vyādhipraśamanārthaṃ candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho 'dhīṣṭaḥ | sādhu bhagavan kriyatām asyā īter upaśamopāya iti | tato bhagavāṃś candraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho rājānam uvāca: gaccha mahārāja imāṃ saṃghāṭīṃ dhvajāgre baddhā mahatā satkāreṇa sve vijite paryāṭaya, asya ca mahāntam utsavaṃ kuru | sarvaṃ ca mahājanakāyaṃ buddhānusmṛtau samādāpayeti | te svastir bhaviṣyatīti | tato rājñā yathānuśiṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ tathaiva ca kṛtam* | taddhetutatpratyayaṃ ca sarvā ītayaḥ praśāntāḥ | tataḥ sa janakāyo labdhaprasādo rājāmātyapaurāś ca buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ, dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Candra</s> (Moon) arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. The Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital. A king, a consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s>, heard: 'The Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s> has arrived in our realm.' Having heard this, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, he approached the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s>. Having approached, having bowed with his head at the feet of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s>, he sat down to one side. The Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s> instructed the king, the consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s>, seated to one side, in the teachings conducive to awakening. Then the king, the consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s>, having gained faith, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s>, said: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to dwell here for a three-month [rainy season retreat] together with the community of monks. I shall attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> with robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick.' The Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s> consented to the king by his silence. Now at that time a great plague was occurring in the king's city, along with calamities, by which the great populace was exceedingly tormented. Then the king implored the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s> for the alleviation of the disease: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> be pleased to devise a means for the cessation of this calamity.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s>, said to the king: 'Go, great king, tie this <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer monastic robe) to the top of a flagstaff and, with great honor, carry it throughout your realm, and hold a great festival for it. Establish the entire populace in the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>. Then welfare shall be theirs.' Then the king did everything exactly as instructed. And by that cause and that condition, all calamities were pacified. Then that populace, having gained faith — the king, ministers, and citizens — took refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | mayāsau candrasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya mahatī pūjā kṛtā | tasya me karmaṇo vipākena devamanuṣyasaṃprāpakaṃ saṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam* | idānīm api taddhaituky eva vibhūtiḥ, yena yac cintayāmi yat prārthaye tat tathaiva sarvaṃ samṛdhyati | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king — that was I. By me was that great worship offered to the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Candra</s>. As the fruit of that deed of mine, I have experienced great happiness in the cycle of rebirth, leading to [rebirths among] gods and humans. Even now, it is by that very cause that such splendor [comes to pass], whereby whatever I think, whatever I aspire to — all of that is accomplished just so. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

children.text: AVŚ_15 prātihāryam* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_15: The Miracle. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | yadā rājñā ajātaśatruṇā devadattavigrāhitena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājo jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, svayam eva ca rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ, tadā ye aśrāddhās te balavanto jātāḥ, śrāddhās tu durbalāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | yāvad anyatamo vṛddhāmātyo 'śrāddho bhagavacchāsanavidveṣī, sa brāhmaṇebhyo yajñam ārabdho yaṣṭum* | tatrānekāni brāhmaṇaśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni | taiḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ: na kenacic chramaṇagautamaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramitavyam* | atha te brāhmaṇāḥ kṛtāvayaḥ samagrāḥ saṃmodamānā vīthīmadhye vedoktena vidhinā śakram āyācituṃ pravṛttāḥ: ehy ehi ahalyājāra ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), in the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding-ground). When King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, instigated by <s>Devadatta</s>, had deprived his righteous father, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, of his life and had himself been established on the throne, those who lacked faith became powerful, while the faithful became weak. There was a certain elderly minister, lacking faith, hostile to the <s>Bhagavān's</s> teaching. He began to conduct a sacrifice for the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Many hundreds of thousands of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> assembled there. They made a compact: 'No one shall approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> for an audience.' Then those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having completed their preparations, assembled together in joyful concord, and in the middle of the street began to invoke <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) according to the Vedic rite: 'Come, come, O seducer of <s>Ahalyā</s>!'

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrva{vihāra}samāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Meanwhile — for there is nothing unknown, unseen, uncomprehended, or ununderstood by <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. It is indeed the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, of singular protection, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three means of discipline, who have crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, long practiced in the four means of conversion, who have abandoned the five [negative] factors, who have transcended the five destinations, endowed with the six factors, who have fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the seven factors of awakening, who point out the eightfold path, skilled in the nine successive attainments, empowered with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who surpass a hundred <s>Śakras</s> in authority — three times at night and three times during the day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye they survey the world, and knowledge-and-vision operates: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into a narrow place? Who has fallen into difficulty, distress, and a narrow place? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who gravitates toward the lower realms? Whom should I, having rescued from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, should I extend a hand to pull them out? Whom, deprived of noble wealth, should I establish in the sovereignty of noble wealth? Whose eyes, covered by the film of ignorance, should I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? Whose unplanted roots of merit should I plant? Whose planted ones should I ripen? Whose ripened ones should I liberate?' And he declares:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its bounds,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_15.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the time for those to be trained, his calves.' // AVŚ_15.1 //

children.text: paśyati bhagavān: ime brāhmaṇāḥ pūrvāvaropitakuśalamūlā gṛhītamokṣamārgāḥ svahitaiṣiṇo 'bhimukhā nirvāṇe bahirmukhāḥ saṃsārād akalyāṇamitrasaṃsārgād idānīṃ macchāsanaṃ vidviṣanti, yanv aham eṣāṃ vinayahetor autsukyam āpadyeyeti | atha bhagavāñ chakraveṣam abhinirmāya taṃ yajñavāṭaṃ divyenāvabhāsenāvabhāsya avataritum ārabdhaḥ | tatas te brāhaṇā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditā udagraprītisaumanasyajātā
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw: 'These <s>brāhmaṇas</s> have roots of merit planted in the past, have grasped the path to liberation, are desirous of their own welfare, face toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, [yet] turn away from <s>saṃsāra</s> — but now, through association with unwholesome friends, they are hostile to my teaching. Let me exert myself for the sake of their training.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having magically assumed the guise of <s>Śakra</s>, illuminating that sacrificial enclosure with a divine radiance, began to descend. Then those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, delighted, pleased, joyful, filled with exultation, gladness, and delight,

children.text: ekasamūhenoktavantaḥ: ehy ehi bhagavan, svāgataṃ bhagavata iti | tato bhagavān śakraveṣadhārī prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | eṣa śabdo rājagṛhe samantato visṛtaḥ: yajñe śakro devendro 'vatīrṇa iti | yaṃ śutvānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni | tato bhagavān āvarjitā brāhmaṇā iti viditvā śakraveṣam antardhāpya buddhaveṣeṇaiva sthitvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā ṣaṣṭyā brāhmaṇasahasrair viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, anekaiś ca prāṇiśatasahasrair bhagavati śraddhā pratilabdhā ||
children.translated_text: exclaimed in unison: 'Come, come, <s>Bhagavān</s>, welcome to the <s>Bhagavān</s>!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wearing the guise of <s>Śakra</s>, sat upon the very seat that had been prepared. The news spread throughout <s>Rājagṛha</s> on all sides: '<s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, has descended at the sacrifice!' Having heard this, many hundreds of thousands of beings assembled. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> were won over, made the guise of <s>Śakra</s> disappear and, remaining in the guise of the <s>Buddha</s>, gave such a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> penetrating the four noble truths that, upon hearing it, sixty thousand <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, shattering with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the false view of a personal self that rises to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry; and many hundreds of thousands of beings gained faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yāvad ebhir brāhmaṇair bhagavantam āgatya satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam*, anekaiś ca prāṇiśatasahasrair mahān prasādo 'dhigata iti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: Then the monks, their doubts aroused, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that these <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having come to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, achieved the vision of the truths, and that many hundreds of thousands of beings gained great faith!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur. By me were these deeds performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruits]? For, monks, deeds that are performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; but rather, in the very aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that are taken up, do deeds performed ripen — both wholesome and unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_15.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conjunction and the right time, they assuredly bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_15.1 //
'Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); *{variant: deeds even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>;}*

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani indradamano nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | sā rājadhānī tīrthikāvaṣṭabdhā | aśrauṣīd anyatamo rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ: indradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho 'smākaṃ vijitam anuprāpta iti | śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgato yenendradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavata indradamanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktam indradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair (Speyer: bodhisatvakarakair) dharmaiḥ samādāpayati | atha sa rājā labdhaprasāda utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yenendradamanaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya indradamanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat*: adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃs traimāsyavāsāya | ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti | bhagavān āha: asti te mahārāja vijite kaścid vihāro yatrāgantukā gamikāś ca bhikṣavo vāsaṃ kalpayiṣyantīti? rājovāca: nāsti bhagavan, kiṃ tarhi tiṣṭhatu bhagavān, ahaṃ vihāraṃ kārayiṣyāmi, yatrāgantukā gamikāś ca bhikṣavo vāsaṃ kalpayiṣyantīti | tato rājñā tathāgatasyārthe vihāraḥ kāritaḥ aviddhaprākāratoraṇo gāvākṣaniryūhajālārdhacandravedikāpratimaṇḍita
children.translated_text: 'In the distant past, monks, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Indradamana</s> (Tamer of Indra) arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He, wandering through the countryside on a teaching tour, arrived at a certain royal capital. That capital was under the control of heretical teachers. A certain king, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, heard: "The Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradamana</s> has arrived in our realm." Having heard, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, he approached the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradamana</s>. Having approached, having bowed with his head at the feet of the Blessed One <s>Indradamana</s>, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s>, he sat to one side. To the king, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, seated to one side, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradamana</s> inspired him with teachings conducive to awakening. Then that king, having gained faith, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradamana</s>, said: "May the Blessed One consent to remain for a three-month residence. I shall attend the Blessed One with robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick." The Blessed One said: "Do you have, great king, in your realm any monastery where visiting and departing monks may take up residence?" The king said: "There is none, Venerable One, but wait — I shall have a monastery built where visiting and departing monks may take up residence." Then by the king, a monastery was built for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with unbroken walls and gateways, adorned with latticed windows, projections, net-work, half-moons, and railings,

children.text: āstaraṇopeto jalādhārasaṃpūrṇas tarugaṇaparivṛto nānāpuṣpaphalopetaḥ | kṛtvā ca bhagavataḥ saśrāvakasaṃghasya niryātitaḥ | adhīṣṭaś ca bhagavān mahāprātihāryaṃ prati | tato bhagavatā indradamanena samyaksaṃbuddhena rājño 'dhyeṣayā mahāprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ buddhāvataṃsakavikrīḍitam*, yaddarśanād rājā sāmātyanaigamajānapadaḥ sarve ca nāgarāḥ suprasannāḥ śāsane saṃraktatarāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: furnished with carpets, provided with water-reservoirs, surrounded by groves of trees, equipped with various flowers and fruits. Having built it, he presented it to the Blessed One together with the community of disciples. And he requested the Blessed One to perform a great miracle. Then the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradamana</s>, at the king's request, displayed a great miracle — a play of the <s>Buddha</s>'s ornamented display — upon seeing which the king, together with his ministers, townspeople, and country-dwellers, and all the citizens, became deeply faithful and more devoted to the teaching.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | mayā sā indradamanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhā pūjā kṛtā | tasya me karmaṇo vipākena saṃsāre 'nantaṃ sukham anubhūtam* | idānīṃ me tathāgatasya sata iyaṃ śāsanaśobhā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king — that was I. By me, such worship was performed for the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradamana</s>. By the ripening of that deed of mine, I have experienced endless happiness in the cycle of rebirth. And now, for me the <s>Tathāgata</s>, this is the splendor of the teaching. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_16 pāñcavārṣikam* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_16: The Quinquennial Festival. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | yadā devadattena mohapuruṣeṇa bhagavacchāsane 'narthasahasrāṇi kṛtāni, na ca śakitaṃ bhagavato romeñjanam api kartum*, tadā rājānam ajātaśatrum āmantritavān*: kriyatāṃ rājagṛhe kriyākāro na kenacic chramaṇasya gautamasyopasaṃkramitavyam*, piṇḍakena vā pratipādayitavyaḥ | evam ayam alabdhalābho 'labdhasaṃmāno niyatam anyadeśaṃ saṃkrāntiṃ kariṣyatīti | rajñā tathā kāritam* | tatra ye upāsakā dṛṣṭasatyās te rodituṃ pravṛttāḥ: hā kaṣṭam anāthībhūtaṃ rājagṛhanagaraṃ yatra hi nābhodumbarapuṣpadurlabhaprādurbhāvaṃ (Speyer: nāmodumbarapuṣpadurlabhaprādurbhāvaṃ) buddhaṃ bhagavantam āsādya tasya na śakyate saṃgrahaḥ kartum iti | eṣa śabdaḥ śrutiparaṃparayā bhikṣubhiḥ śrutaḥ | tata āyuṣmatānandena yathāśrutaṃ bhagavato niveditaḥ | bhagavān āha: alpotsukas tvam ānanda bhava, tathāgatā evātra kālajñāḥ | api tu yāvac chāsanaṃ me tāvac chrāvakāṇām upakaraṇavaikalyaṃ na bhaviṣyati prāg evedānīm iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s> in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel-feeding Ground). When thousands of injuries to the Blessed One's teaching had been committed by the deluded <s>Devadatta</s>, yet not even a hair of the Blessed One could be disturbed, then he addressed King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'Let a ban be imposed in <s>Rājagṛha</s>: no one shall approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, nor provide him with alms. Thus, having obtained neither gain nor honor, he will surely migrate to another region.' The king had it done accordingly. Thereupon those lay-followers who had seen the truth began to weep: 'Alas, how wretched! The city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> has become orphaned, since, having encountered the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — whose appearance is as rare as the blossom of the <s>udumbara</s> (fig tree) — it is unable to honor him!' This cry, passing from ear to ear, was heard by the monks. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> reported it to the Blessed One as he had heard it. The Blessed One said: 'Be of little concern, <s>Ānanda</s>; the <s>Tathāgatas</s> alone are the knowers of the [right] time in such matters. Moreover, as long as my teaching endures, there will be no lack of requisites for the disciples — how much less so now!'

children.text: atrāntare śakrasya devānām indrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate | sa paśyati bhagavacchāsanasyaivaṃvidhāṃ vikṛtim* | sahadarśanād eva dāyakadānapatīnāṃ utsāhasaṃjananārthaṃ buddhotpādasya māhātmyasaṃjananārtham ajātaśatror devadattasya ca madadarpacchittyartham ātmanaś ca prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ sakalaṃ rājagṛham udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsyoccaiḥśabdham udāritavān: eṣo 'ham adyāgreṇa bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ divyaiś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upasthāsyāmi | ity uktvā yena
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, knowledge-and-vision arose in <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, below [in his heaven]. He perceived the disturbance to the Blessed One's teaching. The very moment he perceived it, for the purpose of generating enthusiasm in donors and benefactors, for the purpose of proclaiming the greatness of the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>, for the purpose of cutting the pride and arrogance of <s>Ajātaśatru</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>, and for the purpose of generating faith in himself, he illuminated all of <s>Rājagṛha</s> with a splendid radiance and proclaimed aloud: 'From this day forward, I shall attend the Blessed One together with the community of disciples with divine robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick!' Having said this, he approached

children.text: bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte sthitaḥ | atha śakro devendro bhagavantam idam avocat: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān asminn eva rājagṛhe nagare | ahaṃ bhagavantam upasthāsyāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair iti | bhagavān āha: alaṃ kauśika kṛtam etad yāvad eva cittam abhiprasannam* | bahavo hi loke puṇyakāmā iti | śakraḥ prāha: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān pañca varṣāṇi | tathāgatasyārthe pañcavārṣikaṃ kariṣyāmīti | bhagavān āha: alaṃ kauśika kṛtam etad yāvac cittam abhiprasannam* | bahavo hi loke puṇyakāmā iti | śakraḥ prāha: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān pañca divasān iti | tato bhagavān svapuṇyabalapratyakṣīkaraṇārthaṃ śakrasya ca devendrasyānugrahārtham anāgatapañcavārṣikaprabandhahetoś cādhivāsitavāṃs tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: the Blessed One. Having approached and bowed with his head at the Blessed One's feet, he stood to one side. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, said to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One consent [to remain] here in this very city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. I shall attend the Blessed One with robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick.' The Blessed One said: 'Enough, <s>Kauśika</s>; it is sufficient that your mind has been filled with faith. For there are many in the world who desire merit.' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'May the Blessed One consent [to let me serve] for five years. I shall perform a quinquennial festival for the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Enough, <s>Kauśika</s>; it is sufficient that your mind has been filled with faith. For there are many in the world who desire merit.' <s>Śakra</s> said: 'May the Blessed One consent for five days.' Then the Blessed One, for the purpose of making manifest the power of his own merit, for the purpose of favoring <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, and for the sake of establishing the tradition of future quinquennial festivals, consented by his silence.

children.text: atha śakro devendro bhagavas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā tad veṇuvanaṃ vaijayantaṃ prāsādaṃ pradarśitavān*, divyāni cāsanāni, divyāḥ puṣkaraṇīr divyaṃ ca bhojanam* | atha bhagavān prajñapta eva āsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | tataḥ śakro devendraḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā anekadevatāsahasraparivṛtaḥ svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati | anekaparyāyeṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcataram āsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tato bhagavān śakraṃ devendraṃ saparivāraṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati | paśyati ca rājā ajātaśatrur upariprāsādatalagataḥ san bhagavato veṇuvane evaṃvidhāṃ pūjāṃ* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar vipratisārajāto mahāntaṃ prasādaṃ praveditavān* | rājagṛhanivāsinaś ca paurā dharmavegapṛaptā rājānam upasaṃkramyaivam ūcuḥ: muṣyante deva mahārāja rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurāḥ, yatra nāma devāḥ pramattāḥ santaḥ pramādavihāriṇo divyān viṣayān apahāya bhagavantaṃ pūjayanti | sādhu deva ughāṭyatāṃ kriyākāra iti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, knowing the Blessed One's consent by his silence, made the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove) appear as the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace, with divine seats, divine lotus-pools, and divine food. Then the Blessed One sat on the very seat that had been prepared. Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, knowing that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, surrounded by many thousands of deities, served and satisfied them with his own hands. Having in many ways served and satisfied them with his own hands, and knowing that the Blessed One had finished eating, with washed hands and the bowl removed, he took a lower seat and sat in front of the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, together with his retinue, with a discourse on <s>Dharma</s>. And King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, being on the upper floor of the palace, saw such worship of the Blessed One in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>. Having seen it, stricken with remorse, he was filled with great faith. And the citizens dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, seized by the force of the <s>Dharma</s>, approached the king and said: 'The citizens of <s>Rājagṛha</s> are being robbed, Your Majesty! For even the gods, though heedless beings who dwell in heedlessness, abandoning divine pleasures, worship the Blessed One. Please, Your Majesty, lift the ban!'

children.text: tato rājñā ajātaśatruṇā kriyākāram udghāṭya rājagṛhe nagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam*: kriyatāṃ bhagavataḥ satkāro yathāsukham iti | tato rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurāḥ saparivārā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditā udagraprītisaumanasyajātāḥ puṣpagandhamālyāny ādāya bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | tato devair manuṣyaiś ca bhagavato mahān satkāraḥ kṛtaḥ, bhagavatā ca tad adhiṣṭhānaṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā anekair devamanuṣyaiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having lifted the ban, had a bell-proclamation made throughout the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>: 'Let worship of the Blessed One be performed as you please!' Then the citizens of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, with their retinues, joyful, delighted, elated, filled with keen joy and happiness, taking flowers, fragrances, and garlands, approached the Blessed One to see him. Then by gods and humans a great worship of the Blessed One was performed, and the Blessed One, at that sacred place, gave such a discourse on <s>Dharma</s> penetrating the four noble truths to gods and humans, that upon hearing it, many gods and humans realized the vision of the truths.

children.text: bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pūjāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃśayajātā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavataḥ śāsane evaṃvidha utsava iti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau,
children.translated_text: The monks, having seen the worship of the Blessed One, filled with curiosity, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that such a festival has occurred in the Blessed One's teaching!' The Blessed One said: 'It was by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in former lives, that deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur. By me these deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element,

children.text: na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_16.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_16.1 //
'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ratnaśailo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyāṃ dharmabuddhir nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyāṃ mahatī ītiḥ | tatas tena rājñā ītipraśamanahetor bhagavān śrāvakasaṃghatraimāsye bhaktenopanimantritaḥ |trāyāṇāṃ māsānām atyayena sā ītiḥ praśāntā | tato rājño nāgaraiś cāvarjitamānasais tathāgatasya saśrāvakasaṃghasya pañcavārṣikaṃ kṛtam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), in a former age, a perfectly awakened Buddha named <s>Ratnaśaila</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly awakened one, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One. While wandering on a tour of the countryside, he arrived at a certain royal capital. In that capital, a king named <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> was ruling, and in that capital there was a great calamity. Then that king, for the purpose of pacifying the calamity, invited the Blessed One together with the <s>saṃgha</s> (community) of disciples to a meal for the three months of the rainy season retreat. At the end of three months, the calamity was pacified. Then the king, together with the citizens whose minds had been won over, held a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival) for the <s>Tathāgata</s> together with his <s>saṃgha</s> of disciples. And he said:

children.text:
rājabhūtena ānanda ratnaśailo mahādyutiḥ |
  avīṣṭaḥ śāntikāmena akārṣīt pañcavārṣikam* || AVŚ_16.2 || iti ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Ānanda</s>, when I was a king, <s>Ratnaśaila</s> of great splendor was invited by one desiring peace, and a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival) was held." (AVŚ 16.2)

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | yan mayā ratnaśailasya tathāgatasya pañcavārṣikaṃ kṛtam*, tena me saṃsāre mahatsukham anubhūtam* | taddhaitukaś cedānīṃ tathāgatasyaivaṃvidhaḥ satkāraḥ | parinirvṛtasya ca me śāsane anekāni pañcavārṣikaśatāni bhaviṣyati | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: "What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks)? He who was the king at that time, in that era — I was he. Because I held a <s>pañcavārṣika</s> (quinquennial festival) for the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśaila</s>, I experienced great happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence). And due to that very cause, there is now such honor for the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), in my teaching there will be many hundreds of <s>pañcavārṣikas</s> (quinquennial festivals). Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, you should train thus: 'We shall honor the Teacher, we shall revere the Teacher, we shall respect and worship him. Having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell in reliance upon him.' Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, should you train yourselves."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te ca bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.

children.text: AVŚ_17 stutiḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 17: The Hymn of Praise (ed. <s>Speyer</s>, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ pañcamātrāṇi gāndharvikaśatāni goṣṭhikānāṃ prativasanti | tatra ca kāle supriyo nāma gāndharvikarājo 'bhyāgataḥ | tasyaivaṃvidhā śaktiḥ: ekasyāṃ tantryāṃ sāpta svarān ādarśayati, ekaviṃśatiṃ mūrcchināḥ | sa ṣaṇmahānagarāṇy apaṭukāny udghoṣayamāṇaḥ śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ | śrāvastīnivāsibhiś ca gāndharvikai rājñe niveditam* | rājāha: alpotsukā bhavantu bhavantaḥ, vayam atra kālajñā bhaviṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: The Buddha, the Blessed One, honored, revered, respected, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (eagle beings), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents) — thus worshipped by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, the Buddha, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the <s>saṃgha</s> (community) of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, five hundred musician guilds were residing in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. And at that time, a king of musicians named <s>Supriya</s> arrived. His skill was of this kind: on a single string he could display seven notes and twenty-one <s>mūrcchanās</s> (melodic modulations). Proclaiming the six great cities as defeated, he arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The musicians residing in <s>Śrāvastī</s> reported this to the king. The king said: "Do not be anxious, sirs; we shall know the right time for this."
[editorial page reference]

children.text: atha supriyasya gāndharvikarājasyaitad abhavat: evam anuśrūyate rājā prasenajid gāndharve 'tīva kuśalaḥ | yanv aham anena saha vādam ārocayeyam iti | tataḥ supriyo gāndharvikarājo yena rājā prasenajit kauśalas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalam idam āvocat*: śrutaṃ me rājan yathā tvaṃ gāndharvakuśala iti | yadi te aguru, mīmāṃsasveti | tato rājñā prasenajitā tasya vikṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ | uktaś ca: sādho asti me gurur jetavane sthito 'nuttaro gāndharvikarājaḥ | ehi tat samīpaṃ yāsyāma iti | atha rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ pañcamātrair gāndharvikaśataiḥ parivṛtaḥ supriyeṇa gāndharvikarājenānekaiś ca prāṇiśatasahasrair jetavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the musician-king <s>Supriya</s> had this thought: "Thus it is heard that King <s>Prasenajit</s> is exceedingly skilled in music. Let me challenge him to a contest." Then the musician-king <s>Supriya</s> approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>. Having approached, he said this to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>: "I have heard, O king, that you are skilled in music. If it is not burdensome to you, let us have a trial." Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> put him off, and said: "Good sir, I have a teacher dwelling in <s>Jetavana</s>, the unsurpassed king of musicians. Come, let us go to his presence." Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, surrounded by five hundred musicians, together with the musician-king <s>Supriya</s> and many hundreds of thousands of beings, went to <s>Jetavana</s>.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: In this regard, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unperceived, or uncomprehended by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones. For it is the <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law) of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, having a single care, dwelling in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three bases of taming, who have crossed beyond the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, long practiced in the four means of gathering disciples, who have abandoned the five factors, transcended the five destinies, endowed with six factors, who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, who are guides of the eightfold path, skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, mighty with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, distinguished above a thousand sovereigns — three times at night and three times during the day, surveying the world with the Buddha-eye, knowledge and vision arises: "Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into straits? Who has fallen into hardship, distress, and straits? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is tending toward the lower realms? Who is headed toward the lower realms? Whom shall I rescue from the lower realms and establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, shall I extend the hand of rescue? Whom, deprived of the noble treasures, shall I establish in the sovereignty of the noble treasures? For whom, whose eyes are covered by the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I purify vision with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? For whom shall I plant roots of merit not yet planted? For whom shall I ripen those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already ripened?" And he said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: "The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might perhaps transgress its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_17.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the Buddha would never transgress the proper time for those to be trained, who are like his calves." (AVŚ 17.1)

children.text: tato bhagavān vaineyajanānugrahārthaṃ laukikaṃ cittam utpāditavān* | aho bata pañcaśikho gandharvaputraḥ saptagandharvasahasraparivṛto vaiḍūryadaṇḍāṃ vīṇām ādāya matsakāśam upasaṃkrāmed iti | sahacittotpādāt pañcaśikho gandharvaputraḥ saptagandharvasahasraparivṛto bhagavantaṃ yathāvad abhyarcya bhagavato vaiḍūryadaṇḍāṃ vīṇām upanayati sma | tataḥ supriyo gandharvarājo bhagavataḥ purastād vīṇām anuśrāvitum ārabdhaḥ | yata ekasyāṃ tantryāṃ sapta svarāṇi ekaviṃśatiṃ mūrcchanāś ca darśayitum ārabdhaḥ, yac chravaṇād rājā prasenajid anyatamaś ca mahājanakāyaḥ paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ | tato bhagavān api vaiḍūryadaṇḍāṃ vīṇām āśrāvitavān*: yata ekaikasyāṃ tantryām aneke svaraviśeṣā mūrcchanāś ca bahuprakārā darśitāḥ, te ca śūnyākāreṇaiva | idaṃ ca śarīraṃ vīṇāvad ādarśitavān*, svarān indriyavat, mūrcchanāś cittadhātuvat* | yac chravaṇād āvarjitaḥ supriyo gandharvarājo vīṇāṃ gandhakuṭyāṃ niryātya bhagavatsakāśe pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, for the purpose of benefiting those to be trained, produced a worldly thought: "Oh, if only <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the <s>gandharva</s> (celestial musician) prince, surrounded by seven thousand <s>gandharvas</s>, would come to my presence bringing a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) with a lapis lazuli neck!" The moment the thought arose, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, the <s>gandharva</s> prince, surrounded by seven thousand <s>gandharvas</s>, having properly worshipped the Blessed One, presented to the Blessed One a <s>vīṇā</s> with a lapis lazuli neck. Then the <s>gandharva</s> king <s>Supriya</s> began to play the <s>vīṇā</s> before the Blessed One. When he began to display seven notes and twenty-one <s>mūrcchanās</s> (melodic modulations) on a single string, upon hearing which King <s>Prasenajit</s> and a certain great multitude of people were struck with supreme amazement. Then the Blessed One too played the lapis lazuli <s>vīṇā</s>: on each single string he displayed manifold varieties of notes and <s>mūrcchanās</s> of many kinds, and these with the aspect of emptiness. And he demonstrated that this body is like a <s>vīṇā</s>, the notes are like the sense faculties, and the <s>mūrcchanās</s> are like the mental element. Upon hearing which, the <s>gandharva</s> king <s>Supriya</s> was won over, and having deposited his <s>vīṇā</s> in the perfumed chamber, he went forth into the homeless life in the presence of the Blessed One. Through his diligent effort, exertion, and striving, having understood this fivefold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) to be unstable, and having rejected all conditioned states by virtue of their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating,
[editorial page reference]

children.text: parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣākṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), he directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an arhat). He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion in all three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, equal-minded toward space and the palm of the hand, like a sandalwood log and an axe, one whose egg-shell had been split open by knowledge, who had attained knowledge, the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), and the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), who had turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor. He became worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the <s>devas</s> (gods) including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: tata āvarjitā devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā bhhagavacchāsane rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ | pañcānām api gāndharvikaśatānāṃ prītisaumanasyajātānām etad abhavat*: vayaṃ nīce karmaṇi vartāmahe kṛcchravṛttayaś ca | yan nu vayaṃ rājānaṃ vijñāpya bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ nagarapraveśenopanimantrayemahīti | yāvat tair gāndharvikair labdhānujñair bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho nagarapraveśenopanimantritaḥ | adhivāsitaṃ ca bhagavatā teṣāṃ gāndharvikāṇāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena | tatas tair gāndharvikair rājāmātyapaurajānapadasahāyaiḥ sarvā śrāvastī nagarī apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallā gandhodakapariṣiktā nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇā vicitradhūpadhūpitā puṣpavitānamaṇḍitā | te ca gāndharvikāḥ svayam eva vīṇām ādāya mṛdaṅgaveṇupaṇavādiviśeṣair upasthānaṃ cakruḥ, praṇītena cāhāreṇa bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ saṃtarpayāmāsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, having been won over, began to provide protection, defense, and guardianship for the teaching of the Blessed One. The five hundred musician guilds, having become filled with joy and delight, had this thought: "We are engaged in a lowly profession and live with difficulty. Let us petition the king and invite the Blessed One together with the <s>saṃgha</s> of disciples for a ceremonial entry into the city." Then those musicians, having obtained permission, invited the Blessed One together with the <s>saṃgha</s> of disciples for a ceremonial entry into the city. And the Blessed One consented to those musicians by silence. Then those musicians, together with the royal ministers, citizens, and countryfolk as helpers, cleared all of the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> of stones, gravel, and pebbles, sprinkled it with fragrant water, strewed it with various flowers, perfumed it with diverse incense, and adorned it with canopies of flowers. And those musicians themselves, taking up <s>vīṇās</s>, provided entertainment with various <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (drums), <s>veṇus</s> (flutes), <s>paṇavas</s> (small drums), and other instruments, and they satiated the Blessed One together with the <s>saṃgha</s> of disciples with excellent food.

children.text: tato bhagavān smitam akārṣīt* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One smiled. For it is the <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law) that whenever the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, produce a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue forth from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down having become cool, and in the cold hells they fall down having become warm. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think: "Have we, sirs, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?" For the purpose of generating faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth a magical creation. Seeing the creation, they think: "We have certainly not passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance; by his power our distinctive sufferings have been alleviated." Having generated faith in the creation, and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in those hells, they take rebirth among <s>devas</s> and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — proclaim "impermanent, suffering, empty, without self," and speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth! Renounce! Apply yourselves to the Buddha's teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_17.2 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut." (AVŚ 17.2)

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live heedfully,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_17.3 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering.' // AVŚ_17.3 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra (billion-world) universe, follow the <s>Bhagavān</s> from behind. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to prophesy about past deeds, they vanish behind him. If he wishes to prophesy about the future, they vanish in front of him. If he wishes to prophesy a birth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy an animal birth, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy a birth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy a human birth, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (lesser universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy a divine birth, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of supreme, perfect awakening, they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: And those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: 'A sheaf [of rays], variegated, adorned with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: has issued forth from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_17.4 ||
children.translated_text: as if by the sun at its rising.' // AVŚ_17.4 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he speaks [these] verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: 'Free from [the cycle of] arising, rid of wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme causes [of good] in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_17.5 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile as white as a conch, a lotus-stalk.' // AVŚ_17.5 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: 'Having yourself understood [this matter] at this very time by your heroic wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, <s>Jinendra</s> (Lord of Victors), for the listeners who are longing [to know] —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_17.6 ||
children.translated_text: O Bull among Sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen.' // AVŚ_17.6 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_17.7 || iti
children.translated_text: 'Not without reason do the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> (Fully Awakened), the Lords, steady as the ocean and the king of mountains, display a smile; those masses of people desire to hear about that for whose sake the Steadfast Ones display their smile.' // AVŚ_17.7 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda ebhir gāndharvikair mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | ete ānanda gāndharvikāḥ anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yathākālānugatāṃ pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya anāgate 'dhvani varṇasvarā nāma pratyekabuddhā bhaviṣyanti hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya | ayam eṣāṃ deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how these musicians have made such an offering to me?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, these musicians, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, having accumulated the <s>pratyeka</s> (solitary) awakening that is achieved in due course, shall in a future age become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Awakened Ones) named <s>Varṇasvara</s> (Of Beautiful Voice), compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, fond of secluded lodgings, each worthy of receiving offerings individually, [shining] for the world. This is [the fruit of] their <s>Dharma</s>-offering — namely, their act of faith in my presence.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayānāṃ chettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta bhagavatā kuśalamūlāni kṛtāni yeṣām ayam anubhāva iti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: The monks, their doubts aroused, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What roots of merit, Venerable Sir, were performed by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the effect of which is this [worship]?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur. By me were these deeds performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruits]? For, monks, deeds that are performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; but rather, in the very aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that are taken up, do deeds performed ripen — both wholesome and unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_17.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conjunction and the right time, they assuredly bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_17.1 //
'Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); *{variant: deeds even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>;}*

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani prabodhano nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | atha rājña udyānaṃ sarvakuśalasaṃpannaṃ babhūva | atha sa bhagavāṃs tad udyānaṃ praviśya rājānugrahārtham anyatamaṃ vṛkṣam upaniśritya niṣaṇṇaḥ | tataḥ saṃstaraṃ prajñapya tejodhātuṃ samāpannaḥ | atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ strīmayena tūryeṇa vādyamānenodyānaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | atha sa rājā tad udyānam anuvicaran dadarśa bhagavantaṃ prabodhanaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ prāsādikaṃ prasādanīyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ parameṇa cittadamavyupaśamena samanvāgataṃ suvarṇayūpam iva śriyā jvalantam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prasādajātaḥ sa rājā sāntaḥpuro vividhena vādyena vādyamānena bhagavantaṃ tataḥ samādheḥ prabodhayāmāsa, praṇītena cāhareṇa pratipāditavān*, anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtavān* ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Prabodhana</s> (The Awakener) arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He, wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital. Now the king's garden was endowed with all excellences. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, entering that garden, sat down leaning against a certain tree for the purpose of benefiting the king. Then, having prepared a seat, he entered the attainment of the fire element. Then a king, a consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s>, entered the garden accompanied by music played by women. As the king was wandering through the garden, he beheld the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Prabodhana</s> — inspiring, faith-producing, of tranquil mind, endowed with the supreme calm and subduing of the mind, blazing with splendor like a golden sacrificial post. Having seen him, the king, filled with faith, together with his inner household, accompanied by various instruments being played, awakened the <s>Bhagavān</s> from that meditative attainment, provided him with choice food, and made an aspiration for supreme, perfect awakening.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | yan mayā prabodhanasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūjā kṛtā, tenaiva hetunā idānīṃ mama gāndharvikair evaṃvidhaṃ satkāraḥ kṛtaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king — that was I. Because I worshipped the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Prabodhana</s>, for that very reason now the musicians have made such an offering to me. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

children.text: AVŚ_18 varadaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_18: <s>Varada</s> (The Boon-Giver). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | atha śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ pāradāriko maline karmaṇi vartate | sa rājapuruṣair gṛhītvā rājña upanāmitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta's</s> Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Now in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a certain adulterer was engaged in impure conduct. He was seized by the king's men and brought before the king.

children.text: tato rājñā aparādhika iti kṛtvā vadhya utsṛṣṭaḥ | sa rājapuruṣair nīlāmbaravasanair udyataśastraiḥ karavīramālābaddhakaṇṭheguṇo rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣv anuśrāvyamāṇo dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇa apanīyate ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, considering him an offender, released him to be executed. He was led out by the king's men, clad in blue garments, with weapons raised, a garland of <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) flowers bound about his neck, being proclaimed throughout the streets, lanes, crossroads, and intersections, and taken out through the southern gate of the city.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrva{vihāra}samāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Meanwhile — for there is nothing unknown, unseen, uncomprehended, or ununderstood by <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>.
