It is indeed the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, of singular protection, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three means of discipline, who have crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, long practiced in the four means of conversion, who have abandoned the five [negative] factors, who have transcended the five destinations, endowed with the six factors, who have fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the seven factors of awakening, who point out the eightfold path, skilled in the nine successive attainments, empowered with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who surpass a hundred <s>Śakras</s> in authority — three times at night and three times during the day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye they survey the world, and knowledge-and-vision operates: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into a narrow place? Who has fallen into difficulty, distress, and a narrow place? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who gravitates toward the lower realms? Whom should I, having rescued from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, should I extend a hand to pull them out? Whom, deprived of noble wealth, should I establish in the sovereignty of noble wealth? Whose eyes, covered by the film of ignorance, should I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? Whose unplanted roots of merit should I plant? Whose planted ones should I ripen? Whose ripened ones should I liberate?' And he declares:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its bounds,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_18.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the time for those to be trained, his calves.' // AVŚ_18.1 //

children.text: atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | dadarśa sa puruṣo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam śītyānuvañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya bhagavantam idam avocat*: varāho 'smi bhagavan*, iṣṭaṃ me jīvitaṃ prayaccheti | tato bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate: gaccha ānanda rājānaṃ prasenajitam* | vada: anuprayaccha me etaṃ puruṣam*, pravrājayāmīti | athāyuṣmān ānando yena rājā prasenajit kauśalas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ kauśalaṃ bhagavadvacanenovāca: anujānīhi, bhagavān etaṃ puruṣaṃ pravrājayatīti | bhavyarūpa iti viditvā rājñā prasenajitkauśalenānujñātaḥ | sa bhagavatā pravrājita upasaṃpaditaś ca | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣākṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. That man beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him, falling at the feet of the Blessed One, he said: 'I am a condemned man, Blessed One; grant me the gift of my life!' Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, to King <s>Prasenajit</s>. Tell him: "Hand over this man to me; I shall ordain him."' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>. Having approached, he spoke to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> on behalf of the Blessed One: 'Give your permission; the Blessed One will ordain this man.' Knowing him to be of suitable appearance, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> gave permission. He was ordained by the Blessed One and admitted to full ordination. And by striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this very wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> with its five hazards as unstable, having overcome all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating, through the abandonment of all defilements he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in all three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, equanimous as the sky and the palm of the hand, like sandalwood to the axe [that cuts it], his eggshell of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the knowledges, superknowledges, and analytical insights, turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor. He became one worthy of worship, veneration, and salutation by gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayānāṃ chettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavatā sarvaṃ cintitamātraṃ samṛdhyatīti | bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu
children.translated_text: The monks, filled with curiosity, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that everything the Blessed One merely thinks is accomplished!' The Blessed One said: 'It was by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in former

children.text: jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: lives that deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur. By me these deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_18.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_18.1 //
'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani indradhvajo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | tasyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ brāhmaṇo vedavedāṅgapārago rājño 'grāsanikaḥ | athendradhvajaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya tāṃ rājadhānīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | adrākṣīt sa brāhmaṇa indradhvajaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyaṃjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar mūlanikṛtta iva drumo bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatyovāca: vāraho 'smi sugata, niṣīdatu bhagavān agrāsana iti | atha bhagavān indradhvajaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tasyānugrahārtham agrāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | agrāsane niṣaṇṇaś cendradhvajaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tena brāhmaṇena padaśatena stutaḥ, praṇītena cāhareṇa pratipāditaḥ, anuttarāyāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam* | taddhaitukaṃ yāvad āvarjitā rājāmatyapaurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'In the distant past, monks, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Indradhvaja</s> (Banner of Indra) arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He, wandering through the countryside on a teaching tour, arrived at a certain royal capital. In that capital a Brahmin, who had mastered the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, was the king's chief dining-companion. Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradhvaja</s>, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered that capital for alms. That Brahmin beheld the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradhvaja</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him, falling at the Blessed One's feet like a tree cut at the root, he said: "I am a condemned man, <s>Sugata</s>; let the Blessed One sit in the chief seat." Then the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradhvaja</s>, for the sake of his benefit, sat in the chief seat. Having sat in the chief seat, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Indradhvaja</s> was praised by that Brahmin with a hundred verses, provided with fine food, and a resolve toward supreme perfect awakening was made. As a result, the king, ministers, and citizens were won over.'

children.text: tat kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena brāhmaṇo babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | yan me indradhvajasya tathāgatasya pūjā kṛtā, taddhaitukaṃ ca me saṃsāre anantaṃ sukham anubhūtam* | api yac cintayāmi, yat prārthaye, tat sarvaṃ samṛdhyati | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the Brahmin — that was I. Since I worshipped the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Indradhvaja</s>, as a result I have experienced endless happiness in the cycle of rebirth. Moreover, whatever I think, whatever I desire — all that is accomplished. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_19 kāśikavastram* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_19: The Cloth of <s>Kāśī</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | yadā rājñā bimbisāreṇānekaprāṇiśatasahasraparivāreṇa satyāni dṛṣṭāni, tadā tena kṛtapratyupakārasaṃdarśanārthaṃ buddhapūjāsaṃvartanārthaṃ gṛhavistarasaṃdarśanārthaṃ buddhotpādabahumānasaṃjananārthaṃ ca bhagavān
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. When King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, together with a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of living beings, had realized the truths, then he — for the purpose of demonstrating his gratitude, for the purpose of promoting worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, for the purpose of displaying the abundance of his household, and for the purpose of generating esteem for the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> — the Blessed One,

children.text: saśrāvakasaṃgho rājakule bhaktenopanimantritaḥ, māgadhakānāṃ ca paurāṇām ājñā dattā: bhagavato nagarapraveśe puṣpagandhamālyavilepanaiḥ pūjā kartavyā, sarvaṃ ca rājagṛhaṃ nagaram apagatapāṣāṇasarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpayitavyam*, nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇam ucchritadhvajapatākaṃ yāvac ca veṇuvanaṃ yāvac ca rājagṛham*, atrāntarā sarvo mārgo vicitrair vastrāir ācchādayitavya iti | amātyaiś ca sarvam anuṣṭhitam* | tato rājā bimbisāraḥ svayam eva bhagavato mūrdhni śataśalākaṃ chatraṃ dhārayati, pariśeṣāḥ paurāḥ bhikṣusahasrasya ||
children.translated_text: together with the community of disciples, was invited to a meal at the royal palace, and a command was given to the citizens of <s>Magadha</s>: 'At the Blessed One's entrance into the city, worship must be performed with flowers, fragrances, garlands, and unguents; the entire city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> must be prepared, cleared of stones, gravel, and rubble, strewn with various flowers, with raised banners and flags — from the <s>Veṇuvana</s> to <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the entire road in between must be covered with colorful cloths.' And all was carried out by the ministers. Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s> himself held a hundred-ribbed parasol over the Blessed One's head, while the remaining citizens [held parasols] for the thousand monks.

children.text: atha bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ śāntaḥ śāntaparivāro mukto muktaparivāra āśvasta āśvastaparivāro vinīto vinītaparivāro 'rhann arhatparivāro vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāro vṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛto gaja iva kalabhagaṇaparivṛtaḥ siṃha iva daṃṣṭrigaṇaparivṛto haṃsa iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛto suparṇīva pakṣigaṇaparivṛto vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ svaśva iva turagagaṇaparivṛtaḥ śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto deśika ivādhvagagaṇaparivṛtaḥ sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ śreṣṭhīva paurajanaparivṛtaḥ koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaś cakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaś candra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛto dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛto virūḍha iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛto virūpākṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛto dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivṛto vemacitrīvāsuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛto brahmā iva brahmakāyikaparivṛtaḥ stimita iva jalanidhiḥ sajala iva jaladharo vimada iva gajapatiḥ sudāntair indriyair asaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāro 'nekair āveṇikair buddhadharmaiḥ parivṛto bhagavāṃs tat puraṃ praviśati ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One — tamed, with a tamed retinue; peaceful, with a peaceful retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; comforted, with a comforted retinue; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with an <s>Arhat</s> retinue; free from passion, with a retinue free from passion; inspiring faith, with a retinue inspiring faith — like a bull surrounded by a herd of cows, like an elephant surrounded by a troop of young elephants, like a lion surrounded by a pack of fanged beasts, like a royal swan surrounded by a flock of geese, like a great bird (<s>Suparṇī</s>) surrounded by a flock of birds, like a preceptor surrounded by a group of students, like a fine horse surrounded by a herd of steeds, like a hero surrounded by a band of warriors, like a guide surrounded by a group of travelers, like a caravan-leader surrounded by a group of merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by the townsfolk, like a fortress-king surrounded by a council of ministers, like a <s>Cakravartin</s> surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by a host of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Gandharvas</s>, like <s>Virūḍha</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Nāgas</s>, like <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) surrounded by a host of <s>Yakṣas</s>, like <s>Vemacitri</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Asuras</s>, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by a host of the Thirty-three [gods], like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s> — like a tranquil ocean, like a rain-bearing cloud, like a musth-free lord of elephants — with well-tamed faculties, with an undisturbed deportment, surrounded by many unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the Blessed One entered that city.

children.text: yadā ca bhagavatā indrakīle pādo nyastaḥ, tadeyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitā | bhagavataḥ purapraveśe evaṃrūpāṇy adbhutāni bhavanty anyāni ca | tadyathā: saṃkṣiptāni viśālībhavanti, hastinaḥ krośanti aśvāś ca heṣante ṛṣabhā nardante gṛhagatāni vividhavādyabhāṇḍāni svayaṃ nadanti, andhāś cakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante, badhirāḥ śrotraṃ mūkāḥ pravyāharaṇasamarthā bhavanti, pariśiṣṭendriyavikalā indriyāṇi paripūrṇāni pratilabhante, madyamadākṣiptā vimadībhavanti, viṣapītā nirviṣībhavanti, anyonyavairiṇo maitrīṃ pratilabhante, gurviṇyaḥ svastinaḥ prajāyante, bandhanabaddhā vimucyante, adhanā dhanāni pratilabhante, āntarikṣāś ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā divyaṃ puṣpam utsṛjanti ||
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One placed his foot on the city threshold, this great earth trembled in six ways. At the Blessed One's entrance into the city, such wondrous marvels occur, among others: things that were contracted expand; elephants trumpet, horses neigh, bulls bellow; various musical instruments within the houses sound of themselves; the blind gain sight, the deaf gain hearing, the mute become able to speak; those deprived of other faculties regain them in full; those intoxicated with drink become sober; those who have consumed poison become free of poison; mutual enemies gain friendliness; pregnant women give birth safely; those bound in prison are released; the impoverished obtain wealth; and in the sky, gods, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> release divine flowers.

children.text: atha bhagavān evaṃvidhayā vibhūtyā rājakulaṃ praveṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | rājā ca bimbisāraḥ svayam eva bahirdvāraśālastho gośirṣacandanodakena pādyaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ pādau bhikṣusaṃghasya ca prākṣalayati | sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śatarasenāhāreṇa pratipādayāmāsa | bhuktavantaṃ kāśikavastrair ācchāditavān* | taddhaitukaṃ ca āvarjitā māgadhakāḥ paurāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, with such splendor, began to enter the royal palace. And King <s>Bimbisāra</s> himself, standing at the outer gate-hall, having taken foot-washing water of <s>gośīrṣa</s> sandalwood, washed the feet of the Blessed One and of the community of monks. Having ascertained that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, he served them with food of a hundred flavors. After [the Blessed One] had eaten, he covered [him] with cloths of <s>Kāśī</s>. As a result, the citizens of <s>Magadha</s> were won over.

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kutremāni bhagavatā kuśalamūlāni kṛtāni, yato bhagavata evaṃvidhā pūjā bhikṣusaṃghasya ceti |
children.translated_text: Then the monks, filled with curiosity, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'Where were these roots of merit of the Blessed One planted, such that there is this kind of worship for the Blessed One and the community of monks?'

children.text: bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca |
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'It was by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in former lives, that deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur. By me these deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_19.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_19.1 //
'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani kṣemaṃkaro nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ: kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann asmākaṃ rājadhānīm anuprāpta iti | śrutvā ca mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgataḥ | yena bhagavān kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya kṣemaṃkarasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktam kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati | atha sa rājā labdhaprasādaḥ kṣemaṃkaraṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ rājakule nimantrya śatarasenāhāreṇa pratipādayāmāsa | śatasāhasreṇa ca vastreṇācchādayāmāsa | parinirvṛtasya ca samantayojanaṃ stūpaṃ kāritavān krośam uccatvena ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> (Bringer of Security) arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He, wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital. A king, a consecrated <s>Kṣatriya</s>, heard: 'The Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, has arrived at our royal capital.' Having heard, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, he approached the Blessed One, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>. Having approached, having bowed with his head at the feet of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, he sat to one side. To the king, the consecrated <s>Kṣatriya</s>, seated to one side, the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> gave instruction in the teachings conducive to awakening. Then that king, having gained faith, invited the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> to the royal household and served him with a meal of a hundred <s>rasas</s> (flavors). And he covered him with a hundred thousand garments. And after [the <s>Buddha</s>'s] <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, he had a <s>stūpa</s> built extending one <s>yojana</s> on all sides, and one <s>krośa</s> in height.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | yan mayā kṣemaṃkarasya samyaksaṃbuddhasyaivaṃvidhāṃ pūjā kṛtā, tena mayā saṃsāre 'nantaṃ sukham anubhūtam* | idānīṃ tenaiva hetunā rājā bimbisāreṇāpi tathāgatasya me evaṃvidhā pūjā kṛtā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king — that was I. By me, such worship was performed for the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>. By that deed of mine, I have experienced infinite happiness in the cycle of rebirth. And now, by that very cause, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> too has performed such worship for me, the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall revere, honor, respect, and worship the Teacher. Having revered, honored, respected, and worshiped the Teacher, we shall dwell in dependence upon him." Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_20 divyabhojanam* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 20 — <s>Divyabhojana</s> (Divine Food). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | tatra anyataraḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrels' Feeding Ground). There, a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, whose wealth equaled that of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera),
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 51]

children.text: vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī tīrthyābhiprasannaś ca | sa āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanenāvarjitaḥ śāsane ca avatārito bhagavaty atyartham abhiprasannaḥ | sa ca gṛhapatir udārādhimuktaḥ | tenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana uktaḥ: sahāyo me bhava, icchāmi bhagavataḥ pūjāṃ kartum iti | adhivāsayaty āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas tasya gṛhapates tūṣṇībhāvena, athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas taṃ gṛhapatim ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavantam idam avocat: ayaṃ bhadanta gṛhapatir ākāṅkṣati bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojayitum* | tad asya bhagavān adhivāsayed anukampām upādāyeti | adhivāsayati bhagavāṃs tasya gṛhapates tūṣṇībhāvnea | atha sa gṛhapatir bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā śatarasam āhāraṃ samudānayati, puṣpagandhamālyavilepanāni ca | āyuṣmatāpi mahāmaudgalyāyanena śakro devendro 'dhīṣṭaḥ: kriyatām asya gṛhapater upasaṃhāra iti | tataḥ śakreṇa devendreṇa veṇuvanaṃ nandavanam abhinirmitam*, airāvaṇasupratiṣṭhitasadṛśāni ca nāgasahasrāṇi # # # [gap?] vālavyajanena vījayanti | supriyapañcaśikhatumbaruprabhṛtīni (Speyer: ŚtumburuŚ) cānekāni gandharvasahasrāṇy upanītāni ye vicitrair vādyaviśeṣair vādyaṃ kurvanti, divyaṃ ca sudhābhojanam* | tataḥ sa gṛhapatir divyamānuṣair upakaraṇair bhagavantam upasthāya sarvāṅgeṇa bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇīdhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti ||
children.translated_text: who rivaled <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth — was devoted to the heterodox teachers. He was won over by the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> and brought into the teaching, and became exceedingly devoted to the Blessed One. That householder was of lofty aspiration. He said to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Be my helper — I wish to perform worship for the Blessed One.' The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> consented to the householder by his silence. Then the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, taking that householder along, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and worshiped the Blessed One's feet with his head, he sat to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'This householder, Venerable Sir, wishes to feed the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples. May the Blessed One consent, out of compassion.' The Blessed One consented to the householder by his silence. Then the householder, knowing the Blessed One's consent by his silence, prepared a meal of a hundred <s>rasas</s> (flavors), along with flowers, fragrances, garlands, and unguents. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> also requested <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>: 'Provide assistance to this householder.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, transformed the <s>Veṇuvana</s> into a likeness of the <s>Nandana</s> garden, and [conjured] thousands of <s>Nāgas</s> resembling those stationed upon <s>Airāvaṇa</s> # # # [gap?] who fan with yak-tail whisks. And many thousands of <s>Gandharvas</s> — <s>Supriya</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, <s>Tumburu</s>, and others — were brought, who performed music with various and exquisite instruments; and divine <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia) food [was provided]. Then that householder, having served the Blessed One with divine and human provisions, prostrated himself with his whole body at the Blessed One's feet and began to make an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, may I, in a blind world without a guide, without a leader, become a <s>Buddha</s> — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates those who are not liberated, who gives comfort to those who are not comforted, who brings to complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya gṛhapater hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutā nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the chain of causes and the chain of actions of that householder, manifested a smile. It is indeed the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, manifest a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward and some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. It occurs to them: 'Have we perhaps departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation. Seeing the emanation, they think: 'Indeed, we have neither departed from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having gained faith in the emanation and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in that hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels of the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 52]

children.text: brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Non-self!' and recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_20.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!" // <s>AVŚ</s> 20.1 //

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_20.2 || iti
children.translated_text:
"He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,
having abandoned the cycle of births, shall make an end of suffering." // <s>AVŚ</s> 20.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire three-thousand-fold great-thousand world-system, follow behind the Blessed One. If the Blessed One wishes to prophesy past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind the Blessed One. If he wishes to prophesy future events, they disappear in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in a hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they disappear at the heel. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a hungry ghost (<s>preta</s>), they disappear at the big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they disappear at the knees. If he wishes to prophesy the sovereignty of a powerful universal monarch, they disappear in the left palm. If he wishes to prophesy universal monarchy (<s>cakravartin</s>), they disappear in the right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a god, they disappear at the navel. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappear at the mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūṣṇīṣe 'ntarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared at the Blessed One's <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A sheaf of a thousand various, multicolored hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: emitted from within your mouth —

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the quarters in all directions were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_20.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the sun at its rising — // <s>AVŚ</s> 20.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recited verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, who are beyond birth, free from despondency and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme causes in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: they do not without reason display

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_20.4 ||
children.translated_text: a smile white as a conch-shell or lotus-stalk, those Victors who have conquered their foes." // <s>AVŚ</s> 20.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā *{adhigatya}*
children.translated_text: "Having yourself comprehended this moment with the understanding of a hero, O <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager, O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, Lord of Victors —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with firm, supreme, auspicious words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_20.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen." // <s>AVŚ</s> 20.5 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 53]

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_20.6 || iti
children.translated_text:
"The Fully Awakened Ones, the Lords, possessing the steadfastness of the mountain-king of the salt sea,
do not display a smile without cause.
For whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile —
those multitudes of people desire to hear that." // <s>AVŚ</s> 20.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena gṛhapatinā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda gṛhapatir anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya mahākaruṇāparibhāvitāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya divyānnado nāma samyaksaṃbuddhā bhaviṣyanti daśabhir balaiś caturbhir vaiśāradyais tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ | etac ca prakaraṇaṃ rājā bimbisāro māgadhakāś ca paricārakāḥ śrutvā paraṃ vismayam āpannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this householder has performed such worship toward me?' 'Indeed, Venerable Sir.' 'This householder, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, having accumulated the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) accumulated over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) pervaded by great compassion, shall become a Fully Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Divyānnada</s> (Giver of Divine Food), endowed with the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the three unique bases of mindfulness, and great compassion. This is his gift of <s>Dharma</s>: the serene faith of his mind directed toward me.' And King <s>Bimbisāra</s> and the Magadhan attendants, having heard this account, were filled with the utmost amazement.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhagavan yāvad anena gṛhapatinā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho divyamānuṣībhir ṛddhibhir abhyarcita iti || bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having doubts arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "Behold, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how much the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>śrāvakasaṃgha</s> (community of disciples) has been honored by this householder with divine and human supernatural powers!" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It is by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, that formerly in other births these <s>karmas</s> (actions) were performed and accumulated, their provisions obtained, their conditions matured, standing present like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. By me were these <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated — who else would experience their results? O <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, <s>karmas</s> performed ripen only in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), whether wholesome or unwholesome;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_20.1 ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained the right combination and the right time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. || AVŚ_20.1 ||
<s>Karmas</s> (actions) do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (eons). *{also: karmas even in hundreds of kalpas.|}*

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani pūrṇo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | atha pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamāṃ rājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ | aśrauṣīd rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ: pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikāṃ carann asmākaṃ rājadhānīm anuprāpta iti | śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgato yena bhagavān pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya pūrṇasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarakair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati | atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pūrṇaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ traimāsyaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upanimantritavān* | adhivāsitaṃ ca pūrṇena samyaksaṃbuddhena rājñas tūṣṇībhāvena | atha rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ pūrṇasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā traimāsyaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upasthāpya bhagavato ratnamayapratimāṃ kārayitvā buddhaharṣaṃ kāritavān*, yatrānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair mahāprasādo labdhaḥ | tathetutatpratyayaṃ ca te parinirvṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Pūrṇa</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at a certain royal capital. A king, a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior-noble) anointed on the head, heard: "The <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside, has arrived at our royal capital." Having heard, he, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s> and sat down to one side. The <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s> instructed the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, seated to one side, in the <s>dharmas</s> (teachings) that lead to awakening. Then the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, invited the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s> together with the <s>śrāvakasaṃgha</s> for three months with robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick. And the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s> consented by silence to the king. Then the king, the <s>kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, understanding the consent of the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s> by his silence, served him for three months with robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick, had a jeweled image of the <s>Bhagavān</s> made, and organized a <s>buddhaharṣa</s> (Buddha-rejoicing festival), at which many hundreds of thousands of beings gained great faith. And through that cause and condition they attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation).

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | yan mayā pūrṇasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya tādṛśī pūjā kṛtā, tena me saṃsāre 'nantaṃ sukham anubhūtam*, tenaiva ca hetunā tathāgatasya ca me śreṣṭhinā śakreṇa ca īdṛśī pūjā kṛtā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who at that time, at that occasion, was the king — that was I. Because I performed such worship of the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> <s>Pūrṇa</s>, I experienced endless happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), and by that very cause such worship was performed for me, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by the merchant-chief and by <s>Śakra</s>. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, you should train thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, we will revere him, we will respect him, we will worship him. Having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Teacher, we will dwell relying upon him.' Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, should you train.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: tṛtīyo vargaḥ |
children.translated_text: The third <s>varga</s> (chapter).

children.text: tasyoddānam*:
children.translated_text: Its <s>uddāna</s> (summary verse):

children.text: candano hy atha padmaś ca cakraṃ daśaśirās tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Candana</s> and then <s>Padma</s>, <s>Cakra</s>, <s>Daśaśiras</s> likewise,

children.text: sūkṣmatvak* śītadīptaś ca nāvikā gandhamādanaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Sūkṣmatvak</s>, <s>Śītadīpta</s>, <s>Nāvikā</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>,

children.text: nirmalo valgusvaraś ca vargo bhavati sattamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nirmala</s> and <s>Valgusvara</s> — this is the seventh <s>varga</s> (chapter).

children.text: AVŚ_21 candanaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_21 <s>Candana</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran gaṅgātīram anuprāptaḥ | tena khalu punaḥ samayena gaṅgātīrasya nātidūre stūpam avarugṇaṃ vātātapābhyāṃ pariśīrṇam* | bhikṣubhir dṛṣṭvā bhagavān pṛṣṭaḥ kasya bhagavann ayaṃ stūpa iti | bhagavān āha: candano nāma pratyekabuddho babhūva, tasyeti | bhikṣava ūcuḥ: kuto bhagavaṃś candanasya pratyekabuddhasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ceti | bhagavān āha: icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śrotuṃ yathā candanasya pratyekabuddhasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ca? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, respected, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchant-chiefs, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents) — thus worshipped by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines and provisions for the sick, together with the <s>śrāvakasaṃgha</s>, wandering on a tour through the <s>Magadha</s> country, arrived at the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Now at that time, not far from the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there was a <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary monument) that was crumbling, decayed by wind and sun. The <s>bhikṣus</s>, having seen it, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Whose is this <s>stūpa</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "There was a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) named <s>Candana</s>; it is his." The <s>bhikṣus</s> asked: "What, <s>Bhagavān</s>, was the origin and the establishment of the name of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> <s>Candana</s>?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Do you wish to hear, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the origin and the establishment of the name of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> <s>Candana</s>?" "Yes, <s>Bhadanta</s> (Venerable One)." "Then listen, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak."

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati | so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate tadyathā: ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ | sahajāḥ sahadhārmikā nityānubaddhā api devatā āyācate | asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | tac ca naivam* | yady evam abhaviṣyad ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ | api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | katameṣāṃ trayāṇām* | mātāpitarāu raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau, mātā {ca} kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī, gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati | eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati | tasya codyāne mahāpadmini | tatra padmam atipramāṇaṃ jātam* | tad divase divase vardhate na tu phullati | tata ārāmikeṇa rājñe niveditam* | rajñā uktaḥ parīkṣyatām etat padmam iti | yāvad apareṇa samayena sūryodaye tat padmaṃ vikasitam* | tasya ca padmasya karṇikāyāṃ dārakaḥ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvāvasthitaḥ, abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling the kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, with quarrels, conflicts, disputes, and tumults pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. A righteous king, a <s>dharmarāja</s> (king of righteousness), he ruled the kingdom by <s>dharma</s>. He was childless, yet longing for a son, and he prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other special deities, namely: garden deities, forest deities, crossroads deities, intersection deities, deities who accept <s>bali</s> (offerings), as well as deities who are innate, co-religious, and ever-attendant. Now there is this common saying in the world that sons and daughters are born through the act of praying. But that is not so. For if it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just as a <s>cakravartin</s> (wheel-turning monarch) king has. Rather, it is from the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. Which three? The mother and father are passionate and have come together, the mother is healthy and in her fertile period, and a <s>gandharva</s> (being seeking rebirth) is present. From the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born. He continued devoted to praying. Now in his garden there was a great lotus pond. There an extraordinarily large lotus appeared. It grew day by day but did not bloom. Then the garden-keeper reported this to the king. The king said: "Examine this lotus." After some time, at sunrise, that lotus opened. And on the pericarp of that lotus, a boy was seated cross-legged — handsome, good-looking,

children.text: prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaś chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhur vistīrṇalalāṭaḥ uccaghoṣaḥ saṃgatabrūs tuṅganāsaḥ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtagātro 'śītyānuvyañjanair virājitagātraḥ | tasya mukhāt padmagandho vāti śarīrāc ca candanagandhaḥ | tata ārāmikeṇa rājñe niveditam* | tato rājā sāmātyaḥ sāntaḥpuraś ca tad udyānaṃ gataḥ | sahadarśanāt tena dārakeṇa rājā saṃbhāṣitaḥ: ehi tāta, ahaṃ te 'putrasya putra iti | tato rājā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita uvāca: evam eva putra yathā vadasīti | tato rājā padminīm avagāhya taṃ dārakaṃ padmakarṇikāyāṃ gṛhītvā pāṇitale sthāpitavān* | yatra yatra sa dārakaḥ pādau sthāpayati, tatra tatra padmāni prādurbhavanti | tatas tasya candana iti nāma kṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: pleasing, fair-complexioned, golden-hued, with an umbrella-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, a deep voice, joined eyebrows, a prominent nose, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being), his limbs resplendent with eighty secondary characteristics. From his mouth wafted the fragrance of lotuses, and from his body the fragrance of sandalwood. Then the garden-keeper reported this to the king. Then the king, together with his ministers and the women of the inner palace, went to that garden. Upon seeing him, the boy addressed the king: "Come, father — I am the son of you who are sonless." Then the king, overjoyed and delighted, said: "Just so, my son, as you say!" Then the king waded into the lotus pond, took the boy from the lotus pericarp, and placed him on the palm of his hand. Wherever that boy set his feet, there lotuses appeared. Therefore they gave him the name <s>Candana</s> (Sandalwood).

children.text: yadā candano dārako 'nupūrveṇa mahān saṃvṛttaḥ, tadā nāgarai rājā vijñaptaḥ: ihāsmākaṃ deva nagaraparva pratyupasthitam* | tad arhati devaś candanaṃ kumāram utsraṣṭam* (Speyer: utsraṣṭum)| asmābhiḥ saha parvānubhaviṣyati, padmaiś ca sarvam adhiṣṭhānam alaṃkariṣyatīti | rājāha: evam astv iti | tataś candanaḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣito 'mātyaputraparivṛto vividhair vādyair vādyamānai rājakulād bahir upayāti nagaraparva pratyanubhavitum* | tatra tasya gacchataḥ padavinyāse padavinyāse padmāni prādurbhavanti darśanīyāni manoramāṇi ca | tāny arkaraśmibhiḥ spṛṣṭamātrāṇi mlāyanti śuṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: When the boy <s>Candana</s> had gradually grown up, the citizens petitioned the king: "Here, Your Majesty, our city festival is at hand. May Your Majesty be pleased to release Prince <s>Candana</s>. He will enjoy the festival together with us, and will adorn the entire ground with lotuses." The king said: "So be it." Then <s>Candana</s>, adorned with all ornaments, surrounded by the sons of ministers, with various musical instruments being played, went forth from the royal palace to enjoy the city festival. There, at each step as he walked, lotuses appeared — beautiful and delightful. But as soon as they were touched by the rays of the sun, they wilted and withered.

children.text: atha tasya śuddhasatvasya kalyāṇāśayasya pūrvabuddhāvaropitakuśalamūlasya taddarśanād yoniśo manasikāra utpannaḥ: yathemāni padmāni utpannamātrāṇi śobhante, arkaraśmiparitāpitāni mlāyanti śuṣyanti, evam etad api śarīram iti | tasyaivaṃ cintayatas tulayata uparīkṣamāṇasya saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyadharmā abhimukhībhūtāḥ | te tasyaiva janakāyasya madhye sthitena pratyekabodhiḥ sākṣātkṛtā | yāvac chuddhāvāsakāyikair devais tasmai kāṣāyāṇy upanāmitāni | tāni ca prāvṛtya gaganatalam utpatitaḥ, vicitrāṇi ca prātihāryāṇi kartuṃ pravṛttaḥ, yaddarśanād rājñāmātyanaigamasahāyena mahān prasādaḥ pratilabdho vicitrāṇi ca kuśalamūlāny avaropitāni | bhagavān āha: ataś candanasya pratyekabuddhasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ceti ||
children.translated_text: Then, for that being of pure nature, of virtuous disposition, with roots of merit planted under former <s>Buddhas</s>, from seeing that, a proper mental reflection arose: "Just as these lotuses are beautiful the moment they appear, yet when heated by the rays of the sun they wilt and wither — so too is this very body." As he thus reflected, considered, and examined, the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening) became manifest before him. Standing right there in the midst of that crowd of people, he realized <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening). Thereupon the gods of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) heavens offered him saffron-colored robes. Having donned them, he flew up into the sky and proceeded to perform various miraculous displays, at the sight of which the king together with his ministers, townspeople, and companions gained great faith, and various roots of merit were planted. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Such was the origin and the establishment of the name of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> <s>Candana</s>."

children.text: bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta candanena pratyekabuddhena karmāṇi kṛtāni yenāsya śarīraṃ sugandhi tīkṣṇendriyaś ceti | bhagavān āha: kāśyape bhagavati pravrajito babhūva, tatrānena keśanakhastūpe gandhāvasekaḥ kṛtaḥ, puṣpāṇi cāvaropitāni, pratyekabodhau cānena mārgo bhāvitaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "What <s>karmas</s> (actions), <s>Bhadanta</s> (Venerable One), did the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> <s>Candana</s> perform, that his body was fragrant and his faculties were keen?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> he had gone forth as a renunciant, and there he anointed a <s>stūpa</s> of hair and nail relics with fragrant paste, offered flowers, and cultivated the path toward <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening). Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, you should train thus: 'We will honor the Teacher, we will revere him, we will respect him, we will worship him. Having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped the Teacher, we will dwell relying upon him.' Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, should you train."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_22 padmaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_22 <s>Padma</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | ācaritam etan madhyadeśe yadārāmikāḥ padmāny ādāya vīthīṃ gatvā vikrīṇate | atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | anyatamā ca strī dārakaṃ svabhujābhyām ādāya vīthīm avatīrṇā | dadarśa ca sa dārako buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prasādajātaḥ sahasā bāhum abhiprasārya ārāmikasakāśāt padmaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavato mūrdhni prakṣiptavān* | tatas tat padmaṃ śakaṭaśakramātraṃ (Speyer: śakaṭacakramātraṃ) bhūtvopari vihāyasi sthitam* | bhagavantaṃ ca gacchantam anugacchati, tiṣṭhantaṃ tiṣṭhati | tato bhagavatā padmarāgasadṛśā prabhā utsṛṣṭā sakalā śrāvastī avabhāsitā, taddhaitukaṃ ca rājāmātyapaurāḥ āvarjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta's</s> Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. It was the custom in the middle country that gardeners would take lotuses and go to the street to sell them. Now the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dressed in the forenoon and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. A certain woman, carrying a child in her arms, had descended into the street. That child saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with the eighty minor characteristics, embellished with a fathom-wide halo, of surpassing brilliance exceeding a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him, filled with faith, he suddenly stretched out his arm and, snatching a lotus from a gardener, cast it at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> head. That lotus, becoming the size of a cart-wheel, remained suspended in the sky above. It followed the <s>Bhagavān</s> as he walked, and stood still when he stood still. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> emitted a radiance resembling the color of rubies, illuminating all of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and by that cause the king, ministers, and citizens were won over.

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitam upadarśitam* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile. It is a natural law that whenever <s>Bhagavāns</s> display a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue forth from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward proceed to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — and in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the specific torments of those beings are alleviated. This thought arises in them: 'Have we departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' For the purpose of generating faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth a magical creation. Having seen the magical creation, they think thus: 'We have indeed not departed from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is an unprecedented being, by whose power our specific torments have been alleviated.' Having set their minds with faith upon the magical creation, and having exhausted the karma that was to be experienced in hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those [rays] that go upward proceed to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' — and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: 'Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_22.1 ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant [shakes off] a reed hut.' // AVŚ_22.1 //

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'Whoever in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live heedfully,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_22.2 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering.' // AVŚ_22.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra (billion-world) universe, follow the <s>Bhagavān</s> from behind. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to prophesy about past deeds, they vanish behind him. If he wishes to prophesy about the future, they vanish in front of him. If he wishes to prophesy a birth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy an animal birth, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to prophesy a birth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to prophesy a human birth, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>balacakravartin</s> (lesser universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to prophesy sovereignty as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy a divine birth, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (disciple's awakening), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy the attainment of supreme, perfect awakening, they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: And those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: 'A sheaf [of rays], variegated, adorned with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: has issued forth from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_22.3 ||
children.translated_text: as if by the sun at its rising.' // AVŚ_22.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he speaks [these] verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: 'Free from [the cycle of] arising, rid of wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme causes [of good] in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_22.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile as white as a conch, a lotus-stalk.' // AVŚ_22.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: 'Having yourself understood [this matter] at this very time by your heroic wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, <s>Jinendra</s> (Lord of Victors), for the listeners who are longing [to know] —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_22.5 ||
children.translated_text: O Bull among Sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen.' // AVŚ_22.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_22.6 || iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Not without reason do the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> (Fully Awakened), the Lords, steady as the ocean and the king of mountains, display a smile; those masses of people desire to hear about that for whose sake the Steadfast Ones display their smile.' // AVŚ_22.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena dārakeṇa prasādajātena tathāgatasya padmaṃ kṣiptam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda dārako 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca pañcadaśa kalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati | divyamānuṣasukham anubhūya padmottaro nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: ya buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how this child, filled with faith, cast a lotus at the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, this child, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this gift of <s>Dharma</s>-offerings, for fifteen <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) shall not fall into the lower realms. Having experienced divine and human happiness, he shall become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Awakened One) named <s>Padmottara</s> (Supreme Lotus). This is [the fruit of] his <s>Dharma</s>-offering — namely, his act of faith in my presence. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall make offerings to <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and disciples." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

children.text: AVŚ_23 cakram* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_23: The Wheel. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | rājagṛhe 'nyatamaḥ sārthavāho mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | tasya bhāryā yauvanavatī | sā svāmino 'rthe utkaṇṭhati paritapyati, na cāsyā bhartā āgacchati | tayā nārāyaṇasya praṇipatya pratijñātam*: yadi me śīghram āgacchati, ahaṃ te sauvarṇacakraṃ pradāsyāmīti | tatas tasyāḥ svāmī svastikṣemābhyāṃ mahāsamudrād aśu pratyāgataḥ | tayā sauvarṇacakraṃ kāritam* | sā dāsīgaṇaparivṛtā cakram ādāya gandhadhūpapuṣpaṃ ca, devakulaṃ saṃpratisthitā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), in the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding-ground). In <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a certain caravan-leader had descended into the great ocean. His wife was in the bloom of youth. She was anxious and distressed on account of her husband, but he did not return. She prostrated before <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and made a vow: 'If he returns quickly, I shall give you a golden wheel.' Then her husband returned swiftly and safely from the great ocean. She had a golden wheel fashioned. Surrounded by her troop of maidservants, taking the wheel along with fragrances, incense, and flowers, she set out for the temple.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Meanwhile — for there is nothing unknown, unseen, uncomprehended, or ununderstood by <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>.
