It is indeed the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, of singular protection, dwelling in calm and insight, skilled in the three means of discipline, who have crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, long practiced in the four means of conversion, who have abandoned the five [negative] factors, who have transcended the five destinations, endowed with the six factors, who have fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the seven factors of awakening, who point out the eightfold path, skilled in the nine successive attainments, empowered with the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who surpass a hundred <s>Śakras</s> in authority — three times at night and three times during the day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye they survey the world, and knowledge-and-vision operates: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into a narrow place? Who has fallen into difficulty, distress, and a narrow place? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who gravitates toward the lower realms? Whom should I, having rescued from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of desires, should I extend a hand to pull them out? Whom, deprived of noble wealth, should I establish in the sovereignty of noble wealth? Whose eyes, covered by the film of ignorance, should I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? Whose unplanted roots of merit should I plant? Whose planted ones should I ripen? Whose ripened ones should I liberate?' And he declares:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its bounds,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_23.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the time for those to be trained, his calves.' // AVŚ_23.1 //

children.text: paśyati bhagavān: iyaṃ dārikā maddarśanāt pratyekabodheḥ kuśalamūlāny avaropayiṣyatīti | tataḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | athāsau dārikā dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc ca labdhaprasādā bhavati sauvarṇacakraṃ kṣeptam ārabdhaḥ | tataś ceṭikayā vāryate: nāyaṃ nārāyaṇa iti sā vāryamāṇāpi tīvraprasādā āvarjitamānasā buddhasya bhagavata upari sauvarṇacakraṃ nikṣipya gandhamālyaṃ ca dattavatī ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One perceived: 'This girl, upon seeing me, will plant the roots of merit for <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening).' Then, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken up his bowl and robe, surrounded and attended by the community of monks, he entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Then that girl beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a fathom-wide aura of light, surpassing in radiance a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious in every way. And the moment she saw him, she was filled with faith and began to throw a golden wheel [at him as an offering]. Then a maidservant tried to stop her: 'This is not <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!' But though restrained, she, with intense faith and captivated mind, cast the golden wheel upon the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, and offered a garland of fragrant flowers as well.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 60]

children.text: tato bhagavān smitaṃ dadarśitum* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ taṃ nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One displayed a smile. It is indeed the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, manifest a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward and some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. It occurs to them: 'Have we perhaps departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation. Seeing the emanation, they think: 'Indeed, we have neither departed from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having gained faith in the emanation and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in that hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels of the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Non-self!' and recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_23.2 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!" // <s>AVŚ</s> 23.2 //

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: "He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_23.3 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of births, shall make an end of suffering." // <s>AVŚ</s> 23.3 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire three-thousand-fold great-thousand world-system, follow behind the Blessed One. If the Blessed One wishes to prophesy past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind the Blessed One. If he wishes to prophesy future <s>karma</s>, they disappear in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in a hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they disappear at the heel. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a hungry ghost (<s>preta</s>), they disappear at the big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they disappear at the knees. If he wishes to prophesy the sovereignty of a powerful universal monarch, they disappear in the left palm. If he wishes to prophesy universal monarchy (<s>cakravartin</s>), they disappear in the right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a god, they disappear at the navel. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappear at the mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared at the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A sheaf of a thousand various, multicolored hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: emitted from within your mouth —

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the quarters in all directions were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_23.4 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the sun at its rising — // <s>AVŚ</s> 23.4 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 61]

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recited verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, who are beyond birth, free from despondency and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme causes in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: they do not without reason display

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_23.5 ||
children.translated_text: a smile white as a conch-shell or lotus-stalk, those Victors who have conquered their foes." // <s>AVŚ</s> 23.5 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself comprehended this moment with the understanding of a hero,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager, O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, Lord of Victors —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with firm, supreme, auspicious words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_23.6 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen." // <s>AVŚ</s> 23.6 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_23.7 || iti
children.translated_text:
"The Fully Awakened Ones, the Lords, possessing the steadfastness of the mountain-king of the salt sea,
do not display a smile without cause.
For whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile —
those multitudes of people desire to hear that." // <s>AVŚ</s> 23.7 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anayā dārikayā tathāgatasya sauvarṇacakraṃ kṣiptam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣā ānanda dārikā anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca pañcadaśa kalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati, divyaṃ mānuṣaṃ sukham anubhūya ca cakrāntaro nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ iti | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this girl has cast a golden wheel upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>?' 'Indeed, Venerable Sir.' 'This girl, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, for fifteen <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) shall not fall into a state of perdition; and having experienced divine and human happiness, she shall become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Awakened One) named <s>Cakrāntara</s> (Between the Wheels), compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, fond of secluded lodgings, worthy of receiving offerings individually, [shining] for the world. This is her gift of <s>Dharma</s>: the serene faith of her mind directed toward me.' Therefore, monks, you should train thus: 'We shall perform acts of reverence toward <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples).' Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_24 daśaśirāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 24 — <s>Daśaśiras</s> (Ten-Headed). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran gaṅgātīram anuprāptaḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena | adrākṣus te bhikṣavo dūrata eva purāṇastūpaṃ vātātapavarṣair avarugṇaṃ prarugṇam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kasyaiṣa bhadanta stūpa iti | bhagavān āha: daśaśirasaḥ pratyekabuddhasyeti | bhikṣavaḥ ūcuḥ: kuto bhadanta daśaśirasaḥ pratyekabuddhasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ceti | bhagavān āha: icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śrotum iti? ta ūcuḥ: evaṃ bhadanteti | tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, wandering through the <s>Magadha</s> country, arrived at the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> together with the community of monks. Those monks saw from afar an ancient <s>stūpa</s>, battered and broken by wind, heat, and rain. Having seen it, they asked the Blessed One: 'Whose <s>stūpa</s> is this, Venerable Sir?' The Blessed One said: 'It is the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Daśaśiras</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>.' The monks said: 'Whence, Venerable Sir, was the origin and spiritual realization of <s>Daśaśiras</s> the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Do you wish to hear, monks?' They said: 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, monks, listen well and attentively; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 62]

children.text: taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati | sa ca rājā aputraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate | tadyathā: ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ | sahajāḥ sahadhārmikā nityānubaddhā api devatā āyācate | sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭati | tasya codyāne nahatī padminī utpalapadmakumudapadmapuṇḍarīkasaṃchannā haṃsacakravākakāraṇḍavādiśakunopaśobhitā nalinī | tatra padmam atipramāṇam akaṇṭakaṃ sahotpannam* | tad divase divase vardhate na tu phullati | tata ārāmikeṇa rājñe niveditam* | rajñā uktaḥ: parirakṣyatām etat padmam iti | yāvad apareṇa samayena sūryodaye tat padmaṃ vikasitam* | tasya padmasya karṇikāyāṃ dārakaḥ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvāvasthitaḥ, abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaś chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhur vistīrṇalalāṭa uccaghoṣaḥ saṃgatabrūs tuṅganāsaḥ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛto 'śītyānuvyañjanair virājitagātraḥ | taṃ dṛṣṭvā ārāmikeṇa rājñe niveditam* | śrutvā rājā sāmātyaḥ sāntaḥpuraś ca tad udyānaṃ gataḥ | dadarśa rājā padmakarṇikāyāṃ tathā vibhājamānam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita udagraprītisaumanasyajātaḥ padminīm avagāhya taṃ gṛhītvā mahatā satkāreṇa svagṛham ānīya śramaṇabrāhmaṇanaimittikānāṃ nivedya trīṇi saptakāny ekaviṃśatiṃ divasān jātasya jātimahaṃ kṛtvā daśaśirā iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtavān* ||
children.translated_text: free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. A righteous <s>Dharma</s>-king, he ruled the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>. Now that king was childless, and desiring a son, he prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other special deities — such as garden-deities, forest-deities, crossroad-deities, intersection-deities, offering-receiving deities — as well as innate, co-dharmic, and ever-attending deities. He remained devoted to these supplications. In his park there was a beautiful lotus-pond, covered with blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, and white lotuses, adorned with swans, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, and other birds. There, in that pond, a lotus of extraordinary size, thornless, had spontaneously appeared. Day by day it grew, but did not bloom. Then the park-keeper reported this to the king. The king said: 'Guard this lotus carefully.' Then, on a later occasion, at sunrise, that lotus opened. Upon the receptacle of that lotus sat a boy, cross-legged — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, fair-complexioned, golden-skinned, with a parasol-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, a deep voice, joined eyebrows, a high-bridged nose — adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics. Having seen him, the park-keeper reported this to the king. Having heard, the king, together with his ministers and his inner household, went to that park. The king beheld him shining thus upon the lotus receptacle. And having seen him, joyful, delighted, elated, filled with keen joy and happiness, he descended into the lotus-pond, took the boy, and with great honor brought him to his own house. Having informed <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and soothsayers, he held a birth-festival for twenty-one days — three sets of seven — and gave him the name <s>Daśaśiras</s> (Ten-Headed).

children.text: daśaśirā dārakaḥ aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cott{aptott}aptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca kumāraḥ śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ | sa paśyati pitaraṃ rājadharme sthitaṃ sāvadyam avadyāni karmāṇi kurvāṇam* | dṛṣṭvā ca kumāraḥ saṃvignaḥ pitaraṃ vijñāpayāmāsa: anujānīhi māṃ tāta, pravrajiṣyāmi svākhyāte dharmavinaye iti | yāvat pitrānujñātaḥ keśaśmaśru avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ | tena vinopadeśena saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣān dharmān āmukhīkṛtya pratyekā bodhiḥ sākṣātkṛtā | sa gaganatalam utpatya pituḥ sakāśe vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi cakāra | tato rājñā traimāsya piṇḍakenopanimantritaḥ | sa śarīrabhārodvahanaparikhinno vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi darśayitvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirvṛtim upajagāma | tasyaiṣa stūpa iti ||
children.translated_text: The boy <s>Daśaśiras</s> (Ten-Headed) was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, skimmed ghee, and other choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. That prince was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition, devoted to his own welfare and that of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>, and affectionate toward his subjects. He saw his father, established in the duties of kingship, committing blameworthy deeds with fault. Having seen this, the prince, filled with spiritual urgency, petitioned his father: 'Give me permission, father; I wish to go forth into the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' Having received permission from his father, he shaved off his hair and beard, put on the saffron robes, and with perfect faith went forth from the household life into homelessness. Without any instruction, having mastered the thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>), he directly realized <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s> (solitary awakening). Rising into the sky, he performed various miracles before his father. Then the king invited him for a three-month meal offering. Wearied by carrying the burden of the body, having displayed various miracles, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, he attained <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. 'This is his <s>stūpa</s>.'

children.text: atha bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta daśaśirasā karmāṇi kṛtāni, yena mātuḥ kukṣau nopapannaḥ, padma upapanna iti || bhagavān āha: daśaśirasaiva bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | daśaśirasā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca |
children.translated_text: Then the monks, filled with curiosity, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds did <s>Daśaśiras</s> perform, Venerable Sir, that he was not born in his mother's womb but was born in a lotus?' The Blessed One said: 'It was by <s>Daśaśiras</s> himself, monks, that deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur. The deeds performed and accumulated by <s>Daśaśiras</s> — who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api |}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_24.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_24.1 //
'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | atha vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | anyataraś ca sārthavāhaḥ padmam ādāya vīthīṃ pratipannaḥ | athāsau paśyati vipaśyinaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanād bhagavata upari tat padmaṃ cikṣepa | tat kṣiptamātraṃ bhagavata upari śakaṭacakramātraṃ bhūtvā bhagavantaṃ gacchantam upagacchati, tiṣṭhantam anutiṣṭhati | yāvad vipaśyinā samyaksaṃbuddhena sa sārthavāhaḥ pratyekabodhau vyākṛtaḥ | tato hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditamanāḥ svagṛham āgataḥ | prajāpatī cāsya tena kālena prajāyamānā sasvaraṃ kranditavatī | tena paricārikā pṛṣṭā: kim idam iti | tayā samākhyātam* | tataḥ sārthavāhaḥ saṃvignaḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: mā kadācit saṃsāre mātuḥ kukṣāv upapadyeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'In the distant past, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, surrounded by a company of monks, preceded by the community of monks, entered <s>Bandhumatī</s> the royal capital for alms. A certain caravan-leader, holding a lotus, was walking along the street. He beheld the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Upon seeing him, he cast that lotus upward over the Blessed One. The moment it was cast, it became as large as a cart-wheel over the Blessed One — following him when he walked, standing still when he stood. Then by the Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>, that caravan-leader was prophesied for <s>Pratyekabuddhahood</s>. Thereupon, joyful, delighted, and elated, he returned to his own house. And his wife, at that time giving birth, cried out in pain. He asked the maidservant: "What is this?" She explained. Then the caravan-leader, filled with spiritual urgency, began to make an aspiration: "May I never be reborn in a mother's womb in the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>."'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena sārthavāho babhūva, ayaṃ sa daśaśirāḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ | tena kuśalamūlenaikaviṃśatiṃ kalpān na kadācin mātuḥ kukṣāv upapannaḥ | paścime cāsya bhave iyaṃ vibhūtiḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the caravan-leader — that was <s>Daśaśiras</s> the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. By that root of merit, for twenty-one <s>kalpas</s> he was never born in a mother's womb. And in his last birth, this was his glory. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall perform acts of service toward <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_25 sūkṣmatvak* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_25: <s>Sūkṣmatvak</s> (Fine-Skinned). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ prabhūtavittopakaraṇaḥ parbhūtasatvasvāpateyaḥ prabhūtamitrāmātyajñātisālohitaḥ | sa ca gṛhapatiḥ śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ | tasyaitad abhavat: ime bhogāḥ jalacandrasvabhāvāḥ marīcisadṛśā anityā adhruvā anāśvāsikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇaḥ pañcabhir ugradaṇḍaiḥ sādhāraṇāḥ | yanv aham asārebhyo bhogebhyaḥ sāram ādadyām iti | tena bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho bhaktenopanimantritaḥ | gṛhaṃ cāpagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive resources, of abundant goods, cattle, and property, with abundant friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen — that householder was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition, devoted to his own welfare and that of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>. He thought thus: 'These possessions are like a reflection in water, like a mirage, impermanent, unstable, unreliable, subject to change, shared with five dire forces. Let me extract what is essential from these insubstantial possessions.' By him, the Blessed One together with the community of disciples was invited to a meal. His house was cleared of stones, gravel, and rubble,

children.text:
candanavāripariṣiktaṃ vicitragandhaghaṭikāsurabhidhūpadhūpitaṃ nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇam* | puṣpāsanāni prajñaptāni | tataḥ susvādaśītarasapānāni bhakṣyabhojyāni ca sajjīkṛtya bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati: samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti | tato bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena tasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | atha sa gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaviṣṭaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītenāhāreṇa svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati | svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcatarāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān gṛhapatiṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati | anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya tūṣṇīṃbhūtaḥ | atha sa gṛhapatir labdhaprasādaḥ pādayor nipatya cetanāṃ puṣṇāti |
  tato bhagavān smitaṃ vidarśitavān* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ satvānāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ {taṃ} nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text:
sprinkled with sandalwood water, perfumed with various fragrant incense-balls and aromatic smoke, and strewn with various flowers. Flower-seats were prepared. Then, having prepared delicious, cool drinks and food, both savory and nourishing, he sent a messenger to announce the time to the Blessed One: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready; may the Blessed One come when he thinks fit.' Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, surrounded by a company of monks, preceded by the community of monks, proceeded to the dwelling of that householder. Having arrived, he sat on the seat prepared before the community of monks. Then that householder, knowing that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, served and satisfied them with his own hands with pure and excellent food. Having served and satisfied them with his own hands, and knowing that the Blessed One had finished eating, with washed hands and the bowl removed, he took a lower seat and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One instructed, inspired, roused, and gladdened the householder with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, inspired, and roused him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, [the Blessed One] became silent. Then that householder, having gained faith, fell at [the Blessed One's] feet and nourished his aspiration.
Then the Blessed One displayed a smile. It is indeed the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward and some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. It occurs to them: 'Have we perhaps departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to produce faith in those beings, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation. Seeing that emanation, they think: 'Indeed, we have neither departed from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having gained faith in the emanation and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in that hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels of the truths. Those that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Non-self!' and recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: 'Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_25.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!' // AVŚ_25.1 //

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: 'He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_25.2 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of births, shall make an end of suffering.' // AVŚ_25.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante |
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire three-thousand-fold great-thousand world-system, follow behind the Blessed One. If the Blessed One wishes to prophesy past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind the Blessed One.

children.text: anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: he wishes to predict future <s>karma</s>, they vanish in front of him. When he wishes to predict rebirth in the hells, they vanish at the soles of his feet. When he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. When he wishes to predict rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toes. When he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees. When he wishes to predict the sovereignty of a lesser <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. When he wishes to predict the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s>, they vanish in his right palm. When he wishes to predict rebirth among the <s>devas</s> (gods), they vanish at his navel. When he wishes to predict <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (the awakening of a disciple), they vanish at his mouth. When he wishes to predict <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (the awakening of a solitary buddha), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (the hair-tuft between the brows). When he wishes to predict supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and vanished at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "Of manifold kinds, adorned with a thousand hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: a cluster of rays has issued forth from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the quarters in every direction have been illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_25.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he spoke these verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, rid of misery and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme causes of good in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_25.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile white as conch-shell or lotus-fiber."

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself realized the truth at that very moment, O hero, through your wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are filled with longing, O <s>śramaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme words,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_25.5 ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen, with your auspicious speech."

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_25.6 || iti
children.translated_text: "Not without cause do the perfectly awakened <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>, the protectors, steady as the ocean, mountains, and kings, display a smile. The multitudes of people long to hear about the one for whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena śreṣṭhinā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda śreṣṭhī anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca sūkṣmatvag iti nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ iti | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, this guild-master (<s>śreṣṭhin</s>) who has performed such an offering to me?" "Yes, Venerable Sir." "This guild-master, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this generation of the thought of awakening, and by this relinquishment of gifts, shall become a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha) named <s>Sūkṣmatvac</s> (Fine-skinned). This gift of his is the faith he has generated toward me." "Therefore, O monks, you should train thus: 'We shall render service to the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble disciples (<s>āryaśrāvakas</s>).' Thus, O monks, should you train."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Elated, those monks rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Vaidya, p. 66]

children.text: AVŚ_26 śītaprabhaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>Avadānaśataka</s> 26: <s>Śītaprabha</s> (Cool Radiance) (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text:
buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyāṃ anyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ | tasyaitad abhavat: ime bhogā jalacandrasvabhāvā gajakarṇasadṛśā anityā adhruvā anāśvāsikā vipariṇāmadharmāṇaḥ pañcabhir ugradaṇḍaiḥ sādhāraṇāḥ | yanv aham asārebhyo bhogebhyaḥ sāram ādadyām iti | tena grīṣmakāle vartamāne bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho bhaktenopanimantritaḥ | gṛhaṃ cāpagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ candanavāripariṣiktaṃ vicitragandhaghaṭikāsurabhidhūpadhūpitaṃ nānāpuṣpābhikīrṇam* | puṣpāsanāni prajñaptāni | tataḥ śītarasāni pānakāni bhakṣyabhojyāni ca sajjīkṛtya bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati: samayo bhadanta, sajjaṃ bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti | tato bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena tasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | atha sa gṛhapatiḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati | anekaparyāyena śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcatarāsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavāṃs taṃ gṛhapatiṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati | anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya
tūṣṇīṃbhūtaḥ | atha sa gṛhapatir labdhaprasādaḥ pādayor nipatya cetanāṃ puṣṇāti |
  tato bhagavān smitaṃ vidarśitavān* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ {taṃ} nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān,
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, bedding, seats, and medicines for the sick as requisites, together with the community of monks (<s>śrāvakasaṃgha</s>), was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>), wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. He was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition, devoted to his own welfare and that of others, compassionate, great-souled, and fond of the <s>Dharma</s>. This thought occurred to him: "These worldly possessions are like reflections of the moon in water, like the ears of an elephant — impermanent, unstable, unreliable, subject to change, and shared with the five harsh penalties (fire, flood, kings, thieves, and unworthy heirs). Let me extract the essence from these essenceless possessions." Then, as the summer season was at hand, he invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of monks for a meal. His house was cleared of stones, gravel, and pebbles, sprinkled with sandalwood water, fumigated with incense from jars of various fragrances, and strewn with many kinds of flowers. Flower-seats were arranged. Then, having prepared cool drinks, foods to be chewed and eaten, he announced the time to the <s>Bhagavān</s> through a messenger: "It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come at whatever time he sees fit." Then in the forenoon the <s>Bhagavān</s> dressed, took his bowl and robe, and surrounded by the company of monks, attended by the assembly of monks, approached the householder's dwelling. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared for him at the head of the assembly of monks. Then that householder, knowing the <s>Buddha</s>-led assembly of monks to be comfortably seated, with his own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent food to be chewed and eaten. Having with his own hands served and satisfied them in many ways with pure and excellent food to be chewed and eaten, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s> had finished eating, with hands washed and bowl removed, he took a lower seat and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, incited, inspired, and delighted that householder with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, incited, inspired, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he became silent. Then the householder, having gained faith, fell at his feet and nurtured his aspiration. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile. For it is a natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that whenever <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> display a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue forth from his mouth — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down as cool, and in the cold hells they fall down as warm. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think: "Have we, sirs, fallen from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?" To generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth an emanation. Having seen that emanation, they think: "Indeed, we have not fallen from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, by whose power our distinctive sufferings have been alleviated." Having generated faith in the emanation, they exhaust the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in hell and take rebirth among <s>devas</s> and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>,
[Vaidya, p. 67]

children.text: yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — they proclaim: "All is impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self," and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive, go forth, devote yourselves to the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_26.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut."

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: "For whoever shall dwell heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_26.2 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering."

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>), followed behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Now, if the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to predict past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. When he wishes to predict future <s>karma</s>, they vanish in front of him. When he wishes to predict rebirth in the hells, they vanish at the soles of his feet. When he wishes to predict rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. When he wishes to predict rebirth as a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost), they vanish at his big toes. When he wishes to predict rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees. When he wishes to predict the sovereignty of a lesser <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), they vanish in his left palm. When he wishes to predict the sovereignty of a <s>cakravartin</s>, they vanish in his right palm. When he wishes to predict rebirth among the <s>devas</s> (gods), they vanish at his navel. When he wishes to predict <s>śrāvakabodhi</s> (the awakening of a disciple), they vanish at his mouth. When he wishes to predict <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (the awakening of a solitary buddha), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (the hair-tuft between the brows). When he wishes to predict supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and vanished at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "Of manifold kinds, adorned with a thousand hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: a cluster of rays has issued forth from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the quarters in every direction have been illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_26.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun."

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he spoke these verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from rebirth, rid of misery and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme causes of good in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_26.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile white as conch-shell or lotus-fiber."

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself realized the truth at that very moment, O hero, through your wisdom,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are filled with longing, O <s>śramaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme words,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_26.5 ||
children.translated_text: O bull among sages, dispel the doubt that has arisen, with your auspicious speech."
[Vaidya, p. 68]

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_26.6 || iti
children.translated_text: "Not without cause do the perfectly awakened <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>, the protectors, steady as the ocean, mountains, and kings, display a smile. The multitudes of people long to hear about the one for whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena gṛhapatinā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda gṛhapatir anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca śītaprabho nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ iti | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> manifest a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this householder has performed such an act of devotion toward me? Yes, <s>Bhadanta</s>. This householder, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this arising of the thought of enlightenment, and by this relinquishment of a gift, shall become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha) named <s>Śītaprabha</s> (Cold Radiance). This is the fruit of his gift — the faith he placed in my presence. Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: we shall perform acts of devotion toward <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples). Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_27 nāvikāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: [Avadāna 27: The Boatmen]

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran gaṅgātīram anuprāptaḥ | atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena nāvikās tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya nāvikān idam avocat*: uttārayantu bhavanto mām imāṃ nadīm iti | nāvikā ūcuḥ: tarapaṇyaṃ prayaccheti | tato bhagavāṃs tān nāvikān idam avocat*: aham api bhavanto nāvikaḥ pūrvam āsam* | mayā hi rāganadīpatito nandas tāritaḥ, dveṣārṇavapatito aṅgulimālaḥ, mānārṇavapatito mānastabdho māṇavaḥ, mohārṇavapatito urubilvakāśyapas tāritaḥ | na ca me tarapaṇyaṃ yācitā iti | tathāpy ucyamānā na pratipādyante tārayitum* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), <s>yakṣas</s> (spirits), <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians), and <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents) — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, bedding and seats, and medicines for the sick as requisites, together with the community of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), wandering on a tour through the <s>Magadha</s> country, arrived at the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by a company of monks and preceded by the <s>saṃgha</s> of monks, approached the boatmen and, having approached, said this to the boatmen: "Good sirs, ferry me across this river." The boatmen said: "Pay the ferry-toll." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to those boatmen: "Good sirs, I too was formerly a boatman. I ferried <s>Nanda</s>, who had fallen into the river of passion; <s>Aṅgulimāla</s>, who had fallen into the ocean of hatred; the proud young <s>Mānastabdha</s>, who had fallen into the ocean of pride; and <s>Urubilvakāśyapa</s>, who had fallen into the ocean of delusion. And no ferry-toll was demanded of me." Yet even when thus addressed, they would not consent to ferry him across.

children.text:
anyatamena nāvikena bhagavato aṣṭāṅgopetaṃ svaraṃ śrutvā tāṃ ca rūpasaṃpadaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasādajātenoktam*: ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham uttārayiṣyāmīti | tato bhikṣavo nāvam abhirūḍhāḥ | bhagavān ṛddhyā agrata eva tasya nāvikasyāpārimāt tīrāt pārime tīre sthitaḥ | tataḥ sa nāvikas tad ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā āvarjitamanāḥ pādayor nipatitaḥ | tasmai bhagavatā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tena nāvikena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 69 --------------------
children.translated_text: A certain boatman, having heard the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s voice endowed with eight qualities and having seen that perfection of form, said with faith arisen: "I shall ferry the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of <s>śrāvakas</s> across." Then the monks boarded the boat. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, by supernatural power, stood already on the far shore ahead of that boatman, having crossed from the near shore to the far shore. Then that boatman, having seen that miraculous display of supernatural power, with his mind won over, fell at his feet. The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave him such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> as penetrates the Four Noble Truths, and having heard it, that boatman, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising with its twenty peaks, attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). He, having seen the truths, uttered an inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>) three times: "This for us, [editorial page reference]

children.text: bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadanta</s>, was not done by our mother, not by our father, not by the king, not by the gods, not by beloved kinsmen and relatives, not by departed ancestors, not by <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (brahmins) — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been crossed over, the doors to the lower realms have been shut, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and humans." And he said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: "By your power, the terrifying

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path to the lower realms, fraught with many faults, has been shut;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: The gate to heaven, rich in merit, has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_27.1 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) has been found by me.

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer: suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_27.2 ||
children.translated_text: and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.
And by relying on you, I have today attained a pure, perfectly clear eye of wisdom, free from blemish;

children.text:
naravarendra narāmarapūjita
  vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayam* | (Speyer: vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmaya)
  bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
  saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_27.3 || iti
children.translated_text: O best of men, worshipped by humans and gods, free from birth, old age, death, and disease — O sage whose sight is difficult to obtain in a thousand existences, today your sight has borne fruit."

children.text: dvitīyasya nāvikasya mahān vipratisāra utpannaḥ | tena bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya atyayo deśitaḥ, bhagavāṃś ca saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The second boatman was seized by great remorse. He fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and confessed his transgression, and he served the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of <s>śrāvakas</s> with almsfood.

children.text: bhagavatā smitaṃ vidarśitam* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ {taṃ} nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva {vayaṃ} bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile. It is the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, manifest a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue forth from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down having become cool, and in the cold hells they fall down having become warm. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think: "Have we, good sirs, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?" To generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth a magical emanation. Having seen that emanation, they think: "We have certainly not passed away from here, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance — by his power our distinctive sufferings have been alleviated." They, having placed their minds in faith toward the emanation, exhaust the <s>karma</s> (action) to be experienced in hell, take rebirth among gods and humans, and there become vessels for the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens, proclaim: "All is impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self," and they speak two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_27.4 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), as an elephant crushes a reed hut.

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: Whoever shall dwell diligently in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline),

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_27.5 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering."
[editorial page reference]

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm, follow behind the <s>Bhagavān</s> step by step. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to declare past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If he wishes to declare future <s>karma</s>, they vanish in front. If he wishes to declare rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to declare rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to declare rebirth as a hungry ghost, they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to declare rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to declare the sovereignty of a powerful universal monarch, they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to declare the sovereignty of a wheel-turning monarch, they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to declare rebirth among the gods, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to declare the enlightenment of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to declare the enlightenment of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (the hair-tuft between the brows). If he wishes to declare supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (the crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A cluster of manifold rays, painted with a thousand colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: issued forth from within your mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_27.6 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun.

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he spoke these verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, free from becoming, rid of wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: are the supreme sources of benefit in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the victorious <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_27.7 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile white as a conch shell or lotus fiber.

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: Having yourself realized this at that very moment through your wisdom, O hero,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager to hear, O <s>Śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), O lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words, O bull among sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_27.8 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen."

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_27.9 || iti
children.translated_text: "Not without cause do the perfectly enlightened protectors, steadfast as the salt-ocean and the king of mountains, display a smile; the multitudes of people desire to hear about the one for whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile."

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anena nāvikena mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda nāviko 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca anāgate 'dhvani saṃsārottaraṇo nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is. Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> manifest a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this boatman has placed his faith in my presence? Yes, <s>Bhadanta</s>. This boatman, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this arising of the thought of enlightenment, and by this relinquishment of a gift, shall in a future age become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha) named <s>Saṃsārottaraṇa</s> (Crossing Beyond <s>Saṃsāra</s>). This is the fruit of his gift — the faith he placed in my presence. Therefore, monks, you should train yourselves thus: we shall perform acts of devotion toward <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples). Thus, monks, should you train yourselves.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those monks rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[editorial page reference]

children.text: AVŚ_28 gandhamādanaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: [Avadāna 28: <s>Gandhamādana</s>]

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | ācaritam etan madhyadeśe: bhūyasā madhyadeśanivāsino jānapadā vicitrair anulepanair gātram anulimpanti | yāvad anyatamo gṛhapatiputraḥ | tasya dārikā śrāddhā bhadrā kalyāṇāśayā lohitacandanaṃ pinaṣṭi | bhagavāṃś ca pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | adrākṣīt sā dārikā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca dārikāyā mahān prasāda utpannaḥ | tato labdhaprasādāyā etad abhavat*: kiṃ mamānenaivaṃvidhena jīvitena yāham īdṛśaṃ kṣetram āsādya na śaknomi dāridryadoṣād bhagavataḥ kārān kartum iti ||
