children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrels' Feeding Ground). It was the custom in that central region: the inhabitants of the central lands commonly anoint their bodies with various kinds of unguents. Now there was a certain householder's daughter. She — faithful, virtuous, of good disposition — was grinding red sandalwood. And the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken up his bowl and robe, surrounded and attended by the community of monks, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. That girl beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a fathom-wide aura of light, surpassing in radiance a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious in every way. And upon seeing him, a great faith arose in the girl. Then, filled with faith, this thought occurred to her: 'What is the use of such a life as mine, when, having encountered such a field [of merit], I am unable on account of poverty to perform acts of worship for the Blessed One!'

children.text: tatas tayā svajīvitam agaṇayitvā ubhau pāṇī lohitacandanena pralipya bhagavataḥ pādayor aṅgade kṛte, bhagavatā ca ṛddhyā sakalaṃ rājagṛhanagaraṃ candanagandhenāpūritam* | tato dārikā tat pratihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasannacittā bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya cetanāṃ puṣṇāti: anena kuśalamūlena pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ sākṣāt kuryām iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, disregarding her own livelihood, she smeared both her hands with red sandalwood paste and made ornaments upon the Blessed One's feet; and by the Blessed One's supernatural power, the entire city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> was filled with the fragrance of sandalwood. Then the girl, upon seeing that miracle, with a mind filled with faith, prostrated at the Blessed One's feet and nurtured this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I directly realize <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening).'

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitaṃ vidarśitam* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ {taṃ} nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One displayed a smile. It is indeed the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, manifest a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some go downward and some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells — <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down cooled, and in the cold hells they fall down warmed. Thereby the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. It occurs to them: 'Have we perhaps departed from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to produce faith in them, the Blessed One sends forth an emanation. Seeing the emanation, they think: 'Indeed, we have neither departed from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance, and by his power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having gained faith in the emanation and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in that hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels of the truths. Those rays that go upward, having gone to the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trayastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 72]

children.text: abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heavens — proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Non-self!' and recite two verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_28.1 ||
children.translated_text: Crush the army of Death, as an elephant crushes a reed hut!" // <s>AVŚ</s> 28.1 //

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: "He who shall live heedfully in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_28.2 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of births, shall make an end of suffering." // <s>AVŚ</s> 28.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ {karma} vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having traversed the entire three-thousand-fold great-thousand world-system, follow behind the Blessed One. If the Blessed One wishes to prophesy past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind the Blessed One. If he wishes to prophesy future events, they disappear in front. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth in a hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as an animal, they disappear at the heel. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a hungry ghost (<s>preta</s>), they disappear at the big toe. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a human, they disappear at the knees. If he wishes to prophesy the sovereignty of a powerful universal monarch, they disappear in the left palm. If he wishes to prophesy universal monarchy (<s>cakravartin</s>), they disappear in the right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth as a god, they disappear at the navel. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappear at the mouth. If he wishes to prophesy the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he wishes to prophesy supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared at the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, questioned the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A sheaf of a thousand various, multicolored hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: emitted from within your mouth —

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the quarters in all directions were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_28.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the sun at its rising — // <s>AVŚ</s> 28.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recited verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, who are beyond birth, free from despondency and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the supreme causes in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: they do not without reason display

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_28.4 ||
children.translated_text: a smile white as a conch-shell or lotus-stalk, those Victors who have conquered their foes." // <s>AVŚ</s> 28.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself comprehended this moment with the understanding of a hero,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager, O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, Lord of Victors —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with firm, supreme, auspicious words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_28.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen." // <s>AVŚ</s> 28.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_28.6 || iti
children.translated_text:
"The Fully Awakened Ones, the Lords, possessing the steadfastness of the mountain-king of the salt sea,
do not display a smile without cause.
For whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile —
those multitudes of people desire to hear that." // <s>AVŚ</s> 28.6 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 73]

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anayā dārikayā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣā ānanda dārikā kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca gandhamādano nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati | ayam asyā deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that this girl has performed such worship toward me?' 'Indeed, Venerable Sir.' 'This girl, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, shall become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Awakened One) named <s>Gandhamādana</s> (Fragrance-Intoxicating). This is her gift of <s>Dharma</s>: the serene faith of her mind directed toward me. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall perform acts of reverence toward <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples)." Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_29 nirmalaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 29 — <s>Nirmala</s> (Spotless). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyāṃ amyatama ārāmikaḥ | sa dantakāṣṭham ādāya śrāvastīṃ praviśati | naimittikaś ca dvāre 'vasthitaḥ | sa kathayati: ya etad dantadhāvanaṃ bhakṣayiṣyati, sa śatarasaṃ bhojanaṃ bhakṣayiṣyati | tad vacanam ārāmikeṇa śrutam* | śrutvā caivaṃ cintayāmāsa: kasmāyetad dantadhāvanaṃ dadyām* | yena me mahān saṃmānaḥ syād iti | tasyaitad abhavat*: ayaṃ buddho bhagavān sacarācare loke jaṅgamaṃ puṇyakṣetram abandhyamahāphalaṃ ca | yanv aham idaṃ buddhāya bhagavate dadyām iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain park-keeper. He, taking a tooth-stick, was entering <s>Śrāvastī</s>. And a soothsayer was standing at the gate. He said: 'Whoever eats this tooth-cleaning stick will eat a meal of a hundred flavors.' The park-keeper heard that statement. Having heard, he thought: 'To whom should I give this tooth-stick so that it might bring me great honor?' This occurred to him: 'This <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, is the supreme field of merit in the world of moving and unmoving beings — unfailing and of great fruit. Let me give this to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One.'

children.text: atha sa ārāmiko dantakāṣṭham ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt* | ekāntasthitaḥ sa ārāmiko bhagavantam idam avocat*: idaṃ bhagavan dantakāṣṭhaṃ pratigṛhyatāṃ mamāntikād anukampām upādāyeti | atha bhagavān ārāmikasyānugrahārthaṃ gajabhujasadṛśaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya gṛhītavān*, gṛhītvā bhakṣitavān*, bhakṣayitvā cainam ārāmikasyāgrato visarjitavān*, visarjya tad dantakāṣṭhaṃ pṛthivyāṃ nikhātavān* | nikhātamātram eva ca tacchākhāpatrapuṣpaphalasamṛddho mahānyagrodhaḥ parimaṇḍalas tatraiva kṣaṇe nirvṛttaḥ | yasya cchāyāyāṃ niṣadya bhagavatā anekeṣāṃ devamanuṣyāṇāṃ dharmo deśitaḥ | tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā bhagavān* śatarasenāhāreṇa pratipāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that park-keeper, taking the tooth-stick, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and worshiped the Blessed One's feet with his head, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the park-keeper said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept this tooth-stick from me, out of compassion.' Then the Blessed One, for the benefit of the park-keeper, extended his arm — golden-hued, resembling an elephant's trunk — and accepted it. Having accepted it, he chewed it. And having chewed it, he released it in front of the park-keeper. Having released it, he planted that tooth-stick in the earth. The very moment it was planted, a great banyan tree, abundant in branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits, perfectly rounded, came into being right then and there. Sitting in its shade, the Blessed One taught the <s>Dharma</s> to many gods and humans. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> served the Blessed One with a meal of a hundred flavors.

children.text: atha sa ārāmiko bhagavadupasthānāt prātihāryāc cāvarjitamanā mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānām kartum ārabdhaḥ: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ sākṣātkuryām iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that park-keeper, his mind won over by the Blessed One's grace and the miracle, fell at his feet like a tree cut at the root and began to make an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I directly realize <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening).'

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitaṃ vidarśitam* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One displayed a smile. It is indeed the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, manifest a smile, at that moment blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from their mouths — some going downward
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 74]

children.text: gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ {taṃ} nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells of <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down having become cold, and in the cold hells they fall down having become hot. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think thus: 'Have we, sirs, fallen from this place, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth an emanation. Having seen that emanation, they think thus: 'Indeed we have not, sirs, fallen from this place, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance; by his power our distinctive sufferings have been alleviated.' Having placed their minds in serene faith toward the emanation, and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those [rays] that go upward, having gone to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' — and recite a pair of verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: Strive forth! Go forth! Yoke yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_29.1 ||
children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death, as an elephant [shakes off] a reed hut! // AVŚ_29.1 //

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: He who in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live heedfully,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_29.2 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering. // AVŚ_29.2 //

children.text: atha tā arciṣas trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum anvāhiṇḍya bhagavantam eva pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanugacchanti | tad yadi bhagavān atītaṃ karma vyākartukāmo bhavati, bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'ntardhīyante | anāgataṃ {karma} vyākartukāmo bhavati, purastād antardhīyante | narakopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādatale 'ntardhīyante | tiryagupapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pārṣṇyām antardhīyante | pretopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, pādāṅguṣṭhe 'ntardhīyante | manuṣyopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, jānunor antardhīyante | balacakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, vāme karatale 'ntardhīyante | cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having wandered throughout the three-thousand-great-thousand world system, follow behind the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to declare past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If he wishes to declare future <s>karma</s>, they vanish in front. If he wishes to declare rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to declare rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to declare rebirth as a hungry ghost, they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to declare rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to declare a minor universal monarch's sovereignty, they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to declare a <s>Cakravartin</s>'s sovereignty, they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to declare rebirth among the gods, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to declare <s>Śrāvaka</s> awakening, they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to declare <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening, they vanish at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the brows). If he wishes to declare unsurpassed perfect awakening, they vanish at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, vanished at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: A cluster of a thousand diverse colors,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: issued from within the mouth;

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around are illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_29.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun. // AVŚ_29.3 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 75]

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he recites these verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: Free from worldly arising, pride and wretchedness abandoned,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme cause in the world;

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s>, conquerors of foes, display

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_29.4 ||
children.translated_text: a smile as white as a conch shell or lotus fiber. // AVŚ_29.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: Having yourself realized the truth through wisdom, O Hero,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager, O ascetic, Lord of Conquerors,

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with steadfast and supreme words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_29.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen, with auspicious [words]. // AVŚ_29.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_29.6 || iti
children.translated_text: Not without reason do the awakened Lords, steadfast as the ocean, salt-sea, and mountain-king, display a smile; that for the sake of which the steadfast ones display a smile — the multitudes of people desire to hear. // AVŚ_29.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda anenārāmikeṇa mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | eṣa ānanda ārāmiko 'nena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trayodaśa kalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyati, paścime bhave paścime nikete paścime samucchraye paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe nirmalo nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati | ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause or condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, how this gardener has performed such a service to me?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'This gardener, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this root of merit, by this arising of the mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, for thirteen <s>kalpas</s> shall not fall into a state of woe. In his last existence, his last abode, his last arising, his last attainment of a bodily form, he shall become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Nirmala</s> (the Stainless). This was his gift — namely, the arising of serene faith in me.' Therefore, monks, you should train thus: 'We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him.' Thus indeed, monks, should you train.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_30 valgusvarāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_30: <s>Valgusvarāḥ</s> (Pleasant Voices). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | saṃbahulāś ca goṣṭhikā madyamadākṣiptā vīṇāmṛdaṅgapaṇavair vividhair vādyair vādyamānair nṛtyanto gāyanta utpalapadmapuṇḍarīkavārṣikādibhir udārapuṣpair āsaktakaṇṭheguṇā viśiṣṭāmbaravasanā bahiḥ śrāvastyā nirgacchanti | bhagavāṃś ca śrāvastyāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | dadṛśus te goṣṭhikā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta</s>'s Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. A large number of revelers, intoxicated with wine, playing various instruments — <s>vīṇās</s>, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and <s>paṇavas</s> — dancing, singing, wearing garlands of <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>vārṣikī</s>, and other fine flowers around their necks, dressed in distinguished garments, were going out of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Those revelers beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 76]

children.text: jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc ca teṣāṃ yo 'sau madyamadaḥ sa prativigataḥ | tato vigatamadyamadāḥ prasādāvarjitamanaso nṛtyagītavādyair bhagavataḥ upasthānaṃ cakruḥ, nīlapadmāni copari bhagavato nicikṣipuḥ | nikṣiptāni copari bhagavato nīlakūṭāgāro nīlacchatraṃ nīlamaṇḍapa ivāvasthitāni | tāni ca bhagavantaṃ gacchantam anugacchati, tiṣṭhantam anutiṣṭhanti | bhagavatā ca nīlaprabhā utsṛṣṭā, yayā śrāvastī indranīlamaṇisadṛśaprabhā avasthitā ||
children.translated_text: like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. And upon seeing him, their intoxication from wine vanished. Then, their intoxication gone and their minds won over by faith, they performed worship to the <s>Bhagavān</s> with dancing, singing, and music, and they scattered blue lotuses above the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The blue lotuses, scattered above the <s>Bhagavān</s>, remained in place like a blue mansion, a blue parasol, a blue pavilion. And as the <s>Bhagavān</s> walked, they followed; when he stood still, they stood still. And a blue radiance was emitted by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, by which <s>Śrāvastī</s> appeared as if possessing the radiance of a blue sapphire.

children.text: atha the goṣṭhikā labdhaprasādāḥ cetanāṃ puṣṇānti: anena vayaṃ kuśalamūlena pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ sākṣātkūryāmeti ||
children.translated_text: Then those revelers, having gained faith, formed an aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may we directly realize <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening.'

children.text: tato bhagavatā smitaṃ vidarśitam* | dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavantaḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti, tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo mukhān niścārya kāścid adhastād gacchanti, kāścid upariṣṭād gacchanti | yā adhastād gacchanti, tāḥ saṃjīvaṃ kālasūtraṃ saṃghātaṃ rauravaṃ mahārauravaṃ tapanaṃ pratāpanam avīcim arbudaṃ nirarbudaṃ aṭaṭaṃ hahavaṃ huhuvam utpalaṃ padmaṃ mahāpadmaṃ narakān gatvā ye uṣṇanarakās teṣu śītībhūtā nipatanti, ye śītanarakās teṣūṣṇībhūtā nipatanti | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabhyante | teṣām evaṃ bhavati: kiṃ nu vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, āhosvid anyatropapannā iti | teṣāṃ prasādasaṃjananārthaṃ bhagavān nirmitaṃ visarjayati | teṣāṃ {taṃ} nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati: na hy eva vayaṃ bhavanta itaś cyutāḥ, nāpy anyatropapannāḥ | api tv ayam apūrvadarśanaḥ satvaḥ, asyānubhāvenāsmākaṃ kāraṇāviśeṣāḥ pratiprasrabdhā iti | te nirmite cittam abhiprasādya tan narakavedanīyaṃ karma kṣapayitvā devamanuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇanti, yatra satyānāṃ bhājanabhūtā bhavanti | yā upariṣṭād gacchanti, tāś cāturmahārājikāṃs trayastriṃśān, yāmāṃs tuṣitān nirmāṇaratīn paranirmitavaśavartino brahmakāyikān brahmapurohitān mahābrahmaṇaḥ parīttābhān apramāṇābhān ābhāsvarān parīttaśubhān apramāṇaśubhāñ śubhakṛtsnān anabhrakān puṇyaprasavān bṛhatphalān abṛhān atapān sudṛśān sudarśanān akaniṣṭhān devān gatvā anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmety udghoṣayanti, gāthādvayaṃ ca bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: Thereupon the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a smile. It is the nature of things that whenever <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, display a smile, at that time blue, yellow, red, and white rays issue from his mouth — some go downward, some go upward. Those that go downward, having gone to the hells of <s>Saṃjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṃghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tapana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> — in the hot hells they fall down having become cold, and in the cold hells they fall down having become hot. Thereby the distinctive sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think thus: 'Have we, sirs, fallen from this place, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' In order to generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth an emanation. Having seen that emanation, they think thus: 'Indeed we have not, sirs, fallen from this place, nor have we been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is a being of wondrous appearance; by his power our distinctive sufferings have been alleviated.' Having placed their minds in serene faith toward the emanation, and having exhausted the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in hell, they take rebirth among gods and humans, where they become vessels for the truths. Those [rays] that go upward, having gone to the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s>, <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Abṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, proclaim: 'Impermanent! Suffering! Empty! Without self!' — and recite a pair of verses:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: Strive forth! Go forth! Yoke yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching!

children.translated_text: Shake off the army of death, as an elephant [shakes off] a reed hut! // AVŚ_30.1 //

children.text: yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
children.translated_text: He who in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> shall live heedfully,

children.text: prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_30.2 ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned the cycle of birth, shall make an end of suffering. // AVŚ_30.2 //

children.translated_text: Then those rays, having wandered throughout the three-thousand-great-thousand world system, follow behind the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to declare past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If he wishes to declare future <s>karma</s>, they vanish in front. If he wishes to declare rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to declare rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to declare rebirth as a hungry ghost, they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to declare rebirth as a human, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to declare a minor universal monarch's sovereignty, they vanish in his left palm.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 77]

children.text: cakravartirājyaṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, dakṣiṇe karatale 'ntardhīyante | devopapattiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, nābhyām antardhīyante | śrāvakabodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, āsye 'ntardhīyante | pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, ūrṇāyām antardhīyante | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākartukāmo bhavati, uṣṇīṣe antardhīyante ||
children.translated_text: If he wishes to prophesy <s>Cakravartin</s> (Universal Monarch) kingship, they disappear at his right palm. If he wishes to prophesy rebirth among the gods, they disappear at his navel. If he wishes to prophesy <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple) awakening, they disappear at his mouth. If he wishes to prophesy <s>Pratyeka</s> (solitary) awakening, they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the eyebrows). If he wishes to prophesy supreme perfect awakening, they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).

children.text: atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata ūrṇāyām antarhitāḥ | athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha:
children.translated_text: Then those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared at the Blessed One's <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.text: nānāvidho raṅgasahasracitro
children.translated_text: "A manifold cluster, variegated with a thousand hues,

children.text: vaktrāntarān niṣkasitaḥ kalāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: issued forth from within your mouth —

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād
children.translated_text: by which the directions on all sides were illuminated,

children.text: divākareṇodayatā yathaiva || AVŚ_30.3 ||
children.translated_text: just as by the rising sun." // AVŚ_30.3 //

children.text: gāthāś ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: And he spoke these verses:

children.text: vigatodbhavā dainyamadaprahīṇā
children.translated_text: "Free from [worldly] arising, having abandoned wretchedness and pride,

children.text: buddhā jagaty uttamahetubhūtāḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s>, supreme causes [of good] in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhamṛṇālagauraṃ
children.translated_text: not without reason do the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), who have conquered their foes,

children.text: smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ || AVŚ_30.4 ||
children.translated_text: display a smile white as a conch-shell or lotus-fiber." // AVŚ_30.4 //

children.text: tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā
children.translated_text: "Having yourself comprehended this moment with the understanding of a hero,

children.text: śrotṝṇāṃ śramaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣitānām* |
children.translated_text: for the listeners who are eager, O <s>Śramaṇa</s>, Lord of Victors —

children.text: dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir
children.translated_text: with firm, supreme, auspicious words, O Bull among Sages,

children.text: utpannaṃ vyapanaya saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ || AVŚ_30.5 ||
children.translated_text: dispel the doubt that has arisen." // AVŚ_30.5 //

children.text:
nākāsmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ
  saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ |
  yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrāḥ
  taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughāḥ || AVŚ_30.6 || iti
children.translated_text:
"The Fully Awakened Ones, the Lords, possessing the steadfastness of the mountain-king of the salt sea,
do not display a smile without cause.
For whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile —
those multitudes of people desire to hear that." // AVŚ_30.6 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: evam etad ānanda, evam etat | nāhetvapratyayam ānanda tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti | paśyasy ānanda ebhir goṣṭhikair mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam* | evaṃ bhadanta | ete ānanda goṣṭhikā anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca viṃśatyantarakalpān vinipātaṃ na gamiṣyanti, paścime bhave paścime nikete paścime samucchraye paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe valgusvarā nāma pratyekabuddhā bhaviṣyanti | ayam eṣāṃ deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasāda iti | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakeṣu kārān kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Ānanda</s>, so it is! Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Fully Awakened Ones display a smile. Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that these guild-members have performed such worship toward me?' 'Indeed, Venerable Sir.' '<s>Ānanda</s>, these guild-members, by this root of merit, by this aspiration of mind, and by this relinquishment of gifts, for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) shall not fall into a state of perdition; and in their last birth, last abode, last arising, last attainment of bodily existence, they shall become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Solitary Awakened Ones) named <s>Valgusvarā</s> (Sweet-Voiced). This is their gift of <s>Dharma</s>: the serene faith of their minds directed toward me.' Therefore, monks, you should train thus: 'We shall perform acts of service toward <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples).' Thus indeed, monks, should you train.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: caturtho vargaḥ |
children.translated_text: The Fourth Section.

children.text: tasyoddānam:
children.translated_text: Its summary verse:

children.text: padmakaḥ kavaḍaś caiva dharmapālaḥ śibis tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Padmaka</s>, <s>Kavaḍa</s>, and <s>Dharmapāla</s>, and <s>Śibi</s>,

children.text: surūpo maitrakanyaś ca śaśo dharmagaveṣiṇā |
children.translated_text: <s>Surūpa</s>, <s>Maitrakanyā</s>, <s>Śaśa</s>, <s>Dharmageṣin</s> (Seeker of Dharma),

children.text: anāthapiṇḍaḥ subhadraś ca vargo bhavati samudditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Anāthapiṇḍa</s>, and <s>Subhadra</s> — such is the section proclaimed.

children.text: AVŚ_31 padmakaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_31: <s>Padmaka</s> (The Lotus One). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śaratkālasamaye bhikṣavo rogeṇa bādhyante pītapāṇḍukāḥ kṛśaśarīrā durbalāṅgāḥ | bhagavāṃs tv alpābādho 'lpātaṅko 'rogo balavān* | taddarśanād bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta ete bhikṣavaḥ śāradikena rogeṇa bādhyante, pītapāṇḍukāḥ kṛśaśarīrā durbalāṅgāḥ | bhagavāṃs tv alpābādho 'lpātaṅko balavān arogajātīyaḥ, samapākayā ca grahaṇyā samanvāgata iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In the autumn season, the monks were afflicted with illness — yellow and pale, with emaciated bodies and feeble limbs. But the Blessed One was of little illness, of little affliction, free from disease, and strong. Seeing this, the monks asked the Blessed One: 'Behold, Venerable Sir, these monks are afflicted by autumnal illness — yellow and pale, with emaciated bodies and feeble limbs. But the Blessed One is of little illness, of little affliction, strong, of healthy constitution, and endowed with even digestion.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: tathāgatenaivaitāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'It is by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, that in former lives these deeds were performed and accumulated, with provisions gathered and conditions ripened, standing present like a flood, certain to occur. These deeds were performed and accumulated by me — who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api | *{auch: karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api|}*
sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_31.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_31.1 //
'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ padmako nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam (Speyer: akaṇṭhakam) ekaputram iva rājyaṃ kārayati | sa ca rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ sarvapradaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca mahatī tyāge vartate | tasmiṃś ca samaye vārāṇasyāṃ kālavaiṣamyād dhātuvaiṣamyād vā vyādhir utapannaḥ | prāyaḥ satvānāṃ pāṇḍurogaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | tato rājñā tān dṛṣṭvā kāruṇikam utpāditam: mayā hy eṣāṃ paritrāṇaṃ karaṇīyaṃ cikitsā ceti | tataḥ sa rājā sarvaviṣayanivāsino vaidyān saṃnipātya teṣāṃ satvānāṃ nidānam āśayānuśayaṃ copalakṣya
children.translated_text: In the distant past, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Padmaka</s> (Lotus) was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo — he ruled the kingdom without harm or obstacle, as if it were an only son. That king was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition, devoted to his own welfare and that of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>, affectionate toward his subjects, a giver of all things, one who renounces all, relinquishing without attachment — he dwelt in great generosity. At that time, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, whether from an unfavorable season or an imbalance of humors, a disease arose. Most beings were afflicted with jaundice. Then the king, having seen them, was moved with compassion: 'I must provide them with protection and treatment.' Then that king, having assembled physicians from all his domains and having observed the underlying condition and latent tendencies of those beings,

children.text: svayam ārabdhaś cikitsāṃ sarvauṣadhasamudānayaṃ ca kartum* | tataś cikitsyamānānāṃ teṣāṃ satvānāṃ bahavaḥ kālā atikrāntāḥ | na ca śakyante vaidyadravyauṣadhaparicārakasaṃpannā api cikitsitum* | tato rājñā sarvavaidyān āhūya ādarajātena punaḥ pṛṣṭāḥ: ko 'tra hetur na me duścikitsyā iti | vaidyā vicārya guṇadoṣānekamatenāhuḥ: deva kālavaiṣamyād dhātuvaiṣamyāc ca lakṣyāmahe | api tu deva asty ekabhaiṣajyaṃ rohito nāma matsyaḥ | yadi tasya prāptiḥ syāt, śakyante cikitsitum iti | tato rājā rohitaṃ matsyaṃ samanveṣitum ārabdhaḥ | sa bahubhir api cārapuruṣair mṛgyamāṇo na labhyate | tatas te rājñe niveditavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: himself undertook to administer treatment and to procure all medicines. Then, as those beings were being treated, many seasons passed. Yet they could not be cured, even with physicians, medicines, remedies, and attendants fully provided. Then the king, having summoned all physicians, asked again with earnest concern: 'What is the reason that they cannot be cured by me?' The physicians, having deliberated on the virtues and defects, said unanimously: 'Your Majesty, we observe that it is due to an unfavorable season and an imbalance of humors. However, Your Majesty, there is one remedy — a fish called <s>rohita</s>. If it could be obtained, they could be cured.' Then the king began to search for the <s>rohita</s> fish. Though sought by many scouts, it could not be found. Then they reported this to the king.

children.text: atha rājā apareṇa samayena bahiryāṇāya nirgacchati | te ca vyādhina ekasamūhena sthitvā rājānam ūcuḥ: paritrāyasva mahārāja asmān asmād vyādheḥ | prayaccha jīvitam iti | tato rājā karuṇadīnavilambitair akṣarair ucyamānas tadāturavacanaṃ śrutvā kāruṇyād ākampitahṛdayaḥ sāśrudurdinavadanaṃ cintayāmāsa: kiṃ mamānenaivaṃvidhena jīvitena rājyaiśvaryādhipatyena vā īdṛśena, yo 'haṃ pareṣāṃ duḥkhārtānāṃ na śakto 'smi śāntiṃ kartum iti | evaṃ vicintya rājā mahāntam arthotsargaṃ kṛtvā jyeṣṭhaṃ kumāraṃ rājyaiṣvaryādhipatyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpya bandhujanaṃ kṣamayitvā paurāmātyāṃś ca kṣamayitvā dīnān samāśvāsya aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgataṃ vrataṃ samādāya upariprāsādatalam abhiruhya dhūpapuṣpagandhamālyavilepanaṃ ca kṣiptvā prāṅmukhaṃ praṇidhiṃ kartuṃ prārabdhaḥ: yena satyena satyavacanena mahāvyasanagatān satvān vyādhiparipīḍitān dṛṣṭvā svajīvitam iṣṭaṃ parityajāmi | anena satyena satyavākyena asyāṃ vālukāyāṃ nadyāṃ mahān rohitamatsyaḥ prādurbhaveyam* | ity uktvā prāsādatalād ātmānaṃ mumoca ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, on a later occasion, went out for an excursion. Those afflicted persons, standing together in a group, said to the king: 'Save us, O Great King, from this disease! Grant us our lives!' Then the king, hearing the words of those sick people, spoken in tones piteous and hesitant with compassion, his heart shaken with pity, his face tearful as on a cloudy day, reflected: 'What use is such a life for me, or such royal sovereignty and dominion, when I am unable to bring peace to those who are suffering?' Having reflected thus, the king made a great sacrifice of his possessions, established his eldest prince in the royal sovereignty and dominion, took leave of his kinsmen, took leave of his ministers and counselors, consoled the afflicted, and having undertaken a vow endowed with the eight factors, ascended to the top of his palace-terrace, offered incense, flowers, fragrance, garlands, and ointments, and facing east, began to make his aspiration: 'By the truth of this truthful speech — that having seen beings fallen into great calamity, tormented by disease, I relinquish my own beloved life — by this truth, by this true word, may I appear as a great <s>rohita</s> fish in this sandy river!' Having spoken thus, he cast himself from the palace-terrace.

children.text: sa patitamātraḥ kālagato nadyāṃ vālukāyāṃ mahān rohitamatsyaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ | iti devatābhiḥ sarvavijite śabda utsṛṣṭaḥ: eṣa dīrghakālamahāvyādhyutpīḍitānām amṛtakalpo nadyāṃ vālukāyāṃ mahān rohitamatsya prādurbhūtaḥ iti | yataḥ sahaśravaṇān mahājanakāyaḥ śastravyagrakaraḥ piṭakān ādāya nirgatya vividhais tīkṣṇaiḥ śastrair jīvita eva māṃsāny utkartitum ārabdhaḥ | sa ca bodhisatvo vikartyamānaśarīras tān sarvān maitryā sphuran sabāṣpāśruvadanaś cintayāmāsa: lābhā me sulabdhāḥ yan nāma ime satvā madīyena māṃsarudhireṇa sukhino bhaviṣyantīti | tad anenopakrameṇa satvān dvādaśavarṣāṇi svakena māṃsarudhireṇa saṃtarpayāmāsa, na cānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheś cittaṃ nivartitavān* ||
children.translated_text: The moment he fell, he died and was reborn as a great <s>rohita</s> fish in the sandy river. Then the deities proclaimed throughout the entire realm: 'This is the nectar-like remedy for those long tormented by great disease — a great <s>rohita</s> fish has appeared in the sandy river!' Thereupon, upon hearing this, a great multitude of people, with knives in hand, taking baskets, went out and with various sharp instruments began to cut flesh from the living [fish]. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, his body being carved, suffusing them all with loving-kindness, his face wet with tears, reflected: 'How fortunate I am, how well-obtained is this gain, that these beings will find happiness through my flesh and blood!' In this manner, by this means, he nourished beings for twelve years with his own flesh and blood, and did not turn his mind away from supreme perfect awakening.

children.text: yadā teṣāṃ satvānāṃ sa vyādhir upaśāntas tadā tena rohitamatsyena śabda udīritaḥ: śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ satvāḥ | ahaṃ sa rājā padmakaḥ | mayā yuṣmākam arthe svajīvitaparityāgenāyam evaṃvidha ātmabhāva upāttaḥ | mamāntike cittaṃ prasādayadhvam* | yadāham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim
children.translated_text: When the disease of those beings had subsided, that <s>rohita</s> fish uttered this proclamation: 'Hear, good beings! I am that King <s>Padmaka</s>. For your sake, by relinquishing my own life, I have taken on this form of bodily existence. Generate faith in your minds toward me! When I attain supreme perfect awakening,

children.text:
abhisaṃbhotsye, ahaṃ tadā yuṣmān atyantavyādheḥ parimocya atyantaniṣṭhe nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāmīti | tacchravaṇāt sa janakāyo labdhaprasādo rājāmātyapaurāś ca puṣpadhūpamālyavilepanair abhyarcya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ: atiduṣkarakāraka, yadā tvam anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyethāḥ, tadā te vayaṃ śrāvakāḥ syāmeti |
  bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena padmako nāma rājā babhūva, ahaṃ sa | yad evaṃvidhāḥ parityāgāḥ kṛtāḥ, tena me saṃsāre 'nantasukham anubhūtam* | idānīm apy anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ, samapākayā ca grahaṇyā samanvāgataḥ | yena me aśitapītakhāditāsvāditaṃ samyak sukhena pariṇamati | alpābādho rogatātītaś cāsmi | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yat sarvasatveṣu dayāṃ bhāvayiṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text:
I shall then liberate you from the ultimate disease and establish you in the ultimate cessation, <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' Upon hearing this, that multitude of people, having gained faith, together with the king's ministers and citizens, having worshipped with flowers, incense, garlands, and ointments, began to make aspirations: 'O performer of supremely difficult deeds! When you attain supreme perfect awakening, may we become your <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples).'
The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king named <s>Padmaka</s> — that was I. Such were the sacrifices I made, and thereby I experienced immeasurable happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Now too, having attained supreme perfect awakening, I am endowed with even digestion, whereby food and drink consumed and tasted by me is properly and comfortably digested. I am of little illness and have transcended disease. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall cultivate compassion toward all beings." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_32 kavaḍaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_32: <s>Kavaḍa</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: saced bhikṣavaḥ satvā jānīyur dānasya dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākaṃ yathāhaṃ jānāmi dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipakām*, apīdānīṃ yo 'sāv apaścimakaḥ kavaḍaś carama ālopaḥ, tato 'pi nādatvā asaṃvibhajya paribhuñjīta sacel labheta dakṣiṇīyaṃ pratigrāhakam* | na caiṣām utpannaṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhet* | yasmāt tarhi satvā na jānanti dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam*, yathāhaṃ jānāmi dānasya phalaṃ dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam*, tasmāt te adatvā asaṃvibhajya paribhuñjate āgṛhītena cetasā, utpannaṃ caiṣāṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'If, monks, beings knew the fruit and ripening of giving and of sharing gifts as I know the fruit and ripening of giving and of sharing gifts, then even their very last morsel, their final mouthful, they would not consume without giving, without sharing, if they could find a worthy recipient. And no arisen stinginess would persist in dominating their minds. But since, monks, beings do not know the fruit of giving and the ripening of sharing gifts as I know the fruit of giving and the ripening of sharing gifts, therefore they consume without giving, without sharing, with minds possessed [by greed], and arisen stinginess persists in dominating their minds.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | idam uktvā sugato hy athāparam etad uvāca śāstā:
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Having said this, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Teacher, then spoke further:

children.text: evaṃ hi satvā jānīyur yathā proktaṃ maharṣiṇā |
children.translated_text: If beings knew, as declared by the great sage,

children.text: vipākaḥ saṃvibhāgasya yathā bhavati mahārthikaḥ || AVŚ_32.1 ||
children.translated_text: how the ripening of sharing is of great benefit, // AVŚ_32.1 //

children.text: nādatvā paribhuñjīran na syur matsariṇas tathā |
children.translated_text: they would not consume without giving, nor would they be miserly,

children.text: na caiṣām āgrahe cittam utpadyeta kadācana || AVŚ_32.2 ||
children.translated_text: nor would a grasping mind ever arise in them. // AVŚ_32.2 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 81]

children.text: yasmāt tu na prajānanti bālā mohatamovṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: But because the foolish, enveloped in the darkness of delusion, do not understand,

children.text: tasmāt tu bhuñjate satvā āgṛhītena cetasā |
children.translated_text: therefore beings consume with minds possessed [by greed],

children.text: utpannaṃ caiṣāṃ mātsaryaṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati || AVŚ_32.3 ||
children.translated_text: and arisen stinginess persists in dominating their minds. // AVŚ_32.3 //

children.text: yadā bhagavatā etat sūtraṃ bhāṣitaṃ tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavān dānasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate dānasaṃvibhāgasya ca phalavipākam iti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yat tathāgato dānasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate, dānasaṃvibhāgasya phalavipākam iti | yan mayātīte 'dhvani yācanakahetor mukhadvāragataḥ svakavaḍaḥ parityaktaḥ | tac chruṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye 'ham* ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had spoken this <s>sūtra</s>, the monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the <s>Bhagavān</s> speaks in praise of giving and the ripening of sharing gifts!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is so wonderful in this, monks, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks in praise of giving and the ripening of sharing gifts? For in a past age, for the sake of a beggar, I gave up a morsel that was already at my mouth. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* (Speyer: akaṇṭhakam ) | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ kārayati | sa rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ sarvapradaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca | mahatī tyāge vartate | yāvad apareṇa samayena mahaddurbhikṣaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ durbhikṣāntarakalpasadṛśam* | tatas te janakāyā durbhikṣākālabhayabhītāḥ kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhakapolāḥ pretāśrayasadṛśāḥ saṃgamya samāgamyaikasamūhena rājānam upasṛtya jayenāyuṣā vardhayitvocuḥ: deva paritrāyasva asmān asmād durbhikṣabhayāt* | prayaccha jīvitam iti | tato rājā koṣṭḥāgārikaṃ puruṣam āmantritavān*: asti bho puruṣa koṣṭhāgāre annapānaṃ yad asmākaṃ syād eṣāṃ ca janakāyānām*? iti śrutvā koṣṭhāgārika āha: parigaṇya deva sasyāni ākhyāsyāmīti | tato gaṇitakuśalair gaṇanāṃ kṛtvā sarveṣāṃ viṣayanivāsināṃ divase divase ekakavaḍo rājño dvau kavaḍāv iyantaṃ kālaṃ bhaviṣyatīti samākhyātam* | tato rājā janakāyān āhūyoktavān*: tena hi bhavanto divasānudivasam āgatya rājakule kavaḍam abhyavahṛtya gacchateti | tatas te pratidivasam āgatya pratyekam ekaikaṃ kavaḍam abhyavahṛtya yatheṣṭaṃ gacchanti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless (Speyer: <s>akaṇṭhakam</s>). He guarded his kingdom as though it were his only son. That king was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, tender toward his subjects, a giver of all things, a renouncer of everything, one who gave up without attachment, and he practiced great generosity. Then, on a later occasion, a great famine arose, comparable to the famine at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>. The populace, frightened by the terror of famine, emaciated with hunger, their throats and cheeks hollow, resembling the abode of ghosts, assembled and gathered together as one group, approached the king, greeted him with wishes of victory and long life, and said: 'Lord, save us from this dread of famine! Grant us our lives!' Then the king summoned the storekeeper and asked: 'Good man, is there food and drink in the storehouse sufficient for us and for this multitude of people?' Upon hearing this, the storekeeper said: 'Let me count the provisions, Your Majesty, and I shall report.' Then, having the accountants skilled in calculation make a reckoning, it was announced that for all the inhabitants of the realm, at the rate of one morsel per person per day and two morsels for the king, the supplies would last for a certain period. Then the king summoned the people and said: 'In that case, sirs, come each day to the royal court, eat one morsel, and go.' So they came each day, and each person, having eaten one morsel each, went as they pleased.

children.text: athānyatamo brāhmaṇas tasyāṃ gāṇanāyāṃ nāsīt* | parebhyaś ca śrutvā rājānam uvāca: deva janapadagatena me śrutā gaṇanā | dīyatāṃ mamāpi kavaḍa iti | tato rājā svakāt kavaḍadvayād ekaṃ brāhmaṇāya dattavān* | ekaṃ kavaḍaṃ janasāmānyam abhyavahartuṃ pravṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now a certain Brahmin had not been included in that count. Having heard from others, he said to the king: 'Your Majesty, I was in the countryside when the count was made. Let a morsel be given to me as well.' Then the king gave one of his own two morsels to the Brahmin. He then set about eating just one morsel, the same share as the common people.

children.text: śakrasya devendrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate | tasyaitad abhavat*: atiduṣkaraṃ bata vārāṇaseyo rājā karoti, yanv aham enaṃ mīmāṃseyeti | atha śakro devendro brāhmaṇaveṣam ātmānam abhinirmāya bhojanakāle rājānam upasṛptaḥ | jayenāyuṣā ca vardhayitvovāca: bubhukṣito kuruṣva svakakavaḍenānugraham iti | tato rājā svajīvitaparityāgaṃ vyavasāyakāruṇyāt svakavaḍaṃ brāhmaṇāya datvānāhāratāṃ pratipannaḥ | yāvat ṣaḍbhaktacchedā anenopakrameṇa kṛtāḥ | taṃ ca mahājanakāyaṃ bhuñjānaṃ dṛṣṭvā parāṃ prītim āpede | atha śakro devendras taṃ rājño 'tiduṣkaraṃ vyavasāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇaveṣam antardhāpya svena rūpeṇa sthitvā rājānaṃ saṃvardhayāmāsa: sādhu sādhu mahārāja, āvarjitā
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, possesses knowledge-and-vision that operates from below. This thought occurred to him: 'The king of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> is doing something extremely difficult; let me test him.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, transformed himself into the appearance of a Brahmin and approached the king at mealtime. Having greeted him with wishes of victory and long life, he said: 'I am hungry — show me favor with your own morsel.' Then the king, out of his resolve to sacrifice his own life and out of compassion, gave his own morsel to the Brahmin and undertook fasting. In this manner, six meals were foregone. And seeing that great multitude of people eating, he attained the highest joy. Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, seeing the king's extraordinarily difficult resolve, made the Brahmin disguise disappear and, standing in his own form, praised the king: 'Well done, well done, great king! We have been won over
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 82]

children.text: vayaṃ bhavatānena duṣkareṇa vyavasāyena, sanāthaś cāyaṃ janakāya īdṛśena prajāpālakena | na duṣyatāṃ tava vijite sarvabījāni, vāpy antām* | ahaṃ saptame divase tathāvidhaṃ māhendraṃ varṣam utsrakṣyāmi, yena sarvasasyāni niṣpatsyanta iti | rājñā tathā kāritam* | śakreṇāpi tathāvidhaṃ mahendraṃ varṣam utsṛṣṭam*, yena durbhikṣaṃ vinivartitaṃ subhikṣaṃ prādurbhūtam* ||
children.translated_text: by your difficult resolve, and this multitude of people is blessed to have such a protector of subjects! Let all the seeds in your realm not perish, and let them sprout! In seven days I shall release such a <s>Māhendra</s> (great Indra) rain that all crops will ripen.' The king acted accordingly. And <s>Śakra</s> released such a <s>Māhendra</s> rain that the famine was ended and abundance prevailed.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena brahmadatto nāma rājā babhūva, ahaṃ sa | mayā tāny evaṃvidhe durbhikṣe vartamāne svajīvitaparityāgād evaṃvidhāni dānāni dattāni | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad dānāni dāsyāmaḥ puṇyāni kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> — that was I. By me, when such a famine was occurring, through the sacrifice of my own life, such acts of giving were performed. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall give gifts and perform meritorious deeds." Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_33 dharmapālaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_33: <s>Dharmapāla</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | yadā devadattena mohapuruṣeṇa bhagavato vadhārthena dhanapālako hastināga utsṛṣṭaḥ, udapāno viṣacūrṇena cāvakīrṇaḥ, vadhakapuruṣāś cotsṛṣṭāḥ | sa bhagavato dīrgharātraṃ vadhakaḥ pratyarthikaḥ pratyamitraḥ, bhagavāṃś cāsya maitracitto hitacitto 'nukampācittena na pratyupasthitaḥ | tadā bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhagavan yāvad ayaṃ devadatto bhagavato vadhāyodyataḥ, bhagavāṃś cāsya maitracitto hitacitto 'nukampacittenā pratyupasthita iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. When <s>Devadatta</s>, that deluded man, had released the elephant <s>Dhanapālaka</s> to kill the <s>Bhagavān</s>, had poisoned a well, and had sent murderers — he who for a long time had been a killer, adversary, and enemy of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, while the <s>Bhagavān</s> had remained disposed toward him with a mind of loving-kindness, goodwill, and compassion — then the monks asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'See, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how this <s>Devadatta</s> is intent on the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s destruction, yet the <s>Bhagavān</s> remains disposed toward him with a mind of loving-kindness, goodwill, and compassion!'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ tathāgato vigatarāgo vigatadveṣo vigatamohaḥ parimukto jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvākārajñaḥ sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāptaḥ | yat tu mayā atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohena daharakavayasyavasthitena vadhāya parākrāntasyāsyāntike naivaṃ cittaṃ dūṣitam* | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye 'ham* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is so wonderful in this, monks, that now the <s>Tathāgata</s> — free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, omniscient, knowing all modes, having attained mastery over all knowledge and its objects — [remains thus]? But in a past age, when I still had passion, hatred, and delusion, being of a young and boyish disposition, even when he was engaged in violence against me, I did not harbor an evil thought toward him. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | sa rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ sarvapradaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca mahatī tyāge vartate | tasya ca rājño durmatir nāma devī caṇḍā roṣaṇī sāhasikā | ekaputraś ca dharmapālo nāmnā tasyā eva durmatyāḥ sakāśāj jātaḥ | sa ca dharmapālo dayāvān śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless. He protected his kingdom as though it were his only son. That king was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, tender toward his subjects, a giver of all things, a renouncer of everything, one who gave up without attachment, and he practiced great generosity. That king had a queen named <s>Durmatī</s> — cruel, wrathful, and reckless. And she had one son, named <s>Dharmapāla</s>, born from that very <s>Durmatī</s>. And that <s>Dharmapāla</s> was compassionate, faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 83]

children.text: ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ | sarveṣāṃ ca vārāṇaseyānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām iṣṭaḥ kāntaḥ priyo manāpo darśanena | sa copādhyāyasakāśaṃ gatvā dārakaiḥ saha lipiṃ paṭhati ||
children.translated_text: devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, tender toward his subjects. He was dear, beloved, pleasant, and agreeable to all the Brahmins and householders of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> in appearance. And he, having gone to his teacher, was studying writing together with the other boys.

children.text: yāvad rājā apareṇa samayena vasantakālasamaye saṃpuṣpiteṣu pādapeṣu haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīvañjīvakanirghoṣite vanaṣaṇḍe devyā sahāntaḥpuraparivṛta udyānabhūmiṃ nirgataḥ | tatra ca rājña udyāne 'ntaḥpurajanena saha krīḍata īrṣyāroṣaparītā durmatir devī kupitā | rājñā cāsyā ardhaṃ pītakaṃ varjitam* | tayā kupitayā rājcaḥ saṃdeśo visarjitaḥ: putrasyāhaṃ rudhiraṃ pibeyam*, yady ahaṃ tavārdhaṃ pītakaṃ pibeyam iti | kāmān khalu pratisevamānasya nāsti kiṃcit pāpakaṃ karmākaraṇīyam iti | tato rājā brahmadatto dhārmiko 'pi san kāmarāgaparyavasānavigamād antaḥpurajanena sāntvyamāno 'pi krodhāgninā prajvalitaḥ | tatas tena saṃpravṛddhakrodhenājñā dattā: gacchata, dharmapālasya galaṃ chitvā rudhiraṃ pāyayatainām iti ||
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, in the spring season, when the trees were in bloom, the king went out to the garden grounds with his queen, surrounded by the inner household, in a forest grove resounding with the calls of swans, cranes, peacocks, parrots, mynahs, cuckoos, and <s>jīvañjīvaka</s> birds. There, while the king was sporting in the garden with the women of the inner household, the queen <s>Durmati</s> (Ill-Minded), seized by jealousy and anger, became enraged. The king had rejected half of her drink. Furious, she sent a message to the king: 'I would rather drink the blood of my son than drink your half-drunk beverage!' Indeed, for one indulging in sensual pleasures, there is no evil deed too wicked to commit. Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, though righteous, being consumed by the fire of anger at the culmination of his desire and passion, even though pacified by the women of the inner household, with his rage fully grown, issued a command: 'Go! Cut <s>Dharmapāla</s>'s throat and make her drink his blood!'

children.text: tato dārakaśālāvasthito dharmapālaḥ kumāraḥ śrutvā rodituṃ pravṛttaḥ | evaṃ cāha: dhik satvasabhāgatāṃ saṃsāre, yatra nāma krodhavaśād aṅganiḥsṛtam api sutaṃ parityajantīti | tato dharmapālaḥ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaḥ pituḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati: sādhu tāta prasīda | niraparādhaṃ mā māṃ parityākṣīḥ | iṣṭāś ca sarveṣāṃ pitṝṇāṃ putrā iti | rājā kathayati: putraka yadi te mātā kṣamate, aham api kṣame iti | tato dharmapālaḥ prarudan mātuḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ pādayor nipatya kṛtakarapuṭa uvāca: amba kṣamasva, mā māṃ jīvitād vyaparopayeti | sā evaṃ karuṇadīnavilambitair akṣarair ucyamānā na kṣamate | tato vadhyaghātais tīkṣṇena śastreṇa dharmapālasya kumārasya galaṃ chitvā durmatir devī rudhiraṃ pāyitā | na ca durmatyā vipratisāro jātaḥ | dharmapālo 'pi kumāro mātāpitṛvadhyaghāteṣu cittaṃ prasādya kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Dharmapāla</s>, who was in the nursery, upon hearing this, began to weep. And he said: 'Alas for the state of being a living being in <s>saṃsāra</s>, where, overcome by anger, one would abandon even a son born from one's own body!' Then <s>Dharmapāla</s>, adorned with all his ornaments, fell at his father's feet and said: 'Please, father, be gracious! Do not abandon me, who am without fault! Sons are dear to all fathers.' The king replied: 'Son, if your mother forgives you, I too shall forgive.' Then <s>Dharmapāla</s>, weeping, approached his mother, fell at her feet, and with palms joined said: 'Mother, please forgive me! Do not deprive me of my life!' But she, though addressed with such pitiable, plaintive, and hesitant words, would not relent. Then the executioners, with a sharp weapon, cut the throat of Prince <s>Dharmapāla</s>, and the queen <s>Durmati</s> was made to drink his blood. Nor did <s>Durmati</s> feel any remorse. And Prince <s>Dharmapāla</s> too, having generated a mind of faith toward his parents and the executioners, passed away.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena dharmapālo nāma kumāro babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | sā durmatir devī, eṣa devadattaḥ | tadāpi me vadhakahastagatenāsya maitraṃ cittam utpāditam* | idānīm apy aham asya vadhāyodyatasya maitracitto hitacittaḥ anukampācittaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yat sarvasatveṣu maitraṃ cittaṃ bhāvayiṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the prince named <s>Dharmapāla</s> — that was I.
