The queen <s>Durmati</s> — that is <s>Devadatta</s>. Even then, when I was in the hands of my executioner, I generated a mind of friendliness toward him. And now too, toward him who is intent on killing me, I am one of friendly mind, benevolent mind, compassionate mind. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall cultivate a mind of friendliness toward all beings." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_34 śibiḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_34: <s>Śibi</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick,

children.text: saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ dvau saṃnipātau bhavataḥ | eka āṣāḍhyāṃ varṣopanāyikāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ kārtikyāṃ pūrṇamāsyām* | tatra bhikṣavaḥ pātrāṇi pacanti, cīvarāṇi dhāvayanti, pāṃsukūlāni ca sīvyanti | yāvad anyatamo bhikṣuś cīvaraṃ syotukāmaḥ sūcīchidraṃ sūtrakaṃ na śaknoti pratipādayitum* | sa karuṇadīnavilambitair akṣarair uvāca: ko loke puṇyakāma iti | bhagavāṃś cāsya nātidūre caṃkrame caṃkramyate | tato bhagavān gambhīramadhuraviśadakalaviṅkamanojñadundubhinirghoṣo gajabhujasadṛśabāhum abhiprasārya kathayati: ahaṃ bhikṣo loke puṇyakāma iti | tato 'sau bhikṣur bhagavataḥ pañcāṅgopetaṃ svaram upaśrutya saṃbhrāntas tvaritatvaritaṃ bhagavataḥ pāṇiṃ gṛhītvā svaśirasi sthāpayitvāha: bhagavan*, anena te pāṇinā trīṇi kalpāsaṃkhyeyāni dānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñā upacitāḥ | atha ca punar bhagavān enam āha: atṛpto 'haṃ bhikṣo puṇyaiḥ, labdharaso 'haṃ bhikṣo puṇyaiḥ, ato me tṛptir nāstīti ||
children.translated_text: together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the monks had two assemblies. The first was on the full-moon day of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> at the beginning of the rains-retreat; the second was on the full-moon day of <s>Kārttika</s>. At that assembly, the monks were firing their bowls, washing their robes, and sewing their rag-robes. A certain monk, wishing to sew his robe, was unable to thread the thread through the eye of the needle. He said with pitiable, plaintive, and halting words: 'Who in this world desires merit?' The Blessed One was walking on the walkway not far from him. Then the Blessed One, with a voice deep, sweet, clear, beautiful as a <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow) bird, delightful as a drum, extending his arm like the trunk of an elephant, said: 'I, monk, am one who desires merit in this world.' Then that monk, having heard the Blessed One's voice endowed with the five qualities, startled and in haste, took the Blessed One's hand and placed it on his own head, saying: 'Blessed One, with this very hand of yours, over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, you have accumulated <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (effort), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).' And yet the Blessed One said to him: 'I am unsatisfied with merit, monk; I have tasted the flavor of merit, monk, and therefore I have no satiety.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavān puṇyamayaiḥ, saṃskārair atṛpta iti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ tathāgato vigatarāgo vigatadveṣo vigatamohaḥ parimukto jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvākārajñaḥ sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāptaḥ | yat tv aham atīte 'dhvani sarāgaḥ sadveṣaḥ samohK‍h̲ 'parimukto jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyo tṛptaḥ puṇyamayaiḥ saṃskāraiḥ | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye 'ham* ||
children.translated_text: The monks, filled with curiosity, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the Blessed One is unsatisfied with meritorious formations!' The Blessed One said: 'What is so astonishing in this, monks, that now the <s>Tathāgata</s>, free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, omniscient, knowing all aspects, having attained mastery over all knowledge and the knowable [is unsatisfied with merit]? But when in the past I was with passion, with hatred, with delusion, not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, even then I was not satisfied with meritorious formations. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapurvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani śibighoṣāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ śibir nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | sa ca śibī rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ sarvapradaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca | mahatī tyāge vartate | sa kalyam (Speyer: kālyam ) evotthāya yajñavāṭaṃ praviśya annam annārthibhyaḥ prayacchati, vastraṃ vastrārthibhyaḥ | dhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarnamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālādīnāṃ (Speyer: ŚpravāḍāŚ ) parityāgaṃ karoti | na cāsau puṇyamayaiḥ saṃskārais tṛptiṃ gacchati | so 'ntaḥpuraṃ praviśyāntaḥpurajanasya bhaktācchādanaṃ prayacchati, kumārāṇām amātyānāṃ bhaṭabalāgrasya naigamajānapadānām* ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in the royal capital of <s>Śibighoṣā</s>, a king named <s>Śibi</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless. He ruled the kingdom as though it were his only son. That King <s>Śibi</s> was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition, devoted to his own welfare and that of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>, affectionate toward his subjects, a giver of everything, a renouncer of everything, one who gave without attachment. He engaged in great generosity. Rising early in the morning, he entered the sacrifice-hall and gave food to those who sought food, garments to those who sought garments. He made gifts of wealth, grain, gold, silver, jewels, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch-shells, crystal, coral, and the like. Yet he was not satisfied with meritorious formations. Entering the inner chambers, he provided food and clothing to the women of the inner household, to the princes, to the ministers, to the soldiers and the army, and to the townspeople and country-dwellers.'

children.text: atha rājñaḥ śiber etad abhavat*: saṃtarpitā anena manuṣyabhūtāḥ, kṣudrajanto 'vaśiṣṭāḥ, kena saṃtarpayitavyā iti | sa parityaktavibhavasarvasva ekaśāṭakanivasitaḥ svaśarīrāvaśeṣaś cintām āpede | tasyaitad abhavat: kṣudrajantubhyaḥ svaśarīram anuprayacchāmīti | sa śastreṇa svaśarīraṃ takṣayitvā yatra daṃśamaśakās tatrotsṛṣṭakāyaḥ pratiṣṭhate | priyam ivaikaputrakaṃ rudhireṇa saṃtarpayati ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śibi</s> thought: 'The human beings have been satisfied by me; the small creatures remain — by what shall they be satisfied?' Having renounced all his wealth and possessions, clad in a single garment, with only his own body remaining, he fell into thought. He thought: 'I shall offer my own body to the small creatures.' With a weapon he cut into his own body and, where the flies and mosquitoes were, he set his body down and remained still. He nourished them with his blood, as if they were his beloved only son.

children.text: śakrasya devendrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate | tasyaitad bahavat*: kim ayaṃ śibī rājā satvānām artham evaṃ karoti, uta karuṇayā? yanv aham enaṃ vijñāseyeti | tato bhinnāñjanam asivarṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Knowledge-and-vision arose in <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, below [in his heaven]. He thought: 'Is this King <s>Śibi</s> doing this for the sake of beings, or out of compassion? Let me test him.' Then, taking the form of a vulture, dark as collyrium, black as a sword blade,

children.text: gṛdhraveśam ātmānam abhinirmāya rājñe śibeḥ sakāśam upasaṃkramya mukhatuṇḍakenākṣyutpāṭayituṃ pravṛttaḥ | na ca rājā saṃtrāsam āpadyate | kiṃ tu maitrīviśālābhyāṃ nayanābhyāṃ taṃ gṛdhram ālokya kathayati: vatsa, yan madīyāc charīrāt prayuñjase, tena praṇayaḥ kriyatām iti | tataḥ āvarjitaḥ śakro devendro brāhmaṇaveṣam ātmānam abhinirmāya rājñaḥ śibeḥ purastāt sthitvā: sādhu pārthiva, dīyatām etan nayanadvayam iti | rājovāca: mahābrāhmaṇa gṛhyatāṃ yad abhirucitam*, na me 'tra vighnaḥ kaścid astīti | tataḥ śakro devendro bhūyasyā mātrayābhiprasanno brāhmaṇaveṣam antardhāpya svarūpeṇa sthitvā rājānam abhyutsāhayann uvāca: sādhu sādhu bhoḥ pārthiva, suniścitā te buddhiḥ, akampyas te praṇidhiḥ; anugatā te satveṣu mahākaruṇā, yatra nāma tvaṃ saṃtrāsakareṣu dharmeṣu viśāradoḥ | na cirāt tvam anena vyavasāyenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase ||
children.translated_text: he approached King <s>Śibi</s> and with his beak began to gouge out his eye. The king felt no alarm. Rather, gazing at that vulture with eyes broad with loving-kindness, he said: 'Dear one, of what belongs to my body you may make use — take it as you please.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, won over [by his virtue], assumed the form of a Brahmin and, standing before King <s>Śibi</s>, said: 'Well done, O king! Give me these two eyes.' The king replied: 'Great Brahmin, take whatever pleases you; there is no obstacle on my part.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of gods, greatly pleased beyond measure, concealed his Brahmin disguise, stood in his own form, and encouraged the king, saying: 'Well done, well done, O king! Your resolve is firmly established, your aspiration is unshakable; your great compassion follows beings, inasmuch as you are fearless in terrifying circumstances! Before long, by this resolve of yours, you shall attain supreme perfect awakening.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena śibir nāma rājā babhūva, ahaṃ sa | tadānīm api puṇyamayaiḥ saṃskārais tṛptir nāsti, prāg evedānīm* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad dānāni dāsyāmaḥ, puṇyāni kariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king named <s>Śibi</s> — that was I. Even then I was not satisfied with meritorious formations — how much less so now! Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall give gifts and perform merit." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_35 surūpaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_35: <s>Surūpa</s> (Beautiful). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | yadā bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadā madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam*, anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoty āneñjamānair (Speyer: aniñjamānair )indriyaiḥ, tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta yāvad dharmaratnasyāmī bhājanabhūtāḥ satvā ādareṇa śrotavyaṃ manyanta iti | bhagavān āha: yathā tathāgatena bhikṣava ādarajātena dharmaḥ śrutaś codgṛhītaś ca, tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. When the Blessed One, having risen from meditation, taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies in a most sweet manner — pure as honey without beeswax — and the assembly of many hundreds heard the most sweet <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One's presence with unwavering faculties, then the monks, filled with curiosity, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, how these beings, who are vessels for the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, consider it worthy to be heard with attention!' The Blessed One said: 'Just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, monks, heard and memorized the <s>Dharma</s> with earnestness, so listen, attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapurvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ surūpo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | sa ca rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ sarvapradaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca | mahatī tyāge vartate | tasya ca rājñaḥ sundarikā nāma devī abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Surūpa</s> (Handsome) was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and free from thorns. He guarded the kingdom as if it were his only son. That king was faithful, virtuous, of noble intention, devoted to the welfare of himself and others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, fond of his subjects, a giver of all, a renouncer of all, one who renounced without attachment. He was engaged in great generosity. That king had a queen named <s>Sundarikā</s> (Beautiful One) — lovely, attractive, inspiring faith,

children.text: sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā, sundarakaś ca nāmnā ekaputraḥ iṣṭaḥ kāntaḥ priyo manāpaḥ kṣānto 'pratikūlaḥ | athāpareṇa samayena rājñaḥ surūpasya dharme abhilāṣa utpannaḥ | tena sarve amātyāḥ saṃnipātyoktāḥ: paryeṣata me grāmaṇyo dharmān, dharmo me rocata iti | tatas te amātyāḥ kṛtakarapuṭā rājānaṃ vijñāpayanti: durlabho mahārāja dharmaḥ | śrūyate mahārāja buddhānāṃ loke utpādād dharmasyotpādo bhavatīti | tato rājñā suvarṇapiṭakaṃ dhvajāgre baddhvā sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam*: yo me dharmaṃ vakṣyati, tasyemaṃ suvarṇapiṭakaṃ dāsyāmi, mahatā ca satkāreṇa satkariṣyāmīti | tato bahavaḥ kālā atikrāntāḥ | na ca kaścid dharmadeśaka upalabhyate | tataḥ sa rājā dharmahetor utkaṇṭhati paritapyati ||
children.translated_text: endowed with all limbs and parts — and an only son named <s>Sundara</s> (Beautiful), who was beloved, dear, cherished, pleasant, patient, and agreeable. Then, on a later occasion, a longing for the <s>Dharma</s> arose in King <s>Surūpa</s>. He assembled all his ministers and said: 'Search for the <s>Dharma</s> for me, O officials — the <s>Dharma</s> delights me.' Then those ministers, with palms joined, informed the king: 'The <s>Dharma</s> is rare, great king. It is heard, great king, that the <s>Dharma</s> arises in the world only when <s>Buddhas</s> arise.' Then the king had a golden casket tied to the top of a flagstaff and a bell-proclamation made throughout his entire realm: 'Whoever will teach me the <s>Dharma</s>, to him I shall give this golden casket and honor him with great reverence.' But many ages passed, and no teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> could be found. Then the king was anxious and distressed on account of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text:
śakrasya ca devānām indrasyādhastāj jñanadarśanaṃ pravartate | sa paśyati rājānaṃ dharmahetor vihanyamānam* | tasyaitad abhavat*: yanv ahaṃ surūpāṃ rājānam mīmāṃseyeti | tato yakṣarūpam ātmānam abhinirmāya vikṛtakaracaraṇanayano 'nekapariṣanmadhyagataṃ rājānam etad avocat*: nanu dharmābhilāṣī bhavān*, aham te dharmaṃ vakṣyāmīti | tato dharmaśravaṇāt prītiprāmodyajāto rājā yakṣam etad uvāca: brūhi guhyaka dharmān śroṣyāmīti | guhyaka uvāca: sukhitasya bata mahārāja dharmā abhilasanti | bubhukṣito 'smi bhojanaṃ tāvan me prayaccheti | tac chrutvā rājā pauruṣeyānām amantrayāmāsa: ānīyantām asya bhakṣyabhojyaprakārā iti | yakṣa āha: sadyohatarudhiramāṃsabhakṣyo 'ham* | etaṃ me sundaram ekaputrakaṃ prayaccheti | śrutvā rājā paraṃ viṣādam āpannaḥ: kadācit karhicin me 'dya dharmaśabda āsāditaḥ | so 'py anargheṇa mūlyeneti | tataḥ sundaraḥ kumāras tad upaśrutya pituḥ pādayor nipatya rājānam vijñāpayāmāsa: marṣaya deva | pūryatāṃ devasyābhiprāyam*, prayaccha māṃ guhyakāyāhārārtham iti | tato rājā tam ekaputrakam iṣṭaṃ kāntaṃ priyaṃ manāpaṃ kṣāntam apratikūlaṃ dharmasyārthe yakṣāya dattavān* |
  tato yakṣeṇa ṛddhibalādhānād rajñaḥ parṣadaś ca tathā darśito yathāṅgapratyaṅgāni pṛthagvikṛtya bhakṣitāni, rudhiraṃ ca pīyamānam* | # # # dṛṣṭvā rājā dharmābhilāṣī na niṣādam āpannaḥ | sa guhyako rājānam uvāca: atṛpto 'smi bhoḥ pārthiva, bhūyo me prayaccheti | tato rājā tasmai dayitāṃ bhāryāṃ dattavān* | sāpi tenaivākāreṇa darśitā | tato bhūyo rājānam uvācā: bho pārthiva, adyāpi tṛptir na labhyata iti | tato rājā yakṣam uvāca: vatsa datto me ekaputrako bhāryā ca dayitā, kiṃ bhūyaḥ prārthayase iti | guhyaka uvāca: svaśarīraṃ me prayaccha | anena tṛptim upayāsyāmīti | rājovāca: yadi svaśarīraṃ te pradāsyāmi, kathaṃ punar dharmaṃ śroṣyāmi? kiṃ nu pūrvaṃ me dharmaṃ vada, paścād gṛhītadharmā śarīraṃ parityakṣyāmīti | tato guhyakena rājānaṃ pratijñāyāṃ pratiṣṭḥāpyānekaśatāyāḥ pariṣadaḥ purastād dharmo deśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now knowledge-and-vision arose below in <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods. He saw the king tormented by his longing for the <s>Dharma</s>. This thought occurred to him: 'Let me test King <s>Surūpa</s>.' Then, having magically created himself in the form of a <s>yakṣa</s> — with distorted hands, feet, and eyes — he appeared in the midst of the many assemblies and said to the king: 'Are you not one who desires the <s>Dharma</s>? I shall teach you the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then the king, filled with joy and delight at the prospect of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, said to the <s>yakṣa</s>: 'Speak, O <s>Guhyaka</s>, I shall listen to the <s>Dharma</s>.' The <s>Guhyaka</s> said: 'It is easy for the comfortable to desire the <s>Dharma</s>, great king. I am hungry — first give me food.' Hearing this, the king addressed his attendants: 'Let varieties of food and drink be brought for him.' The <s>yakṣa</s> said: 'I eat the flesh and blood of the freshly slain. Give me this beautiful only son of yours.' Hearing this, the king was plunged into the deepest sorrow: 'Only once, ever, have I encountered the word of the <s>Dharma</s> — and even that comes at a priceless cost.' Then Prince <s>Sundara</s>, having overheard this, fell at his father's feet and petitioned the king: 'Be patient, Your Majesty. Let the king's intention be fulfilled — give me to the <s>Guhyaka</s> for his food.' Then the king gave that only son — beloved, dear, cherished, pleasant, patient, and agreeable — to the <s>yakṣa</s> for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>yakṣa</s>, by the power of his supernatural ability, displayed to the king and his assembly how, having torn the limbs and parts asunder, he devoured them, and how blood was being drunk. ### Having seen this, the king, desirous of the <s>Dharma</s>, was not cast into despair. The <s>Guhyaka</s> said to the king: 'I am not sated, O lord of the earth — give me more.' Then the king gave him his beloved wife. She too was shown [being devoured] in the same manner. Then again he said to the king: 'O lord of the earth, even now satisfaction is not obtained.' Then the king said to the <s>yakṣa</s>: 'Child, I have given my only son and my beloved wife — what more do you desire?' The <s>Guhyaka</s> said: 'Give me your own body. With that I shall be satisfied.' The king said: 'If I give you my own body, how then shall I hear the <s>Dharma</s>? First teach me the <s>Dharma</s>, and then, having grasped the <s>Dharma</s>, I shall relinquish my body.' Then the <s>Guhyaka</s>, having made the king stand firm in his promise, taught the <s>Dharma</s> before the assembly of many hundreds:

children.text: priyebhyo jāyate śokaḥ priyebhyo jāyate bhayam* |
children.translated_text: 'From the dear ones arises grief; from the dear ones arises fear;

children.text: priyebhyo vipramuktānāṃ nāsti śokaḥ kuto bhayam iti || AVŚ_35.1 ||
children.translated_text: for those who are freed from the dear ones, there is no grief — whence then fear?' // AVŚ_35.1 //

children.text: tato rājā asyā gāthāyāḥ sahaśravaṇāt prahlāditamanāḥ prītisaumanasyendriyajāto yakṣam uvāca: idaṃ guhyaka śarīram*, yatheṣṭaṃ kriyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, his mind gladdened at the very hearing of this verse, filled with joy, gladness, and delight, said to the <s>yakṣa</s>: 'Here is my body, O <s>Guhyaka</s> — do with it as you please.'

children.text: tataḥ śakro devendro rājānaṃ meruvadakampyam anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau viditvā yakṣarūpam antardhāpya svarūpeṇa sthitvā prasādavikasitābhyāṃ nayanābhyām ekena pāṇinā putraṃ gṛhītvā dvitīyena ca bhāryāṃ rājānam abhyutsāhayann uvāca: sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa | dṛḍhasaṃnāhas tvam* | nacirād anena vyavasāyena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase | ayaṃ ca te iṣṭajanasamāgama iti | tato rājā śakraṃ devendram idam avocat*: sādhu sādhu kauśika, kṛto 'smākaṃ dharmābhiprāyaḥ pūritaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, recognizing the king as unshakable as Mount <s>Meru</s> in his resolve for supreme, perfect awakening, made the <s>yakṣa</s>-form disappear and, standing in his own form, with eyes blooming with faith, holding the son in one hand and the wife in the other, encouraging the king, said: 'Excellent, excellent, O noble one! Your resolve is firm. Before long, by this determination, you shall attain supreme, perfect awakening. And here is the reunion with your beloved ones.' Then the king said to <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Kauśika</s>! Our intention regarding the <s>Dharma</s> has been accomplished and fulfilled.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena surūpo nāma rājā babhūva, ahaṃ sa | sundaraḥ kumāra ānandaḥ | sundarikā eṣā eva yaśodharā | tadāpi me bhikṣavo dharmahetor iṣṭabandhuparityāgaḥ svajīvitaparityāgaś ca kṛtaḥ, prāg evedānīm* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad dharmaṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | dharmaṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king named <s>Surūpa</s> — that was I. Prince <s>Sundara</s> was <s>Ānanda</s>. <s>Sundarikā</s> was this very <s>Yaśodharā</s>. Even then, monks, for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>, the renunciation of beloved kinsmen and the renunciation of my own life were performed by me — how much more so now! Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the <s>Dharma</s>. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the <s>Dharma</s>, we shall dwell relying upon it." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

children.text: AVŚ_36 maitrakanyakaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_36: <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: sabrahmakāṇi bhikṣavas tāni kulāni yeṣu kuleṣu mātāpitarau samyaṅ mānyete, samyak pūjyete, samyak sukhena parihriyete | tat kasya hetoḥ? brahmabhūtau hi kulaputrasya mātāpitarau sahadharmeṇa | sācāryakāṇi tāni kulāni yeṣu kuleṣu mātāpitarau samyaṅ mānyete, samyak pūjyete, samyak sukhena parihriyete | tat kasya hetoḥ? ācāryabhūtau hi kulaputrasya mātāpitarau sahadharmeṇa | āhavanīyāni tāni kulāni yeṣu kuleṣu mātāpitarau samyaṅ mānyete, samyak pūjyete, samyak sukhena parihriyete | tat kasya hetoḥ? āhavanīyau hi kulaputrasya
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jeta's</s> Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Those families, monks, where mother and father are properly honored, properly worshipped, and properly cared for with comfort — those families dwell with <s>Brahmā</s>. Why is that? Because, for a son of good family, mother and father are like <s>Brahmā</s> in their nature. Those families dwell with a teacher. Why is that? Because, for a son of good family, mother and father are like a teacher in their nature. Those families dwell with the <s>āhavanīya</s> (the sacred offering-fire). Why is that? Because, for a son of good family,

children.text: mātāpitarau sahadharmeṇa | sāgnikāni tāni kulāni yeṣu kuleṣu mātāpitarau samyaṅ mānyete, samyak pūjyete, samyak sukhena parihriyete | tat kasya hetoḥ? agnibhūtau hi kulaputrasya mātāpitarau sahadharmeṇa | sadevakāni tāni kulāni yeṣu kuleṣu mātāpitarau samyaṅ mānyete, samyak pūjyete, samyak sukhena parihriyete | tat kasya hetoḥ? devabhūtau hi kulaputrasya mātāpitarau sahadharmeṇa | idam avocad bhagavān* | idam uktvā sugato hy athāparam etad uvāca śāstā:
children.translated_text: mother and father are like the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire in their nature. Those families dwell with fire. Why is that? Because, for a son of good family, mother and father are like fire in their nature. Those families dwell with the gods. Why is that? Because, for a son of good family, mother and father are like gods in their nature.' This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Having said this, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Teacher, said further:

children.text: brahmā hi mātāpitarau pūrvācāryau tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: 'Mother and father are <s>Brahmā</s>, and likewise the first teachers;

children.text: āhavanīyau putrasya agniḥ syād daivatāni ca || AVŚ_36.1 ||
children.translated_text: they are the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire for the son, and fire itself, and divinities. // AVŚ_36.1 //

children.text: tasmād etau namasyeta satkuryāc caiva paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, the wise one should pay them homage and honor them —

children.text: udvartanena snānena pādānāṃ dhāvanena ca |
children.translated_text: with massaging, bathing, washing of feet,

children.text: athavā annapānena vastraśayyāsanena ca || AVŚ_36.2||
children.translated_text: or with food and drink, with clothing, bedding, and seats. // AVŚ_36.2 //

children.text: tayā sa paricaryayā mātāpitṛṣu paṇḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'By that service to mother and father, the wise one

children.text: iha cānindito bhavati pretya svarge ca modate || AVŚ_36.3 ||
children.translated_text: is blameless in this world, and after death rejoices in heaven.' // AVŚ_36.3 //

children.text: yadā bhagavatā etat sūtraṃ bhāṣitam*, tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavān mātāpitṛguruśuśrūṣāvarṇavādīti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ tathāgato vigatarāgo vigatadveṣo vigatamohaḥ parimukto jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvākārajñaḥ sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāpto mātāpitṛguruśuśrūṣāyā varṇavādī | yat tu mayā atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ mātuḥ svalpam apakāraṃ kṛtvā mahaduḥkham anubhūtam* | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had spoken this <s>sūtra</s>, the monks, their doubts aroused, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the <s>Bhagavān</s> speaks in praise of devotion to parents and teachers!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is so wonderful, monks, that now the <s>Tathāgata</s> — free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, omniscient, knowing all modes, having attained mastery over all knowledge — speaks in praise of devotion to parents and teachers? But in a past age, when I still had passion, hatred, and delusion, was not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — having done a slight wrong to my mother, I experienced great suffering. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapurvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ mitro nāma sārthavāho babhūva āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putrā jāyante mriyante cā | sa kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham* | na me putro na duhitā | mamātyayāt sarvasvāpateyam aputrakam iti kṛtvā rājño vidheyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | tasya vayasyakenopadiṣṭam*: yadi te putrā jāyante, tasya dārikānāma sthāpayitavyam* | evam asau cirajīvī bhaviṣyatīti | so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate | tadyathā ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ | sahajāḥ sahadhārmikā nityānubaddhā api devatā āyācate | asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti | tac ca naivam* | yady evam abhaviṣyad ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ | api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti | katameṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānām*? mātāpitarāu raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau, mātā {ca} kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī |
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a caravan-leader named <s>Mitra</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He took a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, sons were born to him but they died. Resting his cheek on his hand, he stood absorbed in worry: 'My house is full of manifold wealth, yet I have no son, no daughter. After my death, all my property, being without an heir, will become subject to the king.' A friend advised him: 'When sons are born to you, you should give [the child] a girl's name. In this way, the child will be long-lived.' He, sonless but longing for a son, prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other particular deities — such as garden deities, forest deities, crossroad deities, intersection deities, and deities who receive <s>bali</s> offerings. He also prayed to the innate deities, those sharing the same <s>dharma</s>, and those constantly attendant. And there is this popular saying in the world that sons and daughters are born through the power of prayer. But that is not so. If it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just as a <s>Cakravartin</s> king does. Rather, it is from the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. What are those three conditions? The parents are passionate and have come together, the mother is healthy and in her fertile period,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 89]

children.text:
gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati | eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | sa ca āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati | anyatamaś ca satvo 'nyatamasmāt satvanikāyāc cyutaḥ tasya prajāpatyā kukṣim avakrāntaḥ | paṃcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme | katame paṃca | raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti, viraktaṃ {puruṣaṃ} jānāti | kālaṃ jānāti, ṛtuṃ jānāti | garbham avakrāntaṃ jānāti | yasya sakāśād garbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti | dārakaṃ jānāti | dārikāṃ jānāti | saced dārako bhavati dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | saced dārikā bhavati vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | sā āttamanāttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati: diṣṭyāryaputra vardhase | āpannasatvāsmi saṃvṛttā | yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti | so 'py āttamanāttamanāḥ pūrvakāyam abhyunnamayya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya udānam udānayati: apy evāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam* | jāto me syān nāvajātaḥ | kṛtyāni me kurvīta | bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyāt | dāyād yaṃ pratipadyeta | kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt* | asmākaṃ cāpy atītakālagatānām alpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā asmākaṃ nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādekṣyati: idaṃ tayor yatratatropapannayor gacchator anugacchatv iti | āpannasatvāṃ caināṃ viditvopariprāsādatalagatām ayantritāṃ dhārayati | śīte śītopakaraṇair uṣṇe uṣṇopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptair āhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhārair hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīm apsarasam iva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcān mañcaṃ pīṭhāt pīṭham anavatarantīm adharāṃ bhūmim* | na cāsyāḥ kiṃcid amanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ yāvad eva garbhasya paripākāya | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaś chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhur vistīrṇalalāṭa uccaghoṣaḥ saṃgatabrūs tuṅganāsaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: ayaṃ dārako mitrasya
putraḥ kanyā ca | tasmād bhavatu dārakasya maitrakanyako nāmeti ||
children.translated_text: and a <s>Gandharva</s> (spirit seeking rebirth) is present. From the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born. And he continued devoted to prayer. A certain being, having died from a certain class of beings, entered the womb of his wife. There are five distinctive qualities in a certain wise type of woman. What five? She knows when a man is passionate, she knows when he is dispassionate; she knows the right time, she knows the fertile period; she knows when a conception has occurred; she knows from whom the conception has taken place; she knows whether it is a boy; she knows whether it is a girl. If it is a boy, it rests on the right side of the womb. If it is a girl, it rests on the left side of the womb. She, overjoyed, announced to her husband: 'Congratulations, noble husband! I have become pregnant. And since it rests on the right side of my womb, it will surely be a boy.' He too, overjoyed, raising his upper body and extending his right arm, uttered this joyful exclamation: 'May I indeed behold the long-desired face of a son! May a son be born to me, not stillborn. May he perform my duties. May he, having been supported, support me in return. May he receive the inheritance. May my family lineage endure for a long time. And when we too have passed away, may he, having given gifts and performed meritorious deeds, whether few or many, dedicate the merit in our name: "May this reach those two, wherever they may be reborn."' Having learned that she was pregnant, he kept her on the upper floor of the palace, carefully attended, providing her in the cold season with things suitable for the cold, in the hot season with things suitable for the heat, with foods prescribed by physicians — not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent, with foods free from bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent [excess] — her limbs adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>Apsaras</s> wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, not descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the lower floor. Nor was any unpleasant sound allowed to reach her ears, until the embryo had fully matured. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, fair-complexioned, of golden hue, with a parasol-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, a resonant voice, joined eyebrows, a prominent nose, endowed with all major and minor limbs. At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'This boy is the son of <s>Mitra</s>, and [he is to be called] a girl.' Therefore, let the boy's name be <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>.

children.text: maitrakanyako dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍena anyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | pitā cāsya mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ, tatraiva ca nidhanam upayātaḥ | yadā maitrakanyako mahān saṃvṛtas tadā mātaram uvāca: amba pitāsmākaṃ kiṃkarmaphalopajīvī āsīt? tataḥ paścād aham api (Speyer: ahaṃ pi ) tathā kariṣyāmīti | mātā kathayati: putraka pitā te okkarika āsīt* | ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ tvam okkarikatvaṃ kuru | sā cintayati: yady aham asmai vakṣyāmi mahāsamudravaṇig āsīd iti, eṣo 'pi kadācin mahāsamudram avatīrṇas tatraiva nidhanam upagacched iti ||
children.translated_text: The boy <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, yogurt, butter, ghee, the cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. And his father had set out upon the great ocean, and there he met his end. When <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> had grown up, he said to his mother: 'Mother, what was our father's livelihood? Afterwards, I too shall do the same.' The mother said: 'Son, your father was a cake-maker.' 'If that is your wish, then become a cake-maker.' She thought to herself: 'If I tell him he was an ocean-going merchant, he too might someday set out upon the great ocean and meet his end there.'

children.text: tenaukkarikāpaṇo vyavasthāpitaḥ | tataḥ prathame divase catvāraḥ kārṣāpaṇāḥ saṃpannāḥ | te 'pi tena mātur niryātitāḥ: ebhir amba śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakān pratipādayasveti |
children.translated_text: He established a cake-shop. Then, on the first day, four <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins) were earned. He gave them to his mother, saying: 'With these, mother, give to <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, and wanderers.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 90]

children.text: yāvad apareṇocyate: pitā te gāndhikāpaṇika āsīd iti, tenaukkaritvaṃ tyaktvā gāndhikāpaṇo vyavasthāpitaḥ | aṣṭau kārṣāpaṇāḥ saṃpannāḥ | te 'pi tena mātur niryātitāḥ | yāvad apareṇocyate: pitā te hairaṇyika āsīd iti, tena tamāpaṇaṃ tyaktvā hairaṇyikāpaṇo vyavasthāpitaḥ | tataḥ prathame divase ṣoḍaśa kārṣāpaṇāḥ saṃpannāḥ | te 'pi tena mātur niryātitāḥ | dvitīye divase dvātriṃśat kārṣāpaṇāḥ saṃpannāḥ | te 'pi tena mātur niryātitāḥ | yāvad dhairaṇyikair īrṣyāprakṛtaiḥ sarvān adhiṣṭhānavyavahārān viditvoktaḥ: maitrakanyaka, kiṃ tavānayā adharmajīvikayā? pitā te mahāsamudravaṇig āsīt* | kena tvaṃ kusaṃvyavahāre niyukta iti | sa hairaṇyikavacanasaṃcodito mātur gatvā kathayati: amba evam anuśrūyate pitāsmākaṃ mahāsamudravaṇig āsīd iti | tad anujānīhi, aham api mahāsamudram avatariṣyāmīti | mātā kathayati: evam etat putraka | kiṃ tu tvaṃ bāla ekaputrakaś ca | mā māṃ parityajya mahāsamudram avatariṣyasīti | sa īrṣyāprakṛtibhir akalyāṇamitrair vipralabdho na nivartate | tatas tena mātur vacanam avacanaṃ kṛtvā vārāṇasyām nagaryāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam*: śṛṇvantu bhavanto vārāṇasīnivāsino vaṇijaḥ: maitrakanyakaḥ sārthavāho mahāsamudram avatariṣyati | ye yuṣmākam utsahante maitrakanyakena sārthavāhena sārdham aśulkenāgulmenātarapaṇyena mahāsamudram avatartum*, te mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānayantv iti | sa kṛtakutūhalamaṅgalasvastyayanaḥ pañcavaṇikśataparivāraḥ śakaṭair bhārair mūṭaiḥ piṭakaiḥ uṣṭrair gobhir gardabhaiḥ mahāsamudragamanīyaṃ paṇyaṃ samudānīya saṃprasthitaḥ | mātā cāsya snehavyākulahṛdayā sāśrusurdinavadanā pādayor lagnā: putraka mā māṃ parityajya mahāsamudram avatareti | atha sa evaṃ karuṇadīnavilambitair alpākṣarair (Speyer: apy akṣarair ) ucyamānaḥ kṛtavyavasāyo mātaraṃ pādena śirasy abhihatya sārthasahāyaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ | mātrā coktaḥ: mā me putraka asya karmaṇo vipākam anubhavethā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then someone told him: 'Your father was a perfume-dealer.' So he abandoned the cake trade and established a perfume-shop. Eight <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> were earned. These too he gave to his mother. Then someone told him: 'Your father was a gold-dealer.' So he abandoned that shop and established a gold-dealer's shop. On the first day, sixteen <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> were earned. These too he gave to his mother. On the second day, thirty-two <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> were earned. These too he gave to his mother. Then the gold-dealers, being of a jealous disposition, having learned of all his commercial activities, said to him: '<s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, what is this unlawful livelihood of yours? Your father was an ocean-going merchant. By whom have you been set to this base trade?' He, spurred by the words of the gold-dealers, went to his mother and said: 'Mother, it is heard that our father was an ocean-going merchant. Therefore, give me permission — I too shall set out upon the great ocean.' The mother said: 'It is true, son. But you are young and an only child. Do not abandon me to set out upon the great ocean.' He, led astray by those of jealous nature — his false friends — would not turn back. Then, disregarding his mother's words, he had a proclamation sounded by bell throughout the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: 'Hear, O merchants dwelling in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>! The caravan-leader <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> will set out upon the great ocean. Those among you who wish to cross the great ocean with the caravan-leader <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, without tolls, without customs duties, without transit fees — let them prepare their ocean-going merchandise!' He, having performed the auspicious rites and benedictions, accompanied by five hundred merchants, with carts, loads, bundles, baskets, camels, oxen, and donkeys, set forth carrying ocean-going merchandise. And his mother, her heart troubled with affection, her face tearful and mournful, clung to his feet: 'Son, do not abandon me to cross the great ocean!' But he, thus addressed with pitiable, feeble, and faltering words of few syllables, having made his resolve, kicked his mother on the head with his foot and departed with the caravan. And his mother said: 'Son, may you not experience the ripening of this deed!'

children.text: yāvad asau grāmanigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīpaṭṭanāny avalokayan samudratīram anuprāptaḥ | sa pañcabhiḥ purāṇaśatair vahanaṃ bhṛtvā paṃca pauruṣeyān gṛhītvā āhāraṃ nāvikaṃ kaivartaṃ karṇadhāraṃ ca trir api ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | yāvad vahantaṃ makareṇa matsyajātenānayād vayasanam āpāditam* | tato maitrakanyakaḥ phalakam āsādya sthalam anuprāptaḥ | tataḥ sthale cañcūryamāṇo nadūrān nagaraṃ ramaṇakaṃ nāmnā dṛṣṭavān* | sa tad upajagāma | yāvat tataś catasro 'psaraso nirgatāḥ, abhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prāsādikāḥ | tāḥ kathayanti: ehi maitrakanyaka, svāgataṃ te, idam asmākam annagṛhaṃ pānagṛhaṃ vastragṛhaṃ śayyāgṛhaṃ maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālavividhajātarūparajatasaṃpūrṇam* | āgaccha raṃsyāmaha iti | sa tābhiḥ saha anekāni varṣāṇi ratim anubhūtavān*, yathāpi tatkṛtapuṇyaḥ satvaḥ kṛtakuśalaḥ | dakṣiṇapaddhatigamanāc cainaṃ vārayanti | sa yato dakṣiṇāyāḥ paddhater nivāryate, tataḥ suṣṭhutaram utkaṇṭhito gantum* | yāvat punar api dakṣiṇena pathā gacchan paśyati sadāmattaṃ nāma nagaram* | sa tatra dvārībhūtaḥ | yāvat tasmād apy aṣṭāv apsaraso nirgatāḥ abhirūpatarā darśanīyatarāḥ prāsādikatarāḥ | tāḥ kathayanti: ehi maitrakanyaka, svāgataṃ te, idam asmākam annagṛhaṃ pānagṛhaṃ vastragṛhaṃ śayyāgṛhaṃ maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālavividhajātarūparajatasaṃpūrṇam* | āgaccha raṃsyāmaha iti | sa tābhiḥ sahānekāni varṣāṇi ratim anubhūtavān*
children.translated_text: Passing through villages, market-towns, kingdoms, and royal capitals, he arrived at the ocean shore. Having hired a vessel for five hundred <s>purāṇas</s>, and having taken five servants, a cook, a boatman, a fisherman, and a helmsman, and having thrice sounded the bell-proclamation, he set out upon the great ocean. Then the vessel was wrecked by a <s>Makara</s> (sea-monster), a kind of fish, and brought to ruin. Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, having grasped a plank, reached dry land. Wandering about on dry land, he saw not far off a city called <s>Ramaṇaka</s> (Delightful). He went there. Four <s>Apsarases</s> came out, beautiful, lovely, and charming. They said: 'Come, <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, welcome to you! Here is our food-hall, drink-hall, garment-hall, and bedchamber, filled with jewels, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, crystal, coral, and various kinds of gold and silver. Come, let us enjoy ourselves!' He enjoyed pleasures with them for many years, as would a being of accumulated merit and wholesome deeds. They also warned him against going by the southern path. But the more he was restrained from the southern path, the more intensely he desired to go. Going again by the southern path, he saw a city called <s>Sadāmatta</s> (Ever-Joyful). He arrived at its gate. From that city too, eight <s>Apsarases</s> came out, even more beautiful, even more lovely, even more charming. They said: 'Come, <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, welcome to you! Here is our food-hall, drink-hall, garment-hall, and bedchamber, filled with jewels, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, crystal, coral, and various kinds of gold and silver. Come, let us enjoy ourselves!' He enjoyed pleasures with them for many years.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 91]

children.text: yathāpi tatkṛtapuṇyaḥ satvaḥ kṛtakuśalaḥ | tā apy asya dakṣiṇāṃ paddhatiṃ vārayanti | sa yato dakṣiṇāyāḥ paddhater nivāryate, tataḥ suṣṭhutaram utkaṇṭhito gantum* | yāvat punar api dakṣiṇena pathā gacchan paśyati nandanaṃ nāma nagaram* | sa tatra dvārībhūtaḥ | yāvat tasmād api ṣoḍaśāpsaraso nirgatāḥ abhirūpatarā darśanīyatarāḥ prāsādikatarāḥ | tāḥ kathayanti: ehi maitrakanyaka, svāgataṃ te, idam asmākam annagṛhaṃ pānagṛhaṃ vastragṛhaṃ śayyāgṛhaṃ maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālavividhajātarūparajatasaṃpūrṇam* | āgaccha raṃsyāmaha iti | sa tābhiḥ saha anekāni varṣāṇi ratim anubhūtavān* yathāpi tatkṛtapuṇyaḥ satvaḥ kṛtakuśalaḥ | tā apy asya dakṣiṇāṃ paddhatiṃ vārayanti | sa yato dakṣiṇāyāḥ paddhater nivāryate, tataḥ suṣṭhutaram utkaṇṭhito gantum* | yāvat punar api dakṣiṇena pathā gacchan paśyati brahmottaraṃ nāma prāsādam* | sa tatra dvārībhūtaḥ | yāvat tasmād api dvātriṃśad apsaraso nirgatāḥ abhirūpatarā darśanīyatarāḥ prāsādikatarāḥ | tāḥ kathayanti: ehi maitrakanyaka, svāgataṃ te, idam asmākam annagṛhaṃ pānagṛhaṃ vastragṛhaṃ śayyāgṛhaṃ maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālavividhajātarūparajatasaṃpūrṇam* | āgaccha raṃsyāmaha iti | sa tābhiḥ saha anekāni varṣāṇi ratim anubhūtavān* yathāpi tatkṛtapuṇyaḥ satvaḥ kṛtakuśalaḥ | tā apy asya dakṣiṇāṃ paddhatiṃ vārayanti | sa yato dakṣiṇāyāḥ paddhater nivāryate, tataḥ suṣṭhutaram utkaṇṭhito gantum* ||
children.translated_text: As is the case with a being who has made merit, who has performed good deeds — they too block his southern path. Since he is prevented from the southern path, he becomes even more eager to go. Then, going again along the southern road, he sees a city called <s>Nandana</s>. He arrived at its gate. From it too came forth sixteen <s>Apsarases</s>, more beautiful, more comely, more pleasing. They said: 'Come, <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, welcome to you! This is our food-hall, drink-hall, garment-hall, and bed-chamber, filled with gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, and various kinds of gold and silver. Come, let us sport together!' He enjoyed pleasures with them for many years. As is the case with a being who has made merit, who has performed good deeds — they too block his southern path. Since he is prevented from the southern path, he becomes even more eager to go. Then, going again along the southern road, he sees a palace called <s>Brahmottara</s>. He arrived at its gate. From it too came forth thirty-two <s>Apsarases</s>, more beautiful, more comely, more pleasing. They said: 'Come, <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, welcome to you! This is our food-hall, drink-hall, garment-hall, and bed-chamber, filled with gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, and various kinds of gold and silver. Come, let us sport together!' He enjoyed pleasures with them for many years. As is the case with a being who has made merit, who has performed good deeds — they too block his southern path. Since he is prevented from the southern path, he becomes even more eager to go.

children.text: yathā dakṣiṇā paddhatiṃ gacchati, tathāsyecchā vardhate | yāvat punar api dakṣiṇena yathā gacchan paśyaty ayomayaṃ nagaram* | sa tatra praviṣṭaḥ | praviṣṭamātrasya cāsya dvāraṃ pihitam* | tato 'bhyantaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tatrāsya dvāraṃ pihitam* | tato 'bhyantaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ | yāvat puruṣaṃ paśyati mahāpramāṇam* | mūrdhni cāsya ayomayaṃ cakraṃ bhramaty ādīptaṃ pradīptaṃ saṃprajvalitam ekajvālībhūtam* | tasya śiraso yat pūyaśoṇitaṃ pragharati, so 'syāhāraḥ | tato maitrakanyakas taṃ puruṣaṃ pṛṣṭavān*: bho puruṣa, kas tvam iti | sa kathayati: ahaṃ mātur apakārīti | udāhṛtamātre ca tena puruṣeṇa maitrakanyakasya tat karmābhimukhībhūtam*: aham api mātur apakārīti manye tenaivāhaṃ karmaṇā ihākṛṣṭa iti | atha tasminn antare ākāśāc chabdo nirgataḥ: ye baddhās te muktāḥ, ye muktās te baddhāḥ | ity uktamātre tasya puruṣasya mūrdhni cakram antarhitam*, maitrakanyakasya mūrdhni prādurbhūtam* | tato duḥkhārtaṃ maitrakanyakam avekṣya sa puruṣo gāthayā pratyabhāṣata:
children.translated_text: As he goes along the southern path, so does his desire increase. Then, going again along the southern road, he sees a city made of iron. He entered it. The moment he entered, the gate was shut. Then, having entered further within, there too the gate was shut. Then, having entered still further within, he saw a man of enormous size. On his head an iron wheel was spinning — blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire. The pus and blood that dripped from his head — that was his food. Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> asked that man: 'O man, who are you?' He said: 'I wronged my mother.' The moment that man had uttered these words, the <s>karma</s> turned toward <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>: 'I too have wronged my mother — surely it is by that very <s>karma</s> that I have been drawn here.' Then at that moment a voice issued forth from the sky: 'Those who were bound are freed; those who were freed are bound.' The moment this was spoken, the wheel vanished from that man's head and appeared upon <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>'s head. Then, seeing <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> afflicted with pain, that man addressed him with a verse:

children.text: atikramya ramaṇakaṃ sadāmattaṃ ca nandanam* |
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond <s>Ramaṇaka</s> and <s>Sadāmatta</s> and <s>Nandana</s>,

children.text: brahmottaraṃ ca prāsādaṃ kena tvam ihāgataḥ || AVŚ_36.1 ||
children.translated_text: and the palace <s>Brahmottara</s> — by what [path] have you come here? // AVŚ_36.1 //

children.text: maitrakanyakaḥ prāha:
children.translated_text: <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> spoke:

children.text: atikramya ramaṇakaṃ sadāmattaṃ ca nandanam* |
children.translated_text: Having passed beyond <s>Ramaṇaka</s> and <s>Sadāmatta</s> and <s>Nandana</s>,

children.text: brahmottaraṃ ca prāsādam icchayāham ihāgataḥ || AVŚ_36.2 ||
children.translated_text: and the palace <s>Brahmottara</s> — by desire have I come here. // AVŚ_36.2 //

children.text: dūraṃ hi karṣate karma dūrāt karma pravartate |
children.translated_text: Far does <s>karma</s> drag [one], from afar does <s>karma</s> set in motion;

children.text: tatra prakarṣate karma yatra karma vipacyate || AVŚ_36.3 ||
children.translated_text: there does <s>karma</s> drag [one] to where <s>karma</s> ripens. // AVŚ_36.3 //

children.text:
tena karmavipākena cakraṃ vahati mastake |
  ādīptaṃ saṃprajvalitaṃ mama prāṇoparodhakam* || AVŚ_36.4 || iti
children.translated_text:
By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, I bear a wheel upon my head —
blazing, flaming, obstructing my very life-breath. // AVŚ_36.4 //

children.text: puruṣa prāha:
children.translated_text: The man spoke:

children.text:
tvayā praduṣṭacittena mātā duṣkarakārikā |
  pādenābhyāhatā mūrdhni tasya te karmaṇaḥ phalam* || AVŚ_36.5 || iti
children.translated_text:
By you, with wicked intent, your mother — who performed difficult deeds [for you] —
was struck on the head with your foot; this is the fruit of that <s>karma</s>. // AVŚ_36.5 //

children.text: maitrakanyakaḥ prāha:
children.translated_text: <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> spoke:

children.text:
kati varṣasahasrāṇi cakraṃ vartsyati mastake |
  ādīptaṃ saṃprajvalitaṃ mama prāṇoparodhakam* || AVŚ_36.6 || iti
children.translated_text:
For how many thousands of years will this wheel remain upon my head —
blazing, flaming, obstructing my very life-breath? // AVŚ_36.6 //

children.text: puruṣa prāha:
children.translated_text: The man spoke:

children.text:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca |
  ādīptam āyasaṃ cakraṃ tava mūrdhni bhramiṣyati || AVŚ_36.7 || iti
children.translated_text:
For sixty thousand years and six thousand more,
this blazing iron wheel shall spin upon your head. // AVŚ_36.7 //

children.text: maitrakanyaka āha: bhoḥ puruṣa, asti kaścid anyo 'pīhāgamiṣyatīti? puruṣaḥ prāha: ya evaṃvidhakarmakārī bhaviṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> said: 'O man, is there anyone else who will also come here?' The man said: 'Whoever performs such <s>karma</s> [shall come here].'

children.text: tato maitrakanyako duḥkhavedanābhibhūtaḥ satvānām antike kāruṇyaṃ janayitvā taṃ puruṣam āha: icchāmy ahaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa sarvasatvānām arthe idaṃ cakraṃ upari śirasā dhārayitum* | mā kaścid anyo 'py evaṃvidhakarmakārī ihāgacchatv iti | ity uktamātre maitrakanyakasya bodhisatvasya tac cakraṃ saptatālamātraṃ mūrdhni udgamyākāśe sthitam* | sa ca kālaṃ kṛtvā tuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitrakanyaka</s>, overwhelmed by painful sensations, having aroused compassion toward all beings, said to that man: 'I wish, O man, to bear this wheel upon my head for the sake of all beings. May no one else who has performed such <s>karma</s> ever come here!' The moment these words were spoken, the wheel rose seven palm-tree heights from the head of <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and remained suspended in the sky. And he, having passed away, was reborn in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven among the gods.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena maitrakanyaka āsīt, ahaṃ sa | yan mayā saṃvyavaharatā mātā kārṣāpaṇaiḥ pratipāditā, tasya me karmaṇo vipākena caturṣu mahānagareṣu mahatsukham anubhūtam* | yataś ca mātuḥ parītto 'pakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, tasya me karmaṇo phalavipākenaivaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhūtam* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yan mātāpitṛṣu kārān kariṣyāmo nāpakārān* | tad ete doṣā na bhaviṣyanti ye maitrakanyakasya | pṛthagjanasya eṣa eṣa guṇagaṇo bhaviṣyati yas tasyaiva devaputrabhūtasya | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* | tat kasya hetoḥ? duṣkarakārakau hi bhikṣavaḥ putrasya mātāpitarau āpyāyakau poṣakau saṃvardhakau stanyasya dātārau, citrasya jambūdvīpasya darśayitārau | ya ekenāṃsena putro mātaraṃ dvitīyena pitaraṃ pūrṇaṃ varṣaśataṃ pariharet*, yad vā asyāṃ mahāpṛthivyāṃ maṇayo muktā vaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālarajatajātarūpam aśmagarbho musāragalvo lohitikā dakṣiṇāvartaḥ, ity evaṃrūpe vā aiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayet*, na iyatā putreṇa mātāpitroḥ kṛtaṃ vā syād upakṛtaṃ vā | yas tv asāv aśrāddhaṃ mātāpitaraṃ śraddhāsaṃpadi samādāpayati, vinayati, niveśayati, pratiṣṭhāpayati, duḥśīlaṃ śīlasaṃpadi, matsariṇaṃ tyāgasaṃpadi, duṣprajñaṃ prajñāsaṃpadi, samādāpayati, vinayati, niveśayati, pratiṣṭhāpayati, iyatā putreṇa mātāpitroḥ kṛtaṃ vā syād upakṛtaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> — that was I. When I, engaged in trade, provided for my mother with <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> (coins), by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> I experienced great happiness in four great cities. But since a slight offense was committed against my mother, by the fruit-ripening of that <s>karma</s> I experienced such suffering. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall render service to our parents, not disservice." Then those faults that befell <s>Maitrakanyaka</s> shall not befall you. That mass of virtues that was his when he became a <s>Devaputra</s> (son of the gods) — that mass of virtues shall be yours, as ordinary beings. Thus, monks, should you train. And why? Because, monks, mother and father are ones who have performed difficult deeds for a son — nurturers, sustainers, rearers, givers of milk, revealers of this wondrous <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Even if a son were to carry his mother on one shoulder and his father on the other for a full hundred years, or were to establish them in sovereignty over this great earth — rich in gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, silver, gold, emerald, <s>musāragalva</s>, ruby, and right-spiraling conch — even by this much a son would not have done enough or repaid [his parents]. But the son who leads faithless parents to the attainment of faith, guides them, instructs them, and establishes them therein; who leads unvirtuous parents to the attainment of virtue, miserly parents to the attainment of generosity, unwise parents to the attainment of wisdom — who guides, instructs, and establishes them therein — by this much a son would have done enough and repaid [his parents].'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_37 śaśaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_37: <s>Śaśa</s> (The Hare). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyāṃ anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jātaḥ | sa unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛtaḥ | pitā cāsya dhanakṣayam anuprāpto bhogakṣayam anuprāptaḥ | sa ca vistīrṇasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavas taṃ putraṃ kālānukālaṃ jñātisakāśaṃ preṣayati | sa tair jñātibhis tathā lālito yathā teṣu pravṛddhasnehaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. In the course of his sporting, delighting, and amusing himself, in time his wife became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born. He was raised and nurtured until he grew up. His father, however, had suffered the depletion of his wealth and the exhaustion of his possessions. And he, having extensive friends, relatives, and kinsmen, would send his son to his kinsmen from time to time. He was so cherished by those kinsmen that his deep affection for them grew.

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena jetavanaṃ nirgataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sa prasādajātaś ca bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā saṃsāravairāgyikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā saṃsāre doṣadarśī nirvāṇe guṇadarśī mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | sa evaṃ pravrajitaḥ san jñātibhiḥ saha saṃsṛṣṭo viharati | tato bhagavāṃs taṃ gṛhisaṃsargān nivārya araṇye niyojayate | sa tatra nābhiramate | yāvad bhagavāṃs taṃ trir api gṛhisaṃsargān nivārayati: vatsa anekadoṣaduṣṭo 'yaṃ gṛhisaṃsargaḥ | santi cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi iṣṭāni kāntāni priyāṇi manāpāni kāmopasaṃhitāni rañjanīyāni | śrotravijñeyāḥ śabdāḥ, ghrāṇavijñeyā gandhāḥ, jihvāvijñeyā rasāḥ, kāyavijñeyāni spraṣṭavyāni, manovijñeyā dharmāḥ iṣṭāḥ kāntāḥ priyā manāpāḥ kāmopasaṃhitā rañjanīyāḥ kaṇṭakabhūtāḥ | anekaparyāyeṇa cāsya araṇyaguṇāḥ saṃvarṇitāḥ, yatra sthitasya kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ vṛddhir bhavati | yāvat tena kulaputreṇa bhagavantaṃ kalyāṇamitram āgamya araṇyavāsena vasatā yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānenedam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣākṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | sa pūrvanivāsam anusmṛtya bhagavato 'syātiduṣkarāṇi dṛṣṭvā bhagavantam upasaṃkramya sagauravaḥ stauti mānayati ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, on a later occasion, he went out to the <s>Jetavana</s>. And there he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Filled with faith, having prostrated at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> taught him a discourse conducive to weariness with <s>saṃsāra</s>, having heard which, seeing danger in <s>saṃsāra</s> and seeing virtue in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, he obtained his parents' permission and went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. Having thus gone forth, he continued to associate with his lay kinsmen. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, preventing him from association with householders, directed him to the forest. He found no pleasure there. The <s>Bhagavān</s> admonished him three times, turning him away from householder association: 'Child, this association with householders is corrupt with many faults. There are forms cognizable by the eye — pleasant, agreeable, charming, endearing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. There are sounds cognizable by the ear, smells by the nose, tastes by the tongue, tangibles by the body, and mental objects cognizable by the mind — pleasant, agreeable, charming, endearing, connected with sensual desire, enticing, [yet] like thorns.' In many ways the virtues of forest-dwelling were praised to him, where one's wholesome qualities increase. Until that son of good family, having the <s>Bhagavān</s> as his spiritual friend, dwelling in the forest, exerting himself, striving, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Recollecting his former lives and seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s extremely difficult deeds, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and praised and honored him with reverence.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 94]

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta, yāvad ayaṃ kulaputro bhagavatā yāvat trir api grāmāntān nivārya araṇye niyojitaḥ, yāvad arhatve pratiṣṭhāpita iti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ mayā vigatarāgeṇa vigatadveṣeṇa vigatamohena parimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ sarvajñena sarvākārajñena sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena ayaṃ kulaputro yāvan trir api grāmāntān nivārya araṇye niyojitaḥ, yāvad arhatve pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ | yat tu mayā atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsair ayaṃ kulaputraḥ svajīvitaparityāgena grāmāntān nivārya araṇyavāse niyuktaḥ | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, questioned the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, how this son of good family was three times turned back by the Blessed One from the borders of the village and directed to the forest, until he was established in <s>Arhatship</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'What is wonderful in this, monks, that now, by me — one who is free from passion, free from aversion, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, omniscient, knowing all modes, having attained mastery over all knowledge and its objects — this son of good family has been three times turned back from the borders of the village and directed to the forest, until he was established in <s>Arhatship</s>? But in the past, by me — one who was with passion, with aversion, with delusion, not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — this very son of good family was turned back from the borders of the village and engaged in forest-dwelling, at the cost of my own life. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani anyatarasmin girikandare prasravaṇapuṣpaphalakandasaṃpanno ṛṣiḥ prativasati kaṣṭatapāḥ phalamūlāmbubhakṣo 'jinavalkalavāsī agnihotrikaḥ | tasya ca ṛṣeḥ śaśo vayasyo mānuṣapralāpī | sa divasānudivasaṃ trir ṛṣisamīpam upasaṃkrāmati | upasaṃkramyābhivādanaṃ kṛtvā vividhābhiḥ kathābhiḥ saṃmodate | tāv evaṃ pravṛddhasnehau pitāputravad avasthitau | yāvat kālāntareṇa mahaty anāvṛṣṭiḥ prādurbhūtā, yayā nadyudapānāny alpasalilāni saṃvṛttāni, puṣpaphalaviyuktāś ca pādapāḥ | tataḥ sa ṛṣis tatrāśramapade upabhogaviharān nābhiramate | so 'jinacīravalkalāny abhisaṃkṣeptum ārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in a certain mountain cave, endowed with springs, flowers, fruits, and roots, there dwelt a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) — one who practiced severe austerities, eating only fruits, roots, and water, clothed in antelope-hide and bark-garments, a maintainer of the sacred fire. And that <s>ṛṣi</s> had a hare as a companion, one who could speak in human language. Three times every day the hare would approach the <s>ṛṣi</s>. Having approached and paid respects, he would delight in various conversations with him. The two, their affection having grown, lived together like father and son. Then, after some time, a great drought arose, by which the rivers and wells became depleted of water, and the trees were bereft of flowers and fruit. Then that <s>ṛṣi</s> could no longer find pleasure in dwelling and subsisting in that hermitage. He began to pack up his antelope-hide, rags, and bark-garments.'

children.text: atha śaśas taṃ tathā pravṛttaṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭavān*: maharṣe kva gamiṣyasīti | ṛṣir āha: grāmāntam eva gamiṣyāmi (Speyer: avagamiṣyāmi), tatra pakvabhaikṣeṇa yāpayiṣyāmīti | tataḥ sa ṛṣivacanam upaśrutya jātasaṃtāpo mātāpitṛviyogam iva manyamānaḥ pādayor nipatya tam ṛṣim uvāca: mā māṃ parityaja | api ca anekadoṣasaṃkulo gṛhavāso 'nekaguṇasaṃpannaś cāraṇyavāsa iti | sa bahv apy ucyamāno na nivartate | tataḥ sa śaśenocyate: yady avaśyaṃ gantavyam*, kiṃ nu adyeha tāvat pratīkṣasva, śvo yathābhipretaṃ yāsyasīti | tatas tasya ṛṣer etad abhavat*: niyatam ayaṃ mām āhārajātenopanimantrayitukāmaḥ | yasmād ime tiryagyonigatāḥ prāṇinaḥ saṃcayaparā iti | tena tasya pratijñātam* ||
children.translated_text: Then the hare, seeing him thus prepared, asked: 'Great sage, where will you go?' The <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'I shall go to the borders of the village. There I shall sustain myself on cooked alms-food.' Then the hare, upon hearing the <s>ṛṣi</s>'s words, was struck with grief, considering it as if a separation from his parents, and falling at his feet, said to the <s>ṛṣi</s>: 'Do not abandon me! Moreover, the householder's life is fraught with many faults, while the forest-dwelling life is endowed with many virtues.' Though pleaded with at length, the <s>ṛṣi</s> would not turn back. Then the hare said: 'If you must go, at least wait here for today; tomorrow you may go as you wish.' Then this occurred to the <s>ṛṣi</s>: 'Surely he wishes to invite me with some kind of food. For these creatures born in the animal realm are devoted to hoarding.' So he agreed to the hare's request.

children.text: atha kṛtāhnikam āhārakāle śaśa upasaṃkramya tam ṛṣiṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya kṣamayitum ārabdhaḥ: kṣamasva mama maharṣe yan mayā ūhāpohavirahitena tiryagyonāv upapannena tava kiṃcid apakṛtaṃ syāt* | ity uktvā sahasotplutyāgnau prapatitaḥ | tataḥ sa ṛṣir jātasaṃvego bāṣpadurdinamukhaḥ priyaikaputram ivopaguhyovāca (Speyer: ivopagṛhyovāca): vatsa kim idam ārabdham iti | śaśa uvāca: maharṣe araṇyapriyatayā madīyena māṃsenāhorātraṃ yāpayiṣyasi | kiṃ ca:
children.translated_text: Then, when his daily observances were complete and the time for eating had come, the hare approached, circumambulated the <s>ṛṣi</s>, and began to ask forgiveness: 'Forgive me, great sage, if I, being born in the animal realm and lacking the capacity for deliberation and reflection, have in any way offended you.' Having spoken thus, he suddenly leapt into the fire. Then the <s>ṛṣi</s>, stricken with spiritual urgency, his face clouded with tears, embracing the hare as if a beloved only son, said: 'Child, what have you done?' The hare said: 'Great sage, out of love for the forest life, you shall sustain yourself day and night on my flesh. Moreover:

children.text:
na santi mudgā na tilā na taṇḍulā vane vivṛddhasya śaśasya kecana |
  śarīram etat tv analābhisaṃskṛtaṃ mamopayojyādya tapovane vasa || AVŚ_37.1 || iti
children.translated_text:
"There are no lentils, no sesame, no rice — nothing whatsoever — for a hare raised in the forest.
But this body of mine, consecrated by fire,
partake of it today and dwell in the grove of austerities." // <s>AVŚ</s> 37.1 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 95]

children.text: tataḥ sa ṛṣiḥ śaśavacanam upaśrutya jātasaṃvega uvāca: yady evaṃ tava priyatayā kāmam ihaiva jīvitaṃ parityakṣyāmi, na ca grāmāntam avatariṣyāmīti | śrutvaitad vacanaṃ śaśaḥ prītamanāḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | ūrdhvamukhaś ca gaganatalam abhivīkṣya yācituṃ pravṛttaḥ | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Then the <s>ṛṣi</s>, upon hearing the hare's words, was struck with spiritual urgency and said: 'If that is so, then out of love for you I shall willingly give up my life right here, but I shall not descend to the borders of the village.' Hearing these words, the hare became joyful in mind. And looking upward at the vault of the sky, he began to pray. And he said:

children.text: araṇye me samāgamya viveke ramate manaḥ |
children.translated_text: "In the forest, having come together in solitude, my mind delights.

children.text: anena satyavākyena māhendraṃ deva varṣa nu || AVŚ_37.2 ||
children.translated_text: By this truthful word, O <s>Deva</s>, send the <s>Māhendra</s> rain!" // <s>AVŚ</s> 37.2 //

children.text: ity uktamātre bodhisatvānubhāvena māhendrabhavanam ākampitam* | devatānāṃ cādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: kiṃ kṛtam api | paśyanti bodhisatvānubhāvād iti | yāvac chakreṇa devendreṇa māhendravarṣaṃ vṛṣṭaṃ yena tadāśramapadaṃ punar api tṛṇagulmauṣadhipuṣpaphalasamṛddhaṃ saṃvṛttam* ||
children.translated_text: The moment these words were spoken, by the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the palace of <s>Māhendra</s> (Indra) was shaken. And the knowledge-and-vision of the deities operates from below: 'What has been done?' They perceive it by the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, released a <s>Māhendra</s> rain, by which that hermitage once again became rich in grasses, shrubs, herbs, flowers, and fruits.

children.text: tatas tena ṛṣiṇā śaśaṃ kalyāṇamitram āgamya tatra vasatā pañcābhijñāḥ sākṣātkṛtāḥ | tataḥ sa ṛiṣiḥ śaśam uvāca: bhoḥ śaśa, tena duṣkareṇa vyavasāyena kāruṇyabhāvāc ca kiṃ prārthayase iti | tenoktam*: andhe loke anāyake apariṇāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayita, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti | tataḥ sa ṛṣir idaṃ vacanam upaśrutya śaśam abravīt: yadā tvaṃ buddho bhavethāḥ, asmākam api samanvāharethā iti | śaśa uvāca: evam astv iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that <s>ṛṣi</s>, having gained the hare as a spiritual friend and dwelling there, directly realized the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>). Then the <s>ṛṣi</s> said to the hare: 'Friend hare, by that difficult resolve and out of compassion, what do you aspire to?' The hare said: 'May I, in a blind world without a guide, without a leader, become a <s>Buddha</s> — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates those who are not liberated, who gives comfort to those who are not comforted, who brings to complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' Then the <s>ṛṣi</s>, upon hearing these words, said to the hare: 'When you become a <s>Buddha</s>, remember us as well.' The hare said: 'So be it.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena śaśa āsīt, ahaṃ sa | ṛṣir eṣa kulaputraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yat kalyaṇāmitrā vihariṣyāmaḥ kalyāṇasahāyāḥ kalyāṇasaṃparkāḥ, na pāpamitrā na pāpasahāyā na pāpasaṃparkā | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the hare — that was I. And that <s>ṛṣi</s> is this son of good family. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall dwell with spiritual friends, with spiritual companions, with spiritual associates — not with evil friends, not with evil companions, not with evil associates." Thus, monks, should you train.'
