children.text: athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat*: iha mama bhadanta ekākino rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasyaivaṃ cetasi cetaḥparitarka udapādi: upārdham idaṃ brahmacaryasya yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ iti | bhagavān āha: mā tvam ānanda evaṃ vocaḥ: upārdham idaṃ brahmacaryasya yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ iti | sakalam idam ānanda kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ? māṃ hy ānanda kalyāṇāmitram āgamya jātidharmāṇaḥ satvā jātidharmatayā (Speyer: jātidharmatāyāḥ) parimucyante, jarāvyādhiśokamaraṇaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsadharmāṇaḥ satvā upāyāsadharmatāyāḥ parimucyante | tad anenaiva te ānanda paryāyeṇa veditavyaṃ yat sakalam idaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Here, Venerable Sir, while I was alone, secluded, in meditation, this reflection arose in my mind: "Half of this holy life consists of spiritual friendship (<s>kalyāṇamitratā</s>), spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association."' The Blessed One said: 'Do not say so, <s>Ānanda</s>: "Half of this holy life consists of spiritual friendship, spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association." The whole (<s>sakalam</s>) of this holy life, <s>Ānanda</s> — entire, complete, pure, and stainless — consists of spiritual friendship, spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association. And why? Because, <s>Ānanda</s>, by relying on me as a spiritual friend, beings subject to birth are freed from the nature of birth; beings subject to old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair are freed from the nature of despair. By this method, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should understand that the whole of this holy life — entire, complete, pure, and stainless — consists of spiritual friendship, spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 96]

children.text: AVŚ_38 dharmagaveṣī | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: <s>AVŚ</s> 38 — <s>Dharmagaveṣī</s> (Seeker of the <s>Dharma</s>). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | ācaritam etad anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateḥ: kalyam evotthāya bhagavato darśanāyopasaṃkramya jetavanaṃ svayaṃ saṃmārṣṭum* | athānyatamena kālena anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateḥ kaścid vyākṣepaḥ samutpannaḥ | tato bhagavān puṇyakāmānāṃ satvānāṃ puṇyatīrthopadarśanārthaṃ svayam eva saṃmārjanīṃ gṛhītvā jetavanaṃ saṃmārṣṭuṃ pravṛttaḥ | bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāśrāvakā api śāradvatīputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapanandarevataprabhṛtayaḥ saṃmārṣṭuṃ pravṛttāḥ | tato jetavanaṃ saha śrāvakaiḥ saṃmṛjya upasthānaśālāṃ praviśya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | niṣadya bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: pañceme bhikṣava ānuśaṃsāḥ saṃmārjane | katame pañca? ātmanaś cittaṃ prasīdati | parasya cittaṃ prasīdati | devatānāṃ manaso bhavati prāsādikam* | saṃvartanīyaṃ kuśalamūlam upacinoti | kāyasya ca bhedāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyate | iti pañcānuśaṃsāḥ saṃmārjane ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — revered, honored, esteemed, and worshiped by kings, princes, wealthy men, townspeople, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, renowned, of great merit, an obtainer of robes, alms-food, beds and seats, and medicines for the sick and other requisites, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. It was the practice of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: rising early each morning, he would approach the <s>Jetavana</s> to see the Blessed One and would himself sweep it clean. Now on a certain occasion, some distraction arose for the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Then the Blessed One, in order to show beings desirous of merit a ford of meritorious action, himself took up a broom and began to sweep the <s>Jetavana</s>. Seeing the Blessed One, the great disciples too — <s>Śāriputra</s> (Son of <s>Śāradvatī</s>), <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Revata</s>, and others — began to sweep. Then, having swept the <s>Jetavana</s> together with the disciples, the Blessed One entered the assembly hall and sat upon the seat prepared before the community of monks. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'There are these five benefits of sweeping, monks. What five? One's own mind is purified. Others' minds are purified. It is pleasing to the minds of the deities. One accumulates the root of merit leading to [favorable rebirth]. And upon the dissolution of the body, one is reborn among the gods in a happy heavenly realm. These are the five benefits of sweeping.'

children.text: tataś catasraḥ parṣado bhagavataḥ sakāśāt saṃmārjanasyeti pañcānuśaṃsān upaśrutya prasādajātāḥ prītisaumanasyaprasannacittāḥ svasvāsanād utthāya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavantam etad ūcuḥ: vayaṃ bhagavan bhagavata upasthāpakāḥ (Speyer: upasthāyakāḥ) sarvaṃ jetavanaṃ sadā saṃmārṣṭum icchāmaḥ | asmākam anugrahaṃ kuru | tato bhagavāṃs tāsāṃ tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayati | tatas tāś catasraḥ parṣado bhagavato 'dhivāsanāṃ viditvā saṃmārjanīgṛhītvā sarvaṃ jetavanaṃ saṃmārṣṭuṃ pravṛttāḥ | sarvaṃ jetavanaṃ cārāmamārgaparyantaṃ saṃmārjya bhagavato dharmadeśanāṃ śrotum ekānte niṣaṇṇā ādarayuktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the four assemblies, having heard from the Blessed One these five benefits of sweeping, filled with faith, joyful, delighted, and with minds made serene by happiness, rose from their seats and, joining their palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'We, Venerable Sir, as attendants of the Blessed One, wish to sweep the entire <s>Jetavana</s> at all times. Grant us your favor.' Then the Blessed One consented to them by his silence. Then those four assemblies, knowing the Blessed One's consent, took up brooms and began to sweep the entire <s>Jetavana</s>. Having swept the entire <s>Jetavana</s>, including the garden paths and their surroundings, they sat down to one side, attentive, to hear the Blessed One's teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir api taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ | tena śrutaṃ yathā bhagavatā mahāśrāvakasahāyena svayam eva jetavanaṃ saṃmṛṣṭam iti | bhagavatā deśitān saṃmārjane pañcāsnuśaṃsān upaśrutya vipratisārībhūtaḥ iti cintitavān: kimarthaṃ mayā bhagavato vihāre tasmin puṇyakṣetre, yatrādyaivāropitaṃ bījam adyaiva phalaṃ saṃpadyate, svalpasyānantaṃ phalaṃ niṣpadyate, tathāgatasaṃmukhībhūte sarvaśrāvakasaṃvāsite 'tīva manoramabhūmau sarvadevāsuramanuṣyagandharvagaruḍakinnaramahoragāṇāṃ manoharṣāspadībhūte sarvabhūtapretapiśācayakṣarākṣasanārakadrohiṇām anavakāśe sarvamāramārakāyikānāṃ devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ cānavakāśabhuvane bhagnābhibhavajāte rāgadveṣamohamātsaryerṣyāmānaduṣṭasatvānām aviditaprabhāve pāpācārāṇām alabdhāgamane pāpamitrahastagatānām amanāpajāte śraddhāvigatānāṃ tyāgadharmarahitānām adṛṣṭacintitabhāvane duḥśīlānāṃ kuvṛttinām amanogamane dayābhāvavirahitānāṃ krodhināṃ paruṣabhāṣiṇām alabdhaśaraṇe vīryahīnakusīdavṛttināṃ tyaktārambhāśamināṃ sudūrībhūte dhyānacyutamuṣitasmṛtīnāṃ kudṛṣṭicāriṇāṃ kumārgaprasthitānām andhakārībhūte duṣprajñānāṃ kubuddhilabdhajñānāntarāṇām aprāptāgamanabhāve dātṝṇām atīva manorathakṛte suśīlayuktānāṃ manoramavāse kṣamācāriṇām
children.translated_text: The householder Anāthapiṇḍada also arrived at that spot. He heard that the Blessed One himself, together with the great disciples, had swept the Jetavana. Having overheard the five benefits of sweeping taught by the Blessed One, he became filled with remorse and thought thus: 'Why did I allow my mind to be distracted from sweeping the Blessed One's <s>vihāra</s> — that field of merit where a seed planted today bears fruit this very day, where even a small [deed] produces infinite fruit; a place graced by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s presence, inhabited by all the disciples, an exceedingly delightful ground that inspires joy in the hearts of all <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, humans, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>; a place giving no quarter to all <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and those hostile from the hells; a place giving no foothold to all <s>Māras</s>, <s>Mārakāyika</s> gods, and humans, where those overwhelmed [by evil] are defeated; a place whose power is unknown to beings corrupted by passion, hatred, delusion, envy, jealousy, and pride; a place unapproachable by those of evil conduct; a place unpleasant for those fallen into the hands of evil companions, devoid of faith, lacking the virtue of generosity; a place inconceivable to the ill-disciplined, those of bad conduct; a place beyond the mental reach of those devoid of compassion, wrathful, and harsh in speech; a place affording no refuge to the lazy, indolent in their ways, who have abandoned their undertakings and are unpeaceful; a place far removed from those who have fallen from <s>dhyāna</s>, whose mindfulness is confused, who follow wrong views and have set out on wrong paths; a place of darkness for those of poor wisdom, whose knowledge is obstructed by bad understanding; a place beyond the reach of [the ungenerous], but exceedingly fulfilling the aspirations of generous ones; a delightful abode for those endowed with good conduct; [a place] for those who practice patience,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 97]

children.text:
ādarāgamanalabdhe vīryārabdhānāṃ nityānugamanaprāpte dhyānaratānām ālīnabhūvane prajñādhāriṇāṃ prabodhaprakāśāparityaktakṣetre etādṛśe buddhavikrīḍite vihāre saṃmārṣṭuṃ cittākṣepaḥ kṛtaḥ | na punaḥ kadāpi mayā tathā kṣamaṃ kartum* | iti niścitya punas tasyaitad abhavat: yatra bhagavatā mahāśrāvakasahāyena svayaṃ saṃmārjanaṃ kṛtam*, katham aham asyopari yāsyāmi?
  tato 'nāthapiṇḍado 'patrapamāṇarūpo lajjāparigatahṛdayas tatrāvasthāne sthitaḥ | jānakāḥ pṛcchakā buddhā bhagavantaḥ | tena bhikṣavaḥ pṛṣṭāḥ: ka eṣa iti | bhikṣava ūcuḥ: anāthapiṇḍado bhadanta bhagavato lajjāyamānarūpo 'patrāpyaparigatahṛdayo necchati bhagavataḥ sakāśam atropariṣṭāt pādanyāsenopasaṃkramitum*, yatra nāma bhagavatā mahāśrāvakasahāyena svayaṃ jetavanaṃ saṃmṛṣṭam iti | tatas taṃ bhagavān āha: gṛhapate buddhavacanaṃ ###<possibly restore: śrutvā bhagavatā> praveṣṭavyam* | kasmāt? saddharmagauravā hi buddhā bhagavantaḥ, dharmo hy arhatāṃ gurur iti | tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gāthābhigītena gāyan yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastād ekānte niṣaṇṇo dharmakathāśravaṇāya | tato bhagavatā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśitaḥ samādāpitaḥ samuttejitaḥ saṃpraharṣitaḥ | so 'nekaparyāyeṇa bhagavatā dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśitaḥ samādāpitaḥ samuttejitaḥ saṃpraharṣitaḥ saṃprakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
a place to which those of energetic exertion eagerly come; an ever-accessible abode for those delighting in <s>dhyāna</s>; a sheltered haven for bearers of wisdom; a field never forsaken by the light of awakening — in such a <s>vihāra</s>, the playground of the <s>Buddha</s>, I allowed my mind to be distracted from sweeping! Never again shall I permit myself to be so negligent!' Having resolved thus, he further thought: 'Where the Blessed One himself, together with the great disciples, has personally swept — how can I walk upon that ground?'
Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, ashamed and with a heart overcome by modesty, stood still at that very spot. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are knowers and inquirers. The monks were asked by him: 'Who is this?' The monks said: 'It is the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, Venerable Sir, who, being ashamed, his heart overcome by modesty, does not wish to approach the Blessed One's presence from above by the step of his foot, since the Blessed One himself together with the great disciples has personally swept the <s>Jetavana</s>.' Then the Blessed One said to him: 'Householder, having heard the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, you should enter. Why? Because the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, have reverence for the true <s>Dharma</s>, for the <s>Dharma</s> is the teacher of the <s>Arhats</s>.' Then <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, singing hymns in verse, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and worshipped the Blessed One's feet, he sat down to one side in front [of the Blessed One] to hear the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, by means of a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him. Having been thus instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One through many methods of <s>Dharma</s> discourse, he departed.

children.text: tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavān dharme sādarajātaḥ sagauravajāto dharmasyaiva varṇaṃ bhāṣata iti | paśya bhadanta yāvad dharmaratnasyāmī bhājanahūtaḥ satvā ādareṇa sarvaṃ jetavanaṃ saṃmārṣṭuṃ pravṛttāḥ, dharmaṃ ca śrotavyaṃ manyanta iti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ tathāgato vigatarāgadveṣamoho 'tha parimukto jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsair dharme sādarajātaḥ sagauravajāto dharmasyaiva varṇaṃ bhāṣate | yat tu mayā atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsair dharmahetoḥ svajīvitasyāpi parityāgaḥ kṛtaḥ | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Then the monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the Blessed One has arisen with reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, with esteem for the <s>Dharma</s>, and speaks only in praise of the <s>Dharma</s>! See, Venerable Sir, how these beings, worthy vessels of the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>, have with devotion set about sweeping the entire <s>Jetavana</s> and consider the <s>Dharma</s> worthy of hearing!' The Blessed One said: 'What is so wonderful in this, monks, that now the <s>Tathāgata</s> — free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, and liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — has arisen with reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, with esteem for the <s>Dharma</s>, and speaks only in praise of the <s>Dharma</s>? But in a past age, when I still had passion, still had hatred, still had delusion, and was not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>, I even renounced my own life! Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | sa ca rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ sarvapradaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca mahatī tyāge vartate | so 'pareṇa samayena devyā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa sā devī satvavatī saṃvṛttā | dohadaś cāsyāḥ samutpannaḥ: subhāṣitaṃ śṛṇuyām iti | tayā rājñe niveditam* | rājñā naimittikān āhūya pṛṣṭāḥ | ta ūcuḥ: deva asya satvasyānubhāva iti | tatas tena rājā saubhāṣaṇikasyārthe suvarṇapiṭako grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless. He guarded the kingdom as though it were his only son. And that king was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, fond of the <s>Dharma</s>, affectionate toward his subjects, generous in all things, a renouncer of all, given to detached renunciation, and he abided in great generosity. On a later occasion, he was sporting, enjoying himself, and amusing himself with the queen. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, in the course of time the queen became pregnant. And a longing arose in her: 'I wish to hear well-spoken words!' She informed the king. The king summoned the soothsayers and asked them. They said: 'Your Majesty, this is due to the influence of the child in the womb.' Thereupon the king, for the purpose of hearing well-spoken words, had a golden bowl sent around through the villages, cities, market-towns, provinces, and royal capitals,

children.text:
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 98 --------------------
paryaṭitaḥ | na ca tat subhāṣitam upalabhyate | yāvat paripūrṇair navabhir māsaiḥ sā devī prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaś chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhur vistīrṇalalāṭa uccaghoṣaḥ saṃgatabrūs tuṅganāsaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatv asya dārakasya nāmeti | amātyā ūcuḥ: yasmād ayaṃ dārako 'jāta eva subhāṣitaṃ gaveṣate tasmād bhavatu dārakasya subhāṣitagaveṣī nāmeti | tasya subhāṣitagaveṣīti nāma kṛtam* | subhāṣitagaveṣī dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | yadā krameṇa mahān saṃvṛttas tadāpi subhāṣitaṃ gaveṣate, na ca labhate ||
children.translated_text:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 98]
but no such well-spoken words could be found. When the full nine months were completed, the queen gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, fair-complexioned, golden in color, with a head shaped like a parasol, with long arms, a broad forehead, a deep voice, joined eyebrows, a prominent nose, and endowed with all major and minor limbs. At his birth, a birth festival was held, and a name was determined: 'What shall be the name of this boy?' The ministers said: 'Since this boy sought well-spoken words even before he was born, let the boy's name be <s>Subhāṣitagaveṣī</s> (Seeker of Well-Spoken Words).' So the name <s>Subhāṣitagaveṣī</s> was given to him. The boy <s>Subhāṣitagaveṣī</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two to carry him on their hips, two as wet-nurses, two as playmates, and two as bath-nurses. He was raised by those eight nurses and grew up nourished on milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. When in due course he had grown up, he still sought well-spoken words, but could not find them.

children.text: sa pitur atyayād rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ amātyānām ājñāpayati: subhāṣitena me grāmaṇyaḥ prayojanam* | gaveṣata me subhāṣitam api | tatas tair amātyaiḥ sakale jambūdvīpe hiraṇyapiṭakāḥ subhāṣitahetoḥ saṃdarśitāḥ | na ca subhāṣitam āsāditam* | tatas te rājñe niveditavantaḥ | tataḥ sa rājā subhāṣitaśravaṇahetor utkaṇṭhati paritapyati ||
children.translated_text: Established in the kingship upon his father's passing, he commanded his ministers: 'I have need of well-spoken words. Seek out well-spoken words for me!' Then those ministers displayed golden bowls throughout the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the sake of well-spoken words, but no well-spoken words were obtained. They reported this to the king. Thereupon that king yearned and burned with longing to hear well-spoken words.

children.text: śakrasya devānām indrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate | sa paśyati rājānaṃ subhāṣitaśravaṇahetor vihanyamānam* | tasyaitad abhavat*: yanv ahaṃ rājānaṃ mīmāṃseyeti | atha śakro devānām indro guhyakarūpadhārī bhūtvā vikṛtakaracaraṇanayano rājñaḥ purastād gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Below <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, his knowledge-and-vision operates. He perceived the king being tormented by his desire to hear well-spoken words. This thought occurred to him: 'Let me test the king.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, assuming the form of a <s>Guhyaka</s> (a spirit), with deformed hands, feet, and eyes, spoke a verse before the king:

children.text:
dharmaṃ caret sucaritaṃ nainaṃ duścaritaṃ caret* |
  dharmacārī sukhaṃ śete asmiṃl loke paratra ca || AVŚ_38.1 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'One should practice the <s>Dharma</s>, practice what is well done; one should not practice what is ill done.
The practitioner of the <s>Dharma</s> sleeps happily in this world and in the next.' // AVŚ_38.1 //

children.text: tato rājā vismitotphulladṛṣṭis (Speyer: vismayotphulladṛṣṭis) taṃ guhyakam uvāca: brūhi brūhi guhyaka tāvan me, etāṃ gāthāṃ śroṣyāmīti | tato guhyako rājānam uvāca: yadi yad bravīmi tan me kariṣyasi, evam aham api yadājñāpayiṣyasi, tat kariṣyāmīti | rājovāca: kim ājñāpayiṣyasīti | guhyaka uvāca: saptāhorātrāṇi khadirakāṣṭhair agnikhadāṃ tāpayitvā tatra yady ātmānam utsrakṣyasi, tatas te 'haṃ punar gāthāṃ vakṣyāmīti | tacchravaṇāc ca rājā prītamanās taṃ guhyakam uvāca: evam astv iti | tato rājñā guhyakaṃ pratijñāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam* saptame divase rājā subhāṣitaśravaṇahetor agnikhadāyām ātmānam utsrakṣyati | ye 'dbhutāni draṣṭukāmāḥ, āgacchantv iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, his eyes wide with wonder (Speyer: his eyes wide with astonishment), said to that <s>Guhyaka</s>: 'Speak, speak again, <s>Guhyaka</s>! I wish to hear this verse!' Then the <s>Guhyaka</s> said to the king: 'If you will do what I say, then I too will do what you command.' The king said: 'What will you command?' The <s>Guhyaka</s> said: 'Having heated a fire-pit with <s>khadira</s> (acacia) wood for seven days and nights, if you will cast yourself into it, then I shall recite the verse to you again.' And upon hearing this, the king, delighted in mind, said to the <s>Guhyaka</s>: 'So be it!' Then, having established the <s>Guhyaka</s> in his promise, the king had a bell-proclamation made throughout his entire domain: 'On the seventh day, the king will cast himself into a fire-pit for the sake of hearing well-spoken words! Those who wish to see a wonder, let them come!'

children.text: tato 'nekeṣu prāṇiśatasahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu gaganataleṣu cānekeṣu devatāśatasahasreṣu saṃnipatiteṣu bodhisatvasyādhyāśayaśuddhitām avagamyādbhutabhāvaṃ ca draṣṭum ihāvatasthuḥ | atha sa guhyaka ākāśam utpatya bodhisatvam uvāca: kriyatāṃ mahārāja yathāpratijñātam iti | tato rājā jyeṣṭhaṃ kumāraṃ rājye 'bhiṣicya amātyān naigamajānapadāṃś ca kṣamayitvā janakāyaṃ cāśvāsya agnikhadāsamīpam upagamya imāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Then, when many hundreds of thousands of beings had assembled, and in the vault of the sky many hundreds of thousands of deities had also assembled — having perceived the purity of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s aspiration and having come to witness this extraordinary event — they stood there. Then that <s>Guhyaka</s>, rising into the sky, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'Fulfill your promise, great king!' Then the king, having consecrated his eldest prince on the throne, having asked forgiveness of the ministers, townspeople, and countryfolk, and having consoled the multitude, approached the fire-pit and spoke this verse:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 99]

children.text: eṣāṅgārakhadā mahābhayakarī jvālārkaraktopamā
children.translated_text: 'This is the charcoal-pit, terrible and fearsome, its flames red as the sun —

children.text: dharmārthe prapatāmi niścitamanā niḥsādhvaso jīvite |
children.translated_text: for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s> I plunge in, my mind resolute, without fear for my life.

children.text: eṣā cāgnikhadā bhaviṣyati śubhā puṇyānubhāvān mama
children.translated_text: And this fire-pit, by the power of my merit, shall become auspicious for me —

children.text: śītā candanapaṅkavāsitajalā padmākulā padminī || AVŚ_38.2 ||
children.translated_text: cool, a lotus pond fragrant with sandalwood-paste water, full of lotuses.' // AVŚ_38.2 //

children.text: ity uktvā bodhisatvas tasyām agnikhadāyāṃ patitaḥ | patitamātrasya cāsya agnikhadā padminī prādurbhūtā | tataḥ śakro devānām indras tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā yakṣarūpam antardhāpya svarūpeṇa sthitvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> plunged into that fire-pit. The moment he fell in, the fire-pit transformed into a lotus pond! Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, seeing that exceedingly wondrous miracle that captivated both gods and men, caused the <s>Yakṣa</s> form to disappear, and standing in his own form, spoke a verse:

children.text:
dharma caret sucaritaṃ nainaṃ duścaritaṃ caret* |
  dharmacārī sukhaṃ śete loke 'smiṃ ca paratra || AVŚ_38.3 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'One should practice the <s>Dharma</s>, practice what is well done; one should not practice what is ill done.
The practitioner of the <s>Dharma</s> sleeps happily in this world and in the next.' // AVŚ_38.3 //

children.text: atha bodhisatvena tāṃ gāthām udgṛhītvā suvarṇapatreṣv abhilikhya kṛtsne jambudvīpe grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhāniṣu paryaṭitā ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having learned that verse, had it inscribed on golden plates and circulated throughout the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — in villages, cities, market-towns, provinces, and royal capitals.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ahaṃ sa | tadāpi me subhāṣitaśravaṇahetoḥ svajīvitaṃ parityaktaṃ prāg evedānīm* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad dharmaṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | dharmaṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king — that was I. Even then, for the sake of hearing well-spoken [words], I renounced my own life — how much more so now! Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the <s>Dharma</s>. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the <s>Dharma</s>, we shall dwell relying upon it." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_39 anāthapiṇḍadaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_39: <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastyāṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | yāvad anupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇo rājamārgam avatīrṇaḥ | tatra ca rājamārge 'nyatamo brāhmaṇo 'bhyāgataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ suciraṃ nirīkṣya pṛthivyāṃ lekhāṃ niṣkṛṣya (Speyer: nikṛṣya) bhagavantam uvāca: bho gautama, na tāvad ut te lekhā laṅghayitavyā,
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Wandering on his alms-round in due order, he came down to the royal highway. There on the royal highway a certain Brahmin had arrived. He beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him and having gazed at him for a long time, he drew a line on the ground and said to the Blessed One: 'Ho, <s>Gautama</s>! You shall not cross this line

children.text: yāvan me pañca purāṇaśatāni nānuprayacchasīti | tato bhagavān karmaṇām avipraṇāśasaṃdarśanārtham adattādānavairamaṇyārthaṃ ca indrakīla iva tasmin pradeśe sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: until you give me five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> (old coins).' Then the Blessed One, for the purpose of demonstrating the imperishability of <s>karma</s> and for the purpose of [teaching] abstention from taking what is not given, stood in that spot like a <s>pillar of Indra</s>.

children.text: eṣa ca śabdaḥ śrāvastyāṃ samantato visṛtaḥ: yathā kila bhagavān rājamārge 'nyatamena brāhmaṇena pañcānāṃ purāṇaśatānām arthaṃ vidhārita iti | tato rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ sahaśravaṇād evāmātyagaṇaparivṛtto yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavantam idam avocat*: gacchatu bhagavān, ahaṃ pradāsyāmīti | na mahārāja tvayaitāni dātavyāni, api tv anyenaitāni dātavyānīti | tathā viśākhā mṛgāramātā ṛṣidattapurāṇau sthapatī śakrabrahmādayo devā vaiśravaṇaprabhṛtayaś catvāro lokapālā hiraṇyasuvarṇam upādāya bhagavantam upasṛptāḥ | tān api bhagavān uvāca: na bhavadbhir etāni dātavyānīti | yāvad anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā śrutam* | sa hiraṇyasuvarṇasya helāṃ pūrayitvā upari pañca purāṇaśatāni datvā bhagavantam upagataḥ: bhagavan*, idaṃ pratigṛhyatām iti | bhagavān āha: gṛhapate tvayā etāni dātavyāni | dīyatāṃ brāhmaṇāyeti | tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā sā suvarṇahelā brāhmaṇāya dattā ||
children.translated_text: This news spread throughout <s>Śrāvastī</s> on all sides: 'The Blessed One has been detained on the royal highway by a certain Brahmin for five hundred <s>purāṇas</s>!' Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, the moment he heard this, surrounded by his retinue of ministers, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said to the Blessed One: 'Let the Blessed One go; I shall pay.' 'No, great king, these are not to be given by you; rather, by another they are to be given.' Likewise, <s>Viśākhā</s> <s>Mṛgāramātā</s>, <s>Ṛṣidatta</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s> the builders, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other gods, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera) and the four World-Guardians, taking gold and silver, approached the Blessed One. To them also the Blessed One said: 'These are not to be given by you.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard about it. He filled a palanquin with gold and silver, placed five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> on top, and approached the Blessed One [saying]: 'Blessed One, please accept this.' The Blessed One said: 'Householder, it is you who must give these. Give them to the Brahmin.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> gave that palanquin of gold to the Brahmin.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarājikā ca parṣat sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhagavan yāvad anena brāhmaṇena bhagavān vidhārito 'nāthapiṇḍadena ca kārṣāpaṇā dattāḥ | kutaś ca prabhṛti bhagavān asmai dhārayata iti | bhagavān āha: icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śrotum*? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye | tathāgatenaitāni <V: The portion from tathāgatenaitāni up to khalu dehinām is out of place here.> bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu avaśyaṃbhāvīni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ bāhye pṛthivīdhātau nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca |
children.translated_text: The monks, filled with curiosity, together with the assembly including the king, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'See, Blessed One, how the Blessed One was detained by this Brahmin, and how <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> gave the coins! And since when has the Blessed One owed him this debt?' The Blessed One said: 'Do you wish to hear, monks?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, monks, listen well and carefully; I shall speak. By the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, in former lives' — [Note: The portion from 'By the Tathāgata himself' up to 'surely bear fruit for embodied beings' is out of place here.] — 'deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_39.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_39.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | tasya jyeṣṭhaḥ kumāro yuvarājaḥ | so 'pareṇa samayena vasantakālasamaye saṃpuṣpiteṣu pādapeṣu haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīvañjīvakanirghoṣite vanaṣaṇḍe amātyaputraparivṛtaḥ krīḍati ramate | vayaso 'matyaputraḥ vayasyaḥ | so 'pareṇa puruṣeṇa sārdham akṣaiḥ krīḍitavān* | tato 'mātyaputras tena puruṣeṇa pañca purāṇaśatāni nirjitaḥ | rājaputraś cāsya pratibhūr avasthitaḥ | ### <There seem to be a long gap.> tena me saṃsāre 'nantam bhogavyasanam anubhūtam* |
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless. He guarded the kingdom as though it were his only son. His eldest prince was the heir-apparent. On a later occasion, in the spring season, when the trees were in bloom, in a forest grove resounding with the calls of swans, cranes, peacocks, parrots, mynahs, cuckoos, and <s>jīvañjīvaka</s> birds, he was sporting, surrounded by the sons of ministers. A son of the minister was his companion and age-fellow. He gambled with dice against another man. The minister's son lost five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> to that man, and the prince had stood as his guarantor. ### [There seems to be a long gap.] Because of that, I have experienced endless suffering of ruin in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: idānīm apy abhisaṃbuddhabodhhir anena bādhitaḥ | iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, adattādānasya ca prahāṇāya vyāyantavyam*, yathā evaṃvidhā doṣās tasya | evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: And even now, having attained the awakening of a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, I have been obstructed by him. Therefore, monks, deeds that are entirely dark have entirely dark results; entirely bright [deeds have] entirely bright [results]; mixed [deeds have] mixed [results]. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds, and you should strive for the abandonment of taking what is not given, since such are its faults. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_40 subhadraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_40: <s>Subhadra</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kuśinagaryāṃ viharati sma mallānām upavartane yamakaśālavane | atha bhagavāṃs tad eva parinirvāṇakālasamaye āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma: prajñāpaya ānanda tathāgatasya antareṇa yamakaśālayor uttarāśirasaṃ mañcam* | adya tathāgatasya rātryā madhyame yāme nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya antareṇa yamakaśālayor uttarāśirasaṃ mañcaṃ prajñāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvāikānte 'sthāt* | ekāntasthita āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat | prajñapto bhadanta tathāgatasya antareṇa yamakaśālayor uttarāśirā mañcaḥ | atha bhagavān yena mañcas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya dakṣinena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati pāde pādam ādhāya alokasaṃjño smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan nirvāṇasaṃjñām eva manasi kurvan ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, near the <s>Mallas</s>' <s>Upavartana</s>, in the grove of twin <s>Śāla</s> trees. Then the Blessed One, at that very time of <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Prepare, <s>Ānanda</s>, a couch for the <s>Tathāgata</s> between the twin <s>Śāla</s> trees, with the head to the north. Today, in the middle watch of the night, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One. Having prepared a couch between the twin <s>Śāla</s> trees with the head to the north, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet with his head and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'The couch has been prepared, Venerable Sir, for the <s>Tathāgata</s> between the twin <s>Śāla</s> trees, with the head to the north.' Then the Blessed One approached the couch. Having approached, he lay down on his right side, placing foot upon foot, mindful, with clear awareness of wakefulness, keeping the perception of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in mind.

children.text: tena khalu samayena kuśinagaryāṃ subhadraḥ parivrājakaḥ prativasati jīrṇavṛddho mahallakaḥ | sa viṃśatiśatavayaskaḥ kauśināgarāṇāṃ mallānāṃ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rhan saṃmataḥ | aśrauṣīt subhadraḥ parivrājakaḥ: atra śramaṇasya gautamasya rātryā madhyame yāme anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | asti ca dharmeṣu kāṅkṣāyitatvam*, āśā ca me saṃtiṣṭhate, pratibalaś ca me sa bhagavān gautamaḥ tatkāṅkṣāyitatvaṃ prativinodayitum* | śrutvā ca punaḥ kuśinagaryā niṣkramya yena yamakaśālavanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time, the wandering ascetic <s>Subhadra</s> was residing in <s>Kuśinagarī</s> — old, aged, advanced in years. He was one hundred and twenty years old, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, regarded as an <s>Arhat</s>. <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic heard: 'Tonight, in the middle watch of the night, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>'s <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging.' And he had some doubts regarding certain teachings, and hope remained in him: 'The Blessed <s>Gautama</s> is capable of dispelling my doubts regarding those teachings.' Having heard this, he went out from <s>Kuśinagarī</s> and proceeded to the grove of twin <s>Śāla</s> trees.

children.text: tena khalu samayena āyuṣmān ānando bahir vihārasyābhyavakāśe caṃkrame caṃkramyate | adrākṣīt subhadraḥ parivrājaka āyuṣmantam ānandam* | dūrād eva dṛṣṭvā ca punar yenāyuṣmān ānandas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramyāyuṣmatānandena sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisāryaikānte 'sthāt* | ekāntasthitaḥ subhadraḥ parivrājaka āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat*: śrutaṃ me ānanda adya śramaṇasya gautamasya rātryā madhyame yāme nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau
children.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> was walking on the walking-path in the open air outside the <s>vihāra</s>. <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic saw the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Having seen him from afar, he approached the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>. Having approached, he exchanged with the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> various kinds of pleasing and courteous conversation face to face, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'I have heard, <s>Ānanda</s>, that tonight, in the middle watch of the night, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>'s <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging

children.text: parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | asti ca me dharmeṣu kāṅkṣāyitatvam*, āśā ca me saṃtiṣṭhate, pratibalaś ca me sa bhagavān gautamas tatkāṅkṣāyitatvaṃ prativinodayitum* | saced bhagavata ānanda asty aguru, praviśema, pṛcchema kaṃcid eva pradeśam*, saced avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnavyākaraṇāya | ānanda āha: alaṃ subhadra | mā bhagavantaṃ viheṭhaya | śrāntakāyo bhagavān*, klāntakāyaḥ sugataḥ | dvir api trir api subhadraḥ parivrājaka āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat* śrutaṃ bho ānanda adya śramaṇasya gautamasya rātryā madhyame yāme anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati, asti ca me dharmeṣu kāṅkṣāyitatvam* | āśā ca me saṃtiṣṭhate | pratibalaś ca me sa bhagavān gautamas tatkāṅkṣāyitatvaṃ prativinodayitum* | saced bhagavata ānanda, asty aguru, praviśema, pṛcchema kaṃcid eva pradeśam*, saced avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnasya vyākaraṇāya | dvir api trir api āyuṣmān ānandaḥ subhadraṃ parivrājakam idam avocat: alaṃ subhadra, mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhaya, śrāntakāyo bhagavān*, klāntakāyaḥ sugataḥ | punar api subhadraḥ parivrājaka āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat*: śrutaṃ bho ānanda purāṇānāṃ parivrājakānām antikāj jīrṇānāṃ buddhānāṃ (Speyer: vṛddhānāṃ) mahatāṃ caraṇācāryāṇām*: kadācit karhicit tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā loke utpadyante, tadyathā udumbaraṃ puṣpam* | tasya cādya bhagavato gautamasya rātryā madhyame yāme anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | asti ca me dharmeṣu kāṅkṣāyitatvam* | āśā ca me saṃtiṣṭhate | pratibalaś ca me sa bhagavān gautamas tatkāṅkṣāyitatvaṃ prativinodayitum* | saced bhagavata ānanda asty aguru, praviśema, pṛcchema kaṃcid eva pradeśam*, saced avakāśaṃ kuryāt praśnavyākaraṇāya | punar apy ānandaḥ subhadraṃ parivrājakam idam avocat*: alaṃ subhadra | mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhaya | śrāntakāyo bhagavān*, klāntakāyaḥ sugataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will take place. And I have doubts regarding certain teachings, and hope remains in me. The Blessed <s>Gautama</s> is capable of dispelling those doubts. If it is not troublesome to the Blessed One, <s>Ānanda</s>, let me enter and ask about some point, if he would grant the opportunity for answering my question.' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'Enough, <s>Subhadra</s>! Do not trouble the Blessed One. The Blessed One's body is weary; the <s>Sugata</s>'s body is exhausted.' A second and a third time, <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'I have heard, friend <s>Ānanda</s>, that today, in the middle watch of the night, the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>'s <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging. And I have doubts regarding certain teachings. And hope remains in me. The Blessed <s>Gautama</s> is capable of dispelling those doubts. If it is not troublesome to the Blessed One, <s>Ānanda</s>, let me enter and ask about some point, if he would grant the opportunity for answering my question.' A second and a third time, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic: 'Enough, <s>Subhadra</s>! Do not trouble the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The Blessed One's body is weary; the <s>Sugata</s>'s body is exhausted.' Then again <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'I have heard, friend <s>Ānanda</s>, from the ancient wandering ascetics, the aged and wise ones (Speyer: the elders), the great teachers of conduct: "Only rarely, at certain times, do <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> arise in the world — like the blossoming of the <s>Udumbara</s> flower." And today, in the middle watch of the night, the Blessed <s>Gautama</s>'s <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging. I have doubts regarding certain teachings. Hope remains in me. The Blessed <s>Gautama</s> is capable of dispelling those doubts. If it is not troublesome to the Blessed One, <s>Ānanda</s>, let me enter and ask about some point, if he would grant the opportunity for answering my question.' And again <s>Ānanda</s> said to <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic: 'Enough, <s>Subhadra</s>! Do not trouble the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The Blessed One's body is weary; the <s>Sugata</s>'s body is exhausted.'

children.text: imāṃ ca punar āyuṣmatā ānandasya subhadreṇa parivrājakenā sārdham antarākathāṃ viprakṛtām aśrauṣīd bhagavān divyena śrotreṇa viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣeṇa | śrutvā ca punar āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat: alam ānanda | mā subhadraṃ parivrājakaṃ vāraya | praviśatu, pṛcchatu yad yad evākāṅkṣati | ayaṃ me paścimo bhaviṣyati anyatīrthikaparivrājakaiḥ sārdham antarākathāsamudāhāraḥ | ayaṃ ca me caramo bhaviṣyati sākṣācchrāvakāṇām ehibhikṣukayā pravrajitānām*, yaduta subhadra parivrājakaḥ | atha subhadra parivrājako bhagavatā kṛtāvakāśo hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita udagraprītisaumanasyajāto yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisāryaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ subhadraḥ parivrājako bhagavantam idam avocat: yānīmāni bho gautama pṛthagloke tīrthyāyatanāni: tadyathā pūraṇaḥ kāsyapaḥ, māskarī gośālīputraḥ, sañjayī vairūṭīputraḥ, ajitaḥ keśakambalaḥ, kukudaḥ kātyāyanaḥ, nirgrantho jñātaputraḥ, pratyajñāsiṣur me svāṃ svāṃ pratijñāṃ ### ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, with his divine ear — purified and surpassing the human — heard this conversation between the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic. Having heard it, he said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Enough, <s>Ānanda</s>! Do not turn away <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic. Let him enter and ask whatever he wishes. This will be my last conversation with wandering ascetics of other schools. And this will be my last direct disciple ordained with the words "Come, monk" — namely, <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic.' Then <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic, having been given the opportunity by the Blessed One — joyful, pleased, delighted, elated, filled with gladness and happiness — approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged various pleasing and courteous conversation face to face with the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic said this to the Blessed One: 'These various sectarian establishments in the world, Sir <s>Gautama</s> — namely <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Sañjayī Vairūṭīputra</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, <s>Kukuda Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Nirgrantha Jñātaputra</s> — did they all realize their own claims? ###'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke this verse:

children.text: ekānnatriṃśatko vayasā subhadra
children.translated_text: At the age of twenty-nine, <s>Subhadra</s>,

children.text: yat prāvrajaṃ kiṃkuśalaṃ gaveṣī |
children.translated_text: I went forth, seeking what is wholesome.

children.text: pañcāśad varṣāṇi samādhikāni
children.translated_text: More than fifty years

children.text: yasmād ahaṃ pravrajitaḥ subhadra || AVŚ_40.1 ||
children.translated_text: have passed since I went forth, <s>Subhadra</s>. // AVŚ_40.1 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 103]

children.text: śīlaṃ samādhiś caraṇaṃ ca vidyā
children.translated_text: Virtue, concentration, conduct, and knowledge,

children.text: caikāgratā cetaso bhāvitā me |
children.translated_text: and one-pointedness of mind have been cultivated by me.

children.text: āryasya dharmasya pradeśavaktā
children.translated_text: A teacher of a portion of the Noble <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: ito bahir vai śramaṇo 'sti nānyaḥ || AVŚ_40.2 ||
children.translated_text: outside of this, there is no other ascetic. // AVŚ_40.2 //

children.text:
yasya subhadra dharmavinaye āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgo nopalabhyate, prathamaḥ śramaṇas tatra nopalabhyate | dvitīyas tṛtīyaś caturthaḥ śramaṇas tatra nopalabhyate | yasmiṃs tu subhadra dharmavinaye āryāṣṭāṅgo mārga upalabhyate prathamaḥ śramaṇas tatropalabhyate | dvitīyas tṛtīyaś caturthaḥ śramaṇas tatropalabhyate | asmiṃs tu subhadra dharmavinaye āryāṣṭāṅgo mārga upalabhyate | iha prathamaḥ śramaṇa upalabhyate, iha dvitīyaḥ, iha trtīyaḥ, iha caturthaḥ | na santi ito bahiḥ śramaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā | śūnyāḥ parapravādāḥ śramaṇair vā brāhmaṇair vā | evam atra parṣadi samyaksiṃhanādaṃ nadāmi |
  asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe subhadrasya parivrājakasya virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur utpannam* | atha subhadraḥ parivrājako dṛṣṭadharmā prāptadharmā paryavagāḍhadharmā tīrṇakāṅkṣas tīrṇavicikitso 'parapratyayo 'nanyaneyaḥ śāstuḥ śāsanadharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāpta utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yenāyuṣmān ānandas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya āyuṣmantaṃ ānandam idam avocat | lābhā bhadanta ānandena sulabdhā yad bhagavatā ānando mahācāryeṇa mahācāryāntevāsikābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ | api tu asmākam api syur lābhāḥ sulabdhā yad vayaṃ labhemahi svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam* | athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat*: ayaṃ bhadanta subhadraḥ parivrājaka ākāṅkṣate svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam* | tatra bhagavān subhadraṃ parivrājakam āmantrayate | ehi bhikṣo, cara brahmacaryam* | saiva tasyāyuṣmataḥ pravrajyābhūt sopasaṃpat, sa bhikṣubhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadra</s>, in whatever <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> the Noble Eightfold Path is not found, therein no first ascetic is found, no second, third, or fourth ascetic is found. But, <s>Subhadra</s>, in whatever <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> the Noble Eightfold Path is found, therein the first ascetic is found, the second, third, and fourth ascetic is found. In this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, <s>Subhadra</s>, the Noble Eightfold Path is found. Here the first ascetic is found, here the second, here the third, here the fourth. The teachings of other schools are devoid of true ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Thus I roar the lion's roar of truth in this assembly. When this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, there arose in <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic the dustless, stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye (<s>dharmacakṣus</s>) regarding all phenomena. Then <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic — having seen the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, having penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>, having crossed beyond doubt, having crossed beyond uncertainty, self-reliant, not dependent on others, having attained confidence in the Teacher's teaching — rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and with palms joined toward the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'It is a gain for you, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, well-gained, that <s>Ānanda</s> has been anointed by the Blessed One, the great Teacher, with the anointing of a great Teacher's disciple. Moreover, it would be our gain too, well-gained, if we could obtain the going-forth, the full ordination, the status of a monk in this well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'This <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic, Venerable Sir, desires the going-forth, the full ordination, the status of a monk in this well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>.' Thereupon the Blessed One addressed <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic: 'Come, monk, live the holy life.' That itself was the venerable one's going-forth, his full ordination, his attainment of monkhood.

children.text: evaṃ pravrajitaḥ sa āyuṣmān eko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramatta ātāpī prahitātmā vyahārṣīt* | eko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramatta ātāpī prahitātmā viharan* yad arthaṃ kulaputrāḥ keśaśmaśru avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajanti, tad anuttaraṃ brahmacaryaparyavasānaṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñayā sākṣātkṛtyopasaṃpadya pravedayati: kṣīṇā me jātiḥ, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nānyam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi | ājñātavān āyuṣmān arhan babhūva suvimuktaḥ | athāyuṣmataḥ subhadrasyārhatvaprāptasya vimuktisukhaṃ pratisaṃvedayata etad abhavat*: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ śāstāraṃ parinirvāpayantaṃ paśyeyam* | yanv ahaṃ prathamataraṃ parinirvāpayeyam iti | tatrāyuṣmān subhadraḥ prathamataraṃ parinirvṛtaḥ, tataḥ paścād bhagavān* ||
children.translated_text: Thus ordained, the venerable one, dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, exerted himself. Dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute — for the very purpose for which sons of good family, having shaved off hair and beard, donning the saffron robes, with right faith go forth from the household life into homelessness — that supreme goal of the holy life, he directly realized, attained, and declared by his own higher knowledge in this very life: 'Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done; I know of no further becoming beyond this.' The venerable one became an <s>Arhat</s>, well-liberated. Then, when the venerable <s>Subhadra</s> had attained <s>Arhatship</s>, experiencing the bliss of liberation, this thought occurred to him: 'It would not be fitting for me to witness the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the Teacher. Rather, let me attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> first.' Thereupon the venerable <s>Subhadra</s> attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> first, and afterwards the Blessed One.

children.text: yadā bhagavatā paścimaśayanopagatena dharmoparodhikāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ vartamānāyām*, chidyamāneṣu dharmeṣu, mucyamāneṣu saṃdhiṣu, subhadro 'rhatve pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ, bahavaś ca kauśīnāgarā mallā dharme niyuktāḥ, tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta, yad ayaṃ subhadraḥ parivrājako bhagavatā chidyamāneṣu dharmeṣu mucyamānāsu saṃdhiṣu saṃsāravāgurāyā mocayitvā yāvad atyantaniṣṭhe nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpita iti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ mayā vigatarāgeṇa vigatadveṣeṇa vigatamohena parimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ subhadraḥ parivrājakaḥ saṃasāravāgurāyā mocayitvā yāvad atyantaniṣṭhe
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One, having taken his final resting position, while painful feelings were present, while the elements of existence were being cut off and the joints of being were being released, had established <s>Subhadra</s> in <s>Arhatship</s>, and many <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> had been established in the <s>Dharma</s>, then the monks, in whom doubt had arisen, questioned the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic was freed by the Blessed One from the snare of <s>saṃsāra</s>, while the elements of existence were being cut off and the joints were being released, and established in ultimate <s>Nirvāṇa</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'What is wonderful in this, monks, that now — by me, one who is free from passion, free from aversion, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — <s>Subhadra</s> the wandering ascetic has been freed from the snare of <s>saṃsāra</s> and established in ultimate
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 104]

children.text: nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ | yat tu mayā atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsair ūhāpohavirahitena tiryagyonāv upapannena svajīvitaparityāgena subhadraḥ paritrātaḥ, kauśīnāgarāś ca mallāḥ | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? But in a past age, by me — one who was with passion, with aversion, with delusion, not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, devoid of reasoning and analysis, born in an animal state — at the cost of my own life, <s>Subhadra</s> was rescued, and the <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s> [were saved]. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani anyatarasyāṃ parvatadaryāṃ mṛgayūthapaḥ prativasati anekamṛgasahasraparivāraḥ paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī | tac ca mṛgayūthaṃ lubdhakena vicārya rājñe niveditam* | tato rājñā caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena nirgatya tan mṛgayūthaṃ sarvaṃ saṃkaṭīkṛtam* | tato yūthapater etad abhavat*: yady aham idānīm imān na rakṣiṣyāmi, adyaiva te sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyantīti | tato yūthapatiḥ samantato vyavalokayitum ārabdhaḥ: katamena pradeśenāsya mṛgakulasya niḥsaraṇaṃ syād iti | sa paśyati tasyāṃ parvatadaryāṃ nadīṃ vahamānām* | sā ca nadī ahāryahāriṇī śīghrasrotāḥ, te ca mṛgā durbalāḥ | tato yūthapatiḥ sahasā tāṃ nadīm avatīrya madhye sthitvā śabdam udīrayati: āgacchantu bhavantaḥ, etasmāt kūlād utplutya mama pṛṣṭe pādān sthāpayitvā paratra kūle pratitiṣṭhata | anenopāyena jīvitaṃ vaḥ paśyāmi, ato 'nyathā maraṇam iti | tatas tair mṛgais tathaiva kṛtam* | atha tasya pṛṣṭhe kṣuranipātātvak chinnā | māṃsarudhirāsthirāśir vyavasthitaḥ | na cāsya vyavasāyo nivṛttaḥ tadgatakāruṇyo mṛgāṇām antike | tataḥ sarveṣu laṅghiteṣu pṛṣṭhato 'valokayituṃ pravṛttaḥ: mā kaścid atrālaṅghitaṃ (Speyer: Śto) bhaviṣyatīti | sa paśyati mṛgaśāvakam ekam alaṅghitam* | tato yūthapatiś chidyamāneṣu marmasu mucyamānāsu saṃdhiṣu iṣṭajīvitam agaṇayitvā kūlam uttīrya mṛgaśāvakaṃ pṛṣṭham adhirohya nadīm uttārya kūle sthāpayitvā taṃ mṛgagaṇam uttīrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā maraṇakāle praṇidhiṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: yathā me ime mṛgā ayaṃ ca mārgaśāvaka iṣṭena jīvitenācchāditāḥ, vyasanāt paritrātāḥ, evam apy aham anāgate 'dhvani anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhya etān saṃsāravāgurāyā mocayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in a certain mountain gorge, there dwelt a leader of a deer-herd, accompanied by many thousands of deer — wise, discerning, and intelligent. That deer-herd was tracked by a hunter and reported to the king. Then the king, having gone forth with his four-fold army, surrounded and trapped that entire herd of deer. Then the herd-leader thought: 'If I do not protect them now, this very day they will all perish.' So the herd-leader began to look around in all directions: 'By which route might this deer-herd escape?' He saw a river flowing through that mountain gorge. But the river was irresistibly powerful, with a swift current, and the deer were weak. Then the herd-leader suddenly plunged into that river, stood in the middle, and called out: 'Come, friends! Leaping from this bank, place your feet upon my back, and land upon the far bank. By this means I see life for you; otherwise there is death.' The deer did just so. Then the skin on his back was cut as if by the fall of razors. He stood there as a mass of flesh, blood, and bones. Yet his resolve did not waver, his compassion being directed toward the deer. When all had leaped across, he began to look behind: 'Let no one remain here who has not crossed.' He saw one young fawn that had not crossed. Then the herd-leader, though his vital spots were being pierced and his joints were coming apart, disregarding his own dear life, climbed up the bank, placed the fawn on his back, carried it across the river, set it on the bank, and seeing the entire herd safely across, at the time of death began to make a vow: 'Just as these deer and this fawn have been sheltered by my dear life and rescued from calamity, so may I too, in a future age, having attained supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), liberate them from the snare of <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena mṛgapatir āsīt*, ahaṃ sa | mṛgā ime kauśīnāgarā mallāḥ | mṛgaśāvakaḥ ayam eva subhadraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the lord of the deer-herd — that was I. The deer are these <s>Mallas</s> of <s>Kuśinagara</s>. The fawn is this very <s>Subhadra</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta subhadreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni yena paścimaḥ sākṣācchrāvakāṇām iti | bhagavān āha: subhadreṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | na bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca |
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Subhadra</s> perform that he became the last of the direct disciples?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Subhadra</s> himself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated. They do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_40.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_40.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśatisahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | atha bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. Now the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, had
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 105]

children.text: bhāgineyo 'śoko nāmnā | sa bhagavatsakāśe mokṣārthī pravrajitaḥ | sa svādhīnaṃ mokṣaṃ manyamāno na vyāyacchate | yāvad dīrghakālaprakarṣeṇāśoko janapade varṣoṣitaḥ | bhagavāṃś ca kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgniḥ paścimaśayanopagataḥ, aśokaś ca bhikṣur aśokasyādhastāt pratisaṃlīno babhūva | atha yā devatā tasminn aśokavṛkṣe vyuṣitā, sā bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvāṇaṃ śrutvā rodituṃ pravṛttā | tasya rudantyā aśrubindavo 'śokasya kāye nipatituṃ pravṛttāḥ | athāśoka ūrdhvamukhas tāṃ devatāṃ rudantīm āha: kimarthaṃ devate rudyata iti | devatovāca: adya rātryā madhyame yāme bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | athāśoko devatāvacanam upasṛtya marmaviddha iva pracalitavān* | so 'pi karuṇakaruṇaṃ rodituṃ pravṛttaḥ | tato devatayā pṛṣṭaḥ: kimarthaṃ rodiṣīti | aśoka uvāca: guruviyogāj jñātiviyogāc ca | kāśyapo me samyaksaṃbuddho mātulaḥ | so 'haṃ visrabdhavihārī na vyāyatavān* | dūre cāsau | ahaṃ ca pṛthagjanaḥ | apakṛṣṭatvād adhvano na śakṣyāmi viśeṣam adhigantum iti | devatovāca: yadi punar ahaṃ bhavantaṃ bhagavatsakāśam upanayeyam*, kiṃ śakyam iti | aśoka uvāca: tathā hi me buddhiḥ paripakvā, yathā sahadarśanād eva bhagavataḥ śakṣyāmi viśeṣam adhigantum iti | tato devatayā aśoko bhagavatsakāśam ṛddhyanubhāvān nītaḥ | tasya bhagavaddarśanāt prasāda utpannaḥ | prasādajātasya ca bhagavatā kāśyapena tathāvidho dharmo deśitaḥ yacchravaṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | prathamataraṃ cāyuṣmān aśokaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ, tato bhagavān kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a nephew named <s>Aśoka</s>. He had gone forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, seeking liberation. But considering liberation to be easily attainable, he did not exert himself. After a long passage of time, <s>Aśoka</s> had spent the rains-retreat in the countryside. The <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, entered his final repose. And the monk <s>Aśoka</s> was seated in meditation beneath an <s>aśoka</s> tree. Now a deity who inhabited that <s>aśoka</s> tree, upon hearing of the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, began to weep. As she wept, her teardrops began to fall upon <s>Aśoka</s>'s body. Then <s>Aśoka</s>, looking upward, said to the weeping deity: 'Why do you weep, O deity?' The deity said: 'Tonight, in the middle watch, the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, will take place.' Then <s>Aśoka</s>, upon hearing the deity's words, was struck as if pierced in the vitals. He too began to weep most piteously. Then the deity asked him: 'Why do you weep?' <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'Because of the separation from my teacher and the separation from my kinsman. The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> is my maternal uncle. And I, being complacent, did not exert myself. Moreover, he is far away. And I am still an ordinary person. Because of the great distance, I shall not be able to attain any spiritual distinction.' The deity said: 'But if I were to convey you to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, would it be possible [for you to attain distinction]?' <s>Aśoka</s> said: 'My faculties are so ripened that upon merely seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>, I shall be able to attain spiritual distinction.' Then the deity, by her supernatural power, conveyed <s>Aśoka</s> to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Upon seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>, faith arose in him. And to him, now filled with faith, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> taught such a <s>Dharma</s> that upon hearing it he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. The Venerable <s>Aśoka</s> attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> first, and then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sā devatā āyuṣmato 'śokasya parinirvāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā prītim utpādayāmāsa | cintayati ca: yaḥ kaścid anenāyuṣmatā viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ, sarvaḥ sa mām āgamya | evam apy aham anāgate 'dhvani yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena uttaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛtaḥ: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti, tasyāham eva paścimaśayanopagatasya caramaḥ sākṣācchravakāṇām ehibhikṣukayā pravrajitānāṃ bhaveyam*, pūrvataraṃ ca bhagavataḥ parinirvāpayeyam*, tato bhagavān* śākyamunir iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that deity, seeing the <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> of the Venerable <s>Aśoka</s>, generated joy and reflected: 'Whatever spiritual distinction this Venerable one attained, all of that was due to me. Likewise, in a future age, the one whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> prophesied as a young Brahmin named <s>Uttara</s>, saying: "You, young man, when the lifespan of people is one hundred years, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>" — may I be the last of his direct disciples, ordained with the formula "Come, monk" (<s>ehibhikṣukā</s>), and may I attain <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> before the <s>Bhagavān</s>; and then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> [shall follow].'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau devatā, ayaṃ sa subhadraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yat kalyāṇamitratā vihariṣyāmaḥ kalyāṇsahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? That deity — this is <s>Subhadra</s>. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall dwell with spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitratā</s>), spiritual companions, spiritual associates — not with evil friends, not with evil companions, not with evil associates." Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text:
athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat: iha mama bhadanta ekākino rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasya evaṃ cetasi cetaḥparitarka udapādi: upārdham idaṃ brahmacaryasya yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ iti | {bhagavān āha:} mā tvam ānanda evaṃ vocaḥ: upārdham idaṃ brahmacaryasya yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ iti | sakalam idam ānanda
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 106 --------------------
children.translated_text:
Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here, Venerable Sir, while I was alone, secluded, in meditation, this reflection arose in my mind: "Half of this holy life consists of spiritual friendship (<s>kalyāṇamitratā</s>), spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association."' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do not say so, <s>Ānanda</s>: "Half of this holy life consists of spiritual friendship, spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association." The whole of this holy life, <s>Ānanda</s> —
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 106]

children.text: kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpamitratā na pāpasahāyatā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ? māṃ hy ānanda kalyāṇamitram āgamya jātidharmāṇaḥ satvā jātidharmatāyāḥ parimucyante, jarāvyādhiśokamaraṇaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsadharmāṇaḥ satvā upāyāsadharmatāyāḥ parimucyante | tad anenaiva te ānanda paryāyeṇa veditavyaṃ yat sakalam idaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ yaduta kalyāṇamitratā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasaṃparkaḥ, na pāpasahāyatā na pāpamitratā na pāpasaṃparkaḥ | ity evaṃ te ānanda śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: entire, complete, pure, and stainless — consists of spiritual friendship, spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association. And why? Because, <s>Ānanda</s>, by relying on me as a spiritual friend, beings subject to birth are freed from the nature of birth; beings subject to old age, disease, sorrow, death, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair are freed from the nature of despair. By this method, <s>Ānanda</s>, you should understand that the whole of this holy life — entire, complete, pure, and stainless — consists of spiritual friendship, spiritual companionship, spiritual association — not evil friendship, not evil companionship, not evil association. Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 107]

children.text: paṃcamo vargaḥ
children.translated_text: Chapter Five

children.text: tasyoddānam*:
children.translated_text: Its summary (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.text: guḍaśālā ca bhaktaṃ ca toyaṃ varcaghaṭena ca |
children.translated_text: The sugar-hall, food, water, and the vessel for excrement;

children.text: koliko hy uttaraś cāpi jātyandhaḥ śreṣṭhir eva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Kolika</s> and <s>Uttara</s>, the blind-from-birth, and the guild-master;

children.text: putro jāmbālakaś caiva vargo bhavati samudditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the son and <s>Jāmbālaka</s> — thus this chapter is proclaimed.

children.text: AVŚ_41 guḍaśālā | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_41: <s>Guḍaśālā</s> (The Sugar-Hall). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | yadā bhagavatā anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhir abhisaṃbuddhā, tadāyuṣmadbhyāṃ śāriputramaudgalyāyanābhyām iyaṃ pratijñā kṛtā: na tāvat piṇḍakaṃ paribhokṣyāmahe (Speyer: paribhokṣyāvahe), yāvan narakatiryakpretebhya ekasatvam api na mocayāva iti | tatas tāv āyuṣmatau kālena kālaṃ kadācin narakacārikāṃ carataḥ, kadācit tiryakpretacārikāṃ carataḥ | tau tatra satvānāṃ vividhayātanābhyāhatānām asatpralāpaṃ dṛṣṭvā tān āgatya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadām ārocayataḥ | te 'pi śrutvā saṃvegam āpadyante | tatas tau tad adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathāvidhāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kurutaḥ, yayā aneke satvā viśeṣam adhigacchanti, dharmaśravaṇakathāyāś ca bhājanībhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had attained supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), the Venerables <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> made this vow: 'We shall not eat alms-food until we have liberated at least one being from the realms of hell, animals, and hungry ghosts.' Thereupon those two Venerables would from time to time undertake tours of the hells, and at other times tours of the animal and hungry ghost realms. There, having witnessed the various torments afflicting beings and their delirious ravings, they would come back and report to the four assemblies. They too, upon hearing, became spiritually stirred. Then those two Venerables would give such teachings based on those accounts that many beings attained spiritual distinction and became worthy vessels for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pretacārikāṃ carann adrākṣīt pretaṃ parvatakūṭaprakhyaṃ samudrasadṛśakukṣiṃ sūcīchidropamamukhaṃ svakeśasaṃchannam ādīptaṃ samyakprajvalitam ekajvālībhūtaṃ dhyāyantam ārtasvaraṃ krandantam*, duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanām anubhavantam*, yena yenoccāraprasrāvabhūmis tena tenānvāhiṇḍamānaṃ tad api kṛcchreṇāsādayantam* | tataḥ sthaviraḥ pretaṃ papraccha: kiṃ te bhoḥ karma kṛtaṃ yenaivaṃvidhāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayasa iti | preta āha: āditye hi samudgate na dīpena prayojanam* | bhagavantam etam arthaṃ paripṛccha | sa te asmākīnāṃ karmaplotiṃ vyākariṣyatīti | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
