children.translated_text: On a later occasion, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, wandering on a tour of the realm of hungry ghosts, beheld a <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) — resembling a mountain peak in size, with a belly like the ocean, a mouth like the eye of a needle, covered with his own hair, ablaze, fully burning, become a single mass of flame, brooding, crying out in a distressed voice, experiencing painful, intense, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations, wandering to wherever there was ground for excrement and urine, and even that he could scarcely reach. Then the elder asked the <s>preta</s>: 'What <s>karma</s> did you perform, sir, that you experience such painful, intense, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations?' The <s>preta</s> said: 'When the sun has risen, there is no need for a lamp. Ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about this matter; he will explain the record of our <s>karma</s>.' Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam* | anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoty anijyamānair indriyaiḥ | tato buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūrvālāpinaḥ priyālāpinaḥ ehīti svāgatavādinaḥ
children.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having risen from meditation, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies — sweet as sweet can be, like honey free from impurity. And several hundred members of the assembly were listening to the sweet <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s> with undistracted senses. Now, <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are those who speak first, who speak kindly, who say 'Come, welcome!'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 108]

children.text: smitapūrvaṃgamāś ca | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: ehi maudgalyāyana svāgataṃ te, kutas tvam etarhy āgacchasīti | maudgalyāyana āha: āgacchāmy ahaṃ bhadanta pretacārikāyāḥ | tatrāhaṃ pretam adrākṣaṃ sūcīchidropamamukhaṃ parvatopamakukṣiṃ svakeśasaṃchannaṃ durgandhaṃ paramadurgandham* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: and who are preceded by a smile. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Come, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, welcome to you! From where do you come now?' <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> said: 'I come, Venerable Sir, from a tour of the realm of hungry ghosts. There I beheld a <s>preta</s> with a mouth like the eye of a needle, a belly like a mountain, covered with his own hair, foul-smelling, extremely foul-smelling.' And he said:

children.text: viśuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhapuṭaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ pravṛddhaśailopamacarvitāśrayaḥ | (Speyer: Ścañvitāśrayaḥ )
svakeśasaṃchannamukho digambaraḥ susūkṣmasūcīsadṛśānanaḥ kṛśaḥ || AVŚ_41.1 ||
children.translated_text: his face covered with his own hair, naked, his face like the finest needle, emaciated — // AVŚ_41.1 //
With parched throat and lips, greatly afflicted, his body a receptacle [of suffering] like a great mountain,

children.text: nagnaḥ svakeśasaṃchanno asthiyantravaducchritaḥ |
children.translated_text: naked, covered with his own hair, standing erect like a skeleton-machine,

children.text: kapālapāṇir ghoraś ca krandan samabhidhāvati || AVŚ_41.2 ||
children.translated_text: terrible, with a skull in his hand, crying out he runs about — // AVŚ_41.2 //

children.text:
bubhukṣayā pipāsayā klānto vyasanapīḍitaḥ |
  ārtasvaraṃ krandamāno duḥkhāṃ vedati vedanām* |
  kiṃ tena prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ martyaloke sudāruṇam* || AVŚ_41.3 || iti
children.translated_text: exhausted by hunger and thirst, afflicted by misfortune, crying out in a distressed voice, he experiences painful sensations. What terrible sin did he commit in the world of mortals? // AVŚ_41.3 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: pāpakārī maudgalyāyana sa pretaḥ | icchasi tasya karmaplotiṃ śrotum*? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi maudgalyāyana śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That <s>preta</s> is an evildoer, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Do you wish to hear the record of his <s>karma</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, listen well and carefully, and attend; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ maudgalyāyana rājagṛhe nagare 'nyataraḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tasya pañcamātrāṇīkṣuśālaśatāni, yatra cekṣuḥ pīḍyate | asati ca buddhānām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya | yāvad anyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho hīnadīnānukampakī prāntaśayanāsanasevī | sa pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | sa ca bhadantaḥ kṣayavyādhinā spṛṣṭaḥ | tasya vaidyenekṣurasa upadiṣṭaḥ | sa śreṣṭhisakāśaṃ yantraśālām upasaṃkrāntaḥ | śreṣṭhinā ca sa pratyekabuddho dṛṣṭaḥ kāyaprāsādikaś cittaprāsādikaś ca | dṛṣṭvā śreṣṭhinā uktaḥ: kenāryasya prayojanam iti | pratyekabuddhaḥ kathayati: gṛhapate ikṣuraseneti | tatas tena gṛhapatinā bhṛtakapuruṣasyājñā dattā āryasyekṣurasaṃ prayaccheti | sa ca gṛhapatiḥ kenacid eva karaṇīyena bahir yānāya saṃprasthitaḥ | atha tasya puruṣasya parakīye dravye mātsaryam utpannam*: yady aham asya rasaṃ dāsye, punar apy eṣa āgamiṣyatīti | tena aniṣṭagatitrayaprapātanamreṇa sarvābhimatagatidvayanirākariṣṇunā atyantadūrāpagatenāryadharmebhyaḥ pāpaṃ cittam utpādya sa pratyekabuddha uktaḥ: āhara bhikṣo pātram*, dehi, rasaṃ te dāsyāmīti | asamanvāhṛtya arhacchrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartata iti | hīnadīnānukampitayā bhṛtyapuruṣo 'yam asyānugrahaḥ kartavya iti tat pātram upanāmitam* | tato 'sau durācāro nirghṛṇahṛdayas tad gṛhītvā pratiguptaṃ pradeśaṃ gatvā prasrāveṇā pūrayitvā upari ikṣurasenācchādya tasmai pratyekabuddhāyānupradadau | tena saṃlakṣitam* sa cintayati: bahv anena tapasvinā pāpaṃ kṛtam api | sa tad ekānte chorayitvā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He had five hundred sugarcane-pressing mills where sugarcane was pressed. Now, in the absence of the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arise in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, inclined to remote lodgings and meals, worthy of offerings as sole individuals in the world. There was a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, inclined to remote lodgings. In the morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, he entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. That venerable one was afflicted with a wasting disease. A physician had prescribed sugarcane juice for him. He approached the guild-master's pressing mill. The guild-master saw that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, who was pleasing in body and pleasing in mind. Having seen him, the guild-master said: "What does the noble one require?" The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> said: "Householder, sugarcane juice." Then the householder gave an order to his hired servant: "Give sugarcane juice to the noble one." And the householder himself set out on some business outside. Then envy arose in that servant regarding another's property: "If I give him juice, he will come again." Then, with a mind inclined toward the three woeful destinations, rejecting both desired destinations, utterly far removed from noble qualities, having generated an evil thought, he said to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>: "Bring your bowl, monk; give it here, I shall give you juice." Without reflecting that the knowledge-and-vision of <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> does not operate [regarding food offered], and [thinking] with compassion for the lowly and destitute, "This hired servant wishes to do me a kindness," he handed over his bowl. Then that wicked man, merciless at heart, took it, went to a concealed spot, filled it with urine, covered it on top with sugarcane juice, and gave it back to that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. The <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> perceived [the deception]. He thought: "Much evil has been done by this wretch." He poured it out in a secluded place and departed.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 109]

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyase maudgalyāyana yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena bhṛtakapuruṣa āsīt', ayaṃ sa pretaḥ | tasya karmaṇo vipākena saṃsāre 'nantaṃ duḥkham anubhūtavān* | idānīm api pretabhūtaḥ prakṛṣṭataraṃ duḥkham anubhavati | tasmāt tarhi te maudgalyāyana mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyaṃ yathā evaṃvidhā doṣā na syur ye pretasya | iti hi maudgalyāyana ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi te maudgalyāyana ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ te maudgalyāyana śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>? He who at that time, in that era, was the hired servant — he is this <s>preta</s>. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he has experienced endless suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Even now, having become a <s>preta</s>, he experiences the most intense suffering. Therefore, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, you must strive for the abandonment of envy, so that the faults that befell this <s>preta</s> may not [befall you]. For, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanā āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, delighted in mind, and others — <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, and the rest — rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_42 bhaktam* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_42: <s>Bhaktam</s> (Food). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ {śrāvastyāṃ} viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ anyatarasmin vṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya | aśrauṣīd āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pretyāḥ śabdam ārtasvaraṃ krandantyāḥ, duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānāyā bhaktaṃ mārgantyāḥ: bubhukṣitāsmi mārṣāḥ, pipāsitāsmi mārṣā iti | tataḥ sthaviramahāmaudgalyāyanena pretī dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭā ca: kiṃ te pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ yenaivaṃvidhāni duḥkhāny anubhaviṣyasīti | pretī āha: āditye hi samudgate na dīpena prayojanam* | bhagavantam etam arthaṃ pṛccha, sa te asmākīnāṃ karmaplotiṃ vyākariṣyatīti | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at {<s>Śrāvastī</s>}, in <s>Jeta</s>'s Grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> was seated at the base of a certain tree for his midday rest. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> heard the sound of a female <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) crying out in a distressed voice, experiencing painful, intense, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations, searching for food: 'I am hungry, sirs! I am thirsty, sirs!' Then the elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having seen the female <s>preta</s>, asked her: 'What sin did you commit that you experience such sufferings?' The female <s>preta</s> said: 'When the sun has risen, there is no need for a lamp. Ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about this matter; he will explain the record of our <s>karma</s>.' Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam* | anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoty anijyamānair indriyaiḥ | tato buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūrvālāpinaḥ priyālāpinaḥ ehīti svāgatavādinaḥ smitapūrvaṃgamāś ca | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: ehi maudgalyāyana svāgataṃ te, kutas tvam etarhy āgacchasīti | maudgalyāyana āha: āgacchāmy ahaṃ bhadanta pretacārikāyāḥ | tatrāhaṃ pretīm adrākṣaṃ sūcīchidropamamukhīṃ parvatopamakukṣiṃ svakeśasaṃchannāṃ nagnām ārtasvaraṃ krandantīṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānām* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having risen from meditation, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies — sweet as sweet can be, like honey free from impurity. And several hundred members of the assembly were listening to the sweet <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s> with undistracted senses. Now, <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are those who speak first, who speak kindly, who say 'Come, welcome!' and who are preceded by a smile. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Come, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, welcome to you! From where do you come now?' <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> said: 'I come, Venerable Sir, from a tour of the realm of hungry ghosts. There I beheld a female <s>preta</s> with a mouth like the eye of a needle, a belly like a mountain, covered with her own hair, naked, crying out in a distressed voice, experiencing painful, intense, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations.' And he said:

svakeśasaṃchannamukhī digambarā susūkṣmasūcīsadṛśānanā kṛśā || AVŚ_42.1 ||
children.translated_text: her face covered with her own hair, naked, her face like the finest needle, emaciated — // AVŚ_42.1 //
With parched throat and lips, greatly afflicted, her body a receptacle [of suffering] like a great mountain,

ārtasvaraṃ krandamānā duḥkhāṃ vindanti vedanām* || AVŚ_42.3 ||
children.translated_text: crying out in a distressed voice, she experiences painful sensations. // AVŚ_42.3 //
exhausted by hunger and thirst, afflicted by misfortune,

children.text:
kiṃ tayā prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ martyaloke sudāruṇam* |
  yena evaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavati bhayānakam* || AVŚ_42.4 || iti
children.translated_text: What terrible sin did she commit in the world of mortals, that she experiences such fearful suffering? // AVŚ_42.4 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: pāpakāriṇī maudgalyāyana sā pretī | icchasi tasyā karmaplotiṃ śrotum*? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi maudgalyāyana śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That female <s>preta</s> is an evildoer, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Do you wish to hear the record of her <s>karma</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, listen well and carefully, and attend; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ maudgalyāyana atīte 'dhvani viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tasyāṃ ca vārāṇasyām anyatamā gṛhapatipatnī matsariṇī kuṭukuñcikā āgṛhītapariṣkārā kākāyāpi baliṃ na pradātuṃ vyavasyati, prāg evānyeṣāṃ yācakānām* | sā śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakān dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ pradūṣayati | yāvad anyataraḥ piṇḍapātikas tasyā gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tasyās taṃ dṛṣṭvā mātsaryam utpannam* | cittaṃ ca pradūṣya imāṃ cintām āpede: yady aham asya satkāraṃ kariṣyāmi, punar apy eṣa āgamiṣyatīti | tatas tayā pāpakāriṇyā aniṣṭaṃ paralokabhayam avigaṇayya sa bhikṣur upanimantrya dvāraṃ baddhvā bhaktacchedaṃ kāritaḥ | bahu ca paribhāṣyoktaḥ: iyaṃ te bhikṣo satkriyā | mā punar idaṃ gṛhaṃ pravekṣyasīti ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, in a past age, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. In that <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a certain householder's wife was envious, a miser, tight-fisted with her possessions — she would not even consent to give an offering to a crow, let alone to other beggars. Seeing ascetics, brahmins, the wretched, and wanderers, she would corrupt her mind. Then a certain alms-seeking monk entered her house. Upon seeing him, envy arose in her. And having corrupted her mind, she conceived this thought: "If I show him hospitality, he will come again." Then that evildoer, disregarding the fearful consequences in the next world, invited the monk in, shut the door, and caused him to go without food. And she abused him harshly, saying: "This is your hospitality, monk! Do not ever enter this house again!"'

children.text: sā tena mātsaryeṇāsevitena bhāvitena bahulīkṛtena preteṣūpapannā | evaṃvidhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavati | tasmāt tarhi maudgalyāyana mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyam* | ete doṣā na bhaviṣyanti, te tasyāḥ pretyā iti ||
children.translated_text: She, by that jealousy — cultivated, developed, and made habitual — was reborn among the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts). She experiences sufferings of this kind. Therefore, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, one must strive for the abandonment of jealousy. Those faults will not arise, those that belong to that female <s>preta</s>.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasa āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, delighted in mind, along with others — <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.translated_text: AVŚ_43: <s>Pānīya</s> (Water). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pretacārikāṃ caran pretīm adrākṣīd dagdhasthūṇāsadṛśīṃ svakeśasaṃchannāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground). The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, wandering through the realm of <s>pretas</s>, saw a female <s>preta</s> — resembling a burnt pillar, covered with her own hair,

children.text: sūcīchidropamamukhīṃ parvatopamakukṣim ādīptāṃ pradīptāṃ prajvalitām ekajvālībhūtāṃ dhmāyantīṃ tṛṣārtāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānām* | darśanamātreṇa cāsyā nadyudapānāni śuṣyanti | yadā devo varṣati, tadā tasyā upari savisphuliṅgāṅgāravarṣaṃ patati | dṛṣṭvā tām āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyana āha: kiṃ tvayā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yenaivaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavasīti | pretī āha: pāpakāriṇy ahaṃ bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana | etam ārthaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛccha | sa te asmākīnāṃ karmaplotiṃ kathayiṣyati, yāṃ śrutvā anye 'pīha satvāḥ pāpāt karmaṇaḥ prativiraṃsyantīti | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: her mouth like the eye of a needle, her belly like a mountain, blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire, smoldering, tormented by thirst, experiencing painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations. At the mere sight of her, rivers and wells dried up. Whenever it rained, upon her there fell a rain of sparks and embers. Having seen her, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said: 'What evil deed did you commit, that you experience such suffering?' The female <s>preta</s> said: 'I am an evildoer, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about this matter. He will tell you the web of our <s>karma</s>, hearing which other beings too will turn away from evil deeds.' Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam* | anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoty anijyamānair indriyaiḥ | tato buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūrvālāpinaḥ priyālāpina ehīti svāgatavādinaḥ smitapūrvaṃgamāś ca | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: ehi maudgalyāyana svāgataṃ te, kutas tvam etarhy āgacchasīti | mahāmaudgalyāyana āha: āgacchāmy ahaṃ bhadanta pretacārikāyāḥ | tatrāhaṃ pretīm adrākṣaṃ dagdhasthūṇāsadṛśīṃ svakeśasaṃchannāṃ sūcīchidropamamukhīṃ parvatopamakukṣim ādīptāṃ pradīptāṃ prajvalitām ekajvālībhūtāṃ dhmāyantīm ārtasvaraṃ kradantīṃ tṛṣārtāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānām* | darśanamātreṇa cāsyā nadyudapānāni śuṣyanti | yadā devo varṣati tadā asyā upari savisphuliṅgam aṅgāravarṣaṃ patati | bhagavān āha: pāpakāriṇī maudgalyāyana sā pretī | icchasi tasyā karmaplotiṃ śrotum*? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi maudgalyāyana śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Now at that time the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having arisen from meditative absorption, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies — sweet as honey, like pure honey free from impurities. And the assembly of many hundreds was listening to the sweet <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s> with unwavering faculties. Now the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are ones who speak first, who speak kindly, who say 'come' and 'welcome,' and who are preceded by a smile. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Come, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, welcome to you! Where do you come from now?' <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said: 'I come, Venerable Sir, from wandering in the realm of <s>pretas</s>. There I saw a female <s>preta</s> — resembling a burnt pillar, covered with her own hair, her mouth like the eye of a needle, her belly like a mountain, blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire, smoldering, crying out in a voice of distress, tormented by thirst, experiencing painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations. At the mere sight of her, rivers and wells dried up. Whenever it rained, upon her there fell a rain of sparks and embers.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That female <s>preta</s> is an evildoer, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Do you wish to hear the web of her <s>karma</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, listen well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ maudgalyāyana atīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrakalpe viṃśatisahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tatrānyatamo bhikṣur adhvānaṃ pratipannaḥ | sa tṛṣārtaḥ kūpam upasṛptaḥ | tatrānyatarā dārikā pānīyaghaṭaṃ pūrayitvā sthitābhūt* | sā bhikṣuṇoktā: tṛṣārto 'haṃ bhagini, pānīyam anuprayaccheti | tasyā mātsaryam utpannam* | sā āgṛhītapariṣkārā bhikṣum uvāca: bhikṣo yadi mriyase, na te dadāmi pānīyam*, ghaṭo me ūno bhaviṣyatīti | tato 'sau bhikṣus tṛṣārto nirāśaḥ prakrāntaḥ | tato 'sau dārikā tena mātsaryeṇāsevitena bhāvitena bahulīkṛtena kālaṃ kṛtvā preteṣūpapannā | evaṃvidhāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate | tasmāt tarhi maudgalyāyana evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yan mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyaṃsyāmahe | ity evaṃ te maudgalyāyana śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, in a past age, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of <s>Devas</s> and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Deer Park at Sarnath), in the <s>Mṛgadāva</s>. There a certain monk had set out on a journey. Tormented by thirst, he approached a well. There a certain girl was standing, having filled her water-pot. That monk said to her: "I am tormented by thirst, sister; please give me water." Jealousy arose in her. She, holding onto her vessel, said to the monk: "Monk, even if you die, I will not give you water — my pot will become less full!" Then that monk, tormented by thirst, departed without hope. And that girl, by that jealousy — cultivated, developed, and made habitual — upon dying was reborn among the <s>pretas</s>. She experiences such painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations. Therefore, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, you should train thus: "We shall strive for the abandonment of jealousy." Thus, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanā āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, delighted in mind, along with others — <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and others — rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_44 varcaghaṭaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_44: <s>Varcaghaṭa</s> (The Pot of Excrement). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text:
buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisamarpya yena gṛdhrakūṭaḥ parvatas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvatam avagāhyānyatarad vṛkṣamūlaṃ niśritya niṣaṇṇo divāvihārāya | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pretīm ādrakṣīd dagdhasthūṇāsadṛśīṃ nagnāṃ svakeśasaṃchannāṃ sūcīchidropamamukhīṃ parvatopamakukṣim ādīptāṃ pradīptāṃ prajvalitām ekajvālībhūtāṃ dhmāyantīm ārtasvaraṃ kradantīṃ tṛṣārtāṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānām* | durgandhāṃ paramadurgandhāṃ varcaḥsadṛśīṃ varcohārāṃ tad api kṛcchreṇāsādayantīm* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ saṃvignaḥ | pretīṃ ca papraccha:
  kiṃ tvayā prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yasya te īdṛśaṃ phalam iti |
  pretī āha: pāpakāriṇy <MS: prāgapakāriṇy> ahaṃ bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana | etam ārthaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛccha | sa te asmākīnāṃ karmaplotiṃ vyākariṣyati (Speyer: Śṣyatīti) | yāṃ śrutvānye 'pi satvāḥ pāpakarmaṇaḥ prativiraṃsyantīti | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Having wandered through <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms, having finished his meal, returning from his alms-round after the meal, having put away his bowl and robe, he approached <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain. Having approached and entered <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> Mountain, he sat down at the foot of a certain tree for the day's meditation. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> saw a female <s>preta</s> — resembling a burnt pillar, naked, covered with her own hair, her mouth like the eye of a needle, her belly like a mountain, blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire, smoldering, crying out in a voice of distress, tormented by thirst, experiencing painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations. She was foul-smelling, supremely foul-smelling, resembling excrement, feeding on excrement, and even that she obtained with difficulty. Having seen her, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> was struck with spiritual urgency. And he asked the female <s>preta</s>:
'What evil deed did you commit, of which this is the fruit?'
The female <s>preta</s> said: 'I am an evildoer, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Ask the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, about this matter. He will explain the web of our <s>karma</s>, hearing which other beings too will turn away from evil deeds.' Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam* | anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān {madhura}madhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoty anijyamānair indriyaiḥ | tato buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūrvālāpinaḥ priyālāpinaḥ ehīti svāgatavādinaḥ smitapūrvaṃgamāś ca | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: ehi maudgalyāyana svāgataṃ te, kutas tvam etarhy āgacchasīti | maudgalyāyana āha: āgacchāmy ahaṃ bhadanta pretacārikāyāḥ | tatrāhaṃ pretīm adrākṣaṃ dagdhasthūṇāsadṛśīṃ nagnāṃ svakeśasaṃchannāṃ sūcīchidropamamukhīṃ parvatopamakukṣim ādīptāṃ pradīptāṃ prajvalitām ekajvālībhūtām ārtasvaraṃ krandantīṃ duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānām* | darśanamātreṇa cāsyā nadyudapānāni śuṣyanti | yadā devo varṣati, tadā tasyā upari savisphuliṅgam aṅgāravarṣaṃ patati, durgandhāṃ paramadurgandhāṃ varcaḥsadṛśāṃ ca varcāhārāṃ tad api kṛcchreṇāsādayantīm* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Now at that time the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having arisen from meditative absorption, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies — sweet as honey, like pure honey free from impurities. And the assembly of many hundreds was listening to the sweet <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Bhagavān</s> with unwavering faculties. Now the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are ones who speak first, who speak kindly, who say 'come' and 'welcome,' and who are preceded by a smile. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Come, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, welcome to you! Where do you come from now?' <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> said: 'I come, Venerable Sir, from wandering in the realm of <s>pretas</s>. There I saw a female <s>preta</s> — resembling a burnt pillar, naked, covered with her own hair, her mouth like the eye of a needle, her belly like a mountain, blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire, crying out in a voice of distress, experiencing painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations. At the mere sight of her, rivers and wells dried up. Whenever it rained, upon her there fell a rain of sparks and embers. She was foul-smelling, supremely foul-smelling, resembling excrement, feeding on excrement, and even that she obtained with difficulty.' And he said:

children.text: {nagnā svakeśasaṃchannā asthiyantravaducchritā |}
ārtasvaraṃ krandamānā duḥkhāṃ vindati vedanām* || AVŚ_44.1 ||
children.translated_text: crying out in a voice of distress, she experiences painful sensation.' // AVŚ_44.1 //
'Naked, covered with her own hair, raised up like a skeleton on a frame,

children.text: yena hi varcadhānāni tena dhāvati duḥkhitā |
children.translated_text: 'Wherever there are deposits of excrement, there she runs in misery;

children.text: varcaḥ pāsyāmi bhokṣye ca tac ca duḥkhena labhyate || AVŚ_44.2 ||
children.translated_text: "I shall drink excrement, I shall eat it" — and even that is obtained with difficulty.' // AVŚ_44.2 //

children.text: kiṃ tayā prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ martyaloke sudāruṇam* |
children.translated_text: 'What terrible evil did she commit in the world of mortals,

children.text: yena evaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavati bhayānakam* || AVŚ_44.3 ||
children.translated_text: that she experiences such fearful suffering?' // AVŚ_44.3 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: pāpakāriṇī maudgalyāyana sā pretī | icchasi tasyāḥ karmaplotiṃ śrotum*? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi maudgalyāyana śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That female <s>preta</s> is an evildoer, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Do you wish to hear the web of her <s>karma</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, listen well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ maudgalyāyana vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho hīnadīnānukampī prāntaśayanāsanasevī ca | sa vyādhito vārāṇasīṃ piṇḍāya prāviśati | yāvad asya vaidyena sāṃpreyaṃ bhojanam upadiṣṭam* | sa yenānyatamasya śreṣṭhino niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | tena ca śreṣṭhinā dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaś ca: kena te ārya prayojanam iti | tenoktaṃ kulasāṃpreyeṇa bhojaneneti | tataḥ śreṣṭhinā vadhvā ājñā dattā: āryāya sāṃpreyaṃ bhojanaṃ dātavyam iti | atha tasyā vadhvā mātsaryam utpannam*: yady aham asmai adya bhojanaṃ pradāsyāmi, śvo bhūya āgamiṣyatīti | tayā ekāntam apasṛtya varcasaḥ pātraṃ pūrayitvā upari bhaktena pracchādya tasmai pratyekabuddhāya dattam* | asamanvāhṛtya śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate | tena pratigṛhītam* | pratigṛhya saṃlakṣitaṃ yathaitad durgandham* | nūnam anayā amedhyasya pūritam iti | tato 'sau mahātmā tadekānte chorayitvā prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Awakened One) — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, frequenting secluded lodgings. He, being ill, entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms. A physician had prescribed restorative food for him. He approached the dwelling of a certain guild-master. That guild-master saw him and asked: "What do you need, noble one?" He said: "Restorative food befitting a good family." Then the guild-master gave instructions to his daughter-in-law: "Give the noble one restorative food." But jealousy arose in that daughter-in-law: "If I give him food today, tomorrow he will come again." She went aside to a secluded place, filled a pot with excrement, covered it on top with cooked food, and gave it to that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Without reflecting — for the knowledge-and-vision of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> does not operate [in such matters] — he accepted it. Having accepted it, he noticed that it was foul-smelling: "Surely she has filled it with filth." Then that great-souled one, having discarded it in a secluded place, departed.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyase maudgalyāyana yāsau tena kālena tena samayena śreṣṭhivadhukā, iyaṃ sā pretī | yad upādāyānayā tādṛkpāpaṃ kṛtam* | tataḥ prabhṛti nityaṃ narakatiryakpreteṣūpapadyate, nityaṃ ca varcāhārā | tasmāt tarhi te maudgalyāyana mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyaṃ yathā ete doṣā na syur ye tasyāḥ pretyā | evaṃ maudgalyāyana śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>? She who at that time, in that era, was the merchant's daughter-in-law — she is that very <s>pretī</s> (female hungry ghost). Because of the evil deed committed by her, from that time onward she is constantly reborn among the denizens of hell, the animals, and the <s>pretas</s>, and she is constantly a feeder on excrement. Therefore, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, you must strive for the abandonment of <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness), so that these faults that afflict that <s>pretī</s> may not arise [in you]. Thus, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanā āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, delighted in mind, and the other <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and others rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_45 maudgalyāyanaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_45: <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | tena khalu punaḥ samayena antarā ca rājagṛham antarā ca veṇuvanam atrāntare pañca pretaśatāni dagdhasthūṇākṛtīni nagnāni svakeśasaṃchannāni parvatopamakukṣīṇi sūcīchidropamamukhāni ādīptāni pradīptāni saṃprajvalitāny ekajvālībhūtāny ārtasvaraṃ pralapamānāni duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. Now at that time, between <s>Rājagṛha</s> and the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, in the intervening space, there were five hundred <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) — their forms like burnt stumps, naked, covered only by their own hair, with bellies as large as mountains, mouths as narrow as the eye of a needle, ablaze, burning, fully inflamed, become a single mass of flame, crying out in anguished voices, experiencing painful, intense, harsh, bitter,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 114]

children.text: amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānāni vāyumaṇḍalavadākāśe paribhramanti, na kvacit pratiṣṭhāṃ labhante | athāyuṣmān mahamaudgalyāyanaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | tena te pretā dṛṣṭāḥ, tair api pretair āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ | tatas te ekasamūhenāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam upasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya karuṇadīnavilambitair akṣarair ekaraveṇocuḥ: vayaṃ smo bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana rājagṛhe pañca śreṣṭhiśatāny abhūvan* | te vayaṃ matsariṇaḥ kuṭukuñjakā āgṛhītapariṣkārāḥ | svayaṃ tāvad asmābhir dānapradānāni na dattāni, pareṣām api dānapradāneṣu dīyamāneṣu vighnāḥ kṛtāḥ, dakṣiṇīyāś ca bahavaḥ pretavādena paribhāṣitāḥ: pretopapannā iva yūyaṃ nityaṃ paragṛhebhyo bhaikṣyam aṭatha (Speyer: aṭhatha) | ete vayaṃ kālaṃ kṛtvā evaṃvidheṣu preteṣūpapannāḥ | iti bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana ye 'smākaṃ jñātayo rājagṛhe prativasanti, teṣām asmākīnāṃ karmaplotiṃ nivedya chandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayitvā asmākaṃ nāmnā dakṣiṇādeśanāṃ kārayitvā cāsmākaṃ pretayoner mokṣaḥ syād iti | adhivāsayaty āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pretānāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena | tata āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanena teṣāṃ jñātigṛhebhyaś cchandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ śvo bhaktenopamantritaḥ | pretānāṃ ca niveditam*: śvo bhagavān sabhikṣusaṃgho bhaktenopanimantritaḥ, tatra yuṣmābhir āgantavyam iti | jñātīnām apy ārocitam*: bhavadbhir āgantavyaṃ tatra jñātibhojane | tān pretān drakṣyāmaḥ | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ svayam evodyukto bhojanaṃ pratijāgaritum* ||
children.translated_text: disagreeable sensations, spinning through the sky like whirlwinds, finding no resting place anywhere. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. He saw those <s>pretas</s>, and those <s>pretas</s> also saw the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Then they all together approached the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Having approached, with pitiful, wretched, faltering words, they cried out in one voice: 'We were, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, five hundred guild-masters in <s>Rājagṛha</s>. We were miserly, grasping, hoarders of possessions. Not only did we ourselves fail to give charitable gifts, but when others were giving, we created obstacles; and we reviled many worthy recipients of offerings with the taunt of being <s>pretas</s>: "Like beings reborn as <s>pretas</s>, you are always begging from the houses of others!" Having died, we have been reborn among such <s>pretas</s> as these. Therefore, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, inform our relatives dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>; report to them the fruit of our <s>karma</s>; and having obtained their consent, feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> in our name, and have the dedication of merit made in our name — so that we may be freed from the <s>preta</s> realm.' The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> consented to the <s>pretas</s> by his silence. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having obtained consent from their relatives' households, invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for a meal the next day. He also informed the <s>pretas</s>: 'Tomorrow the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks has been invited for a meal; you must come there.' He also told the relatives: 'You must come to that feast for the kin. We shall see those <s>pretas</s>.' Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> himself stayed up to watch over the preparations for the meal.

children.text: atha prabhātāyāṃ rajanyām āhāre sajjīkṛte gaṇḍīdeśakāle saṃprāpte tān pretān na paśyati | tata āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano divyena cakṣuṣā tān pretān samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ | sarvasminn eva magadhamaṇḍale nādrākṣīt* | yāvat krameṇa cāturdvīpikaṃ vyavalokayituṃ pravṛttaḥ | tatrāpi nādrākṣīt* | tato yāvad asya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate, tato vyavalokayituṃ pravṛttaḥ | tatrāpi nādrākṣīt* | tata āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ saṃvigno bhagavate nivedayāmāsa: bhagavan, na me dānapatayo dṛśyanta iti | bhagavān āha: ayaṃ maudgalyāyana mā khedam āpadyasva | sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaviṣayam atikramya aparimāṇā lokadhātavaḥ santi | tatra te karmavāyunā kṣiptāḥ | api maudgalyāyana adya tathāgatabalaṃ paśya | sarvajñajñānadarśanaṃ vyaktīkariṣyāmi | tathāgatavikurvitaṃ darśayiṣyāmi | ākoṭyatāṃ gaṇḍīti | tato gaṇḍyām ākoṭitāyāṃ sarvo bhikṣusaṃghaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ, pretajñātayo 'nye ca kautūhalyābhyāgatāḥ satvāḥ pretadarśanotsukāḥ saṃnipatitāḥ | tato bhagavatā ṛddhyā tathā darśitaṃ yathā pretā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhuñjānaṃ paśyanti, smṛtiṃ ca pratilabhante: jñātayo asmad arthe buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayantīti | tato bhagavān pañcāṅgopetena svareṇa dakṣiṇām ādiśati:
children.translated_text: Then, when the night had passed and the food had been prepared, when the time came to strike the gong, he did not see those <s>pretas</s>. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> began to search for those <s>pretas</s> with his divine eye. He did not see them in the entire realm of <s>Magadha</s>. Gradually he began to survey the four continents — even there he did not see them. Then, as far as his knowledge-and-vision extended, he began to look — even there he did not see them. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, spiritually stirred, reported to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, I cannot see my donors!' The Blessed One said: 'Do not distress yourself about this, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Beyond the range of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, there are immeasurable world-systems. There they have been blown by the winds of <s>karma</s>. But, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, today behold the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! I shall make manifest the knowledge-and-vision of the Omniscient One; I shall display the miracle of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Let the gong be struck!' Then, when the gong was struck, the entire <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks assembled, and the relatives of the <s>pretas</s> and other beings who had come out of curiosity, eager to see the <s>pretas</s>, also assembled. Then the Blessed One displayed such a miracle by his supernatural power that the <s>pretas</s> could see the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, eating; and they recovered their mindfulness [thinking]: 'Our relatives are feeding the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for our sake.' Then the Blessed One, with a voice endowed with five qualities, dedicated the merit:

children.text:
ito dānād dhi yat puṇyaṃ tat pretān anugacchatu |
  uttiṣṭhantāṃ kṣipram ete pretalokāt sudāruṇāt* || AVŚ_44.1 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'Whatever merit arises from this gift, may it follow those <s>pretas</s>!
May they swiftly arise from that most terrible <s>preta</s> realm!' // AVŚ_44.1 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 115]

children.text: yāvad bhagavatā tad adhiṣṭhānā tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā anekair prāṇiśatasahasrair mātsaryamalaṃ prahāya satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | te ca pretā bhagavati cittam abhiprasādya kālagatāḥ, praṇīteṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> through that blessing that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of beings abandoned the stain of <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) and gained the vision of the truth. And those <s>pretas</s>, having generated faith in the Blessed One, died and were reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyakāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | paśyanti pretebhyaś cyutāḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittam ahiprasādyeti | atha pretapūrviṇāṃ devaputrāṇām etad abhavat: nāsmākaṃ pratirūpaṃ syāt, yad vayaṃ paryuṣitaparivāsā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmema | yan nu vayam aparyuṣitaparivāsā eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmemeti | atha pretapūrviṇo devaputrāś calavimalakuṇḍaladharā hārārdhahāravirājitagātrā maṇiratnavicitramaulayaḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātrās tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmapuṇḍarīkamandāravādīnāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā samantato venuvaṃ kalandakanivāpam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavataṃ puṣpair ākīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān pretapūrviṇāṃ devaputrāṇām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā pretapūrvikair devaputrair mahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ | te labdhalābhā iva vaṇijo bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tatraivāntarhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or a <s>Devakanyā</s> has been newly reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what deed?' They perceived: 'We have passed away from the <s>preta</s> realm and have been reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, by generating faith in the Blessed One.' Then those <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been <s>pretas</s> thought: 'It would not be fitting for us to approach the Blessed One for an audience after having rested overnight. Rather, let us approach the Blessed One for an audience without having rested overnight.' Then those <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been <s>pretas</s> — wearing shimmering, spotless earrings, their bodies adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, their crowns studded with jewels and precious gems, their bodies anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, and <s>spṛkkā</s> (aromatic substances) — that very night, having filled their laps with divine flowers of <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>mandārava</s>, and other [heavenly flowers], illuminated the entire <s>Veṇuvana</s> <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> with their brilliant radiance, scattered flowers upon the Blessed One, and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, inclination, nature, and character of those <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been <s>pretas</s>, delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, those <s>Devaputras</s> attained a great spiritual distinction. Like merchants who have gained their profit, they circumambulated the Blessed One three times and vanished right there.

children.text: tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate | sādhu sādhu mahāmaudgalyāyana | saphalaṃ te vaiyāvṛtyaṃ saṃvṛttam* | yat te # # # pretā deveṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ | te 'syāṃ rātrau matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntāḥ | teṣāṃ mayā dharmo deśitaḥ | te labdhodayā labdhalābhāḥ prakrāntā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>! Your service has been fruitful. Your ### <s>pretas</s> have been established among the gods. They came to my presence this very night. I taught them the <s>Dharma</s>. Having gained their spiritual progress and their profit, they departed.'

children.text: tata āyuṣmatā mahāmaudgalyāyanena teṣāṃ jñātīnām ārocitam* | te śrutvā paraṃ vismayam upagatā bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādayāmāsur bhūyaś ca satkāraṃ pracakrur iti | tasmāt tarhi te maudgalyāyana mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyam* | ete doṣā na bhavanti ye teṣāṃ pretānām iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> informed their relatives. Having heard, they were filled with supreme wonder and generated faith in the Blessed One, and offered further acts of worship. 'Therefore, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, you must strive for the abandonment of <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness). These faults that afflicted those <s>pretas</s> will not arise [in you].'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanā āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, delighted in mind, and the other <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and others rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_46 uttaraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_46: <s>Uttara</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | rājagṛhe 'nyataraḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. In <s>Rājagṛha</s> there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported with her,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 116]

children.text: ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jātaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād uttare nakṣatre jātas tasmād bhavatūttara iti nāma | uttaro dārako unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛtaḥ | pitā cāsya kālagataḥ | uttaraś ca gṛhe svāmī saṃvṛttaḥ | tenāpaṇaḥ sthāpitaḥ | krīṇāti vikrīṇīte krayavikrayeṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayati | sa divasānudivasaṃ bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāmati | tasya bhagavatsaṃdarśanāt saddharmaśravaṇāc ca bhagavacchāsane prasādo jātaḥ | tasya pravrajyācittam utpannam* | sa mātaraṃ vijñāpayāmāsa: amba anujānīhi māṃ bhagavacchāsaneṣu pravrajiṣyāmīti | tato mātā kathayati: putra tvam ekaputrakaḥ | yāvad ahaṃ jīvāmi, tāvan na pravrajitavyam* | mṛtāyāṃ mayi yathākaraṇīyaṃ kariṣyasīti | sa cottaro yat kiṃcid upārjayati tat sarvaṃ mātre 'nuprayacchati: anena amba śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakān pratipādayasveti | sā cāsya mātā lubdhā kuṭukuñcikā matsariṇī āgṛhītapariṣkārā tān kārṣāpaṇān gopayitvā ye śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ piṇḍārthinas tad gṛhaṃ praviśanti, tān paribhāṣate: pretopapannā iva yūyaṃ nityaṃ paragṛhebhyo bhaikṣam aṭatheti | sā ca putraṃ visaṃvādayati: aham adya iyatāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ bhojanaṃ prayacchāmīti ||
children.translated_text: He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, in the course of time his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born. At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since he was born under the <s>Uttara</s> constellation, let his name be <s>Uttara</s>.' The boy <s>Uttara</s> was raised, nourished, and grew up. His father passed away. <s>Uttara</s> became the master of the household. He established a shop. He bought and sold, making his livelihood through trade. Day after day he would approach the Blessed One. From seeing the Blessed One and hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, faith arose in him regarding the Blessed One's teaching. The thought of going forth arose in him. He petitioned his mother: 'Mother, give me permission — I wish to go forth in the Blessed One's teaching.' Then the mother said: 'Son, you are my only child. As long as I am alive, you must not go forth. When I am dead, you may do as you wish.' And <s>Uttara</s> gave everything he earned to his mother: 'With this, mother, give to <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, and wanderers.' But his mother was greedy, tight-fisted, miserly, and possessive of her belongings. She hoarded those coins, and whenever <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seeking alms entered that house, she would abuse them: 'You are like beings reborn as <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), always begging from others' houses!' And she deceived her son, saying: 'Today I have given food to such-and-such number of monks.'

children.text: yāvad asau kālaṃ kṛtvā preteṣūpapannā | uttaraś ca mātṛviyogād dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣākṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In due time she died and was reborn among the <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts). <s>Uttara</s>, grieving the separation from his mother, having given gifts and performed meritorious deeds, went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: sa gaṅgātīre parṇakuṭiṃ kṛtvā dhyāyati | sā cāsya mātā pretalokopapannā nagnā dagdhasthūṇāsadṛśī svakeśaromasaṃchannā sūcīchidropamamukhī parvatopamakukṣir ādīptā saṃprajvalitā ekajvālībhūtā ārtasvaraṃ kradantī āyuṣmantam uttaram upasaṃkrāntā | yāvad āyuṣmatā uttareṇa sā pretī dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭā ca: kā tvam evaṃvidheti | pretī āha:
children.translated_text: He made a leaf-hut on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and meditated there. His mother, having been reborn in the realm of <s>pretas</s> — naked, resembling a burnt pillar, covered with her own hair, with a mouth like the eye of a needle, a belly like a mountain, blazing, burning, a single mass of flame — crying out in a voice of agony, approached the venerable <s>Uttara</s>. When the venerable <s>Uttara</s> saw that <s>pretī</s> (female hungry ghost), he asked: 'Who are you, in such a state?' The <s>pretī</s> said:

children.text: ahaṃ te jananī snigdhā yayā jāto 'si putraka |
children.translated_text: 'I am your loving mother, by whom you were born, dear son.

children.text: annapānaviyukteṣu preteṣu samupāgatā || AVŚ_46.1 ||
children.translated_text: I have come among the <s>pretas</s>, deprived of food and drink.' // AVŚ_46.1 //

children.text: pañcaviṃśati varṣāṇi yataḥ kālagatā hy aham* |
children.translated_text: 'Twenty-five years have passed since I died.

children.text: nābhijānāmi pānīyaṃ kuto bhaktasya darśanam* || AVŚ_46.2 ||
children.translated_text: I have not known even water — how much less the sight of food!' // AVŚ_46.2 //

children.text: saphalān vṛkṣān gacchāmi niṣphalā me bhavanti te |
children.translated_text: 'I go to trees bearing fruit, but they become fruitless for me.

children.text: pūrṇāni sarāṃsi gacchāmi tāni śuṣkāṇi santi me || AVŚ_46.3 ||
children.translated_text: I go to full lakes, but they become dry for me.' // AVŚ_46.3 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 117]

children.text: sukhaṃ bhadantasya hi vṛkṣamūlaṃ udakaṃ bhajate śītala bhājanesmim* |
children.translated_text: 'Happy indeed is the tree-root for you, Venerable Sir, and cool water rests in your vessel.

children.text: kṛpā janayitvā {janetvā} kṛpaṇāyai mahyaṃ dadasva toyaṃ tṛṣārtitāyai || AVŚ_46.4 ||
children.translated_text: Having aroused compassion for me, the wretched one, give water to me who is tormented by thirst!' // AVŚ_46.4 //

children.text: tata uttaro mātaram uvāca: amba nanu purā tvaṃ mayā manuṣyabhūtā dānāni dāpitā, puṇyāni kāriteti | pretī āha: na mayā putraka mātsaryābhibhūtayā dānāni dattāni, puṇyāni vā kṛtāni | sarvaṃ tadarthajātaṃ pāpacittayā agnikhadāyāṃ nikhātam* | tad idānīṃ putraka jñātigṛhaṃ gatvā chandanabhikṣaṃ kṛtvā mama nāmnā buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojaya, dakṣiṇām ādeśaya, deśanāṃ ca kāraya | evaṃ pretayoner mama mokṣaḥ syād iti | uttara āha: evam astu amba | kiṃ tu tvayā buddhānte sthātavyam iti | pretī āha: putrakā, apatrape nagnā hriyānviteti | uttara āha: amba yadā pāpaṃ karoṣi, tadā nāpatrapitā | idānīṃ kimarthaṃ phalakāle vyapatrapasa iti | pretī āha: evaṃ bhavatu, āgamiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Uttara</s> said to his mother: 'Mother, did I not, when you were a human being, cause you to give gifts and perform meritorious deeds?' The <s>pretī</s> said: 'Son, overwhelmed by miserliness, I neither gave gifts nor performed meritorious deeds. All the wealth designated for that purpose I buried in a charcoal-pit with a wicked mind. Now, son, go to the relatives' house, beg for sandalwood, and in my name feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, dedicate the merit, and have a teaching given. In this way, I may be freed from the realm of <s>pretas</s>.' <s>Uttara</s> said: 'So be it, mother. But you must stand at the end [of the assembly] before the <s>Buddha</s>.' The <s>pretī</s> said: 'Son, I am ashamed — I am naked and filled with embarrassment.' <s>Uttara</s> said: 'Mother, when you were doing evil, you felt no shame. Now, at the time of reaping the fruit, why are you ashamed?' The <s>pretī</s> said: 'Very well, I shall come.'

children.text: tata uttareṇa jñātigṛhebhyaś chandanabhikṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ śvo bhaktenopanimantritaḥ | gaṇḍīkāle ca buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ samnipatitaḥ | sā ca pretī budhānte sthitā | pretīdidṛkṣukāny anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni | te tāṃ pretīṃ vikṛtāśrayāṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ saṃvegam upagatāḥ bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādayāmāsuḥ | tataḥ āyuṣmān uttaro buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya pretyā nāmnā dakṣiṇādeśanāṃ kārayāmāsa | bhagavāṃś ca pañcāṅgopetena svareṇa svayam eva dakṣiṇādeśanām ādiśati:
children.translated_text: Then <s>Uttara</s>, having begged sandalwood from the relatives' houses, invited the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for the next day's meal. At the time of the bell, the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> assembled. And that <s>pretī</s> stood at the end [of the assembly] behind the <s>Buddha</s>. Many hundreds of thousands of beings assembled, wishing to see the <s>pretī</s>. Having seen that <s>pretī</s> with her disfigured form, they were seized with the utmost spiritual urgency and purified their minds in the presence of the Blessed One. Then the venerable <s>Uttara</s>, having satisfied the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> with choice food, had the dedication of merit made in the name of the <s>pretī</s>. And the Blessed One himself, with a voice endowed with five qualities, pronounced the dedication of merit:

children.text:
ito dānād dhi yat punyaṃ tat pretīm anugacchatu |
  uttiṣṭhatāṃ kṣipram iyaṃ pretalokāt sudāruṇāt || AVŚ_46.5 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'Whatever merit arises from this gift, may it reach the <s>pretī</s>!
May she quickly arise from this terrible realm of <s>pretas</s>!' // AVŚ_46.5 //

children.text: yāvad bhagavatā tad adhiṣṭhānaṃ tasyāḥ pretyā mahataś ca janakāyasya tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā anekaprāṇiśatasahasrair satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | sā ca prasannacittā kālagatā pretamaharddhikeṣūpapannā || āyuṣmatottareṇa samanvāhṛtā pretamaharddhikeṣūpapannā | tata āyuṣmatā uttareṇoktam*: amba asti te śaktiḥ | kriyatāṃ dānotsarga iti | pretamaharddhikovāca: putra na śakyāmi | nāsti me dāne 'bhilāṣa iti | tata āyuṣmān uttaraḥ pretamaharddhikām uvāca:
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One gave a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> of such a kind, for the benefit of that <s>pretī</s> and the great multitude of people, that upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained the vision of truth. And she, with a purified mind, died and was reborn among the <s>pretas</s> of great supernatural power. The venerable <s>Uttara</s> investigated and found she had been reborn among the <s>pretas</s> of great supernatural power. Then the venerable <s>Uttara</s> said: 'Mother, you now have the ability. Make a gift!' The <s>pretī</s> of great supernatural power said: 'Son, I cannot. I have no desire for giving.' Then the venerable <s>Uttara</s> said to the <s>pretī</s> of great supernatural power:

children.text:
adyāpi te tiṣṭhati tac charīraṃ vivṛddhanirmāṃsatvagasthicarmam* |
  lobhāndhakārāvṛtalocanāyā nivartitaṃ yat tvayā pretaloke || AVŚ_46.6 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'Even now that body of yours remains — with swollen flesh, dried skin, bones, and hide.
With eyes blinded by the darkness of greed, you have been consigned to the realm of <s>pretas</s>.' // AVŚ_46.6 //

children.text: yāvad āyuṣmatā uttareṇa subahu paribhāṣya ekā yamalī labdhā | tataḥ sā saṃghāya dattā | yena ca bhikṣuṇā saṃghamadhyāt sā yamalī krītā, tena mānavake sthāpitā | tatas tayā pretyā rātrāv upāgatyāpahṛtā | tatas tena bhikṣuṇā āyuṣmata uttarāya niveditam* | uttareṇa gatvā pretīṃ paribhāṣya punar apy ānīya dattā | evaṃ yāvat trir api tasya bhikṣoḥ sakāśād apahṛtā, āyuṣmatā cottareṇānīya dattā | bhikṣuṇā ca sā pāṭayitvā cāturdiśāya bhikṣusaṃghāya vilepanikāyāṃ
children.translated_text: Then, after much reproaching by the venerable <s>Uttara</s>, she gave a single <s>yamalī</s> (a pair of garments). That was given to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. The monk who obtained that <s>yamalī</s> from the distribution within the <s>Saṃgha</s> entrusted it to a servant-boy. But that <s>pretī</s>, coming at night, stole it away. Then that monk reported it to the venerable <s>Uttara</s>. <s>Uttara</s> went and, having reproached the <s>pretī</s>, brought it back and gave it again. In this way, she stole it three times from that monk, and the venerable <s>Uttara</s> brought it back and gave it each time. Then the monk tore it apart and had it sewn into ointment-cloths for the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 118]

children.text: sīvitā | tatas tayā na punar apahṛtā | ata eva mātsaryaṃ satvānāṃ viḍambanakaraṃ dṛṣṭvā mātsaryaprahāṇāya dhyāyitavyam* | tathā evaṃvidhā doṣā na syur yathā tasyāḥ pretyā iti ||
children.translated_text: After that she did not steal it again. Therefore, having seen how miserliness brings disgrace upon beings, one should meditate for the abandonment of miserliness, so that such faults as befell that <s>pretī</s> may not arise.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, and the other <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and others rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_47 jātyandhā | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_47: <s>Jātyandhā</s> (The Blind-Born). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | athāyuṣmān nandakaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisamarpya pretacārikāṃ carati sma | adrākṣīd āyuṣmān nandakaḥ pretīṃ dagdhasthūṇāsadṛśīṃ jātyandhāṃ svakeśaromasaṃchannāṃ sūcīchidropamamukhīṃ parvatopamakukṣiṃ durgandhāṃ śmaśānasadṛśīṃ kākair gṛdhraiḥ śvabhiḥ śṛgālaiś cābhidrutām* | ye 'syāḥ samantata utpāṭyotpāṭya māṃsaṃ bhakṣayanti | sā marmavedanābhyāhatā ārtasvaraṃ krandati duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti | āyuṣmān nandakaḥ saṃvignaḥ pṛchati: kiṃ tvayā bhagini prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yenaivaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavasīti | pretī āha: āditye hi samudgate na dīpena prayojanam* | bhagavantam etam arthaṃ pṛccha | sa te asmākīnāṃ karmaplotiṃ vyākariṣyatīti | yāṃ śrutvā anye 'pīha satvāḥ pāpāt prativiraṃsyantīti | athāyuṣmān nandako yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Then the venerable <s>Nandaka</s>, having dressed in the morning, taking his bowl and robe, wandered through <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Having completed his meal, having returned from the alms-round after the afternoon meal, having put away his bowl and robe, he went on a tour of the realm of <s>pretas</s>. The venerable <s>Nandaka</s> saw a <s>pretī</s> — resembling a burnt pillar, blind from birth, covered with her own hair, with a mouth like the eye of a needle, a belly like a mountain, foul-smelling, like a cemetery, beset by crows, vultures, dogs, and jackals, who were tearing off her flesh from all sides and eating it. She, struck by pain in her vital parts, cried out in agony, experiencing painful, intense, sharp, bitter, unpleasant sensations. The venerable <s>Nandaka</s>, filled with spiritual urgency, asked: 'Sister, what evil have you done that you experience such suffering?' The <s>pretī</s> said: 'When the sun has risen, there is no need for a lamp. Ask the Blessed One about this matter. He will explain the thread of our <s>karma</s>. Having heard it, other beings too in this world will turn away from evil.' Then the venerable <s>Nandaka</s> approached the Blessed One.

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam* | anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoty anijyamānair indriyaiḥ | tato buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūrvālāpinaḥ ehīti svāgatavādinaḥ smitapūrvaṃgamāś ca | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ nandakam idam avocat*: ehi nanadaka, svāgataṃ te, kutas tvaṃ nandaka etarhy āgacchasīti | nandaka āha: āgacchāmy ahaṃ bhadanta pretacārikāyāḥ | tatrāhaṃ pretīm adrākṣaṃ dagdhasthūṇāsadṛśīṃ svakeśaromasaṃchannāṃ sūcīchidropamamukhīṃ parvatopamakukṣiṃ durgandhāṃ śmaśānasadṛśīṃ kākair gṛdhraiḥ śvabhiḥ śṛgālaiś cābhidrutām*, ye 'syāḥ samantata utpāṭyotpāṭya māṃsaṃ bhakṣayanti | sā marmavedanābhyāhatā ārtasvaraṃ krandati duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukām amanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānām* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: At that time, the Blessed One, having emerged from his seclusion, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies — sweet as sweet, like honey without dregs. An assembly of many hundreds was listening to the sweet <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One with undistracted faculties. Now <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are those who speak first, who say 'Come' and 'Welcome,' and who smile beforehand. Thereupon the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Nandaka</s>: 'Come, <s>Nandaka</s>, welcome to you! From where do you come now, <s>Nandaka</s>?' <s>Nandaka</s> said: 'I come, Venerable Sir, from a tour of the realm of <s>pretas</s>. There I saw a <s>pretī</s> — resembling a burnt pillar, covered with her own hair, with a mouth like the eye of a needle, a belly like a mountain, foul-smelling, like a cemetery, beset by crows, vultures, dogs, and jackals, who were tearing off her flesh from all sides and eating it. She, struck by pain in her vital parts, cried out in agony, experiencing painful, intense, sharp, bitter, unpleasant sensations.' And he said:

children.text: viśuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhapuṭā suduḥkhitā pravṛddhaśailopamacarvitāśrayā |
children.translated_text: 'With dried-up throat and lips, deeply suffering, her form like a great swollen mountain,

children.text: svakeśasaṃchannamukhī digambarā susūkṣmasūcīsadṛśānanā kṛśā || AVŚ_47.1 ||
children.translated_text: her face covered with her own hair, naked, emaciated, with a face like the finest needle.' // AVŚ_47.1 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 119]

children.text: nagnā svakeśasaṃchannā asthiyantravaducchritā |
children.translated_text: 'Naked, covered with her own hair, raised up like a skeleton of bones,

children.text: kapālapāṇinī ghorā krandantī paridhāvate || AVŚ_47.2 ||
children.translated_text: a skull-bowl in her hand, terrifying, she runs about crying.' // AVŚ_47.2 //

children.text: bubhukṣayā pipāsayā klāntā vyasanapīḍitā |
children.translated_text: 'Tormented by hunger and thirst, exhausted, afflicted by misfortune,

children.text: ārtasvaraṃ krandamānā duḥkhāṃ vindati vedanām* || AVŚ_47.3 ||
children.translated_text: crying out in a distressed voice, she experiences painful sensation. // AVŚ_47.3 //

children.text:
kiṃ tayā prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ martyaloke sudāruṇam* |
  yena evaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavati bhayānakam* || AVŚ_47.4 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
What terrible sin did she commit in the world of mortals,
that she experiences such fearful suffering? // AVŚ_47.4 //

children.text: bhagavān āha: pāpakāriṇī nandaka sā pretī | icchasi tasyā karmaplotiṃ śrotum*? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi nandaka śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That female <s>preta</s> is an evildoer, <s>Nandaka</s>. Do you wish to hear the record of her <s>karma</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, <s>Nandaka</s>, listen well and carefully, and attend; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ nandaka asminn eva bhadrakalpe viṃśatisahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | vārāṇasyām anyatamā śreṣṭhiduhitā | sā dharmābhilāṣiṇī | yāvad asau dharmaṃ śrutvā saṃsāradoṣadarśinī nirvāṇe guṇadarśinī saṃvṛttā | sā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitā | tasyā arthaṃ jñātibhir bhikṣuṇīvarṣakaḥ kāritaḥ | sā tatra śaikṣāśaikṣībhir bhikṣuṇībhiḥ sārdhaṃ prativasati | yāvat tayā pramādāc chikṣāśaithilyaṃ kṛtam* | tato bhikṣuṇībhir duḥśīleti niṣkāsitā | tatas tayā dānapatir gṛhebhyaḥ pravṛttakāni chandakāni # # # <The gap may be filled ou by ācchinnāni; Speyer: kurkuraiḥ śṛgālaiś ca.> śaikṣāśaikṣīṇāṃ ca avarṇo bhāṣitaḥ | bhikṣavaś ca ye śīlavantaḥ, tān dṛṣṭvā nayane nimīlitavatī ||
children.translated_text: In former times, <s>Nandaka</s>, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there was a certain guild-master's daughter. She was desirous of the <s>Dharma</s>. Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, she came to see the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the virtues of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Having obtained her parents' permission, she went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. For her sake, her kinsmen had a nuns' retreat built. She dwelt there together with nuns who were learners and those beyond learning. But through negligence, she became lax in her training. Then the nuns expelled her, saying she was of bad conduct. Thereupon she intercepted the supplies of food and robes that donors sent from their households to the nuns [gap in text; Speyer suggests: which were seized by dogs and jackals], and she spoke ill of the nuns who were learners and beyond learning. And whenever she saw monks who were virtuous, she would shut her eyes.

children.text: kiṃ manyase nandaka yā sā śreṣṭhiduhitā, iyaṃ sā pretī | yat tayā varṣake mātsaryaṃ kṛtam*, tena preteṣūpapannā | yat tayā naityakasamucchedaḥ kṛtas tena kākair gṛdhraiḥ kurkuraiś cābhidrutā | yat tayā śaikṣāśaikṣīṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnām avarno bhāṣitaḥ, tena daurgandhyam āsāditam* | yat tayā śīlavato bhikṣūn dṛṣṭvā nayane nimīlite, tena jātyandhā saṃvṛttā | iti hi nandaka ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi te nandaka ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ te nandaka śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Nandaka</s>? That guild-master's daughter — she is this female <s>preta</s>. Because she acted with jealousy during the rains-retreat, she was reborn among the <s>pretas</s>. Because she cut off the regular offerings, she is assailed by crows, vultures, and dogs. Because she spoke ill of the nuns who were learners and beyond learning, she has acquired a foul stench. Because she shut her eyes upon seeing virtuous monks, she has been born blind. Therefore, <s>Nandaka</s>, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, <s>Nandaka</s>, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, <s>Nandaka</s>, should you train.

children.text: asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe daśabhiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: ime cānye ca ādīnavā mātsarye vāgduścarite ceti jñātvā mātsaryasya vāgduścaritasya ca prahāṇāya vyāyantavyam* | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: While this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, a hundred thousand beings attained the vision of truth.
