There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'These and other dangers attend jealousy and verbal misconduct. Knowing this, you must strive for the abandonment of jealousy and verbal misconduct. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, along with others — <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and the rest — rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 120]

children.text: AVŚ_48 śreṣṭhī | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_48: <s>Śreṣṭhī</s> (The Guild-Master). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | so 'pareṇa samayena jetavanaṃ nirgataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā saṃsāravairāgyikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā saṃsāradoṣadarśī nirvāṇe guṇadarśī bhūtvā bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | pravrajitaś ca jñāto mahāpuṇyaḥ saṃvṛtto lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇām* | sa gṛhītapariṣkāro labdhaṃ labdhaṃ saṃcayaṃ karoti, na tu sabrahmacāribhiḥ saha saṃvibhāgaṃ karoti | sa tena mātsaryeṇa sevitena bhāvitena bahulīkṛtena pariṣkārādhyavasitaḥ kālagataḥ svake layane preteṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. On a later occasion, he went out to the <s>Jetavana</s>. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him, he prostrated at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> taught him a discourse conducive to weariness with <s>saṃsāra</s>, having heard which, seeing the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the virtues of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, he went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. Having gone forth, he became known as one of great merit, receiving robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. But having acquired requisites, he would hoard whatever he obtained and did not share with his fellow monks. By that jealousy — cultivated, developed, and made habitual — fixated on his requisites, he died and was reborn as a <s>preta</s> in his own cell.

children.text: tato 'sya sabrahmacāribhir muṇḍikāṃ gaṇḍīṃ parāhatya śarīrābhinirhāraḥ kṛtaḥ | tato 'sya śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā vihāram āgatāḥ | tato layanadvāraṃ vimucya pātracīvaraṃ pratyavekṣitum ārabdhāḥ | yāvat paśyanti taṃ pretaṃ vikṛtakaracaraṇanayanaṃ paramabībhatsāśrayaṃ pātracīvaram avaṣṭabhyāvasthitam* | tathāvikṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhikṣavaḥ saṃvignā bhagavate niveditavantaḥ | tato bhagavāṃs tasya kulaputrasyānugrahārthaṃ śiṣyagaṇasyodvejanārthaṃ mātsaryasya cāniṣṭavipākasaṃdarśanārthaṃ bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtas taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ | tato 'sau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cāsya bhagavato 'ntike prasādo jātaḥ | sa vyapatrapitavān* | tato bhagavān sajalajaladagambhīradundubhisvaraḥ pretaṃ paribhāṣitavān: bhadramukha tvayaivaitad ātmavadhāya pātracīvaraṃ samudānītam*, yenāsyapāyeṣūpapannaḥ | sādhu mamāntike cittaṃ prasādaya, asmāc ca pariṣkārāc cittaṃ virāgaya | mā haiva itaḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā narakeṣūpapatsyasa iti | tataḥ pretaḥ saṃghe pātracīvaraṃ niryātya bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya atyayaṃ deśitavān* | tato bhagavatā pretasya nāmnā dakṣiṇā ādiṣṭā:
children.translated_text: Then his fellow monks, having struck the shaven-headed gong, carried out the funeral rites for his body. After performing the honor due to his body, they returned to the monastery. Then, having opened the door of his cell, they began to inspect his bowl and robes. There they saw that <s>preta</s> — with distorted hands, feet, and eyes, of an extremely hideous form — standing guard over the bowl and robes. Having seen him so distorted, the monks were spiritually shaken and reported it to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the sake of benefiting that son of good family, for the sake of stirring spiritual urgency in the community of disciples, and for the sake of demonstrating the undesirable results of jealousy, surrounded by the community of monks and preceded by the <s>Saṃgha</s>, arrived at that place. Then that <s>preta</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. And the moment he saw the <s>Bhagavān</s>, faith arose in him. He became ashamed. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, with a voice deep as a rain-cloud's thunder, addressed the <s>preta</s>: 'Friend, it was you yourself who accumulated these bowl and robes to your own destruction, by which you have been reborn in the woeful states. It would be well if you were to generate faith in my presence and detach your mind from these requisites, lest after dying from here you be reborn in the hells.' Then the <s>preta</s>, having surrendered the bowl and robes to the <s>Saṃgha</s> and falling at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, confessed his transgression. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> dedicated the merit in the <s>preta</s>'s name:

children.text:
ito dānād dhi yat puṇyaṃ tat pretam anugacchatu |
  uttiṣṭhatu kṣipram ayaṃ pretalokāt sudāruṇāt* || AVŚ_48.1 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
Whatever merit arises from this gift, may it follow that <s>preta</s>;
may he swiftly rise from the terrible realm of <s>pretas</s>! // AVŚ_48.1 //

children.text: tataḥ sa preto bhagavati cittaṃ prasādya kālagataḥ pretamarddhikeṣūpapannaḥ | tataḥ pretamaharddhikaś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravirājitagātro maṇiratnavicitramauliḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātras
children.translated_text: Then that <s>preta</s>, having generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, died and was reborn among the <s>pretas</s> of great supernatural power. Then, as a <s>preta</s> of great supernatural power — wearing gleaming earrings, his body resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, his crown adorned with various jewels and gems, his body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, and other fragrances —
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 121]

children.text: tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ jetavanam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavataṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | bhagavatā tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā prasādajātaḥ prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on that very night, having filled his lap with divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> flowers, he illuminated the entire <s>Jetavana</s> with a magnificent radiance, scattered flowers over the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, having heard it, he departed filled with faith.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ, yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhagavan asyām rātrau brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | api sa pretaḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā pretamaharddhikeṣūpapannaḥ | sa imāṃ rātriṃ matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | tasya mayā dharmo deśitaḥ | sa prasādajātaḥ prakrāntaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavo mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyam* | ete doṣā na bhaviṣyanti, ye tasya śreṣṭhinaḥ pretabhūtasya | ity evaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw the magnificent radiance in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Having seen it, filled with doubt, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> this night?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. Rather, that <s>preta</s>, having died, was reborn among the <s>pretas</s> of great supernatural power. He came to my presence this night. I taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. Filled with faith, he departed. Therefore, monks, you must strive for the abandonment of jealousy. The faults that befell that guild-master who became a <s>preta</s> shall not arise [in you]. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, along with others — <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and the rest — rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_49 putrāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_49: <s>Putrāḥ</s> (The Sons). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | athāyuṣmān nāladaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrāntaḥ pātracīvaraṃ pratisamarpya pretacārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. Then the venerable <s>Nālada</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Having wandered through <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms, having finished his meal, returning from his alms-round after the meal, having put away his bowl and robe, he set out on a tour of the realm of <s>pretas</s>.

children.text: sa gṛdhrakūṭaparvatasāmantake pretīṃ dadarśa yamarākṣasasadṛśīṃ rudhirabinducitām asthiśakalāparivṛtāṃ śmaśānamadhya ivāvasthitam* | rātriṃdivena pañca putrān prasūya tādṛśaṃ duḥkham anubhūya putrasnehe saty api kṣutkṣāmatayā putrāṃs tān bhakṣayantīm* | tataḥ sthaviro nāladas tāṃ pṛṣṭavān: kiṃ tvayā prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yenaivaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavasīti | pretī āha: āditye hi samudgate na dīpena prayojanam* | bhagavantam etam arthaṃ paripṛccha | sa te asmākīnāṃ karmaplotiṃ vyākariṣyatīti | yāṃ śrutvā anye 'pīha satvāḥ pāpāt karmaṇaḥ prativiraṃsyantīti | athāyuṣmān nālado yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Near <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain he saw a female <s>preta</s> — resembling a <s>Yama</s>-demon, spattered with drops of blood, surrounded by heaps of bones, standing as if in the middle of a charnel ground. Day and night she gave birth to five sons, and even while experiencing such suffering, though she felt maternal love, out of the agony of hunger she devoured those very sons. Then the elder <s>Nālada</s> asked her: 'What sin did you commit that you experience such suffering?' The female <s>preta</s> said: 'When the sun has risen, there is no need for a lamp. Ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about this matter. He will explain the record of our <s>karma</s>, hearing which other beings too will turn away from evil deeds.' Then the venerable <s>Nālada</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: tena khalu samayena bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam* | anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ
children.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having risen from meditation, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies — sweet as sweet can be, like honey free from impurity. And several hundred members of the assembly were listening to the sweet <s>Dharma</s>
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 122]

children.text: śṛṇoty anijyamānair indriyaiḥ | tato buddhā bhagavantaḥ pūrvālāpinaḥ ehīti svāgatavādinaḥ smitapūrvaṃgamāś ca | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ nāladam idam avocat*: ehi nālada, svāgataṃ te, kutas tvaṃ nālada etarhy āgacchasīti | nālada āha: āgacchāmy ahaṃ bhadanta pretacārikāyāḥ | tatrāhaṃ pretīm adrākṣaṃ yamarākṣasasadṛśīṃ rudhirabinducitām asthiśakalāparivṛtāṃ śmaśānamadhya ivāvasthitam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: was listening with undistracted senses. Now, <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are those who speak first, who say 'Come, welcome!' and who are preceded by a smile. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Nālada</s>: 'Come, <s>Nālada</s>, welcome to you! From where do you come now, <s>Nālada</s>?' <s>Nālada</s> said: 'I come, Venerable Sir, from a tour of the realm of hungry ghosts. There I beheld a female <s>preta</s> resembling a <s>Yama</s>-demon, spattered with drops of blood, surrounded by bone fragments, standing as if in the midst of a cremation ground.' And he said:

children.text:
pañca putrān ahaṃ rātrau divā pañca tathāparān* |
  bhakṣayāmi janitvā tān nāsti tṛptas tathāpi me || AVŚ_49.1 || iti
  kiṃ tayā prakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ martyaloke sudāruṇam* |
  yena evaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavati bhayānakam* || AVŚ_49.2 || iti
  bhagavān āha: pāpakārī nālada sā pretī | icchasi tasyāḥ karmaplotiṃ śrotum*? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi nālada śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: 'Five sons at night, and five more during the day — I devour them after giving birth, yet even so I am never satisfied.' // AVŚ_49.1 // 'What terrible sin did she commit in the world of mortals, that she experiences such fearful suffering?' // AVŚ_49.2 // The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That female <s>preta</s> is an evildoer, <s>Nālada</s>. Do you wish to hear the record of her <s>karma</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, <s>Nālada</s>, listen well and carefully, and attend; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ nālada atīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām 'nyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato naiva putro na duhitā | sa kare kapolaṃ kṛtvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham* | na me putro na duhitā | mamātyayāt sarvasvāpateyam aputrakam iti kṛtvā rājavidheyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate sma | tadyathā ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ | sahajāḥ sahadhārmikā nityānubaddhā api devatā āyācate sma | asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti | tac ca naivam* | yady evam abhaviṣyad ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ | api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | katameṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānām*? mātāpitarāu raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau, mātā kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī, gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati | eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | tasya devatārādhane 'pi sati na putro na duhitā ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, <s>Nālada</s>, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. Yet as he sported, delighted, and amused himself, neither a son nor a daughter was born to him. Resting his cheek on his hand, he sat absorbed in worry: "My household is endowed with abundant wealth, yet I have neither son nor daughter. After my death, all my property, being without an heir, will pass to the king's control." Sonless and desiring a son, he prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other special deities — such as garden deities, forest deities, crossroad deities, intersection deities, and deities who accept offerings; he even prayed to deities who are innate, who share the same <s>dharma</s>, and who are constantly attendant. Now there is this common belief in the world that sons and daughters are born through prayer. But that is not so. If it were, each person would have a thousand sons, just as a <s>Cakravartin</s> king does. Rather, it is from the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. What three conditions? The mother and father are passionate and united; the mother is healthy and in her fertile period; and a <s>Gandharva</s> (being seeking rebirth) is present. From the conjunction of these three conditions sons and daughters are born. For him, despite his devotion to the deities, neither son nor daughter was born.'

children.text: tasyaivaṃ buddhir utpannā: dvitīyāṃ bhāryām anayāmi | kadācit sā satvavatī syād iti | tena sadṛśāt kulād dvitīyā bhāryā ānītā | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa sā āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | tayā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditayā svāmine niveditam: diṣṭyā āryputra vardhase | āpannasatvāsmi saṃvṛttā | yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati, niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti | so 'py āttamanāttamanāḥ pūrvakāyam abhyunnamayya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya udānam udanayati: apy evāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ
children.translated_text: This thought arose in him: 'I shall take a second wife. Perhaps she will bear children.' He brought a second wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, in the course of time she became pregnant. Joyful, elated, and delighted, she informed her husband: 'Congratulations, noble lord! I have become pregnant. And since the child rests leaning toward my right side, it will surely be a boy.' He too, overjoyed, raising his upper body and extending his right arm, uttered this exclamation: 'If only I might see
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 123]

children.text: putramukhaṃ paśyeyam* | jāto me syān nāvajātaḥ | kṛtyāni me kurvīta | bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyāt* | dāyād yaṃ pratipadyeta | kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt* | asmākaṃ cāpy atītakālagatānām alpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā asmākaṃ nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādekṣyate: idaṃ tayor yatrayatropapannayor gacchator anugacchatv iti | āpannasatvāṃ caināṃ viditvopariprāsādatalagatām ayantritāṃ dhārayati śīte śītopakaraṇair uṣṇe uṣṇopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptair āhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhāraiḥ | hārārdhahāravirājitagātrīm apsarasam iva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcān mañcaṃ pīṭhāt pīṭham anavatarantīm adharimāṃ bhūmim* | na cāsyāḥ kiṃcid amanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ yāvad eva garbhasya paripākāya ||
children.translated_text: the face of a son, long desired! May my son be born and not stillborn! May he perform my duties! Having been supported, may he support me in return! May he receive the inheritance! May my family lineage endure for a long time! And when we have passed away, may he give gifts, whether small or great, perform merits, and dedicate the offering in our names: "May this [merit] follow those two wherever they are reborn."' Knowing her to be pregnant, he kept her on the upper floor of the mansion, unrestrained, providing her with cold remedies in the cold season and warm remedies in the hot season, with foods prescribed by physicians — neither too bitter, nor too sour, nor too salty, nor too sweet, nor too pungent, nor too astringent, avoiding foods that are bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, or astringent — her body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like an <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymph) roaming in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, not descending from couch to couch, from seat to seat, to the ground below. And she was not allowed to hear any unpleasant sound, until the full maturation of the embryo.

children.text: tatas tasyāḥ pūrvikāyāḥ prajāpatyāḥ prathamapatnyās tāṃ bahumānāl lālitāṃ (Speyer: laḍitaṃ) dṛṣṭvā īrṣyā samutpannā | cintayanti: yady eṣā putraṃ janayiṣyati, niyataṃ māṃ bādhayiṣyati | sarvathopāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyam iti | kāmān khalu pratisevyamānasya (Speyer: pratisevamānasya) nāsti kiṃcit pāpaṃ karmācaraṇīyam iti | tayā aniṣṭagatiprapātanamugdhayā visrambham utpādya tathāvidhaṃ garbhaśātanaṃ dravyaṃ dattaṃ yena pītamātreṇaiva tasyās tapasvinyāḥ srasto garbhaḥ | tatas tayā dvitīyapatnyā sarvajñātīn saṃnipātya sā prathamā patnī samanuyujyate: tvayā me visrambham utpādya śātanaṃ dravyaṃ dattam*, yena me srasto garbha iti | tato 'sau prathamapatnī jñātimadhye śapathaṃ kartuṃ pravṛttā: yadi mayā garbhaśātanaṃ dravyam anupradattaṃ syāt*, ahaṃ pretī bhūtvā jātāñ jātān putrān bhakṣayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the first wife, the senior consort, seeing the second wife being pampered with such great respect, became jealous. She thought: 'If she bears a son, she will surely oppress me. I must devise some means.' For indeed, one who indulges in sensual desires will not shrink from any evil deed. That woman, bewildered and inclined toward woeful destinations, having gained the other's trust, gave her a substance that caused miscarriage, by which, the moment it was consumed, the poor woman's embryo was expelled. Then the second wife, having assembled all her kinsmen, confronted the first wife: 'You gained my trust and gave me an abortifacient substance, by which my embryo was expelled.' Then that first wife began to swear an oath in the midst of her kinsmen: 'If I gave an abortifacient substance, may I become a female <s>preta</s> who devours her own sons the moment they are born!'

children.text: kiṃ manyase nālada yāsau śreṣṭhibhāryā, iyaṃ sā pretī | yat tayā īrṣyāprakṛtayā garbhaśātanaṃ dattaṃ tena preteṣūpapannā | yat tayā mṛṣāvādena śapathaḥ kṛtaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena rātriṃdivena pañca putrān prasūya tān eva bhakṣayati | tasmāt tarhi te nālada vāgduścaritaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyaṃ yathā evaṃvidhā doṣā na syur ye tasyāḥ pretyāḥ | ity evaṃ te nālada śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'What do you think, <s>Nālada</s>? She who was the guild-master's wife — she is this female <s>preta</s>. Because she, motivated by jealousy, gave the abortifacient, she was reborn among the <s>pretas</s>. Because she swore a false oath, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, she gives birth to five sons by night and five by day and devours them. Therefore, <s>Nālada</s>, you must strive for the abandonment of wrong speech, so that the faults that befell that female <s>preta</s> may not arise [in you]. Thus, <s>Nālada</s>, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanā āyuṣmān nālado 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. The venerable <s>Nālada</s>, delighted in mind, and others — <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and the rest — rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_50 jāmbālaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_50: <s>Jāmbāla</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho vaiśālīm upaniśritya viharati markaṭahradatīre kūṭāgāraśālāyām* | tena khalu samayena vaiśālyām anyatarasyāṃ nagaraparikhāyāṃ pañca pretaśatāni prativasanti vāntāśāny ujjhitāśāni kheṭamūtropajīvīni pūyaśoṇitaviṣṭhāhārāṇi ghorāṇi prakṛtiduḥkhitāni ca | āha ca:
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Vaiśālī</s>, on the bank of the Monkey Pond, in the Gabled Hall. At that time, in a certain moat of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, five hundred <s>pretas</s> were dwelling — feeding on vomit, feeding on refuse, subsisting on phlegm and urine, eating pus, blood, and excrement, terrible and miserable by nature. And it is said:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 124]

children.text:
vāntāśā ujjhitāśāś ca kheṭamūtropajīvitaḥ |
  pūyaśoṇitaviṣṭhāśā ghorāḥ prakṛtiduḥkhitāḥ || AVŚ_50.1 || iti ||
children.translated_text: 'Feeding on vomit, feeding on refuse, subsisting on phlegm and urine, eating pus, blood, and excrement — terrible and miserable by nature.' // AVŚ_50.1 //

children.text: tasyāṃ ca vaiśālyām anyataro brāhmaṇaḥ | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | daurgandhaṃ cāsyāḥ kāye saṃvṛttam* | tatas tena brāhmaṇena naimittikā āhūya pṛṣṭāḥ | te kathayanti: yo 'yam udarastho dārakas tasyāyaṃ prabhāva iti | yāvad asau navānāṃ māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto durvarṇo durdarśano avakoṭimako 'medhyamrakṣitagātro durgandhaś ca | tathāpy asau snehapāśānubaddhābhyāṃ paramabībhatso 'pi mātṛpitṛbhyāṃ saṃvardhitaḥ | so 'medhyasthāneṣv evābhiramate saṃkārakūṭe jambāle, keśāṃl luñcati, amedhyaṃ mukhe prakṣipati | tasya bālo jāmbāla iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: In that <s>Vaiśālī</s> there was a certain Brahmin. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. And a foul odor arose from her body. Then that Brahmin summoned soothsayers and questioned them. They said: 'This is the influence of the child in her womb.' After the completion of nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — ugly, hideous, misshapen, his body smeared with impurities, and foul-smelling. Nevertheless, bound by the cords of affection, though he was supremely repulsive, he was raised by his mother and father. He delighted only in foul places — rubbish heaps and cesspools; he would pull out hair, and put filth in his mouth. So the boy acquired the name <s>Jāmbāla</s> (Cesspool).

children.text: yāvad asāv itaś cāmutaś ca paribhraman pūraṇena kāśyapena dṛṣṭaḥ | tasyaitad abhavat: yādṛśeṣu sthāneṣv ayam abhiramate, nūnam ayaṃ siddhapuruṣaḥ | yanv aham enaṃ pravrājayeyam iti | sa tena pravrājito nagnaḥ paryaṭati satkriyāsu ca vartate | tatas tena paryaṭatā vaiśālīparikhāyāṃ pañca pretaśatāni dṛṣṭāni | sa pūrvakarmavipākasaṃbandhāt tāṃ nagaraparikhām avatīrya taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgamya samāgamya saṃmodate, sakhitvaṃ cābhyupagataḥ | yāvad apareṇa samayena jāmbālo dārakaḥ kvacit prayojanena vyākṣipto vaiśālīṃ praviṣṭaḥ | bhagavāṃś ca tāṃ nagaraparikhām anuprāptaḥ | dadṛśus te pretā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cāsya bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatitāḥ | bhagavatā uktāḥ: kiṃ bhavatāṃ bādhata iti | te ūcuḥ: pipāsitāḥ smo bhagavann iti | tato bhagavatā pañcabhyo 'ṅgulibhyo 'ṣṭāṅgopetasya pānīyasya pañca dhārā utsṛṣṭāḥ, yena tāni pañca pretaśatāni saṃtarpitāni | tatas te bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādya kālagatāḥ | praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As he wandered here and there, he was seen by <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>. This thought arose in him: 'Given the kinds of places in which this one delights, surely he is an accomplished being. Let me ordain him.' He was ordained by him and wandered about naked, engaging in [their] practices. Then, while wandering, he saw five hundred <s>pretas</s> in a moat of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. By the connection of past <s>karma</s> ripening, he descended into that city moat and, having met and assembled with them, he rejoiced and accepted their companionship. On a later occasion, <s>Jāmbāla</s> the boy entered <s>Vaiśālī</s>, diverted by some errand. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at that city moat. Those <s>pretas</s> saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment they saw him, they fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet. The <s>Bhagavān</s> asked: 'What afflicts you?' They said: 'We are thirsty, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> released from his five fingers five streams of water endowed with the eight qualities, by which those five hundred <s>pretas</s> were satisfied. Then they, having placed their minds in serene faith toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, died and were reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven.

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyakāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | te paśyanti pretebhyaś cyutāḥ, praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittam ahiprasādyeti || atha pretapūrviṇāṃ devaputrāṇām etad abhavat: nāsmākaṃ pratirūpaṃ syāt, yad vayaṃ paryuṣitaparivāsā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmema | yan nu vayam aparyuṣitaparivāsā eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmemeti | atha pretapūrviṇo devaputrāś calavimalakuṇḍaladharā hārārdhahāravirājitagātrā maṇiratnavicitramaulayaḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātrās tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvāṃ kūṭāgāraśālāṃ udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavataṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān pretapūrviṇāṃ devaputrāṇām āśayānuśayaṃ
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that when a <s>Devaputra</s> (son of a god) or a <s>Devakanyā</s> (divine maiden) has recently been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' They saw: 'We have passed away from the realm of <s>pretas</s>, we have been reborn among the exalted gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) heaven, and it was by generating faith in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then this thought occurred to those <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been <s>pretas</s>: 'It would not be fitting for us to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience after having spent the night. Rather, let us approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience without having spent the night.' Then those <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been <s>pretas</s> — wearing gleaming, pure earrings, their bodies resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, their crowns adorned with various gems and jewels, their bodies anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, musk, and other fragrances — on that very night, having filled their laps with divine flowers of <s>utpalas</s>, lotuses, <s>kumudas</s>, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> blossoms, illuminating the entire gabled hall with a magnificent radiance, showering the <s>Bhagavān</s> with flowers, they sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies,

children.text: dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā pañcabhir devaputraśatair viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalam anuprāptam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyā labdhalābhā iva vaṇijaḥ, saṃpannasasyā iva karṣakāḥ, śūrā iva vijitasaṃgrāmāḥ, sarvarogaparimuktā ivāturā yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatās tayaiva vibhūtyā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: temperament, and nature of those <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been <s>pretas</s>, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which five hundred <s>Devaputras</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) that rises to twenty peaks, attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, like merchants who have gained their profit, like farmers whose crops have ripened, like heroes who have won their battle, like the sick who have been freed from all disease — with the very same splendor with which they had come into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, they circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and returned to their own abodes.

children.text: atha jāmbālo nagaraparikhām āgatas tān pretān nādrākṣīt* | tataḥ samanveṣitum ārabdhaḥ | sa ca tān parimārgamāṇaḥ khedam āpanno na ca tān āsādayati ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jāmbāla</s>, having come to the city moat, did not see those <s>pretas</s>. He began to search for them. And as he searched for them, he grew weary but could not find them.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttakānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya <ca> buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: In this regard, nothing is unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or uncomprehended by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. It is the natural law of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s> — who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, sole protectors, abiding in <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three means of taming, having crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipādas</s>), long practiced in the four means of attraction (<s>saṃgrahavastus</s>), having abandoned the five factors [of hindrance], having transcended the five destinies, endowed with the six factors, having perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>), guides of the Eightfold Path, skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, possessing the strength of the ten powers (<s>daśabalas</s>), their fame filling the ten directions, distinguished by mastery over a thousand [qualities] — three times at night and three times during the day, they survey the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye and knowledge-and-vision operates: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into difficulty, hardship, and distress? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is tending toward the lower realms? Who is heading toward the lower realms? Whom shall I, having raised from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of sensual desire, shall I extend the hand of rescue? Whom, bereft of the noble wealth, shall I establish in the sovereignty of noble wealth? Whose eyes, covered by the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? For whom shall I plant wholesome roots not yet planted? For whom shall I bring to maturity those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already matured?' And he said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even the ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its boundary,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_50.2 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the [appointed] time for those who are to be trained.' // AVŚ_50.2 //

children.text: tato bhagavāñ jāmbālasya kulaputrasyānugrahārthaṃ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto vaiśālīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | yāvad anupūrveṇa piṇḍapātam aṭan vīthīm avatīrṇaḥ | jāmbālaś ca itas tato 'nvāhiṇḍamāno bhagavato 'grataḥ sthitaḥ | atha dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike citaṃ prasāditaṃ* | sa prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya kṛtakarapuṭa uvāca: yadi bhagavan mādṛśānāṃ satvānām asmin dharmavinaye pravrajyāsti; labheyaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām iti | tato bhagavān mahākaruṇāparigatahṛdayaḥ satvānām āśayānuśayajñas taṃ bhavyarūpaṃ viditvā rajabhujasadṛśaṃ suvarṇavarṇabāhum abhiprasāryedam avocat*: ehi bhikṣor cara brahmacaryam* | ity uktamātre bhagavatā saptāhāvaropitair iva keśair dvādaśavarṣopasaṃpannasyeva bhikṣor īryāpathena pātrakarakavyagrahasto 'vasthitaḥ | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the benefit of the son of good family <s>Jāmbāla</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by a company of monks, attended by the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, entered <s>Vaiśālī</s> for alms. Walking on his alms-round in due order, he descended into a street. And <s>Jāmbāla</s>, wandering here and there, came to stand before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. At the very sight, he generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Filled with faith, he fell at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said with palms joined: 'If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is ordination in this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> for beings such as myself, may I receive ordination in this well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, whose heart was encompassed by great compassion, who knows the dispositions and latent tendencies of beings, recognizing him as a fit vessel, extended his golden arm, beautiful as the trunk of a royal elephant, and said: 'Come, monk, practice the holy life!' The moment the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke these words, with hair as if shaved seven days ago, standing in the deportment of a monk ordained for twelve years, with bowl and water-jug in hand, he stood [transformed]. And he said:

children.text: ehīti coktaḥ sa tathāgatena muṇḍaś ca saṃghāṭiparītadehaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Called "Come!" by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, tonsured, his body clad in the monastic robe,

children.text: sadyaḥ praśāntendriya eva tasthāv evaṃ sthito buddhamanorathena || AVŚ_50.3 ||
children.translated_text: at once he stood with senses pacified — thus established by the <s>Buddha</s>'s wish.' // AVŚ_50.3 //

children.text: tato 'sya bhagavatā manasikāro dattaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣākṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | so 'rhatvaprāpto 'pi lūhenābhiramate | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāṃ lūhādhimuktānām*, yaduta jāmbālo bhikṣur iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave him a subject of meditation. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. And even after attaining <s>Arhatship</s>, he delighted in coarse [conditions]. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'This one, monks, is the foremost among my monk-disciples who are inclined to coarse [conditions] — namely, the monk <s>Jāmbāla</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kiṃ bhadanta jāmbālena sthavireṇa karma kṛtaṃ yenaivaṃvidhaṃ duḥkham anubhavatīti | bhagavān āha: jāmbalenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | jāmbālenaiva karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, questioned the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s> did the elder <s>Jāmbāla</s> perform, Venerable Sir, that he experiences such suffering?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Jāmbāla</s> himself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Jāmbāla</s> himself who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_50.4 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_50.4 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrake kalpe catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ krakucchando nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa śobhāvatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | tasyāṃ ca rājadhānyām anyatamena gṛhapatinā vihāraḥ kārito yatra nānādigdeśavāsino bhikṣava āgantavyaṃ gantavyaṃ vastavyaṃ ca manyante | tasmiṃś ca vihāre pṛthagjano bhikṣur naivāsikaḥ | sa cātīvātivāmatsarī (Speyer: cātīvāvāsamatsarī) | āgantukān bhikṣūn dṛṣṭvā 'bhiṣajyate kupyati vyāpadyate madguḥ pratitiṣṭhati kopaṃ saṃjanayati | ye tu tasmād vihārād bhikṣavaḥ prakrāmanti, tān dṛṣṭvā prītiprāmodyabahalaḥ pratyudgamyābhāṣate ca | yāvad apareṇa samayena janapadād arhadbhikṣur āgataḥ | sa ca vihārasvāmy anāgāmī | tenāsāv īryāpathena saṃlakṣito 'rhann iti | tataḥ prasādajātena śvo bhaktena jentākasnātreṇa copanimantritaḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena | sa cāvāsiko bhikṣus tatra nāsīt* | yāvad dvitīye divase jentākasnātre pratipādite bhakte sajjīkṛte āvāsiko bhikṣur āgataḥ | so 'pi jentākasnātraṃ praviṣṭaḥ | paśyati vihārasvāminam ekaśāṭakanivasitam āgantukasya bhikṣoḥ parikarma kurvāṇam* | tato 'sya mātsaryam utpannam* | tena praduṣṭacittena kharaṃ
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was forty thousand years, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Krakucchanda</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Śobhāvatī</s>. In that capital, a certain householder had built a monastery where monks from various regions and lands considered it a place to come, to go, and to dwell. In that monastery, a certain ordinary (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) monk was the resident. He was exceedingly jealous regarding lodgings. Seeing visiting monks arrive, he would become hostile, angry, ill-disposed — he would sulk like a cormorant and generate rage. But when monks departed from that monastery, seeing them leave, he would become full of joy and gladness and would come forward to bid them farewell. Then on a later occasion, an <s>Arhat</s> monk arrived from the countryside. The resident monastery-owner was a <s>Non-returner</s> (<s>Anāgāmin</s>). He recognized the visitor by his deportment as an <s>Arhat</s>. Then, having generated faith, he invited him for the next day's meal and a bath in the steam-house, together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks. But the resident monk was not present there. Then on the second day, when the steam-bath was being provided and the food was prepared, the resident monk arrived. He too entered the steam-house. He saw the monastery-owner, wearing a single garment, personally attending to the visiting monk. Then jealousy arose in him. With a corrupted mind, he uttered harsh

children.text: vākkarma niścāritam*: varaṃ khalu te bhikṣo amedhyena śarīram upaliptam*, na tu evaṃvidhasya dānapateḥ sakāśād upasthānaṃ svīkṛtam iti | tatas tenārhatā tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsitam*: mā haivāyaṃ tapasvī gāḍhatarasya karmaṇo bhāgī bhaviṣyatīti | yāvat sāmagrīdeśakāle saṃprāpte naivāsikena bhikṣuṇā śrutam*: arhato 'ntike tvayā cittaṃ pradūṣitam iti | śrutvā cāsya vipratisāro jātaḥ | tato 'rhato bhikṣoḥ pādayor nipatyāha: kṣamasva ārya yan mayā tvayi paruṣā vāg niścāriteti | tato 'rhaṃs tasya prasādābhivṛddhyarthaṃ gaganatalam abhyudgamya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayitum ārabdhaḥ | tato 'sya bhūyasā vipratisāraḥ samutpannaḥ | tena tasya purastāt tat karma atyayenādeśitaṃ prakāśitam uttānīkṛtam*, ca na cānena śakitaṃ naiṣṭhikaṃ jñānam utpādayitum* | yāvan maraṇakālasamaye praṇidhiṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: yan mayārhato 'ntike cittaṃ pradūṣitam*, kharaṃ ca vākkarma niścaritam*, mā asya karmaṇo vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayeyam* | yat tu mayā paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ dānapradānāni dattāni saṃghasya copasthānām kṛtam*, tasya karmaṇo vipākena anāgatān samyaksaṃbuddhān ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: speech: 'It would be better for you, monk, to have your body smeared with filth than to have accepted personal service from such a patron!' Then the <s>Arhat</s> endured it in silence, [thinking]: 'Let not this wretched one become a partaker of even heavier <s>karma</s>.' Then, when the right conditions, place, and time had come together, the resident monk heard: 'You have corrupted your mind toward an <s>Arhat</s>!' Having heard this, remorse arose in him. Then, falling at the feet of the <s>Arhat</s> monk, he said: 'Forgive me, noble one, for the harsh words I have uttered against you!' Then the <s>Arhat</s>, for the increase of his faith, rose into the sky and began to display various miraculous feats. Then even greater remorse arose in him. Before that [<s>Arhat</s>], he confessed and disclosed and laid open that <s>karma</s> as a transgression. Yet he was unable to generate the ultimate knowledge. Then, at the time of death, he began to make an aspiration: 'Since I have corrupted my mind toward an <s>Arhat</s> and uttered harsh speech, may I not experience the fruit of that <s>karma</s>! But by the merit of what I have recited, studied, the gifts of generosity I have given, and the service I have rendered to the <s>Saṃgha</s> — by the fruit of that <s>karma</s>, may I please future Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddhas</s> and may I not displease them!'

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayenāvāsiko bhikṣuḥ, ayam evāsau jāmbālaḥ | yad anenārhato 'ntike kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam*, asya karmaṇo vipākenānantaṃ saṃsāre duḥkham anubhūtam* | tenaiva ca karmāvaśeṣeṇa etarhi paścime bhave evaṃ durgandhaḥ paramadurgandho 'medhyāvaskarasthānanivāsābhiprāyaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yat punar anena tatra paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ dhātukauśalam āyatanakauśalaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalaṃ ca kṛtam*, tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yan mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyam * | tat kasya hetoḥ? ete doṣā na bhaviṣyanti, ye jāmbālasya pṛthagjanabhūtasya | eṣa eva guṇagaṇo bhaviṣyati, yo 'sau tasyaivārhatvaprāptasya | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was that resident monk — he is this very <s>Jāmbāla</s>. Because he uttered harsh speech in the presence of an <s>Arhat</s>, as the ripening of that deed he experienced endless suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. And by the residual force of that very <s>karma</s>, even now, in this last birth, he has become so foul-smelling, supremely foul-smelling, inclined to dwelling in unclean and refuse-filled places. But because he had studied and recited there, and had cultivated skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and skill in determining what is possible and impossible — by that, having gone forth in my teaching, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: you must strive for the abandonment of <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness). For what reason? So that these faults that befell <s>Jāmbāla</s> while he was an ordinary person may not arise; and so that this very host of virtues may arise that belongs to that same one who has attained <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, and the other <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and others rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 128]

children.text:
ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ |
tasyoddānam*:
children.translated_text:
The Sixth Section.
Its summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.text: kṛṣṇasarpaś ca candraś ca sālaḥ śrīmatir eva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇasarpa</s> (Black Serpent) and <s>Candra</s> (Moon), <s>Sāla</s> and <s>Śrīmati</s>,

children.text: vastraṃ śukaś ca dūtaś ca mahiṣaḥ poṣadhaś ca vai |
children.translated_text: <s>Vastra</s> (Cloth), <s>Śuka</s> (Parrot), <s>Dūta</s> (Messenger), <s>Mahiṣa</s> (Buffalo), <s>Poṣadha</s> (Observance Day),

children.text: x x x x x haṃso bhavati paścimaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [...] and <s>Haṃsa</s> (Swan) is the last.

children.text: AVŚ_51 kṛṣṇasarpaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_51: <s>Kṛṣṇasarpa</s> (Black Serpent). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | rājagṛhe nagaradvāre 'nyataro gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | sa ca matsarī kuṭukuñcaka āgṛhītapariṣkāraḥ kākāyāpi baliṃ na pradātuṃ vyavasyati | sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇavanīpakān dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ pradūṣayati | svake codyāne mahān hiraṇyasuvarṇasya rāśiḥ sthāpitaḥ | sa tatra gṛddho 'dhyavasitaḥ kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. At the city gate of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there was a certain householder — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. And he was miserly, grasping, a hoarder of possessions — he would not even consent to give an offering of food to a crow. Seeing <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and wandering mendicants, he would become ill-disposed in mind. A great heap of gold and silver had been placed in his own garden. Attached to it and clinging to it, he died.

children.text: sa kālaṃ kṛtvā tasyaivopari āśīviṣa utapanno mahān kṛṣṇasarpo dṛṣṭiviṣaḥ | atha ye tad udyānaṃ janakāyāḥ praviśanti, tān prekṣitamātreṇa jīvitād vyaparopayati | eṣa ca śabdo rājagṛhe nagare samantato visṛtaḥ: ye amukam udyānaṃ praviśanti, sarve te nidhanam upayāntīti | janakāyena ca rājñe bimbisārāya niveditam* ||
children.translated_text: Having died, he was reborn right on top of that [treasure] as a venomous serpent — a great black snake whose very gaze was poisonous. Those people who entered that garden he killed by merely glancing at them. And this report spread on all sides throughout the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>: 'All who enter that garden meet their death!' The populace reported this to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>.

children.text: atha rājño bimbisārasyaitad abhavat*: kas taṃ śakyati vinetum anyatra buddhād bhagavata iti | atha rājā bimbisāro mahājanakāyaparivṛto yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ bimbisāraṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati | anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm* | atha rājā bimbisāra utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat*: iha bhagavan rājagṛhe nagare 'muṣminn udyāne mahānāśīviṣaḥ kṛṣṇasarpo dṛṣṭiviṣaḥ prativasati, mahājanavipraghātaṃ karoti | sādhu bhagavāṃs tam vinayed anukampām upādāyeti | adhivāsayati bhagavān rājño bimbisārasya tūṣṇībhāvena | atha rājā bimbisāro bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>: 'Who can tame that one, other than the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One?' Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, surrounded by a great multitude, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet with his head and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, who was seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, [the Blessed One] fell silent. Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and extending his palms joined together toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'Here, Blessed One, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in a certain garden, there dwells a great venomous black serpent whose very gaze is poisonous. It is causing great destruction among the people. May the Blessed One, out of compassion, tame it!' The Blessed One consented to King <s>Bimbisāra</s> by his silence. Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, knowing the Blessed One's consent by his silence, worshipped the Blessed One's feet with his head, rose from his seat, and departed.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyā eva rātrer atyayāt pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya yena tad udyānaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavatā sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāḥ kanakavarṇā marīcaya utsṛṣṭāḥ,
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, when that very night had passed, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, approached that garden. Having approached, the Blessed One emitted rays of golden light, surpassing in brilliance a thousand suns,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 129]

children.text: yais tad udyānaṃ sarvam avabhāsitam* | kalpasahasraparibhāvitāś ca maitryaṃśava utsṛṣṭāḥ, yair asya spṛṣṭamātraṃ śarīraṃ prahlāditam* | atha sa āśīviṣa itaś cāmutaś ca prekṣitum ārabdhaḥ: kasya prabhāvān mama śarīraṃ prahlāditam iti | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike citaṃ prasāditaṃ* | prassannacittasya ca bhagavatā tan mayyā gatyās tan mayyā yonyā dharmo deśitaḥ: bhadramukha tvayaivaitad dravyam upārjitam* | yena tvam āśīviṣagatim upapāditaḥ | sādhu mamāntike cittaṃ prasādya, asmāc ca nidhānāc cittaṃ virāgaya | mā haiva itaḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā narakeṣūpapatsyasa iti | yadāsya bhagavatā jātiḥ smāritā, tadā rodituṃ pravṛttaḥ | atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthe bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: by which that entire garden was illuminated. And he emitted rays of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), cultivated over a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, by which the serpent's body was soothed the moment they touched it. Then that venomous serpent began to look this way and that: 'By whose power has my body been soothed?' And he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. And at the very sight, he generated faith in the Blessed One. And when his mind was filled with faith, the Blessed One taught him the <s>Dharma</s> suited to that realm, suited to that form of birth: 'Good sir, this very wealth was accumulated by you, by which you have been brought to the state of a venomous serpent. It would be well for you to generate faith in my presence and to turn your mind away from this treasure. Otherwise, having died from here, you will be reborn in the hells.' When the Blessed One reminded him of his [former] birth, he began to weep. Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: idānīṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmi tiryagyonigatasya te |
children.translated_text: 'What will I do now for you, one gone to the animal realm?

children.text: akṣaṇapratipannasya kiṃ rodiṣi nirarthakam* || AVŚ_51.1 ||
children.translated_text: Fallen into an inopportune state, why do you weep to no purpose?' // AVŚ_51.1 //

children.text:
sādhu prasādyatāṃ cittaṃ mahākāruṇike jine |
  tiryagyoniṃ virāgyeha tataḥ svargaṃ gamiṣyasi || AVŚ_51.2 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'It would be well to generate faith in the Conqueror, the greatly compassionate one.
Turn away from the animal realm here, and then you shall go to heaven.' // AVŚ_51.2 //

children.text: yāvad bhagavatā pātre prakṣipya veṇuvanaṃ nītaḥ | atrāntare rājñā māgadhena janakāyena ca śrutaṃ yathāsāv āśīviṣo bhagavatā vinīta iti ||
children.translated_text: Thereupon the Blessed One placed him in his bowl and brought him to the <s>Veṇuvana</s>. Meanwhile, King <s>Māgadha</s> (i.e., <s>Bimbisāra</s>) and the populace heard that the venomous serpent had been tamed by the Blessed One.

children.text:
athāsāv āśīviṣaḥ svāśrayaṃ jugupsamāno 'nāhāratā pratipannaḥ | bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādya kālagataḥ, praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ |
  dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | paśyati: āśīviṣebhyaś cyutaḥ, praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādyeti || athāśīviṣapūrvakasya devaputrasyaitad abhavat: na mama pratirūpaṃ syāt*, yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāso bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam* | yan nu aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | athāśīviṣapūrvako devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravirājitagātro maṇiratnavicitracūḍaḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātras tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ veṇuvanaṃ kalandakanivāsam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsayan bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān āśīviṣapūrvikasya devaputrasyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā āśīviṣapūrvakeṇa devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text:
Then that venomous serpent, repelled by his own form, undertook a fast unto death. Having generated faith in the Blessed One, he died and was reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.
It is the nature of things that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or a <s>Devakanyā</s> has been newly reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what deed?' He perceived: 'I have passed away from the venomous serpents and have been reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, by generating faith in the Blessed One.' Then this thought occurred to the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a venomous serpent: 'It would not be fitting for me to approach the Blessed One for an audience after having rested overnight. Rather, let me approach the Blessed One for an audience without having rested overnight.' Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a venomous serpent — wearing shimmering, spotless earrings, his body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, his crown studded with jewels and precious gems, his body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, and <s>spṛkkā</s> — that very night, having filled his lap with divine flowers of <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>mandārava</s>, illuminated the entire <s>Veṇuvana</s> <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> with his brilliant radiance, scattered flowers upon the Blessed One, and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, inclination, nature, and character of the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a venomous serpent, delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> leading to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a venomous serpent shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body) rising with its twenty peaks, and attained the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (Stream-entry). Having seen the truth, he uttered this exclamation three times: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, not by our father, not by a king, not by the gods, not by beloved kinsmen and relatives, not by departed ancestors, not by <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — what the Blessed One has done for us! The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been crossed over, the doors to the lower realms have been shut, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and men!' And he said:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 130]

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: 'By your power, the dreadful

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path of the lower realms, full of many faults, has been closed.

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: The path to heaven, rich in merit, has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_51.3 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found by me.' // AVŚ_51.3 //

children.text: tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
children.translated_text: 'By relying on you, I have today obtained

children.text: mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ |
children.translated_text: the pure, supremely purified eye [of the <s>Dharma</s>], free from faults.

children.text: prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
children.translated_text: I have attained the peaceful state, dear to the Noble Ones,

children.text: tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_51.4 ||
children.translated_text: and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.' // AVŚ_51.4 //

children.text:
naravarendra narāmarapūjita
  vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayaṃ |
  bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
  saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_51.5 || iti
avanamya tataḥ pralambahāraḥ
children.translated_text: Then, bowing low, wearing his pendant necklace,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: he worshipped both feet, filled with joy.

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitārīṃ
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated the Conqueror of foes to the right,

children.text: suralokābhimukho divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_51.6 ||
children.translated_text: he departed toward the world of the gods, facing heaven.' // AVŚ_51.6 //

'O best of men, worshipped by humans, gods, and <s>asuras</s>,
free from birth, old age, death, and disease,
whose sight is so hard to obtain in a thousand lifetimes —
today, O Sage, your sight has been fruitful.' // AVŚ_51.5 //

children.text: athāśīviṣapūrvako devaputro vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ, saṃpannasasya iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam upagatas tayaiva vibhūtyā tasyām eva rātrau rājño bimbisārasya sakāśam upasaṃkramya sarvaṃ rājakulam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya rājānaṃ prabodhya etad uvāca: mahārāja uttiṣṭha uttiṣṭha, kiṃ svapiṣīti | atha rājā prabuddhaḥ paśyati tam udāram avabhāsaṃ taṃ ca devaputram* | dṛṣṭvā prītamanās taṃ papraccha kas tvam iti | sa kathayati: ahaṃ sa dṛṣṭyāśīviṣo bhagavatā tatrodyāne vinītaḥ, kālaṃ kṛtvā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ | bhagavantaṃ ca me paryupāsya satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | sa idānīṃ prabodhayāmi | gatvā tad udyānam amukasmāt pradeśān mahānidhānam utpāṭya mama nāmnā bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojaya, dakṣiṇādeśanāṃ ca kārayeti | adhivāsayati rājā bimbisāro devaputrasya tūṣṇībhāvena | athāśīviṣapūrvako devaputro rājñas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā tatraivāntarhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a venomous serpent — like a merchant who has gained his profit, like a farmer whose crop has ripened, like a warrior who has won his battle, like a sick man freed from all disease — with the same splendor with which he had come to the Blessed One's presence, that very night he approached King <s>Bimbisāra</s>. Having illuminated the entire royal palace with his brilliant radiance and awakened the king, he said this: 'Great king, arise, arise! Why do you sleep?' Then the king, having awoken, saw that brilliant radiance and that <s>Devaputra</s>. Having seen him, delighted in mind, he asked: 'Who are you?' He replied: 'I am that same venomous serpent who was tamed by the Blessed One in that garden. Having died, I have been reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. And having attended upon the Blessed One, I gained the vision of truth. Now I come to awaken you. Go to that garden; from a certain spot, dig up a great treasure; and in my name, feed the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the Blessed One, and have the dedication of merit made.' King <s>Bimbisāra</s> consented to the <s>Devaputra</s> by his silence. Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a venomous serpent, knowing the king's consent by his silence, vanished right there.

children.text: atha sa rājā bimbisāras tasyām eva rātrau māgadhānāṃ paurajānapadānāṃ nivedya tad udyānaṃ gatvā nidhānam utpāṭya bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ traimāsyaṃ bhojayitvā bhagavantaṃ papraccha: kāni bhagavann aśīviṣapūrvakeṇa devaputreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenāśīviṣeṣūpapannaḥ: kāni karmāṇi kṛtāni yena deveṣūpapannaḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam iti? bhagavān āha: yat tenātimātro lobha utpāditaḥ, śramaṇabrāhmaṇavanīpakānāṃ cāntike cittaṃ praduṣitam*, tenāśīviṣeṣūpapannaḥ | yan mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditam*, tena deveṣūpapannaḥ | kāśyape ca samykasaṃbuddhe upāsakabhūtena śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam*, tena satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam iti | tasmāt tarhi mahārāja mātsaryaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyam* | ete doṣā na bhaviṣyanti ye āśīviṣasya | eṣa eva guṇagaṇo bhaviṣyati, yas tasyaiva devaputrasyety evaṃ te mahārāja śikṣitavyam* | atha rājā bimbisāro bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, on that very night, having informed the citizens and countryfolk of <s>Magadha</s>, went to that park, unearthed the treasure, and having fed the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples for three months, asked the Blessed One: 'What <s>karma</s>, Blessed One, was performed by the <s>Devaputra</s> who was formerly a venomous snake, by which he was reborn among venomous snakes? What <s>karma</s> did he perform by which he was reborn among the gods and attained the vision of truth?' The Blessed One said: 'Because he generated excessive greed and harbored ill-will toward <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and wanderers, he was reborn among venomous snakes. Because he purified his mind in my presence, he was reborn among the gods. And because, in the time of the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, as a lay-follower, he took refuge and accepted the precepts, he attained the vision of truth. Therefore, great king, one must strive for the abandonment of miserliness. Those faults that befell the venomous snake shall not arise [in you]. That very host of virtues that belonged to that <s>Devaputra</s> shall be yours. Thus, great king, should you train.' Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, having rejoiced at and approved the Blessed One's words, having worshipped the Blessed One's feet with his head, rose from his seat and departed.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, and the other <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and others rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 131]

children.text: AVŚ_52 candraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_52: <s>Candra</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ karṣako brāhmaṇaḥ | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvajanamanonayanaprahlādanakaraḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya jātau sarvalokānāṃ nayanaprahlādanam*, tasmād bhavatu asya dārakasya candra iti nāmeti | sa ca tena brāhmaṇena kṛcchreṇa labdhaḥ | na cāsyānyaḥ putro na duhitā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain farmer-Brahmin. He took a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, gladdening the eyes and hearts of all people. At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since at his birth all people's eyes were gladdened, let this boy's name be <s>Candra</s> (Moon).' And he had been obtained by that Brahmin with great difficulty. Nor did he have any other son or daughter.

children.text: sa unnīto vardhito mahān saṃvṛttaḥ | sa sarvalokaprahlādanakaratvād brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhiḥ kṛtsnaṃ nagaram anvāhiṇḍyata iti | sa brāhmaṇas tasmin bhūyasyā mātrayādhyavasito nityam eva kramasthānaśayyāsu saṃrakṣaṇaparo 'vatiṣṭhite | tasya ca brāhmaṇasyānāthapiṇḍadasamīpe gṛham* | atha sa brāhmaṇadārako 'nāthapiṇḍadasaṃsargāj jetavanaṃ gatvā buddhavacanaṃ śṛṇoti | tena bhagavacchāsane prasādaḥ pratilabdhaḥ | sa cālpāyuṣkaḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was raised, nourished, and grew up. Because of his ability to gladden all people, the Brahmin householders would take him on tours throughout the entire city. And that Brahmin was exceedingly devoted to him, always standing guard over him at every step, position, and resting-place. That Brahmin's house was near <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s. Then that Brahmin boy, through association with <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, went to the <s>Jetavana</s> and heard the word of the <s>Buddha</s>. Thereby he gained faith in the Blessed One's teaching. And he, being short-lived, died and was reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven.
