children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaś ca kena karmaṇeti | paśyati manuṣyebhyaś cyutaḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittam ahiprasādyeti | atha brāhmaṇapūrviṇo devaputrasyaitad abhavat: na mama pratirūpaṃ syāt*, yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāso bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam* | yanv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | atha brāhmaṇapūrvako devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravirājitagātro maṇiratnavicitracūḍaḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātras tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ jetavanam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavataṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān brāhmaṇapūrvakasya devaputrasyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā brāhmaṇapūrvakeṇa devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalam prāptam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that for a <s>Devaputra</s> or <s>Devakanyā</s> newly reborn [in heaven], three thoughts arise: 'From where did I pass away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' He saw: 'Having passed away from among humans, I have been reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, through having purified my mind in the presence of the Blessed One.' Then this thought arose in the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a Brahmin: 'It would not be proper for me, having spent the night, to approach the Blessed One for an audience. Rather, let me approach the Blessed One for an audience without having spent the night.' Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a Brahmin — wearing gleaming earrings, his body resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, his crown adorned with various jewels and gems, his body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, and other fragrances — on that very night, having filled his lap with divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> flowers, illuminated the entire <s>Jetavana</s> with a magnificent radiance, scattered flowers over the Blessed One, and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, having known the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a Brahmin's disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a Brahmin shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he thrice uttered this joyful exclamation: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by kings, nor by gods, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by departed ancestors, nor by <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — what the Blessed One has done for us! The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been transcended, the doors to the woeful states have been shut, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and humans.' And he said:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 132]

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: 'By your power, the terrible

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path of the woeful states, fraught with many faults, has been shut.

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: 'The meritorious path to heaven has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_52.1 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been obtained by me.' // AVŚ_52.1 //

children.text: tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
children.translated_text: 'By relying on you, the flawless,

children.text: mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ |
children.translated_text: supremely pure eye [of the <s>Dharma</s>] has today been attained by me.

children.text: prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
children.translated_text: 'The peaceful state, beloved of the Noble Ones, has been reached,

children.text: tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_52.2 ||
children.translated_text: and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.' // AVŚ_52.2 //

children.text:
naravarendra narāmarapūjita
  vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayaṃ |
  bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
  saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_52.3 || iti
avanamya tataḥ pralambahāraś
children.translated_text: Then, bowing with his dangling necklace,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhinandya jātaharṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: delighting in his two feet, filled with joy,

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: having circumambulated the Conqueror of Enemies to the right,

children.text: suralokābhimukho divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_52.4 ||
children.translated_text: he departed toward the realm of the gods, ascending to heaven. // AVŚ_52.4 //

'O best of men, worshipped by humans and gods,
free from birth, old age, death, and disease,
whose sight is hard to obtain in thousands of existences —
fruitful indeed, O Sage, is your vision today!' // AVŚ_52.3 //

children.text: atha brāhmaṇapūrvako devaputro vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ, sasyasaṃpanna iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva {vi}jitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā hi vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatas tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a Brahmin — like a merchant who has gained profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won the battle, like a sick man freed from all diseases — with the same splendor with which he had come to the Blessed One's presence, returned to his own celestial abode.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ | yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhagavann asyāṃ rātryāṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ, api yo 'sāv ekaputro 'sya brāhmaṇasya putro 'lpāyuṣkaḥ kālagataḥ, sa mamāntike cittam abhiprasādya praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ, so 'syāṃ rātrau matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | tasya mayā dharmo deśitaḥ, dṛṣṭasatyaś ca svabhavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw a magnificent radiance in the Blessed One's presence. Having seen it, filled with doubt, they asked the Blessed One: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the Blessed One this night, Blessed One?' The Blessed One said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. Rather, that Brahmin's only son who was short-lived and died — he, having purified his mind in my presence, was reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. He came to my presence this night. I taught him the <s>Dharma</s>, and having seen the truth, he returned to his own celestial abode.'

children.text: atra cāntare sa brāhmaṇas tam ekaputrakam iṣṭaṃ kāntaṃ priyaṃ manāpaṃ kṣāntam apratikūlaṃ śmaśāne nirhṛtyotsaṅge kṛtvā karuṇakaruṇaṃ vilapan* kathayati: hā putraka hā ekaputraketi | jñātayaḥ subahv api śokavinodanaṃ kurvaṇā na śaknuvanty utthāpayitum* | sa kākakuraraśvaśṛgālagṛdhraparivṛtaḥ prakīrṇakeśībhiḥ strībhir anugato mahājanakāyena codvīkṣyamāṇas tiṣṭhati | tato 'sya putro devabhūtaḥ pitaraṃ paridevamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāruṇyād ākampitahṛdayaḥ pituḥ śokavinodanārtham ṛṣiveṣadhāriṇam ātmānam abhinirmāya śmaśānasamīpe pañcatapāvasthitaḥ | atha sa brāhmaṇas tam ṛṣiṃ papraccha: bho maharṣe anena tapasā kiṃ prārthayasa iti | ṛṣir āha: rājyaṃ prārthaye, sauvarṇaś ca me rathaḥ syān nānāratnavicitraḥ, sūryācandramasau rathacakre syātām*, catvāraś ca lokapālāḥ purastān nameyuḥ | so 'haṃ taṃ ratham abhiruhyemāṃ mahāpṛthivīm anvāhiṇḍeyeti | brāhmaṇaḥ kathayati:
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, that Brahmin, having carried his only son — dear, beloved, pleasant, agreeable, pleasing, not displeasing — to the cremation ground, placed him on his lap and lamented pitifully: 'Alas, my son! Alas, my only son!' The relatives, though making many efforts to console his grief, were unable to raise him up. He stood there, surrounded by crows, kuraras, dogs, jackals, and vultures, followed by women with disheveled hair, watched by a great multitude of people. Then his son, now a god, seeing his father lamenting, his heart shaken with compassion, for the purpose of dispelling his father's grief, created the appearance of a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) and stood near the cremation ground performing the five-fire austerity. Then that Brahmin asked the <s>ṛṣi</s>: 'Great sage, what do you seek to obtain by this austerity?' The <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'I seek kingship, and I wish for a golden chariot adorned with various jewels, with the sun and moon as its wheels, and the four World-Guardians bowing before me. Then I would mount that chariot and travel about this great earth.' The Brahmin said:

children.text:
yadi varṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ tapiṣyasi nirantaram* |
  na lapsyase 'pi tat sthānaṃ paramatapasāpi hi || AVŚ_52.5 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'Even if you perform austerities for a full hundred years without interruption,
you will not obtain that state even by the most extreme austerity.' // AVŚ_52.5 //

children.text: ṛṣiḥ kathayati: tvaṃ ca punar anena mṛtakuṇapenāśucinā paramadurgandhena śavena kāṣṭhabhūtena kiṃ prārthayasa iti | brāhmaṇaḥ prāha: priyo me ekaputrakaḥ kālagataḥ, taṃ prārthaya iti | ṛṣir āha:
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛṣi</s> said: 'And you — what do you seek to obtain with this dead body, impure, supremely foul-smelling, a corpse, become like a log of wood?' The Brahmin said: 'My dear only son has died. I seek him.' The <s>ṛṣi</s> said:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 133]

children.text:
yadi varṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ rodiṣyasi nirantaram* |
  na lapsyase 'pi taṃ putraṃ ruditena hi kiṃ tava || AVŚ_52.6 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'Even if you weep for a full hundred years without interruption,
you will not obtain that son — what use is weeping to you?' // AVŚ_52.6 //

children.text: tatas tasya brāhmaṇasya bhūtam ṛṣivacanam avagatya prasādo jātaḥ | prasādajātaś cāha: kas tvam iti | tata ṛṣis taṃ veṣam antardhāpya svaveṣeṇa sthitvā pitaram āha: ahaṃ te sa ekaputrako bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādya kālagataḥ | praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ | tava śokavinodanārtham ihāgataḥ | ehi tvaṃ tāta buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccha, apy eva tvam api saṃsārasamatikrāmaṃ kuryā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then that Brahmin, recognizing the truth of the <s>ṛṣi</s>'s words, was filled with faith. Filled with faith, he said: 'Who are you?' Then the <s>ṛṣi</s>, causing that disguise to disappear and standing in his own [divine] form, said to his father: 'I am that only son of yours. Having purified my mind in the presence of the Blessed One, I died and was reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. I have come here to dispel your grief. Come, father, take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. Perhaps you too may cross beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>.'

children.text: atha sa brāhmaṇo mṛtaśarīram apahāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tena brāhmaṇeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalam prāptam* | sa labdhodayo labdhalābho bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that Brahmin, abandoning the dead body, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and worshipped the Blessed One's feet, he sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One gave him a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to penetration of the Four Noble Truths. Having heard it, that Brahmin shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having gained a [spiritual] dawn and a [spiritual] profit, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet with his head, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and departed.

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhagavan, yāvad anena devaputreṇāyaṃ pitā śokaṃ vinodya satyadarśane pratiṣṭhāpita iti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad anenaitarhi dṛṣṭasatyena pitā paritrātaḥ | yat tv anena atīte 'dhvani pṛthagjanena satā yāvat trir api pitā jīvitād vyavaropyamāṇaḥ paritrātaḥ | tac chruṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Then the monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'See, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how this <s>Devaputra</s> has dispelled his father's grief and established him in the vision of truth!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is so wonderful in this, monks, that now, having seen the truth, he has rescued his father? But in a past age, when he was still an ordinary person, he rescued his father three times even as his father was being led to execution. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamaḥ pāradārikaḥ | tasya putro bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśayo 'tīva lokasyābhimataḥ | yāvad asya pitrā cauryaṃ kṛtam* | tato rājñā vadhyatām ity ājñaptam* | tataḥ putreṇa yāvat trir api rājānaṃ vijñāpya iṣṭena jīvitenācchāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain adulterer. His son was virtuous, well-intentioned, and greatly beloved by the people. Then his father committed theft. The king ordered: 'Let him be executed!' Then the son, having petitioned the king three times, sheltered his father at the cost of his own dear life.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena pāradārika āsīt*, ayaṃ sa brāhmaṇaḥ | pāradārikaputro 'yam eva brāhmaṇadārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the adulterer — he is this Brahmin. The adulterer's son is this very Brahmin boy.'

children.text: bhikṣava ūcuḥ: kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena pitāputrābhyāṃ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe upāsakabhūtābhyāṃ śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam* | tenedānīṃ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ, sarvadharmā anātmānaḥ, śāntaṃ nirvāṇam iti nirvāṇe yatnaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The monks said: 'What <s>karma</s> did the father and son perform that they attained the vision of truth?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Under the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, being lay devotees, they took the refuges and undertook the training precepts. By that, they have now attained the vision of truth. Therefore, monks, all conditioned things are impermanent; all phenomena are without self; <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is peace — one must strive for <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo 'nye ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādayo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, along with others — <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and the rest — rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 134]

children.text: AVŚ_53 sālaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_53: <s>Sāla</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu punaḥ samayena śrāvastyāṃ sālabhañjikā nāma parva pratyupasthitam* | tatrānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatya sālapuṣpāṇy ādāya krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti | yāvad anyatarā śreṣṭhidārikā sālapuṣpāṇy ādāya śrāvastīṃ praviśati | bhagavāṃś ca bhikṣugaṇaparivṛtaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā nirgacchati | dadarśa sā dārikā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ prasādajātayā bhagavān sālapuṣpair avakīrṇaḥ | tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pratinivṛttā: bhūyo 'nyāni gṛhasyārthe āneṣyāmīti | yāvad asau sālavṛkṣam adhirūḍhā patitā | bhagavataḥ kṛtopasthānā kālagatā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā yāvat sālapuṣpavimānālaṃkṛtā devasamitim upasaṃkrāntā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, the festival called <s>Sālabhañjikā</s> had arrived in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. There, many hundreds of thousands of beings assembled, taking <s>śāla</s> flowers, and sported, delighted, and amused themselves. Then a certain guild-master's daughter, carrying <s>śāla</s> flowers, was entering <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by a company of monks, was leaving <s>Śrāvastī</s> after his alms-round. That girl beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Having seen him, filled with faith, she scattered <s>śāla</s> flowers over the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then, having circumambulated him, she turned back, thinking: 'I shall bring more flowers from home.' While she had climbed a <s>śāla</s> tree, she fell. Having rendered service to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, upon dying she was reborn among the exalted gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, adorned with a <s>śāla</s>-flower palace, and she approached the assembly of the gods.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca kāle śakro devendraḥ sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāṃ devagaṇasya madhye buddhasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate, dharmasya saṃghasya ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate | dadarśa śakro devendras tāṃ devakanyāṃ sālapuṣpavimānālaṃkṛtām uttaptakuśalamūlām* | dṛṣṭvā ca gāthayā pratyabhāṣata:
children.translated_text: At that time, <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, in the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall, amidst the throng of gods, was speaking in praise of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, beheld that divine maiden adorned with a <s>śāla</s>-flower palace, her roots of merit blazing with intensity. Having seen her, he addressed her with a verse:

children.text: gātraṃ kena vimṛṣṭakāñcananibhaṃ padmotpalābhaṃ tava
children.translated_text: By whom has your body been made to gleam like burnished gold, radiant as lotus and blue lotus?

children.text: gātraśrīr atulā kṛteyam iha te dehāt prabhā niḥsṛtā |
children.translated_text: Your bodily splendor is unequaled — from your body a radiance has shone forth.

children.text: vaktraṃ kena vibuddhapadmasadṛśaṃ cāmīkarābhaṃ tava
children.translated_text: By whom has your face been made to resemble a fully opened lotus, gleaming like fine gold?

children.text: brūhi tvaṃ mama devate phalam idaṃ yat karmajaṃ bhujyate || AVŚ_53.1 ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, O deity, what <s>karma</s>-born fruit is this that you enjoy? // AVŚ_53.1 //

children.text: devatā prāha:
children.translated_text: The deity replied:

children.text: saśrāvako narāditya ākīrṇo varalakṣaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The Sun among Men, accompanied by his disciples, adorned with the finest marks —

children.text: tat karma kuśalaṃ kṛtvā rājate 'bhyadhikaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: having performed that wholesome <s>karma</s> [toward him], there radiates about me more abundantly

children.text: jalajenduviśuddhābhaṃ vadanaṃ kāntadarśanam* || AVŚ_53.2 ||
children.translated_text: a face of beauty, pure as a water-born lotus and the moon. // AVŚ_53.2 //

children.text: śakraḥ prāha:
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: aho guṇamayaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam* |
children.translated_text: Ah, what a field of merit, endowed with virtues, free from all faults!

children.text: yatra nyastaṃ tvayā bījam iṣṭaṃ svargopapattaye || AVŚ_53.3 ||
children.translated_text: There you planted a seed, desired for rebirth in heaven! // AVŚ_53.3 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 135]

children.text: ko nārcayet pravarakāñcanarāśigauraṃ
children.translated_text: Who would not worship the <s>Buddha</s>, bright as a heap of finest gold,

children.text: buddhaṃ viśuddhakamalāyatapatranetram* |
children.translated_text: with eyes broad and pure as lotuses?

children.text: yatrādhikārajanitāni varāṅganānāṃ
children.translated_text: For by meritorious deeds performed toward him, the faces of noble women

children.text: rejur mukhāni kamalāyatalocanani || AVŚ_53.4 ||
children.translated_text: shine with lotus-wide eyes! // AVŚ_53.4 //

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | sā paśyati: manuṣyebhyaś cyutā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā, bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādyeti | atha tasyā devakanyāyā etad abhavat: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāsā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam* | yanv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsā eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | atha sā devakanyā calavimalakuṇḍaladharā hārārdhahāravirājitagātrī maṇiratnavicitracūḍā kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātrī anekadevatāśatasahasraparivṛtā tenaiva sālapuṣpavimānena saha bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavāṃs tasyā devatāyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā tayā devakanyayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sā dṛṣṭasatyā trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na devatābhir na rājñā neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or a <s>Devakanyā</s> is newly reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where did I pass away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' She saw: 'I passed away from among humans and have been reborn among the exalted gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, by generating faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.' Then this thought arose in that divine maiden: 'It would not be fitting for me to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience after having spent the night. Rather, let me approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> without having spent the night.' Then that divine maiden — wearing gleaming, pure earrings, her body resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, her crown adorned with various gems and jewels, her body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, and other fragrances — surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of deities, with that very <s>śāla</s>-flower palace, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. She scattered flowers over the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing her disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which that divine maiden, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) that rises to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, she thrice uttered this exclamation: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by the gods, nor by the king, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by deceased ancestors, nor by ascetics and brahmins — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; the mountains of bones have been crossed over; the doors to the woeful states have been shut; the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened; we have been established among gods and humans.' And she said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: By your power, the terrible

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path to the woeful states, fraught with many faults, has been shut;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: the meritorious path to heaven has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_53.5 ||
children.translated_text: and by me the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found. // AVŚ_53.5 //

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer: suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇā ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_53.6 ||
children.translated_text:
and I have reached the peaceful state, beloved of the noble ones,
and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering. // AVŚ_53.6 //

By relying on you, today I have obtained
the pure, stainless, supremely purified eye [of truth];

children.text:
naravarendra narāmarapūjita
  vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayaṃ |
  bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
  saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_53.7 || iti
avanamya tataḥ pralambahārā
children.translated_text: Then, bowing down with long-hanging necklaces,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣā |
children.translated_text: having worshipped both feet, filled with joy,

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: and having circumambulated the Conqueror of Foes to the right,

children.text: suralokābhimukhī divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_53.8 ||
children.translated_text: she ascended to heaven, facing the world of the gods. // AVŚ_53.8 //

O best of men, worshipped by humans and gods,
free from birth, old age, death, and disease —
O sage, your sight, so difficult to obtain in thousands of existences,
has today borne fruit! // AVŚ_53.7 //

children.text: athāsau devakanyā vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ, sasyasaṃpanna iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatā tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: Then that divine maiden, like a merchant who has gained his profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won his battle, like a sick person freed from all disease — with the very same splendor with which she had come to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, she returned to her own abode.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 136]

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ, yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhadanta imāṃ rātriṃ brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | api tu dṛṣṭā yuṣmābhiḥ sā dārikā, yayā aham antarmārgo sālapuṣpair avakīrṇaḥ? evaṃ bhadanta | saiṣā mamāntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagatā praṇīteṣū deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā | sā imāṃ rātriṃ matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | tasyā mayā dharmo deśitaḥ, dṛṣṭasatyā ca svabhavanaṃ gatā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw the magnificent radiance in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Having seen it, filled with doubt, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> this night?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. But did you see that girl who on the road scattered <s>śāla</s> flowers over me?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'She, having generated faith in my presence, upon dying was reborn among the exalted gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. She came to my presence this night. I taught her the <s>Dharma</s>, and having seen the truth, she returned to her own abode. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him." Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_54 śrīmatī | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_54: <s>Śrīmatī</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | rājagṛhe nagare rājā bimbisāro rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | yadā rājñā bimbisāreṇa bhagavataḥ sakāśāt satyāni dṛṣṭāni, tadā rātriṃ bhagavantam upasaṃkrāmati sārdham antaḥpureṇa | atha rājā bimbisāro 'pareṇa samayena saṃprāpte vasantakālasamaye saṃpuṣpiteṣu pādapeṣu haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīvañjīvakanirghoṣite vanaṣaṇḍe devyā sahāntaḥpuraparivṛta udyānabhūmiṃ nirgataḥ | tatra cāntaḥpurikābhī rājā vijñaptaḥ: deva vayaṃ na śaknumo 'hanyahani bhagavantam upasaṃkramitum* | tat sādhu devo 'sminn antaḥpure tathāgatasya keśanakhastūpaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayed* yatra vayam asakṛtpuṣpair gandhair mālyair vilepanaiś chatrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhiḥ pūjāṃ kuryāmeti | yāvad rājñā bimbisāreṇa bhagavān vijñaptaḥ: dīyatām asmabhyaṃ keśanakhaṃ yena vayaṃ tathāgatastūpam antaḥpuramadhye pratiṣṭhāpayāma iti | yāvad bhagavatā keśanakhaṃ dattam* | rājñā bimbisāreṇa mahatā satkāreṇāntaḥpurasahāyena tathāgatasya keśanakhastūpo 'ntaḥpuramadhye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ | tatra cāntaḥpure 'ntaḥpurikā dīpadhūpapuṣpagandhamālyavilepanair abhyarcanaṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. In the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless — guarding his kingdom as if it were his only son. When King <s>Bimbisāra</s> had seen the truths in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, he would visit the <s>Bhagavān</s> at night together with his harem. Then, on a later occasion, when the spring season had arrived, when the trees were in bloom, in a forest grove resounding with the calls of swans, cranes, peacocks, parrots, mynahs, cuckoos, and <s>jīvañjīvaka</s> birds, King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, together with the queen and surrounded by the harem, went out to the pleasure grounds. There the women of the harem informed the king: 'Lord, we are unable to visit the <s>Bhagavān</s> every day. It would be good if Your Majesty would establish a <s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s hair and nails in this harem, where we may repeatedly make offerings with flowers, incense, garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags.' Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s> requested the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May hair and nails be given to us, so that we may establish a <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>stūpa</s> within the harem.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> gave hair and nails. King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, with great honor and together with the harem, established a hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> within the harem. And there in the harem, the women would worship it with lamps, incense, flowers, fragrances, garlands, and ointments.

children.text: yadā punā rājñā ajātaśatruṇā devadattavigrāhitena pitā dhārmiko dharmarājo jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ, svayaṃ ca rājyaṃ pratipannaḥ, tadā bhagavacchāsane sarvedeyadharmāḥ samucchinnāḥ |
children.translated_text: But when King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, instigated by <s>Devadatta</s>, had deprived his righteous father, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, of his life and had himself assumed the kingdom, at that time all gifts to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching were cut off.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 137]

children.text: kriyākāraś ca kārito na kenacit tathāgatastūpe kārāḥ kartavyā iti | yadā pañcadaśyāṃ pravāraṇā saṃvṛttā, tadā tatra keśanakhastūpe na kaścit saṃmārjanaṃ dīpadhūpapuṣpadānaṃ vā kurute | tato 'ntaḥpurikā keśanakhastūpaṃ tathāvidhaṃ rājānaṃ ca bimbisāram anusmṛtya karuṇakaruṇaṃ roditum ārabdhāḥ: hā kaṣṭaṃ dharmarājaviyogād vayaṃ puṇyāt prahīṇā iti | tatra ca śrīmatī nāmāntaḥpurikā | sā svakaṃ jīvitam agaṇayitvā buddhaguṇāṃś cānusmṛtya keśanakhastūpaṃ saṃmṛjya dīpamālām akārṣīt* | yāvad ajātaśatrur upariprasādatalagataḥ tam udāram avabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā papraccha kim idam iti | yāvad anyayā kathitam*: śrīmatyā keśanakhastūpe dīpamālā kṛteti | tataḥ śrīmatīm āhūya kathayati: kim arthaṃ rājaśāsanam atikramasīti | sā kathayati: yady api mayā tava śāsanam atikrāntam*, kiṃ tu dharmarājasya mayā bimbisārasya śāsanaṃ nātikrāntam iti | tatas tena kupitena cakraṃ kṣiptvā jīvitād vyavaropitā | sā bhagavati prasannacittā kālagatā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā ||
children.translated_text: And a decree was issued: 'No one shall perform any services at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>.' When the full-moon day of the <s>Pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony) arrived, no one performed sweeping, lamp-offering, incense-offering, or flower-offering at the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s>. Then the women of the harem, remembering the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s> in its former state and King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, began to weep most pitifully: 'Alas, how grievous! Through separation from the <s>Dharma</s>-king, we have been deprived of merit!' Among them was a harem woman named <s>Śrīmatī</s>. She, disregarding her own life and recollecting the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>, swept the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s> and made a garland of lamps. Then <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, standing on the upper floor of the palace, saw that magnificent radiance and asked: 'What is this?' Another woman told him: '<s>Śrīmatī</s> has made a garland of lamps at the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s>.' Then he summoned <s>Śrīmatī</s> and said: 'Why do you transgress the royal command?' She said: 'Even though I have transgressed your command, I have not transgressed the command of the <s>Dharma</s>-king <s>Bimbisāra</s>.' Then he, enraged, hurled a discus and deprived her of life. She, with a mind of serene faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, died and was reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven.

children.text: tatra kāle devasamitir upasthitā | atha śrīmatī devakanyā samantayojanaṃ divyaprabhāmaṇḍalāvabhāsitā devasamitim upasaṃkrāntā | tataḥ śakro devendras tam udāram avabhāsaṃ divyāṃ ca prabhāṃ samantayojanaṃ dṛṣṭvā papraccha:
children.translated_text: At that time, an assembly of the gods had convened. Then the divine maiden <s>Śrīmatī</s>, illuminating all around for a <s>yojana</s> with the radiance of her divine splendor, approached the divine assembly. Then <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, seeing that magnificent radiance and divine splendor illuminating a <s>yojana</s> all around, asked:

children.text: gātraṃ kena vimṛṣṭakāñcananibhaṃ padmotpalābhaṃ tava
children.translated_text: 'By what [merit] is your body like polished gold, with the luster of lotuses and water-lilies?

children.text: gātraśrīr atulā kṛteyam iha te dehāt prabhā niḥsṛtā |
children.translated_text: This incomparable bodily beauty has been produced for you here, and radiance streams forth from your body.

children.text: vaktraṃ kena vibuddhapadmasadṛśaṃ cāmīkarābhaṃ tava
children.translated_text: By what [merit] is your face like a fully opened lotus, with the gleam of fine gold?

children.text: brūhi tvaṃ mama devate phalam idaṃ yat karmajaṃ bhujyate || AVŚ_54.1 ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, O goddess, what <s>karma</s> produced this fruit that you now enjoy?' // AVŚ_54.1 //

children.text: devatā prāha:
children.translated_text: The goddess replied:

children.text: trailokyanāthaṃ jagataḥ pradīpaṃ nirīkṣya buddhaṃ varalakṣaṇāḍhyam* |
children.translated_text: 'Having beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, Lord of the three worlds, lamp of the world, rich in excellent marks,

children.text: cakāra dīpaṃ vadatāṃ varasya tamonudaṃ kleśatamonudasya || AVŚ_54.2 ||
children.translated_text: I made a lamp for the best of speakers, the dispeller of darkness, the dispeller of the darkness of <s>kleśas</s> (defilements). // AVŚ_54.2 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā prabhāṃ candramarīcivarṇāṃ cakāra bhāvena munau prasādam* |
children.translated_text: Seeing the radiance like the rays of the moon, I generated faith with devotion toward the Sage,

children.text: prabhāṃ ca harṣāt samudīkṣya śāstuś cakre praṇāmaṃ vadatāṃ varasya || AVŚ_54.3 ||
children.translated_text: and beholding with joy the radiance of the Teacher, I made obeisance to the best of speakers. // AVŚ_54.3 //

children.text: tatkarmaṇā śriyā dehaṃ rājate 'bhyadhikaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: By that <s>karma</s>, my body shines surpassingly with splendor,

children.text: jalajenduviśuddhābhaṃ vadanaṃ kāntadarśanam* || AVŚ_54.4 ||
children.translated_text: my face is beautiful to behold, pure as a water-lily and the moon.' // AVŚ_54.4 //

children.text: śakraḥ prāha:
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: aho guṇamayaṃ kṣetraṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam* |
children.translated_text: 'Oh, what a field of virtue, free from all faults,

children.text: yatra nyastaṃ tvayā bījam iṣṭaṃ svargopapattaye || AVŚ_54.5 ||
children.translated_text: in which you planted the seed that desired for rebirth in heaven! // AVŚ_54.5 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 138]

children.text: ko nārcayet pravarakāñcanarāśigauraṃ
children.translated_text: Who would not worship the <s>Buddha</s>, radiant as a heap of finest gold,

children.text: buddhaṃ viśuddhakamalāyatapatranetram* |
children.translated_text: his eyes broad as pure lotuses,

children.text: yatrādhikārajanitāni varāṅganānāṃ
children.translated_text: when by such devotion the faces of excellent women

children.text: rejur mukhāni kamalāyatalocanani || AVŚ_54.6 ||
children.translated_text: shine with eyes broad as lotuses?' // AVŚ_54.6 //

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | sā paśyati: manuṣyebhyaś cyutā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā, bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādyeti | atha śrīmatyā devakanyāyā etad abhavat: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāsā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam* | yanv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsā eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | atha śrīmatī devakanyā divyaprabhāvabhāsapariveṣṭitā divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ veṇuvanaṃ kalandakanivāpam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavāñ chrīmatyā devakanyāyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā srīmatyā devakanyāyā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptam* | sā dṛṣṭasatyā trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or <s>Devakanyā</s> has recently been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' She saw: 'I have passed away from the human realm and have been reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, by generating serene faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then the divine maiden <s>Śrīmatī</s> had this thought: 'It would not be fitting for me to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience after having spent the night. Rather, let me approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience without having spent the night.' Then the divine maiden <s>Śrīmatī</s>, enveloped in the splendor of divine radiance, having filled her lap with divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> flowers, illuminating the entire <s>Veṇuvana</s> at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> with a magnificent radiance, scattered flowers over the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature of the divine maiden <s>Śrīmatī</s>, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which the divine maiden <s>Śrīmatī</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, she uttered this exclamation three times: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by a mother, nor by a father, nor by a king, nor by the gods, nor by beloved relatives and kinsmen, nor by departed ancestors, nor by ascetics and brahmins — that which the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us! The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; the mountains of bones have been crossed over; the doors to the woeful states have been closed; the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened; we have been established among gods and humans.' And she said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: 'By your power, the terrifying

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path of woeful rebirth, full of many faults, has been closed;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: the meritorious path to heaven has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_54.7 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been attained by me. // AVŚ_54.7 //

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer: suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇā ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_54.8 ||
children.translated_text: I have reached the peaceful state beloved of the noble ones, and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering. // AVŚ_54.8 //
Relying upon you, today I have attained pure, supremely pure vision, free from faults;

children.text: naravarendra narāmarapūjita
children.translated_text: O best of men, Lord, worshipped by humans and gods,

children.text: vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayaṃ |
children.translated_text: free from birth, old age, death, and disease,

children.text: bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
children.translated_text: your sight, so hard to obtain in thousands of existences —

children.text: saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_54.9 ||
children.translated_text: today, O Sage, your darśana has borne fruit!' // AVŚ_54.9 //

children.text: avanamya tataḥ pralambahārā
children.translated_text: Then, bowing down, with her long necklace hanging,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣā |
children.translated_text: having worshipped both feet, filled with joy,

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: having circumambulated the conqueror of foes to the right,

children.text: suralokābhimukhī divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_54.10 ||
children.translated_text: she departed toward the world of the gods. // AVŚ_54.10 //

children.text: atha śrīmatī devakanyā vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ, sasyasaṃpanna iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva {vi}jitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatā tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: Then the divine maiden <s>Śrīmatī</s>, like a merchant who has gained his profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won his battle, like a sick person freed from all disease — with the very same splendor with which she had come into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, she returned to her own abode.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 139]

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ | yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhagavann imāṃ rātriṃ brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | api tu rājño bimbisārasya śrīmatī nāmāntaḥpurikā svajīvitam agaṇayitvā buddhaguṇāṃś cānusmṛtya tathāgatasya keśanakhastūpe dīpamālāṃ kṛtavatī | tato rājñā ajātaśatruṇā kupitena jīvitād vyavaropitā | sā mamāntike cittaṃ prasādya kālagatā praṇīteṣū deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā | sā asyāṃ rātrau matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | tasyā mayā dharmo deśitaḥ, dṛṣṭasatyā ca svabhavanaṃ gatā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yac chāstāraṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | śāstāraṃ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvopaniśritya vihariṣyāmaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw the magnificent radiance in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Having seen it, filled with doubt, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> this night?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. Rather, in King <s>Bimbisāra</s>'s harem, the woman named <s>Śrīmatī</s>, disregarding her own life and recollecting the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>, made a garland of lamps at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s>. Then, killed by the enraged King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, she generated serene faith in me, died, and was reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. She came to my presence this night. I taught her the <s>Dharma</s>, and having seen the truth, she returned to her own abode. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship the Teacher. Having honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon him." Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_55 vastram* | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_55: <s>Vastram</s> (Cloth). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | yadā anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā buddhapramukhāya bhikṣusaṃghāya jetavanaṃ niryātitam*, krameṇa {ca} koṭiśataṃ bhagavacchāsane dattam*, tadā tasya buddhir abhavat*: kim atrāścaryaṃ yad ahaṃ dānāni dadāmi, puṇyāni vā karomi, yanv ahaṃ daridrajanānugrahārthṃ śrāvastīnivāsino janakāyāc chandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham upatiṣṭheyam* | evaṃ me mahājanānugrahaḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati, bahu cānena puṇyaṃ prasūtaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā eṣa vṛttānto rājñe niveditaḥ | rājñā sarvasyāṃ śrāvastyāṃ ghaṇṭāghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam*: śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ śrāvastīnivāsinaḥ paurāḥ | adya saptame divase anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir hastiskandhābhirūḍhas tathāgatasya saśrāvakasaṃghasyārthāya cchandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ | yasya vo yan mātraṃ parityaktaṃ tad anupradātavyam iti | yāvat saptame divase anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir hastiskandhādhirūḍhas tathāgatasya saśrāvakasaṃghasyārthāya chandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kartuṃ pravṛttam* | tatra yeṣāṃ yan mātro vibhavas te tan mātraṃ dātuṃ pravṛttāḥ | kecid dhāraṃ prayacchanti, kecit kaṭakam*, kecit keyūram*, kecij jātarūpamālām*,
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. When the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> had donated <s>Jetavana</s> to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, and had gradually given a hundred <s>koṭis</s> (billions) in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s dispensation, this thought occurred to him: 'What is so wonderful about my giving gifts and making merit? Rather, let me, for the benefit of the poor, solicit voluntary contributions from the populace of <s>Śrāvastī</s> and with those attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples. In this way, a great service to the multitude will be accomplished, and by this much merit will be generated.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> reported this plan to the king. The king had a bell-proclamation made throughout all of <s>Śrāvastī</s>: 'Let the honorable citizens of <s>Śrāvastī</s> hear! Seven days from today, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, mounted on the back of an elephant, wishes to make a voluntary collection for the benefit of the <s>Tathāgata</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples. Whatever each of you can afford to part with, that should be given.' On the seventh day, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, mounted on the back of an elephant, set out to make the voluntary collection for the <s>Tathāgata</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples. There, those who possessed whatever measure of wealth began to give accordingly. Some gave necklaces, some bracelets, some armlets, some gold garlands,

children.text:
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 140 --------------------
kecid aṅgulimudrām*, kecin muktāhāram*, kecid dhiraṇyam*, kecit suvarṇam*, kecid antaśaḥ kārṣāpaṇam* | gṛhapatir api parānugrahārthaṃ pratigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: some finger-rings, some pearl necklaces, some silver, some gold, and some even a single <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> (coin). The householder accepted [everything] for the benefit of others.

children.text: yāvad anyatamā strī paramadaridrā | tayā tribhir māsaiḥ kṛcchreṇa paṭaka upārjitaḥ | sā taṃ paṭakaṃ prāvṛtya vīthīm avatīrṇā | anāthapiṇḍadaś ca tayā dūrata evāgacchan*, śaṅkhapaṭahair vādyamānair avalokitaḥ | tayānyatama upāsakaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ: yadi tāvad ayaṃ gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhoho 'ntarbhūmau nigūḍhāny api nidhānāni paśyati, kasmād ayaṃ parakulebhyo bhaikṣyam aṭatīti | sā upāsakenoktā: parānugrahārtham* | ye 'samamarthā bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojayitum*, teṣām arthe 'nugrahaṃ karoti | kathaṃ bahavaḥ sametā bhagavantaṃ pratipādayeyur iti | tatas tayā dārikāyā buddhir utpannā: ahaṃ tāvad akṛtapuṇyā, na me śaktir asti, yad aham ekākinī bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojanena pratipādayeyam* | yanv aham atra kiṃcid anupradadyām iti | sā svakaṃ vibhavam avalokayantī na kiṃcit paśyati ṛte paṭakāt* | sā cintayituṃ pravṛttā: yady aham ihasthaiva paṭakaṃ pradāsyāmi, nagnā bhaviṣyāmi | yanv ahaṃ śaraṇapṛṣṭham abhiruhya paṭakaṃ kṣipeyam iti | tataḥ sā śaraṇapṛṣṭham abhiruhya svaśarīrāt paṭakam avanīya anāthapiṇḍadasyopari kṣiptavatī | sā gṛhapatinā saṃlakṣitā: nūnam asyā eṣa eva vibhavo yad anayā śaraṇasaṃsthayā kṣiptam iti | tena svapauruṣeyāṇām ājñānupradattā | gacchantu bhavantaḥ, avalokayantu kenāyaṃ paṭakaḥ kṣipta iti | tair avalokitā yāvad utkuṭukā niṣaṇṇā | tatas taiḥ pṛṣṭā | tayā coktam*: yo me vibhava āsīt sa me bhagavadguṇānukīrtanaṃ pratiśrutya dāridryabhayabhītayā (Speyer: dāridrabhayabhītayā) tathāgatapramukhe bhikṣusaṃghe datta iti | tatas tair anāthapiṇḍadāya niveditam* | tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā paramavismayajātenā sā dārikā vicitrair vastrair ābharaṇaiś cācchāditā | sā cālpāyuṣkā kālagatā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā | upapannamātrāyās tasyās tathāvidhāni vastrāṇi prādurbhūtāni, na kasyacid anyasya devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā ||
children.translated_text: Now there was a certain woman who was extremely poor. Over three months, with great difficulty, she had earned a single piece of cloth. She wrapped herself in that cloth and came down to the street. <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, approaching from afar, was seen by her amid the sounding of conches and drums. She asked a certain lay devotee: 'If this householder is so wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions — who can even see treasures hidden underground — why is he begging from other families?' The lay devotee said to her: 'For the benefit of others. Those who are unable to feed the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples on their own — for their sake he acts charitably, so that many may combine to provide for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then this thought arose in the girl: 'I am one who has not made merit; I do not have the means to feed the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples on my own. Let me contribute something here.' Looking over her own possessions, she saw nothing except the cloth. She began to reflect: 'If I give the cloth while standing here, I shall be naked. Let me rather climb onto a rooftop and throw the cloth down.' Then she climbed onto a rooftop, removed the cloth from her body, and threw it down upon <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. The householder took note: 'Surely this is her entire wealth, since she, standing on a rooftop, threw it.' He gave orders to his servants: 'Go, sirs, and find out who threw this cloth.' They looked and saw her sitting crouched [naked]. They questioned her. She said: 'Whatever wealth I had — having heard the praise of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s virtues and out of fear of poverty — I have given it to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then his servants reported this to <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, filled with the utmost wonder, covered that girl with fine garments and ornaments. She, being of short lifespan, died and was reborn among the exalted gods of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. The moment she was reborn, garments of such a kind appeared for her as existed for no other <s>Devaputra</s> or <s>Devakanyā</s>.

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | sā paśyati: manuṣyebhyaś cyutā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā, bhagavataḥ paṭakapradānād iti | tato vastradāyikā devakanyā calavimalakuṇḍaladharā hārārdhahāravirājitagātrī maṇiratnavicitracūḍā kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātrī tām eva rātriṃ divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇām puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ jetavanam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān paṭakapradāyikāyā devakanyāyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā paṭakapradāyikāyā devakanyāyā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sā dṛṣṭasatyā trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or a <s>Devakanyā</s> has recently been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' She saw: 'I have passed away from the human realm, I have been reborn among the exalted gods of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, by the gift of cloth to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then the cloth-giving <s>Devakanyā</s> — wearing gleaming, pure earrings, her body resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, her crown adorned with various gems and jewels, her body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, musk, and other fragrances — on that very night, having filled her lap with divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> flowers, illuminating the entire <s>Jetavana</s> with a magnificent radiance, showering the <s>Bhagavān</s> with flowers, she sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature of the cloth-giving <s>Devakanyā</s>, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which the cloth-giving <s>Devakanyā</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) that rises to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, she thrice uttered this inspired exclamation: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by those deceased before us, nor by ascetics and brahmins — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us:

children.text: kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been surmounted, the doors to the lower realms have been closed, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and humans.' And she said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: 'By your power, the terrifying

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path to the lower realms, fraught with many faults, has been blocked;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: the meritorious path to heaven has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_55.1 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found by me.' // AVŚ_55.1 //

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer:suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇā ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_55.2 ||
children.translated_text: I have reached the peaceful state beloved by the noble ones, and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.' // AVŚ_55.2 //

'By relying on you, I have today attained
pure vision, free from fault, supremely clear;

children.text: naravarendra narāmarapūjita
children.translated_text: 'O best of men, worshipped by humans and gods,

children.text: vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayaṃ |
children.translated_text: free from birth, old age, death, and disease —

children.text: bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
children.translated_text: O Sage, whose sight is so difficult to obtain in a thousand existences,

children.text: saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_55.3 ||
children.translated_text: today the sight of you has borne fruit!' // AVŚ_55.3 //

children.text: avanamya tataḥ pralambahārā
children.translated_text: 'Then, bowing down with her pendulous garlands,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣā |
children.translated_text: having reverenced both feet, filled with joy,

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: having circumambulated to the right the Conqueror of Foes,

children.text: suralokābhimukhī divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_55.4 ||
children.translated_text: she departed heavenward, facing the world of the gods.' // AVŚ_55.4 //

children.text: atha paṭapradāyikā devakanyā vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ, sasyasaṃpanna iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatā tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: Then the cloth-giving <s>Devakanyā</s>, like a merchant who has gained his profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won his battle, like a sick person freed from all disease — with the very same splendor with which she had come into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, she returned to her own abode.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ | yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhagavann asyāṃ rātrau bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | yā daridradārikā anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateś chandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kurvāṇasya paṭaṃ datvā kālagatā, praṇīteṣū deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannā, sā imāṃ rātriṃ matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | tasyā mayā dharmo deśitaḥ | sā prasādajātā prakrāntā, dṛṣṭasatyā ca svabhavanaṃ gatā | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava evaṃ śikṣitavyam: yad buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu kārān kariṣyāmo nāpakārān* | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw the magnificent radiance in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Having seen it, filled with doubt, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> this night?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. That poor girl who gave cloth during the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s voluntary collection, having died, was reborn among the exalted gods of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. She came to my presence this night. I taught her the <s>Dharma</s>. Filled with faith, she departed, and having seen the truth, she returned to her own abode. Therefore, monks, you should train thus: "We shall render service to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, not disservice." Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_56 śukaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_56: <s>Śuka</s> (The Parrot). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | rājagṛhe nagare rājā bimbisāro rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | sa ca rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless. He guarded the kingdom as though it were his only son. And that king was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition,

children.text: ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ | yāvad asau bhagavaddarśanotkaṇṭhitaḥ kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ | tato 'mātyar uktaḥ: kimarthaṃ deva śokaḥ kriyata iti | rājovāca: ciradṛṣṭo me sugataḥ | so 'ham ākāṅkṣāmi bhagavato darśanam iti | aśrauṣīd bhagavān divāvihāropagato divyena śrotreṇa viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣeṇa rājā bimbisāra utkaṇṭhita iti | atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛtt{ak}ānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ, kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasya kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anupradadyām*, kam āryadhanavirahitam āryadhanaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, <kasyājñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrasya jñānāñjanaśalākayā cakṣur viśodhayāmi |> kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, fond of the <s>Dharma</s>, affectionate toward his subjects. Now he was longing for the sight of the Blessed One, and resting his cheek upon his hand, he stood absorbed in thought. Then a minister asked: 'Why does Your Majesty grieve?' The king said: 'It has been long since I saw the <s>Sugata</s>. I yearn for the sight of the Blessed One.' The Blessed One, while in his daytime retreat, heard with his divine ear — purified and surpassing the human — that King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was yearning. Meanwhile, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unperceived, or uncomprehended by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. For it is the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones — greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, single-minded in their protection, dwelling in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three grounds of discipline, having crossed the four floods, well-established in the practice of the four bases of supernatural power, long-practiced in the four means of attraction, having abandoned the five hindrances, having transcended the five destinies, endowed with six qualities, having perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s>, adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, guides to the Eightfold Path, skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, mighty with the ten powers, their fame filling the ten directions, distinguished among rulers of a thousand [worlds] — three times at night and three times during the day, surveying the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, their knowledge-and-vision operates: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into straits? Who has fallen into difficulty, distress, and straits? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who tends toward the lower realms? Who is heading toward the lower realms? Whom shall I, having lifted from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? To whom, sunk in the mire of sensual desires, shall I extend a hand to lift them out? Whom, deprived of the noble treasures, shall I establish in the sovereignty of the noble treasures? Whose eyes, covered with the film of the darkness of ignorance, shall I cleanse with the collyrium-stick of knowledge? For whom shall I plant roots of merit not yet planted? For whom shall I bring to maturity roots of merit already planted? For whom shall I liberate roots of merit already matured?' And he said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its boundary,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_56.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the proper time for those to be trained, his spiritual offspring.' // AVŚ_56.1 //

children.text: tato bhagavān rājño bimbisārasyānugrahārthaṃ trayāṇāṃ vārṣikāṇāṃ māsānām atyayāt kṛtacīvaro niṣṭḥitacīvaraḥ samādāya pātracīvaram janapadacārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ | anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ carann anyatamaṃ vanaṣaṇḍam anuprāptaḥ | tatra ca vanaṣaṇḍe manuṣyapralāpī śukaḥ prativasati | tena bhagavān dūrata dṛṣṭaḥ | tatas tvaritatvaritaṃ bhagavantam uvāca: etu bhagavān, svāgataṃ bhagavate, kriyatām asmākam anugrahaḥ, ihaiva vanaṣaṇḍe ekāṃ rātriṃ prativaseti | tato bhagavāñ chukasyānugrahārthaṃ yatra vkṣe śukasyālayas tatra tṛṇasaṃstaraṃ saṃstīrya paryaṅkeṇa niṣaṇṇaḥ, anyavṛkṣeṣu mahāśrāvakāḥ, tataḥ śukaḥ kṛtsnāṃ rātrim itas tatas taṃ vanaṣaṇḍaṃ paryaṭati, mā haiva kaścid bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ viheṭhayiṣyatīti manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā yakṣo vā rākṣaso vā śvāpadaś caṇḍaśṛṅgo veti | tataḥ prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ bhagavantaṃ triḥpradakṣīṇīkṛtya kṣamayitum ārabdhaḥ | kṣamasva bhagavaṃs tiryagyonigato 'ham*, nāsti me vibhavo yena bhagavantam abhyarcayeyam*, api tv aham agrato gacchāmi | rājño bimbisārasya bhagavata āgamanaṃ nivedayāmīti | evam astv iti | yāvad asau rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ | anupūrveṇa rājñaḥ sakāśam anuprāptam* | tasmiṃś ca samaye rājā upariprāsādatalagato niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tataḥ śuko mānuṣapralāpī rājānam uvāca | bho rājan*, viditaṃ te bhavatu: bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghas
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, for the benefit of King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, after the passing of the three months of the rainy season, having made his robe and completed his robe, taking his bowl and robe, set out on a wandering tour of the countryside. Wandering in due course, he arrived at a certain forest grove. And in that forest grove there dwelt a parrot that could speak in human language. He saw the Blessed One from afar. Then, hurrying quickly, he said to the Blessed One: 'Let the Blessed One come! Welcome to the Blessed One! Grant us your favor — please stay for one night in this very forest grove.' Then the Blessed One, for the benefit of the parrot, spread a grass mat at the foot of the tree where the parrot had his nest and sat down cross-legged; the great disciples [settled] in other trees. Then the parrot wandered throughout that forest grove the entire night, this way and that, [watching] lest anyone — whether human or non-human, <s>yakṣa</s> or <s>rākṣasa</s>, wild beast or fierce-horned animal — should trouble the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks. Then, when the night had passed, the parrot circumambulated the Blessed One three times and began to ask forgiveness: 'Forgive me, Blessed One — I am born in the animal realm and have no wealth with which to honor the Blessed One. But I shall go ahead and inform King <s>Bimbisāra</s> of the Blessed One's arrival.' 'So be it.' Thereupon he set out toward the king. In due course he arrived at the king's presence. At that time, the king, having ascended to the upper terrace of his palace, was sporting, enjoying himself, and amusing himself with instrumental music in private. Then the parrot, speaking in human language, said to the king: 'O king, know this: the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 143]

children.text: tava vijitam anuprāptaḥ | tad arhati devo bhaktaṃ sajjīkartum iti | tato rājā tvaritatvaritaṃ prāsādād avatīryāmātyagaṇaparivṛto bhagavato 'rthena āsanakāni prajñapya chatradhvajapatākābhir vicitraiś ca gandhapuṣpadhūpair bhagavantaṃ pratyudgataḥ | tato rājñā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho mahatā satkāreṇa praveśitaḥ, praṇītena cāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has arrived in your domain. Therefore, Your Majesty should prepare a meal.' Then the king, hurrying quickly, descended from his palace and, surrounded by his retinue of ministers, having set up seats, having decorated with parasols, banners, and flags, and with various incense, flowers, and perfumes, went out to welcome the Blessed One. Then the king received the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks with great honor, and satisfied them with excellent food.

children.text: atha śukasyaitad abhavat*: yad bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgha evaṃvibhūtis tat sarvaṃ māmāgamya | iti viditvā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita udagraprītisaumanasyajāto rājñaḥ purastād itaś cāmutaś ca paryaṭan* śyenakenāpahṛtya pañcatvam āpāditaḥ | bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādya kālagataḥ | praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to the parrot: 'That the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks enjoys such splendor — all of this is because of me.' Knowing this, joyful, delighted, pleased, elated with rapture and happiness, he was flying about this way and that before the king when he was seized by a hawk and killed. Having generated faith in the Blessed One, he died and was reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | sa paśyati: tiryagbhyaś cyutaḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādyeti | atha śukapūrviṇo devaputrasyaitad abhavat*: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāso bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam* | yanv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | atha śukapūrvī devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravirājitagātro maṇiratnavicitracūḍaḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātras tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇām puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ jetavanam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavāṃś chukapūrviṇo devaputrasyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā śukapūrviṇā devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or a <s>Devakanyā</s> has been newly reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what deed?'
