He perceived: 'I have passed away from the animal realm and have been reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, by generating faith in the Blessed One.' Then this thought occurred to the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot: 'It would not be fitting for me to approach the Blessed One for an audience after having rested overnight. Rather, let me approach the Blessed One for an audience without having rested overnight.' Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot — wearing shimmering, spotless earrings, his body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, his crown studded with jewels and precious gems, his body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, and <s>spṛkkā</s> — that very night, having filled his lap with divine flowers of <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>mandārava</s>, illuminated the entire <s>Jetavana</s> with his brilliant radiance, scattered flowers upon the Blessed One, and sat down before the Blessed One to hear the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, inclination, nature, and character of the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot, delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> leading to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body), rising with its twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (Stream-entry). Having seen the truth, he uttered this exclamation three times: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, not by our father, not by a king, not by the gods, not by beloved kinsmen and relatives, not by departed ancestors, not by <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — what the Blessed One has done for us! The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been crossed over, the doors to the lower realms have been shut, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and men!' And he said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: 'By your power, the dreadful

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path of the lower realms, full of many faults, has been closed.

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: The path to heaven, rich in merit, has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_56.2 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found by me.' // AVŚ_56.2 //

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer: suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_56.3 ||
children.translated_text: and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.' // AVŚ_56.3 //

'By relying on you, I have today obtained
the pure, supremely purified eye [of the <s>Dharma</s>], free from faults.
I have attained the peaceful state, dear to the Noble Ones,

children.text: naravarendra narāmarapūjita
children.translated_text: 'O best of men, worshipped by humans, gods, and <s>asuras</s>,

children.text: vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayaṃ |
children.translated_text: free from birth, old age, death, and disease,

children.text: bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
children.translated_text: whose sight is so hard to obtain in a thousand lifetimes —

children.text: saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_56.4 ||
children.translated_text: today, O Sage, your sight has been fruitful.' // AVŚ_56.4 //

children.text: avanamya tataḥ pralambahāraś
children.translated_text: Then, bowing low, wearing his pendant necklace,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: he worshipped both feet, filled with joy.

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: Having circumambulated the Conqueror of foes to the right,

children.text: suralokābhimukho divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_56.5 ||
children.translated_text: he departed toward the world of the gods, facing heaven.' // AVŚ_56.5 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 144]

children.text: atha śukapūrvī devaputro vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ, sasyasaṃpanna iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatas tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot — like a merchant who has gained his profit, like a farmer whose crop has ripened, like a warrior who has won his battle, like a sick man freed from all disease — with the very same splendor with which he had come to the Blessed One's presence, returned to his own abode.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ | yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhagavann asyāṃ rātrau bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | api tu dṛṣṭaḥ sa yuṣmābhiḥ śuko yena vayaṃ tasmin vanaṣaṇḍe rātriṃ vastum upanimintritā iti? bhikṣava ūcuḥ: evaṃ bhadanteti | bhagavān āha: sa eṣa bhikṣavaḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā, praṇīteṣū deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapanna iti | bhikṣava ūcuḥ: kāni bhadanta śukapūrvakeṇa devaputreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni yena śukeṣūpapannaḥ, kāni karmāṇi kṛtāni yena deveṣūpapannaḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: śukapūrvakeṇaiva bhikṣavo devaputreṇa pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | śukapūrvakeṇa devaputreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw a magnificent radiance in the Blessed One's presence. Having seen it, filled with doubt, they asked the Blessed One: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the Blessed One this night, Blessed One?' The Blessed One said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. But did you see that parrot by whom we were invited to spend the night in that forest grove?' The monks said: 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' The Blessed One said: 'That parrot, monks, having died, was reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.' The monks asked: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot perform that he was reborn among parrots? And what deeds did he perform that he was reborn among the gods and gained the vision of truth?' The Blessed One said: 'It was the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot himself, monks, who in former births performed and accumulated deeds, whose requisite conditions had matured, whose causes had ripened, which stood before him like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass. The <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a parrot performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their results]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_56.6 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_56.6 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati sma | tasyānyatama upāsakaḥ | tena śikṣāśaithilyaṃ kṛtam* | tasya karmaṇo vipākāc chukeṣūpapannaḥ | yan mayāntike cittaṃ prasāditam*, tena deveṣūpapannaḥ | yat tena pariṣiṣṭāni śikṣāpadāni rakṣitāni, tena satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. A certain lay-follower of his became lax in his training. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he was reborn among parrots. Because he had purified his mind in my presence, he was reborn among the gods. Because he had kept the remaining precepts, he attained the vision of truth. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 145]

children.text: AVŚ_57 dūtaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_57: <s>Dūta</s> (The Messenger). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛhe varṣā upagato veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | atha anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir yena rājā prasenajit kauśalas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ prasenajitaṃ jayenāyuṣā ca vardhayitvā vijñāpayati: yat khalu deva jānīyāś ciradṛṣṭo 'smābhir bhagavān* | paritṛṣitāḥ smo bhagavato darśanāya | icchāmo vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ draṣṭum iti | tato rājā anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim uvāca: kaccit te gṛhapate śrutaṃ kutra bhagavān etarhi varṣā upagata iti? anāthapiṇḍada uvāca: śrutaṃ me deva bhagavān rājagṛhe varṣā upagata iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, had entered the rains-retreat at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> approached King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>. Having approached, and having congratulated the king with wishes for victory and long life, he petitioned: 'May the lord know that it has been long since we have seen the Blessed One. We are thirsting for a sight of the Blessed One. We wish to see the Blessed One.' Then the king said to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'Have you heard, householder, where the Blessed One has entered the rains-retreat?' <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said: 'I have heard, lord, that the Blessed One has entered the rains-retreat at <s>Rājagṛha</s>.'

children.text: tato rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena anāthapiṇḍadādyaiś ca paurajānapadāmātyair anyatamaḥ puruṣo dūtyenāhūyoktaḥ: ehi tvaṃ bho puruṣa, yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāma | upasaṃkramyāsmākaṃ vacanena bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandasva, alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛccha alpātaṅkaṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca | evaṃ ca vada: rājā bhadanta kauśalaḥ śrāvastīnivāsinaś ca paurā ākāṅkṣanti bhagavato darśanam* | evaṃ cāhuḥ: ciradṛṣṭo 'smābhir bhagavān* | paritṛṣitāḥ smo bhagavato darśanāya | ichāmo vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ draṣṭum* | sādhu bhagavāñ chrāvastīm āgacched anukampām upādāyeti | evaṃ deveti sa puruṣo rājñaḥ prasenajitaḥ kauśalasya sāmātyapaurajānapadasya pratiśrutya śrāvastīto 'nupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇo rājagṛhaṃ nagaram anuprāptaḥ | tataḥ pūrvaṃ rājagṛhaṃ nagaram avalokya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekāntaniṣaṇṇaḥ sa puruṣo bhagavantam idam avocat*: rājā bhadanta prasenajit kauśalaḥ śrāvastīnivāsinaś ca paurā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā alpābādhatāṃ pṛcchanti, alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca | evaṃ cāhuḥ: ciradṛṣṭo 'smābhir bhagavān* | paritṛṣitāḥ smo bhagavato darśanāya | ichāmo vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ draṣṭum* | sādhu bhagavāñ chrāvastīm āgacched anukampām upādāyeti | bhagavān āha: sacen me bhoḥ puruṣa rājā bimbisāro 'nujñāsyati; gamiṣyāmīti | tataḥ sa dūto rājānaṃ bimbisāram anujñāpya bhagavantam idam avocat*: anujñāto 'si bhagavan rājñā bimbisāreṇa gamanāya, yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyata iti | adhivāsayati bhagavāṃs tasya puruṣasya tūṣṇībhāvena ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, together with <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> and the other citizens, countryfolk, and ministers, summoned a certain man as a messenger and said: 'Come, good man, go to the Blessed One. Having approached, in our name worship the Blessed One's feet with your head, and inquire about his health — whether he is free from ailment, free from affliction, light in rising, comfortable in his movements, strong, well, blameless, and at ease in his dwelling. And say thus: "King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, Venerable Sir, and the citizens dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> long to see the Blessed One. And they say: 'It has been long since we have seen the Blessed One. We are thirsting for a sight of the Blessed One. We wish to see the Blessed One. It would be well if the Blessed One would come to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, out of compassion.'"' 'Yes, my lord,' that man replied to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> together with his ministers, citizens, and countryfolk, and setting out from <s>Śrāvastī</s>, wandering by stages, he arrived at the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Having first surveyed the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached and worshipped the Blessed One's feet with his head, he sat to one side. Seated to one side, that man said this to the Blessed One: 'King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, Venerable Sir, and the citizens dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> worship the Blessed One's feet with their heads and inquire about your health — whether you are free from ailment, free from affliction, light in rising, comfortable in your movements, strong, well, blameless, and at ease in your dwelling. And they say: "It has been long since we have seen the Blessed One. We are thirsting for a sight of the Blessed One. We wish to see the Blessed One. It would be well if the Blessed One would come to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, out of compassion."' The Blessed One said: 'Good man, if King <s>Bimbisāra</s> grants me permission, I shall go.' Then that messenger, having obtained permission from King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, said this to the Blessed One: 'You have been given permission by King <s>Bimbisāra</s> to depart. May the Blessed One go whenever he sees fit.' The Blessed One consented to that man by his silence.

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs trayāṇāṃ vārṣikāṇāṃ māsānām atyayāt kṛtacīvaro niṣṭhitacīvaraḥ samādāya pātracīvaraṃ mahatā parivāreṇa śrāvastyabhimukho 'bhijagāma | dūto 'pi rathābhirūḍhaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ padbhyāṃ saṃprasthitam* | tato rathād avatīrya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocat*: pratigṛhyatāṃ bhagavann asmākīno ratho 'nukampām upādāyeti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, after the passage of the three months of the rains-retreat, having prepared his robe, taking his bowl and robe, set out toward <s>Śrāvastī</s> with a great retinue. The messenger too set forth, mounted on a chariot. Then he saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, proceeding on foot. He descended from his chariot, and joining his palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'Please accept our chariot, Blessed One, out of compassion.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 146]

children.text: bhagavān āha:
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

children.text:
ṛddhipādarathenāhaṃ samyagvyāyāmavartinā |
  vicarāmi mahīṃ kṛtsnām akṣataḥ kleśakaṇṭhakaiḥ || AVŚ_57.1 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'On the chariot of the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), proceeding with right effort,
I traverse the entire earth, unharmed by the thorns of the <s>kleśas</s> (defilements).' // AVŚ_57.1 //

children.text: dūtaḥ prāha: yady api bhagavān ṛddhipādayānayāyī; tathāpi tu kriyatāṃ mamānugrahārtham anukampeti | atha bhagavān dūtasyānugrahārtham ṛddhyā rathasyopari sthitaḥ | tato bhagavān rathābhirūḍhaḥ śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ | dūtena ca rājñe niveditam* | atha rājā sāmātyaḥ sapaurajānapado bhagavantaṃ pratyudgataḥ | tatraiva ca jetavane rātriṃvāsam upagato dharmaśravaṇāya | sa ca dūto 'lpāyuṣko dharmaṃ śrutvā tasyām eva rātrau kālagataḥ | sa kālaṃ kṛtvā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The messenger said: 'Even though the Blessed One travels by the vehicle of the <s>ṛddhipādas</s>, still, please do so for the sake of blessing me, out of compassion.' Then the Blessed One, for the sake of blessing the messenger, stood upon the chariot by supernatural power. Then the Blessed One, mounted on the chariot, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The messenger reported this to the king. Then the king, together with his ministers, citizens, and countryfolk, came out to meet the Blessed One. Right there in the <s>Jetavana</s>, [the messenger] took up lodging for the night to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And that messenger, being short-lived, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, died on that very night. Having died, he was reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven.

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | sa paśyati: manuṣyebhyaś cyutaḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādyeti | atha dūtapūrviṇo devaputrasyaitad abhavat*: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāso bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam* | yanv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | atha dūtapūrvī devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravirājitagātro maṇiratnavicitracūḍaḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātras tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇām puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ jetavanam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān dūtapūrviṇo devaputrasyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā dūtapūrviṇā devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that for a <s>Devaputra</s> or <s>Devakanyā</s> newly reborn [in heaven], three thoughts arise: 'From where did I pass away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' He saw: 'Having passed away from among humans, I have been reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, through having purified my mind in the presence of the Blessed One.' Then this thought arose in the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been the messenger: 'It would not be proper for me, having spent the night, to approach the Blessed One for an audience. Rather, let me approach the Blessed One without having spent the night.' Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been the messenger — wearing gleaming, pure earrings, his body resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, his crown adorned with various jewels and gems, his body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, and other fragrances — on that very night, having filled his lap with divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> flowers, illuminated the entire <s>Jetavana</s> with a magnificent radiance, scattered flowers over the Blessed One, and sat before the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, having known the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been the messenger's disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been the messenger shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he thrice uttered this joyful exclamation: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by kings, nor by gods, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by departed ancestors, nor by <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — what the Blessed One has done for us! The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been transcended, the doors to the woeful states have been shut, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and humans.' And he said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: 'By your power, the terrible

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path of the woeful states, fraught with many faults, has been shut.

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: 'The meritorious path to heaven has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_57.2 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been obtained by me.' // AVŚ_57.2 //

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer: suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_57.3 ||
children.translated_text: and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.' // AVŚ_57.3 //

children.text: naravarendra narāmarapūjita
children.translated_text: 'O best of men, worshipped by humans and gods,

children.text: vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayaṃ |
children.translated_text: free from birth, old age, death, and disease,

children.text: bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
children.translated_text: whose sight is hard to obtain in thousands of existences —

children.text: saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_57.4 ||
children.translated_text: fruitful indeed, O Sage, is your vision today!' // AVŚ_57.4 //

children.text: avanamya tataḥ pralambahāraś
children.translated_text: Then, bowing with his dangling necklace,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: having worshipped both feet, filled with joy,

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: and having circumambulated the Conqueror of Enemies to the right,

children.text: suralokābhimukho divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_57.5 ||
children.translated_text: he departed toward the realm of the gods, ascending to heaven. // AVŚ_57.5 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 147]

children.text: atha dūtapūrvī devaputro vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ, sasyasaṃpanna iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ, sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā hi vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatas tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been the messenger — like a merchant who has gained profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won the battle, like a sick man freed from all diseases — with the same splendor with which he had come to the Blessed One's presence, returned to his own celestial abode.

children.text: tato rājā prasenajid upariprāsādatalagatas tam udāram avabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ bhagavantaṃ papracha: kiṃ bhagavann imāṃ rātriṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na mahārāja brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ, api tu tāvako dūtaḥ sa mamāntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagataḥ praṇīteṣū deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ | sa imāṃ rātriṃ matsakāśam āgataḥ | tasya mayā dharmo deśitaḥ | sa dṛṣṭasatyaḥ svabhavanaṃ gata iti | tato rājā vismayajātaḥ kathayati: aho buddho aho dharmaḥ aho saṃgho yatra nāma parīttaṃ karma kṛtvā mahān vipāka iti | atha rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Prasenajit</s>, from the upper floor of his palace, seeing that magnificent radiance, asked the Blessed One at dawn: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the Blessed One this night, Blessed One?' The Blessed One said: 'No, great king, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. Rather, that messenger of yours — he, having purified his mind in my presence, died and was reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. He came to my presence this night. I taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen the truth, he returned to his own celestial abode.' Then the king, filled with wonder, said: 'Oh, the <s>Buddha</s>! Oh, the <s>Dharma</s>! Oh, the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Where even a small deed performed yields a great result!' Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, having rejoiced at and approved the Blessed One's words, having worshipped the Blessed One's feet with his head, rose from his seat and departed.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: tisra imā bhikṣavo 'graprajñaptayaḥ | katamās tisraḥ? buddhe agraprajñaptir dharme saṃghe 'graprajñaptiḥ | buddhe 'graprajñaptiḥ katamā? ye kecid satvā apadā vā dvipadā vā bahupadā vā rūpiṇo vā arūpiṇo va saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñinaḥ, tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ | ye kecid buddhe 'bhiprasannāḥ, agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ | teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām* | iyam ucyate buddhe 'graprajñaptiḥ | dharme 'graprajñaptiḥ katamā? ye kecid dharmāḥ saṃskṛtā vā asaṃskṛtā vā, virāgo dharmas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ | ye kecid dharme 'bhiprasannā, agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ | teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām* | iyam ucyate dharme agraprajñaptiḥ | saṃghe 'graprajñaptiḥ katamā? ye kecit saṃghā vā gaṇā vā pūgā vā pariṣado vā, tathāgataśrāvakasaṃghas teṣām agra ākhyātaḥ | ye kecit saṃghe 'bhiprasannāḥ, agre te 'bhiprasannāḥ | teṣām agre 'bhiprasannānām agra eva vipākaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyo deveṣu vā devabhūtānāṃ manuṣyeṣu vā manuṣyabhūtānām* | iyam ucyate saṃghe agraprajñaptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'There are, monks, these three supreme designations (<s>agraprajñapti</s>). What three? The supreme designation regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, the supreme designation regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, and the supreme designation regarding the <s>Saṃgha</s>. What is the supreme designation regarding the <s>Buddha</s>? Whatever beings there are — footless, two-footed, or many-footed, with form or without form, with perception, without perception, or neither with nor without perception — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> is declared supreme among them. Those who have faith in the <s>Buddha</s> have faith in the supreme. For those who have faith in the supreme, a supreme result is to be expected — among the gods for those who become gods, among humans for those who become humans. This is called the supreme designation regarding the <s>Buddha</s>. What is the supreme designation regarding the <s>Dharma</s>? Whatever phenomena there are, whether conditioned or unconditioned, dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) is declared supreme among them. Those who have faith in the <s>Dharma</s> have faith in the supreme. For those who have faith in the supreme, a supreme result is to be expected — among the gods for those who become gods, among humans for those who become humans. This is called the supreme designation regarding the <s>Dharma</s>. What is the supreme designation regarding the <s>Saṃgha</s>? Whatever assemblies, groups, guilds, or communities there are, the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples is declared supreme among them. Those who have faith in the <s>Saṃgha</s> have faith in the supreme. For those who have faith in the supreme, a supreme result is to be expected — among the gods for those who become gods, among humans for those who become humans. This is called the supreme designation regarding the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_58 mahiṣaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_58: <s>Mahiṣa</s> (The Buffalo). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 148]

children.text: saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kośaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ carann anyatamavanaṣaṇḍam anuprāptaḥ | tatra ca vanaṣaṇḍe mahān mahiṣīyūthaḥ prativasati, pañcamātrāṇi ca mahiṣīpālaśatāni | yāvat tatrānyatamo mahiṣo balavān parameṇa balena samanvāgataḥ | sa paramanuṣyāṇāṃ gandham āghrāya pṛṣṭhato 'nudhāvati | bhagavāṃś ca taṃ pradeśam anuprāpatḥ | tato mahiṣīpālair bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho dūrata eva dṛṣṭaḥ | tatas tair uccaiḥ śabdair uktaḥ: bhagavan, imaṃ mārgaṃ varjaya, duṣṭamahiṣo 'tra prativasatīti | bhagavān āha: alpotsukā bhavantu bhavantaḥ | vayam atra kālajñā bhaviṣyāma iti | athāsau duṣṭamahiṣo bhagavantaṃ dūrata eva dṛṣṭvā lāṅgūlam unnāmya yena bhagavāṃs tena pradhāvitaḥ | tato bhagavatā purastāt pañca kesariṇaḥ saṭādhāriṇaḥ (Speyer: keśariṇaḥ saṭadhāriṇaḥ) siṃhā nirmitāḥ, vāme dakṣiṇe ca pārśve dvāv agniskandhau, upariṣṭān mahatyayomayī śilā | tataḥ sa mahiṣaḥ samantato mahābhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavataḥ pādau niśritya dīnavadanaś ca bhagavantaṃ prekṣyate (Speyer: prekṣate) | tato 'sya bhagavatā tanmayyā gatyās tanmayyā yonyās tribhiḥ pādair dharmo deśitaḥ: iti hi bhadramukha sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ, sarvadharmā anātmānaḥ, śāntaṃ nirvāṇam iti | jātiś ca smāritā | sa śrutvā rodituṃ pravṛttaḥ | atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthe bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: together with the community of disciples, while wandering on tour through the <s>Kośala</s> territories, arrived at a certain forest grove. In that forest grove there dwelt a great herd of buffalo, together with about five hundred buffalo herders. Now among them was a certain buffalo that was mighty, endowed with supreme strength. Having caught the scent of a man beyond the ordinary, he would charge in pursuit. The <s>Bhagavān</s> arrived at that place. The buffalo herders saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of disciples from afar. They called out loudly: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, avoid this path! A vicious buffalo dwells here!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do not be concerned, good sirs. We shall know the right moment here.' Then that vicious buffalo, seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar, raised his tail and charged toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> conjured before him five maned lions bearing full manes (Speyer: <s>keśariṇaḥ saṭadhāriṇaḥ</s>), on the left and right sides two masses of fire, and above a great iron boulder. Then that buffalo, seeing great danger all around, took refuge at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and with a pitiful face gazed upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in a manner suited to that animal's state and birth, taught him the <s>Dharma</s> in three padas: 'Thus, friend, all conditioned things are impermanent; all phenomena are without self; <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is peace.' And he reminded him of his [former] birth. Upon hearing this, the buffalo began to weep. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: idānīṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmi tiryagyonigatasya te |
children.translated_text: What can I do for you now, reborn in the animal realm?

children.text: akṣaṇapratipannasya kiṃ rodiṣi nirarthakam* || AVŚ_58.1 ||
children.translated_text: You who have fallen upon an unfavorable occasion — what use is weeping in vain? // AVŚ_58.1 //

children.text:
sādhu prasādyatāṃ cittaṃ mayi kāruṇike jine |
  tiryagyoniṃ virāgyeha tataḥ svargaṃ gamiṣyasi || AVŚ_58.2|| iti ||
children.translated_text:
Rather, generate faith in me, the compassionate Conqueror;
becoming disenchanted with the animal realm here, you shall then go to heaven. // AVŚ_58.2 //

children.text: athāsau duṣṭamahiṣaḥ svāśrayaṃ jugupsamāno 'nāhāratāṃ pratipannaḥ | dīptāgnayas tiryagyonigatāḥ prāṇinaḥ | sa āśu kālaṃ kṛtvā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that vicious buffalo, filled with disgust for his own condition, undertook fasting. Animals born in that realm have blazing digestive fires. He quickly died and was reborn among the exalted gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven.

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | sa paśyati: tiryagbhyaś cyutaḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādyeti | atha mahiṣapūrviṇo devaputrasyaitad abhavat*: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāso bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam* | yanv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | atha mahiṣapūrvī devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravirājitagātro maṇiratnavicitracūḍaḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātras tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ taṃ vanaṣaṇḍam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān mahiṣapūrviṇo devaputrasyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā mahiṣapūrviṇā devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or a <s>Devakanyā</s> is newly reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where did I pass away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' He saw: 'I passed away from the animal realm and have been reborn among the exalted gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, by generating faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.' Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a buffalo had this thought: 'It would not be fitting for me to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience after having spent the night. Rather, let me approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> without having spent the night.' Then the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a buffalo — wearing gleaming, pure earrings, his body resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, his crown adorned with various gems and jewels, his body anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, <s>spṛkkā</s>, and other fragrances — on that very night, having filled his lap with divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> flowers, illuminating the entire forest grove with a magnificent radiance, showering the <s>Bhagavān</s> with flowers, he sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature of the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a buffalo, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which the <s>Devaputra</s> who had formerly been a buffalo, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he thrice uttered this inspired exclamation: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by a king, nor
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 149]

children.text: devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: by the gods, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by deceased ancestors, nor by ascetics and brahmins — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; the mountains of bones have been crossed over; the doors to the woeful states have been shut; the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened; we have been established among gods and humans.' And he said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: By your power, the terrible

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path to the woeful states, fraught with many faults, has been shut;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: the meritorious path to heaven has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_58.3 ||
children.translated_text: and by me the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found. // AVŚ_58.3 //

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer: suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_58.4 ||
children.translated_text: and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering. // AVŚ_58.4 //

By relying on you, today I have obtained
pure, stainless, supremely purified vision, free from faults;

children.text: naravarendra narāmarapūjita
children.translated_text: O best of men, worshipped by humans and gods,

children.text: vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayam* |
children.translated_text: free from birth, old age, death, and disease —

children.text: bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
children.translated_text: your sight, so difficult to obtain in thousands of existences,

children.text: saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_58.5 ||
children.translated_text: today, O Sage, the sight of you has borne fruit! // AVŚ_58.5 //

children.text: avanamya tataḥ pralambahāraś
children.translated_text: Then, bowing down with his long-hanging necklace,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: having worshipped both feet, filled with joy,

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: having circumambulated the Conqueror of Foes to the right,

children.text: suralokābhimukho divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_58.6 ||
children.translated_text: he departed heavenward, facing the world of the gods. // AVŚ_58.6 //

children.text: atha tair mahiṣīpālaiḥ sa udāro 'vabhāso dṛṣṭaḥ, yaṃ dṛṣṭvā kutūhalajātā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: ka eṣa bhagavan*, rātrau divyam avabhāsaṃ kṛtvā bhagavatsakāśam anuprāpta iti | bhagavān āha: sa eṣa bhavanto mahiṣo mamāntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagataḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ | so 'syāṃ rātrau matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | tasya mayā dharmo deśitaḥ | sa dṛṣṭasatyaḥ svabhavanaṃ gataḥ | tatas te mahiṣīpālāḥ paraṃ vismayam āpannāḥ: āścaryaṃ yan nāma ayaṃ tiryagyonigato bhūtvā bhagavantaṃ kalyāṇamitram āsādya deveṣūpapannaḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam* | kathaṃ nāma vayaṃ manuṣyabhūtā viśeṣaṃ nādhigacchemeti? tatas te buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpya bhagavato 'ntike pravrajitāḥ | tair yujyamānair ghaṭamānair vyāyacchamānaiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: Then the buffalo herders saw that magnificent radiance. Having seen it, filled with curiosity, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Who was this, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who came to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence at night, producing a divine radiance?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'That very buffalo, good sirs, having generated faith in my presence, died and was reborn among the exalted gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. He came to my presence this night. I taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen the truth, he returned to his own abode.' Then those buffalo herders were struck with the utmost wonder: 'How amazing that this one, having been born in the animal realm, by encountering the <s>Bhagavān</s> as a spiritual friend, was reborn among the gods and attained the vision of truth! How is it then that we, being humans, should not attain spiritual distinction?' Then they fed the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with the community of disciples, with excellent food. Having been ordained in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, by striving, exerting, and applying themselves, through the abandonment of all defilements, they directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta mahiṣapūrvikeṇa devaputreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni yena mahiṣeṣūpapannaḥ? ebhiś ca mahiṣīpālaiḥ kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yenāhartvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*? bhagavān āha: ebhir eva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | ebhiḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did the <s>Devaputra</s> who was formerly a buffalo perform that he was reborn as a buffalo? And what <s>karma</s> did these buffalo herders perform that they attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By these very ones, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By them deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_58.7 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_58.7 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśatisahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text:
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 150 --------------------
ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tatra ca kāle bhikṣūṇāṃ viniścaye vartamāne tripiṭo bhikṣuḥ pañcaśataparivāro viniścaye 'avasthitaḥ | tatra ca bhikṣavaḥ śaikṣāśaikṣāḥ | te tripiṭaṃ praśnaṃ pṛcchanti | sa na śaknoti vyākartum* | tena kupitena kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam*: ime ca mahiṣā kiṃ prajānantīti | śiṣyair apy asyoktam: ime mahiṣīpālāḥ kiṃ prajānantīti ||
children.translated_text:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 150]
at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. At that time, when the monks were engaged in a doctrinal dispute, a monk versed in the Three Baskets (<s>Tripiṭaka</s>), accompanied by five hundred followers, was involved in the dispute. Among them were monks who were learners and those beyond learning. They asked the <s>Tripiṭaka</s> monk a question. He was unable to answer. In his anger, he let forth harsh speech: 'What do these buffaloes know?' And his disciples likewise said: 'What do these buffalo herders know?'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau mahiṣaḥ, ayam asau tripiṭaḥ | ye te śiṣyāḥ, ime te mahiṣīpālāḥ | tena karmaṇā pañca janmaśatāni mahiṣeṣūpapannāḥ | imāni ca pañca mahiṣīpālaśatāni saṃvṛttāni | yan mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditaṃ tena deveṣūpapannaḥ, satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava vāgduścaritaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyaṃ yathā ete doṣā na bhaviṣyanti ye mahiṣasya mahiṣīpālāṇāṃ ca | eṣa eva guṇagaṇo bhaviṣyati yas tasyaiva devaputrabhūtasya | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who was that buffalo — he is this <s>Tripiṭa</s>. Those who were his disciples — they are the buffalo-herders. By that <s>karma</s>, they were reborn among buffaloes for five hundred births. And these are the five hundred buffalo-herders. Because he generated faith in my presence, he was reborn among the gods, and the vision of truth was accomplished. Therefore, monks, one must strive for the abandonment of verbal misconduct, so that the faults that befell the buffalo and the buffalo-herders may not arise. That same mass of virtues shall be yours as was his when he became a <s>Devaputra</s>. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_59 upoṣadhaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_59: <s>Upoṣadha</s> (The Observance Day). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu punaḥ samayena devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānām upoṣadho nāma devaputro 'sakṛdasakṛd bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāmati dharmaśravaṇāya | yāvad apareṇa samayena upoṣadho nāma devaputraḥ pañcaśataparivāro yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān upoṣadhasya devaputrasya āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā upoṣadhena devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam* | ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ, laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ, pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi, vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi, pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu | āha ca:
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Now at that time, a <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Upoṣadha</s> of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods would repeatedly approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then on a later occasion, the <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Upoṣadha</s>, with a retinue of five hundred, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head, he sat to one side to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature of the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Upoṣadha</s>, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Upoṣadha</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he thrice uttered this inspired exclamation: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by the king, nor by the gods, nor by beloved kinsmen and relatives, nor by departed ancestors, nor by ascetics and brahmins — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us: the oceans of blood and tears have been dried up, the mountains of bones have been surmounted, the doors to the lower realms have been closed, the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened, and we have been established among gods and humans.' And he said:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro
children.translated_text: 'By your power, the terrifying

children.text: hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: path to the lower realms, fraught with many faults, has been blocked;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā
children.translated_text: the meritorious path to heaven has been opened,

children.text: nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ || AVŚ_59.1 ||
children.translated_text: and the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has been found by me.' // AVŚ_59.1 //

children.text:
tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ
  mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ | (Speyer: suviśuddha cakṣuḥ)
  prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ
tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi || AVŚ_59.2 ||
children.translated_text: I have reached the peaceful state beloved by the noble ones, and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.' // AVŚ_59.2 //

'By relying on you, I have today attained
pure vision, free from fault, supremely clear;

children.text: naravarendra narāmarapūjita
children.translated_text: 'O best of men, worshipped by humans and gods,

children.text: vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmayam* |
children.translated_text: free from birth, old age, death, and disease —

children.text: bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana
children.translated_text: O Sage, whose sight is so difficult to obtain in a thousand existences,

children.text: saphalam adya mune tava darśanam* || AVŚ_59.3 ||
children.translated_text: today the sight of you has borne fruit!' // AVŚ_59.3 //

children.text: avanamya tataḥ pralambahāraś
children.translated_text: 'Then, bowing down, with his pendulous garlands,

children.text: caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: having reverenced both feet, filled with joy,

children.text: parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
children.translated_text: having circumambulated to the right the Conqueror of Foes,

children.text: suralokābhimukho divaṃ jagāma || AVŚ_59.4 ||
children.translated_text: he departed heavenward, facing the world of the gods.' // AVŚ_59.4 //

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ | yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃvignā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhagavann imāṃ rātriṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | api tu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu upoṣadho nāma devaputraḥ pañcaśataparivāro māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntaḥ | tasya mayā dharmo deśitaḥ | dṛṣṭasatyaś ca svabhavanaṃ gata iti | bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kuto bhadanta upoṣadhasya devaputrasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ceti | bhagavān āha: icchatha yūyaṃ hikṣavaḥ śrotum? evaṃ bhadanta | tena hi bhikṣavaḥ śṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: Then the monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw the magnificent radiance in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Having seen it, filled with spiritual urgency, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> this night?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. Rather, among the gods of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, a <s>Devaputra</s> named <s>Upoṣadha</s> with a retinue of five hundred came to see me. I taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen the truth, he returned to his own abode.' The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What is the origin and the arising of the name of the <s>Devaputra</s> <s>Upoṣadha</s>, Venerable Sir?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do you wish to hear, monks?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Then, monks, listen well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrakalpe viṃśatisahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvad apareṇa samayena kṛkī rājā bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmati paryupāsanāya | yāvad dvau brāhmaṇāu ṛṣipatanaṃ gatau kenacit karaṇīyena | tābhyāṃ rājā drṣṭo mahatyā rājaṛddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena | tayo rājyābhilāṣo jātaḥ | tābhyām anyatama upāsakaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ: bho buddhopāsaka, kiṃ karma kṛtvā yac cintayati yat prārthayate tad asya sarvaṃ samṛdhyatīti | upāsakenoktam*: ya pariśuddham aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatam upavāsam upavasati, yac cintayati yat prārthayate tad asya sarvaṃ samṛdhyatīti | tatas tau brāhmaṇau āṣāḍhasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśād aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatam upavāsam upalabhyopoṣitau | tadaikena pariśuddho rakṣitaḥ | sa kālaṃ kṛtvā rājñaḥ kṛkeḥ putratvam abhyupagataḥ | tasya sujāta iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* | sa pitur atyayād rājye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of <s>Devas</s> and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. Then on a later occasion, King <s>Kṛkin</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience and attendance. Two brahmins had gone to <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> for some business. They saw the king with the great splendor and great majesty of a king. Desire for kingship arose in them. They asked a certain lay devotee: "O devotee of the <s>Buddha</s>, what deed must one perform so that whatever one wishes and desires is all fulfilled?" The lay devotee said: "One who observes the pure fast endowed with eight factors — whatever he wishes and desires is all fulfilled." Then those two brahmins obtained the fast endowed with eight factors from the householder <s>Āṣāḍha</s> and observed it. By one of them it was kept purely and preserved. He, upon death, was reborn as the son of King <s>Kṛkin</s>. The name <s>Sujāta</s> was given to him. Upon his father's passing, he was established on the throne.'

children.text: dvitīyenopavāsaḥ khaṇḍitaḥ | sa kālaṃ kṛtvā nāgeṣūpapannaḥ | tasyopari divase divase saptakṛtvaḥ taptavālukā nipatati yayā so 'sthiśeṣaḥ kriyate | tasyaitad abhavat*: kasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ kasyāyaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalavipāko yenāham īdṛśaṃ duḥkham anubhavāmīti | sa paśyati: aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgataṃ me upavāsaṃ samādāya śikṣāśaithilyaṃ kṛtaṃ yenāham īdṛśaṃ mahadduḥkhaṃ pratyanubhavāmi | yena punaḥ samādāya rakṣitaṃ tena rājyaṃ pratilabdham iti | tasyaitad abhavat: yanv aham idānīm api
children.translated_text: 'By the second one, the fast was broken. He, upon death, was reborn among the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings). Upon him, day after day, hot sand fell seven times, by which he was reduced to nothing but bones. This thought occurred to him: "Of what <s>karma</s> is this the fruit? By what <s>karma</s>'s ripening do I experience such suffering?" He saw: "Having undertaken the fast endowed with eight factors, I became lax in the training rules, and therefore I experience such great suffering. But the one who, having undertaken it, preserved it — he obtained a kingdom." This thought occurred to him: "Even now, let me

children.text: tāvad aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatm upavāsam upavaseyam* | apy eva nāma nāgayoner mokṣaḥ syād iti | tato nāgavarṇam antardhāpya brāhmaṇavarṇam ātmānam abhinirmāya rājñaḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya jayenāyuṣā ca vardhayitvovāca: aṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatena me mahārāja upavāsena prayojanam* | tad arhati devo 'ṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatam upavāsaṃ paryeṣitum* | atha na paryeṣase, niyataṃ devasya saptadhā mūrdhānaṃ sphālayāmi | ity uktvā tatraivāntarhitaḥ | tato rājā bhītas trastaḥ saṃvigna āhṛṣṭaromakūpo hiraṇyapiṭakaṃ dhvajāgre baddhvā sarvavijite ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kārayāmāsa: yo me 'ṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatam upavāsaṃ deśayiṣyati, tasyaitaṃ hiraṇyapiṭakaṃ dāsyāmi, mahatā satkāreṇa satkariṣyāmīti | yāvad anyatamā vṛddhā strī palagaṇḍaduhitā | tayā rājñaḥ stambho darśitaḥ: atra me stambhe pitā asakṛdgandhadhūpapuṣpārcanaṃ kṛtavān* | tam utpāṭya pratyavekṣasveti | tato rājñā pauruṣeyāṇām ājñā dattā: ayaṃ stambha utpāṭyatām iti | tato rājapuruṣaiḥ stambha utpāṭitaḥ | tasyādhastāt suvarṇapatrābhilikhito 'ṣṭāṅgasamanvāgata upavāso labdhaḥ | saha pañca copāsakaśikṣāpadāni saptatriṃśac ca bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ | tato rājñā tasya nāgasyāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgata upavāso likhitvā dattaḥ | ṛṣipatananivāsibhiś ca dvādaśabhir ṛṣisahasraiḥ saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ pratyakṣīkṛtāḥ | sa ca nāgo 'ṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatam upavāsam upoṣya sthalam udgamyotsṛṣṭakāyo 'vasthitaḥ | so 'nāhāratāṃ pratipaṇṇaḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā pañcaśataparivāraḥ praṇīteṣū deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannaḥ | ato bhikṣavo upoṣadhasyotpattir nāmābhinirvṛttiś ceti ||
children.translated_text: observe the fast endowed with eight factors; perhaps I may be freed from the <s>Nāga</s> birth." Then, concealing his <s>Nāga</s> form and manifesting himself in the form of a brahmin, he approached the king. Having approached and greeted him with blessings for victory and long life, he said: "I require, great king, the fast endowed with eight factors. May your majesty please procure the fast endowed with eight factors." "And if you do not procure it, I shall surely split your head into seven pieces." Having said this, he vanished on the spot. Then the king, frightened, alarmed, shaken, with hair standing on end, tied a basket of gold to the top of a banner and had a bell-proclamation made throughout his entire domain: "Whoever will teach me the fast endowed with eight factors — to him I shall give this basket of gold and honor him with great honor." Now there was a certain old woman, daughter of <s>Palagaṇḍa</s>. She showed the king a pillar: "At this pillar my father repeatedly made offerings of incense, perfume, and flowers. Uproot it and examine it." Then the king gave orders to his men: "Let this pillar be uprooted." Then the king's men uprooted the pillar. Beneath it was found the fast endowed with eight factors, inscribed on a golden plate. Along with it were the five training rules for lay devotees and the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>). Then the king had the fast endowed with eight factors written out and given to that <s>Nāga</s>. And twelve thousand <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) dwelling at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> directly witnessed the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening. That <s>Nāga</s>, having observed the fast endowed with eight factors, emerged onto dry land and stood there, having abandoned his body. Having undertaken the practice of fasting unto death, he passed away together with his retinue of five hundred and was reborn among the exalted gods of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven. Hence, monks, the origin and the arising of the name <s>Upoṣadha</s>.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_60 haṃsāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_60: <s>Haṃsāḥ</s> (The Geese). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyāṃ rājā prasenajit kauśalo rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | yāvad apareṇa samayena rājā prasenajit kauśalo jetavanaṃ nirgato bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramituṃ paryupāsanāya | rājñā ca pañcālena rājñaḥ prasenajit kauśalasya prābhṛtaṃ pañca haṃsaśatāni preṣitāni | yadā rājā jetavanaṃ nirgatas tadā tāni pañca haṃsaśatāny upanāmitāni | tato rājñā prasenajitā teṣām abhayapradānaṃ datvā tatraiva jetavanae samutsṛṣṭāṇi | yadā bhagavān mahāśrāvakaparivṛto 'jine (Speyer: 'śana) upaniṣīdati, tadā te haṃsā bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāmanti | bhagavān api tebhya ālopam anuprayacchanti mahāśrāvakāś ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and thornless. He guarded the kingdom as though it were his only son. Then on a later occasion, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> went out to <s>Jetavana</s> to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience and attendance. The king of <s>Pañcāla</s> had sent five hundred geese as a gift to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>. When the king went out to <s>Jetavana</s>, the five hundred geese were presented to him. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s>, having granted them the gift of safety from harm, released them right there in <s>Jetavana</s>. Whenever the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the great disciples, sat down for meals, those geese would approach the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> and the great disciples would give them morsels of food.

children.text: te muktvā tṛptāḥ praṇītendriyās tiṣṭhanti | yadā bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, tadā te haṃsā bhagavatsakāśaṃ gatvā dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti | te cālpāyuṣkāḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having been released, they stood satisfied with tranquil senses. Whenever the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having risen from meditation, taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies, those swans would go to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence and listen to the <s>Dharma</s>. Being of short lifespan, they died and were reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven.

children.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | paśyanti haṃsebhyaś cyutāḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ, bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādyeti | atha haṃsapūrviṇo devaputrāś calavimalakuṇḍaladharā hārārdhahāravirājitagātrā maṇiratnavicitracūḍāḥ kuṅkumatamālapatraspṛkkādisaṃsṛṣṭagātrās tasyām eva rātrau divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamandāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṅgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ jetavanam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān haṃsapūrviṇāṃ devaputrāṇām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā haṃsapūrvibhir devaputrair viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptam* | te dṛṣṭasatyā vaṇig iva labdhalābhāḥ, sasyasaṃpannā iva karṣakāḥ śūrā iva vijitasaṃgrāmāḥ, sarvarogaparimuktā ivāturāḥ yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatās tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is the natural law that when a <s>Devaputra</s> or <s>Devakanyā</s> has recently been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I passed away? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' They saw: 'We have passed away from [birth as] swans and have been reborn among the excellent gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, by generating serene faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then the <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been swans — wearing gleaming, pure earrings, their bodies resplendent with necklaces and half-necklaces, their crowns adorned with various gems and jewels, their bodies anointed with saffron, <s>tamālapatra</s>, musk, and other fragrances — on that very night, having filled their laps with divine blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, white lotuses, and <s>mandārava</s> flowers, illuminating the entire <s>Jetavana</s> with a magnificent radiance, scattered flowers over the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature of the <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been swans, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which the <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been swans, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, like merchants who have gained their profit, like farmers whose crops have ripened, like heroes who have won their battle, like the sick freed from all disease — with the very same splendor with which they had come into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, they returned to their own abodes.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti | tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike udāro 'vabhāsaḥ | yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ paprachuḥ: kiṃ bhagavann imāṃ rātriṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāṃpatiḥ śakro devendraś catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ? bhagavān āha: na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāṃpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ | api tu dṛṣṭās te yuṣmābhir bhikṣavas tāni pañca haṃsaśatāni rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena ihotsṛṣṭāni? evaṃ bhadanta | tāni mamāntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagatāni, praṇīteṣu deveṣūpapannāni | tāny asyāṃ rātrau matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntāni | teṣāṃ mayā dharmo deśitaḥ | dṛṣṭasatyāni ca svabhavanaṃ gatāni ||
children.translated_text: The monks, applying themselves to the practice of wakefulness during the first and last watches of the night, saw the magnificent radiance in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Having seen it, filled with doubt, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Did <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, or the four World-Guardians come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> this night?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No, monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> Lord of the <s>Devas</s>, nor the four World-Guardians came to see me. But did you, monks, see those five hundred swans that were released here by King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Having generated serene faith in me, they died and were reborn among the excellent gods. They came to my presence this night. I taught them the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen the truth, they returned to their own abodes.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta haṃsapūrvakair devaputraiḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni yena haṃseṣūpapannāḥ, kāni karmāṇi kṛtāni yena deveṣūpapannāḥ satyadarśanaṃ ca kṛtam iti? bhagavān āha: ebhir eva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | ebhiḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, was performed by the <s>Devaputras</s> who had formerly been swans, by which they were reborn as swans? What <s>karma</s> was performed by which they were reborn among the gods and saw the truth?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was they themselves, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was they who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_60.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_60.1 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 154]

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tatraibhiḥ pravrajitaiḥ śikṣāśaithilyaṃ kṛtam* | tena haṃseṣūpapannāḥ | yan mamāntike cittaṃ prasāditaṃ tena deveṣūpapannāḥ | yat pariśiṣṭāni śikṣāpadāni tena satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam iti | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. There, these monks who had gone forth fell lax in their training. By that [laxity] they were reborn as swans. Because they generated serene faith in me, they were reborn among the gods. Because [they had observed] the remaining precepts, they saw the truth.' For, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 155]

children.text: saptamo vargaḥ |
children.translated_text: The seventh chapter.

children.text: tasyoddānam*.:
children.translated_text: Its summary:

children.text: suvarṇābhaḥ sugandhiś ca vapuṣmān balavān priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇābha</s> (Golden-Radiance), <s>Sugandhi</s> (Fragrant), <s>Vapuṣmān</s> (Handsome), <s>Balavān</s> (Mighty), <s>Priya</s> (Beloved),

children.text: padmākṣo dundubhiḥ putrāḥ sūryo mallapatākayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Padmākṣa</s> (Lotus-Eyed), <s>Dundubhi</s> (Drum), <s>Putrāḥ</s> (Sons), <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), and <s>Mallapatākā</s> (Malla Banner).

children.text: AVŚ_61 suvarṇābhaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_61: <s>Suvarṇābha</s> (Golden-Radiance). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'tikrānto mānuṣavarṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇaṃ jāmbūnadaniṣkasadṛśaḥ | suvarṇavarṇayā cānena prabhayā sarvaṃ kapilavastu nagaram avabhāsitam* | taddarśanān mātāpitarāv anye ca kutūhalābhyāgatāḥ satvāḥ paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ | cintayanti ca: kuto 'yam īdṛśaḥ satvaviśeṣa iti | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād anena jātena suvarṇavarṇayā prabhayā sarvaṃ kapilavastu nagaram avabhāsitam*, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya suvarṇābha iti nāmeti | suvarṇābho dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradatto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, receiving robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park.
