In <s>Kapilavastu</s> there was a certain <s>Śākya</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, charming, surpassing human complexion though not yet attaining divine complexion, resembling a golden <s>niṣka</s> (ornamental coin) of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold. With his golden radiance, the entire city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was illuminated. At the sight of him, his parents and other curious beings who had gathered were overcome with supreme wonder. They thought: 'Whence has such an extraordinary being come?' At his birth, a birth celebration was held, and a name was established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since at his birth the entire city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was illuminated by a golden radiance, therefore let the boy's name be <s>Suvarṇābha</s> (Golden-Radiance).' The boy <s>Suvarṇābha</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by these eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond. And he was wise, discerning, intelligent, faithful, virtuous, of good intentions, devoted to his own benefit and the benefit of others, compassionate, great-souled, and a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena rūpamadamatto bahir adhiṣṭhānasya krīḍati | saṃbahulāś ca śākyā nyagrodhārāmaṃ gacchanti | tatas tena suvarṇābhena dṛṣṭāḥ pṛṣṭāś ca: kva bhavanto gacchantīti | tair uktam*: nyagrodhārāmaṃ gacchāmo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ draṣṭum iti | suvarṇābhasya buddha ity aśrutapūrvaṃ nāma śrutvā sarvaromakūpāṇy āhṛṣṭani, paramaṃ ca kutūhalam utpannam* | tasyaitad abhavat*: yanv aham api buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmeyam iti | so 'pi nyagrodhārāmaṃ gacchati | tatas tatra dadarśa suvarṇābhakumāro buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cāsya
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, intoxicated with the pride of his beauty, he was playing outside his estate. A large number of <s>Śākyas</s> were going to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. <s>Suvarṇābha</s> saw them and asked: 'Where are you going, sirs?' They said: 'We are going to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park to see the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' When <s>Suvarṇābha</s> heard the name '<s>Buddha</s>' — never heard before — all the pores of his body stood on end and the utmost curiosity arose in him. This thought occurred to him: 'Let me too approach the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for an audience.' He too went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. There the prince <s>Suvarṇābha</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. And the moment he saw him,

children.text:
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 156 --------------------
yo 'sau rūpamadaḥ sa prativigataḥ | sa bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasya bhagavatā dharmo deśitaḥ | sa taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā pravrajyābhilāṣī saṃvṛttaḥ | yāvan mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat*: labheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam* | careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam iti | tato bhagavān gajabhujasadṛśaṃ suvarṇavarṇabāhum abhiprasārya suvarṇābhadārakam idam avocat*: ehi kumāra, cara brahmacaryam iti |
children.translated_text: [Reference: Vaidya, p. 156] his intoxication with beauty vanished. He worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. Having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, a desire for ordination arose in him. Having obtained permission from his parents, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his head, and with palms joined in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s direction, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, Venerable Sir, receive ordination, full ordination, and the status of a monk in this well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May I practice the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, extending his golden arm, beautiful as the trunk of a royal elephant, said this to the boy <s>Suvarṇābha</s>: 'Come, young man, practice the holy life!'

children.text: ehīti coktaḥ sa tathāgatena muṇḍaś ca saṃghāṭiparītadehaḥ |
children.translated_text: Called 'Come!' by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, tonsured, his body clad in the monastic robe,

children.text: sadyaḥ praśāntendriya eva tasthāv evaṃ sthito buddhamanorathena || AVŚ_61.1 ||
children.translated_text: at once he stood with senses pacified — thus established by the <s>Buddha</s>'s wish. // AVŚ_61.1 //

children.text:
yāvat saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśrur dvādaśavarṣopasaṃpanneryāpathaḥ pātrakaravyagrahasto bhagavataḥ purastāt sthitaḥ | tasya bhagavatā manasikāro dattaḥ | tena yujyamānena vyāyacchamānena ghaṭamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikaraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ |
  bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta suvarṇābhena karmāṇi kṛtāni yenaivaṃrūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ pravrajya ca acirād (Speyer: cāciraṃ) arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: suvarṇābhenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | suvarṇābhena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: Within seven days his hair and beard had grown back, he had attained the deportment of one who had been fully ordained for twelve years, and he stood before the Blessed One with his bowl in his hand. The Blessed One gave him a subject of meditation. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Suvarṇābha</s> perform that he was so handsome, good-looking, and pleasing, and that shortly after going forth he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Suvarṇābha</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Suvarṇābha</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_61.2 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_61.2 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddho buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ | tato rājñā bandhumatā bhagavataḥ śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaḥ stūpaś catūratnamayaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyī</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. Then <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having completed all the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging. Then King <s>Bandhumā</s>, having performed the worship of the Blessed One's relics, established a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of precious materials, extending a full <s>yojana</s> in area, a <s>krośa</s> in height,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 157]

children.text: | stūpamahaś ca prajñaptaḥ | yāvad anyatamo gṛhapatis tasmin stūpamahe vartamāne nirgataḥ | tena tasmāt stūpāt sauvarṇavarṇa ādarśaḥ patito dṛṣṭaḥ | sa tenāvataṃsakaṃ kārayitvā tatra stūpe āropitaḥ | gandhadhūpapuṣpārcanaṃ kṛtvā pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyāmi, evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: and a <s>stūpa</s>-festival was proclaimed. Then a certain householder, during that <s>stūpa</s>-festival, came forth. He saw a golden mirror that had fallen from that <s>stūpa</s>. He had it made into a diadem and placed it upon that <s>stūpa</s>. Having offered incense, perfume, and flowers, having prostrated at its base, he made this aspiration: 'May I too become the recipient of such virtues. May I please a teacher of such a kind.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena gṛhapatir āsīt*, ayaṃ sa suvarṇābhaḥ | yat tena vipaśyinaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya stūpe kārāḥ kṛtāḥ, tenāsyaivaṃvidho rūpaviśeṣaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tad ihaiva janmany arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the householder — that was <s>Suvarṇābha</s>. Because he performed those acts of devotion at the <s>stūpa</s> of the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyī</s>, he came to have such a special beauty of form. Because he made that aspiration, in this very life he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_62 sugandhiḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_62: <s>Sugandhi</s> (The Fragrant One). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ kulaputraḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko atikrānto mānuṣavarṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇam* | tasya mukhān nīlotpalagandho vāti sarvaśarīrāc candanagandhaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya mukān nīlotpalagandho vāti, śarīrāc candanagandhaḥ, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya sugandhir iti nāmeti | sugandhir dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa pūrvahetubalādhānāc chrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ | yadā sugandhir dārakaḥ keyūrahārakaṭakālaṃkṛto vīthīm avatarati, tadā candanagandhena sarvaṃ nagaram āpūrayati | janakāyaś ca divyaṃ gandham āghrāya paraṃ vismayam āpadyte | evaṃ cāha: aho puṇyānāṃ sāmarthyam iti |
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> grove. In <s>Kapilavastu</s> there lived a certain son of a good family — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He took a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, a son was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, surpassing the beauty of humans yet not attaining the beauty of the gods. From his mouth wafted the fragrance of a blue lotus, and from his entire body the fragrance of sandalwood. At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since from his mouth wafts the fragrance of a blue lotus, and from his body the fragrance of sandalwood, let the boy's name be <s>Sugandhi</s> (Fragrant).' The boy <s>Sugandhi</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, yogurt, butter, ghee, the cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. By the force of his former merit, he was faithful, noble, of virtuous intentions, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, and loving of the <s>Dharma</s>. Whenever the boy <s>Sugandhi</s>, adorned with armlets, necklaces, and bracelets, descended into the streets, he would fill the entire city with the fragrance of sandalwood. And the people, smelling the divine fragrance, were filled with the utmost wonder. And they would say: 'Oh, the power of merit!'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 158]

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena sugandhir dārako nyagrodhārāmaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | prasādajātaś ca bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā sugandhidārakeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena vyāyacchamānena ghaṭamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikaraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, the boy <s>Sugandhi</s> went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> grove. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, he purified his mind in the Blessed One's presence. Filled with faith, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave him such a teaching conducive to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, the boy <s>Sugandhi</s> shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he obtained his parents' permission and went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta sugandhinā karmāṇi kṛtāni yenāsya mukhān nīlotpalagandho vāti, sarvaśarīrāc candanagandhaś ca | bhagavān āha: sugandhinaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | sugandhinā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Sugandhi</s> perform that from his mouth wafts the fragrance of a blue lotus, and from his entire body the fragrance of sandalwood?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Sugandhi</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Sugandhi</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_62.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_62.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ | tato rājñā bandhumatā bhagavataḥ śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaḥ stūpaś catūratnamayaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | stūpamahaś ca prajñaptaḥ | tatrānyatamena gṛhapatinā prasādajātena vicitrair gandhaiḥ pralepaṃ datvā dhūpapuṣpārcanaṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyāmi | evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyam*, mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyī</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. Then <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having completed all the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging. Then King <s>Bandhumā</s>, having performed the worship of the Blessed One's relics, established a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of precious materials, extending a full <s>yojana</s> in area, a <s>krośa</s> in height. And a <s>stūpa</s>-festival was proclaimed. There, a certain householder, filled with faith, having anointed [the <s>stūpa</s>] with various fragrances and having offered incense and flowers, made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, this generation of the aspiration for awakening, and this relinquishment of gifts, may I become the recipient of such virtues. May I please a teacher of such a kind, and may I never displease him.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena gṛhapatir āsīt*, ayaṃ sa sugandhiḥ | yad anena vipaśyinaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya stūpe kārāḥ kṛtās tena tena sugandhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ |
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the householder — that was <s>Sugandhi</s>. Because he performed those acts of devotion at the <s>stūpa</s> of the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyī</s>, he has come to possess that fragrance.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 159]

children.text: yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ teneha janmany arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: Because he made that aspiration, in this very life he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_63 vapuṣmān | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_63: <s>Vapuṣmān</s> (The Splendid One). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauro 'tikrānto mānuṣavarṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇaṃ ramyavapuḥ sūkṣmatvaṅ maheśākhyaḥ prāptocchrayakāyaś ca | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya divyaṃ vapuḥ, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya vapuṣmān iti nāmeti | vapuṣmān dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ sarvalokeṣu pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca | tato vapuṣmān yān yān api sa bhūpradeśān* gatvā krāmati, te te 'sya medhyā bhavanti | evaṃvidhaḥ puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. At <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, enjoyed himself, and amused himself with her. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, a son was born to him — handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, fair-complexioned, having surpassed human complexion though not yet attained divine complexion, of lovely form, of delicate skin, of great renown, his body having attained its full stature. At his birth, a birth festival was held, and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since this boy has a divine form (<s>vapus</s>), let the boy's name be <s>Vapuṣmān</s> (The Splendid One).' The boy <s>Vapuṣmān</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two to carry him on their hips, two as wet-nurses, two as bath-nurses, and two as playmates. He was raised by those eight nurses and grew up nourished on milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. And he was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, fond of the <s>Dharma</s>, worthy of worship, honor, and salutation in all worlds. Moreover, whatever regions of the earth <s>Vapuṣmān</s> traversed and walked upon became purified. Such was the greatness of his merit and renown.

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena nyagrodhārāmaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, he went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. And there he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. And at the very sight, he generated faith in the Blessed One's presence. His mind
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 160]

children.text: prasāditam* | prasādajātaś ca bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā vapuṣmatā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena vyāyacchamānena ghaṭamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was filled with faith. Having worshipped the Blessed One's feet, he sat down before him to hear the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. To him, the Blessed One — knowing his disposition, inclination, nature, and character — delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> leading to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, <s>Vapuṣmān</s> shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body), rising with its twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (Stream-entry). Having seen the truth, he obtained permission from his parents and went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself — having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable and ever-changing, and having struck down all the courses of conditioned formations by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving — through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta vapuṣmatā karmāṇi kṛtāni yenāsyaivaṃvidha āśrayo 'rhatvaṃ ca prāptam iti | bhagavān āha: vapuṣmataiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | vapuṣmatā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Vapuṣmān</s> perform that he obtained such a [handsome] body and attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'It was <s>Vapuṣmān</s> himself, monks, who in former births performed and accumulated deeds, whose requisite conditions had been gathered, whose causes had matured, which stood before him like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass. <s>Vapuṣmān</s> performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their results]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_63.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_63.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ | tato 'sya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | tatra ca rājñā bandumatā saputravargeṇa sāmātyagaṇaparivṛtena stūpamahaḥ kṛtaḥ | yāvad anyatamasmin divase 'nyatamo daridrapuruṣaḥ stūpāṅgaṇaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tatra tena puṣpāṇi mlānāni dṛṣṭāni, rajasā ca stūpāṅgaṇo malinīkṛtaḥ | tatas tena buddhaguṇān anusmṛtya prasādajātena saṃmārjanīṃ gṛhītvā stūpaḥ saṃmṛṣṭo nirmālyaṃ cāpanītam* | tato 'pagatarajaṃ stūpaṃ nirmalaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasādajātaḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: anenāhaṃ kuśalena cittotpādena caivaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyāmīty evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyam*, mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having completed the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging, as a fire goes out when its fuel is exhausted, then King <s>Bandhuma</s>, having performed the funeral rites for his body, erected a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of precious substances, one <s>yojana</s> on every side, one <s>krośa</s> in height. And King <s>Bandhuma</s>, together with his sons and surrounded by his retinue of ministers, held a festival at the <s>stūpa</s>. Then on a certain day, a certain poor man entered the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard. There he saw withered flowers and the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard soiled with dust. Then, recollecting the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s> and filled with faith, he took a broom and swept the <s>stūpa</s>, and removed the old offerings. Then, seeing the <s>stūpa</s> freed from dust and spotless, filled with faith, he fell at its feet and made this aspiration: "By this merit and this mental resolve, may I become the recipient of such virtues — may I please a teacher of this kind, and may I never displease [one]."'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 161]

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena daridraḥ puruṣa āsīt*, ayaṃ sa vapuṣmān* | yatas tena stūpaḥ saṃmṛṣṭaḥ, tenābhirūpaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ teneha janmany arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was that poor man — he is this very <s>Vapuṣmān</s>. Because he swept the <s>stūpa</s>, he became handsome. Because he made that aspiration, in this birth he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, deeds that are entirely dark have entirely dark results; entirely bright [deeds have] entirely bright [results]; mixed [deeds have] mixed [results]. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_64 balavān | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_64: <s>Balavān</s> (The Strong One). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. At <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, enjoyed himself, and amused himself with her. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, a son was born to him — handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, endowed with extraordinary human strength. At his birth, a birth festival was held, and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since this boy is strong, let his name be <s>Balavān</s> (The Strong One).' The boy <s>Balavān</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two to carry him on their hips, two as wet-nurses, two as bath-nurses, and two as playmates. He was raised by those eight nurses and grew up nourished on milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. And he was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, fond of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.translated_text: On a later occasion, he went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. And there he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. And at the very sight, he generated faith in the Blessed One's presence. Having worshipped the Blessed One's feet, he sat down before him to hear the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. To him, the Blessed One — knowing his disposition, inclination, nature, and character — delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> leading to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, <s>Balavān</s> shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body), rising with its twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (Stream-entry). Having seen the truth, he obtained permission from his parents and went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself — having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable and ever-changing, having struck down all the courses of conditioned formations
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 162]

children.text: śatanapatanavikaraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving — through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta balavatā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni yenāsyāśrayo balavān*, arhatvaṃ ca prāptam iti | bhagavān āha: balavataiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | balavatā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Balavān</s> perform and accumulate that his body is strong and he has attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Balavān</s> himself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Balavān</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_64.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_64.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaḥ stūpaś catūratnamayaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | tatra stūpamahe vartamāne mahājanakāyena nṛtyatā gāyatā ca stūpaṃ pāṃsunā malinīkṛtam* | yāvad anyatamo gṛhapatiḥ stūpāṅgaṇaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | sa paśyati stūpāṅgaṇaṃ rajasā malinīkṛtaḥ | tatas tena gṛhapatinā buddhaguṇān anusmṛtya prasādajātena tailavyāmiśro gandhakāyo dattaḥ, praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam*: apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syām* | evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder, King <s>Bandhumān</s> performed the funeral honor for his body and erected a <s>stūpa</s> one <s>yojana</s> in extent on all sides, made of four kinds of precious stones, one <s>krośa</s> in height. During a great <s>stūpa</s> festival, the great multitude of people, dancing and singing, had soiled the <s>stūpa</s> with dust. Then a certain householder entered the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard. He saw that the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard had been soiled with dust. Then that householder, recollecting the <s>Buddha</s>'s virtues, filled with faith, offered a fragrant paste mixed with oil, and made an aspiration: 'May I attain such virtues! May I please such a Teacher, and may I never displease him!'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena gṛhapatiḥ, ayaṃ sa balavān* | yad anena vipaśyinaḥ stūpe kārāḥ kṛtās tena balavān saṃvṛttaḥ | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the householder — he is this <s>Balavān</s>. Because he performed services at the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyin</s>, he became strong. Because he made that aspiration, he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 163]

children.text: AVŚ_65 priyaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_65: <s>Priya</s> (The Beloved). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko maheśākhyo priyadarśanaś ca | tasya janmani sarvaṃ kapilavastu nagaraṃ yaśasā āpūritam* | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād ayaṃ jātamātra eva sarvajanapriyaḥ, tasmād asya priya iti nāma bhavatu | priyo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalas tyāgaruciḥ pradānaruciḥ pradāne 'bhirato mahati tyāge vartate | sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakānāṃ vividhair dānavisargaiḥ saṃgrahaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park. In <s>Kapilavastu</s> there was a certain <s>Śākya</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, a son was born to him — handsome, good-looking, graceful, of eminent fame, and pleasing to behold. At his birth, the entire city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was filled with glory. At his birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since this boy, from the very moment of his birth, is beloved by all people, let his name be <s>Priya</s> (Beloved).' The boy <s>Priya</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses, nourished on milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other excellent and choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond. He was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, tender toward his subjects, delighting in renunciation, delighting in giving, devoted to giving, and he practiced great generosity. He showed hospitality to ascetics, brahmins, the wretched, and wayfarers through various acts of giving.

children.text: yāvat priyo dārako 'pareṇa samayena nyagrodhārāmaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | sa prasādajātaś ca bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā priyeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena vyāyacchamānena ghaṭamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, the boy <s>Priya</s> went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The very moment he saw him, he generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Filled with faith, he prostrated at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which <s>Priya</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he obtained his parents' permission and went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta priyeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni yena mahāyaśasāṃ priyo manāpaś ca | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ prāptam iti | bhagavān āha: priyeṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Priya</s> perform and accumulate that he is of great fame and beloved and pleasing [to all]? And that, having gone forth, he attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Priya</s> himself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 164]

children.translated_text: which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Priya</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_65.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_65.1 //

children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder, King <s>Bandhumān</s> performed the funeral honor for his body and erected a <s>stūpa</s> one <s>yojana</s> in extent on all sides, made of four kinds of precious stones, one <s>krośa</s> in height. Then, on a later occasion, in the spring season when the trees were in blossom and flowers of many varieties had appeared, a certain householder petitioned the king: 'I wish, great king, with your majesty's help, to perform a flower-offering at the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyin</s>.' The king said: 'So be it.' Then that householder, with the aid of the king's ministers and officers, having collected various flowers to the sound of bells, performed the flower-offering at <s>Vipaśyin</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>, during which many hundreds of thousands of beings, having generated faith, planted roots of merit.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena gṛhapatir āsīt* ayaṃ sa priyaḥ | yat tena mahārājasahāyena kuśalamūlāny avaropitāni, tena mahājanasya priyo manāpaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ, tenaiva hetunā darśanīyaḥ prasādikaḥ | arhatvaṃ ca prāptam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the householder — he is this <s>Priya</s>. Because he planted roots of merit with the great king's assistance, he has become beloved and pleasing to the multitude, and for that very reason he is handsome and graceful. And he has attained <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_66 padmākṣaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_66: <s>Padmākṣa</s> (Lotus-Eyed). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park. In <s>Kapilavastu</s> there was a certain <s>Śākya</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 165]

children.text: vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'bhinīlapadmanetraḥ divyenendranīlamaṇiratnena śirasy ābaddhena, yena kapilavastu nagaram indranīlavarṇaṃ vyavasthāpitam* | tasya jatau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya padmasadṛśe akṣiṇī, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya padmākṣa iti nāmeti | padmākṣo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmas tyāgaruciḥ pradānābhirato mahati tyāge vartate | sa yena yena gacchati, tena devamanuṣyaiḥ pūjyate 'bhyarcyate ca ||
children.translated_text: competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, a son was born — handsome, good-looking, charming, with eyes like deep blue lotuses, and with a divine <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) gem bound upon his head, by which the entire city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> took on the hue of a sapphire. At his birth, a birth celebration was held, and a name was established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since his eyes are like lotuses, therefore let the boy's name be <s>Padmākṣa</s> (Lotus-Eyed).' The boy <s>Padmākṣa</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by these eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond. And he was faithful, virtuous, of good intentions, devoted to his own benefit and the benefit of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>, delighting in generosity, devoted to giving, engaged in great munificence. Wherever he went, he was worshipped and venerated by gods and humans.

children.text: yatha padmākṣo dārako 'pareṇa samayena nyagrodhārāmaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasāditam* | prasādajātaś ca bhagavatpādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā padmākṣeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo dānapradānāni datvā śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakaduḥkhitān saṃtarpayitvā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | yāvad asau piṇḍapātapraviṣṭo mahājanakāyenodvīkṣyamāṇo jihreti | atha sa padmākṣo bhagavataḥ sakāśam upasaṃkramya bhagavantaṃ vijñāpayāmāsa: sādhu me bhagavāṃs tathā karotu yathā maṇiratnam antardhīyeta | bhagavān āha: karmajaṃ hy etat*, na śakyam antardhāpayitum* | api tu tathā kariṣyāmi yac chrāddhā drakṣyanti nāśrāddhā iti | tato bhagavatā tathā kṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, the boy <s>Padmākṣa</s> went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, he generated serene faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Filled with faith, he worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which <s>Padmākṣa</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, having given gifts of generosity, having satisfied ascetics, brahmins, the wretched, wanderers, and the suffering, and having obtained permission from his parents, he went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. But when he entered [the city] for alms, being gazed upon by the great multitude, he felt ashamed. Then <s>Padmākṣa</s>, approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s>, made this request: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> kindly cause the gem to disappear.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This is born of <s>karma</s>; it cannot be made to disappear. But I shall make it so that the faithful will see it, but not the faithless.' And the <s>Bhagavān</s> made it so.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta padmākṣeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny {upacitāni} yenaivaṃ mahāśakhyo 'rhatvaṃ ca prāptam iti | bhagavān āha: padmākṣeṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | padmākṣeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati?
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Padmākṣa</s> perform and accumulate, by which he was of such great renown and attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Padmākṣa</s> himself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Padmākṣa</s> who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]?'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 166]

children.text: na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: 'Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:'

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_66.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_66.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvendhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ | tatra anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kārān kṛtvā svargamokṣaparāyaṇāni bhavanti | yāvad anyatamaḥ sārthavāho mahāsamudrāt siddhayānapātro 'bhyagataḥ | tena tatra mahindranīlakaṃ ratnam ānitam* | tena vipaśyinaḥ stūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgataguṇān anusmṛtya tan maṇiratnaṃ vipaśyinaḥ stūpavarṣasthālyām upari nibaddham* | tasyānubhāvena digvidiśaḥ sarvā nīlākārā avasthitāḥ | padmaiś ca pūjāṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: aham apy evaṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syām*, evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyī</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyī</s> the perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s> had accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, he attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted. Then King <s>Bandhuma</s>, having performed the due honor to his relics, established a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of precious substances, extending a <s>yojana</s> in all directions. There, many hundreds of thousands of beings, having performed worship, became destined for heaven and liberation. Then a certain caravan-leader, having returned from the great ocean with a successful voyage, brought from there a great <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) gem. Having seen the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyī</s> and recollecting the virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he fastened that gem on top of the rain-drip pan of <s>Vipaśyī</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>. By its power, all the directions and intermediate directions took on a blue hue. And having worshipped with lotuses, he made this aspiration: "May I too become one who attains such virtues, and may I please such a Teacher and never displease him!"'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena sārthavāha āsīt*, ayaṃ sa padmākṣaḥ | yat tena vipaśyinaḥ stūpe maṇiratnam āropitaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākenāsya maṇiratnaṃ śirasi prādurbhūtam* | yan nīlapadmaiḥ pūjā kṛtā tenābhinīlapadmanetraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā teneha janmany arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the caravan-leader — he is this <s>Padmākṣa</s>. Because he placed the gem on <s>Vipaśyī</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> the gem appeared upon his head. Because he worshipped with blue lotuses, he was born with eyes like deep blue lotuses. Because he made the aspiration, in this very life he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.' For, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_67 dundubhisvaraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_67: <s>Dundubhisvara</s> (Drum-Voice). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
