He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 167]

children.text:
paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko maheśākhyaḥ kalaviṅkamanojñabhāṇī (Speyer: kalaviṅkamanojñabhāṣī) dundubhisvaranirghoṣaḥ | tasya jatau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād ayaṃ dārako dundubhisvaraḥ, tasmād asya bhavatu dundubhisvara iti nāmeti | dundubhisvaro dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalas tyāgaruciḥ pradānarucir mahati tyāge vartate |
  yāvad apareṇa samayena dundubhisvaro dārako nyagrodhārāmaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | prasādajātaś ca bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā dundubhisvareṇa dārakeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo dānapradānāni datvā śramaṇabrāhmaṇavanīpakān duḥkhitān saṃtarpayitvā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, a son was born — handsome, good-looking, charming, of great renown, with a voice as sweet as a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird and resounding like a drum. At his birth, a birth celebration was held, and a name was established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since this boy has a drum-like voice, therefore let his name be <s>Dundubhisvara</s> (Drum-Voice).' The boy <s>Dundubhisvara</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by these eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond. And he was faithful, virtuous, of good intentions, devoted to his own benefit and the benefit of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>, fond of his people, delighting in generosity, devoted to giving, engaged in great munificence. On a later occasion, the boy <s>Dundubhisvara</s> went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, he generated serene faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Filled with faith, he worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which the boy <s>Dundubhisvara</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, having given gifts of generosity, having satisfied ascetics, brahmins, wanderers, and the suffering, and having obtained permission from his parents, he went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta dundubhisvareṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny yenābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prasādiko 'rhatvaṃ ca prāptam iti | bhagavān āha: dundubhisvareṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | dundubhisvareṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds did <s>Dundubhisvara</s> perform, Venerable Sir, that he is handsome, comely, pleasing, and has attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Dundubhisvara</s> himself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Dundubhisvara</s> who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_67.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_67.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvendhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | tatrānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kārān kṛtvā svargamokṣaparāyaṇāni bhavanti | yāvad anyatareṇa gṛhapatinā vicitrāṇi vādyabhāṇḍāni puruṣāś ca śikṣayitvā tatra stūpe niryātitāḥ, ye tatra stūpe ahanyahani vādyaviśeṣaiḥ satkāraṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging — like a fire whose fuel is exhausted — King <s>Bandhuma</s>, having performed the honor due to his relics, established a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of jewels, a <s>yojana</s> on each side and a <s>krośa</s> in height. There, many hundreds of thousands of beings, having rendered service, became destined for heaven and liberation. Then a certain householder, having trained men and procured various musical instruments, donated them to that <s>stūpa</s>, and they performed daily worship at that <s>stūpa</s> with special musical offerings.'

children.text: {bhagavān āha:} kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena gṛhapatir āsīt*, ayaṃ sa dundubhisvaraḥ | yat tena vipaśyinaḥ stūpe vādyabhāṇḍāni niryātitāni, tenedānīṃ dundubhisvaraḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | tenaiva hetunedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāṃ karmanām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the householder — he is this <s>Dundubhisvara</s>. Because he donated musical instruments to the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyin</s>, he has now become <s>Dundubhisvara</s> ("Drum-voiced"). By that very cause, he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_68 putrāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_68: <s>Putrāḥ</s> (The Sons). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | mahatī mahatī māṃsapeśī jātā, yāṃ dṛṣṭvā mātāpitarau viṣaṇṇau, anye ca gṛhavāsinaḥ paricārakā jñātayaś ca: ko nāmāyam evaṃvidho jāta iti | yāvad asau gṛhapatiḥ śokāgāraṃ praviśya kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: kasya nivedayeyam*, ko jñāsyati kim etad iti | tasya buddhir utpannā: ayaṃ buddho bhagavān sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī | buddhasya bhagavato nivedayāmi, sa jñāsyatīti | sa yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavantaṃ papraccha | bhagavān āha: mā bhaiṣīs tvaṃ gṛhapate, mā bhaiṣīḥ | suvihite karpāse
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. In <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A great lump of flesh was born, and seeing it, the parents were dismayed, as were the other household servants and relatives: 'What kind of creature has been born!' Then that householder, entering the house of grief, resting his cheek on his hand, sat absorbed in worry: 'To whom should I report this? Who will know what this is?' This thought arose in him: 'This <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, is omniscient, all-seeing. I shall report it to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>; he will know.' He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Fear not, householder, fear not! Place the lump of flesh on well-prepared cotton,

children.text:
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 169 --------------------
māṃsapeśīṃ sthāpayitvā trir divasasya pāṇināpamṛjya kṣīreṇa punaḥ pariprokṣasva yāvat saptāham* | tataḥ sphuṭiṣyati, kumāraśatam utpatsyate | te ca sarve mahānagnabalino bhaviṣyanti | iti śrutvā gṛhapatiḥ paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ | cintayati ca: lābhā me sulabdhā yasya me īdṛśāḥ putrā utpatsyantīti | tena tathaiva kṛtam* | yāvat saptame divase sā māṃsapeśī sphuṭitā | kumāraśatam utpannam* | sarve abhirūpā darśanīyāḥ prāsādikāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā mahānagnabalinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and three times a day wipe it with your hand, then sprinkle it again with milk, for seven days. Then it will split open, and a hundred boys will be born. And they will all be of great naked strength.' Hearing this, the householder was filled with the utmost amazement. He thought: 'Fortunate am I, greatly fortunate, that such sons will be born to me!' He did exactly as instructed. On the seventh day, that lump of flesh split open. A hundred boys were born — all handsome, comely, pleasing, endowed with all limbs and features, of great naked strength.

children.text: yāvat krameṇa unnītā vardhitā mahāntaḥ saṃvṛttāś ca | sarve yauvanamadamattā itaś cāmutaś ca paribhramanto nyagrodhārāmaṃ gatāḥ | atha te dadṛśur buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | teṣāṃ bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā sarvair evaṃ viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | te dṛṣṭasatyā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitāḥ | taiḥ sarvair yujyamānair ghaṭamānair vyāyacchamānaiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhanto babhūvas traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhāḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyāś ca saṃvṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In due course, they were raised, nurtured, and grew up. All of them, intoxicated with the pride of youth, wandering here and there, came to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. There they beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. At the very sight, having reverenced the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, they sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which all of them, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, they obtained their parents' permission and went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. All of them, by striving, exerting, and applying themselves, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. They became <s>Arhats</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. They became worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta kumāraśatena karmāṇi kṛtāny yena mahānagnabalinaḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, sahitāś ca bhrātara iti | bhagavān āha: ebhir eva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | ebhir kṛtānikarmāṇy upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds did the hundred boys perform, Venerable Sir, that they became of great naked strength, and were born together as brothers?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was they themselves, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was they who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena, yatrānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kārān kṛtvā svargamokṣaparāyaṇāni bhavanti | yāvad goṣṭhikānāṃ
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging — like a fire whose fuel is exhausted — King <s>Bandhuma</s>, having performed the honor due to his relics, established a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of jewels, a <s>yojana</s> on each side and a <s>krośa</s> in height, where many hundreds of thousands of beings, having rendered service, became destined for heaven and liberation. Then a guild of

children.text: śataṃ nirgatam* | taṃb stūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgataguṇān anusmṛtya tais tatra stūpe ekapuruṣeṇa vā ekadehinā vā ekātmanā vā ekacitteneva ekātmabhāveneva (Speyer: ekapuruṣeṇevaikadehinevaikātmanevaikacittenevaikātmabhāveneva) sarvair ekasamūhībhūtaiḥ prasannacittakaiḥ prītijātair ekātmanībhūtais tatra stūpe puṇyadhūpagandhamālyavilepanāni naivedyarasarasāgrabhojyāni sarvopahārāṇi copaḍhaukitāni | dhvajavitānacchatrāṇi cāropitāni | āropya ekasamūhībhūtvā ekasvareṇa stūtiṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaśatasahasraṃ kṛtam* | tatas taiḥ sarvair ekātmabhāvenaikacittakena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā: anena kuśalamūlenāsmākaṃ tathaivaikātmajātā ekacittakāḥ samānadehāḥ samānācārāḥ samānadharmāḥ samānapuṇyāḥ samanirvāṇā bhavantu iti | tatraiva stūpe evaṃ bhaktiparāyaṇā nirvṛttāḥ ||
children.translated_text: one hundred went forth. Having seen that <s>stūpa</s> and recollecting the virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, all of them — united as one person, as one being, as one self, as one mind, as one entity — all having become a single group, with serene minds, filled with joy, having become one in spirit, offered at that <s>stūpa</s> meritorious incense, garlands, perfumes, ointments, food offerings, choice delicacies, and all manner of oblations. They raised banners, canopies, and parasols. Having raised them, they became a single group and with one voice offered praise, performing a hundred thousand circumambulations. Then, all of them with one spirit and one mind made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may we be born from one body, of one mind, alike in form, alike in body, alike in conduct, alike in <s>dharma</s>, alike in merit, and alike in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' There, at that very <s>stūpa</s>, they lived out their lives devoted to worship.'

children.text: ### <The text in all MS is mutilated. The para must beginn with kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ ... saṃvṛttāḥ.> {kiṃ manyadhve bhukṣavaḥ ... saṃvṛttāḥ} | tenaiva hetunā idānīm ekapeśījātāḥ samarūpāḥ samadehabhāvāḥ samātmacittāḥ samabalavīryaparākramāḥ samācārāḥ samadharmeṣu parāyaṇāḥ samaṃ srotāpattiphalaṃ prāptāḥ, samaṃ cārhatvaṃ prāptāḥ | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: [Note: The text in all manuscripts is mutilated. The passage should begin with 'What do you think, monks? ... they were.'] By that very cause, they are now born from a single lump of flesh — alike in form, alike in body, alike in mind, alike in strength, valor, and prowess, alike in conduct, destined for the same <s>dharmas</s>, having equally attained the fruit of stream-entry and equally attained <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_69 sūryaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_69: <s>Sūrya</s> (The Sun). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko maheśākhyaḥ śirasi maṇiratnayuktaḥ | ### <Tib transl. seems to add afew sentaneces here, describing the sun line splendour of the gem on the crest. Cf. tasya maṇiratnasya prabhayā sarvaṃ gṛham avabhāsitaṃ sūryasyeva.> | tasya jatau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya dārakasya śirasi maṇiratnaṃ prādurbhūtam*, tasya maṇiratnasya prabhayā sarvaṃ gṛham avabhāsitaṃ sūryasyeva, tasmād asya
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. At <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, enjoyed himself, and amused himself with her. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, a son was born to him — handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, of great renown, with a jewel-gem set upon his head. ### [The Tibetan translation appears to add a few sentences here describing the sun-like splendor of the gem on his crest. Cf. 'By the radiance of that jewel-gem, the entire house was illuminated as if by the sun.'] At his birth, a birth festival was held, and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since on the head of this boy a jewel-gem has appeared, and by the radiance of that jewel-gem the entire house was illuminated as if by the sun, therefore let his
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 171]

children.text:
sūryo nāma bhavatu iti | sūryo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalas tyāgaruciḥ pradānakauśalo mahati tyāge vartate |
  yāvad apareṇa samayena sūryo dārako nyagrodhārāmaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādya svaśirasi maṇiratnam uddhṛtya bhagavata upanāmitam* | tataḥ prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tato bhagavatā sūryasyānukampām upādāya tan maṇiratnam upagṛhyāśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tena sūryeṇa dārakeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo dānapradānāni datvā śramaṇabrāhmaṇavanīpakān duḥkhitān satvān saṃtarpayitvā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
name be <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun).' The boy <s>Sūrya</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two to carry him on their hips, two as bath-nurses, two as wet-nurses, and two as playmates. He was raised by those eight nurses and grew up nourished on milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. And he was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, fond of the <s>Dharma</s>, affectionate toward his subjects, delighting in generosity, skilled in giving, and he abided in great generosity.
On a later occasion, the boy <s>Sūrya</s> went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. And there he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the halo of a fathom's span, of brilliance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, he generated faith in the Blessed One's presence and, having removed the jewel-gem from his own head, offered it to the Blessed One. Then, filled with faith, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet and sat down before him to hear the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, out of compassion for <s>Sūrya</s>, having accepted that jewel-gem and knowing his disposition, inclination, nature, and character, delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> leading to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, upon hearing it, the boy <s>Sūrya</s> shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body), rising with its twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (Stream-entry). Having seen the truth, he gave charitable gifts and satisfied <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, wandering mendicants, and suffering beings. Then, having obtained permission from his parents, he went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself — having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable and ever-changing, and having struck down all the courses of conditioned formations by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving — through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta sūryeṇa dārakeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny yena śirasi maṇiratnaṃ jātam*, yena ca maheśākhyo 'rhatvaṃ ca prāptam iti | bhagavān āha: sūryeṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | sūryeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did the boy <s>Sūrya</s> perform that a jewel-gem appeared upon his head, that he became of great renown, and that he attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'It was <s>Sūrya</s> himself, monks, who in former births performed and accumulated deeds, whose requisite conditions had been gathered, whose causes had matured, which stood before him like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass. <s>Sūrya</s> performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their results]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_69.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_69.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 172]

children.text: sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | yatrānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kārān kṛtvā svargamokṣaparāyaṇāni bhavanti | tatra stūpamaho vartate | śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo vicitrair gandhamālyavilepanaiś chatrair dhvajaiḥ patākābhiḥ pūjāṃ kurvanti | yāvad apareṇa puruṣeṇa rājñāḥ sakāśād dyūtaṃ krīḍataḥ sūryābhāsaṃ (Speyer: sūryāvabhāsaṃ) maṇiratnaṃ nirjitam* | tatas tena prasādajātena vipaśyinaś caitye varṣāsthālyāṃ samāropitam* | tataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: anenāhaṃ kuśalena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syām*, evaṃvidhaṃ śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam*, evaṃvidhena cūḍāyāṃ baddhena mātuḥ kukṣer nirgaccheyam iti ||
children.translated_text: having completed the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging, King <s>Bandhumā</s>, having performed the funeral rites for his body, erected a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of precious substances, one <s>yojana</s> on every side, one <s>krośa</s> in height. There, many hundreds of thousands of beings, having performed acts of devotion, attained rebirth in heaven and liberation. A <s>stūpa</s>-festival was held there. Faithful <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders were making offerings with various incense, garlands, perfumes, parasols, banners, and flags. Then on a later occasion, a certain man, having won a jewel-gem called <s>Sūryābhāsa</s> (Sun-Radiance) (Speyer: <s>Sūryāvabhāsa</s>) in a gambling match with the king, placed it — filled with faith — upon the rain-vessel (<s>varṣāsthālī</s>) of the <s>caitya</s> (shrine) of <s>Vipaśyin</s>. Then, prostrating at its feet, he made this aspiration: "By this merit, this generation of the aspiration for awakening, and this relinquishment of a gift, may I become the recipient of such virtues; may I please a teacher of such a kind and never displease [one]; and may I issue from my mother's womb with such [a gem] bound upon my crown."'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena akṣadhūrta āsīt*, ayaṃ sa sūryaḥ | yat tena vipaśyinaḥ stūpe ratnaṃ samāropitaṃ tenāsya śirasi maṇiratnaṃ prādurbhūtam* | tenaiva hetunā abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ | arhatvaṃ ca sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the gambler — he is this very <s>Sūrya</s>. Because he placed a gem upon the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyin</s>, a jewel-gem appeared upon his head. By that very cause he became handsome, beautiful, and pleasing to behold. And he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, deeds that are entirely dark have entirely dark results; entirely bright [deeds have] entirely bright [results]; mixed [deeds have] mixed [results]. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_70 mallapatākā | (ed. Speyer, vol. I)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_70: <s>Mallapatākā</s> (The Malla Banner). (ed. Speyer, vol. I)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'tikrānto mānuṣaṃ varṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇam* | yadāsau kumāro jātas tadā devatābhir divyāḥ patākāḥ samantata ucchrāpitāḥ, divyāni vādyabhāṇḍāni parāhatāni, divyāni cotpalakumudapadmapuṇḍarīkamāndāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇi kṣiptāni, sarvaṃ ca kapilavastu nagaraṃ yaśasā āpūritam*, sarvagṛheṣu cāsya nāmnā patākā ucchrāpitāḥ | tasya jatau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya jātasya yaśasā sarvaloka
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. At <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> was wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, enjoyed himself, and amused himself with her. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, a son was born to him — handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, having surpassed human complexion though not yet attained divine complexion. When that prince was born, the deities raised divine banners on all sides, divine musical instruments were played, divine flowers of <s>utpala</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>mandārava</s> were scattered, the entire city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was filled with his glory, and in every house banners were raised in his name. At his birth, a birth festival was held, and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since at his birth the glory of all the world
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 173]

children.text:
āpūritaḥ, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya viditayaśā iti nāmeti | viditayaśā dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ |
  yāvad apareṇa samayena nyagrodhārāmaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | prasādajātaś ca bhagavatpādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tena viditayaśasā dārakeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyaḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakebhyo dānapradānāni datvā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | sa yācitacīvaraṃ paribhuṅkte alpam ayācitam*, yācitapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān paribhuṅkte alpam ayācitam* ||
children.translated_text: was filled [with his fame], therefore let the boy's name be <s>Viditayaśas</s> (Of Known Fame).' The boy <s>Viditayaśas</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, yogurt, butter, ghee, the cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. And he was faithful, noble, of virtuous intentions, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, loving of the <s>Dharma</s>, and fond of his people. On a later occasion, he went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> grove. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, he purified his mind in the Blessed One's presence. Filled with faith, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave him such a teaching conducive to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, the boy <s>Viditayaśas</s> shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he gave gifts to <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the wretched, and wanderers, obtained his parents' permission, and went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. He used solicited robes but little unsolicited, and likewise used solicited alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites but little unsolicited.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta viditayaśasā karmāṇi kṛtāny yena jātamātrasya devatābhiḥ patākā ucchrāpitāḥ, yaśasā ca sarvaloka āpūrṇaḥ, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: viditayaśasaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | viditayaśasā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Viditayaśas</s> perform that at the moment of his birth the gods raised banners, his fame filled all the world, and upon going forth he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Viditayaśas</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Viditayaśas</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_70.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_70.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyī</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 174]

children.text: bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | yatra anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kārān kṛtvā svargamokṣaparāyaṇāni bhavanti | yāvad rājñā bandhumatā stūpamahaḥ kāritaḥ | tatra ca stūpamahe vartamāne mallānāṃ madhye patākā ucchrāpitā | yāvad rājamallena rājamallo nihataḥ | tatas tena mallapatākā āsāditā | sa tām ādāya anekaprāṇiśatasahasraparivṛto nānāvicitrair vādyair vādyamānair yena vipaśyinaḥ stūpas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya tathāgataguṇānām anusmaraṇaṃ kṛtvā tāṃ patākāṃ stūpayaṣṭyāṃ baddhvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān*: aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syām*, evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. Then <s>Vipaśyī</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having completed all the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder of clinging. King <s>Bandhumā</s>, having performed the worship of the Blessed One's relics, established a <s>stūpa</s> made of four kinds of precious materials, extending a full <s>yojana</s> in area, a <s>krośa</s> in height. There, many hundreds of thousands of beings, having performed acts of devotion, became destined for heaven and liberation. Then King <s>Bandhumā</s> proclaimed a <s>stūpa</s>-festival. During that <s>stūpa</s>-festival, a banner was raised among the <s>Mallas</s> (wrestlers). Then a royal wrestler was defeated by another royal wrestler. Then [the victor] obtained the wrestling-banner. Taking that banner, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of beings, with various musical instruments being played, he approached the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyī</s>. Having approached and having recalled the virtues of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he tied that banner to the <s>stūpa</s>-pole and made this aspiration: 'May I too become the recipient of such virtues. May I please a teacher of such a kind, and may I never displease him.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena malla āsīt*, ayaṃ sa viditayaśāḥ | yad anena vipaśyinaḥ stūpe kārāḥ kṛtās tena saṃsāre 'nantaṃ sukham anubhūtavān* | tenaiva hetunā idānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the wrestler — that was <s>Viditayaśas</s>. Because he performed those acts of devotion at the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyī</s>, he experienced boundless happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>. By that very cause, he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 175]

children.text: aṣṭamo vargaḥ |
children.translated_text: The eighth chapter.

children.text: tasyoddānam*:
children.translated_text: Its summary:

children.text: suprabhā supriyā caiva śuklā somā tathāparā |
children.translated_text: <s>Suprabhā</s>, <s>Supriyā</s>, and <s>Śuklā</s>, <s>Somā</s>, and further,

children.text: kuvalayā sundarī yaiva muktā caiva kacaṅgalā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kuvalayā</s>, <s>Sundarī</s>, <s>Muktā</s>, and <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>,

children.text: kṣemā virūpā + + vargo bhavati samuddhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣemā</s>, <s>Virūpā</s> + + the chapter is assembled.

children.text: AVŚ_71 suprabhā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_71: <s>Suprabhā</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā divyālaṃkārabhūṣitā maṇiratnena kaṇṭhe ābaddhena | tasmāc ca prabhā nirgacchati, yayā sarvā śrāvastī avabhāsate | tasyā jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād anayā jātamātrayā maṇiratnāvabhāsena sarvā śrāvastī avabhāsitā, tasmād bhavatu dārikāyāḥ suprabheti nāmeti | sā suprabhā dārikā aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattā dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | sā aṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sā dārikā śrāddhā bhadrā kalyāṇāśayā ātmahitaparahitapratipannā | tasyā ye ye yācanakā āgacchanti, tebhyas tebhyaḥ kaṇṭhād alaṃkāram avamucya prayacchati | datte ca punar alaṃkāraḥ prādurbhavati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He took a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A girl was born — beautiful, good-looking, and pleasing, adorned with divine ornaments, with a jewel-gem bound upon her neck. And from that [gem] a radiance emanated, by which all of <s>Śrāvastī</s> was illuminated. At her birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the girl's name?' The relatives said: 'Since at the moment of this girl's birth, all of <s>Śrāvastī</s> was illuminated by the radiance of the jewel-gem, let the girl's name be <s>Suprabhā</s> (Of Beautiful Radiance).' The girl <s>Suprabhā</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. She was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, yogurt, butter, ghee, the cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. She grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. The girl was faithful, noble, of virtuous intentions, devoted to her own welfare and the welfare of others. Whenever any supplicants came to her, she would remove the ornament from her neck and give it to each of them. And after giving it, the ornament would reappear.

children.text: yāvad asau dārikā krameṇa mahatī saṃvṛttā, tadā tasyā bahavo yācanakā āgacchanti, rājaputrā amātyaputrāḥ śreṣṭhiputrāś ca | tair upadrūyamāṇaḥ pitā cāsyāḥ kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: yady ekasmai dāsyāmi, anye me amitrā bhaviṣyantīti | yāvad asau dārikā pitaraṃ cintāparam avekṣyovāca: tāta kim asi cintāpara iti | tena so 'rtho vistareṇa samākhyātaḥ | dārikā kathayati: tāta na te śokaḥ kartavyaḥ | svayam evāhaṃ saptame divase svayaṃvaram avatariṣyāmīti | tataḥ śreṣṭhī rājñaḥ prasenajito nivedya śrāvastyāṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kārayāmāsa: saptame divase suprabhā dārikā svayaṃvaram avatariṣyati, yena vo yat karaṇīyaṃ sa tat karotv iti ||
children.translated_text: When that girl had gradually grown up, many suitors came for her — princes, ministers' sons, and guild-masters' sons. Her father, besieged by them, rested his cheek on his hand and sat absorbed in worry: 'If I give her to one, the others will become my enemies.' Then that girl, seeing her father absorbed in worry, said: 'Father, why are you worried?' He explained the matter to her in detail. The girl said: 'Father, you need not worry. On the seventh day, I myself will hold a <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice [marriage]).' Then the guild-master, having informed King <s>Prasenajit</s>, had a bell-proclamation sounded throughout <s>Śrāvastī</s>: 'On the seventh day, the maiden <s>Suprabhā</s> will hold a <s>svayaṃvara</s>. Let each of you do whatever needs to be done.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 176]

children.text:
tataḥ saptame divase suprabhā dārikā rathābhirūḍhā kāṣāyaṃ dhvajam ucchrāpya buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ citrapaṭe lekhayitvā abhiṣṭuvatī vīthīm avatīrṇā | sā tatra rājaputrair amātyaputraiḥ śreṣṭhiputraiś ca sotkaṇṭhK‍h̲dvīkṣyamāṇā vicitrābhiḥ kathābhiḥ saṃjñapyovāca: sarvathāhaṃ na kenacid aṃśena bhavatāṃ paribhavaṃ karomi | kevalaṃ tu nāhaṃ kāmenārthinī | buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāsmi | tasya sakāśe pravrajiṣyāmīti | tatas te nirbhartsitāḥ pratinivṛttāḥ | suprabhāpi dārikā bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | tasyā bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā suprabhayā dārikayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, abhinirhāraś ca kṛtaḥ | atha suprabhā dārikā utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat*: labheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣuṇībhāvam* | careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam iti | tato bhagavān saṃlakṣayati: anayā asmāc chāsane (Speyer: asmacchāsane) mahadvineyākarṣaṇaṃ kartavyam iti | tato bhagavatoktā: gaccha dārike parṣadam avalokayeti | tataḥ suprabhā dārikā jetavanān nirgatya tatrāgatā | tatraikaikasyaivaṃ bhavati: balenaināṃ harāma iti | te tām ākramitum ārabdhāḥ | tataḥ suprabhā dārikā tair upakramyamāṇā vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājo gaganatalam abhyudgamya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi darśayitum ārabdhā | āśu pṛthagjanasya ṛddhir āvarjanakarī | tatas te tad atyadbhūtaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā uddaṇḍaromāṇo mūlanikṛtta iva drumāḥ pādayor nipatya vijñāpayitum ārabdhāḥ: avatara avatara bhagini, yayaite tvayā dharmāḥ sākṣātkṛtāḥ | asthānam etad yat tvaṃ kāmān paribhuñjīthā iti | tataḥ suprabhā dārikā gaganatalād (Speyer: gagaṇatalād) avatīrya janakāyasya purastāt sthitvā tathāvidhāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavatī, yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam*
| tato bhagavatā mahāprajāpatyāḥ saṃnyastā | tatas tayā pravrājitā upasaṃpāditā ca | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyābhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the seventh day, the girl <s>Suprabhā</s>, having mounted a chariot, raised a saffron-colored banner, had the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, painted on a cloth panel, and descended into the main street, singing his praises. There she was gazed upon with longing by princes, sons of ministers, and sons of guild-masters. Having informed them with various courteous words, she said: 'In no way whatsoever do I show you disrespect. It is simply that I do not desire sensual pleasures. I have gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>. I shall go forth in his presence.' Then they, having been rebuked, turned back. The girl <s>Suprabhā</s> too approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, worshipped the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing her disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which the girl <s>Suprabhā</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>) and accomplished a miraculous manifestation. Then the girl <s>Suprabhā</s>, rising from her seat, arranging her upper robe over one shoulder, and joining her palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, Venerable Sir, obtain ordination, full admission, and the status of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>! May I practice the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'She is to bring about a great conversion of those to be trained in this dispensation.' So the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to her: 'Go, girl, and survey the assembly.' Then the girl <s>Suprabhā</s>, having gone out from <s>Jetavana</s>, came to that place. There, each one thought: 'Let us take her by force.' They began to assault her. Then the girl <s>Suprabhā</s>, being accosted by them, like a royal swan with outstretched wings, ascended into the sky and began to display various miracles. The supernatural power of an ordinary person quickly wins over [others]. Then they, seeing that exceedingly wondrous miracle capable of winning over gods and humans, their hair standing on end, like trees cut at the root, fell at her feet and began to implore: 'Descend, descend, sister! By these <s>dharmas</s> that you have directly realized — it is impossible that you would indulge in sensual pleasures!' Then the girl <s>Suprabhā</s>, having descended from the sky, standing before the multitude, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained the vision of truth. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entrusted her to <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>. She was ordained and received full admission. By striving, exerting, and applying herself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. She became an <s>Arhatī</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of her hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. She became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta suprabhayā dārikayā karmāṇi kṛtāny, yenābhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā, maṇiratnaṃ ca kaṇṭhe prādurbhūtam*, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: suprabhayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni {labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | suprabhayā dārikayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni} | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did the girl <s>Suprabhā</s> perform that she is beautiful, good-looking, and graceful, that a jewel appeared at her throat, and that having gone forth she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Suprabhā</s> herself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By the girl <s>Suprabhā</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 177]

children.text: kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_71.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_71.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvendhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ, tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | yā bandhumato rājño 'gramahiṣī vṛddhībhūtā, tayā vicitrāṇy ābharaṇāni śarīrād avamucya tatra stūpe dattāni | tataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavatī: anena kuśalamūlema cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena cārhatvaṃ prāpnuyām iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. When <s>Vipaśyin</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, having accomplished the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s> element without remainder, King <s>Bandhumān</s> performed the funeral honor for his body and erected a <s>stūpa</s> one <s>yojana</s> in extent on all sides, made of four kinds of precious stones, one <s>krośa</s> in height. The chief queen of King <s>Bandhumān</s>, having grown old, removed her various ornaments from her body and offered them at that <s>stūpa</s>. Then, falling at its foot, she made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, this generation of the thought [of awakening], and this renunciation of a gift, may I attain <s>Arhatship</s>!'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yā sā tena kālena tena samayena rājño bandhumato agramahiṣī āsīt*, iyaṃ sā suprabhā | yad anayā vipaśyinaḥ stūpe vicitrāṇy ābharaṇāni samāropitāni, tenābhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā saṃvṛttā | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? She who at that time, in that era, was the chief queen of King <s>Bandhumān</s> — she is this <s>Suprabhā</s>. Because she offered her various ornaments at the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśyin</s>, she became beautiful, good-looking, graceful, and endowed with all limbs and features. Because she made that aspiration, she has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_72 supriyā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_72: <s>Supriyā</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā śrāvastyadhivāsino janakāyasyātīva priyā | tasyā jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād iyaṃ priyā sarvajanasya, tasmād bhavatu dārikāyāḥ supriyeti nāmeti | jātismarā jātamātrā gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, the wife of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A girl was born — beautiful, good-looking, graceful, endowed with all limbs and features, and exceedingly beloved by the people of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. At her birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'What shall be the girl's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since this girl is beloved by all people, let her name be <s>Supriyā</s> (Well-Beloved).' Remembering her former birth, the moment she was born she spoke this verse:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 178]

children.text: dattaṃ hi dānaṃ bahu vālpakaṃ vā
children.translated_text: A gift given, whether great or small,

children.text: vistīryate kṣetraviśeṣayogāt* |
children.translated_text: is multiplied through the excellence of the field [of merit].

children.text: tasmād dhi deyaṃ viduṣā prayatnāt*
children.translated_text: Therefore, the wise one should give with effort

children.text: buddhāya lokendrasureśvarāya || AVŚ_72.1||
children.translated_text: to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Lord of the World, the Chief of Gods. // AVŚ_72.1 //

children.text: āthāsyā mātāpitarāv anye ca gṛhavāsinas taṃ vākyavyāhāraṃ śrutvā bhītās trastāḥ saṃvignā ākṛṣṭaromakūpāḥ (Speyer: āhṛṣṭaromakūpāḥ) kathayanti: piśācīva seyaṃ dāriketi | sā kathayati: amba nāhaṃ piśācī nāpi rākṣasī, kiṃ tarhi dārikā | icchāmi dānāni dātum iti | tato 'syā mātrā anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater niveditam*: evam eṣā dārikā brūta iti | tatas tena gṛhapatinā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditena bhagavān antargṛhe sabhikṣusaṃgho bhojitaḥ, tasyāś ca nāmnā dakṣiṇādeśanaṃ kāritam* ||
children.translated_text: Then her mother, father, and other members of the household, hearing those words, were frightened, alarmed, and filled with spiritual urgency, their hair standing on end (Speyer: <s>āhṛṣṭaromakūpāḥ</s>), saying: 'This girl is like a demoness!' She said: 'Mother, I am neither a <s>Piśācī</s> (demoness) nor a <s>Rākṣasī</s> (ogress), but rather a girl. I wish to give gifts.' Then her mother reported to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'This is what the girl says.' Then that householder, joyful, elated, and delighted, invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of monks to a meal inside the house, and had the merit-dedication made in her name.

children.text: yāvad asau dārikā krameṇa saptavarṣā saṃvṛttā, mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitā | sā sarvāsāṃ bhikṣuṇīnām iṣṭā kāntā priyā manāpā | yāvat tatra kālena mahādurbhikṣaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ durbhikṣāntarakalpasadṛśam*, yatrānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi annapānaviyogāt kālaṃ kurvanti | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma: gaccha ānanda, madvacanāt supriyāṃ vada: catasras te parṣadas traimāsyaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ pratipādayitavyā iti | tata āyuṣmān ānandaḥ supriyāṃ gatvovāca: bhagavān āha: catasras te pariṣadas traimāsyaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ pratipādayitavyā iti | tataḥ supriyā kṛtakarapuṭā bhagavata ājñāṃ śirasi kṛtvā kathayati: evam astv iti ||
children.translated_text: When that girl had gradually reached the age of seven, having obtained her parents' permission, she went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. She became beloved, dear, pleasing, and agreeable to all the nuns. Then, in the course of time, a great famine arose, comparable to the famine at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, in which many hundreds of thousands of beings perished from lack of food and drink. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and tell <s>Supriyā</s> in my name: "You are to provide the four assemblies for three months with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick."' Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> went to <s>Supriyā</s> and said: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> says: "You are to provide the four assemblies for three months with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick."' Then <s>Supriyā</s>, with palms joined, placing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s command upon her head, said: 'So be it.'

children.text: supriyā śrāvastīm abhisaṃprasthitā gocaravyavalokanārtham* | yāvad eṣā pravṛttir anāthapiṇḍadena śrutā | sa tvaritaṃ supriyāyā agrato bhūtaḥ kathayati: supriye kva gacchasīti | sā kathayati: bhagavān āha traimāsyaṃ vaiyāvṛtyakarmaṇi niyukteti | anāthapiṇḍada uvāca: alpotsukā bhava, ahaṃ tvāṃ sarveṇa pravārayāmīti | supriyā kathayati: kim atrāścaryaṃ yadi tāto dṛṣṭasatyaḥ pravārayati samantato 'ntarhitāni nidhānāny abhisamīkṣya | ahaṃ tu daridrajanasyānugrahaṃ karomīti | tathā pañcabhir upāsakaśatair alpotsukā kriyate | mālikayā devyā, varṣākārayā kṣatriyayā, ṛṣidattapurāṇābhyāṃ sthapatibhyāṃ, viśākhayā mṛgāramātrā, rājñā prasenajitā | aṭavīgatā tatrāpy amanuṣyair manuṣyaveṣadhāribhiḥ pravāryate | tayā evaṃ pravāryamāṇayā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghas traimāsyam upasthitaś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ | tatraiva ca traimāsye yujyamānaghaṭamānavyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyābhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Supriyā</s> set out for <s>Śrāvastī</s> for the purpose of inspecting the alms-round. When this news was heard by <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, he quickly came before <s>Supriyā</s> and said: '<s>Supriyā</s>, where are you going?' She said: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said that I am appointed to the service of attendance for three months.' <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said: 'Be at ease; I shall provide you with everything.' <s>Supriyā</s> said: 'What is so wonderful if father, who has seen the truth, provides, having surveyed the treasures hidden on all sides underground? But I wish to do a service for the poor!' Likewise, she was urged to be at ease by five hundred lay devotees, by Queen <s>Mālikā</s>, by the <s>Kṣatriya</s> lady <s>Varṣākāra</s>, by the architects <s>Ṛṣidatta</s> and <s>Purāṇa</s>, by <s>Viśākhā</s> <s>Mṛgāramātā</s>, and by King <s>Prasenajit</s>. Having gone into the wilderness, even there she was urged by non-human beings in human form. Yet even as she was so urged, the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples was attended by her for three months with robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. And during those very three months, by striving, exerting, and applying herself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. She became an <s>Arhantī</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. She became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.
