children.text: atha bhagavāṃs traimāsyātyayāt kṛtacīvaro niṣṭhitacīvaraḥ samādāya pātracīvaraṃ śrāvastyā rājagṛhaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ sārdhaṃ śrāvakasaṃghena | tataḥ supriyayā bhagavān antarmārge alpotsukaḥ kṛtaḥ | yāvad asau ### {alpo}dikām aṭavīm anuprāptaḥ, gaṇḍīdeśakālo jātaḥ, pathyadanaṃ ca nāsti | tayā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgha upaniveśitaḥ | tataḥ pātraṃ vāme pāṇau pratiṣṭhāpyovāca, pravyāhṛtavatī: yadi puṇyānām asti vipākaḥ, pātram evaṃvidhabhakṣyabhojyādinā paripūryeteti | tato devatayā divyayā sudhayā paripūritam* | tataḥ supriyayā anuparipāṭikayā sarvasya bhikṣusaṃghasya pātrāṇi pūritāni | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣā agrā me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇīnāṃ mama śrāvikāṇāṃ kṛtapuṇyānāṃ yaduta supriyā bhikṣuṇī ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, after the three months had passed, having finished his robe-making, taking his bowl and robe, set out from <s>Śrāvastī</s> to <s>Rājagṛha</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples. Then <s>Supriyā</s> urged the <s>Bhagavān</s> to rest along the way. When they reached a small stretch of wilderness and the time for the gong came, there was no food for the journey. She had the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples rest there. Then, placing her bowl in her left hand, she declared aloud: 'If there is indeed a ripening of merit, may this bowl be filled with food and drink of such a kind!' Then a deity filled it with divine ambrosia (<s>sudhā</s>). Then <s>Supriyā</s>, going in order, filled the bowls of the entire <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'She is the foremost, monks, among my nun-disciples who have made merit — namely, the nun <s>Supriyā</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta supriyayā dārikayā karmāṇi kṛtāny, yenāḍhye kule jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā abhimatā sarvajanasya, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: supriyayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | supriyayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds did the girl <s>Supriyā</s> perform, Venerable Sir, that she was born in a wealthy family, handsome, comely, pleasing, beloved of all people, and having gone forth, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Supriyā</s> herself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Supriyā</s> who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_72.2 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_72.2 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | atha kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ purvāhṇe nivāsya pātracivaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto vārāṇasīṃ nagarīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | yāvad anyataraḥ śreṣṭhī saparijana udyānaṃ gataḥ, prabhūtaṃ ca khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ nītam* | yāvat tasya preṣyadārikayā ### <Acording to Kalpadrumāvadāna it is: peśām ādāya paiṣṭikīm.> | {tayā} bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho 'ntarmārge dṛṣṭaḥ | tasyāḥ prasādajātāyā buddhir utpannā: kiṃ māṃ svāmī dvir api dāsīkariṣyati, yanv ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ bhojayeyam iti | tatas tayā bandhanatāḍanam agaṇayitvā bhaktapeḍām uddhāṭya bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho vicitreṇāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ | tataḥ śreṣṭhinaḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | yāvac chreṣṭhinā uktā: dārike kva sā bhaktapeḍeti | sā kathayati: bhagavān me kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ | iti
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of <s>Devas</s> and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. Then <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by a company of monks, attended by the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, entered the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms. Now a certain guild-master had gone out to a park with his household, and abundant food and drink had been brought along. Meanwhile, his servant-girl [was carrying a container of food]. She saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples along the road. Faith arose in her, and this thought occurred to her: "What if my master makes me a slave again? Let me rather feed the <s>Bhagavān</s>!" Then she, disregarding the punishment of bondage and beating, opened the food-container and satisfied the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of disciples with a variety of food. Then she went to the guild-master's presence. The guild-master said: "Girl, where is the food-container?" She said: "I have fed the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, with alms-food."

children.text: śrutvā śreṣṭhī paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ | tatas tena hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditenoktā: gaccha dārike, adyāgreṇa tvam adāsī bhava, yā tvaṃ mama suptasya jāgarṣīti | sā kṛtakarapuṭā gṛhapatiṃ vijñāpitavatī: anujānīhi maṃ*, bhagavacchāsane pravrajiṣyāmīti | tato 'syāḥ śreṣṭhinā pātracīvaraṃ dattam* | sā svakena pātracīvareṇa bhagavacchāsane pravrajitā | bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya pravacane daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vaiyāvṛtyaṃ kṛtam*, bhaktais tarpaṇair yavāgūpānair nityakair naimittikair (Speyer: nimittikair) dīpamālābhiḥ kaṭhinacīvarair dānapradānāni datvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: yan mayā bhagavate kāśyapāya kṛcchreṇa samudānīya dānapradānāni dattāni, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ pravrajyāhartvaṃ prāpnuyām iti ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the guild-master was filled with the utmost wonder. Then he, joyful, delighted, and overjoyed, said: 'Go, girl! From this day forward you are no longer a slave — you who stay awake while I sleep!' She, with palms joined, informed the householder: 'Grant me permission; I wish to go forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching.' Then the guild-master gave her a bowl and robe. With her own bowl and robe she went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. In the dispensation of <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, she performed attendance service for ten thousand years, giving gifts of food, nourishment, rice-gruel and drinks, regular and special offerings, lamp-garlands, and <s>Kaṭhina</s> robes, and made this aspiration: "By these roots of merit — my gifts of generosity given to <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, gathered with difficulty, my mind's aspiration, and my relinquishment of what should be given — may I attain ordination and <s>Arhatship</s> in the dispensation of <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>!"'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau preṣyadārikā, iyam asau supriyā | yad anayā bhagavān kāsyapaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ, tena āḍhye kule jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā abhimatā sarvajanasya | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? She who was that servant-girl — she is this <s>Supriyā</s>. Because she fed <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> with alms-food, she was born in a wealthy family, handsome, comely, pleasing, beloved of all people. Because she made that aspiration, in this very life she has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_73 śuklā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_73: <s>Śuklā</s> (The Bright One). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | śākyeṣu rohiṇo nāma śākyaḥ prativasati āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ na putro na duhitā | sa kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham*, na me putro na duhitā | mamātyayāt sarvasvāpateyam aputrakam iti kṛtvā rājavidheyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇanaimittikasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavair ucyate: devatārādhanaṃ kuruṣveti | so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberavāsavādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate | tadyathā ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatā balipratigrāhikā devatāḥ | sahajāḥ sahadhārmikā nityānubaddhā api devatā āyācate sma | asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti | tac ca naivam* | yady evam abhaviṣyat*, ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ | api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | katameṣāṃ trayāṇām* | mātāpitarāu
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. Among the <s>Śākyas</s>, there lived a <s>Śākya</s> named <s>Rohiṇa</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, neither a son nor a daughter was born. Resting his cheek on his hand, he sat absorbed in worry: 'My household is endowed with abundant wealth, yet I have neither son nor daughter. Upon my death, all my property, being without an heir, will pass to the king's control.' He was told by ascetics, brahmins, soothsayers, friends, relatives, and kinsmen: 'Make offerings to the deities!' Sonless and desiring a son, he prayed to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra), and other special deities — garden deities, forest deities, crossroad deities, intersection deities, and deities who accept offerings; he even prayed to deities who are innate, who share the same <s>dharma</s>, and who are constantly attendant. Now there is this common belief in the world that sons and daughters are born through prayer. But that is not so. If it were, each person would have a thousand sons, just as a <s>Cakravartin</s> king does. Rather, it is from the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. What three conditions?

children.text: raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau, mātā ca kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī, gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati | eteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca ||
children.translated_text: The mother and father are passionate and united; the mother is healthy and in her fertile period; and a <s>Gandharva</s> (being seeking rebirth) is present. From the conjunction of these three conditions sons and daughters are born.

children.text: sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati | anyatamā ca dārikā anyatamasmāt devanikāyāc cyutvā tasya prajāpatyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntā | tayā svāmine niveditam* | tataḥ svāminocyate: bhadre yadi putraṃ janiṣyasīty evaṃ kuśalam*, atha duhitaram*, tayaiva saha tvāṃ niṣkāsayāmīti | yāvad asāv aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā atikrāntā mānuṣyāṃ varṇam asaṃprāptā ca divyaṃ varṇam*, śuklair vastraiḥ prāvṛtā anupaliptaiva garbhamalena | yāvad rohiṇena śrutaṃ prajāptī te prasūtā dārikā jāteti, sa kupitaḥ praviṣṭaḥ | tato 'sya prajāptyā divyavastrapravṛtā dārikopanītā | tato rohiṇaḥ śākyo dārikāṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ | tasyā jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād iyaṃ śuklavastraparivṛtā jātā, tasmād bhavatu dārikāyāḥ śukleti nāmeti | śuklā dārikā aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattā dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | sā aṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | yathā yathā ca śuklā dārikā vardhate, tathā tathā tāny api vastrāṇi vardhante na ca malinībhavanti, na cāsyāḥ kāyo malenābhibhūyate ||
children.translated_text: He remained devoted to making prayers. A certain girl, having fallen from a certain divine assembly, entered the womb of his wife. She informed her husband. Then the husband said: "Good woman, if you will give birth to a son, that is well; but if to a daughter, I will cast you out together with her." In due course, after eight or nine months, she gave birth. A girl was born — beautiful, lovely, graceful, surpassing human complexion yet not having attained divine complexion, wrapped in white garments, entirely unstained by the impurities of the womb. When <s>Rohiṇa</s> heard that his wife had given birth and a girl was born, he entered in anger. Then his wife presented the girl, wrapped in divine garments, to him. Then <s>Rohiṇa</s> the <s>Śākya</s>, seeing the girl, was overcome with great amazement. At her birth, having performed the birth celebration, a name was determined: "What shall be the name of the girl?" The relatives said: "Since she was born wrapped in white garments, let the name of the girl be <s>Śuklā</s> (White)." The girl <s>Śuklā</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. She was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream, and other increasingly refined provisions. She grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. And as the girl <s>Śuklā</s> grew, those garments also grew and never became soiled, nor was her body ever overcome by dirt.

children.text: yadā śuklā dārikā krameṇa mahatī saṃvṛttā, tadāsyā bahavo yācanakā āgacchanti, rājaputrā amātyaputrāś ca | tatas tair upadrūyamāṇaḥ pitā cāsyāḥ kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: yady ekasmai dāsyāmi, anye me amitrā bhaviṣyantīti | yāvad asau dārikā pitaraṃ cintāparam avekṣyovāca: tāta kim asi cintāpara iti | tena so 'rtho vistareṇa samākhyātaḥ | dārikā kathayati: tāta na te śokaḥ kartavyaḥ, nāhaṃ kāmenārthinī, bhagavacchāsane pravrajiṣyāmi, anujānīhi māṃ tāteti | yāvad asau mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitā | yenaiva vastreṇa prāvṛtā jātā, tata eva paripūrṇaṃ pañcacīvaraṃ saṃpannam* | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyābhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: When the girl <s>Śuklā</s> had gradually grown up, many suitors came for her — princes and ministers' sons. Being importuned by them, her father, resting his cheek on his hand, was absorbed in worry: "If I give her to one, the others will become my enemies." Then the girl, seeing her father absorbed in worry, said: "Father, why are you worried?" He explained the matter to her in detail. The girl said: "Father, you should not grieve. I do not desire sensual pleasures; I will go forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Please permit me, father." Having obtained permission from both her parents, she went forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. From the very garment in which she was born wrapped, a complete set of five robes was produced. Through her diligent effort, striving and exerting herself, having understood this five-limbed wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable, and having overcome all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), she directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship). She became an <s>arhatī</s> (female arhat), free from passion toward the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, with a mind like the open sky and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood, with the egg-shell of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical insights), turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor. She became worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta śuklayā dārikayā karmāṇi kṛtāny, yenāḍhye kule jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā, śuklavastraprāvṛttā | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: śuklayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | śuklayā
children.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, questioned the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What deeds, Venerable One, were performed by the girl <s>Śuklā</s>, that she was born in a wealthy family, beautiful, lovely, graceful, wrapped in white garments, and having gone forth, directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship)?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "By <s>Śuklā</s> herself, monks, in previous births, deeds were performed and accumulated, their provisions gathered, their conditions ripened, standing ready like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. By <s>Śuklā</s>,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 182]

children.text: karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else will experience their results? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_73.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. (AVŚ 73.1)

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvad anyatarā śreṣṭhibhāryā śrāddhā bhadrā kalyāṇāśayā kenacid eva karaṇīyena ṛṣipatanaṃ gatā | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc ca bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | tato 'syā bhagavatā kāśyapena dharmo deśitaḥ | tayā labdhaprasādayā bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham antargṛhe bhojayitvā bhikṣusaṃghāya kaṭhinacīvaram anupradattam*, krameṇa ca mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitā ||
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, monks, in the past, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. A certain merchant's wife, faithful, virtuous, with good intentions, went to <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> on some errand. There she saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, encircled by a fathom-wide aura, with radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Upon seeing him, having paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, she sat down before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> taught her the <s>Dharma</s>. Having gained faith, she fed the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the monastic community in her home, offered <s>kaṭhina</s> robes to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks), and in due course, having obtained permission from both her parents, she went forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau śreṣṭhibhāryā, eṣaivāsau śuklā bhikṣuṇī | yad anayā bhikṣusaṃghāya kaṭhinacīvaram anupradattaṃ tena śuklavastraprāvṛttā jātā | yad brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitas teneha janmany arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? That merchant's wife — she is none other than the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) <s>Śuklā</s>. Because she offered <s>kaṭhina</s> robes to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>, she was born wrapped in white garments. Because she maintained the life of celibacy, in this birth she directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship). Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, entirely bright; for those mixed, mixed. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only in entirely bright deeds. Thus should you train, monks.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_74 somā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 74: <s>Somā</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamo brāhmaṇa āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī trayāṇāṃ vedānāṃ pāragataḥ sanighaṇṭakaiṭabhānāṃ sākṣaraprabhedānām itihāsapañcamānāṃ padaśo vyākaraṇaḥ | sa pañca māṇavakaśatāni brāhmaṇakān mantrān pāṭhayati | tena
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the monastic community, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, wealthy, of great riches and great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches, who had mastered the three <s>Vedas</s> together with the <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, with phonetic analysis, and the <s>Itihāsas</s> as the fifth, skilled in word-by-word grammar. He was teaching five hundred young <s>brāhmaṇa</s> students the sacred mantras. He
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 183]

children.text: putrahetoḥ sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā | tasyā jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: prāyaśo 'smākaṃ putrapautrikayā somanāmāni kriyante | bhavatu dārikāyāḥ someti nāmeti | somā dārikā unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* ||
children.translated_text: brought a wife from a family of equal status for the purpose of having a son. He sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with her. As he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A girl was born — beautiful, lovely, graceful, endowed with all major and minor limbs. At her birth, having performed the birth celebration, a name was determined: "What shall be the name of the girl?" The relatives said: "Generally in our lineage, the names <s>Soma</s> are given to sons and granddaughters. Let the name of the girl be <s>Somā</s>." The girl <s>Somā</s> was raised and nourished with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream, and other increasingly refined provisions. She grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.

children.text:
yadā krameṇa mahatī saṃvṛttā, sā paṇḍitā vyaktā medhāvinī paṭupracārā smṛtimatī śrutidharā ca | yāvad asyāḥ pitā māṇavakān mantrān pāṭhayati, sā śrutamātreṇodgṛhṇāti | śrutvā ca teṣāṃ śāstrāṇāṃ pūrvāpareṇa vyākhyānaṃ karoti | tato 'syā yaśasā sarvā śrāvastī sphuṭā saṃvṛttā | tīrthyāś cāsyā ahanyahani darśanāyopasaṃkrāmanti, tayā ca saha viniścayaṃ kurvanti | yadā bhagavān anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ tadā śrāvastīm āgataḥ | prāyeṇa ye paṇḍitāḥ paṇḍitasaṃkhyātāḥ, te bhagavato darśanāyopasaṃkrāmanti | tataḥ sā tān na paśyantī antarjanam āmantrayate: ko 'tra bhavanto hetur yenaitarhi śāstravido nopasaṃkrāmantīti | te kathayanti: bhagavān sarvajñaḥ śākyamunir nāmeha saṃprāptaḥ, sarve tatpravaṇāḥ saṃvṛttā iti | tato buddha ity aśrutapūrvaṃ ghoṣaṃ śrutvāsyāḥ sarvaromakūpā hṛṣṭāḥ (Speyer: sarvaromakūpāhṛṣṭāḥ ) | tatra somā dārikā buddhaśabdaśravaṇād bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc ca bhagavatpādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | atha bhagavān somāyā dārikāyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān*, yāṃ śrutvā somayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sā dṛṣṭasatyā mahāprajāpatyāḥ sakāśe pravrajitā | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ
devānāṃ pūjyā mānyābhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: When she had gradually grown up, she was wise, eloquent, intelligent, quick-witted, endowed with good memory, and one who retained what she heard. Whenever her father taught the young men the <s>mantras</s>, she would grasp them merely from hearing them once. And having heard the <s>śāstras</s>, she would explain them in sequence, from beginning to end. Thereby her fame spread throughout all of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Sectarian teachers came to see her day after day and engaged in discussions with her. When the Blessed One had attained supreme perfect awakening and came to <s>Śrāvastī</s>, most of the learned men who were counted as scholars would go to see the Blessed One. Then she, no longer seeing them, asked the household servants: 'What is the reason, sirs, that the learned scholars no longer come here?' They said: 'The Blessed One, the omniscient <s>Śākyamuni</s>, has arrived here. All have become devoted to him.' Then, hearing the word '<s>Buddha</s>' — a sound never heard before — all the pores of her body stood on end. Then the girl <s>Somā</s>, upon hearing the word '<s>Buddha</s>', approached the Blessed One. There she beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment she saw him, she worshipped the Blessed One's feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One, knowing the girl <s>Somā</s>'s disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave such a teaching conducive to penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, <s>Somā</s> shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, she went forth in the presence of <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>. Exerting herself, striving, and applying herself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. She became an <s>Arhantī</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of her hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. She became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: yadā bhagavatā bhikṣubhya ājñā dattā: yūyam eva bhikṣavo 'nvardhamāsaṃ prātimokṣasūtroddeśam uddiśateti, tadā mahāprajāpatyā: uddiśatu bhagavān prātimokṣam*, uddiśatu sugataḥ prātimokṣam iti | bhagavān āha: na hi bhikṣuṇyas tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ padaśo dharmam uddiśanti | yadi yuṣmākaṃ kācid utsahate (Speyer: ucchahate) sakṛduktaṃ dhārayitum*, evam aham uddiśeyam iti | tena khalu samayena sā bhikṣuṇī tasyām eva parṣadi saṃniṣaṇṇā saṃnipatitā | atha sā bhikṣuṇī utthāyāsanād yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam etad avocat*: uddiśatu bhagavān prātimokṣam*,
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One had given the monks the instruction: 'You yourselves, monks, should recite the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s> every half-month,' then <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s> said: 'Let the Blessed One recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>! Let the <s>Sugata</s> recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>!' The Blessed One said: '<s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, fully enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> do not recite the <s>Dharma</s> word by word to nuns. But if any of you is able to retain [the teaching] after hearing it once, then I would recite it.' At that time, that nun was seated in that very assembly. Then that nun rose from her seat, and joining her palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'Let the Blessed One recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>!
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 184]

children.text: uddiśatu sugataḥ prātimokṣam* | ahaṃ sakṛduktaṃ dhārayiṣye | tato bhagavatā vistareṇoddiṣṭaḥ, somayā sakṛdukto dhāritaḥ | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣā agrā me bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇīnāṃ mama śrāvikāṇāṃ bahuśrutānāṃ śrutadharīṇāṃ yaduta somā bhikṣuṇī ||
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Sugata</s> recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>! I shall retain it after hearing it once.' Then the Blessed One recited it in full, and <s>Somā</s> retained it after hearing it once. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'This, monks, is the foremost among my nun-disciples who have much learning and who retain what they hear — namely, the nun <s>Somā</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta somayā bikṣuṇyā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni, yenāḍhye kule jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā śrutidharā ca saṃvṛtteti | bhagavān āha: somayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | somayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did the nun <s>Somā</s> perform and accumulate that she was born in a wealthy family, was beautiful, good-looking, and pleasing, and became one who retains what she hears?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Somā</s> herself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Somā</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_74.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_74.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvad anyatarā brāhmaṇadārikā bhagavataḥ kāsyapasya śāsane pravrajitā | tayā tatroddiṣṭaṃ paṭhitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalaṃ ca kṛtam* | na tu śaktitaṃ naiṣṭhikaṃ jñānam utpādayitum* | yasyāś copādhyāyikāyāḥ sakāśe pravrajitāsīt*, sā bhagavatā kāśyapena śrutadharīṇām agrā nirdiṣṭā | tataḥ somayā bhikṣuṇyā maraṇakāle praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: yathā me upādhyāyikā śrutadharīṇām agrā nirdiṣṭā, evam aham apy anāgate 'dhvani yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapenottaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛtaḥ: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti, tasya śāsane pravrajitā bhagavatā śākyamuninā śrutidharīṇām agrā nirdiśyeya ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. A certain Brahmin girl had gone forth in the teaching of the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. She studied, recited, and mastered the aggregates, dependent origination, and the analysis of possibilities and impossibilities. But she was unable to generate the ultimate knowledge. And the preceptress in whose presence she had gone forth was designated by the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> as foremost among those who retain what they hear. Then the nun <s>Somā</s>, at the time of death, made this aspiration: 'Just as my preceptress was designated as foremost among those who retain what they hear, so may I too, in a future age, under the <s>Buddha</s> whom the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> prophesied as the young man named <s>Uttara</s> — "You, young man, in the age when the lifespan of people is a hundred years, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>" — having gone forth in his teaching, may I be designated by the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> as foremost among those who retain what they hear.'

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau brāhmaṇadārikā āsīt*, iyaṃ sā somā bhikṣuṇī | yad anayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*, tena śrutidharīṇām agrā nirdiṣṭā | yad anayā tasyoddiṣṭaṃ paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitam*, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? She who was the Brahmin girl — she is this nun <s>Somā</s>. Because she made that aspiration, she has been designated as foremost among those who retain what they hear. Because she studied, recited, and practiced [the teachings of <s>Kāśyapa</s>], she has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 185]

children.text: AVŚ_75 kuvalayā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_75: <s>Kuvalayā</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | tena khalu samayena rājagṛhe nagare girivalgusamāgamo nāma parva pratyupasthitam* | tatra sarvebhyaḥ ṣaḍbhyo mahānagarebhyo janakāyaḥ saṃnipatati | yāvad dakṣiṇāpathān naṭācārya āgataḥ | tasya duhitā kuvalayā nāma abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā | sā rūpayauvanārogyamadamattā | yadā raṅgamadhyam avatarati, tadā sarvaprekṣakaiḥ sotkaṇṭhair udvīkṣyate | ye cāpratisaṃkhyānabahulās teṣāṃ manāṃsyākarṣati | tatra yadā parva pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati, tadā pūraṇaprabhṛtayaḥ saparṣatkā upasaṃkrāmanti | tataḥ kuvalayā dārikā janakāyam uvāca: asti bhavanto rājagṛhe nagare kaścin manuṣyabhūto yo me rūpeṇa samo viśiṣṭataro veti | janakāyenoktā: asti śramaṇo gautamaḥ saparivāra iti | kuvalayovāca: kim asau manuṣyabhūto 'tha deva iti | manuṣyabhūtaḥ sa tu sarvajña iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. At that time, the festival called <s>Girivalgusamāgama</s> had arrived in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. People assembled there from all the six great cities. A dance-master had arrived from the southern region (<s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>). His daughter, named <s>Kuvalayā</s>, was beautiful, lovely, and charming, endowed with all major and minor limbs. She was intoxicated with the pride of her beauty, youth, and health. When she descended into the arena, all the spectators would gaze at her with eager anticipation. And she captivated the minds of those who were heedless. Now when the festival arrived, <s>Pūraṇa</s> and the other [sectarian teachers], together with their followers, would come. Then the girl <s>Kuvalayā</s> addressed the crowd: 'Is there anyone in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, whether human or otherwise, who is my equal or superior in beauty?' The crowd said: 'There is the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, together with his retinue.' <s>Kuvalayā</s> said: 'Is he a human being or a god?' 'He is a human being, but he is omniscient.'

children.text: tatas tadvacanam upaśrutya kuvalayā sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitā bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ purastāt sthitvā nṛtyati gāyati vādayate strīliṅgāni strīcihnāni strīnimittāni copadarśayati | ye sarāgā bhikṣavas te tayā saṃbhrāmitāḥ | tato bhagavān rāgabahulānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ vinayanārthaṃ kuvalayāyāś ca rūpayauvanamadāpanayanārthaṃ tadrūpān ṛddhyabhisaṃkārān abhisaṃkṛtavān*, yena kuvalayā jīrṇā vṛddhā palitaśiraskā khaṇḍadantā kubjagopānasīvaktrā nirmitā | tatkālasamanantaram eva kuvalāyā ātmānaṃ bībhatsam abhivīkṣya yo 'sau rūpayauvanamadaḥ sa prativigataḥ | rāgabahulāś ca bhikṣavaḥ saṃvignāḥ | tataḥ kuvalayā apagatamadā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ vijñāpitavatī: sādhu me bhagavāṃs tathā dharmaṃ deśayatu, yathāham asmāt pūtikalevarād (Speyer: pūtikaḍevarād) alpakṛcchreṇa parimucyeyeti | atha bhagavān kuvalāyās teṣāṃ cāvītarāgāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tāthavidhāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān*, yāṃ śrutvā kaiścid viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam*, kaiścid anāgāmiphalm*, kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | kuvalayāpi labdhaprasādā bhagavatsakāśe pravrajitā | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā
children.translated_text: Then, hearing those words, <s>Kuvalayā</s>, adorned with all her ornaments, approached the Blessed One's presence. Having approached, she stood before the Blessed One and danced, sang, played instruments, and displayed feminine gestures, feminine marks, and feminine signs. Those monks who had passion were bewitched by her. Then the Blessed One, for the purpose of disciplining the monks full of passion, and for the purpose of removing <s>Kuvalayā</s>'s intoxication with beauty and youth, performed such a miraculous transformation by his supernatural power that <s>Kuvalayā</s> was made to appear old, aged, grey-haired, with broken teeth, bent and hump-backed in face like a rafter. Immediately thereafter, <s>Kuvalayā</s>, seeing herself in that repulsive [form], lost her intoxication with beauty and youth. And the monks full of passion were struck with spiritual urgency. Then <s>Kuvalayā</s>, her pride gone, worshipped the Blessed One's feet with her head and petitioned the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that I may with little difficulty be freed from this foul body!' Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition, inclination, nature, and character of <s>Kuvalayā</s> and of those monks who had not yet become free from passion, delivered such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, some shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-existing body), rising with its twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (Stream-entry); some [realized] the fruit of <s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s> (Once-returner); some the fruit of <s>Anāgāmin</s> (Non-returner); and some, having gone forth, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. <s>Kuvalayā</s> too, having gained faith, went forth in the Blessed One's presence. Exerting herself, striving, and applying herself — having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable and ever-changing, and having struck down all the courses of conditioned formations by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving — through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>, she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. She became an <s>Arhatī</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of her hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 186]

children.text: bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā | tair api naṭais tena saṃvegena sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. She became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Those actors too, through that spiritual urgency, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s>, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavatā kuvalayā naṭadārikā rūpayauvanamadamattā jarayā saṃvejya yāvad atyantaniṣṭhe nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitā iti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ mayā vigatarāgeṇa vigatadveṣeṇa vigatamohena parimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ sarvajñena sarvākārajñena sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena kuvalayā dārikā rūpayauvanamadamattā jarayā saṃvejya yāvad atyantaniṣṭhe nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitā | yat tu mayā atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ kuvalayā dārikā saṃvejya pañcasu vratapradeśeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitā | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the Blessed One, having caused <s>Kuvalayā</s> the dancer's daughter — intoxicated with the pride of her beauty and youth — to feel spiritual urgency through [showing her] old age, established her in ultimate <s>Nirvāṇa</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'What is so wonderful in this, monks, that now — by me, one free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, omniscient, knowing all modes, having attained mastery over all knowledge and its objects — the girl <s>Kuvalayā</s>, intoxicated with the pride of her beauty and youth, has been made to feel spiritual urgency through [showing her] old age and established in ultimate <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? But in a past age, by me — one who still had passion, still had hatred, still had delusion, not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — the girl <s>Kuvalayā</s> was made to feel spiritual urgency and established in five areas of ascetic observance. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | priyam ivaikaputrakaṃ rājyaṃ kārayati | yāvad asau rājā devyā saha krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa devī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dāriko jāto abhirūpo darśanīyo prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaś chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhur vistīrṇalalāṭa uccaghoṣaṇaḥ saṃgatabrūs tuṅganāsaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya pitā kāśirājaḥ, ayaṃ cābhirūpo darśaniyaḥ prāsādikaḥ, tasmād bhavatu dārikasya kāśisundara iti nāma | kāśisundaro dārakaḥ aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | yadā mahāvṛttas tadā yauvarājye 'bhiṣiktaḥ | so 'nekadoṣaduṣṭam anarthamūlaṃ rājatvaṃ viditvā ṛiṣiṣu pravrajitaḥ | sa ca himavatkandare prativasati phalamūlāṃbubhakto 'jinavalkaladhārī agnihotrikaḥ | yāvad apareṇa samayena phalānām artham anyataraṃ parvatakandaram anupravṛttaḥ | yāvat tatra kinnaradārikā | ṛiṣikumāraṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃraktā nṛtyati gāyati vādayati strīcihnāni strīnimittāni strīvikrīḍitāny upadarśayati | yāvat kāśisundareṇa ṛṣiṇā tasyā dārikāyā dharmadeśanā dattā | jīrṇāsi bhagini, prathamas te svaro madhuraḥ snigdhaś ca, paścimas te jarjarībhūta iti | tatas tena tasyā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā kinnarakanyāyā yo 'bhūd rūpamadaḥ
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. He guarded the kingdom as though it were his beloved only son. Now that king was sporting, enjoying himself, and amusing himself with the queen. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, in the course of time the queen became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, fair-complexioned, golden in color, with a head shaped like a parasol, with long arms, a broad forehead, a deep voice, joined eyebrows, a prominent nose, and endowed with all major and minor limbs. At his birth, a birth festival was held, and a name was determined: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since his father is the King of <s>Kāśī</s>, and since he is handsome, beautiful, and pleasing to behold, let the boy's name be <s>Kāśisundara</s> (Beauty of <s>Kāśī</s>).' The boy <s>Kāśisundara</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two to carry him on their hips, two as wet-nurses, two as bath-nurses, and two as playmates. He was raised by those eight nurses and grew up nourished on milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. When he had grown up, he was consecrated as crown prince. Perceiving that kingship was corrupted by many faults and a root of misfortune, he went forth among the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages). He dwelt in a Himalayan cave, subsisting on fruits, roots, and water, clothed in antelope-hide and bark-garments, maintaining the sacred fire. On a later occasion, he went to another mountain cave in search of fruits. There he encountered a <s>Kinnarī</s> maiden. Seeing the young sage, she became enamored and began to dance, sing, play instruments, and display feminine gestures, feminine marks, and feminine frolics. Then the sage <s>Kāśisundara</s> gave her a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>: 'Sister, you are old. At first your voice was sweet and smooth, but now it has become decrepit.' Then he gave her such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, the <s>Kinnarī</s> maiden's intoxication with her beauty
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 187]

children.text: sa prativigataḥ | tayā prasādajātayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: yasmin samaye 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyethāḥ, tadā te 'haṃ śrāvikā syām iti ||
children.translated_text: was dispelled. Filled with faith, she made this aspiration: 'At the time when you attain unsurpassed perfect awakening, may I be your disciple.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena ṛṣikumāro babhūva, ahaṃ saḥ | kinnarakanyā imam eva kuvalayā | bhikṣavo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti: kāni bhadanta kuvalayayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni, yenābhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā saṃvṛttā, kāni karmaṇi kṛtāni yenārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam api | bhagavān āha: kuvalayayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | kuvalayayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the young sage — that was I. The <s>Kinnarī</s> maiden is this very <s>Kuvalayā</s>.' The monks asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Kuvalayā</s> perform and accumulate that she became beautiful, good-looking, and pleasing, and what deeds did she perform that she attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'It was <s>Kuvalayā</s> herself, monks, who in former births performed and accumulated deeds, whose requisite conditions had been gathered, whose causes had matured, which stood before her like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass. <s>Kuvalayā</s> performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their results]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_75.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_75.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ krakucchando nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa śobhāvatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad dakṣiṇāpathād anyataro naṭācārya āgataḥ | tatra śobhanena (Speyer: śobhena) rājñā bhagavataḥ sakāśāt satyadarśanaṃ kṛtvā naṭācāryāṇām ājñā dattā: bauddhaṃ nāṭakaṃ mama purastān nāṭayitavyam iti | tair ājñā śirasi pratigṛhītā: evaṃ bhadanteti | tataḥ sarvanaṭair bauddhaṃ nāṭakaṃ vicārya muninirjitaṃ kṛtam* | yāvad rājño 'mātyagaṇaparivṛtasya purato naṭā nāṭayitum ārabdhāḥ | tatra naṭācāryaḥ svayam eva buddhaveṣeṇāvatīrṇaḥ, pariśiṣṭā naṭā bhikṣuveṣeṇa | tato rājñā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramuditena naṭācāryapramukho naṭagaṇo mahatā dhanaskandhenācchāditaḥ | tatas te bhagavacchāsane labdhaprasādā dānapradānāni datvā samyakpraṇidhānaṃ cakruḥ: anena vayaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca anāgatān buddhān ārāgayema, mā virāgayemeti ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, when the lifespan of people was forty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Krakucchanda</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Śobhāvatī</s>. There, a certain master of actors came from the Deccan. King <s>Śobhana</s> (Speyer: <s>Śobha</s>), having gained the vision of truth in the Blessed One's presence, gave an order to the master of actors: "A Buddhist drama must be performed before me." They accepted the order respectfully: "So be it, Venerable Sir." Then all the actors, having composed a Buddhist drama called <s>Muninirjita</s> ("Conquered by the Sage"), prepared it. Before the king, surrounded by his retinue of ministers, the actors began to perform. There the master of actors himself descended [on stage] in the guise of the <s>Buddha</s>, and the remaining actors in the guise of monks. Then the king, joyful, pleased, and delighted, covered the troupe of actors headed by the master with a great heap of wealth. Then they, having gained faith in the Blessed One's teaching, gave charitable gifts and made a proper aspiration: "By this root of merit, this generation of the thought [of awakening], and this relinquishment of gifts, may we please the <s>Buddhas</s> of the future and not displease them."'

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo ye te naṭāḥ, ime te kuvalayāpramukhāḥ | yad ebhis tatra praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'What do you think, monks? Those actors — they are these very ones headed by <s>Kuvalayā</s>. Because they made that aspiration there, they have now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, deeds that are entirely dark have entirely dark results; entirely bright [deeds have] entirely bright [results]; mixed [deeds have] mixed [results]. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 188]

children.text: AVŚ_76 kāśisundarī | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_76: <s>Kāśisundarī</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho vārāṇasyāṃ viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ rājā brahmadatto rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | priyam ivaikaputrakaṃ rājyaṃ pālayati | yāvad asau rājā devyā saha krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa devī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā | tasyā jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād iyaṃ kāśirājasya duhitā surūpā ca, tasmād bhavatu dārikāyāḥ kāśisundarīti nāmeti | kāśisundarī dārikā aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattā dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | sā 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. In the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, King <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. He protected his kingdom as though it were his beloved only son. That king sported, delighted, and amused himself with his queen. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, in the course of time the queen became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A girl was born — beautiful, good-looking, graceful, endowed with all limbs and features. At her birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'What shall be the girl's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since she is the daughter of the king of <s>Kāśī</s> and is beautiful, let the girl's name be <s>Kāśisundarī</s> (Beauty of Kāśī).' The girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. She was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses, nourished on milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other excellent and choice provisions. She grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond.

children.text: yadā kāśisundarī dārikā krameṇa mahatī saṃvṛttā, tadā prātisīmaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ rājabhī rājñe brahmadattasya dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam*: śrutam asmābhir yathā tava duhitā jāteti | tad arhasy asmākaṃ putrāṇām anyatarasmai anupradātum iti | tato rājā śokāgāraṃ praviśya kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaś cintayati: yady ekasmai dāsyāmi, apareṇa saha me (Speyer: me saha) virodho bhaviṣyatīti | kāśisundarī dārikā sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā pituḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | tayā pitā śokārto dṛṣṭaḥ pṛṣṭaś ca: tāta kimarthaṃ śokaḥ kriyata iti | pitrā asyā yathābhūtaṃ samākhyātam* | tataḥ kāśisundarī pitaram uvāca: kriyatāṃ tāta prātisīmānāṃ rājñāṃ dūtasaṃpreṣaṇam* | saptame divase kāśisundarī dārikā svayaṃvaram avatariṣyati | yena vo yat karaṇīyaṃ sa tat karotv iti | yāvat saptame divase ṣaṭ prātisīmā rājānaḥ saṃnipatitāḥ | kāśisundary api ratham abhiruhya kāṣāyaṃ dhvajam ucchrāpya buddhapaṭaṃ hastena gṛhītvā rājasabhāṃ gatvovāca: śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ prātisīmā rājānaḥ | nāhaṃ bhavatāṃ rūpayauvanakulabhogaiśvaryaṃ tulayāmi, api tu nāhaṃ kāmair arthinī | ya eṣa eva me bhagavān buddhaḥ paṭe likhitas tasyāhaṃ śrāvikā | asya śāsane pravrajiṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: When the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> had gradually grown up, six neighboring kings sent messengers to King <s>Brahmadatta</s>: 'We have heard that a daughter has been born to you. Please give her in marriage to one of our sons.' Then the king, entering his private chamber, resting his cheek on his hand, sat absorbed in worry, thinking: 'If I give her to one, it will mean enmity with the others.' The girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, adorned with all ornaments, approached her father. She saw her father stricken with grief and asked: 'Father, why do you grieve?' Her father explained the situation to her truthfully. Then <s>Kāśisundarī</s> said to her father: 'Send word to the neighboring kings, Father: "On the seventh day, the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s> will descend for a self-choice ceremony (<s>svayaṃvara</s>). Let each of you do whatever you think fit."' On the seventh day, the six neighboring kings assembled. <s>Kāśisundarī</s> too, having mounted a chariot, raised a saffron banner, and holding a painting of the <s>Buddha</s> in her hand, went to the royal court and said: 'Hear me, honorable neighboring kings! I do not weigh your beauty, youth, family, wealth, and sovereignty; rather, I do not desire sensual pleasures. This <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s> painted here on this cloth — I am his female disciple. I shall go forth in his teaching.'

children.text:
yāvad ṛṣipatanaṃ gatvā bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam idam avocat*: labheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣu{ṇī}bhāvam* | careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam iti | tato bhagavato mahāprajāpatyāṃ saṃnyastā | tatas tayā pravrājitā upasaṃpāditā ca | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 189 --------------------
children.translated_text:
Having gone to <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> and worshipping the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, she said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, Venerable Sir, obtain ordination, full admission, and the status of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>! May I practice the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entrusted her to <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>. She was ordained and received full admission. By striving, exerting, and applying herself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing —
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 189]

children.text: viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā | tatas te rājaputrās tasyā rūpayauvanaśobhāṃ samanusmṛtya rāgamadamattāḥ pravrajitām api prārthayituṃ pravṛttāḥ | sā taiḥ prārthyamānā vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājo gaganatalam (Speyer: gagaṇatalam) abhyudgamya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayitum ārabdhā | āśu pṛthagjanasya ṛddhir āvarjanakarī | tatas te rāputrā atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā āhṛṣṭaromakūpāḥ pādayor nipatya kṣamāpayitum ārabdhāḥ: marṣaya bhagini | yathaite tvayā dharmāḥ sākṣātkṛtāḥ, asthānam etad yat tvaṃ kāmān parimuñjīthā iti | tataḥ kāśisundarī dārikā gaganatalād avatīrya janakāyasya purastāt sthitvā tathāvidhāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavatī, yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair mahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. She became an <s>Arhatī</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of her hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. She became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Then those princes, remembering her beauty and youthful charm, maddened by passion, continued to pursue her even after she had gone forth. When accosted by them, she, like a royal swan with outstretched wings, ascended into the sky and began to display various miracles. The supernatural power of an ordinary person quickly wins over [others]. Then those princes, seeing that exceedingly wondrous miracle capable of winning over gods and humans, their hair standing on end, fell at her feet and began to beg forgiveness: 'Forgive us, sister! Since you have directly realized these <s>dharmas</s>, it is impossible that you would indulge in sensual pleasures.' Then the girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>, having descended from the sky, standing before the multitude, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained great spiritual distinction.

children.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta kāśisundaryā karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenaivam ābhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam api | bhagavān āha: kāśisundaryaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | kāśisundaryā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: Then the monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Kāśisundarī</s> perform that she is thus beautiful, good-looking, and graceful? And that, having gone forth, she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Kāśisundarī</s> herself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Kāśisundarī</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_76.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_76.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe triṃśadvarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kanakamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | ### <The name of the place is missing.> | yāvat tatrānyatarā rājaduhitā śrāddhā bhadrā kalyāṇāśayā ātmahitaparahitapratipannā | tayā vihāraṃ kārayitvā sarvopakaraṇaiḥ paripūrya bhagavate saśrāvakasaṃghāya pratipāditaḥ | kanakamunau ca samyaksaṃbuddhe pravrajya daśavarṣasahasrāṇi maitrī bhavitā ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was thirty thousand years, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kanakamuni</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. [The name of the place is missing.] There a certain king's daughter was faithful, virtuous, well-intentioned, devoted to her own welfare and the welfare of others. She had a monastery built, furnished it with all requisites, and presented it to the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of disciples. And having gone forth under the fully enlightened <s>Kanakamuni</s>, she cultivated <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) for ten thousand years.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yā sā rājaduhitā, iyaṃ sā kāśisundarī dārikā | yad anayā vihāraḥ pratipāditas tenābhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā saṃvṛttā | yat kanakamunau bhagavati pravrajya daśavarṣasahasrāṇi maitrī bhāvitā tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? She who was that king's daughter — she is this girl <s>Kāśisundarī</s>. Because she donated a monastery, she became beautiful, good-looking, and graceful. Because she went forth under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kanakamuni</s> and cultivated loving-kindness for ten thousand years, she has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 190]

children.text: AVŚ_77 muktā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_77: <s>Muktā</s> (The Pearl). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyāṃ puṣyo nāma śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā muktāmālayā śirasi baddhayā | tasyā jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asyā jātamātrāyā muktamālā śirasi prādurbhūtaṃ, tasmād bhavatu dārikāyā mukteti nāmeti | muktā dārikā aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattā dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | sā 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a guild-master named <s>Puṣya</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, in the course of time his wife became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A girl was born — beautiful, good-looking, graceful, with a pearl garland bound upon her head. At her birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'What shall be the girl's name?'
