The kinsmen said: 'Since a pearl garland appeared upon her head the moment she was born, let the girl's name be <s>Muktā</s> (Pearl).' The girl <s>Muktā</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. She was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses, nourished on milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other excellent and choice provisions. She grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond.

children.text: yāvan muktā dārikā krameṇa mahatī saṃvṛttā | tasyāḥ sā muktāmālā avatāritā punaḥ prādurbhavati | tataḥ sā dārikā kṛpaṇavanīpakān dṛṣṭvā bhāgasaṃvibhāgaṃ karoti | yadā ca pradeyā saṃvṛttā, tadā tasyā bahavo yācanakā āgacchanti rājaputrā amātyaputrāḥ śreṣṭhiputrāś ca | tato 'syāḥ pitā śokāgāraṃ praviśya kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaś cintayati: yady ekasmai dāsyāmi, anye me 'mitrā bhaviṣyantīti | tato 'sau dārikā pitaraṃ vijñāpayāmāsa: tāta kimarthaṃ śokaḥ kriyata iti | tena yathāvṛttaṃ sarvaṃ tat samākhyātam* | tato dārikā kathayati: tāta nāhaṃ kāmair arthinī | bhagavacchāsane pravrajiṣyāmīti | yāvad anāthapiṇḍadasya supriyo nāma kanīyaḥ putras tena pitā vijñaptaḥ | mamārthāyaitāṃ dārikāṃ yācasveti | tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena puṣyasya gṛhapater dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam*: dīyatāṃ muktā dārikā mama putrāya | evaṃ kṛtaṃ sāṃbandhikaṃ yāvajjīvasukhyaṃ kṛtaṃ ca bhaviṣyatīti | tataḥ puṣyeṇa gṛhapatinā svasyāṃ duhitari so 'rtho niveditaḥ | sā kathayati: samayato yadīndriyāṇāṃ paripākān mayā saha bhagavacchāsane pravrajati, evam ahaṃ taṃ bhartāraṃ varayāmīti | tena tathaiva kṛtam* | yāvad ubhāv eva gṛhān niṣkramya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitau | tābhyāṃ yujyamānābhyāṃ ghaṭamānābhyāṃ vyāyacchamānābhyām idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantau saṃvṛttau traidhātukavītarāgau samaloṣṭakāñcanāv ākāśapāṇitalasamacittau vāsīcandanakalpau vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośau vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptau bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhau | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyau mānyāv abhivādyau ca saṃvṛttau ||
children.translated_text: In due course, the girl <s>Muktā</s> (Pearl) grew up. The pearl necklace, whenever removed from her head, would reappear. Then that girl, seeing the wretched and destitute, shared her possessions with them. When she reached the age of betrothal, many suitors came for her — princes, ministers' sons, and guild-masters' sons. Then her father, entering the house of grief, resting his cheek on his hand, sat absorbed in worry, thinking: 'If I give her to one, the others will become my enemies.' Then that girl informed her father: 'Father, why are you grieving?' He told her the whole story as it happened. Then the girl said: 'Father, I have no desire for sensual pleasures. I shall go forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching.' Now <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> had a younger son named <s>Supriyo</s>, and he had requested his father: 'Ask for this girl on my behalf.' Then <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> sent a message to the householder <s>Puṣya</s>: 'Let the girl <s>Muktā</s> be given to my son. Thus an alliance shall be made and lifelong happiness accomplished.' Then the householder <s>Puṣya</s> conveyed this proposal to his daughter. She said: 'On the condition that, when his faculties have matured, he goes forth with me in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching — on that condition I accept him as my husband.' And so it was done. Both of them left the household life and went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying themselves, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), they directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. They became <s>Arhats</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. They became worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta muktayā karmāṇi kṛtāni yena muktāmālayā śirasy ābaddhayā, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: muktayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | muktayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds did <s>Muktā</s> perform, Venerable Sir, that she was born with a pearl necklace bound upon her head, and having gone forth, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Muktā</s> herself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Muktā</s> who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_77.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_77.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvad anyatamaḥ sārthavāhaḥ sa mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | tataḥ svasti susiddhayānapātra āgataḥ | tatas tena muktāhāraḥ paramaśobhana ānitaḥ | tasya ca bhāryā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā | tena tasyāḥ śirasi baddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of <s>Devas</s> and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. Then a certain caravan-leader descended into the great ocean. He returned safely with a successful voyage. From there he brought a supremely beautiful pearl necklace. His wife was beautiful, comely, and pleasing. He bound it upon her head.'

children.text: vārāṇasyām anyatamo gṛhaptiḥ śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ | tasya buddhir utpannā: yanv ahaṃ chandakabhikṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya śāsane pañcavārṣikaṃ kuryām iti | tena rājñaḥ kṛkiṇo niveditam*: icchāmy ahaṃ chandakabhikṣaṇaṃ samādāpya bhagavataḥ pañcavārṣikaṃ kartum iti | rājñā evam astv iti samanujñātaḥ | athāsau gṛhapatir hastiskandhārūḍho vārāṇāsyāṃ nagaryāṃ rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu cchandakabhikṣaṇaṃ yācituṃ pravṛttaḥ | yāvat sārthavāhabhāryā muktāhāraṃ śiraso 'vamucya tasmiṃś chandakabhikṣaṇe dattavatī | yāvat sārthavāha āgatas taṃ muktāhāraṃ śiraso 'panītaṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭavān*: bhadre kvāsau muktāhāra iti | tatas tayoktam*: āryaputra prītiṃ janaya, prasādam utpādaya, bhagavacchāsane chandakabhikṣaṇe datta it | yāvat sārthavāhena puṣkalena mūlyena niṣkrīya tasyai patnyai dattaḥ | sā necchati punas taṃ grahītum*, parityakto (Speyer: parityaktā) me iti | svāminocyate: bhadre mayā prabhūtena hiraṇyasuvarṇenāyaṃ krītaḥ | kasmān necchasīti | tato 'sau dārikā taṃ gṛhītvā prabhūtaṃ puṣpasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā gandhamālyāni ca gṛhītvā ṛṣipatanaṃ gatā | tato gandhakuṭyāṃ gandhapralepaṃ kṛtvā puṣpair ākīrya muktāhāraṃ bhagavato mūrdhni kṣiptavatī | sa sahasā bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya mūrdhani sthitaḥ | tataḥ prasādajātayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ labhinī syām*, evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a certain householder was faithful, virtuous, of good disposition, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>. This thought occurred to him: "Let me, through voluntary contributions, hold a quinquennial festival (<s>pañcavārṣika</s>) in the dispensation of <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>." He reported this to King <s>Kṛkin</s>: "I wish to solicit voluntary contributions and hold a quinquennial festival for the <s>Bhagavān</s>." The king consented, saying, "So be it." Then that householder, mounted on the back of an elephant, set out to solicit voluntary contributions at the thoroughfares, streets, squares, and intersections of the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. The caravan-leader's wife removed the pearl necklace from her head and gave it in that voluntary collection. When the caravan-leader returned and saw the pearl necklace removed from her head, he asked: "My dear, where is the pearl necklace?" She said: "Rejoice, noble son, and generate faith! I have given it in the voluntary collection in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s dispensation." Then the caravan-leader purchased it back at a great price and gave it to his wife. She refused to take it back, [saying]: "It has been relinquished by me." Her husband said: "My dear, I bought this with a great amount of gold and silver. Why will you not [accept it]?" Then that woman, having taken it, gathered an abundance of flowers, took garlands and perfumes, and went to <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>. Having anointed the perfumed chamber with fragrant paste and strewn it with flowers, she threw the pearl necklace upon the head of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. It immediately settled upon the head of <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>. Then, filled with faith, she made this aspiration: "May I too become one who attains such virtues, and may I please such a Teacher and never displease him!"'

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau tena kālena tena samayena sārthavāhabhāryā, iyaṃ sā muktā | yad anayā bhagavati kāśyape kārāḥ kṛtās tenābhirūpā darśaniyā prāsādikā | muktāhāraś cāsyāḥ
children.translated_text: 'What do you think, monks? She who at that time, in that era, was the caravan-leader's wife — she is this <s>Muktā</s>. Because she rendered service to <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, she became beautiful, comely, and pleasing. And the pearl necklace appeared upon

children.text: śirasi prādurbhūtaḥ | tenaiva hetunedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: her head. By that very cause, she has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_78 kacaṅgalā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_78: <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kacaṅgalāyāṃ viharati kācaṅgalīye vanaṣaṇḍe | tasyāṃ kacaṅgalāyāṃ kacaṅgalā nāma vṛddhā | sā ghaṭam ādāya udakārthinī kūpam upasṛptā | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate: gaccha ānanda, etasyāṃ vṛddhāyāṃ kathaya: bhagavāṃs trṣitaḥ, pānīyam anuprayacchasveti | sā ānandenoktā: ahaṃ svayam evāneṣyāmīti | yāvat kacaṅgalā pānīyaghaṭaṃ pūrayitvā bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ gatā | dadarśa kacaṅgalā buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanād asyāḥ putrasnehaḥ samutpannaḥ, stanābhyāṃ kṣīradhārāḥ prasūtāḥ | sā ūrdhvabāhuḥ putra putreti bhagavantaṃ pariṣvaktum ārabdhā | bhikṣavas tāṃ vārayanti | bhagavān āha: mā yūyaṃ bhikṣava imāṃ vṛddhāṃ vārayata | tat kasya hetoḥ:
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>, in the <s>Kācaṅgalīya</s> forest grove. In that <s>Kacaṅgalā</s> there was an old woman named <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>. She took a pot and, needing water, approached a well. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, and say to that old woman: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> is thirsty; please give him water."' She said to <s>Ānanda</s>: 'I myself shall bring it.' Then <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>, having filled a water-pot, went to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. <s>Kacaṅgalā</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment she saw him, maternal love arose in her, and streams of milk flowed from her breasts. She raised her arms [crying]: 'Son, son!' and began to embrace the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The monks tried to prevent her. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Do not prevent this old woman, monks. And why?

children.text: pañca janmaśatāny eṣā mama mātā āsīn nirantaram* |
children.translated_text: 'For five hundred consecutive births she has been my mother;

children.text: iyaṃ me putrasnehena gātreṣu samaślikṣata || AVŚ_78.1 ||
children.translated_text: she, with her son's love, clings to my body.' // AVŚ_78.1 //

children.text: saced eṣā nivāryeta mama gātreṣu śleṣaṇāt* |
children.translated_text: 'If she were prevented from clinging to my body,

children.text: idānīṃ rudhiraṃ hy uṣṇaṃ kaṇṭhād asyāḥ sravet kṣaṇāt* || AVŚ_78.2 ||
children.translated_text: at once hot blood would flow from her throat.' // AVŚ_78.2 //

children.text: kṛtajñatām anusmṛtya dṛṣṭvemāṃ putralālasām* |
children.translated_text: 'Remembering gratitude, seeing this one doting as a mother,

children.text: kāruṇyād gātrasaśleṣaṃ dadāmi anukampyayā || AVŚ_78.3 ||
children.translated_text: out of compassion I allow the bodily embrace, out of tender care.' // AVŚ_78.3 //

children.text: yāvad asau putrasnehaṃ vinodya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya | bhagavān cāsyā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā kacaṅgalayā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sā dṛṣṭasatyā gāthā bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: When she had dispelled her maternal love, she sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing her disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, she spoke this verse:

children.text: yat kartavyaṃ hi putreṇa mātur duṣkarakariṇā |
children.translated_text: 'What should be done by a son for a mother who has performed difficult deeds —

children.text: tat kṛtaṃ bhavatā mahyaṃ cittaṃ mokṣaparāyaṇam* || AVŚ_78.4 ||
children.translated_text: that you have done for me: you have made my mind inclined toward liberation.' // AVŚ_78.4 //

children.text: durgatibhyaḥ samuddhṛtya svarge mikṣe ca te aham* |
children.translated_text: 'Having rescued me from the lower destinies, [establishing me] in heaven and liberation,

children.text: sthāpitā sarvayatnena viśeṣaḥ sumahān kṛtaḥ || AVŚ_78.5 ||
children.translated_text: you have established me with every effort — a supremely great distinction has been accomplished.' // AVŚ_78.5 //

children.text: yāvad asau svāminam anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitā | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā | yadā bhagavān bhikṣuṇīnāṃ saṃkṣepeṇoddiśya pratisaṃlayanāya praviśati, tadā kacaṅgalā bhikṣuṇīnāṃ vyākaroti | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣāgra me bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇīnāṃ mama śrāvikāṇāṃ sūtrāntavibhāgakartrīṇāṃ yaduta kacaṅgalā bhikṣuṇīti ||
children.translated_text: Then she, having obtained her husband's permission, went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying herself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. She became an <s>Arhantī</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. She became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Whenever the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave a brief outline to the nuns and entered into meditation, <s>Kacaṅgalā</s> would explain it to the nuns in detail. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'She is the foremost, monks, among my nun-disciples who are expounders of the <s>sūtras</s> — namely, the nun <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta kacaṅgalayā karma kṛtaṃ yena vṛddhā pravrajitā, kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena bhagavān paścimagarbhavāsena *{S: paścimagarbhavāsena}* dhāritaḥ, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, sūtrāntavibhāgakartrīṇāṃ cāgrā nirdiṣṭā iti | bhagavān āha: kacaṅgalayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | kacaṅgalayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, questioned the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What deeds, Venerable One, were performed by <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>, that she went forth in old age? What deed was performed that she bore the <s>Bhagavān</s> in her last womb-dwelling? And having gone forth, she directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship) and was declared foremost among those who analyze the <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourses)?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "By <s>Kacaṅgalā</s> herself, monks, in previous births, deeds were performed and accumulated, their provisions gathered, their conditions ripened, standing ready like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. By <s>Kacaṅgalā</s>, deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else will experience their results? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_78.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. (AVŚ 78.1)

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani bodhisatvacaryāyāṃ vartamānasyaiṣā me pañca janmaśatāni mātā āsīt* | nirantaraṃ yadāhaṃ pravrajitum icchāmi, tadā mām eṣā vārayati | tasya karmaṇo vipākena vṛddhā pravrajitā | dānaṃ dadato me dānāntarāyo 'nayā kṛtaḥ | tena daridrā saṃvṛttā | kiṃ tv anayā naivaṃvidhāni maheśākhyasaṃvartanīyāni karmāṇi kṛtāni, yathā mahāmāyā kṛtavatī | tenāham anayā paścime na dhāritaḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajitā āsīt* | tatrānayā śaikṣāśaikṣā bhikṣuṇyo dāsīvādena samudācīrṇāḥ | tena dāsī saṃvṛttā | yat tatrānayā paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ sthānāsthanakauśalaṃ ca kṛtam*, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, sūtrantavibhākartrīṇāṃ cāgratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭā | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, monks, in the past, when I was practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> career, she was my mother for five hundred births. Whenever I wished to go forth, she would prevent me. By the ripening of that deed, she went forth in old age. When I was giving gifts, she created an obstacle to my giving. By that she became poor. However, she did not perform such deeds as would lead to the great role of bearing a supreme being, as <s>Mahāmāyā</s> did. Therefore I was not borne by her in my last birth. Furthermore, she had gone forth under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There she addressed the trainee and non-trainee nuns with the speech of a servant. By that she became a servant. But because she had studied and recited there, and developed skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and skill in the possible and impossible, therefore now she has directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship) and has been declared foremost among those who analyze the <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourses). Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, entirely bright; for those mixed, mixed. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only in entirely bright deeds. Thus should you train, monks.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 194]

children.text: AVŚ_79 kṣemā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 79: <s>Kṣemā</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena rājā prasenajit kauśalo rājā ca brāhmadatta ubhāv apy etau parasparaviruddhau | yāvad rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ svaviṣayaparyantaṃ gatvā kāṣṭhavāṭaṃ baddhvāvasthitaḥ, rājā brahmadattaś ca caturaṅgabalakāyaṃ saṃnāhya hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ nadyāḥ kūle kāṣṭhavāṭaṃ baddhvāvasthitaḥ | yāvad rājñā prasenajitkauśalena tatraivāgramahiṣī nītā | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | brahmadatto 'pi devyā saha krīḍati ramate paricārayati | yenaikadivasa eva rājñaḥ prasenajitkauśalasya duhitā jātā, brahmadattasya putraḥ || yāvad ubhayor api skandhāvāre ### brahmadattasya skandhāvāre pravartate yenāyam evaṃvidha utsava iti | tair ākhyātam*: rājño brahmadattasya putro jāta iti | brahmadattenāpi tathaiva pṛṣṭam* | kathayanti: rājñaḥ prasenajito duhitā jāteti | tato rājñā brahmadattena rājñaḥ prasenajito dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam*: śrutaṃ mayā yathā tava duhitā jāteti | diṣṭyā vardhase | asmākam api putro jātaḥ | kiṃ tu dīyatām eṣā dārikā mama putrāya | evaṃ kṛte sāṃbandhike yāvajjīvaṃ vairotsargaḥ kṛto bhaviṣyatīti | rājñā prasenajitā pratijñātam*: evam bhavatv iti | tatas tābhyāṃ parasparaṃ prītau kṛtāyāṃ kṣeme jāte rājñā brahmadattena dārakasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ kṣemaṃkara iti | rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena dārikāyā jātāyā jātimahaṃ kṛtvā kṣemeti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam* | tāv ubhāv apy unnītau vardhitau | yāvat krameṇa mahāntau saṃvṛttau ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the monastic community, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> and King <s>Brahmadatta</s> were both in conflict with each other. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, having gone to the border of his realm, set up a wooden stockade and stationed himself there, and King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, having equipped his fourfold army — the elephant corps, horse corps, chariot corps, and infantry — set up a wooden stockade on the bank of the river and stationed himself there. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> had brought his chief queen there. He sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with her. <s>Brahmadatta</s> also sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with his queen. On the very same day, a daughter was born to King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, and a son to <s>Brahmadatta</s>. In both military camps ### in <s>Brahmadatta</s>'s camp a festival was taking place, and they inquired about the nature of the celebration. They were told: "A son has been born to King <s>Brahmadatta</s>." <s>Brahmadatta</s> likewise inquired, and they said: "A daughter has been born to King <s>Prasenajit</s>." Then King <s>Brahmadatta</s> sent a messenger to King <s>Prasenajit</s>: "I have heard that a daughter has been born to you. Congratulations! A son has been born to us as well. Please give this girl to my son. If this is done, as in-laws, a lifelong cessation of hostilities will have been made." King <s>Prasenajit</s> agreed: "So be it." Then, with mutual affection established between them and peace achieved, King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, having performed the birth celebration for the boy, gave him the name <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, having performed the birth celebration for the girl, gave her the name <s>Kṣemā</s>. Both were raised and nourished. In due course they grew up.

children.text: atha sa dārako dārikāyā hārārdhahāramālāṃ badhnan kaṇṭhemaṇīn preṣayati | yadāsau dārikā mahatī saṃvṛttā, tayā te pṛṣṭāḥ: kuta etāni prābhṛtāny āgacchanti? preṣyair vistareṇa sa vṛtānta (Speyer: vṛttānta) āveditaḥ | śrutvā ca pitaraṃ vijñāpayāmāsa: tāta nāhaṃ kāmair arthinī, bhagavacchāsane pravrajiṣyāmi, anujānīhi māṃ tāteti | rājā kathayati: naitad dārike śakyaṃ mayā kartum*, yasmāt tava janmani mama kṣemaṃ jātam iti | tato rājñā prasenajitā kauśalena rājño brahmadattasya dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam*: eṣā me dārikā pravrajitum icchati | āgatyaināṃ gṛhāṇeti | yāvad rājñā brahmadattena divasaḥ pratigṛhītaḥ: saptame 'hani āgacchāmīti | yat te kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tat kuruṣveti | eṣa vṛttāntaḥ kṣemayā dārikayā śrutaḥ: saptame divase vivāho bhaviṣyatīti | tataḥ kṣemā bhītā trastā saṃvignā āhṛṣṭaromakūpā śaraṇapṛṣṭham abhiruhya jetavanābhimukhī buddhaṃ bhagavantam āyācituṃ pravṛttā | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Then the boy sent the girl necklaces, half-necklaces, garlands, and jewels for the throat. When the girl had grown up, she asked: "Where do these gifts come from?" The servants informed her of the whole matter in detail. Having heard this, she addressed her father: "Father, I do not desire sensual pleasures; I will go forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Please permit me, father." The king said: "This cannot be done by me, dear girl, because at your birth, peace was established for me." Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> sent a messenger to King <s>Brahmadatta</s>: "This girl of mine wishes to go forth. Come and take her." King <s>Brahmadatta</s> accepted a day: "I will come on the seventh day. Do whatever you need to do." This matter was heard by the girl <s>Kṣemā</s>: "The wedding will take place on the seventh day." Then <s>Kṣemā</s>, frightened, terrified, agitated, with hair standing on end, ascended to the roof of the palace and, facing the <s>Jetavana</s>, began to pray to the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>. She said:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 195]

children.text: kṛpakaruṇavihāro dhyāyamāno maharṣiḥ
children.translated_text: The great sage who dwells in compassion and mercy, meditating,

children.text: praśamadamavidhijñaḥ pāpahaḥ śāntacittaḥ |
children.translated_text: who knows the methods of tranquility and self-control, destroyer of evil, with a peaceful mind —

children.text: mama vidhivadapāyān mocaya tvaṃ hi nāthaḥ
children.translated_text: deliver me duly from misfortune, for you are the protector;

children.text: śaraṇam upagatāhaṃ lokanāthaṃ hy anāthā || AVŚ_79.1 ||
children.translated_text: I, without refuge, have come for refuge to the protector of the world. (AVŚ 79.1)

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛtt{ak}ānām ekārakṣāṇām ekavīrāṇām advitīyānām advayavādināṃ śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: In this regard, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unascertained, or unrecognized by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. For it is the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, sole protectors, sole heroes, without a second, speakers of non-duality, dwelling in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three bases of taming, who have crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, who have abandoned the five limbs, who have transcended the five destinies, endowed with six factors, who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, guides of the eightfold path, skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, whose fame fills the ten directions, distinguished by ten hundred powers of mastery — three times in the night and three times in the day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye they survey the world, and knowledge-and-vision proceeds: "Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into straits? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is heading toward the lower realms? Whom shall I, having lifted from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? For whom shall I plant wholesome roots not yet planted? For whom shall I ripen those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already ripened?" And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_79.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the time for those who are to be guided, like calves to be tended. (AVŚ 79.1)

children.text: atha bhagavān kṣemāyā vinayakālam avekṣya ṛddhyā upasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā kṣemayā anāgāmiphalaṃ prāptam abhijñānirhāraś ca | atha kṣemā atikrāntakāmadhātau labdhapratiṣṭhā ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, perceiving that the time had come for <s>Kṣemā</s>'s spiritual training, approached by supernatural power. Having approached, he gave such a teaching on the four noble truths that, upon hearing it, <s>Kṣemā</s> attained the fruit of non-returning and the exercise of superknowledges. Then <s>Kṣemā</s>, having transcended the realm of desire, was firmly established.

children.text: yāvat saptame divase vivāhakāle saṃprāpte pratyupasthite rājakumāre anekajanaśatasahāye vedīmadhyagatāyāṃ brāhmaṇena purohitena lājā ghṛtasarpiṣānupradattā | tato dārakadārikāhastasaṃśleṣaṇe kriyamāṇe kṣemā paśyatām anekeṣāṃ prāṇiśatasahasrāṇāṃ vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājo gaganatalam abhiruhya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayitum ārabdhā | tato rājā prasenajit kauśalo rājā ca brahmadattaḥ kṣemaṃkaraś ca rājakumāro 'nye ca kutūhalābhyāgatāḥ satvā vismayam upagatāḥ pādayor nipatya vijñāpayitum ārabdhāḥ: marṣaya bhagini ya ete tvayā dharmāḥ sākṣātkṛtāḥ, asthānam etad yat tvaṃ kāmān parimuñjīthā iti | atha kṣemā gaganatalād avatīrya janakāyasya puraḥ sthitvā tathāvidhāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavatī, yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | tataḥ kṣemā dārikā pitaram anujñāpya bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāntā | bhagavatā ca mahāprajāpatyāḥ saṃnyastā | tatas tayā pravrājitā upasaṃpāditā ca | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī
children.translated_text: When on the seventh day the time for the wedding arrived and the prince, accompanied by many hundreds of people, was present, and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> priest had offered parched grain anointed with ghee and clarified butter as she stood in the middle of the wedding altar, then, as the hands of the boy and girl were being joined together, <s>Kṣemā</s>, before the eyes of many hundreds of thousands of beings, like a king of geese with wings outstretched, ascended into the sky and began to display various miraculous feats. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, Prince <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, and other curious onlookers, overcome with wonder, fell at her feet and began to entreat her: "Forgive us, sister! Given the spiritual attainments you have realized, it is impossible that you should indulge in sensual pleasures." Then <s>Kṣemā</s>, descending from the sky and standing before the assembly, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, many hundreds of thousands of beings gained the vision of truth. Then the girl <s>Kṣemā</s>, having obtained permission from her father, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> entrusted her to <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>. She was then ordained and given full ordination. Through her diligent effort, striving and exerting herself, having understood this five-limbed wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable, and having overcome all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), she directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship). She became an <s>arhatī</s> (female arhat),
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 196]

children.text: saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā | yadā bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣā agrā me bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇīnāṃ mama śrāvikāṇāṃ mahāprājñānāṃ mahāpratibhānāṃ yaduta kṣemā bhikṣuṇīti ||
children.translated_text: free from passion toward the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, with a mind like the open sky and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood, with the egg-shell of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical insights), turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor. She became worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks, he said: "This one, monks, is foremost among my <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) disciples in great wisdom and great eloquence, namely the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> <s>Kṣemā</s>."

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta kṣemayā karmāṇi kṛtāni yena mahāprājñānāṃ mahāpratibhānām agrā nirdiṣṭā | bhagavān āha: kṣemayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | kṣemayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Kṣemā</s> perform that she was designated foremost among those of great wisdom and great eloquence?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Kṣemā</s> herself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Kṣemā</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_79.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_79.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvat tatrānyatarā śreṣṭhiduhitā bhagavataḥ kāsyapasya śāsane pravrajitā | tayā bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya śāsane dānapradānāni dattāni, dvādaśa varṣasahasrāṇi ca brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ, na ca kaścid guṇagaṇo 'dhigataḥ, yasyās tūpādhyāyikāyāḥ sakāśe pravrajitā āsīt*, sā bhagavatā kāśyapena prajñāvatīnām agrā nirdiṣṭā | tatas tayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: yathaiṣā upādhyāyikā prajñāvatīnām agrā nirdiṣṭā, evam aham apy anāgate 'dhvani yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena uttaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛtaḥ: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti, tasyāhaṃ śāsane pravrajitvā prajñāvatīnām agrā bhaveyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. There, a certain guild-master's daughter went forth in the teaching of the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. In the teaching of the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>, she gave gifts, and for twelve thousand years she maintained the life of celibacy, but she did not attain any host of virtues. The preceptress in whose presence she had gone forth was designated by the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> as foremost among those endowed with wisdom. Then she made this aspiration: 'Just as this preceptress was designated as foremost among those endowed with wisdom, so may I too, in a future age, under the <s>Buddha</s> whom the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> prophesied as the young man named <s>Uttara</s> — "You, young man, in the age when the lifespan of people is a hundred years, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>" — having gone forth in his teaching, may I become foremost among those endowed with wisdom.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau tena kālena tena samayena śreṣṭhiduhitā, iyaṃ sā kṣemā bhikṣuṇī | yat tayā dānāni pradattāni, tenāḍhye kule pratyājātā | yat tayā dvādaśa varṣasahasrāṇi brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? She who at that time, in that era, was the guild-master's daughter — she is this nun <s>Kṣemā</s>. Because she gave gifts, she was reborn in a wealthy family. Because she maintained the life of celibacy for twelve thousand years, she has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 197]

children.text: AVŚ_80 virūpā | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_80: <s>Virūpā</s> (The Deformed). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena prasenajit kauśalo rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | priyam ivaikaputrakaṃ rājyaṃ pālayati | yāvat sa rājā anyatamayā devyā saha krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārikā jātā aṣṭādaśabhir daurvarṇikair aṅgaiḥ samanvāgatā | tasyā jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā virūpeti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate | yadā krameṇa mahatī saṃvṛttā, tadā yasmai pradīyate, sa tāṃ virūpeti kṛtvā na pratigṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. He guarded the kingdom as though it were his only son. Then the king sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself with a certain queen. As he sported, delighted, and enjoyed himself, his queen became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A girl was born, endowed with eighteen ugly features. At her birth, a birth-celebration was held and the name <s>Virūpā</s> (Deformed) was established. When she had gradually grown up, whichever man she was offered to would refuse her on account of her deformity.

children.text: yāvad dakṣiṇāpathād gaṅgo nāma sārthavāho 'bhyāgato vistīrṇavibhavaḥ | tato rājñaḥ prasenajito buddhir utpannā: ayaṃ gaṅgasārthavāha etasyā doṣeṣv anabhijñaḥ | yanv aham asmai dāsyāmīti | tato rājñā rātrau saṃprāptāyāṃ bhagnacakṣuṣpathe (Speyer: bhagne cakṣuṣpathe) gaṅgaṃ dūtenāhvāpya sā dārikā sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitā bhāryārthe dattā gaṅgāya | ### gaṅgarasthā gaṅgarastheti saṃjñā prādurbhūtā ||
children.translated_text: Then a caravan-leader named <s>Gaṅga</s>, of extensive wealth, arrived from the southern region (<s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>). Then this idea arose in King <s>Prasenajit</s>: 'This caravan-leader <s>Gaṅga</s> is unaware of her faults. Let me give her to him.' Then, when night had fallen and the range of sight was broken, the king summoned <s>Gaṅga</s> through a messenger and gave the girl, adorned with all ornaments, to <s>Gaṅga</s> as his wife. ### And she became known as <s>Gaṅgarasthā</s> ('Dwelling by the <s>Gaṅga</s>').

children.text: yāvad gaṅgena sārthavāhena dvitīye divase prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ sā dārikā dṛṣṭā paramabībhatsā | yāṃ dṛṣṭvā rājāpekṣayā na śaknoty avamoktum* | svagṛhe dhārayati ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the second day, when dawn had broken, the caravan-leader <s>Gaṅga</s> saw that girl — supremely hideous. But having seen her, out of regard for the king, he was unable to reject her. He kept her in his own house.

children.text: yāvad gaṅgaḥ sārthavāhaḥ kasmiṃścit parvaṇy upasthite goṣṭhikānāṃ madhyaṃ gataḥ | goṣṭhikaiś ca kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ: saha bhāryayā amukam udyānaṃ yo no yāsyati, sa goṣṭhikānāṃ pañca purāṇaśatāni daṇḍam anupradāsyatīti | tato gaṅgaḥ svagṛham āgatya śokāgāraṃ praviśya kare kapolaṃ kṛtvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ | tasya buddhir utpannā: varam ahaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyām*, na cāham etām eteṣāṃ darśayeyam* | sahadarśanāc cāvagīto bhaviṣyāmīti | atha gaṅgo dvāraṃ baddhvā pañca purāṇaśatāni
children.translated_text: Then the caravan-leader <s>Gaṅga</s>, when a certain festival arrived, went among his guild-fellows. The guild-fellows had made a wager: 'Whoever among us does not go to such-and-such a park together with his wife shall pay a fine of five hundred <s>purāṇas</s> to the guild-fellows.' Then <s>Gaṅga</s>, having come home, entered his room of sorrow, rested his cheek on his hand, and sat absorbed in worry. This thought arose in him: 'It would be better for me to pay the fine than to show her to them. The moment they see her, I shall be disgraced.' Then <s>Gaṅga</s>, having locked the door, took five hundred <s>purāṇas</s>
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 198]

children.text: daṇḍaṃ gṛhītvā goṣṭhikānāṃ madhyaṃ gataḥ | tato dārikāyā mahad daurmanasyam utpannam*: kiṃ mamānenaivaṃvidhena jīvitena, yatra me na ca svāmicittaṃ sukhitam*, na cāham* | kim atra prāptakālam* | ātmānaṃ ghātayiṣyāmīti | tato rajjuṃ gṛhītvā avarakaṃ praviṣṭā udbandhanahetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the fine and went among the guild-fellows. Then great despondency arose in the girl: 'What use is this kind of life for me, where neither my husband's mind is at ease, nor am I? What is the right course? I shall kill myself.' Then, taking a rope, she entered an inner room with the intention of hanging herself.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛtt{ak}ānām ekārakṣāṇām śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ, ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Now, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unrealized, or uncomprehended by <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones. For it is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones — who are greatly compassionate, whose activity is for the benefit of the world, who give protection without exception, who dwell in calm and insight, who are skilled in the three means of taming, who have crossed the four floods, whose feet are firmly established on the four bases of supernatural power, who have abandoned the five factors [of the lower fetters], who have transcended the five destinies, who are endowed with the six factors, who have fulfilled the six perfections, who are adorned with the blossoms of the seven factors of awakening, who teach the eightfold path, who are skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, who possess the power of the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who are distinguished by their mastery over a thousand — three times at night and three times during the day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, to survey the world, and their knowledge-and-vision operates: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into straits? Who has fallen into difficulty, distress, and straits? Who is inclined toward the woeful states? Who is tending toward the woeful states? Who is heading toward the woeful states? Whom shall I, having lifted from the woeful states, establish in heaven and liberation? For whom shall I plant roots of merit that have not been planted? For whom shall I bring to maturity those that have been planted? For whom shall I liberate those that have matured?' And it is said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its boundary,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_80.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the appointed time for beings to be trained.' // AVŚ_80.1 //

children.text: tato bhagavatā jetavanāvasthitena kanakavarṇā prabhā utsṛṣṭā, yayā tad gṛhaṃ sūryasahasreṇevāvabhāsitam* | ṛddhyā copasaṃkramya tadgalād udbandhanam avamucya dārikāṃ samāśvāsitavān* | ṣaṇṇāṃ sthānānām āścaryādbhuto loke prādurbhāvaḥ | tathāgatasya tathāgatapraveditasya dharmavinayasya manuṣyatvasya āryāyatane pratyājātatvasya indriyair avikalatvasya kuśaladharmacchandakasya āścaryādbhuto loke prādurbhāvaḥ | tato bhagavatā tasyā dārikāyās tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | tato labdhaprasādayā bhagavān bhaktena pratipāditaḥ paṭena cācchāditaḥ | tato dārikāyā apagatā alakṣmīḥ | lakṣmīḥ prādurbhūtā | devakanyeva cāvarakam avabhāsamānā sthitā | bhagavān api prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, from where he was in the <s>Jetavana</s>, sent forth a radiance of golden hue, by which that house was illuminated as if by a thousand suns. Having approached by supernatural power, he loosened the noose from her neck and comforted the girl. There are six circumstances whose manifestation in the world is wondrous and marvelous: the manifestation of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, of the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> taught by a <s>Tathāgata</s>, of human birth, of rebirth in the noble domain, of possessing unimpaired faculties, and of desire for wholesome qualities. Then the Blessed One gave that girl such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, having heard it, she shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). Then, having gained faith, she offered the Blessed One food and covered him with cloth. Thereupon the girl's misfortune departed. Good fortune manifested. And she stood in the inner room, radiant like a goddess. Then the Blessed One departed.

children.text: tato goṣṭhikānāṃ buddhir utpannā: nūnam asya bhāryā paramadarśanīyā saṃvṛttā | sa eṣa īrṣyāprakṛtir daṇḍam utsahate dātum*, na ca tāṃ darśayitum icchati | yan nu vayam enaṃ viruddhair madyaiḥ pāyayitvā tāḍam ādāya gṛham asya gatvā bhāryāṃ paśyemeti | tatas tais taṃ ghanaghanena viruddhamadyena pānena kṣībaṃ (Speyer: kṣīvaṃ) kṛtvā tāḍam apahṛtya gṛhaṃ gatvā dvāram avamucya dārikā dṛṣṭā | tato dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam upagatāś cintayanti: sthāne 'sau na darśayaty asmākam iti | tatas te punar āgatya madyavaśāt suptam utthāpya
children.translated_text: Then an idea arose among the guild-fellows: 'Surely his wife must have become supremely beautiful. He is of a jealous nature and is willing to pay the fine, but does not wish to show her. Let us ply him with strong drink and then, taking the key, go to his house and see his wife.' Then they made him drunk with copious strong drink, took the key, went to his house, opened the door, and saw the girl. Upon seeing her, they were filled with the utmost wonder and thought: 'No wonder he does not show her to us!' Then they went back and, waking him from his drunken sleep,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 199]

children.text: ūcuḥ: lābhās te gaṅga sulabdhāḥ, yasya te evaṃvidhā darśanīyā dāriketi | tato gaṅgo bhūyasyā mātrayā duḥkhī durmanā saṃvṛttā | daṇḍaḥ svayaṃ mayā dattaḥ, ahaṃ cāvagīto jāta iti | tato durmanāḥ svagṛham āgataḥ | dvāram avamucya tāṃ bhāryāṃ dṛṣṭavān vanadevatām iva kusumitamadhye 'tīva vibhrājamānām* | tataḥ pṛcchati: bhadre kim etat*? kiṃ kṛto rūpaviśeṣa iti | tatas tayā yathāvṛttaṃ svāmine samākhyātam* | śrutvā tenāpi bhagavati śraddhā pratilabdhā ||
children.translated_text: said: 'What a gain for you, <s>Gaṅga</s>, well-gained, that you have such a beautiful girl!' Then <s>Gaṅga</s> became all the more distressed and unhappy: 'The fine has been paid by me willingly, and now I have been disgraced.' Then, dejected, he went home. Opening the door, he saw that wife — like a forest goddess shining resplendently amid blossoming flowers. Then he asked: 'Dear one, what is this? How did this transformation of your appearance come about?' Then she told her husband everything that had happened. Having heard it, he too gained faith in the Blessed One.

children.text: yāvad asau dārikā krameṇa bhartāram anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitā | tayā yujyamānayā ghaṭamānayā vyāyacchamānayā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhantī saṃvṛttā traidhātukavītarāgā samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhā | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyā ca saṃvṛttā ||
children.translated_text: In due course, that girl, having obtained her husband's permission, went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying herself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. She became an <s>Arhatī</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of her hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. She became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kiṃ bhadanta gaṅgarasthayā karma kṛtam*, yenāḍhye jātā | kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena virūpā saṃvṛttā, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: gaṅgarasthayaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | gaṅgarasthayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Gaṅgarasthā</s> perform that she was born wealthy? What <s>karma</s> did she perform that she became ugly, and that having gone forth she directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Gaṅgarasthā</s> herself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Gaṅgarasthā</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_80.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_80.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamā śreṣṭhibhāryā caṇḍā rabhasā karkaśā | asati buddhānām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya | yāvad anyataraḥ pratyekabuddhas tad gṛhaṃ praviṣṭo virūpaḥ | sa tayā bahu paribhāṣya gṛhān niṣkāsitaḥ: kenāyaṃ virūpo mama gṛhe praveśita iti | tataḥ pratyekabuddhas tasyā anugrahārthaṃ vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājo gaganatalam abhyudgamya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayitum ārabdhaḥ | tataḥ śreṣṭhibhāryayā vipratisārajātayā ### {kṣamasvety uktaḥ} | yāvad asau kṣamitaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaś ca | praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam*: yan mayā pratyekabuddhaḥ paribhāṣitaḥ, mā asya karmaṇo vipākam anubhaveyam*, evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhinī syāṃ*, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ ca śāstāram ārāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain guild-master's wife — ill-tempered, violent, and harsh. In the absence of the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arise in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and destitute, inclined to remote lodgings and meals, worthy of offerings as sole individuals in the world. Now a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, who was ugly, entered that house. She, having berated him at length, drove him out of the house, saying: 'Who let this ugly one into my house?' Then that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, for her benefit, like a royal swan with outstretched wings, ascended into the sky and began to display various miracles. Then the guild-master's wife, filled with remorse, [begged his forgiveness, saying 'Forgive me']. He was forgiven, and she offered him alms. She made this aspiration: 'Since I have berated a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, may I not experience the fruit of that <s>karma</s>! And may I become the recipient of such <s>dharmas</s>, and may I please a teacher even more distinguished!'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 200]

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yāsau śreṣṭhibhāryā, iyam asau gaṅgarasthā | yad anayā pratyekabuddhaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākenāḍhye rājakule pratyāgatā | yad virūpāvavādena samudācarya gṛhān niṣkāsitaḥ, tena virūpā saṃvṛttā | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajitā āsīt* | tatrānayā paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalam āyatanakauśalaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalaṃ kṛtam*, brahmacaryavāsaś ca paripālitaḥ, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? She who was that guild-master's wife — she is this <s>Gaṅgarasthā</s>. Because she offered alms to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> she was reborn in a wealthy royal family. Because she berated him as ugly and drove him from her house, she became ugly. Furthermore, she had gone forth under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There she recited, studied, attained skill in the aggregates, skill in the sense-bases, skill in dependent origination, and skill in what is possible and what is impossible, and she preserved the life of celibacy — therefore she has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 201]

children.text: navamo vargaḥ |
children.translated_text: Chapter Nine.

children.text: tasyoddānam*.
children.translated_text: Its summary (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.text: samudraḥ sumanāś caiva hiraṇyapāṇis tripiṭena ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Samudra</s>, <s>Sumanā</s>, <s>Hiraṇyapāṇi</s>, and <s>Tripiṭa</s>;

children.text: yaśomitropapādau ca śobhitaḥ kapphiṇas tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśomitra</s>, <s>Upapāda</s>, <s>Śobhita</s>, and <s>Kapphiṇa</s>;

children.text: bhadriko rāṣṭrapālaś ca vargo bhavati samudditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadrika</s> and <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> — thus this chapter is proclaimed.

children.text: AVŚ_81 samudraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_81: <s>Samudra</s> (The Ocean). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ sārthavāhaḥ | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato buddhir utpannā: yāvad ahaṃ yuvā, tāvad dhanasaṃcayaṃ karomi | paścād vṛddhāvasthāyāṃ sukhaṃ parimokṣye iti | tataḥ sārthavāhaḥ pañcavaṇikchataparivāro *{Vaidya: ŚvaṇikśataŚ}* yānapātram ādāya bhāryāsahāyo mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | yāvad prajāvatī āpannasatvā jātā | yāvat taraiva samudramadhye prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam*: yasmāt samudramadhye jātas tasmāt samudra iti nām | yāvad asau sārthavāhaḥ svastikṣemābhyāṃ saṃsidhhayānapātro mahāsamudrāt pratyāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain caravan-leader. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, this thought arose in him: 'While I am still young, I shall accumulate wealth; later, in old age, I shall enjoy it at ease.' Then that caravan-leader, accompanied by five hundred merchants, taking his ship and accompanied by his wife, set out upon the great ocean. Now <s>Prajāvatī</s> (his wife) had become pregnant. And right there, in the midst of the ocean, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, and graceful. At his birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'Since he was born in the midst of the ocean, let his name be <s>Samudra</s> (Ocean).' In due course, that caravan-leader returned safely and successfully from the great ocean with his ship.

children.text: yadā samudro darako mahān saṃvṛttas tadā pitrā sārthavāhatve pratiṣṭhāpya pañcavaṇikchataparivāro *{Vaidya: ŚvaṇikśataŚ}* mahāsamudraṃ saṃpreṣitaḥ | so 'nupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇo grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīpaṭṭanāny avalokayan samudratīram anuprāptaḥ | sa pñcabhiḥ purāṇaśatair vahanaṃ bhṛtvā pañca pauruṣeyān* gṛhītvā āhāraṃ nāvikaṃ kaivartaṃ karṇadhāraṃ ca trir api ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ | tatas teṣāṃ samudramadhyagatānāṃ kālikāvātena tad vahanam itaś cāmutaś ca paribhrāmyate | samudraś ca sārthavāhas tīrthikābhiprasannaḥ | so 'kālamṛtyubhayabhītaḥ ṣaṭ śāstṝn āyācituṃ pravṛttaḥ | tathāpi tad vahanaṃ vāyunā bhrāmyata eva | yāvad anye vaṇijo devatāsahasrāṇy āyācituṃ pravṛttāḥ | āhuś ca:
children.translated_text: When the boy <s>Samudra</s> had grown up, his father established him as a caravan-leader and sent him forth, accompanied by five hundred merchants, upon the great ocean. Traveling by stages, surveying villages, cities, towns, kingdoms, royal capitals, and ports, he reached the seashore. Having hired a vessel for five hundred <s>purāṇas</s>, and having taken five attendants, provisions, a navigator, a fisherman, and a helmsman, and having made the bell-proclamation three times, he set out upon the great ocean. Then, when they were in the midst of the ocean, a <s>kālikā</s> (untimely) storm drove their vessel hither and thither. Now the caravan-leader <s>Samudra</s> was a devotee of the heretical teachers. Frightened by the fear of untimely death, he began to invoke the six [heretical] teachers. Even so, the vessel was tossed about by the wind. Then the other merchants began to invoke thousands of deities. And they said:

children.text: śivavaruṇakuberā vāyur agni mahendro
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Mahendra</s>,

children.text: bhuvi ca tuvimagho yo viśvadevo maharṣiḥ |
children.translated_text: and he who on earth is <s>Tuvimagha</s>, and <s>Viśvadeva</s>, the great sage —

children.text: vayam iha maraṇārtā vaḥ prapannāḥ sma śīghraṃ
children.translated_text: we here, on the verge of death, have taken refuge in you! Quickly

children.text: vyasanam idam upetaṃ trātum icchantu sārtham* ||
children.translated_text: may you wish to rescue this caravan that has met with calamity!
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 202]

children.text: tatas teṣām evam api paridevamānānāṃ nāsti kaścit trātā | yāvat tatrānyatama upāsakaḥ samārūḍhaḥ | sa uvāca: kiṃ vo bhavantaḥ ṣaṭ śāstāra anye ca devatāḥ kariṣyanti? buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pratyakṣadevataṃ bhāvena śaraṇaṃ prapadyadhvam* | sa vas trātā bhaviṣyatīti | tataḥ samudrapramukhāni pañca vaṇikchatāni ekasvareṇa bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapannāni ||
children.translated_text: Yet, even as they thus lamented, there was no one to rescue them. Now among them, a certain lay devotee had embarked. He said: 'What will your six teachers and other deities do for you? Take refuge with your whole heart in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the present deity! He will be your savior.' Then the five hundred merchants led by <s>Samudra</s> took refuge in the <s>Bhagavān</s> with one voice.

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttānām ekārakṣāṇām śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ, ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam*, kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: Now, nothing is unknown, unseen, unrecognized, or uncomprehended by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. It is the natural law of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s> — who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, sole protectors, abiding in <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three means of taming, having crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipādas</s>), having abandoned the five factors [of hindrance], having transcended the five destinies, endowed with the six factors, having perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>), guides of the Eightfold Path, skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, possessing the strength of the ten powers (<s>daśabalas</s>), their fame filling the ten directions, distinguished by mastery over a thousand [qualities] — three times at night and three times during the day, they survey the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye and knowledge-and-vision operates: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has fallen into difficulty? Who has fallen into hardship? Who has fallen into distress? Who has fallen into difficulty, hardship, and distress? Who is inclined toward the lower realms? Who is tending toward the lower realms? Who is heading toward the lower realms? Whom shall I, having raised from the lower realms, establish in heaven and liberation? For whom shall I plant wholesome roots not yet planted? For whom shall I bring to maturity those already planted? For whom shall I liberate those already matured?' And he said:

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even the ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its boundary,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_81.1 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the [appointed] time for those who are to be trained. // AVŚ_81.1 //

children.text: yāvad bhagavatā jetavanāvasthitena sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāḥ kanakavarṇā marīcaya utsṛṣṭāḥ, yais te vaṇijaḥ samantād avabhāsitāḥ | kalpasahasraparibhāvitāś cāṃśava utsṛṣṭāḥ, yaiḥ prahlāditāḥ | kālikāvātaś ca pratyāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, dwelling in <s>Jetavana</s>, released golden rays of light surpassing a thousand suns, by which those merchants were illuminated all around. And he released rays cultivated over a thousand <s>kalpas</s>, by which they were comforted. And the untimely storm subsided.

children.text: yāvat samudraḥ svastikṣemābhyāṃ saṃsiddhayānapātraḥ pratyāgatas tenaiva maraṇasaṃvegena dānapradānāni datvā bandhujanaṃ samāśvāsya śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakān saṃtarpya pañcavaṇikchataparivāro bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In due course, <s>Samudra</s> returned safely and successfully with his ship. With the spiritual urgency born of that brush with death, he gave charitable gifts, consoled his kinsmen, satisfied ascetics, brahmins, the wretched, and wayfarers, and accompanied by five hundred merchants, he went forth into the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: āścaryaṃ bhadanta yad bhagavatā imāni samudrapramukhāni pañca vaṇikchatāni iṣṭena jīvitenācchāditāni, vyasanāt paritrātāni, atyantaniṣṭe ca nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitānīti | bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ mayā vigatarāgeṇa vigatadveṣeṇa vigatamohena parimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ imāni samudrapramukhāni pañca vaṇikchatāni iṣṭena jīvitenācchāditāni,
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, that the Blessed One, at the cost of his own dear life, has sheltered these five hundred merchants headed by <s>Samudra</s>, rescued them from calamity, and established them in ultimate <s>Nirvāṇa</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'What is so wonderful in this, monks, that now — by me, one free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — these five hundred merchants headed by <s>Samudra</s> have been sheltered at the cost of my dear life,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 203]

children.text: vyasanāt paritrātāni, atyantaniṣṭe ca nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitānīti | yat tu mayā atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ ime vaṇijaḥ paritrātāḥ | tac chṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta, bhāṣiṣye ||
