children.translated_text: rescued from calamity, and established in ultimate <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? But in a past age, by me — one who still had passion, still had hatred, still had delusion, not liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair — these very merchants were rescued. Listen to that, and attend well and carefully; I shall speak.'

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany anyatarasmin samudratīre pañcābhijñaḥ ṛṣiḥ prativasati, kaṣṭatayā mūlaphalāmbubhakto 'jinavalkalavāsī agnihotrikaḥ (Speyer: agnihotrakaḥ) | sa ca kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalo vyasanagatānāṃ paritrātā | yāvad vārāṇasyāṃ pañcavaṇikchatāni samudram avatartukāmāni | tāny anupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇāni samudratīram anuprātāni | tam ṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā prasādajātāni pādayor nipatya vijñāpayitum ārabdhāni: yady asmākaṃ bhagavan samudramadhyagatānāṃ kiṃcid vyasanam utpadyate, bhagavatā tāvad ete paritrātavyā iti | tenādhivāsitam*: evaṃ bhavatv iti | tatas te vaṇijo ratnāny ādāya jambudvīpābhimukhāḥ saṃprasthitāḥ | yāvat kālikayā rākṣasyā saṃtrāsitum ārabdhāḥ | tatas tena ṛṣiṇā paritrārāḥ | tataḥ saṃsiddhayānapātrāḥ pratyāgatā ṛṣisamīpam upagamyocuḥ: bho maharṣe anena duṣkareṇa vyavasāyena kāruṇyabhāvāc ca kiṃ prārthayasa iti | tenoktam*: andhe loke 'nāyake buddho bhūyāsam atīrṇānāṃ satvānāṃ tārayitā, amuktānāṃ mocayitā, anāśvastānām āśvāsayitā, aparinirvṛtānāṃ parinirvāpayiteti | tair uktam*: yadā tvaṃ buddho bhaves tadā asmān api samanvāharethā iti | ṛṣir āha: evam astv iti ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, on a certain seashore there dwelt a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) endowed with the five superknowledges — subsisting with difficulty on roots, fruits, and water, clothed in antelope-hide and bark-garments, maintaining the sacred fire (Speyer: <s>agnihotraka</s>). And he was compassionate, great-souled, fond of the <s>Dharma</s>, affectionate toward his people, a rescuer of those fallen into calamity. Now from <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, five hundred merchants wished to cross the ocean. Traveling in due course, they arrived at the seashore. Seeing that <s>ṛṣi</s> and being filled with faith, they fell at his feet and began to petition him: "If, venerable sir, some calamity should befall us while we are in the middle of the ocean, may you rescue us!" He consented: "So be it." Then those merchants, having obtained gems, set out heading toward <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Thereupon they were beset with terror by <s>Kālikā</s> the <s>Rākṣasī</s> (ogress). But they were rescued by that <s>ṛṣi</s>. Then, their voyage completed, they returned and, approaching the <s>ṛṣi</s>, said: "O great sage, by this difficult undertaking and out of compassion, what do you aspire to?" He said: "In a blind world, without a guide, may I become a <s>Buddha</s> — one who ferries across beings who have not crossed, who liberates those not liberated, who gives comfort to those not comforted, who brings to complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s> those who have not attained complete <s>Nirvāṇa</s>." They said: "When you become a <s>Buddha</s>, remember us as well." The <s>ṛṣi</s> said: "So be it."'

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena ṛṣir āsīt*, ahaṃ saḥ | ye te vaṇijaḥ, ime te samudrapramukhās tadāpy ete mayā paritrātāḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajitā babhūvuḥ | tatraibhir indrayaparipākaḥ kṛtaḥ | tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the <s>ṛṣi</s> — that was I. Those merchants — they are these very ones headed by <s>Samudra</s>. Even then I rescued them. Furthermore, they went forth under the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There they accomplished the maturation of their faculties. By that they have now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, deeds that are entirely dark have entirely dark results; entirely bright [deeds have] entirely bright [results]; mixed [deeds have] mixed [results]. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_82 sumanāḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_82: <s>Sumanās</s> (Jasmine). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain householder — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported with her,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 204]

children.text: ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putrāḥ prajāyante ca mriyante ca | tasmiṃś ca gṛhe sthaviro 'niruddhaḥ kulopagataḥ | tato gṛhapater iyaṃ buddhir utpannā: ayaṃ sthavirāniruddho vipākamaheśākhyaḥ, etaṃ tāvad āyāciṣye: yadi me putro jāyate, asya paścācchramaṇaṃ dasyāmīti | tato gṛhapatinā sthavirāniruddho 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ | tataḥ piṇḍakena pratipādyāyācitaḥ: yadi me putro jāto jīvati, sthavirasya paścācchramaṇaṃ dasyāmīti | sthavirāniruddhenoktam*: evam astu, kiṃ tu smartavyā te pratijñeti ||
children.translated_text: enjoyed himself, and amused himself. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, sons were born to him but they also died. Now in that household, the Elder <s>Aniruddha</s> was a regular visitor. Then this thought arose in the householder: 'This Elder <s>Aniruddha</s> is one whose merit has achieved great renown. Let me entreat him: if a son is born to me and lives, I shall give him to the Elder as an attendant.' Then the householder invited the Elder <s>Aniruddha</s> for a meal inside the house. Having served him food, he made this request: 'If a son is born to me and lives, I shall give him to the Elder as an attendant.' The Elder <s>Aniruddha</s> said: 'So be it, but you must remember your promise.'

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena patnyā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | tasyāḥ kāyāt surabhir gandhaḥ pravāti | yāvan navānāṃ māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jātaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko divyasumanaḥkañcikayā prāvṛtaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā sumanā iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* | tataḥ sthavirāniruddham antargṛhe bhaktenopanimantrya sa dārako niryātitaḥ | tataḥ sthavirāniruddhenāsmai kāṣāyāṇi dattāni, āśīr vādaś ca: dīrghāyur bhavatv iti ||
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, he was sporting, enjoying himself, and amusing himself with his wife. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, his wife became pregnant. From her body wafted a fragrant scent. After the passage of nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, beautiful, pleasing to behold, wrapped in a divine garland of jasmine flowers. At his birth, a birth festival was held, and the name <s>Sumanās</s> (Jasmine) was established. Then the Elder <s>Aniruddha</s> was invited for a meal inside the house, and the boy was entrusted to him. Then the Elder <s>Aniruddha</s> gave him saffron-colored robes and a blessing: 'May you be long-lived!'

children.text: yadā saptavarṣo jātas tadā mātāpitṛbhyāṃ sthavirāya dattaḥ | tataḥ sthavirāniruddhena pravrājya manasikāro dattaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | sa ca tīkṣṇendriyaḥ | yadā pāṃsukūlaṃ pratisaṃskaroti, tadā ekaikasmin* sūcīpradeśe aṣṭau vimokṣān samāpadyate ca vyuttiṣṭhate ca ||
children.translated_text: When he was seven years old, he was given by his parents to the Elder. Then the Elder <s>Aniruddha</s>, having ordained him, gave him a subject of meditation. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself — having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable and ever-changing, and having struck down all the courses of conditioned formations by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving — through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. And he was of sharp faculties. Whenever he mended his rag-robes, at each stitch-point he would enter and emerge from the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣas</s>).

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena sthavirāniruddhenoktaḥ: gaccha putraka, nadyā ajiravatyā udakam ānayeti | tataḥ sumanāḥ śramaṇoddeśo ghaṭam ādāyājiravatīm avatīrṇaḥ | tatra snātvā udakasya ghaṭaṃ pūrayitvā vihāyasaṃ prasthitaḥ | agrato ghaṭo gacchati, tataḥ sumanāḥ śramaṇoddeśaḥ | tasmiṃś ca samaye bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate: imaṃ paśya śāriputra śramaṇoddeśam āgacchantam udakasya ghaṭaṃ pūrayitvā smṛtimantaṃ susamāhitendriyam* |
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, the Elder <s>Aniruddha</s> said to him: 'Go, child, and fetch water from the river <s>Ajiravatī</s>.' Then the novice <s>Sumanās</s>, taking a water-pot, descended to the <s>Ajiravatī</s>. Having bathed there and filled the pot with water, he set out through the sky. The pot went in front, and then the novice <s>Sumanās</s> [followed]. At that time, the Blessed One, having emerged from his seclusion, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the four assemblies. There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'See, <s>Śāriputra</s>, this novice coming, having filled a water-pot, mindful, with well-composed faculties!'

children.text: hitvā rāgaṃ ca dveṣaṃ ca abhidhyāṃ ca virāgayan* |
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned passion and hatred, and disenchanting covetousness,

children.text: saṃghārayann imaṃ dehaṃ śobhate udahārakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: bearing along this body, the water-carrier shines!'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 205]

children.text: yadā bhagavatā sumanāḥ śramaṇoddeśo bhikṣusaṃghasya purastāt stutaḥ praśastaś ca, tadā bhikṣūṇāṃ saṃdeho jātaḥ | kāni bhadanta sumanasā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni, yenābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko divyayā ca sumanasāṃ kañcukayā prāvṛtto jātaḥ, tīkṣnendriyaḥ, arhatvaṃ ca prāptam iti | sumanasaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | sumanasā tāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One had praised and commended the novice <s>Sumanās</s> before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, doubt arose in the monks. 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Sumanās</s> perform and accumulate that he was born handsome, beautiful, and pleasing, wrapped in a divine garland of jasmine flowers, endowed with sharp faculties, and attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' 'It was <s>Sumanās</s> himself, monks, who in former births performed and accumulated deeds, whose requisite conditions had been gathered, whose causes had matured, which stood before him like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass. <s>Sumanās</s> performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their results]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_81.2 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_81.2 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad anyatamaḥ sārtavāhaḥ | tasya taruṇāvasthāyāṃ pravrajyācittam utpannam* | tena na śakitaṃ pravrajitum* | yadā vṛddho bhūtas tadā tasya vipratisāro jātaḥ: na me śobhanaṃ kṛtaṃ yad ahaṃ bhagavacchāsane na pravrajita iti | tatas tena keśanakhanastūpe sumanaḥpuṣpāropaṇaṃ kṛtam*, vipaśyī ca samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ | tataḥ tena pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlema cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca anāgatān samyaksaṃbuddhānām ārāgayeyam* | yasya ca śāsane pravrajeyam*, tatra daharāvasthāyām āryadharmān adhigaccheyam iti | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajito babhūva | tatrānena daśa varṣasahasrāṇi brahmacaryāvāsaḥ paripālitaḥ | tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. There was a certain caravan-leader. In his youth, the desire to go forth arose in him, but he was unable to go forth. When he had grown old, remorse arose in him: "I have not done well, for I did not go forth in the Blessed One's teaching." Then he made an offering of jasmine flowers at the <s>stūpa</s> of hair and nail [relics], and served the fully enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s> together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks with food. Then, prostrating at [the <s>stūpa</s>'s] feet, he made this aspiration: "By this root of merit, this generation of the thought [of awakening], and this relinquishment of gifts, may I please the fully enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> of the future. And in whosever teaching I may go forth, may I attain the Noble <s>Dharmas</s> in my youth." Furthermore, he went forth under the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There he maintained the life of celibacy for ten thousand years. By that, he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, deeds that are entirely dark have entirely dark results; entirely bright [deeds have] entirely bright [results]; mixed [deeds have] mixed [results]. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_83 hiraṇyapāṇiḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_83: <s>Hiraṇyapāṇi</s> (Golden-Handed). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain householder, wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with extensive and vast holdings, endowed with wealth rivaling that of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,

children.text: vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | na cāsya putro na duhitā | sa kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham*, na me putro na duhitā | mamātyayāt sarvasvāpateyam aputrakam iti kṛtvā rājavidheyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavair ucyate: devatārādhanaṃ kuruṣveti | asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti | tac ca naivam* | yady evam abhaviṣyat*, ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ | api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | katameṣāṃ trayāṇām* | mātāpitarāu raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau, mātā kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī, gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati | eteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: competing with the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. But he had no son and no daughter. Placing his cheek on his hand, he sat absorbed in worry: 'My household is endowed with manifold riches, yet I have no son and no daughter. After my death, all my property, being without an heir, will become subject to the king.' He was told by <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, friends, relatives, and kinsmen: 'You should propitiate the deities.' And there is this common saying in the world that through prayer, sons and daughters are born. But that is not so. If it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just like a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>). Rather, it is through the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. Which three? The parents must be passionate and united; the mother must be healthy and in her fertile period; and a <s>gandharva</s> (being seeking rebirth) must be present. Through the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born. And he continued devoted to prayer.

children.text: anyatamaś ca satvo 'nyatamasmād devanikāyāc cyutvā tasya prajāpatyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntaḥ | pañcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme | katame pañca | raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti, viraktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti | kālaṃ jānāti ṛtuṃ jānāti | garbham avakrāntaṃ jānāti | yasya sakāśād garbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti | dārakaṃ jānāti | dārikāṃ jānāti | saced dārako bhavati dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | {saced dārikā bhavati vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati |} sā āttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati: diṣṭyā āryaputra vardhase | āpannasatvāsmi saṃvṛttā | yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti | so 'py āttamanāḥ pūrvakāyam abhyunnamayya (Speyer: atyunnamayya) dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya udānam udānayati: apy evāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam* | jāto me syān nāvajātaḥ | kṛtyāni me kurvīta | bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyāt | dāyād yaṃ pratipadyeta | kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt* | asmākaṃ cāpy atītakālagatānām alpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā asmākaṃ nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādekṣyati: idaṃ tayor yatratatropapannayor gacchator anugacchatv iti | āpannasatvāṃ caināṃ viditvopariprāsādatalagatām ayantritāṃ dhārayati, śīte śītopakaraṇair uṣṇe uṣṇopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptair āhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhāraiḥ | hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīm apsarasam iva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcān mañcaṃ pīṭhāt pīṭham anavatarantīm adharāṃ bhūmim* | na cāsyāḥ kiṃcid amanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ yāvad eva garbhasya paripākāya ||
children.translated_text: And a certain being, having fallen from a certain class of <s>devas</s>, descended into the womb of his wife. There are five distinctive characteristics known to certain wise ones:

children.text: sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | pāṇidvaye cāsya lakṣaṇāhataṃ karmavipākajaṃ dīnāradvayam* | yadā tad apanītaṃ bhavati tadā anyat prādurbhavati | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātayaḥ ūcuḥ: yasmād asya jātamātrasya pāṇidvaye lakṣaṇāhataṃ karmavipākajaṃ dīnāradvayaṃ prādurbhūtam*, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya hiraṇyapāṇir iti nāmeti | hiraṇyapāṇir dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | sa śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko
children.translated_text: She, at the end of eight or nine months, gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs. During

children.text: mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ | ya yadā vīthīm avatīrṇo bhavati, tadā śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakān dṛṣṭvā pāṇidvayaṃ prasārayati | tato lakṣaṇāhatasya hiraṇyasuvarṇasya rāśiḥ prādurbhavati, yena tān saṃtarpayati | tasya yaśasā sarvā śrāvastī āpūrṇā ||
children.translated_text: a great soul, desiring <s>dharma</s>, compassionate toward his people. Whenever he descended into the streets, seeing <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, and beggars, with both his hands

children.text: yāvad hiraṇyapāṇir dārako 'pareṇa samayena jetavanaṃ nirgataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike citte prasāditam* | prasādajātaś ca bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tato 'sya bhagavatā dharmo deśitaḥ | sa āyuṣmantam ānandam idam avocat*: icchāmy aham ācārya bhagavataḥ saśrāvakasaṃghasya bhaktaṃ kartum iti | sthavirānandenoktaḥ: vatsa kārṣāpaṇaiḥ prayojanam iti | tato hiraṇyapāṇinā buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṃghasya purastāt sthitvā pāṇidvayaṃ prasārya hiraṇyasuvarṇasya mahān rāśiḥ sthāpitaḥ, yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃghasthaviro 'nye ca bhikṣavaḥ sthavirānandaś ca paraṃ vismayam āpannāḥ | tato hiraṇyapāṇir dārako buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhojayitvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā hiraṇyapāṇidārikeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | dṛṣṭasatyo jñātīnāṃ bhāgasaṃvibhāgaṃ kṛtvā śramaṇabrāhmaṇkṛpaṇanīpakān saṃtarpya mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In time, the boy <s>Hiraṇyapāṇi</s> (Golden-Handed) went out to the <s>Jetavana</s>. Then he saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta hiraṇyapāṇinā karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenāsya pāṇidvaye lakṣanāhataṃ dīnāradvayaṃ jātam*, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: hiraṇyapāṇinaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | hiraṇyapāṇinā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having become doubtful, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What actions, Venerable One, were performed by <s>Hiraṇyapāṇi</s>

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Actions do not perish, even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (world-ages);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_83.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and the right time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. [<s>Avadānaśataka</s> 83.1]

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ
children.translated_text: In the past, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in a bygone age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, there arose a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s>

children.text: puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | atha kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ | tasya rājñā kṛkiṇā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ krośam uccatvena | tatra ca stūpamahe vartamāne dyūtakareṇa dīnāradvayaṃ tasmin stūpe yaṣṭyāṃ samāropitam* | tataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān*: yatra yatra jāyeya, tatra tatra hastagatenaiva suvarṇeneti ||
children.translated_text: the charioteer of men to be tamed, the teacher of <s>devas</s> and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He, dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, was residing at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (Deer Park) in <s>Mṛgadāva</s>

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena dyūtakara āsīt*, ayaṃ sa hiraṇyapāṇiḥ | yad anena stūpe dīnāradvayaṃ samāropitam*, tenāsyaivaṃvidho viśeṣaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who at that time, in that era, was the gambler — he is this <s>Hiraṇyapāṇi</s>. Whatever by him

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: AVŚ_84 tripiṭakaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 84: <s>Tripiṭaka</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena śrāvastyāṃ rājā prasenajit kauśalo rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca {subhikṣaṃ ca} ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | priyam ivaikaputrakaṃ rājyaṃ pālayati | yāvad asau devyā saha krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jātaḥ kāṣāyavastraṃ prāvṛtya śramaṇaveṣadhārī jātismaraś ca | sa jātamātraḥ pṛcchati: kiṃ bhagavān ihaiva śrāvastyāṃ śāriputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapānandaprabhṛtayo vā mahāśrāvakā iti | tato 'sya mātā vismayaharṣapūrṇā kathayati: putraka bhagavān ihaiva śrāvastyāṃ mahāśrāvakāś ceti | yāvad eṣo 'rtho rājñaḥ prasenajito niveditaḥ: putras te jātaḥ | kāṣāyavastraṃ prāvṛtya śramaṇaveṣadhārī jātismaraś ca | sa bhagavato mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ ca pravṛttim anveṣata iti | tato rājñā prasenajitā tasyānugrahāryaṃ bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho bhaktenopanimantritaḥ | atha bhagavān bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena rājñaḥ prasenajito bhaktābhisāras tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ | tato rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ putram utsaṅge kṛtvā bhagavato darśayati: ayaṃ me bhagavan putro jātamātra eṣa
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the monastic community, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> was ruling a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from thieves and disease, and abundant in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. He governed the kingdom as dearly as an only son. He sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with his queen. As he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself, his queen became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born, wrapped in saffron-colored robes, wearing the appearance of a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), and remembering his previous lives. As soon as he was born, he asked: "Is the <s>Bhagavān</s> here in <s>Śrāvastī</s>? And are the great disciples such as <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, and <s>Ānanda</s> here?" Then his mother, filled with wonder and joy, said: "Dear son, the <s>Bhagavān</s> is indeed here in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and so are the great disciples." This matter was reported to King <s>Prasenajit</s>: "A son has been born to you. He was born wrapped in saffron robes, wearing the appearance of an ascetic, and remembering his previous lives. He inquires about the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the great disciples." Then King <s>Prasenajit</s>, out of kindness toward him, invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the monastic community to a meal. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the company of monks and preceded by the monastic community, went to the place where King <s>Prasenajit</s>'s meal offering was. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared for him before the monastic community. Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, placing the boy on his lap, showed him to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "This, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is my son. As soon as he was born, he
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 209]

children.text: bhagavantaṃ smarati, mahāśrāvakāṃś ceti | tato bhagavāṃs taṃ kumāram āmantrayate: ārogyaṃ te tripiṭeti | sa kathayati: vande tathāgatam arhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham iti | tato rājā prasenajit param vismayam āpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: remembered the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the great disciples." Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the boy: "Are you well, <s>Tripiṭa</s>?" He said: "I pay homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One)." Then King <s>Prasenajit</s> was overcome with great amazement.

children.text: yadā saptavarṣo jātas tadā bhagavacchāsane pravrajitas tair eva kāṣāyaiḥ prāvṛtaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he was seven years old, he went forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wearing those very saffron robes. Through his diligent effort, striving and exerting himself, having understood this five-limbed wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable, and having overcome all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship). He became an <s>arhat</s>, free from passion toward the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, with a mind like the open sky and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood, with the egg-shell of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical insights), turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor. He became worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta tripiṭena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yena kāṣāyavastraprāvṛto jātaḥ śramaṇaveṣadhārī jātismaraḥ | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: tripiṭenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | tripiṭena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, questioned the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What deeds, Venerable One, were performed by <s>Tripiṭaka</s>, that he was born wrapped in saffron robes, wearing the appearance of an ascetic, and remembering his previous lives, and having gone forth, directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship)?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "By <s>Tripiṭaka</s> himself, monks, in previous births, deeds were performed and accumulated, their provisions gathered, their conditions ripened, standing ready like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. By <s>Tripiṭaka</s>, deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else will experience their results? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_84.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. (AVŚ 84.1)

children.text:
bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvad rājñaḥ kṛkiṇaḥ putra ṛṣipatanaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cāsya prasādo jātaḥ | sa prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī saṃsāravairāgyikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā saṃsāre doṣadarśī nirvāṇe guṇadarśī bhūtvā rājānaṃ vijñāpayāmāsa: anujānīhi māṃ tāta, bhagavacchāsane pravrajiṣyāmīti | rājovāca: na śakyam etan mayā kartum* | yasmāt te yuvarājābhiṣeko nacireṇa bhaviṣyatīti | kumāraḥ kathayati: alaṃ me rājyena bahudoṣaduṣṭadharmasaṃpannena | avaśyam evāhaṃ bhagavacchāsane pravrajiṣyāmīti | sa pitrā nānujñātaḥ | tenaiko bhaktacchedaḥ kṛtaḥ, dvau trayo vā yāvat ṣaḍ bhaktacchedāḥ kṛtāḥ | tato 'sya vayasyakai rājā vijñaptaḥ | deva anujānīhi kumāraṃ pravrajitum* | mā haiva kālaṃ kariṣyatīti | tato rājñā putraḥ pratijñāṃ
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 210 --------------------
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, monks, in the past, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. The son of King <s>Kṛkin</s> went to <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>. There he saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, encircled by a fathom-wide aura, with radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Upon seeing him, faith arose in him. With faith arisen, having paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he sat down before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character, gave such a teaching inspiring disenchantment with <s>saṃsāra</s> that, upon hearing it, he saw the faults in <s>saṃsāra</s> and the virtues in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and he addressed the king: "Please permit me, father; I will go forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." The king said: "This cannot be done by me, for your consecration as crown prince will take place before long." The prince said: "I have no need of a kingdom endowed with many faults and corrupt conditions. I will certainly go forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." He was not permitted by his father. He undertook one meal-fast, then two, three, up to six meal-fasts. Then his companions addressed the king: "Sire, please permit the prince to go forth, lest he die." Then the king made his son take a vow:

children.text:
karitaḥ: tāvat te 'smākaṃ darśanaṃ na deyam*, yāvat trayaḥ piṭakā adhītā iti | yāvad asau pitaram anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ |
  tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena nacireṇa trayaḥ piṭakā adhītāḥ | yuktam uktapratibhānī dhārmakathikaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | tasyaitad abhavat*: yanv ahaṃ pūrvikāṃ pratijñāṃ niryātayeyam iti | sa pituḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ | sa pṛṣṭaś ca: kiṃ putra asti kiṃcid adhītam iti? tenoktam*: trayaḥ piṭakā iti | tatas tena pitus tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā rājā āttamanāḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | tataḥ prasādajātaḥ kathayati: putra kena te prayojanam iti | tenoktam*: icchāmy ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃgham upanimantrya ṣaḍbhiḥ pariṣkārair ācchādayitum iti | rājā kathayati: yatheṣṭaṃ kuruṣva, vistīrṇaṃ rājakulam iti | tatas tripiṭena bhagavān viṃśatisahasraparivāraḥ praṇītenāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ | ekaikaś ca bhikṣuḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pariṣkārair ācchāditaḥ | tataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: yan mayā idānīṃ kṛcchreṇa pravrajyā pratilabdhā, tathāgate ca saśrāvakasaṃghe kārāḥ kṛtāḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yatra yatra jāyeya tatra tatra kāṣāyavastraprāvṛta eva śramaṇaveṣadhārī jātismaraś ca syām iti ||
children.translated_text:
"You shall not come to see us until you have mastered the three <s>piṭakas</s> (baskets of scripture)." Having obtained permission from his father, he went forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
Through his diligent effort, striving and exerting himself, he soon mastered the three <s>piṭakas</s>. He became a capable, eloquent preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>. He thought: "I should now fulfill my earlier promise." He went to his father. His father asked: "Son, have you studied anything?" He replied: "The three <s>piṭakas</s>." Then he gave his father such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, the king became delighted. Then, with faith arisen, the king said: "Son, what do you need?" He replied: "I wish to invite the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the monastic community and provide them with the six requisites." The king said: "Do as you wish; the royal household is vast." Then <s>Tripiṭaka</s> satisfied the <s>Bhagavān</s> and his retinue of twenty thousand with excellent food. Each monk was provided with the six requisites. Then, falling at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he made a vow: "Since I have now obtained ordination with great difficulty and have rendered service to the <s>Tathāgata</s> and his monastic community, by this wholesome root, this aspiration, and this gift of offerings, wherever I may be born, may I always be born wrapped in saffron robes, wearing the appearance of an ascetic, and remembering my previous lives."

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena kṛkiṇaḥ putraḥ, ayaṃ tripiṭaḥ | tenaiva hetunā āḍhye rājakule putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko jātismaraś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, monks? He who was at that time the son of <s>Kṛkin</s> — he is this <s>Tripiṭaka</s>. By that very cause, he was born as a son in a wealthy royal family, beautiful, lovely, graceful, and remembering his previous lives. Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, entirely bright; for those mixed, mixed. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only in entirely bright deeds. Thus should you train, monks."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_85 yaśomitraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 85: <s>Yaśomitra</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ sārthavāha āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tena khalu samayena durbhikṣam abhūt kṛcchram* | kāntāradurlabhaḥ (Speyer: durlambhaḥ) piṇḍako yācanakena |
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the monastic community, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain caravan leader, wealthy, of great riches and great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal status. He sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with her. At that time there was a famine and hardship. Alms-food was difficult to obtain in the wilderness by begging.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 211]

children.text: naimittikaiś ca nirdiṣṭo devo na varṣiṣyatīti | yāvat sārthavāhapatnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgopetaḥ | yatra ca divase dārako jātas tatraiva divase 'nāvṛṣṭir bhagnā | tasya yaśasā sarvā śrāvastī āpūritā | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya samantād yaśo visṛtam*, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya yaśomitra iti nāmeti | yaśomitro dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* ||
children.translated_text: And the soothsayers had predicted that it would not rain. Meanwhile, the caravan-leader's wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with all limbs. And on the very day the boy was born, the drought was broken. His fame filled all of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since his fame has spread in all directions, let the boy's name be <s>Yaśomitra</s> (Friend of Fame).' The boy <s>Yaśomitra</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, yogurt, butter, ghee, the cream of ghee, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.

children.text: yadā yaśomitro mahān saṃvṛttas tadā jetavanaṃ nirgataḥ kenacid eva karaṇīyena | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cāsya prasādo jātaḥ | prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasya bhagavatā tādṛśī saṃsāravairāgyikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā saṃsāradoṣadarśī nirvāṇaguṇadarśī bhūtvā mātapitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | tasya daṃṣṭrābhyām aṣṭāṅgopetaṃ pānīyaṃ prasravati, yenāsya tṛṣā na bādhate | yadā nidāghakāle bhikṣavas tṛṣārtāḥ pānakasyārthe saṃgham avataranti, tadāpy asau nāvatarati | tato 'sya supremakā bhikṣavaḥ pṛcchanti: kena hetunā bhavatas tṛṣā na bādhata iti | sa kathayati: mamaitābhyāṃ daṃṣṭrābhyām aṣṭāṅgopetaṃ pānīyaṃ prasravati, yena na me tṛṣā bādhatā iti ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Yaśomitra</s> had grown up, he went out to the <s>Jetavana</s> on some errand. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, faith arose in him. Filled with faith, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One gave him a teaching conducive to weariness with <s>saṃsāra</s>. Having heard it, seeing the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the virtues of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, he obtained his parents' permission and went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Exerting himself, striving, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. From between his fangs (canine teeth) flowed water endowed with the eight qualities, by which his thirst was never afflicted. During the hot season, when the monks, tormented by thirst, would assemble in the <s>Saṃgha</s> for the sake of drink, he alone would not descend. Therefore, his fellow monks asked him: 'For what reason are you not afflicted by thirst?' He said: 'From between my two canine teeth, water endowed with the eight qualities flows, by which I am not afflicted by thirst.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta yaśomitreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ, daṃṣṭrāntarāc cāṣṭāṅgopetaṃ pānīyaṃ prasravati, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: yaśomitreṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | yaśomitreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did <s>Yaśomitra</s> perform that he was handsome, good-looking, and pleasing, that water endowed with the eight qualities flows from between his canine teeth, and that upon going forth he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Yaśomitra</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Yaśomitra</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 212]

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_85.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_85.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvad anyataraḥ śreṣṭhiputro 'nyatarasya vṛddhabhikṣoḥ sakāśe pravrajitaḥ | so 'laso necchati samayācārikāṃ caritum* | tataḥ sa brahmacāribhiḥ sthavirasyopasthāyako dattaḥ | sa upasthāyakam ātmānaṃ matvā vṛddhatarāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ sakāśād upasthānaṃ svīkaroti | tasyākuśalamūlāny aparyantāni ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. A certain guild-master's son went forth in the presence of a certain elder monk. He was lazy and did not wish to engage in the regular observances. Then his fellow celibates assigned him as the attendant of the elder. Considering himself an attendant, he accepted the service of even older monks. His unwholesome roots were boundless.

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena glānyaṃ patitaḥ | sthavireṇāsya vaidyopadeśād ghṛtaṃ pānāya dattam* | sa rātrau tṛṣātrāsitaḥ (Speyer: tṛṣā trāsitaḥ) svakaṃ kamaṇḍalukam upagṛhya pānīyaṃ pāsyāmīti paśyati nirudakam* | evam ācāryopādhyāyānām* | yāvat sāṃghikaṃ pānīyamaṇḍapam avatīrṇaḥ | tad api nirudakaṃ paśyati | yāvan nadīcārikām avatīrṇaḥ | sāpi nirudakā saṃvṛttā | sa udvignaḥ svakānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇām udvejanārthaṃ śraddhādeyasya ca gurutvasaṃdarśanārtham*, nadīcārikāyāḥ parivṛkṣaḥ (Speyer: pare vṛkṣaḥ), tatra śāṭakaṃ baddhvā samabhirūḍhaḥ, svakarmāṇi mamety avetya karmapratiśaraṇāvasthitaḥ (Speyer: karmapratisaraṇāvasthitaḥ) | yāvad dvitīye divase prabhātāyāṃ rajanyām etad vṛttāntaṃ sabrahmacāriṇām ārocayati | tato 'sya sabrahmacāriṇaḥ pretakaraṇaṃ śrutvodvignāḥ, itaś cāmutaś cārocayitum ārabdhāḥ | tato 'sya upādhyāyena pānīyam upanāmitam* | tad api na paśyati | tenāpi saṃvignena bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya niveditam* | bhagavatā kāśyapenoktaḥ: gaṇḍīr ākoṭyatām iti | tata upadhivārikeṇa gaṇḍīr ākoṭitā | buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, he fell ill. The elder, on the advice of a physician, gave him ghee to drink. At night, tormented by thirst, he took up his own water-pot to drink, but found it empty. Likewise those of his teachers and preceptors. Then he descended to the communal water-pavilion of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. He saw that it too was empty. Then he went down to the river channel. That too was without water. He, filled with spiritual urgency — for the purpose of stirring urgency in his fellow celibates and for the purpose of demonstrating the gravity of gifts given in faith — at the edge of the river channel, at the other tree, there tied his robe and climbed up, recognizing his own deeds as 'mine' and established in taking refuge in <s>karma</s>. On the second day, at dawn, he told the whole story to his fellow celibates. Then his fellow celibates, hearing of his near-death experience, were shaken with urgency, and began to report it here and there. Then his preceptor offered him water. But he could not even see it. The preceptor too, shaken with urgency, reported it to the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. The Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> said: 'Let the bell be struck.' Then the bell-keeper struck the bell. The <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks, headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, assembled.

children.text: eṣa vṛttānto vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ samantato visṛtaḥ | tato 'nekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipatitāni | yāvad upādhyāyena vṛddhānte niṣādayitvā udakapurṇā kuṇḍikā dattā | vatsa etat pānīyaṃ saṃghe cārayeti | sa pratyakṣaphaladarśī tenaiva saṃvegena buddhe bhagavti śrāvakeṣu ca prasādam utpādya tīvreṇāśayena tad udakaṃ saṃghe cāritavān* | tato bhagavatā tasyānugrahārthaṃ gajabhujasadṛśaṃ bāhum abhiprasārya bhītānām āśvāsanakareṇa tad udakaṃ gṛhītaṃ mahāśrāvakaiś ca | na ca kṣīyate | yāvat sarvasaṃghe cāritam*, tadāpi na kṣīyate | tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā anekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtam* | tasyāpi saṃtāne 'kuśalamūlāni pratisaṃhṛtāni | yadā tasmād glānyād vyutthitaḥ, tadā tena buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ pānīyenālpotsukaḥ kṛtaḥ | dvādaśa varṣasahasrāṇi tena saṃghe pānīyaṃ cāritam* | yāvan maraṇakālasamaye praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān*: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena uttaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛtaḥ: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, tam aham ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam*, daṃṣṭrāntarāc ca me 'ṣṭāṅgopetaṃ pānīyaṃ nirgacched iti ||
children.translated_text: This story spread throughout the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> on all sides. Then many hundreds of thousands of beings assembled. The preceptor, having seated him at the end [of the assembly], gave him a water-pot filled with water: 'Child, distribute this water to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' He, seeing the fruit directly before him, with that very sense of urgency, having generated faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, and in the disciples, with intense aspiration, distributed that water to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Then the Blessed One, for the sake of blessing him, extending his arm like the trunk of an elephant, with a gesture that reassures the frightened, accepted that water, as did the great disciples. And it did not diminish. Even after it had been distributed to the entire <s>Saṃgha</s>, it still did not diminish. Having seen this exceedingly wondrous miracle, which captivated both gods and humans, many hundreds of thousands of beings attained the vision of truth. And in his own mental continuum, the unwholesome roots were retracted. When he recovered from that illness, he served water to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, with little effort. For twelve thousand years he distributed water to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. At the time of death, he made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, this generation of the aspiration for awakening, and this relinquishment of gifts — under the <s>Buddha</s> whom the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> prophesied as the young man named <s>Uttara</s>: "You, young man, in the age when the lifespan of people is a hundred years, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>" — may I please him and never displease him, and may water endowed with the eight qualities flow from between my canine teeth.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 213]

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena bhikṣur āsīt, ayaṃ saḥ | yat tena dvādaśa varṣasahasrāṇi saṃghe pānīyaṃ cāritam*, praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam*, teneha janmani daṃṣṭrāntarād aṣṭāṅgopetam pānīyaṃ nirgacchati | tenaiva hetunārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the monk — that was <s>Yaśomitra</s>. Because he distributed water to the <s>Saṃgha</s> for twelve thousand years and made that aspiration, in this life water endowed with the eight qualities flows from between his canine teeth. By that very cause he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_86 aupapādukaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_86: <s>Aupapāduka</s> (The Spontaneously Born). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu varṣā upagataḥ pāṇḍukambalaśilāyāṃ pārijātasya kovidārasya nātidūre | mātur janitryā dharmaṃ deśayati, anyeṣāṃ ca devānām* | tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ śrāvastyāṃ varṣā upagato jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | atha catasraḥ parṣado yenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ, mahāmaudgalyāyanapādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ | catasraḥ parṣada āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano dharmakathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati | anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm* | atha catasraḥ parṣada utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyam idam avocat*: kaccit te bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana śrutaṃ kutra bhagavān etarhi varṣā upagata iti | mahāmaudgalyāyana āha: śrutaṃ me bhavanto bhagavān deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu varṣā upagataḥ, pāṇḍukambalaśilāyāṃ pārijātasya kovidārasya nātidūre | mātur janitryā dharmaṃ deśayati, anyeṣāṃ ca devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānām iti | atha catasraḥ parṣadaḥ āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanebhyaḥ prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, had gone up to spend the rains-retreat among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, on the <s>Pāṇḍukambalā</s> stone, not far from the <s>Pārijāta</s> coral tree. He was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to his birth-mother and to the other gods. At that time, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> had gone up for the rains-retreat at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Then the four assemblies approached the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, bowed their heads at his feet, and sat down to one side. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the four assemblies with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then the four assemblies, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, and extending their joined palms toward the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Has Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> heard where the <s>Bhagavān</s> has now gone for the rains-retreat?' <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said: 'I have heard, good people: the <s>Bhagavān</s> has gone for the rains-retreat among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, on the <s>Pāṇḍukambalā</s> stone, not far from the <s>Pārijāta</s> coral tree. He is teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to his birth-mother and to the other <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.' Then the four assemblies, having approved and rejoiced at the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s words, bowed their heads at his feet, rose from their seats, and departed.

children.text:
atha catasraḥ parṣadas trayāṇāṃ vārṣikāṇām atyayād yenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramyāyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ | catasraḥ parṣada āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati (Speyer: saṃpradarśayati) samādāpayati samuttejayati
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 214 --------------------
children.translated_text:
Then the four assemblies, after the passage of the three months of the rains, approached the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>. Having approached and bowed their heads at the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s feet, they sat down to one side. The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> instructed, encouraged, inspired,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 214]

children.text: saṃpraharṣayati | anekaparyāyeṇa dhamyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm* | atha catasraḥ parṣada utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyam idam avocat*: yat khalu bhadantamahāmaudgalyāyano jānīyāt* (Speyer: jānāyāc; MS: -maudgalyāyana jānīyā cira-): ciradṛṣṭo 'smābhir bhagavān*, paritṛṣitāḥ smo vayaṃ bhagavato darśanena | icchāmo vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ draṣṭum* | saced bhadantamahāmaudgalyāyasyāguru, sādhu bhadantamahāmaudgalyāyano yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmet+ | upasaṃkramyāsmākaṃ vacanena bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandasva, alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛccha, alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca | evaṃ ca vada: jambūdvīpe bhadanta catasraḥ parṣada ākāṅkṣanti bhagavato darśanam* | evaṃ cāhuḥ: nāsti khalu bhadanta jambūdvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tadrūpā ṛddhir vā anubhāvo vā yena jambūdvīpakā manuṣyā devāṃs trāyastriṃśān (Speyer: trayastriṃśān) abhiroheyuḥ bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramaṇāya paryupāsanāya | asti khalu devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ tadrūpā ṛddhiś cānubhāvaś ca, yena devās trāyastriṃśā jambūdvīpam avatareyur bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramaṇāya paryupāsanāya | sādhu bhagavān devebhyas trāyastriṃśebhyo jambūdvīpam avatared anukampām upādāyeti | adhivāsayaty āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaś catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ tūṣṇībhāvena | atha catasraḥ parṣada āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanebhyaḥ prakrāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and gladdened the four assemblies with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then the four assemblies, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, and extending their joined palms toward the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'May Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> know this: it has been long since we have seen the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and we are parched with longing for a sight of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. We wish to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If it is not troublesome for Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, may Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> please approach the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, please bow your head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet on our behalf, inquire about his health — whether he is free from illness, free from affliction, nimble, comfortable, strong, happy, blameless, and dwelling at ease — and say thus: "In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, Venerable Sir, the four assemblies long for a sight of the <s>Bhagavān</s>." And say also: "The humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, Venerable Sir, do not possess such supernatural power or might that they could ascend to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for seeing, visiting, and attending upon him. But the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods do possess such supernatural power and might that they could descend to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for seeing, visiting, and attending upon him. May the <s>Bhagavān</s>, out of compassion, please descend from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>."' The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> consented to the four assemblies by his silence. Then the four assemblies, understanding the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s consent by his silence, bowed their heads at his feet, rose from their seats, and departed.

children.text: athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano 'ciraprakrāntāś catasraḥ parṣado viditvā tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte tadyathā balavān puruṣaḥ saṃkuñcitaṃ vā bāhuṃ prasārayet*, prasāritaṃ vā saṃkuñcayet*, evam evāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ śrāvastyām antarhito deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣu pratyaṣṭhāt pāṇdukambalaśilāyāṃ pārijātasya kovidārasya nātidūre | tena khalu samayena bhagavān anekaśatāyā devaparṣado dharmaṃ deśayati | adrākṣīc ca mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavantam anekaśatāyā devaparṣadaḥ purastān niṣaṇṇaṃ dharmaṃ deśayantam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ smitaṃ prāvirakārṣīt*: ihāpi bhagavān ākīrṇo viharati tadyathā jambūdvīpe catasṛbhiḥ parṣadbhir iti | atha bhagavān āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya cetasā cittam ājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: na khalu maudgalyāyana svairatvam eṣām*, api tu yadā me evaṃ bhavati: āgacchantv iti, tadā āgacchanti | yadā me evaṃ bhavati: gacchantv iti, tadā gacchanti | iti me cetasā cittam ājñāya āgacchanti ca gacchanti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, knowing that the four assemblies had recently departed, entered into such a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) that, with his mind concentrated — just as a strong man might extend a bent arm or bend an extended arm — even so, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> vanished from <s>Śrāvastī</s> and appeared among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, on the <s>Pāṇḍukambalā</s> stone, not far from the <s>Pārijāta</s> coral tree. At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to an assembly of many hundreds of gods. And <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> seated before an assembly of many hundreds of gods, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen this, he smiled: 'Here too the <s>Bhagavān</s> dwells surrounded, just as in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> by the four assemblies.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known with his own mind the thought in the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s mind, said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Indeed, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, they do not [come and go] of their own free will; rather, when I think, "Let them come," then they come; when I think, "Let them go," then they go. Thus, having known my mind with their minds, they come and go.'

children.text: āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekāntaniṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān maudgalyāyanaḥ sarvāṃ devaparṣadam avalokya bhagavantam idam avocat: vicitrā bateyaṃ devaparṣat saṃniṣaṇṇā saṃnipatitā | santy asyāṃ devaparṣadi devatā yā buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ kāyasya bhedād ihopapannāḥ | santi dharme, santi saṃghe, santi āryakāntaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ, kāyasya bhedād ihopapannāḥ |
children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, having surveyed the entire assembly of gods, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'How marvelous is this assembly of gods, gathered and convened! There are deities in this assembly of gods who, endowed with unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body. There are those [who had faith] in the <s>Dharma</s>, there are those in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and there are those endowed with the virtues dear to the Noble Ones, who have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 215]

children.text: atha bhagavān āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya bhāṣitam anuvarṇayann āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: evam etan maudgalyāyana, evam evam etat* | vicitrā bateyaṃ devaparṣat saṃniṣaṇṇā saṃnipatitā | santy asyāṃ devatā yā buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ, kāyasya bhedād ihopapannāḥ | santi dharme, santi saṃghe, santi āryakāntaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ, kāyasya bhedād ihopapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, approving the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s words, said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'So it is, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, just so! How marvelous is this assembly of gods, gathered and convened! There are deities here who, endowed with unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body. There are those [who had faith] in the <s>Dharma</s>, there are those in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and there are those endowed with the virtues dear to the Noble Ones, who have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body.'

children.text: atha śakro śakro devānām indro bhagavata āyuṣmataś ca mahāmaudgalyāyanasya bhāṣitam anuvarṇayann āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: evam etad bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana, evam etat* | vicitrā bateyaṃ devaparṣat saṃniṣaṇṇā saṃnipatitā | santy asyāṃ devaparṣadi devatāḥ, yā buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ, kāyasya bhedād ihopapannāḥ | santi dharme, santi saṃghe, santy āryakāntaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ, kāyasya bhedād ihopapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, approving the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'So it is, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, just so! How marvelous is this assembly of gods, gathered and convened! There are deities in this assembly of gods who, endowed with unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body. There are those [who had faith] in the <s>Dharma</s>, there are those in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and there are those endowed with the virtues dear to the Noble Ones, who have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body.'

children.text: athānyatamo devaputro bhagavata āyuṣmataś ca mahāmaudgalyāyanasya śakrasya ca devānām indrasya bhāṣitam anuvarṇayann āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat*: evam etad bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana, evam etat* | vicitrā bateyaṃ devaparṣat saṃniṣaṇṇā saṃnipatitā | santy asyāṃ devaparṣadi devatāḥ, yā buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatāḥ kāyasya bhedād ihopapannāḥ | santi dharme, santi saṃghe | santi āryakāntaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ kāyasya bhedād ihopapannā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then a certain <s>Devaputra</s> (young god), approving the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, said this to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'So it is, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, just so! How marvelous is this assembly of gods, gathered and convened! There are deities in this assembly of gods who, endowed with unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body. There are those [who had faith] in the <s>Dharma</s>, there are those in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and there are those endowed with the virtues dear to the Noble Ones, who have been reborn here upon the dissolution of the body.'

children.text: tatrānekāni devatāśatāni anekāni devatāsahasrāṇy anekāni devatāśatasahasrāṇi bhagavataḥ purastāt pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtya tatraivāntarhitāni ||
children.translated_text: There, many hundreds of deities, many thousands of deities, many hundreds of thousands of deities, in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, each individually directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>) and vanished right there.
