children.text: athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ praviviktāṃ devaparṣadaṃ viditvā ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat*: jambūdvīpe bhadanta catasraḥ parṣado bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vandante alpābādhatāṃ ca pṛcchanti, alpātaṅkatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yātrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca | bhagavān āh: sukhino maudgalyāyana bhavantu jambūdvīpe catasraḥ parṣadas tvaṃ ca | mahāmaudgalyāyana āha: jambūdvīpe bhadanta catasraḥ parṣada ākāṅkṣanti bhagavato darśanam* | evaṃ cāhuḥ: nāsti bhadanta jāmbūdvīpakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ tadrūpā ṛddhir vā anubhāvo vā yena jāmbūdvīpakā manuṣyā devāṃs trāyastriṃśān abhiroheyur bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramituṃ paryupāsanāya | asti tu bhadanta devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ tadrūpā ṛddhiś cānubhāvaś ca, yena devās trāyastriṃśā jambūdvīpam avatareyur bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramituṃ paryupāsanāya | sādhu bhagavān devebhyaś trāyastriṃśebhyo 'vatared anukampām upādāya | bhagavān āha: tena hi tvaṃ gaccha maudgalyāyana jambūdvīpam* | gatvā ca catasṛṇāṃ parṣadām ārocaya: avatariṣyati bhavanto bhagavān itaḥ saptame divase devebhyas trāyastriṃśebhyo jambūdvīpaṃ sāṃkāśye nagare āpajjure dāve udumbaramūle iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, perceiving that the assembly of gods had dispersed, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, Venerable Sir, the four assemblies bow their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and inquire about his health — whether he is free from illness, free from affliction, nimble, comfortable, strong, happy, blameless, and dwelling at ease.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'May the four assemblies in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be well, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, and you also.' <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said: 'The four assemblies in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, Venerable Sir, long for a sight of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And they say: "The humans of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, Venerable Sir, do not possess such supernatural power or might that they could ascend to the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for seeing, visiting, and attending upon him. But the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods do possess such supernatural power and might that they could descend to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for seeing, visiting, and attending upon him. May the <s>Bhagavān</s>, out of compassion, please descend from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>."' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'In that case, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, go to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Having gone, announce to the four assemblies: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> will descend from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> on the seventh day from now, at the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>, in the <s>Āpajjura</s> grove, at the foot of an <s>Udumbara</s> tree."'

children.text: athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya pādau śirasā vanditvā tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ saṃpanno yathā samāhite citte tadyathā balavān puruṣaḥ saṃkuñcitaṃ bāhuṃ prasārayet*,
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having acknowledged the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s [instruction] and bowed his head at his feet, entered into such a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) that, with his mind concentrated — just as a strong man might extend a bent arm or bend an extended arm —
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 216]

children.text: prasāritaṃ vā saṃkuñcayet*, evam evāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣv antarhitaḥ, jambūdvīpe pratyaṣṭhāt* | athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano jambūdvīpam āgatya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadām ārocayati: avatariṣyati bhavanto bhagavān itaḥ saptame divase devebhyas trāyastriṃśebhyo jambūdvīpaṃ sāṃkāśye nagare āpajjure dāve udumbaramūle iti ||
children.translated_text: or might contract what is extended — just so, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having disappeared from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, reappeared in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having arrived in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, informed the four assemblies: 'The Blessed One, sirs, will descend from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods to <s>Jambudvīpa</s> in seven days from now, at the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>, in the <s>Āpajjura</s> grove, at the foot of an <s>udumbara</s> tree.' ||

children.text: avatīrṇo bhagavāṃs tataḥ saptame divase devebhyas trāyastriṃśebhyaḥ sāṃkāśye nagare āpajjure dāve udumbaramūle | yadā bhagavān sāmkāśyaṃ nagaram avatīrṇaḥ, tadā anekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi bhagavato darśanāya saṃnipatitāni | tatropapāduko bhikṣuḥ prādurbhūtaḥ | tena bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghas te ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā bhaktenopanimantritāḥ | yāvad gaṇḍīdeśanākāle sahacittotpādād divyāny āsanāny udārapaṭācchāditāni prādurbhūtāni, divyāni ca bhakṣyabhojyāni | tata upapādukena bhagavān divyenāhāreṇa saṃtarpitaḥ | te ca devāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāḥ samyag upasthitāḥ | tato 'sya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvopapādukena bhikṣuṇā idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One descended on the seventh day from that time, from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, at the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>, in the <s>Āpajjura</s> grove, at the foot of an <s>udumbara</s> tree. When the Blessed One had descended to the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s>, many hundreds of thousands of beings had assembled for the sight of the Blessed One. There a spontaneously-born (<s>upapāduka</s>) <s>bhikṣu</s> appeared. By him, the Blessed One together with the community of disciples, and those <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> were invited to a meal. At the time of the bell and teaching, simultaneously with the arising of his thought, divine seats covered with fine cloth appeared, and divine foods and delicacies. Then the Blessed One was satisfied by the spontaneously-born one with divine food, and those <s>Devas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> were properly served. Then the Blessed One, having known his dispositions, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, delivered such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching that, upon hearing it, the spontaneously-born <s>bhikṣu</s>, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> as unstable and ever-changing, having shattered all the courses of conditioned things by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, with a mind as even as the sky and the palm of the hand, as cool as an axe and sandalwood, with the egg-shell [of ignorance] split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, desire, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. ||

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta upapādukena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenopapādukaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ? sahacittotpādāc cāsya yac cintayati, tat prārthayate, tat sarvaṃ saṃṛdhyatīti | bhagavān āha: upapādukenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | upapādukenaiva karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did the spontaneously-born one perform, that he became spontaneously-born? And that simultaneously with the arising of his thought, whatever he thinks, whatever he wishes for, all of that comes to fulfillment?' The Blessed One said: 'By the spontaneously-born one himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By the spontaneously-born one himself were deeds performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:'

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_86.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ 86.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | yāvad anyatarasmin grāmake 'raṇyāyatane pañca bhikṣavo varṣā upagatāḥ tatraikena bhikṣuṇā caturṇāṃ
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He dwelt near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. In a certain village, in a forest-hermitage, five monks had entered the rainy-season retreat. There, one <s>bhikṣu</s> performed service for the four
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 217]

children.text: bhikṣūṇāṃ vaiyāvṛtyaṃ kṛtam* | tair yujyamānair ghaṭamānair vyāyacchamānaiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | pañcamena pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: yathaibhir mām āgamya arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, anena me kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca pravrajitasya upakaraṇaviśeṣair avaikalyaṃ syād iti ||
children.translated_text: monks. Through their striving, exerting, and applying themselves, they directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all defilements. The fifth one, falling at their feet, made this aspiration: 'Just as they have directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> through my [service], by this root of merit, by this arising of thought, and by this relinquishing of gifts, may there be no deficiency in requisites when I go forth as a renunciant.' ||

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena vaiyāvṛtyaṃ kṛtavān*, ayaṃ sa upapāduka iti | bhikṣava ūcuḥ: kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yenopapādukaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ? bhagavān āha: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi (Speyer: viṃśatisahasrāyuṣi) prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tatrānyataraḥ śreṣṭhī | tasya bhāryā prasavakāle duḥkhavedanābhibhūtā ārtasvarā kradanti | sa taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā paraṃ saṃvegam āpannaḥ | sa śokāgāraṃ praviśya kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ | tasya buddhir utpannā: yanv ahaṃ bhagavacchāsane pravrajya praṇidhānaṃ kuryām*, yena na kadācid garbhaśayyāṃ pratyanubhavāmīti | sa tenaiva saṃvegena bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya pravacane pravrajitaḥ | tena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yatra yatra jāyeya, tatra tatropapāduko bhaveyam*, mā kadācid garbhaśayyāṃ pratyanubhaveyam iti ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, performed the service — he is this spontaneously-born one. The monks asked: 'What deed did he perform that he became spontaneously-born?' The Blessed One said: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of humans was twenty thousand years, a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at the Deer Park in <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>. There lived a certain guild-master whose wife, at the time of delivery, overcome by painful feelings, cried out in a distressed voice. Having heard that sound, he became deeply agitated. He entered the chamber of grief and, placing his chin in his hands, stood absorbed in thought. This idea arose in him: "Let me go forth in the Blessed One's teaching and make an aspiration so that I never again experience the lying in a womb." With that very agitation, he went forth under the teaching of the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. He made this aspiration: "By this root of merit, by this arising of thought, and by this relinquishing of gifts — wherever I may be born, there may I always be spontaneously-born, and may I never again experience the lying in a womb." ||

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena sārthavāha āsīt*, ayaṃ sa upapādukaḥ | yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*, tenopapādukaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yat tatrānenendriyāṇi paripācitāni, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the caravan-leader — he is this spontaneously-born one. Because he made that aspiration, he became spontaneously-born. Because his faculties were matured there, he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.' ||

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words. ||

children.text: AVŚ_87 śobhitaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 87: <s>Śobhita</s> (The Adorned One). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme | kapilavastuni anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s>. In <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> was wealthy, possessed of great riches, great resources, of vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>'s riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal [standing]. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. She,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 218]

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'tikrānto mānuṣavarṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇam* | tasya janmany anekāny adbhutāni prādurbhūtāni, yaiḥ kapilavastu nagaraṃ samantataḥ śobhitam* | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya janmani kapilavastu nagaraṃ samantataḥ śobhitam*, tasmād asya bhavatu śobhita iti nāmeti | śobhito dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* ||
children.translated_text: after the passage of eight or nine months, gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, graceful, having surpassed the human complexion but not yet attained the divine complexion. At his birth, many wondrous things appeared, by which the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was adorned on all sides. At his birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since at his birth the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was adorned on all sides, let his name be <s>Śobhita</s> (the Adorned One).' The boy <s>Śobhita</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses, nourished on milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other excellent and choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond. ||

children.text: sa yadā mahān samvṛttas tadā nyagrodhārāmaṃ gato bhagavato darśanāya | dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā śobhitena dārakeṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had grown up, he went to the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s> to see the Blessed One. He saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his body resplendent with eighty minor characteristics, surrounded by a fathom-wide radiance, surpassing the brilliance of a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Upon seeing him, he generated faith in the Blessed One. Having generated faith, he bowed at the Blessed One's feet and sat down before him for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One, having known his dispositions, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, delivered such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching that penetrates the Four Noble Truths, that upon hearing it, the boy <s>Śobhita</s>, having shattered with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the personal self) rising with twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry. Having seen the truth, he asked permission of his parents and went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Through his striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> as unstable and ever-changing, having shattered all the courses of conditioned things by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, with a mind as even as the sky and the palm of the hand, as cool as an axe and sandalwood, with the egg-shell [of ignorance] split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, desire, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. ||

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta śobhitena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'tikrānto mānuṣavarṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇam*, janmani cāsyānekāni adbhutāni prādurbhūtāni, yaiḥ kapilavastu nagaraṃ samantataḥ śobhitam*? bhagavān āha: śobhitenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | śobhitenaiva karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, questioned the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What deeds, Venerable One, were performed by <s>Śobhita</s>, that he was born beautiful, lovely, graceful, surpassing human complexion yet not having attained divine complexion, and at his birth many wonders appeared, by which the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was adorned on all sides?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "By <s>Śobhita</s> himself, monks, in previous births, deeds were performed and accumulated, their provisions gathered, their conditions ripened, standing ready like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. By <s>Śobhita</s> himself, deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else will experience their results? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_87.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. (AVŚ 87.1)
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 219]

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe catvāriṃśadvarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ krakucchando nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa śobhāvatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | śobhena rājñā keśanakhastūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ | yāvat kasmiṃścit parvaṇi pratyupasthite goṣṭhikāḥ stūpasamīpaṃ gatāḥ | tais taṃ stūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā pasādajātaiḥ puṣpāropaṇaṃ kartum ārabdham* | tatraiko goṣṭhikaḥ kathayati: ahaṃ na karomi, mama vibhavo nāstīti | sa taiś ca goṣṭhikamadhyān niṣkāsitaḥ | tasya vipratisāro jātaḥ | tena vicitrapuṣpasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā tasminn eva stūpe puṣpāropaṇaṃ kṛtam* ||
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, monks, in the past, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was forty thousand years, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Krakucchanda</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the royal capital of <s>Śobhāvatī</s>. King <s>Śobha</s> established a <s>stūpa</s> for the hair and nail relics. When a certain festival arrived, the guild members went to the vicinity of the <s>stūpa</s>. Seeing the <s>stūpa</s> and filled with faith, they began to offer flowers. One guild member said: "I will not participate; I have no wealth." He was expelled from the guild. He felt remorse. Then, having gathered various flowers, he made a flower offering at that very <s>stūpa</s>.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena goṣṭhika āsīt, yena vipratisārajātena krakucchandasya keśanakhastūpe puṣpāripaṇaṃ kṛtam*, ayam asau śobhitaḥ | anyāny api hi bhikṣavaḥ śobhitena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī | tena glānaḥ pratyekabuddho dṛṣṭaḥ | tataḥ prasādajātena pādayor nipatya piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ paṭena cācchāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, monks? He who was at that time the guild member who, filled with remorse, offered flowers at the hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Krakucchanda</s> — he is this <s>Śobhita</s>. Furthermore, monks, other deeds were also performed and accumulated by <s>Śobhita</s>. Once upon a time, in the past, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain merchant. He saw a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Awakened One) who was ill. Then, with faith arisen, falling at his feet, he provided him with alms-food and covered him with cloth."

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena śreṣṭhī, ayaṃ śobhitaḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati daridro 'bhūt kāṣṭhahārakaḥ | sa kāṣṭhānām arthe parvatadarīṃ praviṣṭaḥ | tena stūpo dṛṣṭaḥ | tatra ca stūpāṅgaṇe tṛṇāni jātāni | tatas tena prasādajātena tṛṇāny utpāṭya saṃmārjanīṃ gṛhītvā stūpāṅgaṇaṃ ca saṃmṛṣṭam* | tataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deydharmaparityāgena ca abhirūpaḥ syāṃ darśanīyaḥ prasādikaḥ, anāgatāṃś ca buddhān ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: "What do you think, monks? He who was at that time the merchant — he is this <s>Śobhita</s>. Furthermore, under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, he was a poor firewood gatherer. He entered a mountain cave to collect firewood. There he saw a <s>stūpa</s>. Grass had grown in the courtyard of the <s>stūpa</s>. Then, with faith arisen, he uprooted the grass, took a broom, and swept the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard. Then, falling at its base, he began to make a vow: 'By this wholesome root, this aspiration, and this gift of offerings, may I be beautiful, lovely, and graceful, and may I please the future <s>Buddhas</s> and not displease them.'"

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena kāṣṭhahāraka āsīt, ayam evāsau śobhitaḥ | yad anena stūpāṅgaṇaṃ saṃmṛṣṭam*, tena yatra yatra jātas tatra tatrābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prasādikaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | tenaiva hetunedānīm ārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, monks? He who was at that time the firewood gatherer — he is this very <s>Śobhita</s>. Because he swept the <s>stūpa</s> courtyard, wherever he was born, he became beautiful, lovely, and graceful. By that very cause, he has now directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship). Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, entirely bright; for those mixed, mixed. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only in entirely bright deeds. Thus should you train, monks."

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_88 kapphiṇaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 88: <s>Kapphiṇa</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 220]

children.text: saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | tena khalu samayena dakṣiṇāpathe kalpo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | priyam ivaikaputrakaṃ rājyaṃ pālayati | so 'pareṇa samayena devyā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā kapphiṇa iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* | kapphiṇo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | yasminn eva divase kapphiṇaḥ kumāro jātaḥ, tasminn eva divase aṣṭādaśānām amātyasahasrāṇāṃ putrā jātāḥ, sarve mahānagnāḥ | teṣāṃ pratirūpāṇi nāmāni vyavasthāpitāni ||
children.translated_text: together with the monastic community, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, in the southern region (<s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>), a king named <s>Kalpa</s> was ruling a kingdom that was prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from thieves and disease, and abundant in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. He governed the kingdom as dearly as an only son. At a later time, he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with his queen. A son was born to him — beautiful, lovely, graceful, endowed with all major and minor limbs. At his birth, having performed the birth celebration, the name <s>Kapphiṇa</s> was given. The boy <s>Kapphiṇa</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. On the very day Prince <s>Kapphiṇa</s> was born, sons were also born to eighteen thousand ministers, all of great physical strength. Suitable names were given to them.

children.text: yad rājā kalpaḥ kāladharmeṇa saṃyuktaḥ, tasyātyayāt kapphiṇaḥ kumāro rājye pratiṣṭhitaḥ | tāni cāṣṭādaśāmātyaputrasahasrāṇi sarvāṇy amātyatve niyuktāni | athāpareṇa samayena rājā mahākapphiṇo 'ṣṭādaśāmātyasahasraparivṛto mṛgavadhāya nirgataḥ | purastāt pṛṣṭhataś ca sarvabalaugham avalokyāmātyān āmantrayate: asti bhavantaḥ kasyacid evaṃrūpo balaughaḥ tadyathā mamaivaitarhīti? tataḥ priyavādibhir amātyair abhihitam*: deva nānyasya kasyacid iti | atha madhyadeśād vaṇijo dakṣiṇāpathaṃ gatāḥ | tai rājño mahākapphiṇasya prābhṛtam upanītam* | rājñā uktāḥ: bho vaṇijaḥ, kas tatra rājeti | vaṇijaḥ kathayanti: deva kecid deśā gaṇādhīnāḥ kecid rājādhīnā iti | yāvad rājñā mahākapphiṇena śrāvastyādiṣu ṣaṭsu mahānagareṣu dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtam* | yady utthitā bhavatha nopaveṣṭavyam*, śīghram āgantavyam*, anyathā va uttamena daṇḍena samanuśāsiṣyāmīti | etad vacanam upaśrutya ṣaṇmahānagaravāsino rājāno bhītās trastāḥ saṃvignā āhṛṣṭaromakūpāḥ saṃgamya samāgamya ekasamūhena śrāvastīm anuprāptāḥ | tato bhagavatsakāśaṃ gatāḥ | taiḥ sa vṛttānto bhagavato vistareṇa niveditaḥ | bhagavatā te samāśvāsitāḥ, uktāś ca: sa dūto matsakāśam ānetavya iti | tatas tair dūtasya niveditam* | asty asmākaṃ rājādhirāja, taṃ tāvat paśyeti ||
children.translated_text: When King <s>Kalpa</s> passed away according to the law of death, Prince <s>Kapphiṇa</s> was established on the throne. All eighteen thousand ministers' sons were appointed to ministerial positions. At a later time, King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>, accompanied by his eighteen thousand ministers, went out to hunt deer. Looking at his entire army before and behind him, he addressed the ministers: "Sirs, does anyone else have such a mighty army as mine at this time?" Then the ministers, being flatterers, replied: "Sire, no one else does." Meanwhile, merchants from the central region had gone to the southern region. They brought gifts for King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>. The king asked them: "Good merchants, who rules there?" The merchants said: "Sire, some regions are governed by assemblies, and some by kings." Then King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s> sent messengers to the six great cities beginning with <s>Śrāvastī</s>: "If you have risen up, do not sit back down; come quickly; otherwise I will punish you with the supreme penalty." Hearing this message, the kings dwelling in the six great cities, frightened, terrified, agitated, with hair standing on end, gathered and assembled together, and arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s> as one group. They went to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and reported the whole matter to him in detail. The <s>Bhagavān</s> reassured them and said: "That messenger should be brought to me." They informed the messenger: "We have a supreme king; go and see him first."

children.text: tato bhagavatā dūtāgamanam avetya jetavanaṃ catūratnamayam nirmitaṃ devānām iva sudarśanaṃ nagaram* | atra catvāro mahārājāno dauvārikāḥ sthāpitāḥ, airāvatasadṛśā hastinaḥ, bālāhakasadṛśā aśvāḥ, nandīghoṣasadṛśā rathāḥ, vyāḍayakṣsadṛśā manuṣyāḥ | svayaṃ ca bhagavatā cakravartiveṣo nirmitaḥ, saptatālodgataṃ ca simḥāsanaṃ yatra bhagavān niṣaṇṇāḥ | tato dūtas tathāvidhāṃ śobhāṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ | tato bhagavatā lekhaṃ lekhayitvā sa dūto 'bhihitaḥ: kapphiṇo madvacanād vaktavyaḥ: lekhavācanasamakālam eva yady utthito bhavasi, nopaveṣṭavyam*, śīghram āgantavyam* |
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the messenger was coming, magically created the <s>Jetavana</s> made of four kinds of jewels, like the city of <s>Sudarśana</s> of the gods. The four great kings were placed as doorkeepers; there were elephants resembling <s>Airāvata</s>, horses resembling <s>Bālāhaka</s>, chariots resembling <s>Nandīghoṣa</s>, and men resembling <s>Vyāḍa</s> <s>yakṣas</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> himself created the appearance of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), and a lion-throne rising to the height of seven palm trees, upon which the <s>Bhagavān</s> was seated. Then the messenger, seeing such splendor, was overcome with great amazement. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having had a letter written, addressed the messenger: "Tell <s>Kapphiṇa</s> in my name: 'At the very moment you read this letter, if you have risen up, do not sit back down; come quickly.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 221]

children.text: athavā nāgacchasi, aham eva mahatā balaughena sārdham āgamiṣyāmīti | tato dūtena gatvā rājño mahākapphiṇasya lekhaṃ vācikaṃ ca yat saṃdiṣṭaṃ tat sarvaṃ niveditam* ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if you do not come, I myself will come with a great army.'" Then the messenger went and reported to King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s> the letter and the entire verbal message that had been conveyed.

children.text: tataḥ kapphiṇo rājā aṣṭādaśāmātyagaṇasahasraparivṛto 'nupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇaḥ śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ | prātisīmāś ca rājāno rājānaṃ mahākapphiṇaṃ pratyudgatāḥ | tair mahāsatkāreṇa nagaraṃ praveśitaḥ | mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya bhagavato niveditavantaḥ | tato bhagavatā tasyāgamanam avetya jetavanaṃ catūratnamayaṃ nirmitaṃ devānām iva sudarśanaṃ nagaram* | yatra catvāro mahārājāno dauvārikāḥ sthāpitāḥ | airāvatasadṛśā hastinaḥ, bālāhakasadṛśā aśvāḥ, nandīghoṣasadṛśā rathāḥ, vyāḍayakṣasadṛśā manuṣyāḥ | svayaṃ ca bhagavatā cakravartiveṣo nirmitaḥ | saptatālodgataṃ ca siṃhāsanaṃ sarvaṃ tathaiva nirmitam* | tato rājā mahākapphiṇo jetavanaṃ praviṣṭaḥ | sahadarśanād asya yo rūpo rūpamadaḥ, aiśvarye aiśvaryamadaḥ, sa prativigataḥ | baladarpo 'dyāpi pratibādhata eva | tato bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittam utpāditam*: aho bata śakro devendra aindraṃ dhanur ādāya āgacchatv iti | sahacittotpādād bhagavataḥ śakro devendraḥ sārathiveṣeṇa aindraṃ dhanur upanāmayati | bhagavatā mahākapphiṇasyopanāmitam* | tac ca rājā mahākapphiṇa utkraṣṭum api na śaknoti, kutaḥ punar āropayiṣyati | tato bhagavatā saptāyobheryo nirmittāḥ | svayaṃ ca tad dhanur ardhacandrākāreṇāropya śaraḥ kṣiptaḥ, yena tāḥ saptāyobheryaś chidrīkṛtāḥ | tataḥ śabdaṃ nirgataḥ:
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, accompanied by his retinue of eighteen thousand ministers, traveling stage by stage, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The frontier kings came out to receive King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>. With great honor they ushered him into the city. Having refreshed himself from the fatigue of the journey, they informed the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing of his arrival, magically created the <s>Jetavana</s> made of four kinds of jewels, like the city of <s>Sudarśana</s> of the gods. The four great kings were placed as doorkeepers; there were elephants resembling <s>Airāvata</s>, horses resembling <s>Bālāhaka</s>, chariots resembling <s>Nandīghoṣa</s>, and men resembling <s>Vyāḍa</s> <s>yakṣas</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> himself created the appearance of a <s>cakravartin</s>. A lion-throne rising to the height of seven palm trees — everything was created just as before. Then King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s> entered the <s>Jetavana</s>. Upon seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>, his pride in his own beauty and his pride in his sovereignty vanished. But his pride in military power still persisted. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> generated a worldly thought: "If only <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, would come bringing <s>Indra</s>'s bow." At the very instant of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s thought, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, in the guise of a charioteer, offered <s>Indra</s>'s bow. The <s>Bhagavān</s> offered it to <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>. But King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s> could not even lift it, let alone string it. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> created seven iron drums. He himself strung that bow in the shape of a half-moon and shot an arrow, which pierced through all seven iron drums. Then a sound issued forth:

children.text: ārabhadhvaṃ niṣkrāmata yujyadhvaṃ buddhaśāsane |
children.translated_text: "Strive forth, go out, engage yourselves in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: dhunīta mṛtyunaḥ sainyaṃ naḍāgāram iva kuñjaraḥ || AVŚ_88.1 ||
children.translated_text: crush the army of death, as an elephant crushes a hut of reeds." (AVŚ 88.1)

children.text:
yo hy asmin dharmavinaye apramattaś cariṣyati |
  prahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati || AVŚ_88.2 || iti
children.translated_text: For whoever shall live heedfully in this Dharma and Vinaya, having abandoned the cycle of birth and saṃsāra, shall make an end of suffering. // AVŚ_88.2 //

children.text:
sa ca śabdo yāvad akaniṣṭhān devān gataḥ | tato rājñaḥ kapphiṇasya yo 'bhūd balamadaḥ, sa prativigataḥ | tasya buddhir utpannā: kim idam iti | tato bhagavān rājño mahākapphiṇasya cittaprakāram upalakṣya rājaveṣam antardhāpya idaṃ sūtram āradbhavān*: <Cf. DbSū(2)>
  daśabalasamanvāgato bhikṣavas tathāgato 'han samyaksaṃbuddhaś catur vaiśāradyaviśārada udāram ārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ pratijānīte, brahmacaryaṃ pravartayati, parṣadi samyaksiṃhanādaṃ nadati: yadutāsmin satīdaṃ bhavati, asyotpādād idam utpadyate | yaduta avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ | saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam* | vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam* | nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam* | ṣaḍayatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ | sparśapratyayā vedanā | vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā | tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānam* | upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ | bhavapratyayā jātiḥ | jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | yaduta asminn asatīdaṃ na bhavati, asya nirodhād idaṃ nirudhyate | yaduta avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ
children.translated_text: And that sound reached as far as the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods. Then the pride of power that King <s>Kapphiṇa</s> had — that vanished. This thought arose in him: 'What is this?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having perceived the disposition of King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>'s mind, caused the royal guise to disappear and began this discourse: [Cf. DbSū(2)] 'Monks, I, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the fully enlightened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, endowed with the ten powers, confident with the four confidences, claim the supreme, bull-like station, set the holy life in motion, and roar the lion's roar rightly in the assembly: namely, when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises. That is to say: conditioned by ignorance are the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); conditioned by the formations is consciousness; conditioned by consciousness is name-and-form; conditioned by name-and-form are the six sense-bases; conditioned by the six sense-bases is contact; conditioned by contact is feeling; conditioned by feeling is craving; conditioned by craving is grasping; conditioned by grasping is becoming; conditioned by becoming is birth; conditioned by birth arise old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair. Thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering. That is to say: when this does not exist, that does not come to be; from the cessation of this, that ceases. That is to say: from the cessation of ignorance comes the cessation of formations;
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 222]

children.text: | saṃskāranirodhād vijñānanirodhaḥ | vijñānanirodhān nāmarūpanirodhaḥ | nāmarūpanirodhāt ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ | ṣaḍāyatananirodhāt sparśanirodhaḥ | sparśanirodhād vedanānirodhaḥ | vedanānirodhāt tṛṣṇānirodhaḥ | tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodhaḥ | upādānanirodhād bhavanirodhaḥ | bhavanirodhāj jātinirodhaḥ | jātinirodhāj jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante | evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati | svākhyāto me bhikṣavo dharmaḥ, uttāno vivṛtaś chinnaplotiko yāvad devamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksuprakāśitaḥ | evaṃ svākhyāte me dharme uttāne vivṛte chinnaplotike yāvad devamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyaksuprakāśite yāvad alam eva bhikṣavaḥ śraddhāpravrajitena kulaputreṇa alaṃ yogāya alam apramādāya, alaṃ śāstuḥ śāsane yogam āpattum*, kāmaṃ tvaksnāyvasthy avatiṣṭhatām*, pariśuṣyatu śarīrān māṃsaśoṇitam* | atha ca punar yat tadārabdhavīryeṇa prāptavyaṃ sthāmavatā vīryavatā utsāhinā dṛḍhaparākrameṇānikṣiptadhureṇa kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu, tadvahanānuprāptā na vīryasya sraṃsanaṃ bhaviṣyati | tat kasya hetoḥ? duḥkhaṃ hi kusīdo viharati vyavakīrṇa, pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ sāṃkleśikaiḥ paunarbhavikaiḥ sajvarair duḥkhavipākaiḥ āyatyāṃ jātijarāmaraṇīyaiḥ mahataś cārthasya parihāṇir bhavati | ārabdhavīryas tu sukhaṃ viharaty avakīrṇaḥ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ sāṃkleśikaiḥ paunarbhavikaiḥ sajvarair duḥkhavipākaiḥ āyatyāṃ jātijarāmaraṇīyaiḥ | mahataś cārthasya pāripūrir bhavati | maṇḍayeyam idaṃ pravacanaṃ yaduta śāstā ca saṃmukhībhūtaḥ | dharmaś ca deśyata aupaśamikaḥ pārinirvāṇikaḥ saṃbodhigāmī sugatapraveditaḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ātmārthaṃ ca samanupaśyadbhiḥ parārthaṃ cobhayārthaṃ ca, idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣitavyam: kaccin naḥ pravrajyā amoghā bhaviṣyati, saphalā sukhodayā sukhavipākā | yeṣāṃ ca paribhokṣyāmahe cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān*, teṣāṃ ca te kārāḥ kṛtāḥ kaccid atyarthamahāphalā bhaviṣyanti, mahānuśaṃsā mahādyutayo mahāvaistārāḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: from the cessation of formations comes the cessation of consciousness; from the cessation of consciousness comes the cessation of name-and-form; from the cessation of name-and-form comes the cessation of the six sense-bases; from the cessation of the six sense-bases comes the cessation of contact; from the cessation of contact comes the cessation of feeling; from the cessation of feeling comes the cessation of craving; from the cessation of craving comes the cessation of grasping; from the cessation of grasping comes the cessation of becoming; from the cessation of becoming comes the cessation of birth; from the cessation of birth, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair cease. Thus there is the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering. Well-proclaimed by me, monks, is the <s>Dharma</s> — clear, open, with its covering removed, well-illuminated even for gods and humans. In this <s>Dharma</s> of mine, so well-proclaimed, clear, open, with its covering removed, well-illuminated even for gods and humans, it is enough for a son of good family who has gone forth out of faith to strive for exertion, for heedfulness, for applying himself to the Teacher's teaching. Let only skin, sinews, and bones remain — let the flesh and blood dry up from the body! Yet that which is to be attained by one of firm energy, possessed of strength and vigor, of resolute and unflagging effort in wholesome qualities — until that is reached, there shall be no relaxation of effort. For what reason? Because the indolent one dwells in suffering, beset by evil, unwholesome qualities that are defiling, conducive to renewed existence, fraught with distress, and ripening in suffering, leading in the future to birth, old age, and death; and there is the loss of a great purpose. But one of aroused energy dwells happily, unbeset by evil, unwholesome qualities that are defiling, conducive to renewed existence, fraught with distress, and ripening in suffering, leading in the future to birth, old age, and death; and there is the fulfillment of a great purpose. One should adorn this dispensation — namely, that the Teacher is present, and the <s>Dharma</s> is being taught, a <s>Dharma</s> that leads to calm, to <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, that conduces to awakening, proclaimed by the <s>Sugata</s>. Therefore, monks, seeing your own welfare, the welfare of others, and the welfare of both, this is to be practiced: "May our going forth not be fruitless, but fruitful, with a happy outcome, with a happy result. And may the offerings of those whose robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick we shall enjoy — may those acts of theirs be of exceedingly great fruit, of great benefit, of great splendor, of great extent!" Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe rājñā mahākapphiṇena aṣṭādaśāmātyagaṇasahasraparivāreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, King <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>, together with his retinue of eighteen thousand ministers, having shattered the mountain of the view of the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) with its twenty peaks by the vajra of knowledge, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>Srotāpattiphala</s>). He, having seen the truth, went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta kapphiṇena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'ṣṭādaśāmātyagaṇasahasraparivāro mahānagnabalaḥ, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: kapphiṇenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni |
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Kapphiṇa</s> perform that he became handsome, good-looking, and graceful, surrounded by a retinue of eighteen thousand ministers, possessing great physical strength, and that having gone forth he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Kapphiṇa</s> himself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 223]

children.text: kapphiṇena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: By <s>Kapphiṇa</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_88.3 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_88.3 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati bandhumatīyake dāve | yāvad anyatamena sārthavāhena mahāsamudrāt prabhūtāni ratnāny ānītāni | vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saśrāvakasaṃghas traimāsyaṃ bhaktenopanimantritaḥ | vihāraṃ ca kārayitvā cāturdiśāya bhikṣusaṃghāya bhikṣusaṃghāya niryātitavān* ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>, in the <s>Bandhumatīya</s> grove. Now a certain caravan-leader brought back abundant gems from the great ocean. He invited the fully enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s> together with the community of disciples to a three-month meal-offering. And having built a monastery, he donated it to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four quarters.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ yo 'sau sārthavāhaḥ, eṣa evāsau kapphiṇo rājā tena kālena tena samayena | yad anena vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ saśrāvakasaṃghas traimāsyaṃ svāntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ, vihāraṃ ca kārayitvā cāturdiśāya bhikṣusaṃghāya niryātitaḥ ### {tenedānīm abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ} ### aparāṇy api bhikṣavaḥ kapphiṇena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati | so 'pareṇa samayena saṃprāpte vasantakālasamaye, saṃpuṣpiteṣu pādapeṣu, haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukaśārikākokilajīvañjīvakanirghoṣite vanaṣaṇḍe aṣṭādaśāmātyagaṇasahasraparivṛta udyānaṃ nirgataḥ | tena tatrodyāne glānaḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ dṛṣṭaḥ | sa tena sāṃpreyabhojanena traimāsyam upasthitaḥ | parinirvṛtasya ca śarīrastūpaṃ kārayitvā amātyagaṇasahāyena tailābhiṣeko dattaḥ | tena saparivāro mahānagnabalādhānena saṃvṛttaḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajite babhūva | tatrānenendriyaparipākaḥ kṛtaḥ | tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, monks? He who was that caravan-leader — he is this King <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, at that time, in that era. Because he invited the fully enlightened <s>Vipaśyin</s> together with the community of disciples to a three-month meal-offering in his own home and built a monastery and donated it to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four quarters, {he has now become handsome, good-looking, and graceful.} Furthermore, monks, <s>Kapphiṇa</s> performed and accumulated other deeds as well. In former times, monks, in a past age, in the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. He was a righteous king, ruling righteously. On a later occasion, when the spring season had arrived, when the trees were in bloom, in a forest grove resounding with the calls of geese, herons, peacocks, parrots, mynahs, cuckoos, and <s>jīvañjīvaka</s> birds, he went forth to a park surrounded by a retinue of eighteen thousand ministers. There, in that park, he saw a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> who was ill. He attended upon him with food for three months. And when [the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>] had passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, having built a <s>stūpa</s> over his bodily relics, he together with the company of ministers made an offering of oil-anointing. By that he became one with a great retinue, endowed with great physical strength. Furthermore, he went forth under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There he accomplished the maturation of his faculties. By that he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 224]

children.text: AVŚ_89 bhadrikaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_89: <s>Bhadrika</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

children.text: yadā bhagavān ṣaḍvarṣābhisaṃbuddho dvādaśavarṣanirgataḥ kapilavastu anuprāptaḥ, tadā droṇodanāmṛtodanapramukhair anekaiḥ śākyasahasraiḥ satyadarśanaṃ kṛtaṃ sthāpayitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanam* | tato rājā śuddhodanas tāṃ putraśobhāṃ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ | tasya buddhir utpannā: yadi me putro na pravrajito 'bhaviṣyat*, so 'yam abhaviṣyad rājā cakravartī caturantavijetā dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ | sa etarhi jaṭilapravrajitaparivāro na śobhate | yanv ahaṃ śākyakulebhya ekaikaṃ pravrājayeyam iti | tato rājñā śuddhodanena nagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam*: sarvaśākyaiḥ saṃnipattavyam iti | tataḥ sarvaśākyeṣu saṃnipatiteṣu rājā śuddhodanaḥ kathayati: śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ śākyāḥ | yadi sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro na pravrajito 'bhaviṣyat*, yad yuṣmābhir evopasthānaṃ kṛtam abhaviṣyat* | tad idānīm asya pravrajitasya ekaikena kulapuruṣeṇa śākyenopasthāyakena pravrajitavyam iti | tato bhadrikāniruddharevatadevadattaprabhṛtīni pacca kumāraśatāni pravrajitāni | teṣām upālir nāma kalpaka upasthāyakaḥ tān pravrajitān dṛṣṭvā roditum ārabdhaḥ | tataḥ śākyaiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ: kimartham upāle rudyata iti | sa karuṇadīnavilambitair akṣarair uvāca: yūyaṃ pravrajitāḥ | ko mamedānīṃ bhahtācchādanena paripālanaṃ kariṣyatīti | tataḥ śākyā ūcuḥ: tena hi upāle, paṭakaṃ prasārayeti | tena paṭakaḥ prasāritaḥ | tataḥ śākyaiḥ śarīrāvalagnānāṃ hārārdhahāramaṇimukhtāvaiḍūryakeyūrāṅgulīyakānāṃ mahān rāśiḥ kṛtaḥ | tata upāleḥ kalpakasya tān dṛṣṭvā vicitraṃ cālaṃkāram abhivīkṣya yoniśo manasikāra utpannaḥ: ime tāvac chākyāḥ kularūpayuvanavanto 'ntaḥpurāṇi imaṃ cālaṃkāraṃ kheṭavad utsṛjya pravrajitāḥ | kim utāham alpavibhavaḥ imam alaṃkāraṃ gṛhaṃ neṣyāmi? alam anena | yanv aham etān anupravrajeyam iti | athopāliḥ kalpako yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ, upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya bhagavantam idam avocat*: yadi bhagavan mādṛśānāṃ pravrajyā asti, labheyāhaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam*, careyam aham bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam iti | tato bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā pravrājitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who had been fully awakened for six years and had gone forth for twelve years, arrived at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, at that time, many thousands of <s>Śākyas</s> led by <s>Droṇodana</s> and <s>Amṛtodana</s> had attained the vision of truth, except for King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, seeing that splendor of his son, was filled with supreme wonder. This thought arose in him: 'If my son had not gone forth, he would have become a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), a conqueror of the four quarters, a righteous <s>Dharmarāja</s> (king of righteousness). But now, surrounded by matted-haired ascetics as his retinue, he does not look fitting. Let me ordain one person from each <s>Śākya</s> family.' Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had a bell-proclamation made in the city: 'All <s>Śākyas</s> must assemble.' When all the <s>Śākyas</s> had assembled, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: 'Listen, noble <s>Śākyas</s>! If Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> had not gone forth, you yourselves would have served him. Therefore now, for this one who has gone forth, one young man from each <s>Śākya</s> family must go forth as an attendant.' Then five hundred princes led by <s>Bhadrika</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Revata</s>, and <s>Devadatta</s> went forth. Their attendant was a barber named <s>Upāli</s>. Seeing them gone forth, he began to weep. Then the <s>Śākyas</s> asked: 'Why do you weep, <s>Upāli</s>?' He spoke with words faltering, pitiful, and drawn out: 'You have gone forth. Who will now provide for me with food and clothing?' Then the <s>Śākyas</s> said: 'Well then, <s>Upāli</s>, spread out a cloth.' He spread out a cloth. Then the <s>Śākyas</s> made a great heap of necklaces, half-necklaces, jewels, pearls, beryl, armlets, and rings from their own bodies. Then <s>Upāli</s> the barber, seeing those things and gazing upon that splendid ornament, had a proper reflection arise in him: 'These <s>Śākyas</s>, who are of noble family, handsome, and youthful, have cast aside their harems and these ornaments as if they were spittle and gone forth. How much more should I, a man of small means, not carry these ornaments home? Enough of this! Let me follow them and go forth.' Then <s>Upāli</s> the barber approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having approached, fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is ordination for those such as me, may I obtain the going forth, the <s>upasaṃpadā</s> (full ordination), and the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. I would practice the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.' Then he was ordained by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with the <s>ehibhikṣukā</s> ('Come, monk!') ordination.

children.text: tato bhadrikapramukhāni pañca śākyaśatāni bhikṣunepathyadhārīṇi (Speyer: bhikṣuveṣadhārīṇi) buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṃghasya praṇāmaṃ kartúṃ pravṛttāni | te upāliṃ jñātvā kularūpavibhavānvitatvān necchanty upāleḥ
children.translated_text: Then the five hundred <s>Śākya</s> [princes] led by <s>Bhadrika</s>, wearing the attire of monks, proceeded to pay homage to the monastic community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>. But knowing <s>Upāli</s>'s [former status], due to their pride in family, beauty, and wealth, they did not wish to pay homage to <s>Upāli</s>
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 225]

children.text:
praṇāmaṃ kartum* | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ bhadrikam āmantrayate: bhadrika kartavyo 'sya praṇāmaḥ, yasmād idaṃ māmakaṃ śāsanaṃ na kularūpayauvanaiśvaryacāturvarṇyaviśuddhim apekṣata iti | tato mūlanikṛttā iva drumā bhadrikapramukhāni pañca śākyaśatāni dharmatām avalambya pādayor nipatitāni | teṣām pādavandanasamakālam eveyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitā |
  tatrāyuṣmatā bhadrikeṇa yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | sa ca mahātmā hīnadīnānukampī | so 'pareṇa samayena pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ gocarāya prasthitaḥ | yāvad anyataracaṇḍālakaṭhinaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ | tena khalu samayena rājā prasenajit kauśala ekapuṇḍarīkaṃ hastināgam abhiruhya dīrgheṇa cārāyaṇena sārathinā bhagavato darśanāya saṃprasthitaḥ | dadarśa rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhadrikaṃ śāntendriyaṃ śāntamānasam*, parameṇa ca cittadamavyupaśamanasamanvāgataṃ pāṃsukūlaprāvṛtaṃ lūhaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ gṛhītvā tasmāc caṇḍālakaṭhinān nirgacchantam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar dīrghaṃ cārāyaṇaṃ sārathim āmantrayate: syād ayaṃ cārāyaṇa bhadriko bhikṣuḥ? evaṃ yathā vadasi | iti śrutvā rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ saṃmoham āpannaḥ, pṛthivyāṃ mūrcchitaḥ patitaḥ | tato jalapariṣekapratyāgataprāṇacetaso labdhamānasaś cārāyaṇena sārathinotthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text:
to pay homage. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the venerable <s>Bhadrika</s>: '<s>Bhadrika</s>, homage must be paid to him, because this teaching of mine does not depend on distinctions of family, beauty, youth, sovereignty, or the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).' Then, like trees cut at the root, the five hundred <s>Śākya</s> [princes] led by <s>Bhadrika</s>, relying on the <s>Dharma</s>, fell at his feet. At the very moment of their prostration, this great earth trembled with six kinds of quaking.
There, the venerable <s>Bhadrika</s>, by striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable and ever-changing, and having struck down all the courses of conditioned formations by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. And he was a great soul, compassionate toward the lowly and wretched. On a later occasion, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, he set out to <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. He entered a certain outcaste settlement for alms. At that time, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s>, mounted on the royal elephant <s>Ekapuṇḍarīka</s>, had set out with <s>Dīrgha Cārāyaṇa</s> as his charioteer to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>. King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> saw <s>Bhadrika</s> — with senses stilled, with mind at peace, endowed with supreme tranquility and self-control, wrapped in rag-robes, taking meager alms-food and coming out of that outcaste settlement. Having seen him, he addressed <s>Dīrgha Cārāyaṇa</s> the charioteer: 'Could this be, <s>Cārāyaṇa</s>, the monk <s>Bhadrika</s>?' 'Indeed it is, just as you say.' Hearing this, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> was overcome with shock and fell unconscious to the ground. Then, his life and consciousness having returned through the sprinkling of water, having regained his senses, he was raised up by <s>Cārāyaṇa</s> the charioteer.

children.text: tato rājā bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam uvāca: bhagavan, adbhutaṃ me dṛṣṭam* | asau bhadrikaḥ śākyarājaḥ pāṃsukūlaprāvṛto lūhaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ gṛhītvā devamanuṣyāvarjanakareṇātipraśānteneryāpathena piṇḍapātam ādāya caṇḍālakaṭhinān nirgataḥ | tasya mamaitad abhavat*: āścarya yāvat suvinītaṃ bhagavacchāsanam*, yatra nāma evaṃvidhāḥ kumārāḥ sukhaidhitā evaṃvinītapracārāḥ saṃvṛttā iti | bhagavān āha: aparam api mahārāja bhadrikasyāścaryaṃ śṛṇu | ayaṃ mahārāja bhadriko 'raṇyagato vā vṛkṣamūlagato vā śūnyāgāragato vā trir udānayati: aho bata saukhyam* | yad aham apravrajitaḥ san rājakulamadhyagato 'mātyanaigamajānapadasusaṃrakṣitaḥ prākāraparikhādvārastūpābhinigūḍhaḥ pariśaṅkitahṛdayaḥ saṃvignaḥ samantataḥśaṅkī nidrāṃ nāsādayāmi | so 'ham etarhi nirapekṣaḥ kāye jīvite ca sukhaṃ yatratatrastho viharāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Then the king approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, I have seen something wondrous! That <s>Bhadrika</s>, a <s>Śākya</s> king, wrapped in rag-robes, carrying meager alms-food, walking with an exceedingly tranquil deportment that captivates gods and men, came out of an outcaste settlement having collected his alms. This thought arose in me: "How wonderful! How well-trained is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching, in which princes of such standing, raised in luxury, conduct themselves with such discipline!"' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Hear yet another wonder of <s>Bhadrika</s>, O great king. This <s>Bhadrika</s>, O great king, whether gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, utters this <s>udāna</s> (joyful exclamation) three times: "Oh, what happiness! Oh, what happiness! Oh, what happiness!" For when I had not gone forth, dwelling in the midst of the royal palace, well-guarded by ministers, townspeople, and country-folk, concealed behind ramparts, moats, gates, and towers, with an anxious heart, alarmed, suspicious on all sides, I could not find sleep. But now I am free from care, unconcerned about body and life, and I dwell happily wherever I may be.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta bhadrikeṇa pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādika āḍhye rājakule pratyājātaḥ | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: bhadrikeṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | bhadrikeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati?
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Bhadrika</s> perform in previous births, that he was born handsome, beautiful, and pleasing, in a wealthy royal family, and having gone forth, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Bhadrika</s> himself, monks, who in previous births performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood before him like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass. <s>Bhadrika</s> performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience their results?
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 226]

children.text: na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi api kalpaśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_89.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_89.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamaḥ koṭṭamallakaḥ kṣutkṣāmaparigataśarīraḥ itaś cāmutaś cānvāhiṇḍate | yāvad anyatarā dārikā pūpalikā ādāya gacchati | tatas tena koṭṭamallakena sā dārikā pūpalikānām arthe abhibhūtā | tato balād ekām pūpalikām ādāya itas tataḥ (Speyer: ta<tas ta>taḥ) palāyitum ārabdhaḥ | sā cāsya dārikā pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaiva | tato 'sau koṭṭamallakaḥ sahasā nadīcārikām uttīrṇaḥ | asati buddhānām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya | tadā anyataraḥ pratyekabuddhas tasya koṭṭamallakasyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ | tataḥ koṭṭamallasya taṃ pratyekabuddhaṃ śānteryāpathaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahān prasādo jātaḥ | tena svaṃ vyasanam agaṇayya pratyekabuddhāya pūpalikā pratipāditā | tasya vipraharṣasaṃjananārthaṃ vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājo gaganatalam abhyudgamya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayitum ārabdhaḥ | tataḥ koṭṭamallakas tad atyadbhutaṃ devamanuṣyāvarjanakaraṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā mūlanikṛttā iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: yan me siddhavrato dakṣiṇīyaḥ pūpalikayā pratipāditaḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yatra yatra jāyeya, tatra tatroccakulīnaḥ syām*, evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syām*, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a certain <s>koṭṭamallaka</s> (wrestler), his body afflicted with hunger and thirst, was wandering here and there. Just then, a certain girl was going along carrying cakes. That wrestler overpowered the girl for the sake of her cakes. Then, having forcibly seized one cake, he began to run away in all directions. And that girl followed closely behind him. Then that wrestler hastily crossed a river ford. When <s>Buddhas</s> have not arisen in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arise — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, fond of secluded beds and seats, sole worthy recipients of offerings. At that time, a certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stood before that wrestler. Then, seeing that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> with his tranquil deportment, great faith arose in the wrestler. Disregarding his own distress, he offered the cake to the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. To inspire joy in him, [the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>], like a king of geese with wings outspread, rose up into the sky and began to display various miraculous feats. Then the wrestler, seeing that supremely wondrous miracle that captivates gods and men, fell at his feet like a tree cut at the root and began to make an aspiration: 'Since a man of fulfilled vows, a worthy recipient of offerings, has been served by me with a cake — by this root of merit, this generation of the thought [of awakening], and this relinquishment of the gift, wherever I may be born, may I be of noble family, and may I obtain such <s>dharmas</s> (spiritual attainments), and may I please a teacher even more distinguished than this one, and never displease him.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena koṭṭamallakaḥ, ayam asau bhadrikaḥ | yat tena pratyekabuddhaḥ pūlikayā pratipāditaḥ, tasya karmaṇo vipākenāḍhye śākye pratyāgataḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajito babhūva | tatrānena daśa varṣasahasrāṇi brahmacaryāvāsaḥ pratipālitaḥ | tenedānīm ārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the wrestler — he is this <s>Bhadrika</s>. Because he served a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> with a cake, by the ripening of that deed he was born in a wealthy <s>Śākya</s> family. Furthermore, he went forth under the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There he maintained the life of celibacy for ten thousand years. By that, he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, entirely bright; for those mixed, mixed. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only in entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 227]

children.text: AVŚ_90 rāṣṭrapālaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_90: <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ sthūlakoṣṭham upaniśritya viharati sthūlakoṣṭhakīye vanaṣaṇḍe | tena khalu samayena sthūlakoṣṭhake kauravyo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam akhilam akaṇṭakam* | ekaputram iva rājyaṃ pālayati | tasya bhrātṛputro rāṣṭrapālo nāmnā abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | tasya vinayakālam avekṣya bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛtaḥ sthūlakoṣṭhakaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ | dadarśa rāṣṭrapālo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cāsya bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasannam* | sa prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya pravrajyāṃ yācate | tatas taṃ bhagavān āha: vatsa anujñāto 'si mātāpitṛbhyām iti? rāṣṭrapālaḥ kathayati: no bhadanteti | bhagavān āha: na hi vatsa tathāgatā vā tathāgataśrāvakā vā anujñātaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ pravrājayanti, upasaṃpādayanti ceti ||
