children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Sthūlakoṣṭha</s>, in the <s>Sthūlakoṣṭhakīya</s> forest grove. At that time, in <s>Sthūlakoṣṭhaka</s>, a king named <s>Kauravya</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo, whole and free from thorns. He guarded the kingdom as though it were his only son. He had a nephew named <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, who was handsome, good-looking, pleasing, and endowed with all major and minor limbs. Perceiving that the time for his spiritual training had come, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, surrounded by the company of monks and preceded by the monastic community, entered <s>Sthūlakoṣṭhaka</s> for alms. <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, his mind became serene in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Filled with faith, he fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and requested ordination. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to him: 'Child, have you been given permission by your parents?' <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> replied: 'No, Venerable Sir.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Indeed, child, neither <s>Tathāgatas</s> nor disciples of <s>Tathāgatas</s> ordain or give full ordination to one who has not received permission from his parents.'

children.text: tato rāṣṭrapālo mātāpitroḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya buddhasya varṇaṃ bhāṣate: dṛṣṭo mayā bhagavāñ chākyamuniḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | sphītaṃ cakravartirājyam apahāya pravrajitaḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ cāntaḥpurasahasrāṇi | muṇḍaḥ saṃghāṭipravṛtto 'sminn eva sthūlakoṣṭhake piṇḍapātam aṭati | tad arhato yuvāṃ mām anujñātum*: yad ahaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ pravrajitam anupravrajeyam iti | tato 'sya mātāpitarau nānujānītaḥ | tatas tenaiko bhaktacchedaḥ kṛtaḥ | dvau trayo vā yāvac chaḍ bhaktacchedāḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> went to his parents' presence. Having approached, he spoke in praise of the <s>Buddha</s>: 'I have seen the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. He has renounced a prosperous universal kingdom and sixty thousand women of the inner palace. With shaven head and clad in patchwork robes, he walks for alms right here in <s>Sthūlakoṣṭhaka</s>. You ought to grant me permission, so that I may go forth following that <s>Bhagavān</s> who has renounced the world.' But his parents did not give permission. Then he undertook one meal-fast; two, three — up to six meal-fasts.

children.text: atha rāṣṭrapālasya mātāpitarau yena rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputras tenopasaṃkrāntau | upasaṃkramya rāṣṭrapālaṃ gṛhapatiputram idam avocatām*: yat khalu tāta rāṣṭrapāla jānīyāḥ: tvaṃ hi sukumāraḥ sukhaiṣī | na tvaṃ jānako duḥkhasya | duṣkaraṃ brahmacaryam*, duṣkaraṃ prāvivekyam*, durabhiramam ekatvam*, durabhisaṃbodhāny araṇyavanaprasthāni, prāntāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvastum* | ihaiva tvaṃ tāta rāṣṭrapāla niṣadya kāmāṃś ca paribhuṅkṣva, dānāni ca dehi, puṇyāni ca kuru | evam ukte rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputras tūṣṇīm* ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>'s parents approached their son, the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. Having approached, they said this to the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: 'You should know this, dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: you are delicate and comfort-seeking. You have no acquaintance with suffering. The holy life is hard to practice, solitude is hard to practice, being alone is hard to enjoy, forest wildernesses are hard to comprehend, and remote lodgings are hard to endure. Stay right here, dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, and enjoy sensual pleasures, give gifts, and make merit.' When this was said, the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> remained silent.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 228]

children.text: atha rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya mātāpitarau jñātīn udyojayataḥ: aṅga tāvaj jñātayaḥ tātaṃ rāṣṭrapālam utthāpayata | atha rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya jñātayo yena rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputras tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya rāṣṭrapālaṃ gṛhapatiputram evam avocan: yat khalu tāta rāṣṭrapāla jānīyāḥ: tvaṃ hi sukumāraḥ sukhaiṣī | na tvaṃ jānako duḥkhasya | duṣkaraṃ brahmacaryam, duṣkaraṃ prāvivekyaṃ, durabhiramam ekatvam, durabhisaṃbodhāny araṇyavanaprasthāni, prāntāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvastum* | ihaiva tvaṃ tāta rāṣṭrapāla niṣadya kāmāṃś ca paribhuṅkṣva, dānāni ca dehi, puṇyāni ca kuru | evam ukte rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputras tūṣṇīm* ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>'s parents urged his relatives: 'Come now, relatives, raise up our dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>!' Then the relatives of the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> approached him. Having approached, they said this to the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: 'You should know this, dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: you are delicate and comfort-seeking. You have no acquaintance with suffering. The holy life is hard to practice, solitude is hard to practice, being alone is hard to enjoy, forest wildernesses are hard to comprehend, and remote lodgings are hard to endure. Stay right here, dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, and enjoy sensual pleasures, give gifts, and make merit.' When this was said, the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> remained silent.

children.text: atha rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya mātāpitarau rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya vayasyakān udyojayataḥ: aṅga tāvat kumārāḥ, tātaṃ rāṣṭrapālam utthāpayata | atha rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya vayasyakā yena rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputras tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya rāṣṭrapālaṃ gṛhapatiputram idam avocan: yat khalu saumya rāṣṭrapāla jānīyāḥ: tvaṃ hi sukumāraḥ sukhaiṣī | na tvaṃ jānako duḥkhasya | duṣkaraṃ brahmacaryam, duṣkaraṃ prāvivekyaṃ, durabhiramam ekatvam, durabhisaṃbodhāny araṇyavanaprasthāni, prāntāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvastum* | ihaiva tvaṃ saumya rāṣṭrapāla niṣadya kāmāṃś ca paribhuṅkṣva, dānāni ca dehi, puṇyāni ca kuru | evam ukte rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputras tūṣṇīm* ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>'s parents urged his companions: 'Come now, young men, raise up our dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>!' Then the companions of the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> approached him. Having approached, they said this to the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: 'You should know this, dear friend <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: you are delicate and comfort-seeking. You have no acquaintance with suffering. The holy life is hard to practice, solitude is hard to practice, being alone is hard to enjoy, forest wildernesses are hard to comprehend, and remote lodgings are hard to endure. Stay right here, dear friend <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, and enjoy sensual pleasures, give gifts, and make merit.' When this was said, the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> remained silent.

children.text: atha rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya vayasyakā yena rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya mātāpitarau tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya rāṣṭrapālasya gṛhapatiputrasya mātāpitarāv idam avocan*: amba tāta, anujānītaṃ saumya rāṣṭrapālaṃ pravrajituṃ samyag eva śraddhayā agarād anagārikām*, kiṃ mṛtena kariṣyatha? sacet tātaḥ pravrajyāyām abhiraṃsyate, jīvantam enaṃ drakṣyadhve | sacen nābhiramate, kā anyā putrasya gatir anyatra mātāpitarāv eva | evam āvāṃ kumārakāḥ tātaṃ rāṣṭrapālam anujānīyāvaḥ | sacet pravrajyopadarśiṣya{ty ātmānam*} ||
children.translated_text: Then the companions of the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> approached his parents. Having approached, they said this to <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>'s parents: 'Mother, father — permit dear friend <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> to go forth from the household into homelessness with true faith. What will you do with him dead? If he delights in the renunciant life, you will see him alive. If he does not delight in it, what other refuge does a son have besides his parents? Thus we, young men, urge you to give dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> permission. If going forth proves unsatisfactory, he will show himself [to you again].'

children.text: atha rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputro 'nupūrveṇa kāyasya sthāmaṃ ca balaṃ ca saṃjanayya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt* | ekānte sthito rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputro bhagavantam idam avocat*: anujñāto 'smi bhagavan mātāpitṛbhyām* | labheyāhaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam* | careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam* | labdhavān rāṣṭrapālo gṛhapatiputraḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam* | sa evaṃ pravrajitaḥ sann idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo
children.translated_text: Then the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, having gradually restored the strength and vigor of his body, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached and bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I have been given permission by my parents, <s>Bhagavān</s>. May I obtain ordination, full ordination, and monkhood in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May I practice the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.' The householder's boy <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> obtained ordination, full ordination, and monkhood in the well-taught <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Having thus gone forth, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 229]

children.text: vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāṃ {āraṇyakānāṃ }yaduta rāṣṭrapālo bhiksur iti ||
children.translated_text: the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'This one, monks, is foremost among my monk-disciples who are forest-dwellers — namely, the monk <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta rāṣṭrapālena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenāḍhye rājakule pratyājata iti | abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: rāṣṭrapālenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | rāṣṭrapālena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_90.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_90.1 //

The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> perform that he was born in a wealthy royal family, handsome, good-looking, and pleasing, and having gone forth, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> himself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani videharājaḥ saparivāraḥ paracakravitrāsito 'ṭavīm anuprāptaḥ | sa madhyāhne tīkṣṇasūryaraśmiparitāpitaḥ sabalaugha itaś cāmutaś ca paribhramati, mārgaṃ ca nāsādayati | asati ca buddhānām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya | yāvad anyataraḥ pratyekabuddhas tasmin kāntāramārge prativasati | tena kāruṇyam utpādya tasya videharājasya mārgo vyapadiṣṭaḥ, pānīyahradaś ca darśitaḥ, yena sa rājā iṣṭena jīvitenācchāditaḥ | tato rājñā prasādajātena svanagaram ānīya traimāsyaṃ sarvopakaraṇair upasthitaḥ | parinirvṛtasya cāsya śarīrastūpaṃ kārayāmāsa | praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtavān: aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ labhī syām*, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ ca śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, a king of <s>Videha</s> together with his retinue, terrified by an enemy army, reached a wilderness. At midday, scorched by the fierce rays of the sun, he and his troops wandered here and there but could not find a path. Now, in the absence of a <s>Buddha</s>'s arising, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) appear in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, fond of remote lodgings and meals, worthy of individual offerings to the world. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> was dwelling on that wilderness path. Out of compassion, he pointed out the road to that king of <s>Videha</s> and showed him a pool of water, by which the king was sheltered with his dear life. Then the king, filled with faith, brought him to his own city and attended upon him with all requisites for three months. When the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, the king had a <s>stūpa</s> built over his bodily relics. And he made this aspiration: "May I too become one who attains such virtues, and may I please a teacher even more distinguished, and never displease him."'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena rājā babhūva, ayaṃ sa rāṣṭrapālaḥ | aparāṇy api rāṣṭrapālena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ kṛkī rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati | tasya kanīyān putra ṛṣipatanaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king — he is this <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. Furthermore, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> performed and accumulated other deeds as well. In this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of <s>Devas</s> and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. At that time, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Kṛkin</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. A righteous king, a <s>Dharmarāja</s>, he ruled the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>. His younger son went to <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 230]

children.text:
cāsya bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasannam* | prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tato 'sya bhagavatā kāśyapena dharmo deśitaḥ | tena prasādajātena bhagavān kāśyapaḥ saparivāra upasthitaḥ | śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni | parinirvṛtasya ca stūpe kanīyāñ chatram āropitavān* |
  kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau rājaputraḥ, ayam evāsau rāṣṭrapālas tena kālena tena samayena | aparāṇy api rāṣṭrapālena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ mahānagaryām anyatamo mūliko brāhmaṇaḥ | sa mūlānām arthe 'nyatamaṃ parvatam abhirūḍhaḥ | tena tatra paryaṭatā vanānte glānaḥ pratyekabuddho dṛṣṭaḥ | tatas tena prasādajātena tasyopasthānaṃ kṛtam* | yadā glānyād vyutthitaḥ, tadā piṇḍakena pratipādya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ {guṇānāṃ} labhī syām*, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text:
and his mind became filled with faith in the presence of the Blessed One. With faith arisen, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. With faith arisen, he attended upon the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> together with his retinue. He took the refuges and the precepts. And he placed a small parasol upon the <s>stūpa</s> of the deceased [<s>Buddha</s>].
What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the prince — he is this very <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. And <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> performed and accumulated still other deeds. In former times, monks, in a past age, in the great city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain herb-gatherer <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. He ascended a certain mountain in search of herbs. While wandering there, at the edge of a forest he saw a sick <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Then, with faith arisen, he attended upon him. When [the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>] had recovered from his illness, [the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] offered him alms-food and made this aspiration: 'May I too become a recipient of such virtues, and may I please a teacher even more distinguished than this one, and never displease him.'

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena mūliko brāhmaṇaḥ, ayam evāsau rāṣṭrapālaḥ | tasya karmaṇo vipākena saṃsāre na kadācid duḥkham anubhūtavān* | idānīm apy āḍhye rājakule pratyājāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ | tenaiva hetunārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the herb-gatherer <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — he is this very <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, he never experienced suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Even now he has been reborn in a wealthy royal family, handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. By that very cause he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 231]

children.text: daśamo vargaḥ |
children.translated_text: The Tenth Section.

children.text: tasyoddānam*:
children.translated_text: Its summary verse:

children.text: subhūtiḥ sthaviraś cāpi hasta lekuñcikas tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> and the Elder, <s>Hasta</s> and <s>Lekuñcika</s> likewise,

children.text: saṃsāro guptikaś cāpi virūpo gaṅgikena ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> and <s>Guptika</s>, <s>Virūpa</s> and <s>Gaṅgika</s>,

children.text: dīrghanakhaḥ saṃgītiś ca vargo bhavati samudditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dīrghanakha</s> and <s>Saṃgīti</s> — thus the section is proclaimed.

children.text: AVŚ_91 subhūtiḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_91: <s>Subhūti</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | yadā bhagavatā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhya śrāvakā niyuktās teṣu janapadeṣu vineyajanānugrahārtham*, tadā ye 'dhyāyinas te sumerupariṣaṇḍāyāṃ dhyānaparā sthitāḥ | yāvat suparṇipakṣirājena mahāsamudrān nāgapotalaka uddhṛtaḥ | sa taṃ sumerupariṣaṇḍāyām āropya bhakṣayitum ārabdhaḥ | tato nāgapotalako jīvitād vyaparopyamāṇo mahāśrāvakāṇām antike cittam abhiprasādya kālagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. When the Blessed One, having attained the unsurpassed perfect awakening, had assigned his disciples to those lands for the benefit of beings to be trained, the meditators were dwelling absorbed in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) on the terraces of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>. Meanwhile, a young <s>Nāga</s> was lifted from the great ocean by the king of the <s>Suparṇi</s> birds. He carried it up to the terraces of Mount <s>Sumeru</s> and began to devour it. Then the young <s>Nāga</s>, as it was being deprived of its life, generated faith in the presence of the great disciples and died.

children.text: sa kālaṃ kṛtvā śrāvastyāṃ bhūtir nāma brāhmaṇaḥ, tasyāgramahiṣyāḥ kukṣāv upapannaḥ | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya pitā bhūtiḥ, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya subhūtir iti nāmeti | subhūtir dāraka unnīto vardhito mahān samvṛttaḥ | sa pūrveṇa hetubalādhānena atīva roṣaṇaḥ krodhaparyavasthānabahulo mātāpitṛbhyām ātharvaṇād vinivartya ṛṣiṣu pravrājitaḥ | sa ca tatra dhyānaparaḥ saṃyato 'nyatarad vanaṣaṇḍam upaniśritya viharati | tatra ca vanaṣaṇḍe devatā prativasati dṛṣṭasatyā | tasyāḥ kāruṇyam utpannam*: ayaṃ kulaputraḥ krodhaparyavasthānabahalo viśeṣaṃ nādhigacchati | yanv aham enaṃ bhagavaddarśane niyojayeyam iti | tatas tayā devatayā subhūteḥ purastād buddhasya varṇo bhāṣito dharmasya ca saṃghasya ca | tataḥ subhūter bhagavaddarśanahetor abhilāṣa utpannaḥ | tato devatayā ṛddhyanubhāvād (Speyer: ṛddhyānubhāvād) bhagavatsakāśam upanītaḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cāsya yo 'bhūt satveṣv
children.translated_text: Having died, it was reborn in <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the womb of the chief queen of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Bhūti</s>. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be established: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The relatives said: 'Since his father is <s>Bhūti</s>, let the boy's name be <s>Subhūti</s>.' The boy <s>Subhūti</s> was raised, nourished, and grew up. By the force of his previous causal connections, he was extremely irascible, filled with the affliction of anger. His parents, having turned him away from the <s>Ātharvanic</s> [practices], had him go forth among the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages). There, devoted to meditation, restrained, he dwelt near a certain forest grove. And in that forest grove there dwelt a goddess who had seen the truths. Compassion arose in her: 'This young man of good family, filled with the affliction of anger, is not attaining distinction. Let me direct him to an audience with the Blessed One.' Then that goddess praised the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> in the presence of <s>Subhūti</s>. Thereupon a longing to see the Blessed One arose in <s>Subhūti</s>. Then the goddess, by the power of her supernatural ability, brought him into the presence of the Blessed One. And he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. And the moment he saw him, whatever
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 232]

children.text: āghātaḥ, sa prativigataḥ | tataḥ prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā subhūtinā kulaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena maitrībhāvanayā cittaṃ damayitvā sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: hatred he had held toward beings — that departed. Then, with faith arisen, he worshipped the Blessed One's feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The Blessed One, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and character, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths that, having heard it, the young man <s>Subhūti</s>, with the thunderbolt of knowledge, shattered the mountain of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), rising with twenty peaks, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truths, he went forth in the Blessed One's teaching. Through his diligent effort, striving and exerting himself, having tamed his mind through the cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: tatra āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ: kuto 'haṃ cyutaḥ, kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti | paśyati: pañca jātiśatāni nāgebhyaś cyuto nāgeṣv evopapannaḥ | tasya buddhir utpannā: mayā atīva evaṃvidho dveṣapratyayopasaṃbhāraḥ kṛtaḥ, yenāhaṃ pañca janmaśatāni nāgeṣūpapannaḥ | tenaiva hetunā mahadvyasanam anubhūtavān* | idānīṃ punas tathā kariṣyāmi yat pareṣām antike dveṣopasaṃbhāro notpatsyate | yena samanvāgataḥ kāyasya bhedād apāyaṃ durgatiṃ vinipātaṃ narakeṣūpapadyate | so 'raṇyapratipadaṃ samādāya vartate | yadā saṃghe vā grāme vā deśe vā janapade vā bhikṣāhetor vihartukāmo bhavati, tadā pūrvataraṃ gocaram avalokayati: mā māṃ kaścit kāraṇena dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ pradūṣayiṣyati, antataḥ kuntapipīlakā apīti | sa tānīryāpathena praśritenābhiramayati | tena teṣāṃ satvānāṃ cittaprasādo bhavati | evaṃvidhāṃ so 'rhatvaprāpto 'py apatrapām anubhavatīti | tata āyuṣmataḥ subhūter buddhir utpannā: yanv aham idānīṃ mahājanānugrahārthaṃ kuryām iti | tatas tena ṛddhyā pañca suparṇiśatāni nirmitāni, yāni dṛṣṭvā nāgā bhītās trastā saṃvignā itaś cāmutaś ca saṃbhrāntāḥ | tataḥ subhūtinā ṛddhibalena punaḥ paritrātāḥ | tatas teṣāṃ prasannacittānāṃ maitrī vyapadiṣṭā | punar api mahāntaṃ nāgarūpam abhinirmāya pañca garuḍaśatāny abhidrutāni | teṣām api bhītānāṃ maitrī vyapadiṣṭā | evaṃ tena nāgānāṃ garuḍānāṃ ca pañca kulaśatāni vinītāni | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇām araṇāvihāriṇāṃ yaduta subhūtiḥ kulaputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> began to reflect: 'From where did I pass away, and where was I reborn, and by what <s>karma</s>?' He saw that for five hundred births he had passed away from among <s>Nāgas</s> and been reborn among <s>Nāgas</s> again. This thought arose in him: 'I have accumulated an exceedingly great store of causal conditions rooted in hatred, on account of which I was reborn among <s>Nāgas</s> for five hundred lifetimes. By that very cause I experienced great misfortune. Now I shall act in such a way that no store of hatred will arise toward others — for one endowed with [hatred], upon the dissolution of the body, is reborn in a woeful state, an evil destiny, a lower realm, in hell.' He undertook the practice of the forest-dweller (<s>āraṇyapratipada</s>). Whenever he wished to dwell in the <s>Saṃgha</s>, or in a village, or in a district, or in a land, for the sake of alms, he would first survey his territory: 'Let no one, having seen me for any reason, generate an impure thought — not even a beetle or an ant.' He would set them at ease with his calm and gentle deportment. And so a feeling of serene faith arose in those beings toward him. Even though he had attained <s>Arhatship</s>, he still maintained such scrupulousness. Then a thought arose in the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Let me now act for the benefit of the great multitude of beings.' Then, by his supernatural power, he conjured five hundred <s>Suparṇi</s> birds. Seeing them, the <s>Nāgas</s> became frightened, terrified, alarmed, and scattered in all directions. Then <s>Subhūti</s>, by his supernatural power, protected them again. Then, when their minds were serene, he taught them <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). Again, having conjured a great <s>Nāga</s> form, he charged at five hundred <s>Garuḍas</s>. When they too became frightened, he taught them <s>maitrī</s>. In this way he trained five hundred clans of <s>Nāgas</s> and <s>Garuḍas</s>. Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'This one, monks, is foremost among my monk-disciples who dwell in the practice free from conflict (<s>araṇāvihārin</s>) — namely, the young man <s>Subhūti</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta subhūtinā karmāṇi kṛtāni yenāraṇāvihāriṇām agro nirdiṣṭa iti | bhagavān āha: subhūtinaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | subhūtinā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau,
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Subhūti</s> perform that he was designated foremost among those dwelling in the practice free from conflict?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Subhūti</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Subhūti</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 233]

children.text: na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_91.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_91.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tatrāyaṃ pravrajito babhūva | tatrānena dānapradānāni dattāni, daśavarṣashasrāṇi brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ, praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam*: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena uttaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛtaḥ: bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti, tasyāhaṃ śāsane pravrajya araṇāvihāriṇām agraḥ syām iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. There, this one [<s>Subhūti</s>] had gone forth. There he gave gifts, and for ten thousand years he maintained the life of celibacy. And he made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, this generation of the aspiration for awakening, and this relinquishment of gifts — under the <s>Buddha</s> whom the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s> prophesied as the young man named <s>Uttara</s>: "You, young man, in the age when the lifespan of people is a hundred years, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>" — having gone forth in his teaching, may I become foremost among those dwelling in the practice free from conflict.'

children.text: # # # kāni karmāṇi kṛtāni yena nāgeṣūpapannaḥ? aprahīṇatvāt kleśānām udbhrāntatvād indriyāṇām aparyantīkṛtatvāt karmapathānāṃ śaikṣāśaikṣabhikṣuṣu cittaṃ pradūṣya āśīviṣavādena samudācaritāḥ, tena nāgeṣūpapannaḥ | yat tena dānapradānāni dattāni, brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*, araṇāvihāriṇāṃ cāgro nirdiṣṭaḥ | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: [...] what deeds were performed that he was reborn among the <s>nāgas</s> (serpent beings)? Because the <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) had not been abandoned, because the senses were agitated, and because the paths of action had not been fully restrained, having corrupted his mind toward trainee and non-trainee monks and having addressed them with the speech of a venomous serpent, by that he was reborn among the <s>nāgas</s>. Because he had given charitable gifts and maintained the life of celibacy, he has now directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship) and has been declared foremost among those who dwell in <s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict). Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, entirely bright; for those mixed, mixed. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only in entirely bright deeds. Thus should you train, monks.

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_92 sthaviraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 92: <s>Sthavira</s> (The Elder). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā, na prasūyate | yāvad bhūyas tayaiva sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ putro jātaḥ | sa prathamagarbho yathāvasthitaḥ eva mātur udare | yāvat tasyāḥ kramaśo daśa
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the monastic community, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s> in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove) at <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. A certain merchant was wealthy, of great riches and great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal status. He sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with her. As he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant but did not give birth. He continued to sport, enjoy, and amuse himself with her. A son was born to him. But the first embryo remained as it was in the mother's womb. In due course, ten
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 234]

children.text: putrā jātāḥ | sa prathamagarbho mātur udarastha eva | yāvad asau gṛhapatipatnī glānyapatitā | sā upasthīyate mūlagaṇḍapatrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyena | na cāsau vyādhir upaśamaṃ gacchati | yadā cāsyā maraṇāntikī vedanā prādurbhūtā nacireṇa kālaṃ kariṣyatīti, tadā tayā svāmī uktaḥ: yat khalv āryaputra jānīyāḥ mamātra prathamagarbho 'vatiṣṭhate | yadāhaṃ mṛtā bhavāmi, tadā dakṣiṇapārśvaṃ śastreṇa ghātayitvā tataḥ prathamasthitaṃ dārakam uddharethāḥ | ity uktvā:
children.translated_text: sons were born to her. That first embryo remained in the mother's womb. Eventually, the householder's wife fell ill. She was treated with medicines of roots, bulbs, leaves, flowers, and fruits. But the illness did not subside. When death-dealing pain arose in her and she was about to die before long, she said to her husband: "Noble husband, know that

children.text: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ |
children.translated_text: all accumulations end in exhaustion, all risings end in falling,

children.text: saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam* || AVŚ_92.1 ||
children.translated_text: all unions end in separation, and life ends in death. (AVŚ 92.1)

children.text: ity uktvā kāladharmeṇa saṃyuktā ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, she passed away according to the law of death.

children.text: tasyāḥ kālagatāyā nīlapītalohitāvadātair vastraiḥ śibikām (Speyer: śivikām) alaṃkṛtya śītavanaṃ śmaśānaṃ nītvā jīvako (Speyer: jīviko) vaidyarāja āhūtaḥ | eṣa ca śabdo rājagṛhe nagare samantato visṛtaḥ: evam amukastriyā iyanti varṣāṇi garbhaḥ sthitaḥ, tasyāś cānye daśa putrā jātāḥ, na cāsau prathamataram avasthito garbho nirgataḥ | adya jīvako vaidyarājaḥ śastreṇa mṛtāyā udaraṃ ghātayitvā taṃ prathamasthitaṃ dārakam uddhariṣyatīti | taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā kutūhalād bahūni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi śītavanaśmaśāne saṃnipatitāni | pūraṇaprabhṛtayaś ca ṣaṭ* śāstṛpratijñāḥ | tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate: gaccha ānanda, bhikṣūṇāṃ kathaya, bhagavān śmaśānacārikāṃ gantukāmaḥ, yo 'dbhutāni draṣṭukāmaḥ, sa āgacchatv iti | yāvad bhagavān ājñātakauṇḍinyabāṣpamahānāmāniruddhaśāriputramaudgalyāyanakāśyapānandarevataprabhṛtibhir mahāśrāvakaiḥ parivṛtaḥ śītavanaśmaśānaṃ gataḥ | janakāyena ca bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā vivaraṃ kṛtam* | tatra jīvakena tasyāḥ striyā dakṣiṇaḥ kukṣiḥ pāṭitaḥ | tataḥ svayam eva nirgato valipalitacitāṅgaḥ parijīrṇaśarīrāvayavaḥ: pariṇatendriyaḥ kṛśo 'lpasthāmaḥ | nirgatamātraś ca taṃ janakāyam avalokya vācaṃ niścārayati sma: mā bhavanto guruṣu gurusthānīyeṣu mātāpitṛṣv ācāryopādhyāyeṣu kharāṃ vācaṃ niścārayata | mā haivaṃvidhām avasthām anubhaviṣyatha, yad aham āmāśayapakvāśayayor madhye ṣaṣṭi varṣāṇy uṣitaḥ | ity uktvā tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: tṛpyata bhikṣavaḥ sarvabhavopapattibhyaḥ, tṛpyata sarvabhavopapattyupakaraṇebhyaḥ, yatra nāma caramabhavikasya satvasyeyam avasthā | tatra bhagavāṃs taṃ dārakam āmantrayate: sthavirako 'si dārakaḥ? sthavirako 'haṃ bhagavan* | sthavirako 'si dāraka? sthavirako 'smi sugata | sthaviraka iti saṃjñā jātā | tato bhagavatā tadadhiṣṭhānā tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā saṃvignair bahubhiḥ satvaśatair mahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After her death, having adorned a bier with blue, yellow, red, and white cloths, they carried her to the <s>Śītavana</s> (Cool Grove) cremation ground. <s>Jīvaka</s>, the king of physicians, was summoned. This news spread throughout the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> on all sides: "Such-and-such a woman carried an embryo for so many years; she had ten other sons born, yet that first embryo was not born."

children.text: sa ca daśavarṣāṇi gṛhāgāram adhyāsya saptativarṣo bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | gṛdhrakūṭe parvate pañcaviṃśatyā bhikṣubhiḥ sārdhaṃ varṣā upagataḥ | tatra saṃghasthavireṇa kriyākāraṃ kāritaḥ: na kenacit pṛthagjanena pravārayitavyam iti | trayāṇāṃ māsānām atyayāc caturviṃśatyā bhikṣubhir arhatvaṃ prāptam* | sthavira ekaḥ pṛthagjana eva | tataḥ saṃghasthavireṇa pravāraṇāyāṃ vartamānāyāṃ subahu paribhāṣya gaṇamadhyān niṣkāsitaḥ | sa śastram ādāya kuṭiṃ praviśya rudan bahuvidhaṃ paridevate | āha ca:
children.translated_text: He lived as a householder for ten years and then, at seventy years of age, went forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He spent the rainy season retreat on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain together with twenty-five monks. There the senior monk of the community imposed a rule: "No ordinary person (<s>pṛthagajana</s>) shall perform the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony)." After the passage of three months, twenty-four monks attained <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship),
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 235]

children.text: ādīptaṃ kānanaṃ sarvaṃ parvatā pi palīkṛtā |
children.translated_text: "The entire forest is ablaze, even the mountains are scorched,

children.text: athedaṃ pāpakaṃ cittam adyāpi na vimucyate || AVŚ_92.2 ||
children.translated_text: yet this wicked mind is still not liberated even now. (AVŚ 92.2)

children.text: śāntā girinadīśabdāḥ parīttasalilodakāḥ |

children.translated_text: yet this wicked mind is still not liberated even now. (AVŚ 92.3)

children.text: ete hy aṇḍajāḥ pakṣiṇo viratā mandaghoṣakāḥ |

children.translated_text: yet this wicked mind is still not liberated even now. (AVŚ 92.4)

śastram ārādhayiṣyāmi ko nv artho jīvitena me |
  kathaṃ pṛthagjano bhūtvā śāstāram upasaṃkrame || AVŚ_92.6 || iti
children.translated_text: I shall take up the blade — what use is life to me? How can I, remaining an ordinary person, approach the Teacher? (AVŚ 92.6)

children.text: atrāntare nāsti kiṃcid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātam* | dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttānām ekārakṣāṇām śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ, ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ | kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyam*, kasyānavaropitāni kuśalamulāny avaropayeyam *{kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyam}*, kasya paripakvāni vimocayeyam* | āha ca:
children.translated_text: In this regard, there is nothing unknown, unseen, unascertained, or unrecognized by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. For it is the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, who are greatly compassionate, engaged in benefiting the world, sole protectors, dwelling in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), skilled in the three bases of taming, who have crossed the four floods, firmly established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, who have abandoned the five limbs, who have transcended the five destinies, endowed with six factors, who have perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), adorned with the flowers of the seven factors of awakening, guides of the eightfold path, skilled in the nine successive meditative attainments, whose fame fills the ten directions — three times in the night and three times in the day, with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye they survey the world.

children.text: apy evātikramed velāṃ sāgaro makarālayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The ocean, abode of sea-monsters, might transgress its shore,

children.text: na tu vaineyavatsānāṃ buddho velām atikramet || AVŚ_92.7 ||
children.translated_text: but the <s>Buddha</s> would never transgress the time for those who are to be guided, like calves to be tended. (AVŚ 92.7)

children.text: yāvad bhagavatā samanvāhṛtyā copasaṃkramya tathāvidhā dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā sthavirakeṇa idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having reflected and approached, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that, upon hearing it, the Elder, having understood this five-limbed wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> to be unstable, and having overcome all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and disintegrating, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship). He became an <s>arhat</s>, free from passion toward the three realms,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 236]

children.text: tataḥ sthaviro 'rhatvaprāptaḥ samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ: mamāpi kaścid vineya iti | paśyati pañcamātrāṇi vaṇikśatāni kālikāvātavitrāsitāni apāyād vyasanābhimukhāni, mayā tasmād bhayāt paritrātavyānīti | tena mama vineyā bhaviṣyantīti | tataḥ sthavireṇa ṛddhyā gatvā tasmād bhayāt paritrātāḥ | tataḥ prasādajātāḥ sarva eva pravrajitāḥ, manasikāraś caiṣa dattaḥ | taiḥ sarvair eva yujyamānair ghaṭamānair vyāyacchamānaiḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | teṣāṃ ca guṇeṣu na kaścit pratyakṣaḥ | ṣaḍvargikā avadhyāyituṃ pravṛttāḥ: mahallena bhūtvā pañca sārdhavihāriṇāṃ (Speyer: sārdhaṃvihāriṇāṃ) śatāni upasthāpitāni | ete 'py evam eva vinītā bhaviṣyantīti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Elder, having attained <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship), began to reflect: "Do I also have someone to be guided?" He saw about five hundred merchants, terrified by a black storm, facing disaster and heading toward misfortune: "They should be rescued from that danger by me; they will become those whom I am to guide." Then the Elder, traveling by supernatural power, rescued them from that danger. Then, having gained faith,

tata āyuṣmān ānandaḥ sabrahmacārivatsalaḥ parānugrahapravṛtta āyuṣmantaṃ sthavirakanāmān udbhāvayitukāmo yenāyuṣmān sthaviranāmā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya āyuṣmatā sthavireṇa sthaviranāmnā bhikṣuṇā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ | ekānte niṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān ānandaḥ sthaviraṃ sthavirakanāman idam avocat*: pṛcchema vayam āyuṣmantaṃ sthaviraṃ sthavirakanāmānaṃ kaṃcid eva pradeśam*, saced avakāśaṃ kuryāḥ praśnasya vyākaraṇāya | āyuṣmann ānanda, śrutvā te vedayiṣye | araṇyagatenāyuṣman sthavira bhikṣuṇā vṛkṣamūlagatena śūnyāgāragatena katame dharmā abhīkṣṇaṃ manasikartavyāḥ? āha: araṇyagatena āyuṣmann ānanda bhikṣuṇā vṛkṣamūlagatena śūnyāgāragatena dvau dharmāv abhīkṣṇaṃ manasikartavyau: śamathaś ca vipaśyanā ca | śamathaḥ (Speyer: śamatha) sthavira āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ kam arthaṃ pratyanubhavati? vipaśyanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā kam arthaṃ pratyanubhavati? śamatha āyuṣmann ānanda āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛto vipaśyanām āgamya vimucyate | vipaśyanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā śamatham āgamya vimucyate | śamathavipaśyanāparibhāvitam āyuṣmann ānanda śrutavataḥ āryaśrāvakasya cittaṃ dhātuśo vimucyate | tatra sthavira katame dhātavaḥ? yaś cāyuṣmann ānanda prahāṇadhātuḥ, yaś ca virāgadhātuḥ, yaś ca nirodhadhātuḥ | kasya nu sthavira prahāṇāt prahāṇadhātur ity ucyate? kasya virāgād virāgadhātur ity ucyate? kasya nirodhān nirodhadhātur ity ucyate? sarvasaṃskārāṇām āyuṣmann ānanda prahāṇāt prahāṇadhātur ity ucyate | sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ virāgād virāgadhātur ity ucyate | sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhān nirodhadhātur ity ucyate |
  athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ sthavirasya sthavirakanāmno bhikṣor bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya yena pañca bhikṣuśatāni tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya pañca bhikṣuśatānīdam avocat*: araṇyagatenāyuṣmanto bhikṣuṇā vṛkṣamūlagatena śūnyāgāragatena katame dharmā abhīkṣṇaṃ manasikartavyāḥ? araṇyagatena āyuṣmann ānanda bhikṣuṇā vṛkṣamūlagatena śūnyāgāragatena dvau dharmāv abhīkṣṇaṃ manasikartavyau: śamathaś ca vipaśyanā ca | śamatha āyuṣmanta āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ kam arthaṃ pratyanubhavati? vipaśyanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā kam arthaṃ pratyanubhavati? śamatha āyuṣmann ānanda āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛto vipaśyanām āgamya vimucyate | vipaśyanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā śamatham āgamya vimucyate | śamathavipaśyanāparibhāvitam āyuṣmann ānanda śrutavataḥ
children.translated_text:
Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, affectionate toward his fellow practitioners of the holy life and intent on benefiting others, wishing to extol the venerable elder named <s>Sthaviraka</s>, approached the venerable monk named <s>Sthaviraka</s>. Having approached, he sat down to one side after exchanging with the venerable elder <s>Sthaviraka</s> various kinds of cordial and agreeable conversation face to face. Seated to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the elder named <s>Sthaviraka</s>: 'We would like to ask the venerable elder <s>Sthaviraka</s> about a certain matter, if you would grant the opportunity for answering the question.' 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having heard, I shall answer you.' 'Venerable elder, when a monk has gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, what <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) should be frequently attended to in mind?' He replied: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, when a monk has gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, two <s>dharmas</s> should be frequently attended to in mind: <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).' 'Elder, when <s>śamatha</s> is practiced, cultivated, and made much of, what purpose does it serve? When <s>vipaśyanā</s> is practiced, cultivated, and made much of, what purpose does it serve?' '<s>Śamatha</s>, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, when practiced, cultivated, and made much of, leads to liberation through <s>vipaśyanā</s>. <s>Vipaśyanā</s>, when practiced, cultivated, and made much of, leads to liberation through <s>śamatha</s>. The mind of a learned noble disciple, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, that is well-developed in <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, is liberated element by element.' 'Elder, what are those elements?' 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the element of abandonment, the element of dispassion, and the element of cessation.' 'Elder, through the abandonment of what is it called the element of abandonment? Through dispassion toward what is it called the element of dispassion? Through the cessation of what is it called the element of cessation?' 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, through the abandonment of all conditioned formations it is called the element of abandonment. Through dispassion toward all conditioned formations it is called the element of dispassion. Through the cessation of all conditioned formations it is called the element of cessation.'
Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having rejoiced at and approved the words of the monk elder <s>Sthaviraka</s>, approached the five hundred monks. Having approached, he said this to the five hundred monks: 'Venerable ones, when a monk has gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, what <s>dharmas</s> should be frequently attended to in mind?' 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, when a monk has gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, two <s>dharmas</s> should be frequently attended to in mind: <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>.' 'Venerable ones, when <s>śamatha</s> is practiced, cultivated, and made much of, what purpose does it serve? When <s>vipaśyanā</s> is practiced, cultivated, and made much of, what purpose does it serve?' '<s>Śamatha</s>, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, when practiced, cultivated, and made much of, leads to liberation through <s>vipaśyanā</s>. <s>Vipaśyanā</s>, when practiced, cultivated, and made much of, leads to liberation through <s>śamatha</s>. The mind of a learned noble disciple, venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, that is well-developed in <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 237]

Through dispassion toward all conditioned formations it is called the element of dispassion. Through the cessation of all conditioned formations it is called the element of cessation.'

children.text:
āyuṣmān ānandaḥ pañcānāṃ bhikṣuśatānāṃ bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte 'sthāt* | ekāntasthita āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat*: araṇyagatena bhadanta bhikṣuṇā vṛkṣamūlagatena śūnyāgāragatena katame dharmā abhīkṣṇaṃ manasikartavyāḥ? araṇyagatenānanda bhikṣuṇā vṛkṣamūlagatena śūnyāgāragatena dvau dharmāv abhīkṣṇaṃ manasikartavyau: śamathaś ca vipaśyanā ca | śamatho bhadanta āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛtaḥ kam arthaṃ pratyanubhavati? vipaśyanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā kam arthaṃ pratyanubhavati? śamatha ānanda āsevito bhāvito bahulīkṛto vipaśyanām āgamya vimucyate | vipaśyanā āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā śamatham āgamya vimucyate | śamathavipaśyanāparibhāvitānanda śrutavata āryaśrāvakasya cittaṃ dhātuśo vimucyate | tatra bhadanta katame dhātavaḥ? yaś cānanda prahāṇadhātuḥ, yaś ca virāgadhātuḥ, yaś ca nirodhadhātuḥ | kasya nu bhadanta prahāṇāt prahāṇadhātur ity ucyate? kasya virāgād virāgadhātur ity ucyate? kasya nirodhān nirodhadhātur ity ucyate? bhagavān āha: sarvasaṃskārāṇām ānanda prahāṇāt prahāṇadhātur ity ucyate | sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ virāgād virāgadhātur ity ucyate | sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhān nirodhadhātur ity ucyate | āścaryaṃ bhadanta, yāvac chāstuḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ ca arthenārthaḥ, padena padam*, vyañjanena vyañjanaṃ saṃsyandate sameti yadutāgrapadaiḥ | tat kasya hetoḥ? ihāhaṃ bhadanta yena sthaviraḥ sthavirakanāmā bhikṣus tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya sthaviraṃ sthavirakanāmānaṃ bhikṣum etam evārtham ebhiḥ padair ebhir vyañjanaiḥ praśnaṃ pṛṣṭavān* | tena mama eṣa evārtha ebhiḥ padair ebhir vyañjanaiḥ praśnaṃ pṛṣṭena vyākṛtaḥ, tadyathaitarhi bhagavatā | so 'ham āyuṣmataḥ sthavirasya sthaviranāmno bhikṣor bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya yena pañca bhikṣuśatāni tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya pañca bhikṣuśatāny etam evārtham ebhiḥ padair ebhir vyañjanaiḥ praśnaṃ pṛṣṭavān* | tair api mama eṣa evārtha ebhiḥ padair ebhir vyañjanaiḥ praśnaṃ pṛṣṭair vyākṛtaḥ, tadyathaitarhi bhagavatā | tad idaṃ
bhadanta āścaryaṃ yāvac chāstuḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ ca arthenārthaḥ, padena padam*, vyañjanena vyañjanaṃ saṃsyandate sameti yadutāgrapadaiḥ ||
children.translated_text:
The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having rejoiced at and approved the words of the five hundred monks, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, when a monk has gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, what <s>dharmas</s> should be frequently attended to in mind?' '<s>Ānanda</s>, when a monk has gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, two <s>dharmas</s> should be frequently attended to in mind: <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).' 'Venerable Sir, when <s>śamatha</s> is practiced, cultivated, and made much of, what purpose does it serve? When <s>vipaśyanā</s> is practiced, cultivated, and made much of, what purpose does it serve?' '<s>Śamatha</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, when practiced, cultivated, and made much of, leads to liberation through <s>vipaśyanā</s>. <s>Vipaśyanā</s>, when practiced, cultivated, and made much of, leads to liberation through <s>śamatha</s>. The mind of a learned noble disciple, <s>Ānanda</s>, that is well-developed in <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, is liberated element by element.' 'Venerable Sir, what are those elements?' '<s>Ānanda</s>, the element of abandonment, the element of dispassion, and the element of cessation.' 'Venerable Sir, through the abandonment of what is it called the element of abandonment? Through dispassion toward what is it called the element of dispassion? Through the cessation of what is it called the element of cessation?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Ānanda</s>, through the abandonment of all conditioned formations it is called the element of abandonment. Through dispassion toward all conditioned formations it is called the element of dispassion. Through the cessation of all conditioned formations it is called the element of cessation.' 'It is wonderful, Venerable Sir, how the meaning of the Teacher and that of the disciples corresponds — meaning with meaning, word with word, expression with expression — that is, with respect to the chief points. What is the reason for this? Here, Venerable Sir, I approached the venerable monk elder <s>Sthaviraka</s>. Having approached, I asked the venerable monk elder <s>Sthaviraka</s> this very question in these very words and expressions. He answered my question in these very words and expressions, just as the <s>Bhagavān</s> has now done. Then I, having rejoiced at and approved the words of the venerable monk elder <s>Sthaviraka</s>, approached the five hundred monks. Having approached, I asked the five hundred monks this very question in these very words and expressions. They too answered my question in these very words and expressions, just as the <s>Bhagavān</s> has now done. Therefore, Venerable Sir,
it is wonderful how the meaning of the Teacher and that of the disciples corresponds — meaning with meaning, word with word, expression with expression — that is, with respect to the chief points.'

children.text: kaṃ punas tvam ānanda sthavirakaṃ bhikṣuṃ saṃjānīyāḥ? sthavirako bhadanta bhikṣur arhan kṣīṇāśravaḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ kṛtakaraṇīyo 'pahṛtabhāro 'nuprāptasvakārthaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaḥ | tāny api bhikṣuśatāni sarvāṇy arhanti kṣīṇāsravāṇi kṛtakṛtyāni kṛtakaraṇīyāny apahṛtabhārāṇy anuprāptasvakārthaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittāni ||
children.translated_text: 'But whom, <s>Ānanda</s>, do you understand the monk <s>Sthaviraka</s> to be?' 'Venerable Sir, the monk <s>Sthaviraka</s> is an <s>Arhat</s> whose <s>āśravas</s> (taints) are destroyed, who has done what had to be done, who has accomplished the task, who has laid down the burden, who has attained his own goal, who has completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and whose mind is perfectly liberated through right knowledge. And those hundreds of monks too are all <s>Arhats</s> whose <s>āśravas</s> are destroyed, who have done what had to be done, who have accomplished the task, who have laid down the burden, who have attained their own goal, who have completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and whose minds are perfectly liberated through right knowledge.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 238]

children.text: yadā bhagavatā āyuṣmatānandena sthavirakas te ca bhikṣava udbhāvitāḥ prakāśitāś ca, tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta sthavirakeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni, yena ṣaṣṭi varṣāṇi mātuḥ kukṣāv uṣitaḥ, kāni karmāṇi kṛtāni yena dhandhaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ paramadhandhaḥ, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam*? bhagavān āha: sthavirakeṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | sthavirakeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> had thus extolled and made known <s>Sthaviraka</s> and those monks, the monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Sthaviraka</s> perform and accumulate, that he remained in his mother's womb for sixty years? What deeds did he perform that he became slow, exceedingly slow? And having gone forth, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Sthaviraka</s> himself, monks, who in previous births performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood before him like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass. <s>Sthaviraka</s> performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience their results? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_92.8 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_92.8 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | tatrānyataraḥ śreṣṭhīputraḥ sthavirasakāśe pravajitaḥ | sa ca sthaviro 'rhan, sa rāgaviprahīṇaḥ | yāvat tatra deśe parva pratyupasthitam* | tatas taruṇabhikṣuṇā sthavira utthāpyate: uttiṣṭha gocaragrāmaṃ gamiṣyāva iti | sthavira āha: vatsa adyāpi prag eva, gaccha tāvat kuśalapakṣaṃ pratijāgṛhīti | dvir api trir api taruṇabhikṣuṇā sthavira utthāpyate: uttiṣṭha gocaragrāmaṃ gamiṣyāva iti | dvir api trir api sthavira āha: vatsa, adyāpi prag eva, gaccha tāvat kuśalapakṣaṃ pratijāgṛhīti | tatas tena taruṇabhikṣuṇā āhāragṛddhreṇa (Speyer: āhāragṛdhreṇa) kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam* | # # # # # # || # # # {mā svapihi gṛhe ṣaṣṭi varṣasahasrāṇi}, tasya karmaṇo vipākena ṣaṣṭi varṣasahasrāṇi mātuḥ kukṣāv uṣitaḥ | yad abhūd dharmamātsaryaṃ tena duḥprajñaḥ, kṛcchreṇendriyāṇi paripācitāni | yad anena tatra paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ sthānāsthānakauśalaṃ ca kṛtam*, tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavo vāgduścaritaprahāṇāya vyāyantavyam* | ete doṣā na bhaviṣyanti, ye sthavirakasya pṛthagjanabhūtasya | eṣa eva guṇagaṇo bhaviṣyati yas tasyaivārhatvaṃ prāptasya | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. There, a certain merchant's son had gone forth under an elder. And that elder was an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion. Now at that time, a festival had arrived in that region. Then the young monk tried to rouse the elder: 'Get up, we shall go to the village for alms.' The elder said: 'Child, it is still very early; go first and attend to wholesome practices.' A second time and a third time the young monk tried to rouse the elder: 'Get up, we shall go to the village for alms.' A second and third time the elder said: 'Child, it is still very early; go first and attend to wholesome practices.' Then that young monk, greedy for food, uttered a harsh word: '... sleep in the house for sixty thousand years!' By the ripening of that deed, he remained in his mother's womb for sixty thousand years. Because he was stingy with the <s>Dharma</s>, he became dull-witted, and his faculties matured only with great difficulty. But because he studied, recited, and developed skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and skill in distinguishing what is possible and impossible — by that, having gone forth in my teaching, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, you should strive for the abandonment of harsh speech. These faults will not arise that befell <s>Sthaviraka</s> when he was an ordinary person. And this very mass of virtues will come about, just as when he attained <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 239]

children.text: AVŚ_93 hastakaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_93: <s>Hastaka</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ prakṛtijātismaraś ca | sa svakaṃ hastaṃ gṛhītvā āliṅgate cumbati pariṣvajati, vācaṃ bhāṣate: aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhau, aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhakāv iti | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād ayaṃ jātamātra eva hastāv āliṅgate cumbati, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya hastaka iti nāmeti | hastako dāraka aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | yadā tatra deśe kiṃcid bhavati bhayam*, tadā sa janakāyo bhīta itaś cāmutaś codbhrānto bhāṇḍaṃ gopāyati | sa tu hastau gopāyati, janakāyasya caivaṃ kathayati: mā bhavanto dakṣiṇīyeṣu cittaṃ pradūṣayata, mā paruṣāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣayadhvam*, aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhakau, aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhakāv iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain guild-master — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported with her, enjoyed himself, and amused himself. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs, and by nature remembering his past lives. He grasped his own hands, embraced them, kissed them, and hugged them, saying: 'Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands! Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands!' At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was established: 'What shall the boy's name be?' The relatives said: 'Since this boy, the very moment he was born, embraced and kissed his hands, let the boy's name be <s>Hastaka</s> (Little Hands).' The boy <s>Hastaka</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. Whenever any danger arose in that region, the people, frightened and scattered here and there, would protect their goods. But he would protect his hands, and would say to the people: 'Good people, do not corrupt your minds toward those worthy of offerings, do not speak harsh words! Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands! Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands!'

children.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena hastako jetavanaṃ gataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | sa prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tato 'sya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā hastakena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | sa dṛṣṭasatyo mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, <s>Hastaka</s> went to the <s>Jetavana</s>. There he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his limbs resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns — like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, his mind became serene in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Filled with faith, having paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths, hearing which <s>Hastaka</s>, splitting with the thunderbolt of knowledge the mountain of the view of the personal self (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising to twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he obtained permission from his parents and went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 240]

children.text: bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | so 'rhatvaprāpto 'py evam eva bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati: mā bhavanto dakṣiṇīyeṣu cittaṃ pradūṣayata, mā kharāṃ vācaṃ niścārayata | aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhakau, aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhakāv iti ||
children.translated_text: turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Even after attaining <s>Arhatship</s>, he continued to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the monks in this same way: 'Good sirs, do not corrupt your minds toward those worthy of offerings, do not utter harsh speech! Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands! Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands!'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta hastakena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni yenārhatvaprāpto 'py evam eva kathayati: aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhakau, aho bata me hastakau sucireṇa labdhakāv iti | bhagavān āha: pratyakṣakarmaphaladarśī bhikṣavo 'yaṃ pudgalaḥ | icchatha yūyam avadhārayitum*? evaṃ bhadanta | hastakenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | hastakena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Hastaka</s> perform and accumulate that, even after attaining <s>Arhatship</s>, he continues to say: "Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands! Oh, at long last I have obtained my hands!"?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This person, monks, is one who sees the results of <s>karma</s> directly. Do you wish to hear?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.'
