'It was <s>Hastaka</s> himself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Hastaka</s> who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_93.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_93.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśatisahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | yāvat tatra dvau bhikṣū saṃśīlikau | tatraiko bahuśruto 'rhan*, dvitīyo 'lpaśrutaḥ pṛthagjanaś ca | tatra yo 'sāv arhan* bahuśrutaḥ, sa jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ bahūni ca nimantraṇakāni pratilabhate | sa taṃ saṃśīlikabhikṣuṃ yatra nimantrito bhavati, tatra paścācchramaṇaṃ nayati | yāvad anyatamasmin divase 'rhan nimantritaḥ | nimantraṇakaṃ gantukāmas taṃ paścācchramaṇam āgacchati, na ca pratilabhate | tatas tena tasyādarśanād anyo bhikṣur nītaḥ | yāvat tatra taruṇabhikṣubhir auddhatyābhiprāyair evam uktam*: paśyata bhadantā yāvat tenāyaṃ paścācchramaṇo 'dya na nīto 'nyo nīta iti | tatas tena krodhābhibhūtenārhato 'ntike cittaṃ pradūṣya kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam* | # # # # # # # # # # # # tena pañca janmaśatāny ahasto jātaḥ | yadā āśayato vipratisārajātena atyayam atyayato deśitaṃ vivṛtam uttānīkṛtam*, tena hastau pratilabdhau | yat punas tena paṭhitaṃ svādhyāyitaṃ skandhakauśalaṃ dhātukauśalam
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, the Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed tamer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of <s>Devas</s> and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s>, in the Deer Park. Now there were two monks who were companions. One was learned and an <s>Arhat</s>; the second was of little learning and an ordinary person. The one who was an <s>Arhat</s> and learned was renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, and received many meal-invitations. He would take his companion monk as an attendant wherever he was invited. One day, the <s>Arhat</s> was invited to a meal. Wishing to go, he went to fetch his attendant, but could not find him. Since he could not find him, he took another monk. Then certain young monks with restless intentions said: "Look, sirs, today he did not take his usual attendant — he took another!" Then the [companion], overcome with anger, corrupted his mind toward the <s>Arhat</s> and uttered harsh speech. [Lacuna in text.] Because of that, for five hundred births he was born without hands. When, with a change of heart, he felt remorse and confessed the transgression as a transgression, openly, clearly, and fully, by that he regained his hands. And because he had studied, recited, and developed skill in the aggregates, skill in the elements,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 241]

children.text: āyatanakauśalaṃ pratītyasamutpādakauśalaṃ ca kṛtam*, tena mama śāsane pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: skill in the sense-bases, and skill in dependent origination, by that he has now, having gone forth in my teaching, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements). Thus, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_94 lekuñcikaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_94: <s>Lekuñcika</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamo brahmaṇa āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto durvarṇo durdarśano 'vahoḍimakaḥ | jātamātrasya cāsya mātuḥ stanābhyāṃ kṣīram antarhitam* | yāvat tena brāhmaṇena tasyānyā dhātrī ānītā | tasyā api kṣīram antarhitam* | tasya dārikasya karmavipākataḥ | yadāsya kṣīrasaṃbhavaḥ sarvair apy upāyair na saṃbhavati, tadāsau lehenodbhṛtaḥ (Speyer: lehenoddhṛtaḥ) | tasya lekuñcika iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam* | so 'lpeśākhyo 'lpapuṇyaś ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported with her, enjoyed himself, and amused himself. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — of ugly complexion, ugly to look at, dwarfish. The very moment he was born, the milk in his mother's breasts vanished. Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> brought another wet-nurse for him, but her milk also vanished — due to the ripening of that boy's <s>karma</s>. Since his supply of milk could not be obtained by any means whatsoever, he was raised on gruel (<s>leha</s>). Thus his name was established as <s>Lekuñcika</s>. He was of little renown and little merit.

children.text: yadā mahān saṃvṛttas tadā udarapūraṇam api nāsādayati | paśyati ca bhikṣūn sunivasitān suprāvṛtān bhramarasadṛśāni pātrāṇi gṛhītvā śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya praviśataḥ | tāṃś ca pūrṇahastān pūrṇapātrān pratiniṣkrāmataḥ | tasya dṛṣṭvā bhagavacchāsane pravrajyābhilāṣa utpannaḥ | sa mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajito 'py udarapūraṇaṃ nāsādayati | tena tenaiva saṃvegena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had grown up, he could not even obtain enough to fill his belly. He would see monks well-dressed and well-robed, carrying bowls resembling black bees, entering <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. And he would see them coming out with full hands and full bowls. Having seen this, the desire to go forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching arose in him. Having obtained permission from his parents, he went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching, yet even so he could not obtain enough to fill his belly. Driven by that very sense of urgency, by striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 242]

children.text: yāvad asāv apareṇa samayena bhagavato gandhakuṭīṃ saṃmārjituṃ pravṛttaḥ | sa tāṃ saṃmṛjya pātracīvaram ādāya śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat* | tatas tena prabhūtaḥ praṇītaś ca piṇḍapāta āsāditaḥ, yenāsya saṃtarpitānīndriyāṇi mahābhūtāni | tatas tena saṃtarpitendriyeṇa kṛtsnā rātrir dhyānavimokṣasamāpattibhir atināmitā | tato 'sya buddhir utpannā: śobhano 'yam upāyo yanv ahaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ vijñāpayeyam iti | tena sarva eva bhikṣusaṃgho vijñāpitaḥ: ahaṃ bhadanta alpapuṇyo yadā gandhakuṭīṃ saṃmṛjya piṇḍapātaṃ praviśāmi, tadā tṛptiṃ labhe | tan me saṃghaḥ kāruṇyaṃ karotu, nānyena bhagavato gandhakuṭī saṃmrāṣṭavyeti | tataḥ saṃghena kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ: na kenacid bhagavato gandhakuṭī saṃmrāṣṭavyeti | sa visrabdho gandhakuṭīṃ saṃmṛjya paścāc chrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya praviśati ||
children.translated_text: On a later occasion, he began to sweep the Blessed One's <s>gandhakuṭī</s> (perfumed chamber). Having swept it, he took his bowl and robe and entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms. Then he obtained abundant and excellent alms-food, by which his sense faculties and great elements were nourished. Then, with his faculties nourished, he spent the entire night engaged in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberations), and <s>samāpatti</s> (attainments). Then this idea arose in him: 'This is an excellent method; let me inform the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks.' He informed the entire <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks: 'Venerable Sirs, I am of little merit. When I sweep the <s>gandhakuṭī</s> and then go out for alms, I obtain satisfaction. May the <s>Saṃgha</s> show compassion to me — let no one else sweep the Blessed One's <s>gandhakuṭī</s>.' Then the <s>Saṃgha</s> made a formal resolution: 'No one shall sweep the Blessed One's <s>gandhakuṭī</s>.' Thus assured, he would sweep the <s>gandhakuṭī</s> and afterward enter <s>Śrāvastī</s> for alms.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca samaye āyuṣmāñ chāradvatīputraḥ pañcaśataparivāro janapade varṣoṣitaḥ śrāvastyām abhyāgataḥ | tataḥ śāstur gauravajāto gandhakuṭīṃ saṃmārṣṭum ārabdhaḥ | sa āyuṣmatā lekuñcikena lakṣitaḥ | tenocyate: sthavira udare mama prahāro dattaḥ, yat te gandhakuṭī saṃmṛṣṭeti | sthaviraḥ prāha: katham iti? lekuñcikaḥ kathayati: sthavira, yadāhaṃ gandhakuṭīṃ na saṃmārjitavāṃs tadā piṇḍapātaṃ nāsādayāmīti | tataḥ sthaviraśāriputreṇoktam: yady evam aham anyatra nimantritaḥ | alpotsukas tvaṃ bhava | ahaṃ tatra tubhyaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ dāsyāmīti | tataḥ sthaviraśāriputraḥ pañcaśataparivāro nimantraṇakaṃ prasthitaḥ | lekuñciko 'pi tenaiva sārdhaṃ saṃprasthitaḥ | yadā gṛhapater gṛhasamīpaṃ gatas tadā lekuñcikasya karmavipākena tasmin gṛhe mahān kalahaḥ samutpannaḥ | tata āyuṣmato lekuñcikasyaitad abhavat: mamālpapuṇyatayā tatra kalaho jāta iti | tataḥ pratinivṛtya vihāraṃ gatvā bhaktacchedam akarot* | tato dvitīye divase sthaviraśāriputreṇocyate: kimarthaṃ tvaṃ na gata iti | tenoktam*: sthavireṇa nāvagatam*: mamālpapuṇyatayā yādṛśas tatra kalaho jāta iti | tataḥ sthaviraśāriputreṇānyatra divase taṃ puraskṛtya tad gṛhaṃ praveśitaḥ | saṃghamadhye copaviṣṭasya sataḥ pradakṣiṇaś cāhāro dīyate | tatra pariveṣakajano vismarati | tena saṃghamadhye dvitīyo bhaktacchedaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> [<s>Śāriputra</s>], accompanied by five hundred monks, having spent the rainy season in the countryside, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Then, out of reverence for the Teacher, he began to sweep the <s>gandhakuṭī</s>. The venerable <s>Lekuñcika</s> noticed him and said: 'Elder, a blow has been struck to my belly, in that you have swept the <s>gandhakuṭī</s>.' The Elder asked: 'How so?' <s>Lekuñcika</s> said: 'Elder, when I do not sweep the <s>gandhakuṭī</s>, I do not obtain alms-food.' Then the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'If so, I have been invited elsewhere. Do not worry. I will give you alms-food there.' Then the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, accompanied by five hundred monks, set out for the invitation. <s>Lekuñcika</s> too set out together with him. When they reached the vicinity of the householder's dwelling, by the ripening of <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s <s>karma</s>, a great quarrel broke out in that house. Then the venerable <s>Lekuñcika</s> thought: 'Due to my lack of merit, a quarrel has arisen there.' Then, having turned back and gone to the monastery, he went without a meal. On the second day, the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s> asked him: 'Why did you not come?' He replied: 'The Elder did not understand — due to my lack of merit, what a quarrel arose there!' Then on another day, the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s> brought him along first and had him enter that house. And while food was being distributed clockwise as he sat in the midst of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the server forgot him. Thus he went without a meal for a second time in the midst of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

children.text: yāvad iyaṃ pravṛttiḥ sthavirānandena śrutā | śrutvā ca lekuñcikam uvāca: tena hi tvam ihaiva jetavane tiṣṭha, ahaṃ te piṇḍapātam āneṣyāmīti | sthavirānandasyaivaṃvidhā smṛtiḥ | yadā bhagavato 'ntikād aśītir dharmaskandhasahasrāṇy udgṛhītāni # # # | lekuñcikasya ca karmāvaraṇena sthavirānandena vismṛtam* | tatrānena tṛtīyo bhaktacchedaḥ kṛtaḥ | caturthe divase sthavirānandenāsthāṃ kṛtvā piṇḍapāto dattaḥ | so 'pi nirgacchataḥ śvabhir apahṛtaḥ | tatrānena caturtho bhaktacchedaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> heard of this matter. Having heard, he said to <s>Lekuñcika</s>: 'In that case, you stay right here in the <s>Jetavana</s>. I will bring you alms-food.' Such was the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>'s mindfulness — he who had received eighty thousand collections of <s>Dharma</s> teachings from the Blessed One — yet due to <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obstruction), the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> forgot. Thus he went without a meal for a third time. On the fourth day, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, making a special effort, gave him alms-food. But as he was going out, it was snatched away by dogs. Thus he went without a meal for a fourth time.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 243]

children.text: pañcame divase sthaviramaudgalyāyanena śrutvā lekuñcikasyāthāya piṇḍapātaṃ gṛhītvā ṛddhyā saṃprasthitam* | lekuñcikasya karmavipākena suparṇinā pakṣirājena pakṣaiḥ parāhatya mahāsamudre pātitaḥ | tatrānena pañcamo bhatacchedaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the fifth day, the venerable <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, having heard, took alms-food for <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s sake and set out by supernatural power. But due to the ripening of <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s <s>karma</s>, the king of the <s>Suparṇi</s> birds struck him with his wings and cast him down into the great ocean. Thus he went without a meal for a fifth time.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe divase śāriputreṇa śrutam* | tasyaitad abhavat*: yanv ahaṃ lekuñcikasya piṇḍapātaṃ ###################### lekuñcikasya kuṭikādvāre 'vasthitaḥ | tato lekuñcikasya karmavipākena tad api dvāraṃ śilābhir āvṛtam* | tataḥ śāriputreṇa ṛddhyā mokṣyāmīti tat pātraṃ pṛthivyāṃ sthāpitam* | tad api lekuñcikasya karmavipākena | athāśītiṣu yojanasahasreṣu kāñcanamayyāṃ pṛthivyām avasthitam* | tato 'pi sthaviraśāriputreṇa ṛddhyā samuddhṛtya tat piṇḍakaṃ mukhadvāraśleṣite piṇḍapāte tasya karmāvaraṇena tan mukham ekadhanaṃ saṃvṛttam* | tata āyuṣmāñ chāriputro lekuñcikasyābhavyatāṃ jñātvā saṃvignaḥ | tena ca bhadantena ṣaḍ bhaktacchedāḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the sixth day, <s>Śāriputra</s> heard of it. This thought arose in him: 'Let me [bring] alms-food for <s>Lekuñcika</s>' — and he stood at the door of <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s cell. But due to the ripening of <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s <s>karma</s>, that very door became blocked by stones. Then <s>Śāriputra</s>, thinking 'I shall free it by supernatural power,' placed the bowl on the ground. But due to the ripening of <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s <s>karma</s>, it sank down eighty thousand <s>yojanas</s> into the golden earth. Then the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, having retrieved the alms-food by supernatural power and brought it to the entrance of [<s>Lekuñcika</s>'s] mouth, found that due to his <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obstruction), his mouth had sealed shut into a single mass. Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, recognizing <s>Lekuñcika</s>'s hopeless condition, was shaken with spiritual urgency. And the venerable one went without a meal for six days.

children.text: tataḥ saptame divase āyuṣmāl lekuñcikaḥ satvānām udvejanārthaṃ karmaṇāṃ cāvipraṇaśasaṃdarśanārthaṃ karmabalodbhāvanārthaṃ ca bhasmanā pātraṃ pūrayitvā buddhapramukhasya bhikṣusaṃghasya purastān niṣadya udakenāloḍya pītvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ | tam abhivīkṣya bhikṣavaḥ saṃvignāḥ tasya śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta lekuñcikena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenārhatvaprāpto 'pi ṣaḍ bhaktacchedān kṛtvā saptame divase nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛta iti | bhagavān āha: lekuñcikenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | lekuñcikena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: Then, on the seventh day, the venerable <s>Lekuñcika</s> — for the purpose of stirring urgency in beings and for the purpose of demonstrating that deeds do not perish and for the purpose of displaying the power of <s>karma</s> — filled his bowl with ashes and, seated before the <s>Saṃgha</s> of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s>, mixed it with water, drank it, and passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇadhātu</s> (element of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>) without remainder. Having witnessed this, the monks were shaken with urgency. Having performed the funeral rites for his body, doubt arose in them, and they asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Lekuñcika</s> perform that, even though he had attained <s>Arhatship</s>, he went without a meal for six days and on the seventh day passed into the <s>Nirvāṇadhātu</s> without remainder?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Lekuñcika</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Lekuñcika</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_94.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_94.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamā gṛhapatipatnī śrāddhā bhadrā kalyāṇāśayā | sā abhīṣṇaṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakayācanakebhyo dānāni dadāti | tasyā apareṇa samayena bhartā kālagataḥ | yāvad asyāḥ putraḥ svagṛhe svāmī saṃvṛttaḥ | sa ca matsarī kuṭukuñcakaḥ āgṛhītapariṣkāraḥ kākāya baliṃ na pradātuṃ vyavasyati | sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakān dṛṣṭvā cittaṃ pradūṣayati | tasya mātā tenaiva pūrvakrameṇa śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakebhyo dānapradānāny anuprayacchati | tasyāḥ putro mātsaryābhibhūtaḥ kathayati: amba na me rocate (Speyer: rocyate) | mā dānam anuprayaccheti | sā kathayati: putraka iha kule eṣa kuladharma iti |
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain householder's wife — faithful, virtuous, of good intentions. She constantly gave gifts to <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics), <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, wayfarers, and beggars. On a later occasion, her husband died. Then her son became the master of the house. He was miserly, stingy, and tight-fisted — he would not even give a morsel of food to a crow. Upon seeing <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, wayfarers, and beggars, he would become displeased. His mother, following the previous custom, continued to give gifts to <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, wayfarers, and beggars. Her son, overcome by miserliness, said: 'Mother, this does not please me. Do not give gifts.' She said: 'Child, in this family, this is the family tradition.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 244]

children.text: tatas tena pṛthagbhaktena sthāpitā | tathāpy asāv upārdhād dānam anuprayacchati, upārdham ātmanā paribhuñkte | tatas tena mātsaryābhibhūtena krodhenāvṛtabuddhinā bhūyo nivāryata eva | yadā sarvāvasthāyāṃ na śaknoti vārayitum*, tadā mātaram uvāca: amba kiṃcit karaṇīyam asti, avavarakaṃ praviśeti | sā ṛjusvabhāvatayā avavarakaṃ praviṣṭā | tatas tena dvāraṃ baddhvā ekaṃ bhaktacchedaṃ kāritā | sā kathayati: putra bubhukṣitāsmīti | tatas tena kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam*: bhasma khādeti | yāvat tenāsau kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptā sakaruṇakaruṇaṃ vikrośamānā ṣaḍ bhaktacchedān kāritā, tathāpi na pratimuktā | kālagatā | tadāsya mātsaryeṇāvṛtasya mātṛviyogād vipratisāro jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he had her eat separately. Even so, she gave gifts from half [her portion] and consumed the other half herself. Then, overcome by miserliness and with his mind clouded by anger, he prevented her even further. When in every situation he was unable to stop her, he said to his mother: 'Mother, there is something to be done. Enter the inner chamber.' She, being of a straightforward nature, entered the inner chamber. Then he locked the door and made her go without food for one meal. She said: 'Son, I am hungry.' Then he uttered harsh words: 'Eat ashes!' And so he, having brought her to a state of extreme distress, hardship, and anguish, as she cried out pitifully and pathetically, made her go without food for six meals, and still did not release her. She died. Then, when the miserly one's mother had passed away, remorse arose in him.

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena gṛhapatiputraḥ, ayaṃ sa lekuñcikaḥ | yad anena mātur apakāraḥ kṛtas tasya karmaṇo vipākena kalpam avīcau mahānaraka utpannaḥ | tenaiva hetunā idānīm apy arhatvaprāptaḥ ṣaḍ bhaktacchedān kṛtvā bhasmād anāhāra eva parinirvṛtaḥ | anyāny api bhikṣavo lekuñcikena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamo brāhmaṇo devatārcikaḥ sarveṣāṃ vārāṇaseyānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'bhimataś ca sarvajanasya | dharmatā caiṣā yad asati buddhānām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya | yāvad anyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho vārāṇasīṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ | sa ca tatra pūrṇahastaḥ pūrṇapātro nirgacchati | tena brāhmanena dṛṣṭaḥ | tasya mātsaryam utpannam* | kathayati: ānaya yāvat pātraṃ paśyāmīti | asamanvāhṛtya ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartata iti | tena bhadantenopanāmitam* | tatas tena pṛthivyām utsṛjya pādenābhimṛditam* | tatas tena pratyekabuddhena bhaktachedaḥ kṛtaḥ | na ca tasya brāhmaṇasya vipratisāro jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the householder's son — he is this <s>Lekuñcika</s>. Because he committed that offense against his mother, by the ripening of that <s>karma</s> he was born in the great <s>Avīci</s> hell for a <s>kalpa</s>. By that very cause, even now, though he had attained <s>Arhatship</s>, he went without a meal for six days and passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> having consumed nothing but ashes. <s>Lekuñcika</s> performed and accumulated still other deeds, monks. In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who was a worshipper of deities, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by all the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, and respected by all people. And it is a law of nature that when <s>Buddhas</s> have not arisen, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arise in the world — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, fond of remote lodgings and meals, sole worthy recipients of offerings to the world. A certain <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s> for alms. And he came out with full hands and a full bowl. That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> saw him. Miserliness arose in him. He said: 'Bring it here; let me see the bowl.' And he did not reflect that the knowledge-and-vision of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> does not operate [in response to such provocation]. The venerable one offered it to him. Then [the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] threw it on the ground and crushed it with his foot. Thereby the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> went without a meal. And no remorse arose in that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau brāhmaṇaḥ, ayam evāsau lekuñcikaḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajito babhūva | tatrānena brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ | tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who was that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — he is this very <s>Lekuñcika</s>. Furthermore, he went forth under the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There he maintained the life of celibacy. By that he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.

children.text: AVŚ_95 saṃsāraḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_95: <s>Saṃsāra</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 245]

children.text:
saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | śrāvastyām anyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | sa jātamātra eva gṛham avalokya vācaṃ niścārayati sma: duḥkho bhavantaḥ saṃsāraḥ, paramaduḥkhaḥ saṃsāraḥ | ity uktvā tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād ayaṃ jātamātra eva saṃsāra iti ghoṣayati, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya saṃsāra iti nāmeti | saṃsāro dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* |
  yadā saṃsāro dārakaḥ krameṇa mahān saṃvṛttaḥ, sa prakṛtijātismaratvāc ca janakāyasya dharmaṃ deśayati: mā bhavanto guruṣu gurusthānīyeṣu mātāpitṛṣv ācāryopādhyāyeṣu vā kharavācaṃ niścārayata | duḥkhaṃ saṃsāra iti | yāvad apareṇa samayena itaś cāmutaś ca paribhramañ jetavanaṃ nirgataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā saṃsāravairāgyikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā saṃsāro dārakaḥ saṃsāre doṣadarśī bhūtvā mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | so 'rhatvaprāpto 'pi bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati: mā āyuṣmanto guruṣu gurusthānīyeṣu mātāpitṛṣv ācāryopādhyāyeṣu {vā} kharavācaṃ niścārayata | duḥkhaṃ saṃsāraḥ, paramaduḥkhaṃ saṃsāra iti | ++++++++++++++||
children.translated_text:
together with the monastic community, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. In <s>Śrāvastī</s> there was a certain householder, wealthy, of great riches and great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal status. He sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with her. As he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — beautiful, lovely, graceful, endowed with all major and minor limbs. As soon as he was born, he looked around the house and uttered these words: "<s>Saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) is suffering, good people; <s>saṃsāra</s> is the utmost suffering." Having spoken thus, he fell silent. At his birth, having performed the birth celebration, a name was determined: "What shall be the name of the boy?" The relatives said: "Since as soon as he was born he proclaimed '<s>saṃsāra</s>,' let the name of the boy be <s>Saṃsāra</s>." The boy <s>Saṃsāra</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.
When the boy <s>Saṃsāra</s> had gradually grown up, because he naturally remembered his previous lives, he taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the people: "Good people, do not utter harsh words toward your elders and those worthy of respect — parents, teachers, and preceptors. <s>Saṃsāra</s> is suffering." At a later time, wandering here and there, he came to the <s>Jetavana</s>. There he saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, encircled by a fathom-wide aura, with radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. Upon seeing him, he set his mind at ease in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. With faith arisen, having paid homage at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, he sat down before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> taught him a teaching on the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta saṃsāreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni, yena pañca janmaśatāni mṛtakuṇapa eva mātuḥ kukṣer nirgataḥ | pravrajya
children.translated_text: The monks, having doubts, questioned the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: "What deeds, Venerable One, were performed by <s>Saṃsāra</s>, that for five hundred births he emerged from his mother's womb as a dead corpse? And having gone forth,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 246]

children.text: cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: saṃsāreṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | saṃsāreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: he directly realized <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship)?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "By <s>Saṃsāra</s> himself, monks, in previous births, deeds were performed and accumulated, their provisions gathered, their conditions ripened, standing ready like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition. By <s>Saṃsāra</s>, deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else will experience their results? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_95.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. (AVŚ 95.1)

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvany asminn eva bhadrake kalpe viṃśativarṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhīputraḥ sthavirasakāśe pravrajitaḥ | sa ca sthaviro 'rhan, sa rāgaviprahīṇaḥ | yāvat tatra deśe parva samupasthitam* | tatas taruṇabhikṣuṇā sthavira utthāpyate: uttiṣṭha gocaragrāmaṃ gamiṣyāva iti | sthavira āha: vatsa adyāpi prātar eva, gaccha tāvat kuśalapakṣaṃ pratijāgṛhīti | dvir api trir api taruṇabhikṣuṇā sthavira utthāpyate: uttiṣṭha gocaragrāmaṃ gamiṣyāva iti | dvir api trir api sthavira āha: vatsa adyāpi prātar eva, gaccha tāvat kuśalapakṣaṃ pratijāgṛhīti | tatas tena taruṇabhikṣuṇā rasagṛdhreṇa kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam: mā tvaṃ pañcabhir api janmaśatair jīvaḥ kośān nirgaccha, eṣo 'haṃ nirgata iti ||
children.translated_text: Once upon a time, monks, in the past, in this very <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), when the lifespan of people was twenty thousand years, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. In the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a certain merchant's son went forth under an elder. That elder was an <s>arhat</s>,

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena taruṇabhikṣuḥ, ayam saṃsāraḥ | yad anenārhato 'ntike cittaṃ pradūṣya kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritam*, tasya karmaṇo vipākena pañca janmaśatāni mṛtakuṇapa eva mātuḥ kukṣer nirgataḥ | nirgateṣu pañcasu janmaśateṣu idānīm anena manuṣyatvam āsāditam* | tatas tat smṛtvā kathayati: duḥkhaṃ saṃsāraḥ, paramaduḥkhaṃ saṃsāra iti | yad anena vipratisārajātena sthavirasyātyayo deśitaḥ, brahmacaryavāsaś ca paripālitaḥ, tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "What do you think, monks? He who was at that time the young monk — he is this <s>Saṃsāra</s>. Because he corrupted his mind toward the <s>arhat</s> and uttered harsh verbal action, by the ripening of that deed, for five hundred births he emerged from his mother's womb as a dead corpse. After those five hundred births had elapsed, he has now obtained human existence. Remembering that, he says: '<s>Saṃsāra</s> is suffering, <s>saṃsāra</s> is the utmost suffering.' Because he

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 247]

children.text: AVŚ_96 guptikaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ 96: <s>Guptika</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | yadā bhagavatā stavakarṇikanimantritena saupārake nagare mahājanavineyākarṣaṇaṃ kṛtam*, tadā sarvaḥ saupārakanivāsī janakāyo buddhanimno dharmapravaṇaḥ saṃghaprāgbhāro vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, ministers, the wealthy, citizens, merchants, caravan leaders, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, known and of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding, and medicines for the sick, together with the monastic community, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. When the <s>Bhagavān</s>

children.text: saupārake nagare 'nyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jātaḥ jātamātrasya sarvaśarīraṃ piṭakaiḥ sphuṭaṃ saṃvṛttam* | yadā te piṭakāḥ sphuṭitāḥ, tadā ekadhano māṃsapiṇḍaḥ saṃsthitaḥ | pūyaśoṇitaṃ cāsya śarīrāt pragharan mahaddaurgandhaṃ janayati | tato 'sya pitā aiśvaryabalādhānena dravyamantrauṣadhiparicārakasametaḥ svayam evārabdhaś cikitsāṃ kartum*, na cāsau vyādhir upaśamaṃ gacchati karmabalādhānaprāptatvāt* | sa svaśarīraṃ tathā vikṣatam apatrāpya parigṛhītaṃ vastrair gopāyati | tasya guptika iti nāma kṛtam* | yāvad guptiko dārako mahān saṃvṛttas tasya vayasyakāḥ sahajātakāḥ śrāvastyāḥ saupārakanagaram anuprāptāḥ | tatas taiḥ pitur asya kathyate: tāta yady eṣa śrāvastīṃ nīyate, śakyetāsmād vyādheḥ parimocayitum*, yasmāt tatra santi vaidyabhaiṣajādayaḥ sulabhā iti ||
children.translated_text: In the city of <s>Saupāraka</s>, a certain householder was wealthy, of great riches and great possessions, with vast and extensive property, equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal status. He sported, enjoyed, and amused himself with her. As he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born, and as soon as he was born, his entire body was covered with boils.

children.text: tataḥ pitrā tad vacanam upaśrutya prabhūtāni ratnāni paricārakāṃś ca datvā śrāvastīm anupreṣitaḥ | so 'nupūrveṇa vayasyakasahāyaḥ śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ | tatrāpy asya karmajo vyādhiḥ saty api vaidyadravyauṣadhiparicārakabāhulye na śakyate cikitsitum* | yāvad asāv apareṇa samayena jetavanaṃ nirgataḥ | athāsau dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam* | prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | tasmai bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā pañcopādānaskandhā rogato gaṇḍataḥ śalyato 'ghato 'nityato duḥkhataḥ śūnyato 'nātmataś ca deśitāḥ | sa saṃskārānityatāṃ viditvā bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā
children.translated_text: Then his father, hearing that message, gave abundant jewels and attendants and sent him to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. He traveled stage by stage with his companions and arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. There too, his disease born of <s>karma</s> could not be cured despite the abundance of physicians, medicines, drugs, and attendants. At a later time, he went to the <s>Jetavana</s>. There he saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 248]

children.text: sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | te 'py asya sahajātakās tenaiva saṃvegena pravrajitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Those who were born at the same time as him also went forth, impelled by the same spiritual urgency.

children.text: te yenāyuṣmān guptikas tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramyāyuṣmantaṃ guptikam idam avocan*: kim āyuṣman guptika pralopadharma, kiṃ vā atra loke 'pralopadharma? rūpam āyuṣmantaḥ pralopadharma | tasya nirodhān nirvāṇam apralopadharma | vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānam āyuṣmantaḥ pralopadharma | tasya nirodhān nirvāṇam apralopadharma | kiṃ manyadhve āyuṣmantaḥ: rūpaṃ nityaṃ vā anityaṃ vā? anityam idam āyuṣman guptika | yat punar anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā tan na vā, duḥkham*? duḥkham idam āyuṣman guptika | yat punar anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ vipariṇāmadharma, satyam api tac chrutavān āryaśrāvaka ātmata upagacched etan mama, eṣo 'ham asmi, eṣa me ātmety evam etat? no āyuṣman guptika | kiṃ manyadhve āyuṣmantaḥ: vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānaṃ nityaṃ vā anityaṃ vā? anityam idam āyuṣman guptika | yat punar anityaṃ duḥkham*? duḥkham idam āyuṣman guptika | yat punar anityaṃ duḥkhaṃ vipariṇāmadharma, api tac chrutavān āryaśrāvaka ātmata upagacchet*: etan mama, eṣo 'ham asmi, eṣa me ātmeti? no āyuṣman guptika | tasmāt tarhi āyuṣmanto yat kiṃcid rūpam atītānāgatapratyutpannam ādhyātmikaṃ vā bāhyaṃ vā audārikaṃ vā sūkṣmaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā praṇītaṃ vā, yad vā dūre, yad vāntike, tat sarvaṃ naitan mama, naiṣo 'ham asmi, naiṣa me ātmety evam etad yathābhūtaṃ samyakprajñayā draṣṭavyam* | yā kācid vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā yat kiṃcid vijñānam atītānāgatapratyutpannam ādhyātmikaṃ vā bāhyaṃ vā audārikaṃ vā sūkṣmaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā praṇītaṃ vā, yad vā dūre, yad vāntike, tat sarvaṃ naitan mama, naiṣo 'ham asmi, naiṣa me ātmety evam etad yathābhūtaṃ samyakprajñayā draṣṭavyam* | evaṃdarśī āyuṣmantaḥ śrutavān āryaśrāvako rūpād api nirvidyate, vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārebhyo vijñānād api | nirviṇṇo virujyate, virako vimucyate | vimuktam evaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati: kṣīṇā me jātiḥ, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṛtaṃ karaṇīyam* | nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti ||
children.translated_text: They approached the venerable <s>Guptika</s>. Having approached, they said this to the venerable <s>Guptika</s>: 'What, venerable <s>Guptika</s>, is subject to destruction, and what in this world is not subject to destruction?' 'Form, venerable ones, is subject to destruction. Through its cessation, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not subject to destruction. Feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness, venerable ones, are subject to destruction. Through their cessation, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is not subject to destruction. What do you think, venerable ones: is form permanent or impermanent?' 'It is impermanent, venerable <s>Guptika</s>.' 'And that which is impermanent — is it suffering or not?' 'It is suffering, venerable <s>Guptika</s>.' 'And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change — would a learned noble disciple regard it as self, [thinking]: "This is mine, this I am, this is my self"?' 'No, venerable <s>Guptika</s>.' 'What do you think, venerable ones: are feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness permanent or impermanent?' 'They are impermanent, venerable <s>Guptika</s>.' 'And that which is impermanent — is it suffering?' 'It is suffering, venerable <s>Guptika</s>.' 'And that which is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change — would a learned noble disciple regard it as self: "This is mine, this I am, this is my self"?' 'No, venerable <s>Guptika</s>.' 'Therefore, venerable ones, whatever form there is — past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all that should be seen as it really is with right wisdom thus: "This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self." Whatever feeling, perception, formations, whatever consciousness there is — past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all that should be seen as it really is with right wisdom thus: "This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self." Seeing thus, venerable ones, the learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form, disenchanted with feeling, with perception, with formations, and with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate; being dispassionate, he is liberated. In liberation, the knowledge-and-vision arises: "Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done. I know no further existence beyond this."'

children.text: asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe teṣāṃ sahajātakānāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur utpannam* | bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta guptikena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenāsya śārīram evaṃ bībhatsavyādhibahulaṃ durgandhaṃ saṃvṛttam* | kiṃ karma kṛtaṃ yena tīkṣṇaniśitabuddhiḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: guptikenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | guptikena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni |
children.translated_text: While this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, in those born at the same time, the dustless, stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye arose with regard to all phenomena. The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Guptika</s> perform that his body became thus — repulsive, afflicted with many diseases, and foul-smelling? What deed did he perform that he became one of sharp and keen intellect, and that having gone forth he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By <s>Guptika</s> himself, monks, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Guptika</s> deeds were performed and accumulated.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 249]

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_96.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_96.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ anyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī | sa dvitīyaśreṣṭhinā sārdhaṃ viruddhaḥ | tatas tena rājā prabhūtaṃ dhanaṃ datvā vijñāpitaḥ: deva ayaṃ śreṣṭhī aparādhikaḥ, kriyatām asya daṇḍanigraha iti | tato rājñā tasyaivānujñātaḥ | tenāsau svagṛham ānīya talābhis tāḍitaḥ | tato rudhirāvasiktaśarīrasya prabhūtaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca viṣacūrṇaṃ datvoptam*, yenāsya tac charīram ekadhanaṃ māṃsapiṇḍavad avasthitam* | tatas tasya śreṣṭhino vayasyakaiḥ śrutam*: yathā tenaivaṃvidhaṃ karma kṛtam iti | tatas taiḥ sametair bhūtvā # # {upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ} yair upakaraṇaviśeṣais tasmād vyādheḥ parimocitaḥ | tato 'sau tenaiva ca saṃvegena gṛhān niṣkramya pravrajitaḥ | tena anācāryakeṇa saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyān dharmān bhāvayitvā pratyekā bodhiḥ sākṣātkṛtā | tato 'sya cittam utpannam*: bahv anena śreṣṭhinā matsaṃtāpād apuṇyaṃ prasūtam* | yanv aham enaṃ gatvā saṃvejayeyam iti | tatas tasyāgrato gatvā upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayitum ārabdhaḥ | āśu pṛthagjanānām ṛddhir āvarjanakarī | sa mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ vijñāpayati: avatara, avatara mahādakṣiṇīya, kṛtāparādho 'haṃ tavāntike, tvām eva niśritya punaḥ, pratyupasthāsyāmīti | tenāsau pratyekabuddhaḥ kṣamāpayitvā piṇḍakena pratipādya paṭenācchāditaḥ | praṇidhānaṃ ca kṛtam*: yan mayā krodhābhibhūtena tavāparādhaḥ kṛtaḥ, mā asya karmaṇo vipākaṃ pratyanubhaveyam* | yan mayā satkāraḥ kṛtaḥ, anenaivaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syām*, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāram ārāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain guild-master. He was in conflict with a second guild-master. Then, having given a large amount of wealth to the king, he petitioned: "Sire, this guild-master is a criminal; let punishment and restraint be imposed upon him." Then the king authorized him [to act]. He brought that one to his own house and beat him with blows. Then, upon the body drenched with blood, he applied a great quantity of sharp poison-powder, by which his body became a single mass, standing like a lump of flesh. Then the friends of that guild-master heard: "He has committed such a deed against him." Then, having assembled together, {with special remedies} they freed him from that affliction by special remedies. Then he, impelled by that very spiritual urgency, left his household and went forth. Without a teacher, having cultivated the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>), he directly realized <s>Pratyeka</s>-awakening. Then this thought arose in him: 'Much demerit has been generated by that guild-master due to his hostility toward me. Let me now go and give him a sense of spiritual urgency.' Then, having gone before him, ascending into the sky, he began to display various miracles. The supernatural power of an ordinary person quickly wins over [others]. He, like a tree cut at the root, fell at his feet and, with palms joined, petitioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Descend, descend, O greatly worthy one! I have committed an offense against you. Relying upon you again, I shall attend upon you.' Then he begged the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>'s forgiveness, offered him alms-food, and covered him with a cloth. And he made this aspiration: 'Since I, overpowered by anger, committed an offense against you, may I not experience the fruit of that <s>karma</s>! And by the act of reverence I have performed, may I become a recipient of such virtues, and may I please a teacher even more distinguished!'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena śreṣṭhī āsīt*, ayam sa guptikaḥ | tasya karmaṇaḥ prabhāvāt pañca janmaśatāni kaśābhis tāḍyamānaḥ kālaṃ kṛtavān* | tenaiva hetunā ayam evaṃvidhaṃ āśraya āsāditaḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati sahajātakair vayasyakaiḥ sārdhaṃ pravrajita āsīt*| tatraibhir brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ | tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the guild-master — he is this <s>Guptika</s>. By the power of that <s>karma</s>, for five hundred births he was beaten with whips and died. By that very cause he has obtained such a [wretched] bodily form. Furthermore, he went forth under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> together with his companions who were born at the same time. There they preserved the life of celibacy. By that he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 250]

children.text: AVŚ_97 virūpaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_97: <s>Virūpa</s> (The Ugly One). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme | # # # anyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jātaḥ | jātamātrasya sarvaśarīraṃ vikṛtisphuṭaṃ pravṛttam* | durvarṇo durdarśano 'ṣṭādaśabhir doṣavarṇakaiḥ samanvāgataḥ sa dārako bhūtaḥ | tasya mātāpitarau sarvāṅgaṃ durvarṇaṃ durdarśanaṃ vikṛtarūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā cintāparau vyvasthitau | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyvasthāpyate: kiṃ nāma bhavatu dārakasya? jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād ayaṃ jātamātra evaṃ vikṛtarūpaḥ, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya virūpa iti nāma ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. There was a certain householder — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in riches. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, delighted, and amused himself with her. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, his wife became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born. The moment he was born, his entire body broke out in deformities. He was ugly, unsightly, endowed with eighteen marks of disfigurement — that boy became [thus]. His parents, seeing his entire body ugly, unsightly, and of deformed appearance, stood stricken with worry. At his birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since the moment he was born he was of such deformed appearance, let the boy's name be <s>Virūpa</s> (Ugly).'

children.text: ydā mahān saṃvṛttas tadā tasya lajjayā mahān saṃkoco jātaḥ | kutrānyatra gamiṣyāmi, kva tiṣṭhāmi, iti vicārya sujīrṇodyānaṃ jagāma | atha bhagavān mahāśrāvakaparivṛtaḥ sujīrṇodyānaṃ gataḥ | sa bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā jehrīyamāṇa itaś cāmutaś ca palāyitum ārabdhaḥ | tato bhagavatā ṛddhyā tathādhiṣṭhito yan na śaknoti palāyitum* | tato bhagavān saha śrāvakair nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannaḥ | tato nirodhād vyutthāya virūpam ātmānaṃ nirmitavān* | nirmāya śarāvaṃ bhojanapūrṇam ādāya virūpam āgataṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣajāta āmantritavān*: ehi sahāyaka, kuta āgamiṣyate, tiṣṭha, ubhāv api sahitau vatsyāva iti | tato 'sya bhagavatā bhojanaṃ dattam* | prīṇītendriyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ | tato bhagavatā ātmā svaveṣeṇa sthāpitaḥ | tato virūpo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā kathayati: abhirūpataras tvam idānīṃ saṃvṛttaḥ | kasya karmaṇaḥ prabhāvād iti | bhagavān āha: vidyā me asti cittaprasādajananī nāmnā, tasyā eṣa prabhāva iti | tatas tena bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasāditam*, teṣāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇām ālayasamāpannānām* | tato 'sya lakṣmīḥ prādurbhūtā | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: When he had grown up, great shame arose in him on account of his [ugliness]. 'Where else shall I go, where shall I stay?' — having reflected thus, he went to the Overgrown Park. Now the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by great disciples, went to the Overgrown Park. He, seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s>, became ashamed and began to flee this way and that. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, by his supernatural power, so fixed him that he was unable to flee. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with his disciples, entered the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). Then, having emerged from cessation, he created a manifestation of himself in the form of <s>Virūpa</s>. Having created [this form], taking a bowl filled with food, seeing <s>Virūpa</s> approach, he joyfully addressed him: 'Come, friend! Where have you come from? Stay — we two shall dwell together!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave him food. And his faculties became gladdened. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> restored himself to his own appearance. Then <s>Virūpa</s>, seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said: 'You have now become more handsome! By the power of what <s>karma</s> [is this]?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'I have a knowledge called "that which generates serene faith in the mind" — this is its power.' Then he generated serene faith in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and of those great disciples who had attained the meditative attainments. Thereupon beauty manifested in him. And having gone forth, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta virūpeṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenaiva durvarṇo durdarśano 'ṣṭādaśabhir daurvarṇikadoṣaiḥ samanvāgataḥ | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: virūpeṇaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni |
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Virūpa</s> perform, that he was ugly, unsightly, and afflicted with eighteen faults of ugliness, yet having gone forth, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Virūpa</s> himself, monks, who in previous births performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood before him like a flood, which had to inevitably come to pass.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 251]

children.text: virūpeṇaiva karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: 'It was <s>Virūpa</s> himself who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience their results? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases) that deeds performed ripen, whether wholesome or unwholesome:'

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);'

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_97.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_97.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani puṣyo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān* | so 'pareṇa samayenānyatamāṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati | atha puṣyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ | paśyati tasmin kāle dvau bodhisatvau saṃnikṛṣṭau: bhagavāñ chākyamunir maitreyaś ca | maitreyasya svasaṃtatiḥ paripakvā, śāstur vaineyā aparipakvāḥ | śākyamunes tu svasaṃtatir aparipakvā, vaineyāḥ paripakvāḥ | atha puṣyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ śākyamuner bodhisatvasya saṃtatiparipācanārthaṃ himavantaṃ parvatam abhiruhya ratnaguhāṃ praviśa paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā tejodhātuṃ samāpannaḥ | tasmiṃś ca kāle śākyamunir bodhisatvaḥ phalamūlānām arthe himavantaṃ parvatam abhirūḍhaḥ | sa itas tataś cañcūryamāṇo dadarśa puṣyaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvātriṃṣatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam* | sahadarśanāc cānena tathāvidhaṃ cittasamādhānaṃ samāsāditam*, yad ekapādena sapta rātriṃdivāni ekayā gāthayā stutavān*:
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Puṣya</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. On a later occasion, he was dwelling near a certain royal capital. Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Puṣya</s> began to reflect. He saw at that time two <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who were close [to enlightenment]: the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> and <s>Maitreya</s>. <s>Maitreya</s>'s own mental continuum was mature, but his disciples-to-be-trained were not yet mature. <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s own mental continuum was not yet mature, but his disciples-to-be-trained were mature. Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Puṣya</s>, for the sake of maturing the mental continuum of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, ascended the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalaya) mountain, entered a jeweled cave, sat cross-legged, and entered the meditative absorption on the fire element. At that time, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> had ascended the <s>Himavat</s> mountain in search of fruits and roots. Wandering here and there, he beheld the Perfectly Awakened <s>Puṣya</s> — adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of a fathom's span, of radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides. The moment he saw him, he attained such a state of mental concentration that, standing on one foot for seven days and nights, he praised him with a single verse:'

children.text: na divi bhuvi vā nāsmiṃl loke na vaiśravaṇālaye
children.translated_text: 'Not in heaven, nor on earth, nor in this world, nor in the abode of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,'

children.text: na marubhavane divye sthāne na dikṣu vidikṣu vā |
children.translated_text: 'nor in the divine realm of the <s>Maruts</s>, nor in the directions or intermediate directions —'

children.text: caratu vasudhāṃ sphītāṃ kṛtsnāṃ saparvatakānanāṃ
children.translated_text: 'let one traverse the entire vast earth with its mountains and forests:'

children.text: puruṣavṛṣabhāsty anyas tulyo mahāśramaṇas tava || AVŚ_97.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'there is no other bull among men equal to you, O great ascetic!' // AVŚ_97.2 //

children.text: atha puṣyaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ paripakvasaṃtatiṃ śākyamuniṃ bodhisatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā sādhukāram adāt*: sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa |
children.translated_text: Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Puṣya</s>, seeing that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s mental continuum had matured, exclaimed 'Well done!': 'Well done, well done, O noble being!'

children.text: anena balavīryeṇa saṃpannena dvijottama |
children.translated_text: 'By this power and valor, O twice-born one,'

children.text: nava kalpāḥ parāvṛttāḥ saṃstutyādya tathāgatam* || AVŚ_97.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'nine <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) have been eliminated by praising the <s>Tathāgata</s> today.' // AVŚ_97.3 //

children.text: tato bhagavān maheśākhyābhir devatābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ tasyāṃ guhāyāṃ sthitaḥ | tatra guhānivāsinī devatā alpeśākhyatvān na śaknoti tāṃ guhāṃ samabhiroḍhum* | tato vikṛtanayanā bhūtvā bhagavantaṃ bhīṣayate | yadā suciram api bhīṣayamāṇā na śaknoti bhagavato 'pakāraṃ kartum*, tadā tayā prasādo labdhaḥ: śobhano 'yam ṛṣiḥ siddhavrataś ceti | tataḥ sā udāraṃ rūpam abhinirmāya bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya kṣamāpayitvā piṇḍakena pratipāditavatī ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by deities of great fame, remained in that cave. There a cave-dwelling deity, being of little fame, was unable to enter that cave. Then, assuming a distorted appearance, she tried to frighten the <s>Bhagavān</s>. When, even after a long time of trying to frighten him, she was unable to cause any harm to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, she gained faith: 'This <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) is magnificent, one of fulfilled vows.' Then, having manifested a beautiful form, she fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, begged forgiveness, and served him with alms-food.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 252]

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena guhānivāsinī devatā babhūva, ayam virūpaḥ saḥ | tasya karmaṇo vipākena saṃsāre 'nantaṃ duḥkham anubhūtavān* | idānīm api tenaiva hetunā virūpaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ | yad anena paścāc cittaṃ prasāditam*, tenāsya apagatā alakṣmīḥ prādurbhūtā | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? She who at that time, in that era, was the cave-dwelling deity — that is this <s>Virūpa</s>. By the ripening of that deed, he experienced endless suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Even now, by that very cause, he has become ugly. But because he later purified his mind, his misfortune departed and good fortune arose. And having gone forth, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, entirely bright; for those mixed, mixed. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only in entirely bright deeds. Thus indeed, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_98 gaṅgikaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_98: <s>Gaṅgika</s>. (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text:
buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati ṛṣipatane mṛgadāve | vārāṇasyām anyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī | tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam* | sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayato na putro na duhitā | sa kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: anekadhanasamuditaṃ me gṛham*, na me putro na duhitā | mamātyayāt sarvasvāpateyam aputrakam iti kṛtvā rājavidheyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | sa śramaṇabrāhmaṇanaimittikasuhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavair ucyate: devatārādhanaṃ kuruṣveti | so 'putraḥ putrābhinandī śivavaruṇakuberaśakrabrahmādīn anyāṃś ca devatāviśeṣān āyācate | tadyathā ārāmadevatā vanadevatāś catvaradevatāḥ śṛṅgāṭakadevatāḥ | sahajāḥ sahadhārmikā nityānubaddhā api devatā āyācate sma | asti caiṣa loke pravādo yadāyācanahetoḥ putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti | tac ca naivam* | yady evam abhaviṣyad ekaikasya putrasahasram abhaviṣyat tadyathā rājñaś cakravartinaḥ | api tu trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ca | katameṣāṃ trayāṇām* | mātāpitarāu raktau bhavataḥ saṃnipatitau, mātā ca kalyā bhavati ṛtumatī, gandharvaś ca pratyupasthito bhavati | eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ saṃmukhībhāvāt putrā jāyante duhitaraś ceti |
  sa caivam āyācanaparas tiṣṭhati | anyatamaś ca satvo 'nyatamasmāt satvanikāyāc cyutvā tasya prajāpatyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntaḥ | pañcāveṇikā dharmā ekatye paṇḍitajātīye mātṛgrāme | katame
children.translated_text:
The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park. In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there was a certain householder — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported with her, enjoyed himself, and amused himself. As he was thus sporting, enjoying, and amusing himself, neither a son nor a daughter was born. Resting his cheek on his hand, he sat absorbed in worry: 'My household is endowed with abundant wealth, yet I have neither son nor daughter. After my death, all my property, being without an heir, will become the king's property.' He was told by ascetics, brahmins, soothsayers, friends, relatives, and kinsmen: 'Perform worship of the deities.' So he, sonless and longing for a son, made supplications to <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other various deities — garden deities, forest deities, crossroad deities, and intersection deities. He also supplicated innate, co-natured, and constantly accompanying deities. Now there is this common saying in the world: 'Through supplications, sons and daughters are born.' But that is not so. If it were so, each person would have a thousand sons, just like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). Rather, it is through the conjunction of three conditions that sons and daughters are born. What are the three? The mother and father are desirous and have come together, the mother is healthy and in her fertile season, and a <s>gandharva</s> (being to be reborn) is present. Through the conjunction of these three conditions, sons and daughters are born.
While he continued thus absorbed in supplications, a certain being, having departed from another group of beings, entered the womb of his wife. There are five distinguishing characteristics in a certain wise class of women. What are
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 253]

children.text: pañca? raktaṃ puruṣaṃ jānāti viraktaṃ {puruṣaṃ} jānāti | kālaṃ jānāti ṛtuṃ jānāti | garbham avakrāntaṃ jānāti | yasya sakāśād garbho 'vakrāmati taṃ jānāti | dārakaṃ jānāti dārikāṃ jānāti | saced dārako bhavati, dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | saced dārikā bhavati, vāmaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati | sā āttamanāttamanāḥ svāmina ārocayati: diṣṭyā āryaputra vardhase | āpannasatvāsmi saṃvṛttā | yathā ca me dakṣiṇaṃ kukṣiṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati, niyataṃ dārako bhaviṣyatīti | so 'py āttamanāttamanāḥ pūrvakāyam abhyunnamayya (Speyer: atyunnamayya) dakṣiṇaṃ bāhum abhiprasāryodānam udānayati: apy evāhaṃ cirakālābhilaṣitaṃ putramukhaṃ paśyeyam* | jāto me syān nāvajātaḥ | kṛtyāni me kurvīta | bhṛtaḥ pratibibhṛyāt* | dāyād yaṃ pratipadyeta | kulavaṃśo me cirasthitikaḥ syāt* | asmākaṃ cāpy atītakālagatānām alpaṃ vā prabhūtaṃ vā dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā mama nāmnā dakṣiṇām ādekṣyate: idaṃ tayor yatratatropapannayor gacchator anugacchatv iti | āpannasatvāṃ caināṃ viditvā upariprāsādatalagatām ayantritāṃ dhārayati, śīte śītopakaraṇair uṣṇe uṣṇopakaraṇair vaidyaprajñaptair āhārair nātitiktair nātyamlair nātilavaṇair nātimadhurair nātikaṭukair nātikaṣāyais tiktāmlalavaṇamadhurakaṭukakaṣāyavivarjitair āhāraiḥ | hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātrīm apsarasam iva nandanavanavicāriṇīṃ mañcān mañcaṃ pīṭhāt pīṭham anavatarantīm adharāṃ bhūmim* | na cāsyāḥ kiṃcid amanojñaśabdaśravaṇaṃ yāvad eva garbhasya paripākāya | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā gaṅgika iti nāma kṛtam* | gaṅgiko dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* ||
children.translated_text: the five? She knows when a man is passionate and when he is dispassionate. She knows the [right] time and knows the fertile season. She knows when conception has occurred. She knows from whom the conception comes. She knows whether it is a boy or a girl. If it is a boy, he rests against the right side of the womb; if a girl, against the left side.
