She, overjoyed, informed her husband: 'Congratulations, noble husband! I have become pregnant. And since the child rests against my right side, it will surely be a boy.' He too, overjoyed, raising his upper body and extending his right arm, uttered this <s>udāna</s> (joyful exclamation): 'May I at last see the long-desired face of a son! May he be born to me, not stillborn. May he fulfill my duties. May he, having been supported, support me in return. May he receive the inheritance. May my family lineage be long-lasting. And when we too have passed away, may someone, having given gifts great or small and having made merit in our name, dedicate the merit: "May this reach those two, wherever they have been reborn and gone."' And knowing her to be pregnant, he kept her on an upper story of the palace, unrestricted, providing her with appropriate provisions for cold and heat, and with foods prescribed by physicians — not too bitter, not too sour, not too salty, not too sweet, not too pungent, not too astringent, free of bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent [extremes]. Her limbs adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, like a celestial <s>Apsaras</s> wandering in the <s>Nandana</s> grove, she moved from couch to couch, from seat to seat, never descending to the lower floor. And she was protected from hearing any unpleasant sound, all for the maturation of the embryo. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, and pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs. At his birth, having held a birth-festival, the name <s>Gaṅgika</s> was given. The boy <s>Gaṅgika</s> was given to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nourished by the eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream, and other increasingly refined provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake.

children.text: sa ca nirbhedabhāgīyaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ samanvāgato gṛhāvāse nābhiramate | sa mātāpitarau pādayor nipatya vijñāpayati: amba tāta anujānītaṃ mām*, bhagavacchāsane pravrajiṣyāmīti | tato 'sya mātāpitarāv ekaputraka iti kṛtvā nānujānītaḥ | tato gaṅgikasya buddhir utpannā: durlabho manuṣyapratilābhaḥ, durlabhaś ca tathāgataprādurbhāvaḥ, tathendriyasaṃpad api durlabhā | ko me upāyo bhaved yad ahaṃ bhagavacchāsane pravrajeyam iti | tasyaitad abhavat*: yanv ahaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtvā ātmānamātmanā jīvitād vyaparopayeyam*, yathā manuṣyātvam āsādya laghu laghv eva pravrajeyam iti | tenaivaṃ vicintya viṣaṃ bhakṣitam*, na ca kālaṃ karoti | agnau patitaḥ, parvatād ātmānam utsṛṣṭavān*, nadyāṃ cārakāyāṃ patitaḥ, tatrāpi kālaṃ na karoti | tasya buddhir utpannā: kaḥ upāyaḥ syād yena kālaṃ kuryām iti | tasyaitad abhavat*: sarvathāyaṃ rājā ajātaśatruś caṇḍo rabhasaḥ karkaśaḥ sāhasikaś ca | yanv aham asya gṛhe rātrau saṃdhiṃ chindyām iti | sa rājagṛhaṃ nagaraṃ gatvā rātrau saṃprāptāyāṃ bhagne cakṣuṣpathe saṃdhim ārabdhaś chettum* | tato rakṣibhir jīvagrāhaṃ gṛhītvā rājño 'jātaśatror upanītaḥ: ayaṃ deva cauro duṣṭo 'pakārī ca, yo rājakule rātrau saṃdhiṃ chindatīti |
children.translated_text: And he, endowed with wholesome roots belonging to the penetrative class (<s>nirbhedabhāgīya</s>), found no delight in household life. He fell at his parents' feet and entreated them: 'Mother, father, give me permission! I shall go forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching.' But his parents, thinking, 'He is our only son,' did not give permission. Then this thought arose in <s>Gaṅgika</s>: 'A human birth is hard to obtain, the appearance of a <s>Tathāgata</s> is hard to come by, and likewise the full endowment of faculties is also rare. What means might there be for me to go forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching?' This occurred to him: 'What if I make an aspiration and take my own life, so that, having obtained human birth again, I may quickly, very quickly, go forth?' Having thought thus, he ate poison — but he did not die. He threw himself into fire, cast himself from a mountain, and threw himself into the river <s>Ārakā</s> — yet even there he did not die. Then this thought arose in him: 'What means might there be by which I could die?' This occurred to him: 'This King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> is in every way fierce, violent, harsh, and reckless. What if I were to break into his palace at night?' He went to the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, and when night had fallen and the range of sight was broken, he began to break through a wall. Then the guards seized him alive and brought him before King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'This, Your Majesty, is a wicked thief and criminal, who breaks into the royal palace at night.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 254]

children.text: tato rājñā aparādhika iti kṛtvā vadhya utsṛṣṭaḥ | tato vyadhyaghātair nīlāmbaravasanaiḥ karavīramālāsaktakaṇṭheguṇa udyataśastrapāṇibhī rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu śrāvaṇāmukheṣv anuśrāvya dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇa niṣkāsya śītavanaṃ śmaśānaṃ nīyate | sa nīyamānas tān vadhyaghātān āha: śīghraṃ śīghraṃ bhavanto gacchantu, mā kadācid rājñaś cittasyānyathātvaṃ syād iti | tato vyadhyaghātair eṣā pravṛttī rājño niveditā | tato rājñā pratinivartya pṛṣṭhaḥ: ko hetur yat tvam iṣṭaṃ jīvitaṃ parityaktum icchasīti | tena sa vṛttānto vistareṇa rājñe samākhyātaḥ | tato rājā ajātaśatruḥ kadambapuṣpavad āhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ sāśrukaṇṭho rudan mukha udānam udānayati: aho suparipakvā asya buddhisaṃtatiḥ, svavagataḥ saṃsāradoṣaḥ, supratilabdhā śraddhāsaṃpat*, yatra nāmāyaṃ pravrajyāhetor idam iṣṭaṃ jīvitaṃ parityaktuṃ vyavasitaḥ | tato rājñā samāśvāsyoktaḥ: putraka ahaṃ prabhus te jīvitasya | gacchedānīṃ bhagavacchāsane pravrajeti | sa rājñotsṛṣṭo bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, considering him a criminal, released him for execution. Then the executioners, clad in dark blue garments, with garlands of oleander hung around his neck, with weapons raised in their hands, having proclaimed [his crimes] at the thoroughfares, streets, squares, and intersections, and at the places of public announcement, led him out through the southern city gate toward the <s>Śītavana</s> (Cool Grove) cremation ground. As he was being led away, he said to those executioners: 'Go quickly, quickly, good sirs! Lest the king should change his mind!' Then the executioners reported this conduct to the king. Then the king, having had him brought back, asked: 'What is the reason that you wish to give up your dear life?' Then he told the king the whole story in detail. Then King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, his hair-pores bristling like <s>kadamba</s> flowers, his throat choked with tears, weeping, uttered this exclamation: 'Oh, how supremely ripened is his stream of understanding! The fault of <s>saṃsāra</s> is clearly perceived by him! Supremely gained is his endowment of faith, inasmuch as this man is determined to give up his dear life for the sake of going forth!' Then the king, having comforted him, said: 'Son, I am the master of your life. Go now, go forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching.' Released by the king, he went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (defilements), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of the hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāṃ śraddhāpravrajitānāṃ yaduta gaṅgiko vārāṇaseyaḥ śreṣṭhiputra iti ||
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'This one, monks, is foremost among my monk-disciples who have gone forth out of faith — namely, <s>Gaṅgika</s>, the guild-master's son of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta gaṅgikena karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenaiṣāṃ vipākān nāgniḥ kāye 'vakāśati, na viṣam*, na ca śastram*, nodakena kālaṃ karoti, arhatvaṃ cānena prāptam iti | bhagavān āha: gaṅgikenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | gaṅgikenaiva karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Gaṅgika</s> perform, that from the ripening of those deeds, fire did not affect his body, nor poison, nor weapons, nor did he die by water, and he attained <s>Arhatship</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Gaṅgika</s> himself, monks, who in former lives performed and accumulated deeds, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. It was <s>Gaṅgika</s> who performed and accumulated those deeds. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_98.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_98.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryām anyatamaḥ śmaśānamoṣako mātaṅgaḥ | yāvat tena pāthān hatvā bhāṇḍam āsāditam* | tatas tasya pṛṣṭhatas taskarāḥ pradhāvitāḥ | yāvad anyatamasmin śmaśāne pratyekabudho nirodhasamāpattiṃ samāpannaḥ | tato 'sau śmaśānamoṣako
children.translated_text: 'In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain <s>mātaṅga</s> (outcaste) who robbed cremation grounds. He killed some travelers and obtained their goods. Then robbers pursued him from behind. Now in a certain cremation ground, a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> had entered the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). Then that cremation-ground robber,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 255]

children.text: mātaṅgas tasya purastād bhāṇḍam apasṛjya tatraiva nilīnaḥ | tats te taskarāḥ pratyekabuddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā asyārabdhāḥ kṣeptuṃ śastram agniṃ ca | na cāsya cīvarakarṇakam api śaknuvanti cālayitum*, yasmād asau nirodhasamādhiṃ samāpannaḥ | yadā te taskarāḥ śrāntāḥ prakrāntāḥ, tadā sa pratyekabuddhaḥ krameṇa samādhivyutthitaḥ | tatas tena śmaśānamoṣakeṇa mātaṅgena taṃ pratyekabuddhaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syām*, yathā cāyam aparopakramaḥ | evam aham api yatra yatra jāyeya, tatra tatrāparopakramaḥ syām*, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: the <s>mātaṅga</s>, dropped his goods in front of that [<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>] and hid right there. Then those robbers, seeing the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, began to hurl weapons and fire at him. But they could not even move the corner of his robe, because he had entered the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamādhi</s>). When those robbers, exhausted, departed, that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> gradually emerged from his <s>samādhi</s>. Then that cremation-ground robber, the <s>mātaṅga</s>, having offered almsfood to that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, made an aspiration: 'May I too become one who attains such virtues! And just as this one is unassailable by others, may I too, wherever I may be born, be unassailable by others. And may I please a teacher even more distinguished than this one, and never displease him.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena śmaśānamoṣako mātaṅgaḥ, ayam sa gaṅgikaḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajito babhūva | tatrānena brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ | tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the cremation-ground robber, the <s>mātaṅga</s> — he is this <s>Gaṅgika</s>. Furthermore, he went forth under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There he maintained the life of celibacy. By that, he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourselves only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

children.text: AVŚ_99 dīrghanakhaḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_99: <s>Dīrghanakha</s> (Long-Nails). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text:
buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho rājagṛham upaniśritya viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe | tena khalu samayena nāladagrāmake tiṣyo nāma brāhmaṇaḥ | tena śārī nāma dārikā māṭharasakāśāl labdhā | yadā śāriputraḥ sārīkukṣim avakrāntaḥ, tadā bhrātrā saha dīrghanakhena vivādaṃ kurvantī nigrahasthānaṃ prāpayati | # # # # # # # | tato dīrghanakhena dakṣiṇāpathaṃ gatvā bahūni śāstrāṇy adhītāni |
  yāvat krameṇa śāriputro jātaḥ | tena dvir aṣṭavarṣeṇaindraṃ vyākaraṇam adhītam*, sarvavādinaś ca nigṛhītāḥ | so 'nupūrveṇa bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajitaḥ | yāvad dīrghanakhena pravrājakena śrutam*: bhāgineyena te sarve tīrthakarā nigṛhītāḥ | idānīṃ śramaṇagautamasya śiṣyatvam abhyupagata iti |
-------------------- Vaidya, p. 256 --------------------
children.translated_text:
The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, citizens, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus venerated by <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, renowned, of great merit, a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling near <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. At that time, in the village of <s>Nālada</s>, there was a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Tiṣya</s>. He obtained a girl named <s>Śārī</s> from <s>Māṭhara</s>. When <s>Śāriputra</s> entered <s>Śārī</s>'s womb, while debating with her brother <s>Dīrghanakha</s>, she would gain the upper hand. [Lacuna in text.] Then <s>Dīrghanakha</s>, having gone to the southern region (<s>Dakṣiṇāpatha</s>), studied many treatises.
In due course, <s>Śāriputra</s> was born. At the age of sixteen, he studied <s>Aindra</s> grammar and defeated all debaters. Eventually, he went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching. Then the wanderer <s>Dīrghanakha</s> heard: 'Your nephew has defeated all <s>tīrthaṅkaras</s> (founders of rival schools). He has now accepted discipleship under the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>.'
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 256]

children.text: śrutvā cāsya mahatī paribhavasaṃjñā utpannā, sarvaśāstreṣu cāsya anaiṣṭhikasaṃjñā utpannā | tataḥ kramaśo rājagṛham anuprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, a great sense of humiliation arose in him, and a conviction arose that all treatises are unreliable. Then he gradually arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

children.text:
tasmiṃś ca samaye bhagavān pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam* | śāriputro 'pi bhagavataḥ purastāt sthito 'bhūd vyajanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavanataṃ vījayan* | atha dadarśa dīrghanakhaparivrājako bhagavantam ardhacandrākāreṇopaviṣṭaṃ dharmaṃ deśayantam*, śāriputraṃ ca vyajanavyagrahastaṃ bhagavantaṃ vījayamānam* | dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavantam idam avocat*: sarvaṃ me bho gautama na kṣamata iti | bhagavān āha: eṣāpi te agnivaiśyāyana dṛṣṭir na kṣamate, yeyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ: sarvaṃ me na kṣamata iti | eṣāpi me bho gautama dṛṣṭir na kṣamate, yeyaṃ me dṛṣṭiḥ: sarvaṃ me na kṣamata iti | api tu te agnivaiśyāyana evaṃ jānato 'yāś ca dṛṣṭeḥ prahāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati pratinisargo vāntībhāvaḥ; anyasyāś ca dṛṣṭer apratisaṃdhir anupādānam aprādurbhāvaḥ? api me bho gautama evaṃ jānata evaṃ paśyato 'syāś ca dṛṣṭeḥ prahāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati pratinisargo vāntībhāvaḥ anyasyāś ca dṛṣṭer apratisaṃdhir anupādānam aprādurbhāvaḥ | bahujanena te agnivaiśyāyana na saṃsyandiṣyati (Speyer: saṃsyadiṣyati) | # # # # # # ima ucyante tanubhyas tanutarāḥ | loke traya ime agnivaiśyāyana dṛṣṭisaṃniśrayāḥ | katame trayaḥ? ihāgnivaiśyāyana eka evaṃdṛṣṭir bhavati evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me kṣamata iti | punar aparam ihaika evaṃdṛṣṭir bhavati evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me na kṣamata iti | punar aparam eka evaṃdṛṣṭir bhavati evaṃvādī: evaṃ me kṣamate, ekaṃ na me kṣamata iti | tatrāgnivaiśyāyana yeyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ sarvaṃ me kṣamata iti, iyṃ dṛṣṭiḥ saṃrāgāya saṃvartate nāsaṃrāgāya, saṃdveṣāya nāsaṃdveṣāya, saṃmohāya nāsaṃmohāya, saṃyogāya nāsaṃyogāya, saṃkleśāya na vyavadānāya, saṃcayāya nāpacayāya, abhinandanāyopādānāya adhyavasānāya saṃvartate | tatrāgnivaiśyāyana yeyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ: sarvaṃ me na kṣamata iti, iyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ asaṃrāgāya saṃvartate na saṃrāgāya, asaṃdveṣāya na saṃdveṣāya, asaṃmohāya na saṃmohāya, visaṃyogāya na saṃyogāya, vyavadānāya na saṃkleśāya, asaṃcayāya na saṃcayāya | anabhinandanāyānupādānāya anadhyavasānāya
saṃvartate | tatra yeyaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ: ekaṃ me kṣamate, ekaṃ me na kṣamata iti, yat tāvad asya kṣamate, tat saṃrāgāya saṃdveṣāya saṃmohāya saṃyogāya saṃkleśāya, na vyavadānāya nāpacayāya | abhinandanāyopādānāya adhyavasānāya saṃvartate | yad asya na kṣamate, tad asaṃrāgāya saṃvartate na saṃrāgāya, asaṃdveṣāya na saṃdveṣāya, asaṃmohāya na saṃmohāya, asaṃyogāya na saṃyogāya, vyavadānāya na saṃkleśāya, apacayāya na saṃcayāya | anabhinandanāyānupādānāya anadhyavasānāya saṃvartate |
  tatrā śrutavān āryaśrāvaka idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣyate: ahaṃ caivaṃdṛṣṭiḥ syām*, evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me kṣamate | dvābhyāṃ me sārdhaṃ syād vigrahaḥ syād vivādaḥ | yaś ca evaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me na kṣamata iti, yaś ca evaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādi: ekaṃ me kṣamate ekaṃ me na kṣamata iti | vigrahe sati vivādaḥ, vivāde sati vihiṃsā | iti sa tāṃ savigrahāṃ savivādāṃ savihiṃsāṃ ca samanupaśyann
children.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having arisen from meditation, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> most sweetly to the four assemblies, like pure honey without beeswax. <s>Śāriputra</s> also stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, holding a fan and fanning the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the wanderer <s>Dīrghanakha</s> (Long-Nails) saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> seated in the half-moon formation teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Śāriputra</s> fanning the <s>Bhagavān</s> with fan in hand. Having seen him, he addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Master <s>Gautama</s>, nothing is acceptable to me." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "<s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, is this view of yours also not acceptable — this very view that 'nothing is acceptable to me'?" "Master <s>Gautama</s>, this view of mine is also not acceptable — this very view that 'nothing is acceptable to me.'" "But, <s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, for one who knows thus, will there be abandonment of this view, its relinquishment, its being vomited up, and non-connection with another view, non-grasping, non-arising?" "Indeed, Master <s>Gautama</s>, for one knowing thus and seeing thus, there will be abandonment of this view, its relinquishment, its being vomited up, and non-connection with another view, non-grasping, non-arising." "<s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, many will not agree with you. [Textual lacuna] These are said to be thinner than thin. <s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, there are these three bases of views in the world. Which three? Here, <s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, one has this view and makes this assertion: 'Everything is acceptable to me.' Again, another has this view and makes this assertion: 'Nothing is acceptable to me.' Again, another has this view and makes this assertion: 'Some things are acceptable to me, some are not acceptable to me.' Therein, <s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, the view 'everything is acceptable to me' — this view tends toward attachment, not non-attachment; toward hatred, not non-hatred; toward delusion, not non-delusion; toward bondage, not freedom; toward defilement, not purification; toward accumulation, not diminution; it tends toward delight, grasping, and adherence. Therein, <s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, the view 'nothing is acceptable to me' — this view tends toward non-attachment, not attachment; toward non-hatred, not hatred; toward non-delusion, not delusion; toward freedom, not bondage; toward purification, not defilement; toward diminution, not accumulation;
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 257]

children.text: imāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ pratinisṛjati, anyāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ nopādatte | evam asyāś ca dṛṣṭeḥ prahāṇaṃ bhavati pratinisargo vāntībhāvaḥ, anyasyāś ca dṛṣṭer apratisaṃdhir anupādānam aprādurbhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he relinquishes this view and does not take up another view. Thus there is abandonment of this view, its relinquishment, its being vomited up, and non-connection with another view, non-grasping, non-arising.

children.text: tatra śrutavān āryaśrāvaka idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣyate: ahaṃ ced evaṃdṛṣṭiḥ syām evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me na kṣamata iti, dvābhyāṃ me sārdhaṃ syād vigrahaḥ, syād vivādaḥ | yaś ca evaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me kṣamata iti, yaś ca evaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādi: ekaṃ me kṣamate ekaṃ me na kṣamata iti | vigrahe sati vivādaḥ, vivāde sati vihiṃsā, iti sa tāṃ savigrahāṃ savivādāṃ savihiṃsāṃ ca samanupaśyann imāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ pratinisṛjati, anyāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ nopādatte | evam asyāś ca dṛṣṭeḥ prahāṇaṃ bhavati pratinisargo vāntībhāvaḥ | anyasyāś ca dṛṣṭer apratisaṃdhir anupādānam aprādurbhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therein, a learned noble disciple reflects thus: 'If I were to hold this view and make this assertion: "nothing is acceptable to me," I would have conflict with two others — with one who holds the view and asserts "everything is acceptable to me," and with one who holds the view and asserts "some things are acceptable to me, some are not." Where there is conflict, there is dispute; where there is dispute, there is harm.' Thus, seeing this view as involving conflict, dispute, and harm, he relinquishes this view and does not take up another view. Thus there is abandonment of this view, its relinquishment, its being vomited up,

<tatra śrutavān āryaśrāvaka idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣyate: ahaṃ ced evamdṛṣṭiḥ syām evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me na kṣamata iti, dvābhyāṃ me sārdhaṃ syād vigrahaḥ, syād vivādaḥ | yaś caivaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me kṣamata iti, yaś ca evaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādi: ekaṃ me kṣamate ekaṃ me na kṣamate iti | vigrahe sati vivādaḥ, vivāde sati vihiṃsā, iti sa tāṃ savigrahāṃ savivādāṃ savihiṃsāṃ ca samanupaśyann imāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ pratinisṛjati, anyāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ nopādatte | evam asyāś ca dṛṣṭeḥ prahāṇaṃ bhavati pratinisargo vāntībhāvaḥ | anyasyāś ca dṛṣṭer apratisaṃdhir anupādānam aprādurbhāvaḥ ||>
  tatra śrutavān āryaśrāvaka idaṃ pratisaṃśikṣyate: ahaṃ ced evamdṛṣṭiḥ syām evaṃvādī: ekaṃ me kṣamate, ekaṃ me na kṣamata iti, dvābhyāṃ me sārdhaṃ syād vigrahaḥ, syād vivādaḥ | yaś caivaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādī: sarvaṃ me kṣamata iti, yaś ca evaṃdṛṣṭir evaṃvādi: sarvaṃ me na kṣamate iti | vigrahe sati vivādaḥ, vivāde sati vihiṃsā, iti sa tāṃ savigrahāṃ savivādāṃ savihiṃsāṃ ca samanupaśyann imāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ pratinisṛjati, anyāṃ ca dṛṣṭiṃ nopādatte | evam asyāś ca dṛṣṭeḥ prahāṇaṃ bhavati pratinisargo vāntībhāvaḥ | anyasyāś ca dṛṣṭer apratisaṃdhir anupādānam aprādurbhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therein, a learned noble disciple reflects thus: 'If I were to hold this view and make this assertion: "nothing is acceptable to me," I would have conflict with two others — with one who holds the view and asserts "everything is acceptable to me," and with one who holds the view and asserts "some things are acceptable to me, some are not." Where there is conflict, there is dispute; where there is dispute, there is harm.' Thus, seeing this view as involving conflict, dispute, and harm, he relinquishes this view and does not take up another view. Thus there is abandonment of this view, its relinquishment, its being vomited up, and non-connection with another view, non-grasping, non-arising.

children.text: ayaṃ khalv agnivaiśyāyana kāyo rūpī audārikaś cāturmahābhūtika iti āryaśrāvakeṇa abhīkṣṇam udayavyayānudarśinā vihartavyam*, virāgānudarśinā pratinisargānudarśinā vihartavyam* | yatrāryaśrāvakasya abhīkṣṇam udayavyayānudarśino viharataḥ, yo 'sya bhavati kāye kāyacchandaḥ kāyasnehaḥ kāyapremā kāyālayaḥ kāyaviṣaktiḥ kāyādhyavasānam*, tac cāsya cittaṃ na paryādāya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>, this body is material, gross, composed of the four great elements. A noble disciple should dwell constantly observing arising and passing away, observing dispassion, observing relinquishment. When a noble disciple dwells constantly observing arising and passing away, whatever desire for the body, attachment to the body, love for the body, clinging to the body, fixation on the body, or adherence to the body he may have — that does not take hold of his mind.

children.text: tisra imā agnivaiśyāyana vedanāḥ | katamās tisraḥ? sukhā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca | yasmin samaye śrutavān āryaśrāvakaḥ sukhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate, dve asya vedane tasmin samaye niruddhe bhavataḥ: duḥkhā ca aduḥkhāsukhā ca | sukhām eva ca tasmin samaye āryaśrāvako vedanāṃ vedayate | sukhāpi ca vedanā anityā nirodhadharmiṇī | yasmin samaye āryaśrāvako duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate, dve asya vedane tasmin samaye niruddhe bhavataḥ, sukhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca | duḥkhām eva ca tasmin samaye āryaśrāvako vedanāṃ vedayate | duḥkhāpi vedanā anityā nirodhadharmiṇī | yasmin samaye āryaśrāvako aduḥkhāsukhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayate, dve asya vedane tasmin samaye niruddhe bhavataḥ, sukhā duḥkhā ca | aduḥkhāsukhām eva ca tasmin samaye āryaśrāvako vedanāṃ vedayate | aduḥkhāsukhāpi vedanā anityā nirodhadharmiṇī | tasyaivaṃ bhavati: imā vedanāḥ kiṃnidānāḥ kiṃsamudayāḥ kiṃjātīyāḥ kiṃprabhāvā iti? imā vedanā sparśanidānāḥ sparśasamudayāḥ sparśajātīyāḥ sparśaprabhāvāḥ | tasya sparśasya samudayāt tās tā vedanāḥ samudayante
children.translated_text: There are these three feelings, <s>Agnivaiśyāyana</s>. Which three? Pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant. At the time when a learned noble disciple experiences a pleasant feeling, at that time two feelings are ceased for him: the painful and the neither-painful-nor-pleasant. At that time the noble disciple experiences only a pleasant feeling. But even a pleasant feeling is impermanent and subject to cessation. At the time when a noble disciple experiences a painful feeling, at that time two feelings are ceased for him: the pleasant and the neither-painful-nor-pleasant. At that time the noble disciple experiences only a painful feeling.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 258]

children.text: tasya sparśasya nirodhāt tās tā vedanā nirudhyante, vyupaśāmyanti śītībhavanti astaṃgacchanti | sa yāṃ kāṃcid vedanāṃ vedayate sukhāṃ vā duḥkhāṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhā vā, tāsāṃ vedanānāṃ samudayaṃ cāstaṃgamaṃ cāsvādaṃ cādīnavaṃ ca niḥsaraṇaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāmīti, tasya vedanānāṃ samudayaṃ cāstaṃgamaṃ cāsvādaṃ cādīnavaṃ ca niḥsaraṇaṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānata utpannāsu vedanāsv anityatānudarśī viharati, vyayānudarśī virāgānudarśī nirodhānudarśī pratisargānudarśī | sa kāyaparyantikāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānaḥ kāyaparyantikāṃ vedanāṃ vedaya iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | jīvitaparyantikāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamāno jīvitaparyantikāṃ vedanāṃ vedaya iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | bhedāc ca kāyasyorddhvaṃ jīvitaparyādānād ihaivāsya sarvāṇi vedanāni apariśeṣaṃ nirudhyante apariśeṣam astaṃ parikṣayaṃ paryādānaṃ gacchanti | tasyaivaṃ bhavati: sukhām api vedanāṃ vedayato bhedaḥ kāyasya bhaviṣyati | eṣa evānto duḥkhasya | duḥkhām api, aduḥkhāsukhām api vedanāṃ vedayato bhedaḥ kāyasya bhaviṣyati | eṣa evānto duḥkhasya | sa sukhām api vedanāṃ vedayate, visaṃyukto vedayate, na saṃyuktaḥ | duḥkhām api aduḥkhāsukhām api vedanāṃ vedayate, visaṃyukto vedayate, na saṃyuktaḥ | kena visaṃyuktaḥ? visaṃyukto rāgeṇa dveṣeṇa mohena, visaṃyukto jātijarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ, visaṃyukto duḥkhād iti vadāmi ||
children.translated_text: With the cessation of that contact, those various feelings cease, subside, become cool, and disappear. Whatever feeling he experiences — whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — he understands as it truly is the arising, passing away, gratification, danger, and escape regarding those feelings. Understanding as it truly is the arising, passing away, gratification, danger, and escape regarding those feelings, when feelings arise he dwells observing impermanence, observing dissolution, observing dispassion, observing cessation, observing relinquishment. He experiences a feeling limited to the body,

children.text: tena khalu samayena āyuṣmāñ śāriputro 'rdhamāsopasaṃpanno bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sthito 'bhūd vyajanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavantaṃ vījayan* | āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat*: bhagavāṃs teṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇam eva varṇayati, virāgam eva nirodham eva pratiniḥsargam eva varṇayati | yanv ahaṃ teṣāṃ teṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇānudarśī vihareyam*, virāgānudarśī nirodhānudarśī vihareyam*, pratiniḥsargānudarśī vihareyam iti | āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaiṣāṃ dharmāṇām anityatānudarśino viharato vyayānudarśino virāgānudarśino nirodhānudarśinaḥ pratiniḥsargānudarśino viharataḥ anupādāya āsravebhyaś cittaṃ vimuktam* | dīrghanakhasya ca parivrājakasya virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur utpannam* ||
children.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, who had received full ordination half a month earlier, stood behind the Blessed One, holding a fan, fanning the Blessed One. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thought: 'The Blessed One praises only the abandonment of those <s>dharmas</s>, only dispassion, only cessation, only relinquishment. Let me dwell contemplating the abandonment of those various <s>dharmas</s>, contemplating dispassion, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment.' As the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> dwelt contemplating the impermanence of those <s>dharmas</s>, contemplating decay, contemplating dispassion, contemplating cessation, contemplating relinquishment, his mind was liberated from the <s>āsravas</s> (taints) without clinging. And in the wanderer <s>Dīrghanakha</s>, the stainless, spotless <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (eye of the <s>Dharma</s>) arose with regard to <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: atha dīrghanakhaḥ parivrājako dṛṣṭadharmā prāptadharmā paryavagāḍhadharmā tīrṇakāṅkṣas tīrṇavicikitso 'parapratyayo 'nanyaneyaḥ śāstuḥ śāsane (Speyer: śāstraśasane) dharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāpta utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat | lābheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam* | careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam* | labdhavān dīrghanakhaparivrājakaḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam* | evaṃ pravrajitaḥ sa āyuṣmān eko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramatta ātāpī prahitātmā vyahārṣīt* | eko vyapakṛṣṭo 'pramatta ātāpī prahitātmā viharan* yad arthaṃ kulaputrāḥ keśaśmaśru avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajanti, tad anuttaraṃ brahmacaryaparyavasānaṃ
children.translated_text: Then the wanderer <s>Dīrghanakha</s> — having seen the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, having plunged into the <s>Dharma</s>, having crossed beyond doubt, having crossed beyond uncertainty, independent of others, not to be led by others, having attained confidence in the Teacher's teaching with regard to <s>dharmas</s> — rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and said this to the Blessed One: 'May I obtain, Venerable Sir, ordination, full ordination, and monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May I practice the holy life in the Blessed One's presence.' The wanderer <s>Dīrghanakha</s> obtained ordination, full ordination, and monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. Having thus gone forth, the venerable one, dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, exerted himself. Dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute — for the purpose of which sons of good families, having shaved off their hair and beard, donning saffron robes, go forth from the household to homelessness with perfect faith — that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 259]

children.text: dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñayā sākṣātkṛtvā pratipadya pravedayate: kṣīṇā me jātiḥ, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ, kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti | ājñātavān sa āyuṣmān arhan babhūva suvimuktacittaḥ | tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: eṣo 'gro me bhikṣavo bhikṣūṇāṃ mama śrāvakāṇāṃ pratisaṃvitprāptānāṃ yaduta koṣṭhilo bhikṣur iti ||
children.translated_text: he directly realized in this very life, through his own higher knowledge, and having attained it, he declared: 'Destroyed is birth for me, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, I know of no further existence beyond this.' The venerable one became a knower, an <s>Arhat</s>, with a well-liberated mind. Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'This one, monks, is foremost among my monk-disciples who have attained the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) — namely, the monk <s>Koṣṭhila</s>.'

children.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kāni bhadanta mahākoṣṭhilena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni, yena mahāvādī saṃvṛttaḥ | pravrajya cārhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti | bhagavān āha: koṣṭhilenaiva bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | koṣṭhilena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: The monks, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the cutter of all doubts: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Mahākoṣṭhila</s> perform and accumulate that he became a great debater, and having gone forth, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'By <s>Koṣṭhila</s> himself, monks, in former lives, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Koṣṭhila</s> deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, not in the water element, not in the fire element, not in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: 'Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_99.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings.' // AVŚ_99.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ pañcamātrāṇi taskaraśatāni senāpatipramukhāṇi cauryeṇa saṃprasthitāni | yāvat te cañcūryamāṇā anyatamaṃ khadiravaṇam anuprāptāḥ | yāvat senāpatinābhihitāḥ: paśyata yūyaṃ kamalāyatākṣaḥ kaścid aparakīyo manuṣyaḥ saṃvidyate, yena vayaṃ yakṣabaliṃ datvā prakrāmemeti | tatra ca khadiravane pratyekabuddhaḥ prativasati | tatas tais taskaraiḥ paryaṭadbhir dṛṣṭvā senāpatisakāśaṃ nītaḥ | tataś caurasenāpatinā vadhyatām ayam ity ājñā dattā | tato 'sau pratyekabuddhas teṣām anugrahārthaṃ vitatapakṣa iva haṃsarājaḥ khagapatham abhyudgamya vicitrāṇi prātihāryāṇi vidarśayitum ārabdhaḥ | tataḥ senāpatir mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya atyayaṃ deśitavān* | piṇḍakena pratipādya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtavān*: aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syām*, prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, monks, in a past age, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, five hundred robbers, led by their chief, set out on a raid. While prowling about, they reached a certain <s>khadira</s> (acacia) forest. Then the chief said: 'Look around and see whether there is some stranger, some other person, so that having offered him as a <s>yakṣa</s>-sacrifice, we may proceed.' Now in that <s>khadira</s> forest there dwelt a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. The robbers, while wandering about, discovered him and brought him before the chief. Then the robber-chief gave the order: 'Let this one be slain.' Then that <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, for the sake of benefiting them, like a king of geese with wings outspread, rose up into the sky and began to display various miraculous feats. Then the chief, falling at his feet like a tree cut at the root, confessed his transgression. Having offered him alms-food, he made this aspiration: 'May I too become a recipient of such virtues, and may I please a teacher even more distinguished than this one, and never displease him.'

children.text: bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena caurasenāpatiḥ, ayam evāsau koṣṭhilaḥ | bhūyaḥ kāśyape bhagavati pravrajito babhūva | tatrānena daśa varṣasahasrāṇi brahmacaryavāsaḥ paripālitaḥ | tenedānīm arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the robber-chief — he is this very <s>Koṣṭhila</s>. Furthermore, he went forth under the Blessed One <s>Kāśyapa</s>. There he maintained the life of celibacy for ten thousand years. By that he has now directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Therefore, monks, entirely dark deeds have entirely dark results; entirely bright deeds have entirely bright results; mixed deeds have mixed results. Therefore, monks, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, one should devote oneself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: idam avocad bhagavān* | āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan* ||
children.translated_text: This is what the Blessed One said. Those monks, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 260]

children.text: AVŚ_100 saṃgītiḥ | (ed. Speyer, vol. II)
children.translated_text: AVŚ_100: <s>Saṃgīti</s> (The Recitation). (ed. Speyer, vol. II)

children.text: buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājamātrair dhanibhiḥ pauraiḥ śreṣṭhibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣair asurair garuḍaiḥ kinnarair mahoragair iti devanāgayakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragābhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyo lābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ kuśinagaryāṃ viharati mallānām upavartane yamakaśālavane | atha bhagavāṃs tad eva parinirvāṇakālasamaye āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma: prajñāpaya ānanda tathāgatasya āntareṇa yamakaśālayor uttarāśirasaṃ mañcam* | adya tathāgatasya rātryā madhyame yāme nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya antareṇa yamakaśālayor uttarāśirasaṃ mañcaṃ prajñāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthāt* | ekāntasthita āyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam idam avocat*: prajñapto bhadanta tathāgatasya antareṇa yamakaśālayor uttarāśirasaṃ mañcaḥ | atha bhagavān* yena mañcas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya dakṣiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati pādaṃ pādenopadhāya ālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan nirvāṇasaṃjñām eva manasi kurvann iti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped by kings, princes, the wealthy, townsfolk, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — thus worshipped by gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s> — the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, known [as one] of great merit, a recipient of robes, alms-food, bedding-and-seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, together with the community of disciples, was dwelling at <s>Kuśinagarī</s>, at the <s>Upavartana</s> of the <s>Mallas</s>, in the <s>Yamakaśālavana</s> (Grove of Twin <s>Śāla</s> Trees). Then the Blessed One, at the very time of his <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Prepare, <s>Ānanda</s>, between the twin <s>Śāla</s> trees, a couch with the head facing north for the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Today, during the middle watch of the night, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> will take place in the <s>Nirvāṇadhātu</s> without remainder.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> replied to the Blessed One, and having prepared between the twin <s>Śāla</s> trees a couch with the head facing north, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'The couch has been prepared between the twin <s>Śāla</s> trees, Venerable Sir, with the head facing north for the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then the Blessed One approached the couch. Having approached, he lay down on his right side, placing one foot upon the other, mindful with the perception of light, fully aware, keeping in mind the perception of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: tatra bhagavān rātryā madhyame yāme 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ | samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūt* ulkāpātā diśodāhāḥ | antarīkṣe devadundubhayo nadanti | samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati ubhau yamakaśālavanasya drumottamau tathāgatasya siṃhaśayyāṃ śālapuṣpair avākiratām* | samanantaraparinirvṛte bhagavati anyataro bhikṣus tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: There, during the middle watch of the night, the Blessed One passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇadhātu</s> without remainder. Immediately upon the passing of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, at that very moment there was a great earthquake, meteor showers, and blazes on the horizon. In the sky, divine drums resounded. Immediately upon the passing of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, both supreme trees of the twin <s>Śāla</s> grove showered <s>Śāla</s> blossoms upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lion-couch. Immediately upon the passing of the Blessed One, a certain monk, at that moment, spoke this verse:

children.text: sundarau khalv imau śālavanasyāsya drumottamau |
children.translated_text: 'Beautiful indeed are these two supreme trees of the <s>Śāla</s> grove,

children.text: yad avākiratāṃ puṣpaiḥ śāstāraṃ parinirvṛtam* || AVŚ_100.1 ||
children.translated_text: which showered blossoms upon the Teacher who had passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.' // AVŚ_100.1 //

children.text: samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati śakro devendro gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Immediately upon the passing of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, spoke this verse:

children.text:
anityā bata saṃskārā utpādavyayadharmiṇaḥ |
  utpadya hi nirudhyante teṣāṃ vyupaśamaḥ sukham* || AVŚ_100.2 || iti
children.translated_text:
'Impermanent indeed are <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations), subject to arising and decay;
having arisen, they cease — their pacification is happiness.' // AVŚ_100.2 //

children.text: samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati brahmā sahāṃpatir gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Immediately upon the passing of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Sahāṃpati</s> spoke this verse:

children.text: sarvabhūtāni loke 'sminn ikṣepsyanti samucchrayam* |
children.translated_text: 'All beings in this world will relinquish their body;

children.text: evaṃvidho yatra śāstā lokeṣv apratipudgalaḥ |
children.translated_text: when such a Teacher, unequaled in the worlds,

children.text: tathāgatabalaprāptaḥ cakṣumān parinirvṛtaḥ || AVŚ_100.3 ||
children.translated_text: endowed with the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers, the one possessing the [<s>Dharma</s>-]eye, has passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.' // AVŚ_100.3 //

children.text: samanantaraparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati āyuṣmān āniruddho gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Immediately upon the passing of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> spoke this verse:

children.text: sthitā āśvāsapraśvāsā sthiracittasya tāyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Stilled were the in-breaths and out-breaths of the Protector, whose mind was steady;

children.text: ānijyāṃ śāntim āgamya cakṣumān parinirvṛtaḥ || AVŚ_100.4 ||
children.translated_text: having attained the imperturbable peace, the one possessing the [<s>Dharma</s>-]eye has passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>.' // AVŚ_100.4 //
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 261]

children.text: tadābhavad bhīṣaṇakaṃ tadābhūd romaharṣaṇam* |
children.translated_text: 'Then there was terror, then there was hair-raising dread,

children.text: sarvākārabalopetaḥ śāstā kālaṃ yadākarot* || AVŚ_100.5 ||
children.translated_text: when the Teacher, endowed with powers of every kind, passed away.' // AVŚ_100.5 //

children.text:
asaṃlīnena cittena vedanā adhivāsayan* |
  pradyotasy eva nirvāṇaṃ vimokṣas tasya cetasaḥ || AVŚ_100.6 || iti ||
children.translated_text:
'With an unshrunken mind, enduring feelings,
like the extinguishing of a lamp — such was the liberation of his mind.' // AVŚ_100.6 //

children.text: saptāhaparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataś citāṃ pradakṣiṇīkurvan* gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Seven days after the passing of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, circumambulating the funeral pyre of the Blessed One, spoke this verse:

children.text: yena kāyaratanena nāyako brahmalokam agaman maharddhikaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'That jeweled body, with which the Leader, of great supernatural power, went to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> —

children.text: dahyate sma tanujena tejasā pañcabhir yugaśataiḥ sa veṣṭitaḥ (Speyer: veṣṭhitaḥ) || AVŚ_100.7 ||
children.translated_text: that body, born of a [mortal] frame, was consumed by fire, wrapped in five hundred [layers of cloth].' // AVŚ_100.7 //

children.text: sahasramātreṇa hi cīvarāṇāṃ buddhasya kāyaḥ pariveṣṭito 'bhūt* | (Speyer: pariveṣṭhito)
dve cīvare tatra tu naiva dagdhe abhyantaraṃ bāhyam atha dvitīyam* || AVŚ_100.8 ||
children.translated_text: two of those cloths were not burned — the innermost and the outermost.' // AVŚ_100.8 //
'The <s>Buddha</s>'s body was wrapped in a thousand pieces of cloth;

children.text: varṣaśataparinirvṛte buddhe bhagavati pāṭaliputre nagare rājā aśoko rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamaraṃ taskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannam* | dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ pālayati | yāvad apareṇa samayena devyā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati | tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa devī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā | sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā | dārako jāto abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ kuṇālasadṛśābhyāṃ netrābhyām* | tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti | jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya jātamātrasya kuṇālasadṛśe netre, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya kuṇāla iti nāmeti | kuṇālo dārako 'ṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām* | so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣaiḥ | āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam* | tatas taṃ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitaṃ rājā utsaṅgena kṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ prekṣya rūpasaṃpadā praharṣita uvāca: asadṛśo me putro loke rūpeṇeti ||
children.translated_text: A hundred years after the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, had passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, King <s>Aśoka</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with a great multitude of people, with quarrels, disputes, tumults, and disturbances pacified, free from robbers and disease, rich in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. A righteous king, a <s>Dharmarāja</s>, he ruled the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>. On a later occasion, he sported, delighted, and amused himself with his queen. As he sported, delighted, and amused himself, in the course of time the queen became pregnant. After the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, and graceful, with eyes resembling [those of] a <s>kuṇāla</s> bird. At his birth, having held a birth-festival, a name was determined: 'What shall be the boy's name?' The kinsmen said: 'Since the moment he was born his eyes resembled those of a <s>kuṇāla</s> bird, let the boy's name be <s>Kuṇāla</s>.' The boy <s>Kuṇāla</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. He was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses, nourished on milk, curds, butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other excellent and choice provisions. He grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond. Then King [<s>Aśoka</s>], having placed him adorned with all ornaments upon his lap and gazing at him again and again, delighted by the perfection of his beauty, said: 'My son is unequaled in the world in beauty!'

children.text: tatra ca samaye gāndhāre puṣpabherotso nāma grāmaḥ | tatrānyatamasya gṛhapateḥ putro jāto 'tikrānto mānuṣaṃ varṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇam* | janmani cāsya divyagandhodakaparipūrṇā
children.translated_text: Now at that time, in <s>Gāndhāra</s>, there was a village called <s>Puṣpabherotsa</s>. There, to a certain householder, a son was born who had surpassed the human complexion but had not yet attained the divine complexion. And at his birth, a jeweled lotus-pool filled with divinely fragrant water appeared,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 262]

children.text: ratnamayī puṣkariṇī prādurbhūtā, puṣpasaṃpannaṃ ca mahad udyānaṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca | yatra yatra kumāro gacchati tatra tatra ca puṣkariṇī udyānaṃ ca prādurbhavati | tasya sundara iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam* ||
children.translated_text: as well as a great garden abounding in flowers — and a moving one at that. Wherever the boy went, there the lotus-pool and garden would appear. His name was established as <s>Sundara</s> (Beautiful).

children.text: yāvat krameṇa kumāro mahān saṃvṛttam* | tato 'pareṇa samayena puṣpabherotsād vaṇijaḥ kenacid eva karaṇīyena pāṭaliputraṃ gatāḥ | te prābhṛtam ādāya rājñaḥ sakāśam upagatāḥ | tataḥ pādayor nipatya prābhṛtaṃ rājñe upanamayya purastād vyavasthitāḥ | tato rājā aśokas teṣāṃ kuṇālaṃ darśayati: haṃ bho vaṇijaḥ, kadācit kutracid bhavadbhiḥ paryaṭadbhir evaṃvidhaṃ rūpaviśeṣayuktaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvam iti ? tatas te vaṇijaḥ kṛtakarapuṭāḥ pādayor nipatya abhayaṃ mārgayitvā rājānam ūcuḥ: asti deva asmadīye viṣaye sundaro nāma kumāro 'tikrānto mānuṣaṃ varṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ varṇam* | janmani cāsya divyagandhodakaparipūrṇā ratnamayī puṣkariṇī prādurbhūtā, puṣpaphalasamṛddhaṃ ca mahad udyānaṃ jaṅgamam* | yatra yatra ca kumāro gacchati tatra tatra puṣkariṇī udyānaṃ ca prādurbhavati | śrutvā rājā aśokaḥ paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ | kutūhalajātaś ca dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ kṛtavān: eṣa rājā aśoka āgantum icchati sundarasya kumārasya darśanahetoḥ | yad vaḥ kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tat kurudhvam iti | tato mahājanakāyo bhītāḥ: yadi rājā mahāsādhanena ihāgamiṣyati, mā haiva kaṃcid anartham utpādayiṣyatīti | tataḥ sa kumāro bhadrayānaṃ yojayitvā śatasahasraṃ ca muktāhāraṃ prābhṛtasyārthe datvā aśokasya sakāśaṃ preṣitaḥ | so 'nupūrveṇa cañcūryamāṇaḥ pāṭaliputraṃ nagaraṃ prāptaḥ | śatasahasraṃ ca muktāhāraṃ gṛhītvā rājño 'śokasya sakāśam anuprāptaḥ | rājā aśokaś ca sahadarśanāt sundarasya kumārasya rūpaṃ śobhāṃ varṇapuṣkalatāṃ ca divyāṃ puṣkariṇīm udyānaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: In due course, when the boy had grown up, on a later occasion, merchants from <s>Puṣpabherotsa</s> went to <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> on some business. Taking a tribute-gift, they went into the king's presence. Falling at his feet and presenting the tribute to the king, they stood before him. Then King <s>Aśoka</s> showed them <s>Kuṇāla</s>: 'Well, merchants! Have you, in all your travels, ever seen anyone endowed with such extraordinary beauty as this?' Then those merchants, with palms joined, falling at his feet, having begged for assurance of safety, said to the king: 'There is, Sire, in our territory, a boy named <s>Sundara</s> who has surpassed the human complexion but has not yet attained the divine complexion. At his birth, a jeweled lotus-pool filled with divinely fragrant water appeared, and a great garden abounding in flowers and fruit — a moving one. Wherever the boy goes, there the lotus-pool and garden appear.' Hearing this, King <s>Aśoka</s> was filled with the utmost astonishment. Seized with curiosity, he dispatched a messenger: 'King <s>Aśoka</s> wishes to come for the purpose of seeing the boy <s>Sundara</s>. Do whatever you must.' Then the great populace became frightened: 'If the king comes here with great force, he might cause some harm.' Then the boy [<s>Sundara</s>], having yoked an excellent carriage and giving a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [coins] as a tribute-gift, was sent to <s>Aśoka</s>'s presence. Traveling by stages, he arrived at the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. Taking the pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, he came before King <s>Aśoka</s>. And King <s>Aśoka</s>, the moment he saw the boy <s>Sundara</s>'s beauty, splendor, excellence of complexion, the divine lotus-pool, and the garden, was filled with the utmost astonishment.

children.text: tato rājā aśokaḥ sthaviropaguptasya vismayajananārthaṃ sundaraṃ ca kumāram ādāya kukkuṭāgāraṃ gataḥ | tatropaguptapramukhāṇy aṣṭādaśārhatsahasrāṇi nivasanti, taddviguṇāḥ śaikṣāḥ pṛthagjanakalyāṇakāḥ | tataḥ sa sthavirasya pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya | sthaviropaguptenāsya dharmo deśitaḥ | tataḥ kumāraḥ paripakvasaṃtatir dharmaṃ śrutvā pravrajyābhilāṣī saṃvṛttaḥ | sa rājānam aśokam anujñāpya sthaviropaguptasya sakāśe pravrajitaḥ | tena yujyamānena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | arhan saṃvṛttaḥ traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhaḥ | sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, for the purpose of astonishing the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, took the boy <s>Sundara</s> and went to the <s>Kukkuṭāgāra</s> (Cock-house [monastery]). There dwelt eighteen thousand <s>Arhats</s> headed by <s>Upagupta</s>, and twice that number of trainees and virtuous ordinary persons. Then he, having worshipped the Elder's feet, sat down before him for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the boy, whose mental continuum had matured, upon hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, became desirous of going forth. Having obtained permission from King <s>Aśoka</s>, he went forth under the Elder <s>Upagupta</s>. By striving, exerting, and applying himself, having understood this five-fold wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unstable and ever-changing — and having shattered all conditioned states by their nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and dissolving, through the abandonment of all defilements, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, the sky and the palm of his hand as alike, as cool as sandalwood paste and an axe, the egg of ignorance split open by knowledge, having attained the superknowledges, analytical knowledges, and direct knowledge, turned away from worldly gain, honor, and fame. He became one worthy of worship, respect, and veneration by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: tato rājā aśokaḥ saṃdigdhaḥ sthaviraṃ pṛcchati: kāni bhadanta sundareṇa karmāṇi kṛtāni, yenāsyaivaṃvidhaṃ rūpam*, kāni punaḥ karmāṇi yena divyagandhodakaparipūrṇā ratnamayī puṣkariṇī prādurbhūtā, puṣpaphalasamṛddhaṃ ca mahad udyānaṃ jaṅgamam*? sthaviropagupta āha: sundareṇaiva
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, filled with doubt, asked the Elder: 'What deeds, Venerable Sir, did <s>Sundara</s> perform that he has such extraordinary beauty? And what deeds [did he perform] that a jeweled lotus-pool filled with divinely fragrant water appeared, and a great garden abounding in flowers and fruit — a moving one?' The Elder <s>Upagupta</s> said: 'By <s>Sundara</s> himself,
[Reference: Vaidya, p. 263]

children.text: mahārāja pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāni oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni | sundareṇaiva karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni | ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau, api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca:
children.translated_text: Great King, in former births, deeds were performed and accumulated, whose provisions had been gathered, whose conditions had matured, which stood near like a flood, inevitable in their coming to be. By <s>Sundara</s> himself deeds were performed and accumulated. Who else would experience [their fruit]? Monks, deeds performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather, it is in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that deeds performed ripen — both good and bad:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇi kalpakoṭiśatair api |
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even in hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām* || AVŚ_100.1 ||
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they surely bear fruit for embodied beings. // AVŚ_100.1 //

children.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ mahārāja yadā bhagavān parinirvṛtaḥ, tadā āyuṣmān mahākāśyapaḥ pañcaśataparivāro magadheṣu janapadacārikāṃ caran dharmasaṃgītiṃ kartukāmaḥ | yāvad anyatamena daridrakarṣakeṇa mahān bhikṣusaṃgho dṛṣṭaḥ, śāstṛviyogāc chokārto 'dhvapariśrānto rajasāvacūrṇitagātraḥ | tato 'sya kāruṇyam utpannam* | tatas tena kāśyapapramukhāṇi pañca bhikṣuśatāni jentākasnātreṇopanimantritāni | tatas tena nānāgandhaparibhāvitam uṣṇodakaṃ kṛtvā te bhikṣavaḥ snāpitāḥ, cīvarakāṇi śobhitāni | praṇītena cāhāreṇa saṃtarpya śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni datvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam*: asminn eva śākyamuneḥ pravacane pravrajya cārhatvaṃ prāpnuyām iti ||
children.translated_text: In former times, Great King, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> had passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, accompanied by a retinue of five hundred, was wandering on a tour of the <s>Magadha</s> countryside, wishing to hold the <s>Dharmasaṃgīti</s> (Council of the <s>Dharma</s>). Now a certain poor farmer saw the great community of monks — grief-stricken from separation from the Teacher, exhausted by the road, their bodies covered with dust. Compassion arose in him. Then he invited the five hundred monks headed by <s>Kāśyapa</s> to a bath in a steam-house. Having prepared hot water infused with various fragrances, he bathed those monks, cleaned their robes, and satisfied them with excellent food. Having given them the refuges and precepts, he made this aspiration: 'In this very dispensation of <s>Śākyamuni</s>, may I go forth and attain <s>Arhatship</s>.'

children.text: kiṃ manyase mahārāja yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena daridrakarṣakaḥ, ayaṃ sa sundaro bhikṣuḥ | yat tena bhikṣavo jentākasnātreṇa snāpitāḥ, tenāsyaivaṃvidho rūpaviśeṣaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, divyacandanodakaparipūrṇā ramaṇīyā puṣkariṇī puṣpaphalasamṛddhaṃ ca mahad udyānaṃ jaṅgamaṃ prāptam* | yat tena śaraṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni upalabdhāni, teneha janmany arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam* | iti hi mahārāja ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ | tasmāt tarhi mahārāja ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam* ||
children.translated_text: What do you think, Great King? He who at that time, in that era, was the poor farmer — he is this monk <s>Sundara</s>. Because he bathed the monks in a steam-house, he obtained such extraordinary beauty, a delightful lotus-pool filled with divinely fragrant water, and a great garden abounding in flowers and fruit — a moving one. Because he received the refuges and precepts, in this birth he has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus indeed, Great King, entirely dark deeds have an entirely dark result; entirely bright deeds have an entirely bright result; mixed deeds have a mixed result. Therefore, Great King, having rejected entirely dark deeds and mixed deeds, you should apply yourself only to entirely bright deeds. Thus, monks, should you train.'

children.text: atha rāhā aśoka āyuṣmataḥ sthaviropaguptasya bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, having rejoiced in and approved the words of the venerable Elder <s>Upagupta</s>, rose from his seat and departed.
